The side effect inside the expression also makes the data flow hard to read and easy to break when someone edits it.
review.fix: Make `appendRuled` also return the folded `state` it gave to the rule, for example `{ ok: true; event: Event; state: MapState }`. Then build `const call = { ...request, state: written.state }` after the append. Remove the `let`, the assignment inside the expression, and the `!`.

review.impact: `logLines` copies the log path and the JSONL parsing that `readLog` in `src/map/log.ts` already has, and it adds a hand-written `as { ... }` cast for the event shape. `src/cli/serve.test.ts` uses `readLog` for the same job. If the log format or path changes, the e2e helper drifts away from the real reader.
review.fix: Import `readLog` (and `Event` if you need the type) from `../src/map/log.ts`, and define `logLines = (werk) => readLog(join(werk.dir, '.werk', 'log.jsonl'))`. Remove the manual parse and the cast.

review.impact: Two tests repeat the same two `werk.cli(['add', 'g1', ...])` / `werk.cli(['add', 'g2', ...])` setup lines (lines 39-40 and 66-67). If the ghost-chain fixture changes, both copies must change.
review.fix: Move the setup into a small helper, for example `const addGhostChain = (werk: Werk) => { ... }`, and call it from both tests.

review.impact: No test covers two branches of `acceptFromView`. The first is the 400 reply for a malformed percent-encoded id, such as `/api/accept/%E0%A4`. The second is a POST with no `origin` header, which the route accepts. A regression in either branch passes CI.
review.fix: Add two checks to the refusal test. First, `post('%E0%A4')` must give status 400 and must not append to the log. Second, a POST without an `origin` header to a ghost must give status 200. Alternatively, assert that this call is refused, if that is the decided behaviour.

review.impact: `appendRuled` is now the one shared write path for the command line and the server, but it has no direct unit test. Only the command-line tests reach its contract-refusal branch. The server route's refusal path is tested only for rule refusals, not for `checkChange` refusals. Its joined multi-line `refusalText` output is not tested either.
review.fix: Add a `log.test.ts` with three tests. (1) A rule refusal appends nothing and returns its error. (2) A contract refusal appends nothing and returns the joined `refusalText` lines. (3) A pass appends exactly one event with the next `seq` and the ruling's actor.

review.impact: The refused-✓ test covers only an HTTP 409. It does not cover the `fetch` rejection branch ("the server did not answer"). It also does not check that a second press clears the old alert, which the `AcceptButton` doc comment promises.
review.fix: Add a second press after `page.unroute`. Assert that the alert is gone and that `data-proposed` becomes `false`. Optionally, add a `route.abort()` case and assert that the alert contains `werk: the server did not answer`.

review.impact: The origin check compares the Origin header with the request's own Host header, and it does not check the Host value itself. A DNS rebinding attack defeats this check. A page on http://evil.example:PORT rebinds its name to 127.0.0.1. The browser then sends Origin http://evil.example:PORT and Host evil.example:PORT. The two values match, so the server accepts a cross-site POST. That POST appends a node.accepted event with actor 'you' for any ghost. The person did not press the ✓, but the log records that they did. A request with no Origin header also passes, so any HTTP client can do the same. The read routes have the same Host problem, but those routes were there before this change. This change adds the first route that writes.
review.fix: Allow the request only when the Host header names a loopback host on the server's port: 'localhost:<port>', '127.0.0.1:<port>' or '[::1]:<port>'. Use the configured host for a non-default bind. Then require the Origin to equal 'http://' + that allowed Host. Return 403 for any other Host or Origin, and also when the Origin header is missing on this POST route. Add a test that sends a POST with a matching but foreign Host and Origin pair, and expects a 403.

review.impact: `childrenOf` scans all of `graph.nodes` once for each node that the tree draws. This costs O(n²) per call. The change adds ghosts to the scan, so n grows. `refinesTree` also runs again each time the log changes. Each step also copies `seen` with `new Set(seen)`, so the cost grows with depth too. A log with a few thousand cards makes each redraw slower than it needs to be.
review.fix: Make a `Map<parentId, MapNode[]>` from `graph.nodes` in one pass, in log order. Then look up the children of a node in that map. Use one shared path set: add the id before you recurse and remove it after. Do not copy the set at each step.

review.impact: The report compares against the bare string 'amend' and always prints 'Its next hop is stale now.' The text is wrong when the amended card has no card below it. The outcome rule (an amend marks the next hop) now lives in three places: `staleness.ts`, `rules.ts`, and this report.
review.fix: Use the `ReviewOutcome` type for the outcome in the report. Word the amend line without a promise, for example 'Run werk stale to see the next hop.' Another option is to count the new marks from `deriveMarks` after the append.

review.impact: All other rules in `rules.ts` are pure functions of `MapState` only. `rederive` now also takes a `marks` map that the caller must derive from the same log. The pure rules module now depends on `staleness.ts`. A caller can pass marks that do not match `state`, and no check catches it.
review.fix: Keep the module dependency, but make the input consistent. Let `rederive` take `events` and call `deriveMarks(events, state)` inside the function. Another option is to document on `MapVerbCall` that `marks` must come from the same `events`.

review.impact: The change adds four copies of one helper that builds a real, decided card: `card` in `staleness.test.ts`, `card` in `stale-text.test.ts:7`, `decidedCard` in `rules.test.ts:327`, and a variant in `stale.test.ts:13`. If the facts that make a card "decided" change, someone must update every copy, and the copies will drift apart.
review.fix: Move one `decidedCard(id, fields?)` builder into `src/test/map-events.ts`, next to `reopened` and `rederived`. Import it in the three unit test files. Keep the `stale.test.ts` variant only for the extra decide facts that the CLI needs, and build it on top of the shared helper.

review.impact: The `reopenLog` parameter type repeats the literal union `'postponed' | 'rejected'` instead of using the `ReopenReason` type. If someone adds a reason to `REOPEN_REASONS`, this test helper does not accept it.
review.fix: Import `ReopenReason` from `./events.ts` and type the parameter as `reason: ReopenReason`.

review.impact: The test file writes the expression `join(p.dir, '.werk', 'log.jsonl')` four times: in `chainProject`, twice in `refuses`, and in `lastEvent`. If the log location changes, someone must edit every copy.
review.fix: Add one helper, `const logFile = () => join(p.dir, '.werk', 'log.jsonl')`, and use it in all four places.

review.impact: `fixOrder` stops a cycle with the `placed` set. No test covers marked cards that depend on each other, for example b depends_on c and c depends_on b, with both marked stale. If a later change removes the `placed.add` call before the recursion, the function recurses without end, and no test fails.
review.fix: Add a `fixOrder` test: link two decided cards to each other with depends_on, reopen with rejected a card that both depend on, and check that `fixOrder` returns each card one time.

review.impact: The only test with marks has both a stale and a paused card, so both hint lines always print. No test shows that `staleText` leaves out the stale hint when only paused marks exist, or the paused hint when only stale marks exist. The CLI tests use `toContain`, so they also do not check that a hint line is absent. Code that always prints both hints passes every test.
review.fix: Add a `staleText` test with only a postponed reopen. Use `toEqual` on the full output to show that only the paused hint line prints. Add a second test with only a rejected reopen to show that only the stale hint line prints.

review.impact: No test shows that a stale mark stays after the rejected card is decided again. Only a review clears a stale mark. The `lastDecide` check must apply to postponed changes only. If a change also applies it to rejected changes, every test still passes, and a re-decide silently clears stale marks that are still valid.
review.fix: Add a test: reopen `a` with rejected, set `a` to decided again, and check that `b` keeps its stale mark.

review.impact: `reopen` and `rederive` check only that `why` is not blank. A `--why` value that contains a newline or a terminal control sequence goes into the log as it is. `werk stale` then prints it in `traceLine` (src/map/stale-text.ts:7), and nothing escapes it. A newline breaks the one-line-per-trace layout and can create a fake `stale   #x` line. An ANSI escape sequence in the log changes the terminal output. The log is a local file that the user or an agent writes, so the risk is low.
review.fix: Refuse a `why` that contains a control character in `reopen` and `rederive`, for example with `/[\u0000-\u001f\u007f]/.test(why)`. Or escape control characters in `traceLine` before it prints `t.why`. No dependency changes, and no secret handling is in this diff.

review.impact: `below()` scans the whole `state.edges` array on every call. The postponed breadth-first search calls it once for each reached card, so one postponed change costs O(V·E), and the total cost is O(C·V·E) for C changes. The `werk stale` and `werk rederive` commands run this on every call. A map of a few hundred cards stays fast. Cost grows quadratically as the map grows.
review.fix: Before the loop over `changes`, build an index one time: `Map<to, Edge[]>` of the carrying edges. Then `below()` reads only the edges that point to `id` and filters them by `linkedAt` and `isCard`.

review.impact: An archived ticket stays in the `tickets` map, so `unmetBlockers` counts it as a blocker that is not done. A live ticket that is still in building or merging and names an archived ticket in `blockedBy` then shows an unmet blocker forever. Nothing can move the archived ticket to done.
review.fix: Decide what an archived blocker means, and code that rule in the fold. For example, skip archived tickets when it counts blockers: `tickets.get(n)?.column !== 'done' && tickets.get(n)?.archived === undefined`. Add a fold test for this case.

review.impact: The verb parses the leading ticket number from the file name with its own regex. `Ticket.number` in src/ticket/parse.ts already gives this number. The two rules can drift apart. Then `planBoard` archives or keeps a ticket based on a number that differs from the number the checks use.
review.fix: Get the numbers from the parsed tickets. One way: let `checkTickets` return the parsed number of every file, failed files too. Another way: call the parse function once per file. Then pass those numbers to `planBoard`.

review.impact: `appendEvent<N extends object = NewEvent>` accepts any object. A call that passes a board event, or any other object, to the decision log path compiles with no error, so the type no longer protects the decision log. Also, the cast `as Event` in `appendRuling` hides this gap.
review.fix: Constrain `N` to `NewEvent | NewBoardEvent`, or add a separate typed `appendBoardEvent(path, event: NewBoardEvent, actor)` in the board module. Keep `appendEvent` typed to `NewEvent` and remove the `as Event` cast in map-verb.ts.

review.impact: For each answer, the verb reads and folds the full log two times. `appendRuling` then folds it two more times, and `appendEvent` reads it again. The cost grows with the log size multiplied by the answer count. The verb also does the board appends one at a time, and each append reads the whole board log again.
review.fix: Read the log one time per answer and pass the same events to `proposeAnswer(fold(events), …)` and `appendRuling(path, events, …)`. You can also let `appendRuling` accept the folded state that the caller already has.

review.impact: The plan verb imports `appendRuling` from `../map-verb.ts`, which is the generic map-verb runner. The plan verb is not a map verb. This adds a dependency from one CLI module to another CLI module for a log-write rule that is not specific to the CLI.
review.fix: Move `appendRuling` and the `Appended` type into a shared module, such as src/map/append.ts, beside `checkChange` and `appendEvent`. Then let map-verb.ts and plan.ts both import it from there.

review.impact: The plan verb parses the leading ticket number from the file name with its own regex. `parseTicket` in `src/ticket/parse.ts` already derives `Ticket.number` from the same rule. If the rule changes in one place, archiving and the board step disagree on ticket numbers. The test helper in `src/plan/board-plan.test.ts:17` copies the regex a third time.
review.fix: Export one `ticketNumber(name)` helper next to the parser. Use it in `parseTicket`, `plan.ts` and the test. Or let `checkTickets` return the number of every file, failed ones too.

review.impact: Each answer reads and parses the whole log two times: once for `appendRuling` and once for `fold` in `proposeAnswer`. `appendRuling` then folds the same events again. The duplicate reads make it unclear which snapshot the ruling uses.
review.fix: Read the log one time per answer: `const events = readLog(path); appendRuling(path, events, proposeAnswer(fold(events), root, answer))`.

review.impact: The text `the <role> writer exited N: <stderr>` is built two times with the same template, at lines 127 and 145. A change to the message must be made in both places.
review.fix: Let `runWriter` return the stop message, or add a small `exited(name, result)` helper and use it for both writers.

review.impact: `appendEvent(...) as Event` and the `as Event` on `next` are type casts. The generic return type of `appendEvent` does not narrow back to `Event`, so the compiler no longer checks that a ruling event and its envelope form a valid `Event`.
review.fix: Give `appendEvent` an overload for the default `NewEvent` that returns `Event`. Or type `Ruling.event` so that `NewEvent & Pick<Event,'seq'|'at'|'actor'>` is assignable to `Event`, and remove the casts.

review.impact: A nested ternary inside two destructurings (`prev?.archived === undefined ? (prev ?? {}) : {}`) hides one simple rule: a re-plan of an archived ticket resets the column and the reason, and keeps the retries. The line is hard to read and easy to break.
review.fix: Write the rule out: `const live = prev && prev.archived === undefined ? prev : undefined; const column = live?.column ?? 'ready'; const reason = live?.reason;`.

review.impact: No test re-plans a ticket that an earlier plan archived. `planBoard` has `existing.archived` branches at `src/plan/board-plan.ts:85` and `src/plan/board-plan.ts:97`, so this restore path can change without a failing test. `fold.test.ts` covers the fold half only.
review.fix: Add a case with `boardOf(...on(2, 'blocked'), { type: 'ticket.archived', payload: { number: 2, reason: 'x' } })` and a new `02-b.md` file. Assert that the plan emits only `ticket.planned` for 2, with no `ticket.moved`. Assert that `foldBoard` puts ticket 2 in ready, with no reason and not in `archived`.

review.impact: In the archive loop, an open ticket in blocked whose new file fails its own checks takes the 'no event' branch, because only `t.column === 'ready'` moves. No test covers that branch. A change that emits a second move, or that archives the ticket, still passes.
review.fix: In the 'fixed ticket leaves blocked' test, add a case where ticket 2 is already in blocked and `02-b.md` fails its own checks. Assert that `events` is empty for number 2 and that no `archived` line appears.

review.impact: The plan builds its work directory as join(dirname(path), 'plans', root) and later runs rmSync(files.tickets, { recursive: true, force: true }) and rmSync on the answers files. Nothing checks the format of a card id: propose() in src/map/rules.ts accepts any string. A decided card with an id such as '../../src' or an absolute path makes the plan delete '<that dir>/tickets' outside .werk/plans. It also makes the writers write their files there. An agent can propose such an id, so the only guard is that a person accepts the card and decides it without noticing.
review.fix: Before mkdirSync, reject a root that does not match a safe slug pattern, for example /^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$/ (the pattern that answers.ts already uses). Or resolve the path and refuse it when it is not inside join(dirname(path), 'plans'). Also add a case to plan.test.ts for a traversal id.

review.impact: Each headless writer runs with '--permission-mode acceptEdits' and the full process.env. No --allowedTools or directory scope is set, so a writer can edit any file in the project without a prompt, not only the files in plans/<root>/. The prompt tells it to run 'werk show <id>', but no tool allowlist grants that Bash command.
review.fix: Pass an explicit --allowedTools list: Read, Edit and Write, plus a Bash pattern for 'werk show:*'. Keep the writers' edits inside the plan directory where the CLI supports it.

review.impact: For each answer, the code reads and parses the whole decision log twice: `readLog(path)` runs once for `appendRuling` and once for `proposeAnswer`. It folds the log three times: once here and two times inside `appendRuling`. Then `appendEvent` reads the log a fourth time. The cost is O(answers × log size), and it repeats the same parse work for each answer.
review.fix: Read the log one time per answer: `const events = readLog(path); appendRuling(path, events, proposeAnswer(fold(events), root, answer))`. As an option, let `appendRuling` take the fold of `events` that the caller already has, so it does not fold the same events again.

review.impact: The code calls `appendEvent` one time for each board event. Each call reads and parses the whole `board.jsonl` again to find the last `seq`. A plan with many tickets on a large board log does O(events × log size) parse work.
review.fix: Read the board log one time, then assign the `seq` values in order. Then write all of the plan's events with one `appendFileSync`, for example through an `appendEvents(path, events, actor)` helper in `src/map/log.ts`.

causeOfLast.why: main moved the map verbs onto `appendRuled` and added the board fold to the pure-file list, and both changes touched the same lines as this ticket.

review.impact: `setStatus` still lets `werk status <id> open` move a decided card back to open. That path writes `node.status_set`, not `node.reopened`, so it records no reason and no why, and `deriveMarks` puts no stale or paused mark on the cards below. The diff creates two ways to reopen a card, and only one of them carries the marks. A user or an agent can take the old path and hide a real invalidation without a warning.
review.fix: In `setStatus`, refuse a change from `decided` to another status. Point the user to `werk reopen <id> --reason postponed|rejected --why "..."`. Alternatively, send that transition through `reopen` so that one rule controls it.

review.impact: `rules.ts` now imports the `Marked` type from `staleness.ts`, and `rederive` reads only `mark` and `traces[].cause` from it. The rule depends on the full derived-mark shape. A change to `Trace` or `Marked` now also touches the verb rules.
review.fix: Pass `rederive` the smaller value it uses, for example `{ mark: MarkKind; causes: string[] } | undefined` for the one card. Or keep the import and accept the coupling on purpose.

review.impact: Four test files define the same 'decided card' event builder: `card` in staleness.test.ts, stale-text.test.ts and stale.test.ts, and `decidedCard` in rules.test.ts. Each copy differs a little (a title, the decide facts, or extra fields). A change to the decide path must be made in four places, and the copies can drift apart.
review.fix: Add one `decidedCard(id, fields?)` builder to src/test/map-events.ts, next to `reopened` and `rederived`. Import it in all four files. stale.test.ts can add its decide facts on top of the shared builder.

review.impact: The expected output contains hard-coded sequence numbers ('event 35', 'event 36'). These numbers depend on how many events the `card` helper and `chainProject` emit. A change to either helper breaks these tests even though the behavior has not changed, and the cause is hard to see.
review.fix: Compute the sequence number from the log, for example with `lastEvent().seq` right after the reopen. Or derive it from `events.length + 1` in `chainProject` and put that value into the expected string.

review.impact: The `fixOrder` tests use only `depends_on` links. A change that drops the parent from `basisOf` in `src/map/staleness.ts:139` still passes every test, so a child can print before its marked parent and nothing catches it.
review.fix: Add a `fixOrder` case with a `refines` chain p <- k <- g and a rejected reopen of two cards in that chain. Order the reopens so that the child's mark is older than the parent's mark. Then assert that the parent prints first.

review.impact: The 'link made after the change' test covers only `edge.linked`. Nothing tests the `node.proposed` parent branch in `deriveMarks`, which records the time of a `refines` link. If that branch is removed, a card that is proposed under its parent after a reopen gets a wrong mark, and no test fails.
review.fix: Add a case: reopen p as rejected and as postponed. After the reopen, propose, accept and decide a card k with `{ parent: 'p' }`. Assert that `marksOf(...)` is an empty Map.

review.impact: Only paused marks have a test for 'decided again'. Nothing pins the rule that a rejected reopen's stale mark stays after the cause is decided again. A change that clears stale marks on a decide in the same way as paused marks passes all tests.
review.fix: Add a case: `marksOf(...chain, reopened('a', 'rejected'), statusSet('a', 'decided'))`. Assert that b is still marked stale.

review.impact: The test includes `reopened('nope', 'rejected')` but asserts only node a. If fold creates a node for an unknown id on reopen, the test still passes.
review.fix: Also assert `expect(state.nodes.size).toBe(1)` or `expect(state.nodes.has('nope')).toBe(false)`.

review.impact: The only multi-card test has both stale and paused cards, so both footer lines print. If the `has('stale')` or `has('paused')` guard is removed, both footers always print and no test fails. The CLI tests use `toContain` and do not check that the other footer is absent.
review.fix: Add one case with only a rejected reopen and one with only a postponed reopen. Assert the full line array with `toEqual`, so each case shows that the other footer line is absent.

review.impact: `below` scans all of `state.edges` on every call. The postponed walk calls it once for each card it reaches, so one postponed change costs O(N·E), and the whole function costs O(C·N·E) for C changes. `werk stale` and `werk rederive` both run this. Each `rederive` runs it inside `appendRuled`, so the cost grows with the size of the map and the log.
review.fix: Before the loop over changes, build an index from target id to its incoming carrying edges, for example `Map<string, Edge[]>`, in one pass over `state.edges`. Then `below` reads `index.get(id)` and filters by `linkedAt` and `isCard`.

review.impact: `add` copies the whole trace array each time it appends one trace. A card with k traces costs O(k²) copies.
review.fix: Push into the existing array: `const list = traces.get(id); if (list) list.push({ kind, trace }); else traces.set(id, [{ kind, trace }])`.

review.impact: `fixOrder` calls `basisOf` once for each marked card. Each call scans all edges twice, once in its own filter and once in `parentEdge`, so the cost is O(M·E).
review.fix: Build an outgoing-edge index by `from` id one time in `fixOrder`. Then read the depends_on targets and the parent from that index.

causeOfLast.why: another ticket moved the checked append into `appendRuled` in the log module while this ticket added `appendRuling` for the same job in `map-verb.ts`.

review.impact: `appendEvent` now accepts `N extends object`. TypeScript infers `N` from the argument, so the `NewEvent` default never applies. Any caller can append any object to the decision log without a type error. Before this change, the type system blocked a malformed or board event in `log.jsonl`.
review.fix: Keep `appendEvent(path, event: NewEvent, actor)` for the decision log. Add a separate typed `appendBoardEvent(path, event: NewBoardEvent, actor)`, ideally in a board log module. Both can share a private untyped helper.

review.impact: `Bun.spawnSync` throws when `claude` is not on PATH. `runWriter` does not catch the throw. `werk plan` then crashes with a stack trace after it has written the `tier.recorded` event, and the `stop()` path that reports a writer failure does not run.
review.fix: Wrap the spawn in try/catch. Return `{ code: -1, stderr: err.message }` so the caller reports the error through `stop()` as 'the spec writer exited -1: ...'.

review.impact: An archived ticket keeps its old `column` and gets an `archived` marker as a second state field. Each consumer must check `archived === undefined` next to `column`. `planBoard` does this in three places, and the `ticket.planned` case does it with a hard-to-read double destructure. A future consumer that forgets the check treats an archived ticket as open.
review.fix: Make archive a state of the ticket, for example `column: Column | 'archived'` in the fold's internal State, and keep the reason. Or give `planBoard` one helper `isOpen(t)` and use it everywhere.

review.impact: The verb parses ticket numbers from file names with its own regex. `src/ticket/parse.ts` already defines `Ticket.number` as 'the leading digits of the file name'. The two rules can drift apart, and then archive decisions (`fileNumbers`) and placement decisions (`t.number`) disagree.
review.fix: Export one `ticketNumber(name)` function from `src/ticket/parse.ts`. Use it both in the parser and in the plan verb.

review.impact: The leading-number rule for a ticket file name now exists in two places. `src/ticket/parse.ts:96` already derives `number` from the file name. This line runs the same `/^\d+/` regex twice and uses a non-null assertion. If one copy of the rule changes, `planBoard` archives or keeps the wrong tickets.
review.fix: Move the rule into one exported helper, for example `ticketNumber(name): number | null` in `src/ticket/parse.ts`. Use it in the parser and here: `ticketFiles.flatMap((f) => { const n = ticketNumber(f.name); return n === null ? [] : [n] })`. Use the same helper in `src/plan/board-plan.test.ts:16`.

review.impact: Line 123 and line 140 build the same 'the <role> exited <code>[: stderr]' message. A change to the format must be made in two places.
review.fix: Return the failure message from `runWriter`, or add a helper `writerFailure(name, result)`. Then call it from both places.

review.impact: The `ticket.planned` case uses two destructurings and a nested ternary with `?? {}`. The rule is 'a re-planned archived ticket goes back to ready with no reason', but the code does not show it clearly.
review.fix: Write the rule out: `const revived = prev?.archived !== undefined; const column = revived ? 'ready' : (prev?.column ?? 'ready'); const reason = revived ? undefined : prev?.reason`.

review.impact: The four `as string` casts repeat a check that the `missing` filter already made. The compiler does not connect the two, so if someone edits `FIELDS`, a field that is not a string can pass without a type error.
review.fix: Add a type guard such as `isAnswer(r): r is Answer` that checks `FIELDS`. Or build the record with `Object.fromEntries(FIELDS.map((f) => [f, r[f]])) as Answer` once, after the check.

review.impact: No test covers a new ticket file whose number belongs to an archived ticket. `board.archived` is merged into `onBoard`, and two guards check `existing.archived` (lines 87 and 98), but no test reaches those paths. A change could drop the `archived === undefined` check at line 87. An archived ticket whose last column was building would then print 'kept ... in building' and never come back. A change could also drop the check at line 98. Then an archived ticket that was blocked gets a redundant move to ready. All tests would still pass in both cases.
review.fix: Add a board-plan test. Build a board with `on(2, 'building')` and then a `ticket.archived` for 2, and another board with `on(2, 'blocked')` and then a `ticket.archived` for 2. Plan `[file('02-b.md')]` against each. Assert that the events are exactly one `ticket.planned` for 2 with no `ticket.moved`, that the line is 'ready 2 ...', and that `boardOf(...)` puts 2 back in ready. Also assert that an archived ticket of another root gives the 'belongs to' problem.

review.impact: No test checks the list of open tickets that goes into the ticket writer prompt. The test 'a second plan archives' does not check the second launch's prompt. A bug in the root filter or the column filter would leak another subtree's tickets into the prompt, and the tests would not fail. The same bug could also leave out the subtree's own ready or blocked tickets.
review.fix: In the test 'a second plan archives', assert that `p.agentLaunches().at(-1)![1]` contains '1. ' plus the title of ticket 1 and the title of ticket 3. Add a ticket of another root to the board first, and assert that the prompt does not contain it.

review.impact: The re-plan test after an archive checks the column and the reason. It does not check `retries`. The fold keeps `retries` on purpose across an archive (`const { retries = 0 } = prev ?? {}`). A change that resets `retries` would pass the tests.
review.fix: Add `retry(1)` before `archive(1, ...)`. Assert `ticketOf(board, 1).retries` is 1 after the second `ticket(1)`.

review.impact: The plan builds its directory from the root card id with `join(dirname(path), 'plans', root)`. Then it calls `rmSync(files.tickets, { recursive: true, force: true })` and `rmSync(...answers.json)`. `propose` in src/map/rules.ts does not check the format of a card id. If a decided card has an id such as `../..` or `../../../src`, `werk plan` deletes `<that dir>/tickets` recursively, outside `.werk/plans`. It also lets the writers write outside `.werk/plans`. For this to happen, the person must accept and decide such a card. The user runs a destructive recursive delete, so do not trust the id to be a safe path.
review.fix: Before the plan uses `root` as a path segment, check it against a strict pattern, for example `/^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$/` (the SLUG pattern in answers.ts). Also check that `resolve(dir)` stays inside `resolve(dirname(path), 'plans')`. Call `stop()` if either check fails. A better fix also adds the same id check to `propose`.

review.impact: Each `appendEvent` call reads and parses the whole board log only to find the last `seq`. The loop calls it once for each event in `outcome.events`, so one plan costs O(events × log size) reads. That cost grows as the board log grows across many plans. Board logs are small today, so the cost is minor.
review.fix: Add a batch append, for example `appendEvents(path, events, actor)`. It reads the log one time, assigns consecutive `seq` values, and writes all lines in one `appendFileSync` call. Use it for `outcome.events`.

grade.gap: The card names web/md.js and web/style.css. The diff puts the highlighter in src/markdown/highlight.ts and the box style in web/app.css. web/app.css is the only stylesheet in the repo, and the behaviour matches the card (a box, horizontal scroll, no pretty-print), so this is not a contradiction.

The card names web/md.js as the renderer. The diff builds it as src/markdown/render.ts, about 160 lines with no dependencies. The behaviour matches the card: fenced code is handled before any inline rule, an unclosed fence still renders, and all text is escaped first. Card bodies use this renderer. The diff does not build the streaming and SSE part, which is another ticket's work.

review.impact: `inline()` runs `refSegments` on HTML that is already escaped, and on text that holds the private-use placeholders. This makes the reference rule depend on how `escapeHtml` writes its output: for example, `'` instead of `'`, and entity names that hold no hyphen or colon. The comment in `escape.ts` records this rule, but the code does not enforce it. A later change to `escapeHtml`, or a new placeholder format, can create false links or break links without a failing test in `reflink.test.ts`.
review.fix: Run `refSegments` on the raw text pieces before escaping, and escape each string part after the split. Alternatively, add a test in `render.test.ts` that pins the rule: escaped text and placeholder marks never produce a reference.

review.impact: `list()` writes its HTML into the caller's `out` array and returns the next line index. Every other branch of `blocks()` pushes its own result. This mixed contract makes `list()` harder to reuse and test on its own.
review.fix: Return `{ html, next }` from `list()`, and let `blocks()` push the HTML, the same as the other block branches.

review.impact: The why line, the body and the notes now render as Markdown with card links. The `whyNot` line stays plain text. A `#id` in `whyNot` does not link, so one card has two rendering rules for the same kind of text.
review.fix: Render `node.whyNot` through `<Markdown text={node.whyNot} hrefOf={hrefOf} />` in the same way as `why`. If plain text is intentional, add a comment that says why.

review.impact: The `fence as unknown as [string, string, string]` double cast turns off type checking for the match groups. A later change to `FENCE`, for example a new or removed group, does not cause a type error.
review.fix: Read the groups with non-null assertions, as the code does for `heading` (`const marker = fence[1]!; const lang = fence[2] ?? ''`). Or use named groups and read `fence.groups`.

review.impact: `ITEM.exec(line)` runs three times for each list line. `blocks` runs it once only to test the line. `list` runs it again at line 86, and the loop runs it twice per line (in `sameList` and again at line 98). The bound `item` variable in `blocks` is never used.
review.fix: In `blocks`, use `if (ITEM.test(line))`, as `startsBlock` does. In `list`, make `sameList` return the match or null, and push `match[4]` from that result. Then `ITEM` does not run a second time.

review.impact: The fallback regex `/\w+|[\s\S]/y` is a new object for each character that no rule takes. This adds cost on each step of the loop, and it differs from the rules, which are module-level constants.
review.fix: Move it to a module-level constant, for example `const WORD = /\w+|[\s\S]/y`, next to `NUMBER`. Set `WORD.lastIndex = at` in the loop, as the code does for the rule patterns.

review.impact: The test 'an unclosed string or comment still renders' checks only that `textOf` returns the original characters. Plain escaped output with no spans also passes. So the test still passes if the `(?:\*\/|$)` branch is removed from the `com` rule, and an unclosed `/* open` is then left unhighlighted.
review.fix: Also check the tokens. For example, add `expect(tokens(highlight('/* open\nstill', 'js'))).toEqual(['com:/* open\nstill'])`. For the json case, check that `"open` is not given a `tok-str` span.

review.impact: The test 'a heading marker is not a reference' uses `# rollup`. `rollup` has no hyphen, so the bare-id rule rejects it even without the space check. The test does not fail if `#\s+id` is wrongly accepted as a hashed reference.
review.fix: Use an id that is single-word and known, and that only a hashed match can link. Then add a contrast case. For example, `expect(linked('# rollup')).toEqual([])` together with `expect(linked('#rollup')).toEqual(['rollup'])`. Another option is `linked('#\trollup')`.

review.impact: The code-span rule runs before the link rule, so a link URL can hold a set-aside placeholder. Example: `[x](/a`al-diff`)`. The renderer restores the placeholder inside the href value. A card-link code span puts its own `"` there, which closes the href attribute early. The output is `...">x`. Text from the card can now break out of an attribute and write markup into the page through dangerouslySetInnerHTML. The id regex limits the content today, so this is not a script execution. But the guarantee 'the HTML holds no markup that the text did not ask for' is false.
review.fix: Reject a URL that holds a placeholder mark: test the URL for /[\uE000\uE001]/ and leave the whole match as text when it matches. Another option is to match links before code spans. Add a test for `[x](/a`al-diff`)`.

review.impact: SAFE_URL blocks `//other.host` but accepts `/\other.host`. Browsers read a backslash as a slash in http(s) URLs. So `[a](/\evil.dev)` renders as `<a href="/\evil.dev">` and goes to evil.dev. That is the off-host link that the test 'a link to another host with no scheme stays text' says must not render.
review.fix: Change the path branch to `\/(?![\/\\])`, or reject any URL that holds a backslash. Add a test for `[a](/\evil.dev)`.

review.impact: `highlight` builds a new `/\w+|[\s\S]/y` RegExp on every pass of the scan loop where no token rule matches. Most positions in code are plain words, spaces or punctuation, so a large fenced block allocates and compiles one RegExp per plain step. This work is not needed.
review.fix: Move the regex to a module constant, for example `const WORD = /\w+|[\s\S]/y`. Inside the loop, set `WORD.lastIndex = at` before each `exec`. The rule patterns already work this way.

grade.gap: The behaviour is met: src/cli/remove.test.ts 'a remove with reparent keeps the children in the map under the grandparent' passes. The criterion names a 'lift' option, but src/cli/verbs/remove.ts names the switch --reparent and the payload field reparent. If the ticket means the option to be called lift, rename the switch, the usage text and the payload field. If it does not, no change is needed.

review.impact: `postponedCards` is a second copy of the rule for when a postponed reopen stops holding a card, and it disagrees with the first copy. `deriveMarks` in `src/map/staleness.ts` (line 98) lifts a postponed hold only when the card is decided again (`lastDecide > seq`). `postponedCards` lifts it on any `node.status_set` and on any reopen that is not postponed. So `find` and `stale` can disagree about the same card, and a future change to the pause rule has to be made in two places.
review.fix: Keep the postponed-hold rule in one place, in `staleness.ts`. Export a helper from there that returns the cards a postponed reopen still holds, or let `deriveMarks` report them. Make `openCards` call that helper. If the find rule must differ, say so in the module doc and name the difference.

review.impact: The report folds the whole log again (`fold([...events, event])`) only to read the last removal back. This doubles the fold work for each remove. It also ties the CLI output to the order of the `removals` list inside the fold. The restore report, by contrast, reads the state that it already has.
review.fix: Build the report from the state before the event. Compute the branch with a helper exported from `fold.ts`, for example `removalPreview(state, id, reparent)`. Use the same helper in `fold` and in the report, so that the two cannot drift apart.

review.impact: In `Removal`, `parent?: string` is set only when `reparented` is not empty, and the type does not record that link. Each reader must use a non-null assertion that depends on this rule (`r.parent!` in `staleness.ts:73` and `fold.ts:133`). The template string in `show-text.ts` reads `r.parent` with no check. A later change can break the rule and produce `undefined` with no type error.
review.fix: Make `Removal` a discriminated union, for example `{ reparented: [] } | { reparented: string[]; parent: string }`. Or always store `parent` when it exists. Then remove the `!` assertions.

review.impact: `werk find <removed-id>` prints `no card "x" in the map`. Every other verb that gets a removed id prints the restore hint from `refuseRemoved`. The error messages for a removed id are not the same across verbs, and `find` gives the user no path back.
review.fix: Before the generic error, check `state.removed.has(root)`. If it is true, print the same 'was removed from the map. Bring it back first with: werk restore <removal id>' message. Export a small helper from `rules.ts` so that `find` uses the same text as the other verbs.

review.impact: The lookup 'the removal that took this node' is written twice: here as `state.removals.find((removal) => removal.ids.includes(id))!`, and in `src/map/rules.ts:295` as the private `removalOf`. `src/cli/verbs/restore.ts:15` does a similar search by `removal.id`. If the removal model changes, a maintainer must find and update every copy.
review.fix: Export one `removalOf(state, id)` helper from `src/map/fold.ts`, next to the `Removal` type. Use it in `rules.ts`, `show-text.ts` and `restore.ts`.

review.impact: `report` folds the full log again with the new event to recompute which ids the removal takes. This repeats work the rule already depends on, and it runs a second full fold for each call. It also adds a third copy of the `title` lookup that `restore.ts` repeats inline.
review.fix: Pass the post-append state to `report`, if `runMapVerb` can do this. Otherwise move the removal preview into a named helper in `src/map` that the rule and `report` share.

review.impact: In `Removal`, `parent` is optional, but `parent` always has a value when `reparented` is not empty. Because the type does not say this, callers use non-null assertions: `r.parent!` in `staleness.ts:73`, `parent!` in `fold.ts:119`, and an unchecked `#${r.parent}` in `show-text.ts`.
review.fix: Model the relation in the type. Example: `reparent?: { parent: string; children: string[] }` in place of `reparented` and `parent`. Then the callers need no `!`.

review.impact: No test covers the empty-result message `no ... card ... is free to work on`. No test covers the usage error for more than one id (`takes one id at most`). A regression in either path passes the suite.
review.fix: In src/cli/remove.test.ts, add `ok(['find', 'top', '--status', 'proto'])` and assert the empty-result line. Add `refuses(['find', 'a', 'b'], 2, 'takes one id at most')`.

review.impact: The `removed` verb promises 'newest removal first', but each test has at most one removal. If someone removes the `toReversed()` call, no test fails.
review.fix: Remove two separate cards, for example `kid2` and then `bad`. Assert that the `#bad` line comes before the `#kid2` line in the `werk removed` output.

review.impact: No test checks the restore report line `its children are back under it: ...` for a reparented removal. The CLI reparent test never runs a restore, so a wrong or missing line goes undetected.
review.fix: In the CLI reparent test, run `werk restore bad`. Assert that stdout contains `its children are back under it: kid1, kid2`. Assert that `show kid1` again prints `parent: #bad`.

review.impact: Some reparent cases have no test. In one, a removed card has a ghost child: `childrenOf` includes ghosts, so the ghost is reparented. In another, a reparented child is removed on its own before the parent is restored. A regression in how fold handles reparented edges in these cases goes undetected.
review.fix: In src/map/remove.test.ts, add a case for `removed('bad', true)` with a ghost child under `bad`, and assert where the ghost goes. Add a case for `removed('bad', true), removed('kid1'), restored('bad')`, and assert the state of `kid1` and `grandkid`.

review.impact: The `report` callback calls `fold([...events, event])`. This copies the whole log and folds it a second time only to read the last `Removal`. The cost grows with the log size, and `runMapVerb` already folded the same log. The CLI runs once per call, so the cost is small now.
review.fix: Build the `Removal` without a second full fold, or have `appendRuled`/`runMapVerb` return the folded state after the append. Another option is to apply the one new event to the state the verb already has.

review.impact: `withOwn` loops over every edge for every node in the branch. It then calls `heldOnlyByBranch`, which also loops over every edge, for each candidate. That is O(branch × edges + candidates × edges) for each `node.removed` event, and every command that folds the log repeats this work. A large map with many removals makes each fold slower.
review.fix: Index the edges by endpoint once at the start of the removal, with a Map from node id to its edges. Then visit only the edges of each branch node and of each candidate.

grade.gap: src/build/loop.ts stops on green checks alone. The grade and review steps are missing, but another ticket builds them, so this line passes.
src/cli/verbs/build.ts adds the verb 'build'. No card under #werk-cli-build was checked for its form. The card lists 'build' under Build, so the verb name matches.

review.impact: The loop moves the ticket to `building` before the passes start. Only the `finally` block runs cleanup, and it only removes the worktree. Several failures can throw inside the `try`: a `GitError` from `commitPass`, a spawn error when `claude` is not on PATH, or a write error in `appendPassLine`. After any of these, the build ends with no green or red outcome, but the ticket stays in `building`. The verb then refuses every new build with "ticket N is in building, not in ready". No verb moves the ticket back, so the operator must edit `board.jsonl` by hand. Also, `build.ts` only catches `GitError`, so a spawn ENOENT reaches the user as a raw stack trace.
review.fix: Make the error path explicit. Option 1: catch errors inside the loop and append a `ticket.moved` event (back to `ready`, or to `blocked` with a `reason`) before you throw again. Option 2: append the `building` move only after the first pass commit succeeds. In `build.ts`, also report a spawn failure of the agent as a one-line error with exit code 1.

review.impact: `src/build/loop.ts` imports the `Io` type from `../cli/registry.ts`. No other module outside `src/cli` depends on the CLI layer. Now the build domain depends on the command-line layer, which is the wrong direction for the dependency.
review.fix: Let `buildTicket` take a narrow callback such as `report: (line: string) => void`, or move the `Io` type to a shared module. `build.ts` then passes `io.out`.

review.impact: `storiesOf` builds the path `join(dirname(log), 'plans', root, 'spec.md')` again. `src/cli/verbs/plan.ts:94` already builds the same layout inline. If the plan folder layout changes, someone must find and change both copies, and a missed copy silently yields bare story numbers.
review.fix: Add a `planDir(log, root)` helper next to `boardPath` in `src/map/log.ts`. Use it in both places.

review.impact: `if (problem !== undefined || !ticket) return { error: problem! }` uses a non-null assertion that depends on a link `notBuildable` keeps between its two outputs and that the type system cannot see. If `notBuildable` changes, the build can return `{ error: undefined }`, and the verb prints `werk build: undefined`.
review.fix: Use two checks: `if (!ticket) return { error: \`no ticket ${o.ticket} on the board\` }`, then `if (problem) return { error: problem }`. Another option: let `notBuildable` return a discriminated result that carries the narrowed ticket.

review.impact: The test overwrites the bin `claude` with `sleep 5`. That replaces the fake agent, so the `p.scriptAgent(...)` call on the line before it does nothing. The comment says that 'the fake agent replays its steps, then the shell sleeps', and this is false. A reader can believe that the timed-out pass also made `done.txt`.
review.fix: Delete the dead `p.scriptAgent` call and correct the comment. For example: 'A builder that sleeps: replace the fake agent with a shell that sleeps past the limit.' Or add a harness helper that sets a delay on the fake agent, so the test does not write to the PATH directly.

review.impact: `if (problem !== undefined || !ticket) return { error: problem! }` uses a non-null assertion to hide a case that the types allow: `ticket` is undefined and `problem` is undefined. Only the inner logic of `notBuildable` prevents that case. A later edit to `notBuildable` can return `{ error: undefined }` with no type error.
review.fix: Make `notBuildable` narrow the type. For example, return `{ ok: true, ticket } | { ok: false, error }`. Or check `if (!ticket) return { error: `no ticket ${o.ticket} on the board` }` before the call. Then remove the `!`.

review.impact: The loop has two exits for one condition. The `while (!green && ...)` guard and the `break` at line 110 both stop the loop on a green pass. The `!green` part of the guard can never be the reason that the loop stops, so a reader must check both exits.
review.fix: Use `while (pass < o.cap)` and keep the `break` on green. Or remove the `break` and put the red-path code in an `else` branch.

review.impact: `saveFailure` returns the path of the saved file, but no caller reads it. Also, `Worktree.base` (src/build/worktree.ts:10) is set but never read, because `loop.ts` keeps its own `base` variable. The interface has values that nothing uses.
review.fix: Make `saveFailure` return `void`, or use the path (for example, print it in the red-pass line). Remove `base` from `Worktree`, or read `tree.base` in `loop.ts` instead of the separate `base` variable.

review.impact: The agent-timeout part of the test does not check how long the run takes. `spawnWithLimit` sets `timedOut = true` before it sends the kill, so `agentTimedOut: true` and `agentExit: null` are recorded even when the kill fails and the fake `sleep 5` runs to its end. The check-timeout half of the same test has a time bound, so a break in the group kill for the agent passes silently.
review.fix: Time the `slow` run with `performance.now()` and assert `toBeLessThan(4000)`, as the check half of the test does.

review.impact: The tiny-limit test asserts only the prefix. With `limit = 10`, `cutFailure` returns the whole head plus the cut marker, which is far over 10 characters. The function's doc says 'at most `limit` characters in all'. The test accepts output that breaks that contract and does not pin the real behaviour.
review.fix: Assert the full expected string: head plus marker plus an empty tail. Also change the doc comment to say that the head is always kept, even past the limit. Or clamp the result and assert `cut.length <= 10`.

review.impact: Four tests call `project()` two times. `afterEach` cleans only the last `p`, so the temporary root of the first project is never deleted. Each run of the suite leaves temp folders behind.
review.fix: Keep a list of the projects in the test file, and clean all of them in `afterEach`. Or call `p.cleanup()` before the second `project()` call.

review.impact: No test covers the `finally` path, where a pass throws (for example, `commitPass` raises a `GitError`) and the worktree folder must still be removed. No test covers the `the agent exited N` note for an agent with a non-zero exit either. A regression in either path goes undetected.
review.fix: Add a build test with a fake builder reply that has `exit: 3`. Assert `pass 1: red at make check, the agent exited 3` and `agentExit: 3`. Add a test that makes a git step fail, and assert `git worktree list` has one entry after the build.

review.impact: Each pass runs `claude -p` with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` and the full `process.env`, which includes any API keys and cloud credentials. The prompt also carries untrusted text: up to 4,000 characters of check output, plus the ticket brief. A prompt injection in that text can make the agent run any command with the user's credentials. The agent is not limited to the temporary worktree. It can write to the main checkout, for example `.werk/board.jsonl` and `.werk/log.jsonl`, or push with the user's git credentials.
review.fix: Give the agent an environment with only the variables it needs, not `...process.env`. Limit its tools with `--allowedTools`/`--disallowedTools`, or run it in a sandbox. Add a fixed instruction that marks the 'Last failure' section as data, not instructions.

review.impact: The checks run in the worktree that the agent has just changed, so the agent controls the `Makefile` and the test files that decide the result. A builder can change the `test` target to `true` and get a green result. The only guard is one line in the prompt. The loop's 'its own run is the verdict' guarantee does not hold.
review.fix: Before the checks run, compare check-definition files such as `Makefile`, `package.json` scripts and the CI config against `base`, and mark the pass red when they changed. Another option: run the check commands from a copy of those files at `base`.

review.impact: `saveFailure` writes the whole check output, stdout and stderr together, to `.werk/runs/<run>/check-<pass>.txt` next to the decision log. Check output can contain secrets, for example environment dumps or tokens in failing HTTP fixtures. Nothing in the change keeps `.werk/runs/` out of git, so these files can be committed together with the tracked `.werk` logs.
review.fix: Add `.werk/runs/` to the ignore rules that werk creates (or write a `.gitignore` inside `runsDir` on first use). Create the files with mode 0600.

review.impact: `spawnWithLimit` reads all of the child's stdout and stderr into memory as strings, with no size limit. A check can print in a loop, for example a test runner in watch mode or a runaway log. That check can produce gigabytes before the 10-minute `--check-timeout` stops it. The `werk` process then holds all of that output in memory and can run out of memory. Then `saveFailure` writes the whole string to disk, and `cutFailure` keeps only the last 4,000 characters of it.
review.fix: Read the output as a stream. Write each chunk directly to the `check-<pass>.txt` file, or cap the bytes kept in memory. Keep only a tail buffer, for example the last 64 KB, for `cutFailure`. Optionally stop the process group when the output passes a byte limit.

review.impact: The adjacency map copies the whole list for each edge (`[...(needs.get(e.from) ?? []), e.to]`). The work is O(k²) for a node with k `depends_on` edges. `queue.shift()` is also O(n) for each call. Each build calls this function one time on a small map, so the real cost is small.
review.fix: Push onto the existing array: `const list = needs.get(e.from); if (list) list.push(e.to); else needs.set(e.from, [e.to])`. Iterate the queue with an index instead of `shift()`.

review.impact: `agentUsage` calls `JSON.parse` on every line of the agent's stream-json output. A 30-minute `--verbose` session can produce many megabytes of output, but the function needs only the last `result` event. The function parses all the other lines for nothing.
review.fix: Scan the lines from the end and return at the first line that parses as a `result` event. Or skip a line unless it contains `"type":"result"` before you parse it.

review.impact: `toGraph` gives `marks` a default of an empty map. Only a test calls `toGraph` without marks now. A later caller that uses `toGraph(fold(log))`, which was the old pattern in `server.ts`, gets a graph that says no card is marked, and it shows no error. The type does not stop the old call pattern from dropping the marks.
review.fix: Make `marks` a required parameter of `toGraph`, or stop exporting `toGraph` and use `graphOf` as the one public entry point. Change the test to call `toGraph(state, new Map())` or `graphOf`.

review.impact: The stale colour `#b3261e` and the paused colour `#757575` each appear twice: once in `.mark[data-mark=...]` and once in `.marks` / `.marks[data-mark='stale']`. A change to one mark colour must also change the second copy, or the tile badge and the card-page panel show different colours.
review.fix: Define the two colours one time as custom properties, for example `--mark-stale: #b3261e; --mark-paused: #757575;` on `:root`. Use `var(--mark-stale)` and `var(--mark-paused)` in the four rules.

review.impact: The test title says the rejected reopen marks 'only the next hop'. The fixture has no card two hops below `log`: `fold` has no children, and nothing depends on `tests`. The `werk` and `map` assertions check a parent and a sibling, not a card two hops down. If a regression carried a stale mark past one hop, this e2e test would still pass. Only the unit test in `src/map/graph.test.ts` (`Object.keys(graph.marks)` equals `['b']`) covers that case.
review.fix: Add a card two hops below `log`, for example `werk.cli(['link', 'map', 'tests', '--type', 'depends_on'])`, and assert `${card('map')} > a .mark` has count 0. Or rename the test so that it does not claim the next-hop limit.

review.impact: No test renders a trace with reason `amended`. The `changeText` branch that writes 'was amended in a review' has no test. The `.clears` sentence also has no test for either mark kind. A wrong text in either place passes all tests.
review.fix: Add an e2e case: a review with outcome amend on `log`, then open `#tests` and assert the trace contains 'was amended in a review'. In the existing stale and paused card-view tests, also assert the `.clears` text.

review.impact: The sub-cards tree on a card page now gets `marks={graph.marks}`, but no test opens a card page and checks a mark on a sub-card tile. If the `marks` prop is dropped from this `Tree` call or from the nested recursive call, no test fails.
review.fix: In the paused card-view test, open `#log` (its sub-card `fold` is paused) and assert that `getByRole('list', { name: 'sub-cards' })` contains `${card('fold')} > a .mark` with the text 'paused'.

review.impact: `/api/graph` runs on every SSE `changed` event. With this change, each request also runs `deriveMarks`. In `deriveMarks`, `below()` scans all of `state.edges` for each hop. A postponed reopen walks every reachable card, so its cost is O(V·E). The total cost is O(changes·V·E) per request. `add()` also copies the trace array on each append. The cost is small for the current map sizes, but it grows quadratically as the log grows, and it runs on every redraw.
review.fix: In `deriveMarks`, build a `Map<to, Edge[]>` of carrying edges one time before the change loop, and use it in `below()`. In `add()`, push into the existing array. Do not spread it into a new array.

review.impact: `chatTurn` and `noteFromAgent` are async, and the router calls them with `void`. Nothing catches a rejection. `readJson` iterates `req`, and that iteration throws when a client aborts the upload. A large screenshot paste makes an abort more likely. The rejection is then unhandled, and in Bun an unhandled rejection can stop the whole `werk serve` process, with the map, the lock and every chat child.
review.fix: Add `.catch((err) => { if (!res.headersSent) send(res, 500, 'text/plain', `werk: ${err.message}`); else res.destroy() })` to both route calls. Another option is to put a try/catch around `readJson` inside each handler.

review.impact: `ChatPane` opens its own `EventSource('/api/events')`. Each `useLive` instance also opens one, so the page now holds two or more server-sent event (SSE) streams to the same channel. Under HTTP/1.1 a browser allows 6 connections per origin. A few werk tabs use all 6, and then fetches and POSTs (for example `/api/chat`) queue without an end. Each new subscriber also adds another place that parses the event channel.
review.fix: Open the `/api/events` EventSource one time, in a shared hook or context at the `App` level. Let `useLive` subscribe to `changed` and `ChatPane` subscribe to `chat` through it.

review.impact: A tab's child can exit after a crash or a non-zero code. The next `send` then starts a new child with no history. The agent silently loses the conversation context, and the pane shows no sign of it. The only record is a line on the server's stderr.
review.fix: Push a `chat` message for the tab when the child exits, for example a synthetic `{ type: 'result', is_error: true, result: 'the agent exited with code N' }`. Then `received` closes the open reply and tells the person.

review.impact: The `agentTurns` reader (the `.turns.jsonl` path convention, plus the split, filter and parse steps) is copied into `e2e/harness.ts` and `src/test/harness.ts`. `fake-agent.ts` owns the file name. If that file name changes, two copies can drift.
review.fix: Export `turnsPath(scriptPath)` and `readTurns(scriptPath)` from `src/test/fake-agent.ts` or a small shared module, and use them in both harnesses.

review.impact: `noteFromAgent` copies the steps of `acceptFromView`: the local `reply` helper, the 405 check, and the `decodeURIComponent` try/catch that returns 400. `chatTurn` also copies the same-origin check of `acceptFromView` (`origin !== undefined && origin !== \`http://${req.headers.host}\``). There are now three route handlers with this boilerplate. A fix to the origin rule or to id decoding must go into each copy, and one copy can be missed.
review.fix: Move the shared steps into small helpers, for example `isMapPage(req)`, `decodeId(rawId)` and one `replyText(res)` factory. Call them from `acceptFromView`, `chatTurn` and `noteFromAgent`.

review.impact: The `agentTurns` reader in `e2e/harness.ts` is a copy of `agentTurns` in `src/test/harness.ts`. Both copies build the `${scriptPath}.turns.jsonl` path, check `existsSync`, split the lines and parse them. `src/test/fake-agent.ts` also builds the `.turns.jsonl` suffix itself, so the file-name rule is in three places. If the file name or format changes, the two readers can go out of step.
review.fix: Export one `turnsPathOf(scriptPath)` and one `readAgentTurns(scriptPath)` from `src/test/fake-agent.ts`, or from a small shared module. `e2e/harness.ts` already imports from that module. Use these functions in both harnesses and in the fake agent.

review.impact: `ChatPane` opens its own `EventSource('/api/events')`, and `useLive` opens another one in the same page (`App` calls `useLive`). The page then has two server-sent-event connections to the same channel, and the subscribe and parse code exists in two places.
review.fix: Open one shared `EventSource` for the app, for example in a context or a module-level hook. Let `useLive` listen for `changed` and `ChatPane` listen for `chat` on that one connection.

review.impact: Three test files define the same `delta(text)` helper that builds a stream_event text_delta message: `src/cli/serve.test.ts`, `src/chat/transcript.test.ts` and `e2e/chat.spec.ts`. The e2e copy also wraps it in `{ event: ... }`. If the message shape changes, three copies need the same edit.
review.fix: Export one `textDelta(text)` builder from a test helper module, for example `src/test/fake-agent.ts`. Import it in the three test files.

review.impact: The module doc says a child 'starts again at the next turn if it exits'. No test covers this. If the `children.get(tab) === child` delete breaks, a dead child stays in the map. Every later turn on that tab then writes to a closed stdin, and the chat stops working with no test failure.
review.fix: Add a serve.test.ts case. Script the chat role with a reply that has `exit: 1`, or one that ends the process. Send a turn, wait for the exit, and send a second turn. Assert `p.agentLaunches()` has length 2 and that the second turn gets its reply on the event channel.

review.impact: No test covers the failure path of `submit`. The pane clears the draft and images before the POST. If the server refuses the turn (400/403/500), the only feedback is the `role=alert` error. A regression that drops this alert leaves the person with a lost message and no signal, and every test still passes.
review.fix: Add an e2e test. Use `page.route('**/api/chat', r => r.fulfill({ status: 500, body: 'werk: boom' }))`, send a message, and assert that `getByRole('alert')` has the text 'werk: boom'.

review.impact: `expect.arrayContaining([...'--output-format', '--include-partial-messages'])` checks only that each flag appears somewhere. It does not check that `--output-format` is followed by `stream-json`. It does not check `--verbose` either, and the claude CLI needs `--verbose` for stream-json output in `-p` mode. If someone removes `--verbose` or changes the output format value, the test still passes.
review.fix: Assert the flag pairs by position, for example `argv[argv.indexOf('--output-format') + 1] === 'stream-json'`. Add '--verbose' to the expected list.

review.impact: No test covers the 413 branch of `readJson`, which caps the body size. No test covers the `copied: false` response of the note route either. A regression in the size cap or in the no-clipboard path goes unseen.
review.fix: Add a serve test that POSTs a body larger than MAX_BODY_BYTES to /api/chat and expects 413. Add a note-route test with a failing `pbcopy` stub on PATH (`exit 1`), and stub `wl-copy` and `xclip` the same way. Expect `copied: false` and the note still in the log.

review.impact: The streaming test depends on 700 ms sleeps between deltas. `toContainText('The fold')` followed by `not.toContainText('reads')` can fail on a slow CI runner. This happens when the first assertion resolves after the second delta has already arrived, so the test is flaky.
review.fix: Make the gaps longer (for example 2000 ms). A better fix is to gate each delta on a file or a turn signal that the test controls.

review.impact: The chat route compares Origin only with the Host header from the same request. A DNS-rebinding page sends a matching pair: Origin `http://evil.example:4000` and Host `evil.example:4000`. That page passes the check and can POST turns to the chat agent. The agent runs Edit, Write, `Bash(node:*)`, `Bash(python:*)` and `Bash(curl:*)` with no permission prompt. So any website the person visits can run code on their machine and send data out. The same page can also read the agent replies from `/api/events`. The `accept` route uses the same check, but before this change it could only append an accept event. Now the same check controls code execution.
review.fix: Check the Host header against an allowlist of loopback names on the bound port: `127.0.0.1:<port>`, `localhost:<port>` and `[::1]:<port>`, plus the configured `--host`. Do this before every `/api/*` route, `/api/events` included. Then require Origin to be absent or equal to `http://<that allowed host>`. Add a test that sends Host `evil.invalid:<port>` with a matching Origin and expects 403.

review.impact: `tab` can be any non-empty string with no length or count limit. `conversations.send` starts a new long-lived `claude` child for each new tab and keeps it. A buggy page, or any local process (no Origin header), can start an unlimited number of agent processes. This uses up process slots, memory and API quota.
review.fix: Limit `tab` to a short pattern, for example `/^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$/`. Also set a maximum number of live children in `startConversations` and refuse a new tab with 429 when it is full.

review.impact: The tool allowlist contains `Bash(node:*)`, `Bash(bun:*)` and `Bash(python:*)`. Each of these can run any code, so in practice the agent runs any command. The allowlist also contains WebFetch, WebSearch and `Bash(curl:*)`. Text in a fetched page can therefore tell the agent to run code or send project files out, with no prompt to the person.
review.fix: If #werk-pane requires this tool set, add a comment that states the risk. Otherwise remove the general interpreters, or remove WebFetch/WebSearch from the same agent, so that untrusted web content cannot reach a tool that runs code without a prompt.

review.impact: `WERK_COMMAND` quotes the bun path and the main.ts path with `JSON.stringify`, which makes double-quoted shell strings. Inside double quotes the shell still expands `$`, backticks and `\`. A path that contains one of these characters breaks the command that the agent types. Such a path could also run a command substitution.
review.fix: Quote each path for POSIX sh with single quotes, for example `'${p.replaceAll("'", "'\\''")}'`, and do not use JSON.stringify.

review.impact: Each new `tab` string in a POST /api/chat starts a new long-lived `claude` child, and nothing stops a child while the server runs. The client only ever sends 'main'. The server still accepts any non-empty tab name, so a local process or a buggy client can start an unbounded number of agent processes, each using memory and API usage.
review.fix: Accept only known tab names, or set a limit on the number of children. Above the limit, refuse the turn with 429, or stop the least recently used child.

review.impact: `received` returns a new array copy for every message it ignores (lines 26 and 29): assistant, system, tool and input_json_delta events. With `--include-partial-messages` there are many such events, and each one gives `setTranscript` a new reference. ChatPane then renders the whole conversation list again for no change.
review.fix: Return the same `transcript` reference when the message adds nothing. Change the return type to `readonly Entry[]` so React skips the update.

review.impact: `push` calls `JSON.stringify(data)` once for each connected client. The page opens three EventSources (graph, board and chat), and every streamed token goes through `push`. The same chat message is serialized again for every client.
review.fix: Build the frame string one time before the loop, then write that string to each client.

review.impact: `copyToClipboard` uses `Bun.spawnSync` and can try up to three commands in sequence. This blocks the server event loop while it runs, so SSE streaming of chat tokens and other requests stop during the copy.
review.fix: Use async `Bun.spawn` and await `exited`, or send the response first and copy after it.

causeOfLast.why: pass 1 reused the name of a file-level fixture inside one test, and the repo's lint rules forbid that clearly enough to get it right.

grade.gap: This is not a contradiction. Sign 3 of the card says that a tool call with no timeout must not hold the session forever. In src/build/headless.ts (armSilence), the overseer re-arms the silence timer with no limit while a tool call is in flight. Only the 30-minute agent timeout stops a tool call that never returns. The comment says 'it waits one more limit', but the code waits for an unlimited number of limits. A later ticket can add a cap for a tool call in flight.

review.impact: Bun's `FileSink.flush()` can return a Promise. If the agent exits before a write finishes, that Promise rejects outside the try/catch. The result is an unhandled rejection, and `stdinOpen` stays true. The overseer then can send a warning or a permission answer into a closed pipe and never learn that the send failed.
review.fix: Handle the async result: `void Promise.resolve(child.stdin.flush()).catch(() => { stdinOpen = false })`. Or make `send` async and await the flush inside the try.

review.impact: `setInterval(() => void classify(), ...)` drops every error from `classify`. Suppose `spawnWithLimit` throws, for example on a spawn failure or EAGAIN. Then the result is an unhandled rejection, and `classifying` stays true for good, so the loop check stops for the rest of the pass and no record shows it.
review.fix: Put the classifier run in try/finally so that `classifying = false` always runs. Catch the error and treat it as 'no loop seen', or record it as an overseer act.

review.impact: `runHeadless` no longer uses `spawnWithLimit` for the builder. It copies the process-group kill, the time limit and the timing logic from spawn.ts. Two copies of the kill and limit rules can drift apart.
review.fix: Export one shared helper from spawn.ts, for example `killGroup(child)`, or add a streaming option to spawn.ts. Then headless.ts uses that helper and does not keep its own copy.

review.impact: `loop.ts` finds the cancel reason from the `overseer` acts with a type-guard `find`, but `AgentRun.cancelled` already holds the same fact. `cancelNote` takes the whole act but reads only `reason`. Two sources hold the same state, so they can disagree.
review.fix: Change `cancelNote` to take `(reason: 'silence' | 'loop', limits)`. In loop.ts, use `agent.cancelled`. Remove the `Extract<OverseerAct, ...>` guard and the `OverseerAct` import.

review.impact: The literal union `'silence' | 'loop'` appears in four places: `AgentRun.cancelled`, the `cancel` parameter, `OverseerAct`, and `PassLine.agentCancelled`. A new reason needs an edit in each place.
review.fix: Export `type CancelReason = 'silence' | 'loop'` from overseer.ts and use it in all four places.

review.impact: `runHeadless` grew from 8 lines to about 150 lines. One function body now holds the process, the stdin writer, the line reader, three timers, the classifier scheduler and the cancel state machine. About 10 closures share 9 mutable `let` variables (`stdinOpen`, `inFlight`, `ended`, `timedOut`, `cancelled`, `silence`, `classifying`, `warned`, plus `acts` and `events`). Ordering bugs between these flags are hard to see in review. No unit test can reach the timer logic, because it is all local to the function.
review.fix: Move the overseer state machine into a small class or factory, for example `createOverseer(limits, send, stop)`. Give it `onEvent(event)`, `tick()` and `dispose()`, and let it own `acts`, `events`, `inFlight`, `warned`, `classifying`, `cancelled` and the timers. Keep only the spawn, the stdin and stdout code, and the result assembly in `runHeadless`. A fake clock can then test the timer logic directly.

review.impact: The process-group kill (`process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGKILL')` with the `child.kill` fallback) is now copied in `headless.ts` and in `spawn.ts:35`. The timeout-and-stop pattern around it is copied too. A later fix to one copy, for example a SIGTERM grace period or ESRCH handling, will miss the other copy.
review.fix: Export one `killGroup(child)` helper from `spawn.ts`, and call it from both `spawnWithLimit` and `runHeadless`.

review.impact: The literal union `'silence' | 'loop'` is written four times: `AgentRun.cancelled`, the `cancel` parameter in `headless.ts:83`, `PassLine.agentCancelled` in `run-record.ts:21`, and `OverseerAct` in `overseer.ts:22`. A new cancel reason needs four edits, and the compiler does not catch a missed edit in the run-record type.
review.fix: Export `type CancelReason = 'silence' | 'loop'` from `overseer.ts`. Use it in all four places.

review.impact: `loop.ts` finds the cancel reason a second time. It searches `agent.overseer` for the `cancelled` act with a type-guard cast, but `agent.cancelled` already holds the same value. `cancelNote` takes the whole act but reads only `reason`. The code also calls `cancelNote` twice with the same arguments (lines 118 and 131). Two sources of truth can drift apart.
review.fix: Change `cancelNote` to take `(reason: CancelReason, limits)`. In `loop.ts`, compute `const note = agent.cancelled ? cancelNote(agent.cancelled, o.overseer) : undefined` one time. Use `note` for both `agentNote` and `failure`, and delete the `Extract<OverseerAct, ...>` search.

review.impact: `CLASSIFIER_EVENTS` is exported, but no other module imports it. `EVENT_LIMIT` is the matching limit, and it is not exported. The export adds public interface with no user.
review.fix: Remove `export` from `CLASSIFIER_EVENTS`, so that it matches `EVENT_LIMIT`.

review.impact: The pure functions `isLooping`, `classifierAnswer`, `permissionAsk`, `toolsInFlight` and `classifierPrompt` have no unit tests. The CLI tests check them only through one happy path each, so a regression in a rule goes undetected. Examples: `isLooping` matches 'not looping' or '**Looping**'; `classifierAnswer` takes the wrong result; `toolsInFlight` keeps an id after its tool_result arrives in a block of mixed content; `permissionAsk` accepts a subtype that is not `can_use_tool`; `classifierPrompt` does not cut long events or keep only the last 40.
review.fix: Add `src/build/overseer.test.ts` with table tests. Test `isLooping` on 'looping', '`looping`', 'Looping.', 'progressing', 'not looping', '' and undefined. Test `classifierAnswer` on a stream with no result line, a bad JSON line, and two result lines. Test `toolsInFlight` on add, delete, a null event, and an event with no content. Test `permissionAsk` on a wrong subtype, a missing request_id, and a missing tool_name. Test `classifierPrompt` with more than 40 events and one event longer than 600 characters.

review.impact: No test covers a classifier that fails: a non-zero exit, no result event, a classifier timeout (`--classifier-timeout`), or a classifier still running when the builder exits. The code must treat each case as 'not looping' and abort the classifier through the new `signal` in spawn.ts. A change that cancels on a classifier error, or that leaves a classifier process alive, passes all tests.
review.fix: Add a CLI test where the 'loop-classifier' role exits 1 with no result, and one where it sleeps past `--classifier-timeout 100`. Assert that the builder goes green with `overseer: []` and `agentCancelled: null`. Add a spawn.ts test that aborts the signal and asserts that the process stops before its timeout.

review.impact: The fake agent exits 66 when an ask is not allowed, but no test exercises this path. The permission test asserts the exact allow `control_response`, so a deny reaches the test only through the stdin assertion. It does not reach it through the pass result.
review.fix: Keep the exact-response assertion. Optionally add a unit test of `allowAnswer` that checks `behavior: 'allow'` and the unchanged `updatedInput`, so the shape is tested without the timing of a subprocess.

review.impact: The silence and loop tests depend on wall-clock timing: a 1500 ms silence limit, a 150 ms loop tick, and an assert of under 8000 ms for the whole build. These tests have no per-test timeout, unlike the in-flight test, which sets 15_000. On a loaded CI machine the tests can flake. The fake agent can start more slowly than the limit, or the elapsed check can fail.
review.fix: Give the silence and loop tests an explicit per-test timeout, the same as the in-flight test. Add margin to the elapsed-time assertion, or assert on the record fields alone (`agentCancelled`, `agentExit: null`) and drop the elapsed-time assertion.

review.impact: The loop classifier is a full `claude -p` agent with no tool limit. It runs in the worktree and gets the default tool set. Its prompt contains raw builder events, and these include tool results from repository files, command output and fetched web content. That content is untrusted. Text placed in that content can tell the classifier to run Read, Grep or other allowed tools, or to answer `progressing`. A `progressing` answer defeats loop detection. Nothing in the prompt marks the events as data.
review.fix: Start the classifier with no tools and one turn, for example `--tools ''` (or `--disallowedTools` for every tool) and `--max-turns 1`. In `classifierPrompt`, put the events inside a clear delimiter, such as a fenced block. Add a rule that the text in the events is data, and that the classifier must not follow instructions in it.

review.impact: `classifierPrompt(events)` goes on the argv of the classifier process. The events hold up to 40 × 600 characters of tool input and output.
