That text can include secrets the builder read, such as `.env` values, tokens printed by a command, or credentials in config files. On a shared machine, other local users can read argv with `ps`. The builder prompt moved to stdin in this change, but the classifier prompt still goes on argv.
review.fix: Send the classifier prompt on stdin, the same way as the builder: `--input-format stream-json` and one user message. Or pipe plain text on stdin to `claude -p`. Keep stream content off the command line.

review.impact: `allowAnswer` approves every `can_use_tool` ask and returns the input unchanged. Under `bypassPermissions`, an ask that still comes through is usually a protected operation, such as a write outside the worktree or to `.git`/`.claude`. The comment gives the worktree as the reason this is safe. But the overseer never checks that the ask stays inside the worktree. A builder that has been steered by prompt injection gets every escalation approved without a check.
review.fix: Keep allow as the default, but check the ask first. Deny it, or cancel the pass, when the `file_path`/`path`/`notebook_path` input resolves outside `options.cwd`. Also log the denied input in the run record so that a person can review it.

review.impact: The `events` array keeps every parsed event of the session, but the classifier reads only the last `CLASSIFIER_EVENTS` (40). A 30-minute pass with large tool results (file reads, test output) keeps all of those parsed objects in memory, and the `text` string also holds the same data. Memory grows with the length of the session and gives no benefit.
review.fix: Keep a bounded window. After `events.push(event)`, run `if (events.length > CLASSIFIER_EVENTS) events.splice(0, events.length - CLASSIFIER_EVENTS)`, or use a ring buffer. Track 'at least one event seen' with a boolean for the `events.length === 0` guard in `classify`.

review.impact: `(rest + part).split('\n')` scans and copies the whole buffered tail again for each chunk. One long JSON line that spans many chunks, for example a big tool result, costs O(n²) in the line length.
review.fix: Look for '\n' only in the new `part`. If `part` has no newline, append it to `rest` (or push it to an array of pieces) and continue. Split only when a newline arrives.

review.impact: `classifierPrompt` runs `JSON.stringify` on each recent event in full, then cuts the result to 600 characters. Large tool-result events are serialized completely only to throw most of the text away. This happens on each classifier tick.
review.fix: Keep the raw stdout line next to each event in the bounded window, and cut that line. Then the prompt needs no second serialization.

causeOfLast.why: pass 1 wrote two lines that the project's existing oxlint rules reject, and the ticket had no part in that.

grade.gap: Not built yet, which passes: the count of MEDIUM and LOW findings per ticket for the trend report. src/build/run-record.ts records the findings, so a later ticket can count them.
Not built yet, which passes: the trend report itself. The run record keeps the judge cost and the findings for each pass.
Not built yet, which passes: the held-out section. The fixed review areas live in REVIEW_AREAS in src/build/judge.ts, so they are built into the tool.

review.impact: The `JudgeRun` type keeps only `reply`, `costUsd` and `ms`. `runHeadless` also returns `timedOut`, `code` and `stderr`, but these are dropped. When a judge agent times out, crashes, or exits non-zero, it gives `reply: null`. The next builder pass then gets the failure 'the grader gave no readable JSON object…'. The builder cannot fix this. It uses a retry on an infrastructure fault, and the run record does not say why the judge failed.
review.fix: Add `timedOut` and `code` (or the full `AgentRun`) to the `JudgeRun` result. In `judgePass`, report a judge that timed out or exited non-zero as its own problem, for example 'the grader was stopped at its time limit' or 'the grader exited 1'. Write those fields to the `grade`/`review` fields of the `PassLine`. Then the failure text and the run record show the true cause.

review.impact: `green = red === undefined && judgement!.pass` and the later `judgement!.stage` / `judgement!.failure` depend on the reader knowing that `judgement` is defined exactly when `red` is undefined. The type system does not enforce this link. A later edit to the `red ? undefined : …` expression can make these lines throw at runtime.
review.fix: Compute one discriminated verdict, for example `const verdict = red ? { kind: 'checks', red } : { kind: 'judge', judgement: await judgePass(...) }`. Then branch on `verdict.kind` so that TypeScript narrows the type without non-null assertions.

review.impact: The prefix `'agent-script.json.launches.'` duplicates the file name of `scriptPath` and the suffix scheme of `fake-agent.ts` in a literal. If one of them changes, the reset in `scriptAgent` stops deleting the per-role launch counters without an error. Later tests then replay the wrong reply.
review.fix: Derive the prefix from `scriptPath`, for example `basename(scriptPath) + '.launches.'`. Better: export one helper from `fake-agent.ts` that builds the counter path, and use it in both files.

review.impact: The loop uses three non-null assertions on `judgement` (lines 104, 132, 133). The type of `judgement` does not show that it is defined when `red` is undefined. Only the order of the branches guarantees it. A later edit to the branches can cause a runtime TypeError that the type checker does not catch.
review.fix: Make one discriminated value per pass, for example `const verdict = red ? { kind: 'checks', red } : { kind: 'judge', judgement: await judgePass(...) }`, and narrow on `verdict.kind`. Then `green`, the log line and `failure` need no `!`.

review.impact: The harness hardcodes the prefix 'agent-script.json.launches.'. The fake agent builds the same prefix from `${scriptPath}.launches.${name}` in src/test/fake-agent.ts. If someone renames the script file or changes the count-file scheme in one place only, old counts stay between scripts, and the role replies become wrong without any error.
review.fix: Build the prefix from `scriptPath` (`basename(scriptPath) + '.launches.'`), or export one helper that both files use to make the count-file path.

review.impact: `readGrade` and `readFindings` repeat the same steps: get the reply object, check that a named key is an array, then return a 'gave no readable JSON object with a "<key>" array' problem. Each parser also casts every entry to its own ad hoc shape. The two copies can drift apart.
review.fix: Extract a helper such as `replyArray(reply, key): unknown[] | undefined`, and call it from both parsers.

review.impact: `judgementFields` copies `j.grade` field by field into an object of the same shape (`{ pass, lines, problems }`). This copy adds code that has no effect. A new field in `Grade` must also be added here by hand.
review.fix: Use `grade: j.grade` directly. `Grade` already matches the `PassLine['grade']` type.

review.impact: `launchedRoles` is a 13-line loop with manual index handling. It sorts each consecutive group of reviewer roles so that concurrent launches compare in a fixed order. The intent is hard to read, and the helper is easy to break.
review.fix: Assert the sequential roles and the reviewer set separately, for example with `expect(roles.filter(r => !r.startsWith('reviewer-'))).toEqual([...])` and `expect(roles.filter(r => r.startsWith('reviewer-')).toSorted()).toEqual(REVIEWERS.toSorted())`. Or keep the grouping, but use a simpler stable sort keyed on the index of the group.

review.impact: No test checks the argv that the judges get. The grader and the reviewers must run with `--allowedTools` and the read tools only. If a later change drops `readOnly: true` in `loop.ts`, or makes `runHeadless` send `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` again, all tests still pass. Then the judges can edit the worktree after the checks have run.
review.fix: Add an assertion to `src/cli/build.test.ts`. Use `p.agentLaunches()` with `p.agentRoles()`. Check that each grader and reviewer argv holds `--allowedTools` followed by `READ_TOOLS`, and does not hold `bypassPermissions`. Check that the builder argv still holds `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`.

review.impact: No test calls `gradeFailure` on a grade that has problems, such as a missing score or an unreadable reply. The tests check `readGrade().problems` only. If the problem lines drop out of the failure text, no test fails, and the next builder pass gets no reason for the red grade.
review.fix: In `judge.test.ts`, call `gradeFailure(readGrade('I could not grade', lines))`. Assert that the result holds 'no readable JSON'. Also check a grade with a missing line in the `judgePass` grader-fail test.

review.impact: Two edge cases of the parser have no test. The first is a `###` subheading inside the Acceptance criteria section: the loop does not stop there, so the bullets under it become criteria. The second is a grader entry with a duplicate id: the first entry wins. A change to either rule passes the tests.
review.fix: Add one case with a `### Sub` heading and its bullets to the `acceptanceCriteria` test, and assert the result that you want. Add one `readGrade` case with two entries for `ac-1`, one with score 2 and one with score 4, and assert which entry counts.

review.impact: The judge is not read-only. It runs in the builder's worktree, so it loads the project settings (`.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json`), the hooks, and `CLAUDE.md` from that worktree. The builder agent runs with `bypassPermissions` and can write those files. Then the builder can give the judge more tools, run hooks inside the judge session, or tell the grader and the reviewers to pass every line. `--allowedTools` only adds approvals. It does not remove permissions that the project settings give.
review.fix: Start the judge with `--setting-sources user` (or an explicit `--settings` file), and with `--disallowedTools Edit,Write,NotebookEdit` and `--permission-mode default`, so the worktree cannot change the judge's permissions. Alternatively, run the judge in a clean checkout of HEAD that has no `.claude/` folder and no `CLAUDE.md` from the build. As a minimum, fail the pass when the diff touches `.claude/` or `CLAUDE.md`.

review.impact: The prefixes `Bash(git diff:*)`, `Bash(git log:*)` and `Bash(git show:*)` also approve write flags. Examples: `git diff --output=<path>`, `git log --output=<path>`, and `git diff --ext-diff`, which runs a diff driver from the worktree's git config or `.gitattributes`. The builder controls both files. So the 'read-only' judge can write files or run programs, and the builder can plant a diff driver that rewrites the result.
review.fix: Give the judge no Bash tool, because the prompt already holds the diff. If the judge must read more of the diff, run git in werk with fixed arguments (`--no-ext-diff --no-textconv`). Alternatively, add a `--disallowedTools` list that blocks `--output`, `--ext-diff` and `--textconv`.

review.impact: The prompt puts the untrusted diff inside a ```diff fence. The diff can contain a line with ``` that closes the fence, and the text after it reads as prompt instructions (for example, a fake '## Reply' section). This makes it easier for the builder to inject instructions into the grader and the reviewers.
review.fix: Use a fence that is longer than the longest run of backticks in the diff, or wrap the diff in a unique delimiter with a random nonce. Tell the judge that all text inside the delimiter is data, not instructions.

review.impact: Each judge prompt can hold up to 200,000 characters of diff, plus the brief and the cards. `runHeadless` passes the prompt as one argv string (`-p <prompt>`, src/build/headless.ts:25). On Linux, one argv string can be at most 128 KiB (MAX_ARG_STRLEN), so a diff over about 128 KB makes the spawn of all six judges fail with E2BIG. On macOS, the total argv and env limit is about 1 MB. Each failed spawn fails the pass, so a large diff fails every pass until the retry cap. Each retry also runs a full builder pass and the checks again.
review.fix: Send the prompt on stdin, not as an argv string. If stdin is not possible, set DIFF_LIMIT below the per-argument limit, for example 100_000 bytes measured in UTF-8. Then the agent reads the rest with `git diff`.

review.impact: `diffSince` reads the whole `git diff base HEAD` into memory with `Bun.spawnSync` and converts it to a string. Then `cutDiff` keeps only the first 200,000 characters. A pass that commits a large generated file or a lockfile makes the process buffer the full diff, which can be many megabytes, on each green pass. Most of that output is then discarded.
review.fix: Limit the output at the source. For example, run `git diff` with `--stat` and send the patch only up to the limit, or stop reading the stream at DIFF_LIMIT bytes. Also consider excluding lockfiles and binary files, for example with `-- . ':!*.lock'` or `--no-binary`.

causeOfLast.why: the cards did not name DNS rebinding, but an earlier pass let an Origin-equals-Host check control a shell agent, and a correct build must not do that.

review.impact: The pane is not told when a chat child exits or crashes. The exit only goes to the server's stderr. If the child exits before it writes a `result` line, the open reply in the pane keeps `aria-busy=true` and never closes. The next turn starts a new child with no earlier context, and the person is not told.
review.fix: On exit, call `options.onMessage(tab, { type: 'result', is_error: true, result: `the agent exited with code ${code}` })`, or send a dedicated exit message. `received()` in transcript.ts then closes the reply and shows the failure.

review.impact: ChatPane opens a second `EventSource('/api/events')` next to the one that `useLive` opens. Each page now holds two SSE connections. Each `changed` and `chat` event goes out twice, and each consumer decodes only half of what it gets. Browsers allow about 6 HTTP/1.1 connections per host, and two tabs with two streams each use most of them. The event-channel logic is also now in two places.
review.fix: Move the EventSource into one shared hook or context, for example `useEvents(name, handler)`, that opens one connection per page. Then use it in both useLive and ChatPane.

review.impact: Chat children run in `process.cwd()`, but the rest of the server finds the project from `logPath`. If the server runs with a log outside the cwd (WERK_LOG, or a start from a subdirectory), the agent edits and runs werk in a different directory than the map it serves.
review.fix: Pass a project directory in `ServerOptions` from the serve verb. Derive it from `logPath` the same way the verb finds the lock. Use that directory as the conversations `cwd`.

review.impact: `copyToClipboard` uses `Bun.spawnSync` inside the HTTP handler. It can call up to three external commands one after the other. The whole server event loop blocks until they finish, so SSE heartbeats, chat streaming and other requests stall. A clipboard command that hangs, for example `xclip` with no display, blocks the server indefinitely.
review.fix: Make `copyToClipboard` async with `Bun.spawn`, add a short timeout, and await it in `noteFromAgent`.

review.impact: When `readJson` goes over `MAX_BODY_BYTES`, it returns 413 but does not consume or destroy the rest of the request body. The client keeps uploading into a response that has already ended, and the keep-alive connection is left in an unknown state.
review.fix: Call `req.destroy()` (or `req.resume()` with `Connection: close`) before the 413 return.

review.impact: The `${scriptPath}.turns.jsonl` naming rule and the parser for the turns file are copied in three places: src/test/fake-agent.ts, src/test/harness.ts and e2e/harness.ts. If one copy changes, tests read an empty list and fail in a way that is hard to trace.
review.fix: Put a side-effect-free helper module next to fake-agent, for example `turnsPathOf(scriptPath)` and `readAgentTurns(scriptPath)`. Import it in the fake agent and in both harnesses.

review.impact: The `agentTurns` reader is copied from `src/test/harness.ts:89`. Both copies check that the file exists, read it, split it on newlines, drop empty lines and parse each line as JSON. The `${scriptPath}.turns.jsonl` path rule is also written in three places: `src/test/fake-agent.ts:123`, `src/test/harness.ts:90` and `e2e/harness.ts:46`. If one place changes the file name or the line format, the other places keep working without an error and read nothing, so the tests can pass when they should fail.
review.fix: Put a `turnsPathOf(scriptPath)` function and a `readAgentTurns(scriptPath)` function in a small shared module with no side effects, for example `src/test/agent-turns.ts`. Use them from both harnesses and from fake-agent.ts. Do not export them from fake-agent.ts, because that file runs its script when another file imports it.

review.impact: `noteFromAgent` gets the card title out of the `appendRuled` callback by changing the outer variable `let title = ''`. The flow is hard to follow. The title is also `''` when the card does not exist, but in that case the route returns 409 before it uses the title, so the empty-string default is code that never runs.
review.fix: Read the title after a successful write, from the state that `appendRuled` returns or with one `readLog`/`graphOf` lookup. Alternatively, return the title from the callback together with the rule result. Then remove the outer `let`.

review.impact: ChatPane opens its own `EventSource('/api/events')`, and each `useLive` hook opens another one. The page now holds two or three SSE connections to the same channel, and each component has its own code to open and close a connection.
review.fix: Move the EventSource into one shared hook or context that lets a component subscribe to an event name, for example `useEvent('chat', handler)`. Use it in both `useLive` and ChatPane, so that the page opens the channel once.

review.impact: No test covers the documented restart behaviour: when a tab's child exits, the next turn must spawn a new child. If the `children.get(tab) === child` delete were removed or broken, `send` would write to a dead stdin and every later turn on that tab would be lost. Every test still passes in that case.
review.fix: Add a `serve.test.ts` case. Script the chat role as two replies, and make the first one exit with `{ steps: [...], exit: 0 }`. To make the fake agent end its stream-mode loop, add an `exit` step for stream mode or run `process.exit(reply.exit)` after a reply that has `exit` set. Post two turns. Assert that `agentLaunches()` has length 2 and that the second turn's events arrive.

review.impact: No test reaches the 413 size-cap path in `readJson`. A regression in the cap, such as an off-by-unit constant or the check removed, would let a page or process stream any amount of data into memory, and no test would fail.
review.fix: In `serve.test.ts`, POST a body larger than `MAX_BODY_BYTES` to `api/chat`. Assert status 413 and that `agentLaunches()` is empty. If a 32 MiB body is too slow for the test, export the cap or make it configurable.

review.impact: The streaming test depends on timing. `not.toContainText('reads')` and `not.toContainText('from the top.')` hold only during a 700 ms window between fake-agent sleeps. On a loaded CI machine, the next delta can arrive before the assertion runs, and the test fails at random. The pane also opens its `EventSource` on mount with no wait for `: connected`, so a first delta that arrives early is dropped.
review.fix: Wait until the event channel is connected before pressing Enter. Example: wait for the request to `/api/events` to get a response, or expose a ready marker. Replace the fixed sleeps with a gate the test controls, such as a step that waits for a file the test writes. Otherwise increase the sleeps and make the gap explicit, so the intermediate states are reliable.

review.impact: The Shift+Enter test reads `expect(sent).toBe(0)` at once, with no wait. A wrong submit sends its fetch asynchronously, so the request event can fire after the check, and the test passes even when Shift+Enter sends.
review.fix: Before the check, wait a short bounded time, for example `await page.waitForTimeout(300)`. A better way: press Enter after the check, wait for exactly one request, and assert that its text is 'one\ntwo'. This proves that Shift+Enter sent nothing and that the newline is kept.

review.impact: `expect.arrayContaining(['--input-format', 'stream-json', '--output-format', '--include-partial-messages'])` checks only set membership. It still passes when `--input-format` is not followed by `stream-json`, for example `--input-format text --output-format stream-json`. Then the child would not read stdin turns.
review.fix: Assert the value after each flag: `expect(argv[argv.indexOf('--input-format') + 1]).toBe('stream-json')`. Do the same for `--output-format`.

review.impact: The Host/Origin guard only stops browsers. A non-browser client sets its own Host header and sends no Origin. With `werk serve --host 0.0.0.0` (or a LAN address), any machine on the network can send `Host: 127.0.0.1:<port>` and POST /api/chat. That starts an agent with Bash(python:*), Bash(node:*), Bash(curl:*), Write and Edit, which is unauthenticated remote code execution in the project directory. The same caller can POST /api/note/<id> to write log events and set the user's clipboard. Before this change, a non-loopback bind exposed only the read API and accept.
review.fix: For /api/chat and /api/note, refuse a request when `req.socket.remoteAddress` is not a loopback address (127.0.0.0/8, ::1, ::ffff:127.0.0.1). Or turn off the chat and note routes when the bound host is not loopback, and print a warning at startup.

review.impact: Each new `tab` string spawns a new long-lived `claude` child. The server sets no limit on the number of tabs or children. A burst of requests with distinct tab names starts an unbounded number of agent processes, and each one costs API spend and memory.
review.fix: Validate `tab` against a short pattern such as /^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$/ in parseChatRequest. Cap the number of live children in startConversations, and refuse a new tab with 429 when the cap is reached.

review.impact: The allowlist reads as a restriction, but `Bash(python:*)`, `Bash(node:*)` and `Bash(bun:*)` each allow any shell action. `Bash(rm -f /tmp/:*)` is a prefix match, so `rm -f /tmp/../<path>` also passes. The agent also has WebFetch, WebSearch and curl, so a fetched page can inject a prompt that reads project files and sends them out with no confirmation from the person.
review.fix: Document in the comment that this set equals full shell access, so readers do not trust it as a sandbox. Or remove the interpreter and curl entries and let the agent ask for permission for them. Drop the `rm -f /tmp/` entry, because it gives no real limit.

review.impact: Each streamed text delta calls setTranscript, and the pane then re-renders every entry. Each agent entry re-parses its whole Markdown text. With --include-partial-messages, one reply sends hundreds of deltas. The cost of one delta grows with the full conversation length, so a long conversation costs quadratic work and the UI starts to lag. A graph refetch also gives a new hrefOf, which re-renders all entries again.
review.fix: Move one entry into a component that is wrapped in React.memo, for example `const ChatEntry = memo(...)`. Give it the stable props `entry` and `hrefOf`. `append` already keeps the object identity of closed entries, so only the open reply then re-renders on a delta.

review.impact: `received` returns a new array (`[...transcript]`) for every message that it ignores. Examples are tool-call `input_json_delta` pieces, whole assistant messages, tool results and system lines. The agent streams many of these during a tool call. Each new array identity makes React re-render the whole chat pane, and no visible change occurs.
review.fix: Return the input `transcript` unchanged when nothing changes. Change the return type to `readonly Entry[]`, or cast it. Then React's setState bail-out skips the render. Do the same in `closed()` when no entry is open.

review.impact: `readLines` adds each chunk to `rest` and then calls `rest.split('\n')` on the full buffer. One stream-json line can be several MB, for example a tool result with file contents. Such a line arrives in many 64 KB chunks, and each chunk rescans the whole partial line. The cost is quadratic in the line length.
review.fix: Look for '\n' only in the decoded new chunk. Keep the partial pieces in an array, and join them only when a newline arrives.

review.impact: Every agent message goes whole to every SSE client, after one JSON.stringify for each client write. This includes full assistant messages and large tool results. The client drops all of it except text deltas and results. Large tool outputs use bandwidth and parse time on each open page.
review.fix: Call JSON.stringify one time in `push`, outside the client loop. If the wire contract allows it, leave out message types that the pane ignores, such as `user` tool_result lines and whole `assistant` messages.

review.impact: `useLive('/api/graph')` now runs at the App level, so it also runs on the Board view. Each `changed` event then refetches and folds the whole map log, and nothing on that view needs it. ChatPane also opens a third EventSource to /api/events, in addition to the graph and board useLive channels. Each page then holds more of the browser's six HTTP/1.1 connections to the origin.
review.fix: Share one EventSource for each page, for example with a module-level channel or a context that the hooks subscribe to. The graph fetch can stay at the App level only while the map view is shown or the chat needs card links.

causeOfLast.why: werk/85 changed the fake agent's stream-json mode for the build overseer after this ticket changed the same mode for the chat child.

review.impact: The chat child can exit in the middle of a turn: a crash, a kill, or an auth or overload failure before it writes a `result`. When that happens, the pane never gets a closing message. The reply stays open with aria-busy=true. The person sees no error, because the exit code goes only to the server's stderr. `received()` in transcript.ts already handles a failed `result`, but nothing on this path sends one.
review.fix: In the `child.exited` handler, check whether the child got a turn that has no `result` yet. If so, call `options.onMessage(tab, { type: 'result', is_error: true, result: `the agent exited with code ${code}` })`. Track a per-child 'turn open' flag: set it in `send`, and clear it when an `onMessage` message has type 'result'.

review.impact: `send` writes to the stdin of the child in the map with no guard. A child can be dead while its `exited` promise has not resolved yet. In that case the write throws, which gives a 500, or the write is dropped and the server still answers 202. In both cases the turn is lost, and no new child starts. `runHeadless` in src/build/headless.ts already guards the same write with a `stdinOpen` flag and a try/catch.
review.fix: Follow headless.ts: keep a per-child 'stdin open' flag. Clear it when a write throws or when `exited` resolves. In `send`, if the current child cannot take the write, delete it from the map and spawn a new child before you write the line.

review.impact: `close()` sends SIGTERM to the `claude` process only. The pane's agent runs Bash tools (`bun`, `node`, `python`, `curl`). Those grandchildren can outlive `werk serve`. headless.ts spawns with `detached: true` and kills the process group with `process.kill(-pid)` for exactly this reason. The new module does not follow that existing pattern.
review.fix: Spawn the chat child with `detached: true`. In `close()`, call `process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGTERM')`, and fall back to `child.kill()` as headless.ts does. Better: move the spawn and kill code into a shared helper that both modules use.

review.impact: The server gets its project from `options.logPath`. The chat agents get theirs from `process.cwd()`. These two values are not tied together. A caller that starts the server for a log outside the current directory (a test, or a later `--dir` flag) gets agents that edit a different tree than the map shows.
review.fix: Add a `projectDir` field to `ServerOptions`, or derive the directory from `logPath`. Pass that value to `startConversations({ cwd })`, not `process.cwd()`.

review.impact: The page now opens two EventSource connections to `/api/events`: one in useLive and one in ChatPane. Browsers allow only about 6 HTTP/1.1 connections per origin. Two map tabs then use 4 of them. Every client also receives every chat message for every tab, and each of these large messages is broadcast twice per page.
review.fix: Share one EventSource for the page. For example, open it in App or in a small `useEvents` context, and let `useLive` and ChatPane add their listeners to it.

review.impact: `submit` adds the message to the transcript and clears the draft and the images before the POST. If the server refuses the turn (400, 403, 413, 500), the transcript still shows a message that the agent never got. The text and the pasted images are lost, and the person must type and paste them again.
review.fix: Keep the request, and restore `draft` and `images` when `res.ok` is false or fetch throws. Alternatively, add the entry with `sent()` only after a 202 response.

review.impact: `readLines` copies the line-splitting loop from `readStdout` in `src/build/headless.ts:146-160`: decode chunks, split on newline, keep the rest, skip blank lines, flush the last line. A fix to one copy, for example a multi-byte decode fix, does not reach the other copy.
review.fix: Move `readLines` to one shared module, for example `src/agent/lines.ts`. Use it from `conversations.ts` and from `headless.ts`. Keep the `armSilence()` call in the `onLine` callback in `headless.ts`.

review.impact: The `.turns.jsonl` file name is set in three places: `src/test/fake-agent.ts` writes it, and `src/test/harness.ts:99` and `e2e/harness.ts:85` read it. The two `agentTurns` readers repeat the same exists-then-parse-JSON-lines logic. If one place changes the suffix, the other harness reads an empty list and its tests fail with no clear cause.
review.fix: Export one helper from `src/test/fake-agent.ts` or `src/test/harness.ts`, for example `readAgentTurns(scriptPath): unknown[]`, that holds the suffix and the parse. Use it in the fake agent and in both harnesses.

review.impact: Three test files build the same stream-json `text_delta` message: `src/chat/transcript.test.ts:5`, `src/cli/serve.test.ts:293` and `e2e/chat.spec.ts:9`. The e2e copy also wraps it in a step. If the stream-json shape changes, all three copies need the same edit.
review.fix: Export a `textDelta(text)` builder from one test helper module, for example `src/test/fake-agent.ts`, next to `FakeScript`. Import it in the three test files. Wrap it as `{ event: textDelta(t) }` where a script step needs it.

review.impact: The module states that a tab's child starts again at the next turn after it exits. No test covers this. The fake chat child only exits when stdin closes, so no test can make a chat child exit early. If the `children.delete` path breaks, every later turn on that tab writes to a dead stdin, and no test fails. No test sends turns on two tabs either, so no test checks that each tab gets its own child.
review.fix: In src/test/fake-agent.ts, make a chat-role reply with a non-zero `exit` end the process after its steps. Then add a serve.test case: the first turn's reply exits 1, a second turn on the same tab is sent, and the test expects `agentLaunches()` to have length 2 and the second turn to get its reply. Add one case that posts to tabs 'a' and 'b' and expects two launches, with each event carrying the correct tab.

review.impact: No test checks the 413 path of `readJson` when a body is larger than MAX_BODY_BYTES. A regression could remove the size cap, or return 400 or 500 instead, and no test would fail.
review.fix: Export MAX_BODY_BYTES or make it an option, and add a serve.test case. The case posts a body that is one byte over the cap to /api/chat and expects status 413 and `agentLaunches()` to equal [].

review.impact: The note-route test only checks `copied: true` with a fake pbcopy. The path where no clipboard command works (`copied: false`, the note is still appended, status 200) has no test. A change that turns a missing clipboard into an error would pass the tests.
review.fix: Add a case where the first PATH entry has pbcopy, wl-copy and xclip scripts that all exit 1. Expect status 200, `copied: false`, and one note.said event in the log.

review.impact: `expect.arrayContaining` does not check the order of the items or which flag goes with which value. It passes when 'stream-json' follows only one of the two format flags, or when '--output-format' is followed by 'json'.
review.fix: Assert the pairs: expect(argv[argv.indexOf('--input-format') + 1]).toBe('stream-json') and expect(argv[argv.indexOf('--output-format') + 1]).toBe('stream-json'), and check that '--include-partial-messages' and '--verbose' are present.

review.impact: The test checks `expect(sent).toBe(0)` at once, with no wait. A request that Shift+Enter starts by mistake can come after the check, so the test can pass while the composer still sends.
review.fix: Before the count check, wait for a fixed signal. For example, wait until the conversation list has no 'you' entry with `await expect(page.getByRole('list', { name: 'conversation' }).locator('li')).toHaveCount(0)`, or wait with `page.waitForTimeout(300)`. Then assert sent === 0.

review.impact: The guard checks only the Host and Origin headers. It does not authenticate the caller. `werk serve --host 0.0.0.0` is supported, and `allowedHosts` and its test allow the 0.0.0.0 bind on purpose. With that bind, any machine on the network can send `POST /api/chat` with `Host: 127.0.0.1:<port>` and no Origin header. The request passes the guard and starts a claude child. That child runs `Bash(python:*)`, `Bash(node:*)`, `Bash(bun:*)`, `Bash(curl:*)`, `Write` and `Edit` with no permission prompt. The result is unauthenticated remote code execution as the user. `/api/note/<id>` and `/api/accept/<id>` are also open to log writes from the network.
review.fix: Refuse `/api/chat` and `/api/note` when `req.socket.remoteAddress` is not a loopback address. Alternatively, require a per-run secret token: the server generates it at start and gives it to the page and to the agent's environment. Another option is to refuse to start the chat when the bind host is not loopback. Add a test that sends a request with a forged loopback Host from a non-loopback socket and expects 403.

review.impact: The chat agent auto-approves `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`, `Bash(curl:*)`, `Bash(python:*)`, `Bash(node:*)` and `Bash(bun:*)`. Each `Bash(<interpreter>:*)` entry allows any code to run. Text from a fetched web page or a pasted screenshot can carry a prompt injection. That injection can then run code and send project files or secrets to a remote host, and no prompt stops it. The `Bash(rm -f /tmp/:*)` prefix also matches arguments such as `/tmp/ ../home/...`.
review.fix: Remove the interpreter wildcards and `curl` from the allowlist, or keep them and drop `WebFetch` and `WebSearch`, so that untrusted input and unprompted code execution never meet in one agent. If the design requires the interpreters, record the decision and the risk next to the list. Narrow or remove the `rm -f /tmp/` rule.

review.impact: `WERK_COMMAND` quotes the paths with `JSON.stringify`, and the agent then types the result in a shell. JSON quoting is not shell quoting. If the path of the werk checkout or the bun binary contains `$`, a backtick or `\`, the shell expands it, and the command runs the wrong thing or a command that the path contains.
review.fix: Quote each path for the shell with single quotes (replace each `'` with `'\''`), or refuse to start when a path contains shell metacharacters.

review.impact: `tab` accepts any non-empty string of any length, and each new tab value spawns a new long-lived claude child. A local caller, or the page after a bug, can start an unbounded number of agent processes. The tab value also goes unescaped into stderr log lines.
review.fix: Limit `tab` to a short pattern such as `/^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$/`, and cap the number of live children in `startConversations`.

review.impact: The server serializes every agent stdout line and writes it to every `/api/events` client. That includes each partial-message delta, the whole `assistant` messages, and the `user` tool_result messages, which can hold whole file contents. Each page holds two or three EventSource connections: one from `useLive` for the graph, one from `useLive` for the board, and one from `ChatPane`. Only `ChatPane` reads `chat`. So each large tool result goes to the browser two or three times per tab and is then dropped. Also, three of the six HTTP/1.1 connections per origin stay open.
review.fix: Push only what the pane draws: text deltas, `content_block_start` and `result`, or a trimmed message. Send them on a separate chat stream, or on one shared EventSource per page, so the `useLive` connections do not get the chat traffic.

review.impact: Each streamed token calls `setTranscript`. This renders the whole `<ol>` again and runs `<Markdown>` again on every entry, including old replies that are done. Nothing is memoized. The work for each delta grows with the length of the conversation, so a long chat gets slower in proportion to the square of its length while a reply streams.
review.fix: Move each entry into a `React.memo` component. `closed()` and `append()` keep the object references of unchanged entries, so the memo skips the Markdown parse of every entry except the open reply.

review.impact: `received` returns a new array copy for a message that changes nothing. Examples are `assistant`, `system`, tool_result and every `input_json_delta` of a tool call. So `setTranscript` gets a new reference each time and React renders the whole chat log again. A tool call with many input_json_delta events causes many renders that change nothing.
review.fix: Return `transcript` itself when nothing changes, at lines 26 and 29 and for a `content_block_start` with no open text, so React skips the update. Change the return type to `readonly Entry[]` if needed.

review.impact: `copyToClipboard` runs `Bun.spawnSync` for up to three commands inside the request handler. While they run, the event loop is blocked, so SSE pushes, chat deltas and other requests wait. A clipboard command that hangs, for example `xclip` on a display that does not respond, stops the whole server.
review.fix: Use the async `Bun.spawn` with a short timeout, and await it in `noteFromAgent`.

review.impact: The `Judgement` union does not tie `failure` to `pass: false` in the review stage. So `loop.ts` must use non-null assertions (`judgement!.pass`, `judgement!.failure!`) at lines 109 and 151. A later change that sets `pass: false` without a `failure` type-checks, and the next builder prompt then gets the text `undefined`.
review.fix: Split the review stage into `{ stage: 'review'; pass: true; ... }` and `{ stage: 'review'; pass: false; failure: string; ... }`. In `loop.ts`, branch on `red` and on `judgement` so that the type checker narrows them, and remove the `!` assertions.

review.impact: `PassLine.grade` copies the `Grade` shape from `judge.ts` inline, and `judgementFields` in `loop.ts` copies the fields one by one. If someone adds a field to `Grade`, the run record drops that field and the type checker gives no warning.
review.fix: Type `grade` as `Grade` and `review` as `Review & { pass: boolean }`, imported from `judge.ts`. In `judgementFields`, pass `j.grade` through directly.

review.impact: The loop uses three non-null assertions: `judgement!.pass`, `judgement!.stage` and `judgement!.failure!`. The `Judgement` type does not encode that `failure` is set when `pass` is false. Each assertion is an escape hatch. A later change to `judgePass` can drop the failure text, and the type checker will not catch it. The next pass then gets `undefined` concatenated into its prompt.
review.fix: Split the review stage of `Judgement` into two variants: `{ stage: 'review'; pass: true }` with no failure, and `{ stage: 'review'; pass: false; failure: string }`. In the loop, branch on `red` and on `judgement` explicitly, for example `if (red) {...} else if (judgement && !judgement.pass) {...}`. Then no `!` is needed.

review.impact: `PassLine.grade` and `PassLine.review` declare their shapes again by hand. These shapes duplicate `Grade` and `Review & { pass: boolean }` from judge.ts. `judgementFields` in loop.ts copies `j.grade` field by field into an identical object. The two type definitions can drift apart.
review.fix: Type the fields as `grade?: Grade` and `review?: Review & { pass: boolean }` with imports from judge.ts. In `judgementFields`, pass `j.grade` directly and do not rebuild it.

review.impact: The prefix `'agent-script.json.launches.'` repeats the base name of `scriptPath` (line 54) and the suffix format from `nthReply` in fake-agent.ts. If one of these changes, stale counter files stay. The next test then replays the wrong reply, and nothing reports the cause.
review.fix: Derive the prefix from `scriptPath`, for example `basename(scriptPath) + '.launches.'`. Better: export one helper from fake-agent.ts that builds the count path, and use it in both files.

review.impact: `REVIEWERS` repeats the area keys of `REVIEW_AREAS` as a literal list. The `launchedRoles` helper has an index-driven nested loop that sorts each group of concurrent reviewer launches, and it is hard to read. A new review area needs a manual edit here, or the tests fail for a reason that is not obvious.
review.fix: Build `REVIEWERS` from `REVIEW_AREAS.map((a) => `reviewer-${a.key}`)`. Replace `launchedRoles` with a simpler comparison: check the non-reviewer roles in order, and check the reviewer roles as a sorted set.

review.impact: No test covers a pass that the overseer cancels and that then fails at the grader or the review. The new `else` branch builds `cancelled + judgement!.failure!`. If someone drops the cancel note from this branch, every test still passes, so the next pass no longer learns why the overseer cancelled it.
review.fix: Add a test in `src/cli/build.test.ts`. Pass 1 has a silent builder, so the overseer cancels it. Pass 1 then has green checks and a failing grader. Assert that the second builder prompt holds both the cancel note and 'The grader failed the pass.'

review.impact: No test checks a non-integer score (for example 3.5) or a score of 0. No test checks a duplicate line id or an unknown line id in the grader reply. If someone removes the `Number.isInteger` check, or changes the rule 'the first duplicate wins', no test fails.
review.fix: Extend the 'a missing line, a bad score...' test with these entries: `{id:'ac-1', score:3.5}`, `{id:'#cited', score:0}`, a second `ac-2` entry with score 1 after a valid one, and an unknown id. Assert the problems and the pass result.

review.impact: No test covers how `acceptanceCriteria` handles a nested sub-bullet (`  - sub`), a `### Sub` heading inside the section, or a `\r\n` brief. The regexes treat each of these in a specific way. For example, a nested bullet becomes its own delivery line. If someone changes this behavior, no test fails.
review.fix: Add assertions for a brief with a nested bullet, a `###` subheading, and CRLF line ends. Pin the behavior that you want for each one.

review.impact: The read-only test checks only that the `--allowedTools` value starts with 'Read,Grep,Glob'. If someone adds a write-capable tool such as `Bash(git commit:*)` or `Edit` after that prefix, the test still passes.
review.fix: Assert the full value: `expect(argv[argv.indexOf('--allowedTools') + 1]).toBe('Read,Grep,Glob,Bash(git diff:*),Bash(git log:*),Bash(git show:*)')`. Or assert that the value contains no `Edit`, `Write`, or other git verbs.

review.impact: The judges are meant to be read-only, but the prefix rules `Bash(git diff:*)`, `Bash(git log:*)` and `Bash(git show:*)` also allow write flags. Examples are `git diff --output=<path>`, `git log --output=<path>` and `git show --output=<path>`. These commands write any file the process can reach. `--ext-diff` and `--textconv` also run a diff driver from the repository config, and the builder (which has bypassPermissions) can set that config. The builder writes the diff, and the diff goes into the judge prompt. So text in the diff can lead a judge to change the worktree or files outside it, and the next pass then commits those changes. The read-only promise in the comment at line 44 is not enforced.
review.fix: Also give the judges `--disallowedTools` with `Bash(git diff --output*)`, `Bash(git log --output*)`, `Bash(git show --output*)`, `Bash(* --ext-diff*)` and `Bash(* --textconv*)`. A better fix is to run the judges with `--permission-mode plan` or in a sandbox. Another option is to drop the git Bash tools and keep only Read, Grep and Glob, because the prompt already holds the diff. Add a test that checks that the judge argv blocks `--output`.

review.impact: The judges get the full `process.env`, the same as the builder. A judge has fewer tools, but it can still read any environment secret with `git log --format` hooks or a diff driver (see the finding above). It does not need those secrets.
review.fix: Give the judges only the environment variables they need: PATH, HOME, the Claude auth variables and WERK_AGENT_ROLE. Do not copy all of `process.env`.

review.impact: `diffSince` reads the full output of `git diff base HEAD` into memory on each green pass, with no size bound. `cutDiff` then keeps only the first 200,000 characters. A build that commits a large generated file, for example a lockfile, a snapshot, or a binary text dump, makes werk buffer and decode many megabytes, and werk then discards almost all of that data. The cost repeats on each pass.
review.fix: Bound the diff at the source. Two options: run `git diff --stat` together with a size-limited read, or stop reading stdout after DIFF_LIMIT bytes. Pass `-- . ':(exclude)*.lock'`-style excludes, or `--no-ext-diff --text=false`, so that binaries show as one line. Then cut the bounded output in `cutDiff` as now.

causeOfLast.why: `#werk-chat` gives the agent a shell, so an earlier pass should have tied write routes to the connection's real address and not only to forgeable headers.

grade.gap: Most of #werk-wording is in src/chat/prompt.ts. Two rules are missing. First, a card records decisions that hold for any module, not per-module results such as a behaviour list, a coverage threshold or a test plan. Second, a sentence that states a fact a child card expands names that child in parentheses, and a body list that mirrors the children is never correct. Optional: add both rules and assert them in src/chat/prompt.test.ts.

review.impact: The pane never learns when a chat child exits or crashes in the middle of a turn. The exit handler only writes to the server log. In the browser, the open agent reply keeps aria-busy="true" forever and shows no error. The person cannot tell a dead agent from a slow one. The transcript fold in src/chat/transcript.ts only closes a reply when a `result` message arrives.
review.fix: Add an `onExit(tab, code)` callback to ConversationOptions, or emit a synthetic message from the exit handler, for example `{ type: 'result', is_error: true, result: 'the agent exited with code N' }`. Call it through `onMessage` when the exit code is not 0 or when a turn is still open. The existing `received` fold then closes the reply and shows the failure.

review.impact: ChatPane opens its own EventSource to /api/events. useLive already opens one for /api/graph, and opens another for each use. Each page now holds two or more SSE connections to the same channel. The chat listener also has no reconnect handling: `chat` events sent while its connection is down are lost, and the open reply never closes. useLive handles this case for the graph with its `open` refetch.
review.fix: Make one shared event-channel hook or context that owns a single EventSource. useLive subscribes to `changed`/`open` on it, and ChatPane subscribes to `chat`. When the connection reopens, close any open reply in the transcript, or mark it as interrupted.

review.impact: copyToClipboard uses Bun.spawnSync inside the HTTP request handler. Each note request blocks the event loop until up to three child processes finish. This also pauses SSE streaming of chat messages to every client. If one clipboard tool hangs, for example xclip with no display, the whole server stops responding.
review.fix: Make copyToClipboard async with Bun.spawn and await `exited`, and add a short timeout. Then await it in noteFromAgent.

review.impact: `void child.stdin.flush()` drops the returned promise. If the child exits between `children.get` and the write, the flush rejects. The result is an unhandled rejection, not the 500 reply that chatTurn tries to send. The synchronous try/catch in chatTurn does not see this asynchronous failure.
review.fix: Attach a `.catch` that logs the error and removes the child from `children`. Or make `send` async, await the flush, and let chatTurn await it inside its try block.

review.impact: `noteLine` belongs to the note route and the clipboard, not to a chat turn. The module doc comment says turn.ts covers "A chat turn, from the composer to the agent". The server now imports note formatting from the chat-turn module, which weakens the module boundary.
review.fix: Move noteLine next to noteFromAgent, or into a small note module, for example src/chat/note.ts or src/server/note.ts, together with its test.

review.impact: The appendRuled rule callback writes the outer `title` variable as a side effect, so the rule function is no longer pure. The title also comes from the state before the append. That works now, but the pattern hides a data dependency inside a callback that exists to decide a ruling.
review.fix: Read the title after a successful append, for example from the fold of the log or from `written.event`. Or return it with the ruling. Keep the rule callback as `(state) => say(state, id, text, 'agent')`.

review.impact: Two harnesses read the fake agent's turn file in the same way, and three files build its path. `src/test/fake-agent.ts` writes `${scriptPath}.turns.jsonl`. Both `e2e/harness.ts` and `src/test/harness.ts` rebuild that suffix and parse the JSON lines themselves. If the file name or format changes in the fake agent, the change must also be made in both harnesses, or the tests read an empty list without an error.
review.fix: Export one `turnsPath(scriptPath)` helper and one `readTurns(scriptPath)` reader from `src/test/fake-agent.ts` or `src/test/harness.ts`. Use them in the fake agent and in both harnesses.

review.impact: `noteFromAgent` copies code from `acceptFromView`: the `reply` helper, the POST-method check, and the `decodeURIComponent` try/catch with its 400 reply. A third route with an id will copy these lines again, and the copies can drift apart.
review.fix: Move the shared code into one helper, for example `postWithId(req, res, rawId): string | undefined`. The helper sends the 405 or 400 reply and returns the decoded id. Each route then contains only its own logic.

review.impact: Three test files each define their own `delta(text)` stream_event builder: `src/cli/serve.test.ts`, `src/chat/transcript.test.ts` and `e2e/chat.spec.ts`. The e2e copy also wraps the event in a different way. A change to the stream-json shape needs three edits, and a missed edit makes the tests disagree.
review.fix: Put one `textDelta(text)` builder in a shared test module, for example `src/test/stream.ts`, and import it in the three files. The e2e spec can wrap the result in `{ event: ... }` where it calls the builder.

review.impact: The client copies the rule 'a turn needs text or an image' from `parseChatRequest` in `src/chat/turn.ts`. If the server rule changes, the client can block or send turns that the server handles differently.
review.fix: Export a small pure predicate, for example `isEmptyTurn(text, images)`, from `src/chat/turn.ts`. Use it in `parseChatRequest` and in `ChatPane.submit`.

review.impact: Every chat test in this file uses only the tab 'main'. A bug in `startConversations` that sends every tab's turns to one child, or that tags messages with the wrong tab, still passes all of these tests. The tab is the key that routes turns to an agent and routes replies to the pane, but no test asserts that it routes anything.
review.fix: Add a serve test that sends one turn on tab 'a' and one on tab 'b'. Assert that `agentLaunches()` has length 2. Assert that each `chat` event has the tab of the turn that caused it.

review.impact: The module comment says a child 'starts again at the next turn if it exits'. No test covers this. If the `children.get(tab) === child` delete is removed or wrong, the next turn writes to a dead stdin, and the server returns 202 while the turn is silently lost. The 500 path in `chatTurn` is also untested.
review.fix: Add a serve test. Script the chat role so the fake agent exits after the first turn (for example, add an exit step or close stdout). Send a second turn. Assert two launches and two recorded turns.

review.impact: `expect.arrayContaining(['--input-format', 'stream-json', '--output-format', '--include-partial-messages'])` does not check argument order. It passes if `stream-json` follows only one of the two format flags, or if `--verbose` is missing. The real CLI requires `--verbose` together with `--output-format stream-json`.
review.fix: Assert the adjacent pairs. For example, check that `argv[argv.indexOf('--input-format') + 1]` and `argv[argv.indexOf('--output-format') + 1]` are both 'stream-json', and that `argv` contains '--verbose'.

review.impact: No test covers the 413 branch of `readJson` (the 32 MiB cap). No test covers the `copied: false` path of the note route when no clipboard command succeeds. A regression in either branch passes all tests.
review.fix: Add a serve test that POSTs more than MAX_BODY_BYTES to /api/chat and expects 413 with no agent launch. Add a note-route test with a `pbcopy` stub that exits 1. Assert `copied: false` and assert that the note is still appended.

review.impact: The streaming test depends on timing. `not.toContainText('from the top.')` must run inside the 700 ms sleep after the second delta. On a slow CI runner, the third delta can arrive first, and the test then fails although the code is correct.
review.fix: Make the sleeps longer (for example, 1500 ms). Or make the fake agent wait for a signal file before each piece, so the test controls when each piece is sent.

review.impact: `push('chat', { tab, message })` sends every whole agent message to every `/api/events` client. These messages include tool inputs and tool results, such as file contents that the agent reads with `Read` or `Bash`. The guard lets a read (`GET`) through from any peer when the `Host` header matches. A caller on another machine can forge that header. When the server binds to a non-loopback address, any host on the network can open `/api/events` and read project files and secrets that pass through the agent. The guard comment says a public bind "shares the map to read, and never the agent's shell", but the agent's output now leaks.
review.fix: Send `chat` events only to clients whose socket peer passes `isLoopback(req.socket.remoteAddress)`. Another option is to forward only the text deltas and the result. Drop tool_use and tool_result content before the broadcast.

review.impact: `Bash(node:*)`, `Bash(bun:*)` and `Bash(python:*)` each allow any code to run (`node -e ...`). With `WebFetch` and `WebSearch` in the same list and no permission prompt, a web page that injects instructions into the agent can run any command as the user. This list gives the same power as a shell with no limit, so the narrow-looking allowlist gives a false sense of safety.
review.fix: Give the reason in the code: state in a comment that this list is equal to a full shell. Another option is to remove `WebFetch`, or to require a prompt for the interpreter commands.

review.impact: `tab` accepts any non-empty string, and `conversations.send` starts a new long-running `claude` child for each new tab name. The tab map has no limit. Repeated turns with new tab names can start any number of agent processes and use up memory and API quota. Only same-origin or loopback callers can do this.
review.fix: Limit `tab` to a short identifier with a pattern such as `^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$`. Also cap the number of live children, or accept only the known tab names.

review.impact: `onMessage` sends every line from the agent to every open `/api/events` connection. The agent runs with `--verbose --include-partial-messages`, so this includes each token delta, the whole `assistant` message that repeats those deltas, and tool-result messages. A tool result can hold a whole file that the agent read. One page holds two or three EventSource connections: `useLive` for the graph in `App`, `useLive` for the board, and `ChatPane`. The server therefore writes each large message several times per page. The `useLive` listeners ignore `chat` events but still receive and buffer the bytes, and `received()` in the pane drops everything except text deltas and results.
review.fix: Filter on the server before `push`. Send only `stream_event` text deltas, `content_block_start`, and `result` messages, or the fields that the pane uses. Another option is a separate chat SSE route, so that the `changed` listeners in `useLive` do not receive chat traffic.

review.impact: `send` spawns a new long-lived `claude` process for each new `tab` string, and the `tab` value comes from the request body. There is no cap on the number of children and no idle timeout. A client with a bug, or many tabs, can start an unbounded number of agent processes, and each one stays alive until the server closes.
review.fix: Limit the number of live children, for example to a fixed allow-list of tab names or a small maximum. Refuse a request over the limit, or stop the least recently used child. An idle timeout that ends a child with no turn for N minutes also helps.

review.impact: `Bun.spawnSync` blocks the server event loop while it runs up to three clipboard commands one after another. During that time, no SSE chat deltas, no graph reads and no other requests get served. If a clipboard tool is slow or stalls, for example `wl-copy` or `xclip` with a display that does not answer, the whole server stops until the command returns.
review.fix: Use async `Bun.spawn`, await `exited` with a short timeout, and kill the process when the timeout passes.

review.impact: Each text delta copies the whole transcript array with `slice`, and each `result` or `sent` call maps over all entries with `closed`. A long conversation with thousands of streamed deltas therefore costs O(entries) per token, and React state allocates a new array on each delta.
review.fix: Close only the last entry. This is the only entry that can be open, because `open()` checks only `at(-1)`. Replace the last element in `closed`, and do not map the whole list.

review.impact: `useLive('/api/graph')` moved from `MapPage` up to `App`. It now runs on the board view too, so the client fetches the whole graph fold, and the server rebuilds it from the log, on each `changed` event, even when no map is visible. The only reason is to build `hrefOf` for the chat links.
review.fix: Accept the cost and document it. Another option is to fetch the graph for `hrefOf` only when the chat has an agent reply to render, or to throttle refetches while the board view is active.

grade.gap: The test in src/cli/contract.test.ts ('an amend that keeps every fact succeeds') changes only the body. It does not show that the check ignores card text, for example with an empty or placeholder body or title. Add one assertion: an amend with odd text, such as --why 'x', still succeeds.

review.impact: `subjectOf` and `changesFrozen` do not know `edge.unlinked`, but removing a depends_on edge changes a frozen field. A single `edge.unlinked` that goes through `checkChange` gets no subject and no frozen check. Only the comment on `EdgeUnlinked` ("only an amend writes it") keeps a decided card safe. A later rule that returns an `edge.unlinked` as a plain `Ruling`, such as an `unlink` verb, can remove a decided card's basis without a refusal. That breaks the #map-frozen promise in `appendRuled`.
review.fix: Add `case 'edge.unlinked': return event.payload.from` to `subjectOf`. Add `case 'edge.unlinked': return event.payload.type === 'depends_on' || event.payload.type === 'refines'` to `changesFrozen`. The contract check then covers the event wherever it comes from, and the safety no longer depends on the comment.

review.impact: The literal `'amended'` is now added to `ReopenReason` in two places: `NodeReopened.reason` here and `ChangeReason` in `src/map/staleness.ts:21`. If one place adds or renames a change reason, the two places can drift apart without a type error.
review.fix: Define one type in events.ts, for example `export type ChangeReason = ReopenReason | 'amended'`. Use it in `NodeReopened`, and import it in staleness.ts.

review.impact: `appendRuled` computes `seq` and `at` for the batch to fold the check state. Then `appendEvents` reads the log again and computes them a second time. The `'events' in ruling` test also runs twice. The two copies of the numbering logic can disagree, and the shape test repeats.
review.fix: Make the batch and the check function one value: `const [batch, check] = 'events' in ruling ? [ruling.events, (after) => checkAmend(after, ruling.amend)] : [[ruling.event], (after) => checkChange(before, after, ruling.event)]`. Let one helper stamp `seq`, `at` and `actor`, and use it in both `appendRuled` and `appendEvents`.

review.impact: `appendRuled` assigns `seq`, `at` and `actor` to the batch so it can run the check. Then `appendEvents` reads the log again and assigns them a second time. The rule for how a log stamps an event now lives in two places. If one copy changes and the other does not, the check runs on events that differ from the events the log writes. The two `new Date()` calls can also give different `at` values.
review.fix: Make one helper, for example `stamp(prev, batch, actor)`, that assigns `seq`, `at` and `actor`. In `appendRuled`, call it once, run the check on the result, and pass the same stamped events to a writer that only serializes and appends them.

review.impact: `appendRuled` tests `'events' in ruling` on two separate lines: one picks the batch and one picks the check. A later change to one branch can miss the other branch.
review.fix: Branch once. Normalize the ruling to `{ batch, check }`, or use one `if` that sets `batch` and `refusal` together.

review.impact: The inline union `ReopenReason | 'amended'` repeats `ChangeReason` in `src/map/staleness.ts:21`. There are now two definitions of the same set of reasons, and they can drift apart.
review.fix: Define the type one time in `events.ts`, for example `export type ChangeReason = ReopenReason | 'amended'`. Use it in `NodeReopened` and import it in `staleness.ts`.

review.impact: No test checks the log written by an amend batch. The tests do not check that the events get consecutive `seq` values, or that they share one `at` and one `actor`. The contract test only compares event types. If `appendEvents` wrote duplicate or gapped `seq` values, all tests would still pass.
review.fix: Add an assertion to the 'an amend that keeps every fact succeeds' test in src/cli/contract.test.ts. Parse the new log lines and check that their `seq` values are `n+1..n+k` and that each line has the same `at` and `actor`.

review.impact: The refused-amend test proves that nothing changed only by comparing `werk show` output. It does not check the log. A change that wrote events which `show` does not render, such as a reopen followed by a decide, would leave `show` the same and still pass.
review.fix: Record `logLines().length` before the refused amend. Assert that it is the same after the refused amend, in this test and in the 'amend refuses …' test.

review.impact: No test covers a successful `--unlink`. The unlink test only shows the refusal when basis is lost. There is no end-to-end test where the card keeps its basis through a second depends_on edge or a parent and the unlink succeeds. In that case the edge must leave the map.
review.fix: Add a test with a second depends_on edge, or a parent, on `a`. Run `werk amend a --unlink base --summary ...` and assert that it succeeds, that `show a` no longer lists `depends_on -> #base`, and that the other edge stays.

review.impact: The new no-decider options rule has no test for a card without a decider that was decided with `--unchallenged`. A regression that drops the `!node.unchallenged` guard for `decider === undefined` would pass these tests.
review.fix: Add `expect(facts(...noWho, statusSet('a', 'decided', true))).toEqual(['who'])` to the 'a card with no decider needs the option fact' test.

causeOfLast.why: werk/84 merged first and added `agentRoles()` and new imports at the same lines where this ticket added `agentTurns()`.

review.impact: When a chat child exits during a turn (a crash, a bad flag, a non-zero code), only the server's stderr records it. The pane gets no `chat` message, so the open reply keeps aria-busy=true forever and the person sees no error. A turn sent at the same moment can also go to a child that is already dead: `send` writes to it, the write throws, and the caller gets a 500.
review.fix: In the `exited` handler, call `onMessage(tab, { type: 'result', is_error: true, result: `the agent exited with code ${code}` })` when the exit happens while a turn is open, or always on a non-zero exit. `received` already closes the reply and shows the failure. Also check `child.exitCode === null` in `send` before you reuse a child.

review.impact: ChatPane opens its own `EventSource('/api/events')` next to the one in useLive. Each page now holds two SSE connections, and each one gets every `changed` and `chat` event. That uses two of the six HTTP/1.1 connections a browser allows per host. The two components also each own the event channel's wire format.
review.fix: Open one EventSource in one place, for example a shared hook or a context in App. Let MapPage subscribe to `changed` and ChatPane subscribe to `chat` through it.

review.impact: noteFromAgent gets the card title by writing to an outer `let title` from inside the `appendRuled` rule callback. This is a side effect in a function that is meant to only decide a ruling, and the result depends on the order the calls run in. The route also runs `copyToClipboard`, which uses `Bun.spawnSync` and can call up to three processes, on the request path. While it runs, it blocks the event loop for all SSE clients and API calls.
review.fix: Read the title from the event that `appendRuled` returns, or from a fold after the write, instead of from a closure. Use async `Bun.spawn` in clipboard.ts and await it, so the server keeps serving during the copy.

review.impact: When `readJson` goes over MAX_BODY_BYTES, it returns 413 but does not stop the request stream. The client keeps uploading up to its full body size on a connection that the server has already answered.
review.fix: Call `req.destroy()`, or set `connection: close` and stop reading, before you return the 413.

review.impact: `noteLine` is the format of the note route's clipboard line. It does not belong to a chat turn, but it lives in chat/turn.ts. Anyone who reads the module boundary sees a turn module that also owns the note format.
review.fix: Move `noteLine` next to the note route, or into a small `chat/note.ts`.

review.impact: The turn log has three separate copies. `e2e/harness.ts`, `src/test/harness.ts` (`agentTurns`, line 101) and `src/test/fake-agent.ts` each build the `${scriptPath}.turns.jsonl` path on their own. The two harnesses also each read and parse the file in their own way. If the writer changes the file name or the format, a reader stops working without any error and returns `[]`. A test that only checks for zero turns then still passes.
review.fix: Add one small module with no side effects, for example `src/test/turns.ts`. It exports `turnsPath(scriptPath)` and `readTurns(scriptPath)`. Use it in the fake agent and in both harnesses. Do not import `fake-agent.ts` itself, because it runs on import.

review.impact: `noteFromAgent` copies the opening of `acceptFromView`: the `reply` closure, the 405 check for a method that is not POST, and the `decodeURIComponent` try/catch that returns 400. A third route that takes an id would copy it again, and the copies can drift apart.
review.fix: Move the id decode into a helper, for example `cardIdOf(rawId): string | undefined`. Or add a small wrapper that checks the POST method, decodes the id and gives `reply`. Use it in both routes.

review.impact: Three test files each define the same `delta` stream-event builder: `src/cli/serve.test.ts`, `src/chat/transcript.test.ts` and `e2e/chat.spec.ts`. The same `{type:'result', is_error:false}` literal also repeats. A change to the stream-json shape must be made three times.
review.fix: Export `textDelta(text)` and `resultEvent` from one shared test helper, for example next to `FakeScript` in `src/test/`. Import them in all three files.

review.impact: `ChatPane` opens its own `EventSource('/api/events')`, and `useLive` already opens one for the graph. Each page now holds two server-sent-events connections to the same channel. The open, close and parse code for the channel now lives in two places.
review.fix: Open one shared `EventSource` for the channel, for example a `useEvents(name, handler)` hook next to `useLive`. Let both `useLive` and `ChatPane` subscribe to it.

review.impact: No test covers the documented restart: 'a child ... starts again at the next turn if it exits'. If the `children.get(tab) === child` check or the delete breaks, the next turn writes to a dead stdin, and no test fails. No test covers two tabs that get separate children, or `close()` that kills the children.
review.fix: Add a serve test with a chat role script that has `exit: 1`, or a fake child that exits after one reply. Send two turns on one tab. Assert two entries in `agentLaunches()` and two turns recorded. Add a second test: turns on tabs 'a' and 'b' start two launches, and each event carries its own tab.

review.impact: `expect.arrayContaining([...'--input-format', 'stream-json', '--output-format'...])` ignores order and pairing. 'stream-json' can match the value of `--output-format`. The test passes if `--input-format` loses its 'stream-json' value.
review.fix: Assert the pairs: `expect(argv[argv.indexOf('--input-format') + 1]).toBe('stream-json')`, and the same for `--output-format`.

review.impact: No test covers the failure paths of the chat and note routes: the 413 for a body over `MAX_BODY_BYTES`, the 500 when `conversations.send` throws, and `copied: false` when no clipboard command works. A regression in these paths passes the suite.
review.fix: Add a serve test that posts a body over the cap and expects 413. Add a note test with a `pbcopy` stub that exits 1 and no `wl-copy` or `xclip` on PATH. Expect `copied: false` and the note still appended.

review.impact: A non-chat stream-mode launch now replays its steps when stdin closes without a user message, because `nextInput` resolves `undefined`. Before this change it waited. The header comment still says it waits for the first user message. A caller that never sends the prompt now gets a passing replay, so this test fake can hide the bug.
review.fix: In the non-chat stream branch, call `fail(64, 'stdin closed before the first user message')` when `nextInput` returns `undefined`.

review.impact: Reads skip the peer check. With `werk serve --host 0.0.0.0`, a caller on another machine can forge `Host: 127.0.0.1:<port>` and open GET /api/events. The server now pushes each agent message on that channel as a `chat` event (server.ts `onMessage: push('chat', …)`). The stream-json output with `--verbose` holds tool_use inputs and tool_result contents. Any file that the agent reads, for example `.env`, therefore goes to a remote reader. The guard comment says a public bind 'never [shares] the agent's shell or the log', but the shell output leaks.
review.fix: Send `chat` events only to SSE clients whose socket peer is loopback. Another option: put the chat stream on its own route that `refuseApiCall` treats as a write and requires a loopback peer for. Add a test: a GET /api/events from a non-loopback peer gets no `chat` event.

review.impact: The chat agent runs `WebFetch`/`WebSearch` and also `Bash(node:*)`, `Bash(python:*)`, `Bash(bun:*)` and `Bash(curl:*)`, all with no permission prompt. Each interpreter can run any code (`node -e`, `python -c`), so the agent has a full unprompted shell. The agent also reads untrusted web content. A prompt injection in a fetched page can therefore run code and exfiltrate project secrets with curl, and nobody approves it. `Bash(rm -f /tmp/:*)` gives no limit either: it matches `rm -f /tmp/../<any path>`, and the interpreters can delete files in any case.
review.fix: Remove the interpreter and curl entries from the no-prompt list, or remove WebFetch/WebSearch from the same list. Let the remaining Bash use go through a permission prompt to the person. If the decision keeps them, write the risk in #werk-pane and confine the child, for example with a sandbox or with no network egress.

review.impact: `tab` is any non-empty string with no length or count limit. Each new tab value spawns one more long-lived `claude` child (conversations.ts `spawnFor`). A local caller, or a page bug, can start an unbounded number of agent processes.
review.fix: Check `tab` against a short pattern such as `/^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$/`. Put a limit on the number of live children in `startConversations`, and refuse a new tab above that limit.

review.impact: `WERK_COMMAND` quotes paths with `JSON.stringify`. That is JSON quoting, not shell quoting. The agent pastes this command into a shell. A `$`, a backtick or a `\` in the bun path or the werk checkout path then expands or breaks inside the double quotes.
review.fix: Quote each part for POSIX sh: wrap it in single quotes and replace each `'` with `'\''`. Another option: refuse to start when a path holds a shell metacharacter.

review.impact: Each browser tab now holds more EventSource connections to /api/events. App always mounts useLive('/api/graph'), ChatPane opens its own EventSource, and BoardPage adds one more. The board view therefore keeps 3 connections open, where it kept 1 before. Browsers allow about 6 HTTP/1.1 connections per host, and the Vite HMR socket uses one more. With two tabs open on the board, the browser has no free connection. Then fetch('/api/graph'), POST /api/chat and the module loads hang. The server also writes every chat delta once for each extra connection.
review.fix: Open one shared EventSource per page, for example a module-level singleton or a context provider. useLive and ChatPane then add listeners to that one source.

review.impact: send() spawns a new long-lived claude child for each new tab string. The tab value comes from the request body, and nothing limits it. Each request with a new tab name starts one more agent process, and no code closes an idle child before the server stops. A client bug, or a script on this machine, can start an unbounded number of claude processes.
review.fix: Cap the number of live children, for example by refusing a tab that is not in a known set or by rejecting requests above a maximum count. Alternatively, evict and kill the least recently used child when the cap is reached.

review.impact: Each streamed text_delta replaces the transcript array. The pane then renders the Markdown of every entry again, with an index key and no memo, so a reply of T deltas in a conversation of N entries costs O(N·T) Markdown parses. Also, received() returns a new array ([...transcript]) for each ignored message, such as the full assistant message, system and tool events. Each ignored message therefore causes a full re-render with no visible change.
review.fix: Return the same transcript reference from received() when a message adds nothing, so React skips the update. Move each entry into a React.memo component, so only the open reply renders again for each delta.

review.impact: readLines() calls rest.split('\n') on the whole buffered text for each chunk. A long stream-json line, such as a Read tool result with a large file or an image, arrives in many 64 KB chunks. The function then scans that text again for each chunk, so the work is quadratic in the line length.
review.fix: Search for '\n' only in the new chunk, for example with indexOf from the previous length. Keep the partial line in an array of pieces and join it once when the newline arrives.

review.impact: push() calls JSON.stringify(data) once for each connected client. Chat messages, such as tool results, can be large, and there are now several connections per browser tab. The server therefore serializes the same large payload many times for each agent message.
review.fix: Build the SSE frame string once before the loop, and write that string to each client.

review.impact: copyToClipboard() uses Bun.spawnSync in the request handler. It runs up to three commands in sequence. While each command runs, the whole server event loop is blocked, and SSE delivery and other requests stop. A copy command that does not exit, for example an xclip that waits on a display, blocks the server with no time limit.
review.fix: Use the async Bun.spawn and await proc.exited with a timeout. Return the response after that, or copy in the background.

review.impact: The verb copies the actor-claim rule from `actorOf` in src/cli/map-verb.ts:38. The rule says that only `--actor you` gives the actor 'you'. Now two places hold this rule. If one place changes, the board verb and the map verbs give different actors for the same flag.
review.fix: Export `actorOf` from src/cli/map-verb.ts, or move it to src/cli/args.ts. Then call it here: `const actor = actorOf(parsed.flags)`. Delete the copied comment and the inline ternary.

review.impact: The CLI handler holds the restore rule: find the archived ticket, and refuse 'not archived' or 'no ticket on the board'. Map rules are pure functions in src/map/rules.ts, and the board step of a plan is a pure function in src/plan/board-plan.ts. The server and the CLI can both call those functions. The board view (#werk-board-control) cannot use this rule without a copy, and only the slower CLI tests can test the rule.
review.fix: Move the check into a pure function next to the board fold. An example is `restoreTicket(board: Board, number: number): { ok: true; event: NewBoardEvent; ticket: BoardTicket } | { ok: false; error: string }` in src/board/. The verb then parses the arguments, calls the function, appends the event, and prints the result.

review.impact: The verb copies the actor-claim rule from `actorOf` in `src/cli/map-verb.ts:38`. If the rule changes, for example to accept a new actor, someone must edit both places. If one place is missed, the two verbs record the actor in different ways.
