review.fix: Add a render test for `MarkTraces` with `mark: 'paused'`. Assert that the heading text is 'Why this card is stale' and that the badge names the paused kind.

causeOfLast.why: pass 1 put a helper that uses nothing from the test inside the test body, and the project's oxlint rules do not allow that.

grade.gap: No contradiction. A ticket pulses only when it is in building and its session is running (web/src/BoardView.tsx `live`). The session stops counting when the pass ends (headless.ts `session?.end()`) or when the agent process is gone (session-file.ts `alive`), so a build that a person stops by hand also stops the pulse. The log sits above the slice in a 12rem viewport that scrolls, and it shows only while the ticket is in building. One small point: a ticket in building with no session shows an empty 'log of the last session' box. The card does not forbid this.

review.impact: The session file only feeds the board display, but its failures stop the build. `startSession` runs after `Bun.spawn`. If `mkdirSync` or `writeFileSync` throws (for example, a full disk or a permission error), `runHeadless` throws. The detached agent child then has no owner. `session?.entry` inside the stdout handler and `session?.end()` can also throw. Then the pass fails, or the silence timer and stdin are not cleaned up.
review.fix: Make the recorder best-effort. Catch errors inside `startSession`, `entry`, and `end`, for example by wrapping each fs call and logging once. Or create the recorder before the spawn and pass the pid later. A display file must never abort or orphan a builder pass.

review.impact: The board page listens to `session`. The server pushes `session` for each change to `<n>.jsonl`, which means each agent event. During a build, the page refetches the whole board fold on each agent event, debounced to 30 ms. The board needs only the running set, and only a `<n>.json` meta change alters that set.
review.fix: Push two different events: one for a meta change (`<n>.json`, for example `running`) and one for an entry change (`<n>.jsonl`, `session`). The board listens to `changed` and `running`. `AgentLog` listens to `session` and `running`.

review.impact: The modules depend on each other in both directions. `board/session.ts` imports `OverseerAct` from `build/overseer.ts`. `build/session-file.ts` imports `summarise` and the types from `board/session.ts`. The server and the web client also reach into `build/` and `board/` for one feature. The cycle is type-only today, but it couples the two modules.
review.fix: Put `SessionEntry` and the read side (`readSession`, `runningSessions`) together in one module, for example `board/session-file.ts`. Leave only the writer (`startSession`) in `build/`. Or move `OverseerAct` to a shared types module, so that `board` does not import from `build`.

review.impact: The hook joins the event names into a string and splits them again in the effect. This is a workaround for a stable dependency list, and it hides the real value. Each `useLive` call also opens its own `EventSource`. With the drawer open, the page holds two SSE connections to `/api/events`.
review.fix: Keep the names stable with `useMemo` or a module constant. Share one `EventSource` across hooks, for example with a module-level singleton and listener registration.

review.impact: The server repeats the session file names in its own regex, `/^\d+\.jsonl?$/`. `session-file.ts` also defines them, in `metaPath`, `entriesPath` and the `/^\d+\.json$/` filter in `runningSessions`. If the file layout changes in `session-file.ts`, the watcher stops pushing `session` events, and no type check catches it.
review.fix: Export a predicate such as `isSessionFile(name)` from `src/build/session-file.ts`. Use it in the server watcher and in `runningSessions`.

review.impact: The hook joins the `on` array into a string and splits it again inside the effect. This only keeps the dependency array stable. The reader must work out why, and the code breaks for an event name that contains a space.
review.fix: Add a short comment that says why the hook joins the names. Or keep `names` for the dependency array only, and loop over `on` inside the effect.

review.impact: The session route calls `send` with `JSON.stringify` directly. Every other JSON route uses `sendJson`. So a read error in `readSession`, for example an EACCES from `readFileSync`, throws out of the request handler and does not become a 500 response.
review.fix: Read the view first. If it is undefined, send the 404. Otherwise call `sendJson(res, () => view)`. Or wrap the call in `sendJson` and give the 404 its own branch.

review.impact: `readSession` calls `entriesPath(log, ticket)` twice and does an `existsSync` before `readFileSync`. Every other read in this file uses try/catch, so the code uses two styles. The file can also disappear between the two calls.
review.fix: Store the path in one const. Read the file in a try/catch that returns '' on ENOENT, as `readMeta` does.

review.impact: Two tests build the same assistant text event shape by hand: the `said` helper here and the inline `said` object in `src/cli/build.test.ts`. A third test that needs it will copy it again.
review.fix: Export a `said(text)` step builder from `src/test/fake-agent.ts`, next to `FakeStep`, and use it in both tests.

review.impact: No test checks that `runHeadless` writes overseer acts (answered, warned, cancelled) to the session file. The new test checks only `e.event.type` for event entries. If `act()` stops calling `session?.entry`, every test still passes. `session-file.test.ts` tests only the recorder API, not the code in `headless.ts` that calls it.
review.fix: Add a builder step `{ ask: { id: 'r1', tool: 'Bash' } }` to the scripted pass. Then assert that `3.jsonl` contains an entry `{ overseer: { act: 'answered', tool: 'Bash', requestId: 'r1' } }` between the event entries.

review.impact: No test covers a cancelled pass. A pass that the overseer cancels (silence or loop) must still record the `cancelled` act and set `live: false`. If a later edit moves `session?.end()` after an early return in the cancel path, the board shows a dead session as live until the process-liveness check catches it. No test fails.
review.fix: Add a build test where the overseer cancels the builder for silence (as other tests in this file do). Assert that `3.json` has `live: false` and that `3.jsonl` ends with an `overseer` entry whose `act` is `cancelled`.

review.impact: The e2e test does not cover how the agent log scrolls. `AgentLog` follows the newest line unless the person scrolled up (`following` ref and `onScroll`). No test checks this, so a regression in the scroll logic passes all tests.
review.fix: Script enough `said` lines to overflow the 12rem viewport. Assert that `scrollTop + clientHeight` equals `scrollHeight` after a new line arrives. Then scroll up, release a gate, and assert that `scrollTop` stays the same.

review.impact: Each `SessionRecorder.entry` call writes the full raw stream event to `.werk/sessions/<ticket>.jsonl`. This includes the thinking blocks, the complete tool inputs, and the complete tool results. A builder that reads a `.env` file or prints a token leaves that secret in plain text on disk. The file stays after the session ends, and a new pass is the only thing that empties it. The board shows only `summarise()` output, which drops the thinking text and cuts each line to 200 characters. The stored file holds much more than the board needs, and a person who copies or commits `.werk/` copies the secrets too.
review.fix: Store only what the board reads. One option: write `{ at, text: summarise(entry) }` in `entry()` and make `readSession` read that text. Another option: remove the `thinking` text and the tool result `content` before the write. Also state in the module comment that the session files can hold agent output, so `.werk/sessions/` must stay out of version control.

review.impact: The board page listens to `session`. The server pushes `session` on every `.jsonl` append, so every agent event makes the client refetch `/api/board`. That fetch reads and folds the whole `board.jsonl` and runs `runningSessions`. The board needs `session` only when a `<ticket>.json` meta file changes. A busy builder makes several events each second, so the board is folded several times each second for no change.
review.fix: Push two different events from the server: one for meta changes (`/^\d+\.json$/`, for example `running`) and one for entry changes (`/^\d+\.jsonl$/`, for example `session`). Make the board listen to `changed` and `running`. Make `AgentLog` listen to `session` and `running`.

review.impact: `readSession` reads the full `<ticket>.jsonl` and runs `JSON.parse` and `summarise` on every entry on each request. The client requests it after each appended event, so one pass costs O(n²) in total. The file stores raw stream events, and these include full `tool_result` contents such as whole files and command output. A long pass can grow the file to many MB, and the server then parses all of it after each new line. The client also gets every line again each time.
review.fix: Cap the work. One option is to store the summarised `{at, text}` line in the file, not the raw event. Another is to read and send only the last N lines, from a tail read. A third is to add an `?after=<count>` or byte-offset query so the client gets only the new lines and appends them.

review.impact: `AgentLog` renders every line of the session in one list. Index keys are stable, but React still diffs a list that grows with no limit after each refetch. A pass with thousands of events makes each update slower.
review.fix: Show only the last N lines, for example 500, from the server or the client. Or use virtualisation for the list.

grade.gap: This diff adds no new test for this path. The existing e2e test at e2e/map.spec.ts:180 covers it. The new '#id' parsing in src/cli/args.ts makes the path work when a user types a card id as a card writes it.

In src/cli/args.ts, ID_FLAGS lists only 'parent', 'unlink' and 'root'. A future flag that takes a card id does not lose its '#' unless someone adds it to this list. The change contradicts no part of the card.
In src/cli/verbs/add.ts, a new card with no --status now proposes status 'open'. The status goes in as a field of the proposal, and nothing writes outside the log.

review.impact: The rule 'a new card with no status is open' is in the CLI verb, not in the domain rule `propose` in src/map/rules.ts. Other callers of `propose` do not get it. `proposeAnswer` in src/plan/answers.ts:46 creates a `kind: 'card'` with no status, so a card made from a plan answer still has no status. The two paths now give different results for the same domain fact.
review.fix: Move the default into `propose` in src/map/rules.ts: when `req.kind === 'card'` and `req.status === undefined`, set the status to 'open'. Then add.ts can pass `flags.get('status')` again. Add a unit test for `propose` in the rules tests.

review.impact: `parseArgs` is a general argument splitter for every verb, but it now removes a leading `#` from every positional. Some positionals are not card ids: the `session-id` operand of quote, the `outcome` of rederive, the `status` of status, and the `folder` of ticket-check. Each of these now changes without a signal. Domain knowledge about card ids is now in a generic module, and the module-level `ID_FLAGS` list does not depend on the verb. For example, `root` is a card id only for some verbs.
review.fix: Keep `parseArgs` generic. Normalize ids at the point that knows which values are ids. For example, `runMapVerb` in src/cli/map-verb.ts can apply `cardId` to the operands that are ids, and each verb can apply it to its own id flags. Another option: give `parseArgs` an `ids` parameter for each call that names the id flags and says if the positionals are ids.

review.impact: The default kind `flags.get('kind') ?? 'card'` is now computed in `rule` and again in `report`. The two values can drift apart if one of them changes later.
review.fix: Put the default in one small helper, for example `const kindOf = (flags) => flags.get('kind') ?? 'card'`, and call it from both `rule` and `report`.

review.impact: The generic parser holds a global list of flag names from three verbs (`parent` in add, `unlink` in amend, `root` in ticket-check). Nothing connects this list to each verb's own `flags` list. A verb that later adds a new id flag gets no `#` stripping. A verb that uses one of these names for a value that is not an id loses a leading `#` without warning.
review.fix: Let the caller declare its id flags. For example, add an `ids` parameter to `parseArgs`, or mark id flags in each verb's flag declaration in the registry. Then the strip rule stays next to the flag definitions.

review.impact: The `#`-strip rule `replace(/^#/, '')` now exists in three places: `src/cli/args.ts:8`, `src/ticket/parse.ts:102` and `src/build/brief.ts:24`. If the id form changes, all three copies must change together.
review.fix: Export one `cardId` helper from a shared module, and use it in all three places.

review.impact: The `rule` now reads `const kind = flags.get('kind') ?? 'card'`, but `report` still repeats `flags.get('kind') ?? 'card'`. The default kind is in two places, and the two can drift apart.
review.fix: Move the kind default into a small shared helper or constant, and use it in both `rule` and `report`.

review.impact: `refuses(['status', '#a', 'decided'])` also passes without the hash-stripping change. Without it, `#a` names no card, and the verb still exits 1 and leaves the log unchanged. So this line does not show that `#a` reaches card `a` on a write verb. It also does not show that the refusal comes from the missing facts of an open card.
review.fix: Assert on the stderr text that is specific to card `a`. Example: `expect(r.stderr).toContain('a cannot be decided')`. Or run a write verb that succeeds with a hashed id, such as `ok(['edit', '#a', '--who', 'you'])`, and check the change with `show a`.

review.impact: `ID_FLAGS` contains `root`, but no test strips `#` from `--root`. The tests also do not show that a flag outside `ID_FLAGS` keeps its `#` when its value is a card id. Only `--title` is checked. If someone removes `root` from the list, or adds a wrong entry, no test fails.
review.fix: Add `--root #r` to the parseArgs test with `root` in `known`, and expect `['root', 'r']`. Also add a case where the leading `#` stays, for example `--status #x`.

review.impact: The edge cases of `cardId` have no tests. A bare `#` becomes an empty positional. `##a` becomes `#a`, because the code removes only one `#`. A value given as `--parent=#` becomes an empty id. The tests do not fix any of these behaviors.
review.fix: Add assertions for `['##a']` → `['#a']` and for a bare `#`. Pick the behavior you want for the empty id, for example a refusal, and assert it.

review.impact: The test checks the default `open` status for a card and checks that an option has no status. It does not check that an explicit `--status` still wins over the default. If the code changes `??` to always use `open`, no test in this diff fails.
review.fix: Add a card with an explicit status, for example `add b --title B --status decided` or another valid non-open status. Assert that `show b` prints that status and not `open`.

review.impact: `parseArgs` strips one leading `#` from every positional, not only from card ids. `ticket-check` and other verbs read the positional as a folder or a ticket number. So `werk ticket-check '#tickets' ...` silently reads the folder `tickets`, which is a different path than the one the user named. The user gets no error.
review.fix: Strip the `#` only where the verb expects a card id. One option is to let the caller pass the positional kind, for example a `positionalIsId` option. Another option is to call `cardId` inside the map verbs (`map-verb.ts`, `show`, `plan`, `gate`, `run`, `heldout`, `find`, `inbox`) and not in `parseArgs`.

review.impact: A bare `#` as a positional, or as the value of `--parent`, `--unlink` or `--root`, becomes the empty string `''`. No code downstream refuses an empty id, so `werk add '#' --title x` can propose a card whose id is `''`. Before this change, the id was the literal `#`.
review.fix: Refuse an id that is empty after the `#` is stripped. For example, return `{ ok: false, error: 'a card id cannot be empty' }` from `parseArgs` when `cardId(arg) === ''`. Add a test for `['#']` and `['--parent', '#']`.

causeOfLast.why: the code handled a merging ticket on a missing branch correctly (it went back to building), but the test's setup left that ticket's builder running, so the run could not end.

grade.gap: The server has the start route POST /api/board/start (src/server/server.ts, src/server/run.ts). The test src/cli/serve-board.test.ts shows that this route starts the run and that tickets build. But the board page has no start control: web/src/BoardView.tsx does not change in this diff and has no button that calls /api/board/start. Add a start control to the board page for each plan root (Board.roots) that has no active run (Board.runs). The control posts {root} to /api/board/start.

The ticket.reordered fold, the board order, and the scheduler order are present. The test 'a reorder within ready changes the order the run builds the tickets in' in src/cli/run.test.ts proves them. But no drag exists in web/src/BoardView.tsx, so a person cannot reorder from the page. Add drag-and-drop within the ready column that posts {number, to: 'ready', before} to /api/board/move.

The archive rule is correct: only ready and blocked tickets can be archived (src/board/control.ts personAction). The restore verb brings a ticket back (serve-board.test.ts runs 'ticket restore 3'). But nothing asks for confirmation. POST /api/board/archive appends ticket.archived at once. web/src/BoardView.tsx has no archive action and no confirmation dialog. Add an archive action to the board page that shows only on ready and blocked tickets. Before it posts to /api/board/archive, it must show a confirmation. Per #werk-board-control, the confirmation says the ticket is never deleted for good and that an agent can restore it. Add a test that proves the confirmation appears and that a cancel appends no event.

POST /api/board/move to 'building' appends ticket.triggered. A move from building to ready appends ticket.stopped. The run polls the board and aborts the fake builder; serve-board.test.ts and run.test.ts check that the builder processes are no longer alive. But web/src/BoardView.tsx has no trigger icon on a ready ticket and no drag from building to ready. Add a trigger icon on each ready ticket that posts {number, to: 'building'}. Add a drag from building to ready that posts {number, to: 'ready'}.

personAction refuses a move into merging or done ('only the merge loop moves a ticket into ...'). Tests prove this in src/board/control.test.ts and src/cli/serve-board.test.ts (409, no event appended). No edit control or edit route exists. The board page has no drag yet, so the refusal is proven only at the API.

No contradiction in what the diff builds. The person's moves are limited to reorder within ready, trigger from ready to building inside an active run, stop from building to ready, and archive of ready or blocked tickets. A move into or out of blocked is refused, and so is a move into merging or done. Other tickets build the archive confirmation and the drawn controls, and their absence is reported under criteria 1, 3 and 4.

No contradiction. A ticket that a person stopped does not merge, even after a green pass (src/build/run.ts personStopped). A triggered ticket goes through the same merge queue (run.test.ts merge order).

No contradiction. A triggered ticket still waits for module overlap: serve-board.test.ts shows that ticket 5 builds only after ticket 1 stops. The cap of parallel builds still applies. The triggered ticket shows in the building column before its build starts. This is a display question, not a contradiction.

When a person stops a build, the pass that was running is not committed (src/build/loop.ts 'if (o.signal?.aborted) break' before commitPass). The card does not cover a stop by a person, and the branch stays, so this is not a contradiction.

causeOfLast.why: the card clearly asks for a confirmation before an archive, and the earlier passes built the server route but no board page control.

grade.gap: Each part is tested on its own. src/cli/serve-board.test.ts shows the trigger and the stop with the fake builder's pid dead. e2e/board.spec.ts 'inside an active run, the trigger icon...' shows the icon in the browser. One gap: no e2e test drags a building ticket to ready inside an active run and then checks that the builder stopped. The e2e test 'a drag from building to ready stops the build' checks only the column.

The card says a stop returns the ticket to ready. The diff also sets `held` on the ticket (src/board/fold.ts ticket.stopped). Because of `held`, src/build/schedule.ts never starts the ticket again until a person triggers it. A run can then end with 'no ticket can build' (src/cli/run.test.ts). The card does not forbid this, but it adds a rule the card does not state. Also, a triggered ticket shows in building while the module overlap makes it wait (serve-board.test.ts ticket 5). This agrees with #st-build-parallel.

The diff adds the `--poll-every` and `--actor` flags to the run verb (src/cli/verbs/run.ts USAGE). The card says the form of a command lives on one card under #werk-cli-build. No change to that card is part of this diff.

review.impact: The fold applies `ticket.triggered` and `ticket.stopped` in any column. The server rules on a fold it read earlier, then appends with no lock (`boardControl`). This differs from `appendRuled`, which checks the state after the append. Example: a person drags a building ticket to ready while the merge loop moves the same ticket to merging. The `ticket.stopped` event lands after `ticket.moved` to merging and puts the merging ticket back in ready with `held`. A late `ticket.triggered` can also pull a done or blocked ticket into building. Every reader of the board log then sees a move that no rule allows.
review.fix: Guard the fold the same way it already guards `ticket.restored`. Apply `ticket.triggered` only when the ticket is in ready, and `ticket.stopped` only when the ticket is in building. In every other case the event changes nothing. Add a fold test for a stop that arrives after a move to merging.

review.impact: The run only reads `personStopped` from the abort signal, and only the poll branch aborts it. Example: a build ends green, and a person moves the ticket to ready before the next poll. The race returns the finished build, `personStopped` is false, and the loop moves the ticket to merging and merges it. The loop then overrides the person's stop with no message.
review.fix: Call `stopMovedBuilds(o, stops, io)` before you read `personStopped` for a finished build. You can also re-read the ticket's column from the log: if it is not in building, treat the build as stopped.

review.impact: The page has its own copy of the archive rule (`ready` or `blocked`) and the trigger rule (ready, inside an active run). `personAction` in `src/board/control.ts` also has these rules. A change to one copy leaves the other copy wrong. Then the board shows buttons that the server refuses, or hides buttons that the server allows.
review.fix: Export small predicates from `src/board/control.ts`, for example `canArchive(ticket)` and `canTrigger(ticket, active)`. Use them in `personAction` and in `TicketCard`. The page already imports types from `src/board`.

review.impact: The signature of `boardControl` puts three parameters on one line and the others on their own lines. This does not match the formatting of the code around it. Also, the server keeps the `started` map in the request handler's closure, and only `boardControl` uses it. This makes the double-start guard hard to see and hard to test.
review.fix: Format the signature with one parameter per line, the same as the formatter output. Move the double-start guard into `src/server/run.ts`, for example as a small `RunStarter` that holds the map. Then `boardControl` calls one function.

review.impact: The tests copy the same helpers into two files. `launchesOf`/`launches` parse `WERK_FAKE_AGENT_LOG` by hand. `until` polls until a condition holds. `alive` checks a pid. They are in `src/cli/run.test.ts:302-319` and again in `src/cli/serve-board.test.ts:76-89,173-178`. The `Project` harness already reads that log through `agentLaunches()` and `agentRoles()`, so a change to the log format must now be made in three places. The test `alive` also repeats `processAlive` in `src/board/control.ts`, but it handles EPERM differently.
review.fix: Add an `agentPids(role)` (or launches with pid) accessor to `Project` in `src/test/harness.ts`. Move `until` into a shared test module and import it in both files. Use `processAlive` from `src/board/control.ts` in place of the local `alive` copies.

review.impact: The new `moveTo` helper removes `reason` and `held`, then sets the column. The `ticket.moved` case at line 94 repeats the same destructure `{ reason: _, held: __, ...rest }`. A new transient field must be cleared in both places, and one place can be missed.
review.fix: Make the `ticket.moved` case call `moveTo`, and extend `moveTo` to take the optional reason and branch. Or extract one `clearTransient(t)` helper that both places use.

review.impact: The client repeats the server rules. `archivable` (ready or blocked) and `DRAGGABLE` (ready, building) at line 20 copy the rules in `personAction`/`moveRuling` in `src/board/control.ts`. If a rule changes in only one place, the page shows controls that the server refuses, or hides controls that the server allows.
review.fix: Export small predicates from `src/board/control.ts`, for example `canArchive(column)` and `DRAG_COLUMNS`. Use them in both `personAction` and `BoardView`.

review.impact: The condition `before !== undefined && before !== number` is written twice: negated on line 68 and plain on line 69. This makes the reorder branch harder to read.
review.fix: Compute `const anchor = before === number ? undefined : before` one time. Then refuse when `anchor !== undefined && !ready.some(t => t.number === anchor)`, and emit `...(anchor !== undefined && { before: anchor })`.

review.impact: The route list `'/api/board/move' || .../archive || .../start` and the `as 'move' | 'archive' | 'start'` cast must stay in step by hand. The cast hides a mismatch from the type checker. The `boardControl` signature at line 169 is also formatted differently from the code around it.
review.fix: Declare `const BOARD_CONTROLS = ['move', 'archive', 'start'] as const`. Parse the suffix and check it with `BOARD_CONTROLS.includes(...)`, so no cast is needed. Run the formatter on the `boardControl` signature.

review.impact: `debug` is a mutable variable at module level. One test reassigns it, and the next test does not reset it. A timeout in a later test then prints the logs of a project that the earlier test already removed.
review.fix: Pass a debug callback to `until` as an argument, or reset `debug` in the `afterEach` hook.

review.impact: No test covers a drop of a ready ticket on itself (`moveTo(3, 'ready', 3)`). In `moveRuling`, `before === number` sets `target` to undefined. The rule then emits `ticket.reordered {number: 3}` with no `before`, and the fold moves the ticket to the end of ready. A drag released on the ticket's own card therefore reorders the ticket, but the fold treats `number === before` as a no-op. The current tests pass with this defect.
review.fix: Add `expect(rule(moveTo(3, 'ready', 3)))` with the intended result, either a no-op refusal or an event that keeps the position. Then fix `moveRuling` so that a self-drop does not send the ticket to the end. Add an e2e drag of ticket 3 onto itself that asserts `numbers(page, 'ready')` stays `[3, 6]`.

review.impact: The malformed-body test does not cover the `BODY_LIMIT` path in `readBody`. A change that drops the 413 check or reads an unbounded body still passes the test.
review.fix: Post a body longer than 4096 bytes, for example `{ number: 1, pad: 'x'.repeat(5000) }`. Assert status 413, and assert that `events(p)` has the same length as before.

review.impact: No test covers the path where a person stops a build and the stopped pass ends green. Nothing checks that `personStopped` blocks the merge before `built.green` is read. If the order of the checks in `runMergeLoop` changes, a stopped green build merges, and no test fails.
review.fix: Add a run test with a fast green builder. Append `ticket.stopped` after the builder writes and before the loop reads the result, for example with a sleep step at the end of the reply. Assert that main does not move and the ticket stays in ready. Another option is a unit test of the decision with a stubbed `buildTicket`.

review.impact: The refused drag into building asserts only the alert text. It does not check that ticket 6 stays in ready or that the server appends no event. A UI that moves the card optimistically, or a server that appends an event and then reports an error, still passes.
review.fix: Add `await expect(column(page, 'ready').locator('li[data-ticket="6"]')).toBeVisible()`. Also compare `boardEvents(werk.dir)` before and after the drag, the same way the archive-cancel test does.

review.impact: No test covers how the run verb ends with an error. Nothing checks that `run.ended` is appended with the `stopped` reason when `runMergeLoop` throws a `GitError`, for example a missing `--main` branch. A board then shows such a run as active until its pid dies, and a change to the `finally` block is not caught.
review.fix: Run `p.werk(['run', 'root', '--main', 'nope'])` on a project with tickets. Assert that the last event is `run.ended` with a `stopped` reason that contains the git error, and that `run.started` comes before it.

review.impact: The only guard on the new POST routes is the Origin check, and that check compares Origin with the Host header of the same request. A DNS-rebinding page sends Origin `http://evil.example:PORT` and Host `evil.example:PORT`, so the two match and the check passes. The page can then call `/api/board/start`, which spawns a detached `werk run --actor you` process that runs builder agents with tool access in the user's repo. The page can also trigger, stop, reorder and archive tickets, and each of these events is recorded as the person's act (`actor: 'you'`). The weak check already existed on the accept route. This change adds a route that starts processes, so the possible damage is much larger.
review.fix: Before the Origin check, compare the Host header with an allowlist of loopback names (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`, with the bound port). Refuse every other host with 403. Then require an Origin header and require it to match the same allowlist. Put this check in one helper and use it for the accept route and for `boardControl`.

review.impact: `activeRoots` reads the `pid` from `run.started` in the board log and trusts it. `processAlive` says only that some process with that pid exists. After a crash, a reused pid keeps a dead run active. A pid of 0, 1 or a negative number from a crafted log line has the same effect. While the run shows as active, the person can trigger tickets into building, and no merge loop exists to build them. The e2e test uses this gap on purpose when it writes `process.pid` into the log.
review.fix: Accept only a `pid` that is a safe integer greater than 1. If you need a stronger check, also record the process start time or a random run token, and compare that value to tell a live run from a reused pid.

review.impact: The server passes `root` from the board log to `werk run` as a positional argument and does no check on its form. A root that starts with `--`, for example `--main=other`, is parsed as a flag. The run then ignores the plan the person chose or uses a different main branch. Agents write the plan roots, so the person does not control this value.
review.fix: Validate `root` against the card-id format before the spawn, or pass `--` before the positional arguments so that `parseArgs` cannot read the root as a flag.

review.impact: During each build, every poll tick reads and folds the whole board log two times. The default tick is 1 s. `stopMovedBuilds` calls `liveTickets` once, then `continue` sends the loop back to the top, and the top calls `liveTickets` again. The cost of each tick grows with the length of `board.jsonl`, and a long run makes the log long.
review.fix: Read the board one time per tick. Move the stop check to the top of the loop and run it on the `tickets` that the loop already reads there, for example `stopMovedBuilds(tickets, stops, io)`. Then the poll branch only needs `continue`.

causeOfLast.why: werk/90 (the builder session log) merged first and changed the same board server, board page, builder loop and e2e spec as this ticket.

grade.gap: The trigger appends ticket.triggered even when the run already builds 3 tickets or the ticket's modules overlap a running build. The ticket then sits in building with no builder until a slot frees (src/board/control.ts moveRuling; src/build/schedule.ts waiting('building')). The criterion still passes, because the scheduler starts it first.

A stop holds the ticket in ready (`held`), and no run starts it again until a person triggers it (src/board/fold.ts ticket.stopped; src/build/schedule.ts `!t.held`). The card says only 'returning it to ready'. Also, when only held tickets remain, the run ends with 'no ticket can build' (src/cli/run.test.ts). This is an addition, not a contradiction.

The diff adds the flags `--poll-every` and `--actor you` to the run verb (src/cli/verbs/run.ts USAGE). It does not add them to the verb's form card (#werk-cli-build). This is a card follow-up, not a code fault.

review.impact: The loop decides that a person stopped a build only from the AbortSignal. `stopMovedBuilds` sets that signal only after a poll times out. Suppose a person appends `ticket.stopped` and the build ends before the next poll. Then `personStopped` is false. A green build moves to merging and merges, which clears `held` and ignores the stop. A red build stops the whole run as 'stuck'. The board log already says the ticket is in ready, so the two sources of truth disagree.
review.fix: Call `stopMovedBuilds(o, stops, io)` (or read the ticket's column from the board) before you read `personStopped` for a finished build. Then the board state decides whether the build was stopped, and the signal only stops the agent.

review.impact: A failed `spawn` (for example ENOENT or EACCES) reports the failure in an asynchronous 'error' event, and `child.pid` is undefined. The code throws on the missing pid, but nothing listens for 'error'. Node then raises it as an uncaught exception, and the whole `werk serve` process crashes. The 500 reply in `boardControl` does not prevent this.
review.fix: Add `child.on('error', () => {})` (or log the error) before `unref()`, and keep the pid check as the synchronous refusal.

review.impact: The client copies the rules of `board/control.ts`: `DRAGGABLE`, `archivable` (ready or blocked), and `canTrigger` (ready with an active root, but without the unmet-blockers check). The header of control.ts says the view asks the server's rules for each control. Now the two copies can drift. One drift exists already: the trigger icon shows on a ready ticket with unmet blockers, and the server always refuses that click.
review.fix: Let the server compute the allowed controls per ticket with `personAction` and send them in `BoardReply` (for example `controls: {archive, trigger}`). The view then renders those flags and does not copy the rules.

review.impact: The module header says that control.ts holds pure rules. But `processAlive` calls `process.kill`, which is an operating-system probe. Now the board domain module depends on the process API, and the rules and the I/O live in one file.
review.fix: Move `processAlive` to the server (or to a small `process` helper next to `src/server/run.ts`). Keep `activeRoots` with the injected `IsAlive` in control.ts.

review.impact: The start control replies 202 before the run verb validates anything. If the run exits at once (a git error, no ticket, or a bad root), the person sees nothing. The reason goes only to `.werk/runs/run-*.log`, and the board shows the run as active for a moment. There are also two sources of truth for 'active': the `started` map and `activeRoots`.
review.fix: Show the reason from `run.ended.payload.stopped` on the board for the most recent run of each root. Or point the person to the run log path in the 202 reply, and let the page show the last stop reason.

review.impact: The `ticket.moved` case repeats the body of the new `moveTo` helper at line 52. Both strip `reason` and `held` and then set `column`. A future field that a move must clear, such as `held` in this change, must be added in two places. If one place is missed, the two move paths behave differently.
review.fix: Build the `ticket.moved` case on `moveTo`, and add `reason` and `branch` after it. Another option is a shared `withoutTransient(t)` helper that both paths call.

review.impact: The helpers `alive`, `until`, and the fake-agent `launches` reader are copied word for word from `src/cli/run.test.ts:303-318`. The `alive` helper also re-implements `processAlive` from `src/board/control.ts`, with different EPERM handling. A fix to the polling or the log parsing must be made in each copy.
review.fix: Move `until` and `launchesOf(role)` into `src/test/harness.ts` and import them in both test files. Use `processAlive` from `board/control.ts`, or one shared test helper, in place of the local `alive` copies.

review.impact: The control union `'move' | 'archive' | 'start'` is written in four places: the route check, the cast at line 71, the `boardControl` signature at line 189, and `Post` in `web/src/BoardView.tsx:28`. The route test lists the three paths by hand, so a new control needs edits in many places. The `as` cast hides a mismatch from the type checker.
review.fix: Export one `BOARD_CONTROLS = ['move', 'archive', 'start'] as const` with `type BoardControl`. Match the route with `BOARD_CONTROLS.includes(...)` and narrow the type, with no cast. Use `BoardControl` in the server and the client.

review.impact: The client copies the archive rule from `personAction` in `src/board/control.ts`: only a ready or blocked ticket can be archived. A change to the rule in control.ts leaves the button visible on a ticket that the server refuses, or hidden on a ticket that the server allows.
review.fix: Export a small predicate from `board/control.ts`, for example `canArchive(column)`. Use it in `personAction` and in `TicketCard`.

review.impact: The condition `before === undefined || before === number` is written at line 68 and again in negated form at line 69. A reader must work out that the two lines agree, and an edit to one line can break the other.
review.fix: Compute `const after = before === undefined || before === number ? undefined : before` once. Look up `target` from `after`, and refuse when `after !== undefined && !target`.

review.impact: The module-level `let debug` is set by the third test and never reset. A later test that times out in `until` prints the run logs of an earlier project whose directory is already removed, or throws inside the error message.
review.fix: Pass a `debug` callback to `until` as an argument, or reset `debug = () => ''` in `afterEach`.

review.impact: The `boardControl` signature puts three parameters on one line and the closing on the same line. Prettier does not format code like this, so the file does not pass the formatter and is harder to read.
review.fix: Run the project formatter on `src/server/server.ts`.

review.impact: No test covers a ready ticket dropped on itself (`before === number`). In this case `moveRuling` drops `before` and returns `ticket.reordered` with no `before`. The fold then moves the ticket to the end of ready. A person who drops a card back on itself sends it to the bottom of the queue, and no unit test or e2e test catches this.
review.fix: Add `expect(rule(moveTo(2, 'ready', 2)))` and decide the expected result: no event, or a refusal. Then fix `moveRuling` so that a drop on itself does not reorder. Add the same case to the fold test: `reorder(2, 2)` keeps the order.

review.impact: `expect(boardEvents(werk.dir)).toBe(before)` runs right after the dialog closes. The read is synchronous, so a wrong POST sent by Cancel can reach the server after the read, and the test still passes. The 'cancel appends no event' assertion is weak.
review.fix: Wait for the network to go idle, or poll for a short time (for example `await expect.poll(() => boardEvents(werk.dir), { timeout: 500 }).toBe(before)`). Another option: archive a second ticket after the cancel and assert the count is exactly before + 1.

review.impact: The stop test checks that main did not move and that no retry exists. It does not check the new loop.ts rule: a stopped pass makes no commit and runs no checks. A regression that commits the stopped pass on the branch, or runs its checks, still passes.
review.fix: Assert that the branch of ticket 3 has no `werk build 3: pass 1` commit. Also assert that the run log or stdout has no check output for that pass. Another option: add a unit test of `buildTicket` with an aborted signal that asserts `stopped: true`, `passes: 1` and no pass commit.

review.impact: No test covers a signal that is already aborted when `runHeadless` starts (`if (options.signal?.aborted) stop()`). The `removeEventListener` cleanup also has no test. A regression that ignores an early abort lets a stopped ticket start a full agent pass.
review.fix: Add a test that calls `runHeadless` with an AbortSignal that is already aborted. Assert that the run returns stopped and that the fake agent process is not alive.

review.impact: The malformed-body test does not cover the new `BODY_LIMIT` path (413). It also does not cover `start` with a non-string root. The 'refuses and appends nothing' guarantee has no test for an oversized body.
review.fix: Add one POST with a body larger than 4096 bytes and assert status 413 and no new event. Add `post(url, 'start', { root: 1 })` and assert status 409.

review.impact: The only guard on the new write routes is the Origin check, which compares Origin with the request's own Host header, and the server never checks Host. A DNS rebinding page (attacker.example re-resolved to 127.0.0.1) sends Origin and Host that match, so the check passes. That page can then call POST /api/board/start, which spawns `werk run` in a detached process that launches coding agents in the person's repository. It can also archive tickets and stop builds. The accept route used the same pattern before, but it only appended one event. The new start control runs processes, so the cost of the gap is now much higher.
review.fix: Reject a write request unless the Host header is one the server actually listens on, such as `127.0.0.1:<port>`, `localhost:<port>` or the configured `--host` with its port. Compare Origin with that allowed list, not with the request's own Host. Put the check in one helper and use it for both boardControl and acceptFromView.

review.impact: `root` comes from the board log, where agents write plan events, and goes straight into argv as the positional before `--actor you`. If a root starts with `-` (for example `--main`), parseArgs reads it as a flag. The spawned run then gets different options, or fails with a usage error that the person never sees.
review.fix: Refuse a root that starts with `-` in the start control. You can also put a `--` end-of-options marker before the positional, if parseArgs supports one. Another option is to check the root against the same id pattern that the plan verbs use.

review.impact: readBody adds each chunk with `String(chunk)`. A multi-byte UTF-8 character split across two chunks then turns into replacement characters. The limit also counts UTF-16 code units, not bytes. Requests are at most 4 KB, so this does no harm, but the input validation is not exact.
review.fix: Collect the Buffers, check the limit with the total `byteLength`, and decode once with `Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf8')`.

review.impact: On every poll tick (default 1 s), `stopMovedBuilds` reads and folds the whole board log. Then `continue` returns to the top of the loop, where `liveTickets` reads and folds the same log again. Each tick does the full parse and fold twice, and the cost grows with the size of the log.
review.fix: Read the tickets once per iteration. Pass the result of `liveTickets` at the top of the loop to `stopMovedBuilds` on the next tick, or call `stopMovedBuilds` from the top of the loop with the `tickets` that the loop has already read.

review.impact: Each poll tick calls `Promise.race([...building.values(), poll])`. That call adds a new reaction to every pending build promise. A build that runs for a long time (30 min at 1 s polls is about 1800 ticks) keeps all of these reactions until it settles. Memory grows with the build time multiplied by `parallel`.
review.fix: Make one notifier per build and keep it for the life of the build. For example, each build resolves one shared deferred, or pushes to a queue that the loop awaits. Then race that one promise against the poll timer, and do not race every build promise on each tick.

causeOfLast.why: the worktree's dependency install was missing the vite client files, so the CLI crashed at startup; the ticket code and tests were correct, and a clean reinstall made all 513 tests pass with no code change.

review.impact: Now that `missing` also returns 2, it repeats `usage`: both print `werk ticket-check: <problem>` and return 2. The only difference is the USAGE line. If someone later changes the message prefix or the exit code in one helper and not the other, the two ways a call can stop before any check runs will behave differently.
review.fix: Define `missing` first and have `usage` reuse it, for example `const usage = (problem: string) => { const code = missing(problem); io.err(USAGE); return code }`. Keep the order so the problem line still prints before the usage line. Then the prefix and the exit code are written in one place.

review.impact: The new 'one-bad' test checks only that the bad ticket's line appears and that the exit code is 1. It would still pass if the three valid tickets copied in beside it also started failing, or if set checks fired as a side effect. So it doesn't pin down that one shape failure alone causes the exit 1.
review.fix: Also assert the summary line, e.g. expect(r.stdout).toContain('ticket-check: 4 ticket(s), 1 failed their own checks, 1 failure(s) in all'), or assert the whole stdout as the set-broken test does.

review.impact: The 'exits 2 ... never reads as a failed check' table doesn't cover a --spec path that exists but is a directory. In that case existsSync passes, readFileSync throws EISDIR, and the process probably exits 1 with a stack trace. That breaks the guarantee this test now names, and nothing catches it.
review.fix: Add a row such as [['tickets/valid', '--root', 'map', '--spec', 'tickets/valid'], 'no spec file "tickets/valid"'] and make the verb check statSync(specFile).isFile(), as it already checks the folder with isDirectory().

causeOfLast.why: the typecheck failed because files were missing from the installed dependencies (`typescript/lib/tsc.js` and others), not because of the code; after a reinstall it passes with no source change.

review.impact: If a person archives the ticket after the agent of the last pass returns but before its checks finish, which can take minutes, the loop leaves the while loop with green=true. `stopped` is only set when `!green`, so the outcome reads as green. runMergeLoop (src/build/run.ts:187) then moves the archived ticket to merging and merges its branch into main. The old code checked the person's abort signal whether or not the build was green ('nothing of it merges, even a pass that ended green'). That guarantee is gone, though the comment at run.ts:186 still claims it.
review.fix: Set `stopped: true` whenever `archive.signal.aborted` is true, green or not. Either drop `&& !green` here, or check `isArchived` once more after the loop and before returning a green outcome. Then run.ts skips the merge for any archived ticket. Add a test that archives during a slow check.

review.impact: `isArchived` runs inside a `setInterval` callback, and `readLog` throws on any line that is not valid JSON. The poll can hit a partially written append, or a log a person edited by hand. The throw escapes as an uncaught exception, so the try/finally in buildTicket never runs: the build process crashes, its worktree is not removed, and the outcome never reaches runMergeLoop. Before this change the board was read only from awaited code paths, where an error propagated normally.
review.fix: Wrap the poll body in try/catch and treat a failed read as 'not archived yet'. Or poll from an async loop whose errors are awaited, so they reach the existing error handling.

review.impact: `ticket.stopped` is gone from the event union and from the fold, but existing board logs can still contain it. Replaying such a log silently ignores the event, so a ticket a person stopped earlier shows up in building again. The merge loop then resumes it as a rebuild, which reverses the person's past decision.
review.fix: Keep a `ticket.stopped` case in the fold for old logs. Either map it to ready as before, or treat it as an archive, and note in a comment that new code no longer appends it.

review.impact: Building tickets stay draggable even though every drop of one is refused. The only point is to show the server's refusal, so the UI offers an action that cannot succeed and couples the view to a server error message.
review.fix: Limit DRAGGABLE to ready and point people to the archive control on building cards. Or, if the drag must stay to teach the rule, keep it but give it a clear UI affordance instead of relying on a round trip that always fails.

review.impact: The new `alive` helper copies `processAlive` from src/board/control.ts:36, but without the EPERM case. The repo now has two ways to check whether a process is alive, and they can drift apart.
review.fix: Import `processAlive` from src/board/control.ts in the e2e spec and delete the local `alive` function.

review.impact: The new tests type out the string 'archived by a person on the board' (also in src/cli/run.test.ts:332 and :355), but `PERSON_ARCHIVE_REASON` already holds it. If the reason changes, these fixtures go out of date without any error.
review.fix: Use `PERSON_ARCHIVE_REASON` from src/board/control.ts in these event fixtures.

review.impact: The refusal message types out the archivable columns ('ready, blocked or building') right next to the new `ARCHIVABLE` set. Adding or removing a column in the set leaves the message wrong.
review.fix: Build the list in the message from `ARCHIVABLE`, for example `[...ARCHIVABLE].join(', ')`, or put a comment that ties the two together.

review.impact: No test covers a ticket that is archived after its last pass's agent has finished but while its checks are still running, so the pass ends green. In that case `archive.signal.aborted && !green` is false, the outcome has no `stopped`, and runMergeLoop (src/build/run.ts:187 checks `built.stopped`) merges the archived ticket. The old code checked the abort signal whether or not the pass was green ('nothing of it merges, even a pass that ended green'). No test ever pinned that rule, so dropping it went unnoticed.
review.fix: Add a run test where the builder replies green and the archive event is appended before the checks finish, for example with a slow check script. Assert that main does not move and that no ticket.moved to merging is logged. Then make the loop report `stopped` whenever the archive signal fired, green or not, so the test passes.

review.impact: The rewritten archive test no longer asserts the run's exit code or the run.ended event, both of which the old test checked. A regression where the run hangs, exits 0 wrongly, or never appends run.ended after its only ticket is archived would pass.
review.fix: Keep `expect(r.code).toBe(...)` with the code the run now returns, and assert `events().at(-1)` matches `{ type: 'run.ended', payload: { root: 'root', pid: run.pid } }` with the expected stopped reason.

review.impact: The test fakes the archive by appending a raw line with a hard-coded `seq: 0` and a hand-written reason. If the log reader starts to validate or rely on seq order, the test breaks or stops reflecting what the server writes. It also does not exercise the real archive path (personAction plus appendEvent).
review.fix: Append the event the way the server does, through appendEvent with actor 'you' and PERSON_ARCHIVE_REASON, or post to the archive endpoint, instead of writing the JSON line by hand.

review.impact: The archive watch reads and parses the whole board log inside a setInterval callback. `readLog` throws on any line that is not valid JSON. That can happen when the poll catches a line the server or another writer has only half appended, or when a line in the file is corrupt. A throw in a timer callback is an uncaught exception, not a rejection of `buildTicket`. So the process dies without running the `finally` block: the worktree folder is not removed, the authoring promise is not awaited, and the agent's process group can be left running as an orphan. Before this change, the board was read in the awaited merge-loop flow, where a throw propagated through normal error handling.
review.fix: Wrap the poll body in try/catch. On a parse error, skip that tick and try again on the next one, and optionally log it through io. Do not let the error escape the timer. For example: `setInterval(() => { try { if (isArchived(o.log, o.ticket)) archive.abort() } catch { /* a partial or bad line: read again next tick */ } }, ...)`.

review.impact: Each running build now reads and parses the whole append-only board.jsonl once per poll, synchronously, and folds it with foldBoard. This happens every pollMs (1 s by default) and only to check one ticket. With `parallel` builds, the merge loop's process repeats this N times per poll. The old stopMovedBuilds did one read per poll for all builds. The board log only grows, so the cost per tick grows with the project's history. Because readFileSync and JSON.parse block the event loop, the agent stream handling and the merge loop stall on every tick.
review.fix: Read the board once per poll for all builds. For example, have runMergeLoop poll the board, check the archived numbers, and abort per-ticket controllers, which means passing a signal back into BuildOptions; standalone `werk build` keeps its own watch. Another option is to check the file's mtime/size (statSync) before re-reading, and skip the read and fold when the file has not changed since the last tick.

review.impact: After the archive is seen and the controller aborts, the interval keeps reading and folding the board every pollMs until the finally block clears it. That lasts until the agent's process group has stopped and the step author's promise has settled. Every one of those reads is wasted.
review.fix: In the interval callback, call clearInterval(watch) right after archive.abort(), or return early when archive.signal.aborted is already true.

causeOfLast.why: the code was correct; a damaged `node_modules` that the install stamp hid made the tests fail, and a clean reinstall makes all 520 pass with no code change.

grade.gap: Not verified: the grader could not get approval to run `make test`. From the code, the Makefile still installs from the lockfile with `bun install --frozen-lockfile` before `bun run test`, and the new tests (src/test/env.test.ts, src/test/scope.test.ts) start nested `bun test` runs of the fixtures under src/test/fixtures/run/. The builder should run `make test` in a fresh clone with no node_modules and confirm it passes.

Makefile: ROOT/STAMP and the `cd $(ROOT) &&` prefix on every target make each check run in the Makefile's folder when make starts elsewhere with -f. No criterion or user story asks for this (criterion-6 needs only `make test` in a fresh clone), so remove it unless it is needed for criterion-6. src/test/harness.ts serveProject: the SERVE_TIMEOUT_MS timer that kills a server after 20s without an address is also not asked for.

review.impact: makeProject now registers its own cleanup in the per-test scope, but about a dozen test files (for example src/cli/build.test.ts, src/cli/run.test.ts and src/build/merge.test.ts) still keep their own `cleanups` array, `afterEach` and `p.cleanup()` calls. There are now two cleanup paths for each project. Each project directory is removed twice: this is harmless because of `force: true`, but readers can't tell which path is the real one, and the old pattern will get copied.
review.fix: Remove the per-file `cleanups`/`afterEach`/`p.cleanup` code from the remaining test files, as was done in serve.test.ts and serve-board.test.ts. Or mark `Project.cleanup` as deprecated so that the scope is the only way cleanup happens.

review.impact: The scope is a single module-level list that is emptied after every test. A project or server created in `beforeAll` or at the top level of a file would join the first test's scope. It would be deleted or stopped after that test, while later tests still use it. Nothing does this today, but the harness gives no warning if someone does.
review.fix: Say in the doc comment that makeProject and serveProject must only be called inside a test. Or give them a separate file-level scope that is ended from a per-file `afterAll`.

review.impact: `const project = makeProject` and `const serve = serveProject` are aliases that exist only so the old call sites keep working. They are an extra layer of names to follow, and serve-board.test.ts wraps serveProject differently (`serveProject(p).url`), so the two files no longer match.
review.fix: Call makeProject and serveProject directly at the call sites, and drop the aliases.

review.impact: makeProject now adds its own removal to the test scope, and the preload ends that scope after every test. But Project.cleanup is still exported, and about a dozen test files still clean up by hand (for example src/cli/quote.test.ts:11, plan.test.ts:19, build.test.ts:16, cli.test.ts:9-14, harness.test.ts:7). So two cleanup mechanisms now run side by side. The manual one is dead weight, and readers will wonder which one is in charge. serve.test.ts and serve-board.test.ts were moved to the scope, so the codebase is now half on each mechanism.
review.fix: Delete the leftover `afterEach(() => p?.cleanup())` hooks and the `cleanups` array in cli.test.ts. Then either remove `cleanup` from the Project type, or keep it with a doc comment that says it is only for an early, explicit cleanup.

review.impact: The Bun.spawn and Bun.spawnSync wrappers cast with `as never` (four times), plus `as T` and `as typeof Bun.spawn`. This turns off type checking on the very calls that every test's subprocesses go through, so if Bun's spawn signature changes, nothing flags it at compile time.
review.fix: Write one typed helper that works for both overloads, for example `function wrap<F extends typeof Bun.spawn | typeof Bun.spawnSync>(f: F): F`, and use Bun's exported option types (`Parameters<typeof Bun.spawn>`). That way only one cast is left and it is easy to find.

review.impact: The Bun.spawn and Bun.spawnSync overrides have the same body, with only the wrapped function swapped, so a fix to one is easy to miss in the other.
review.fix: Build both from one higher-order function, for example `const defaultEnv = (f) => (a, b) => Array.isArray(a) ? f(a, withEnv(b)) : f(withEnv(a))`.

review.impact: The test that the server starts reads stdout until it sees the address with its own loop. That repeats the address-reading logic in serveProject and in e2e/harness.ts addressOf, and unlike serveProject this copy has no timeout and does not register with the test scope.
review.fix: Give serveProject an optional entry script (TEST_SERVER instead of MAIN serve), or pull the address reader out into a shared helper and use it here.

review.impact: `const project = makeProject` and `const serve = serveProject` (and the same `serve` wrapper in serve-board.test.ts:12) are pure aliases. They add a layer of indirection, and the names in these files no longer match the names in the harness.
review.fix: Call makeProject and serveProject directly (`serveProject(p).url` in serve-board.test.ts), or rename the imports with `import { makeProject as project }` if the short names are worth keeping.

review.impact: `expect(existsSync(realLog)).toBe(false)` can never fail. No test in env.fixture.ts writes to WERK_LOG, so even if WERK_LOG leaked through, this file would still not exist. The only check that really guards against a leaked WERK_LOG is the fixture's direct assertion on process.env. This line suggests extra coverage that isn't there.
review.fix: Make the fixture do something that would write to the map when WERK_LOG leaks, for example run `werk add` with no environment of its own from a project directory, and then keep this assertion. Otherwise, delete the line so the test doesn't claim more than it checks.

review.impact: The outer test only checks for '0 fail' and exit code 0. If the fixture ran fewer tests than expected (some skipped, filtered or not collected), the test would still pass, and the agent-leak and no-script checks in the fixture would silently stop running.
review.fix: Also assert the pass count, e.g. `expect(r.stderr.toString()).toContain('5 pass')`, the same way scope.test.ts checks '1 pass' and '2 fail'.

review.impact: ROOT is used unquoted in `cd $(ROOT)` in every recipe. If the checkout path contains a space or a shell metacharacter, the shell splits or interprets it, so the target fails or runs in the wrong folder.
review.fix: Quote the path in each recipe, for example `cd "$(ROOT)" && ...`. Make prerequisites cannot hold paths with spaces either, so another option is to document that the checkout path must not contain any.

causeOfLast.why: the proposed card says nothing of an archived build merges, and pass 2 returned a green outcome for an archive that came during the checks of the last pass.

grade.gap: Nothing found that falls outside the ticket. Some extra code goes with it, all of it needed to remove the drag-to-stop path (story 83 says no other move returns a building ticket to ready): the ticket.stopped event, the held field, the held filter in schedule.ts and stopMovedBuilds in run.ts are deleted. The extra check in src/build/loop.ts, where an archive that lands while a pass's checks or judges run still ends the build as stopped, also serves story 83.

No contradiction. The card's line about a ticket moving 'back to ready' no longer applies, because werk-board-control now forbids that move. The pulse and log preview end when the session ends, which the e2e test checks.

No contradiction. The builder loop reads the board every pollMs (default 1 s) and aborts the agent's signal. Of the pass that runs, it commits nothing, runs no checks and records no retry. It removes the worktree and keeps the branch, and the merge loop reads built.stopped as a person's stop (src/build/loop.ts, src/build/run.ts). One addition: an archive that lands after the agent exited still ends the build as stopped once that pass's checks finish, with nothing merged. Its checks have already run and its run record line is written, so this is consistent with 'nothing of it merges'.

review.impact: The archive watch calls `isArchived` inside a bare `setInterval` callback. `readLog` throws on any line that is not valid JSON, for example a line the server or the CLI is still appending. An error thrown there is an uncaught exception, not a rejection of `buildTicket`. That kills the whole `werk run` process with every parallel build in it, leaves worktrees behind, and never writes `run.ended`. The old poll in `runMergeLoop` ran on the loop's own await path, so an error there reached the caller.
review.fix: Wrap the poll body in try/catch and treat a failed read as 'not archived yet', since the next tick reads again. Or run the watch as an awaited async loop whose errors reach the build's `finally`.

review.impact: `ticket.stopped` was removed from the event union and from the fold, but existing `.werk/board.jsonl` files can still contain it. The fold now ignores those events silently, so a ticket a person stopped earlier goes back to `building`. The scheduler starts building columns first, so the next `werk run` restarts the build the person stopped.
review.fix: Keep reading legacy `ticket.stopped`, for example by folding it as a move back to ready, or as an archive, with a comment that it is only read for old logs. Or add a migration that rewrites old logs, and document the break.

review.impact: Each build now runs its own timer that reads and folds the whole board log every `pollMs`, and `runMergeLoop` still polls the same log. With `parallel` builds that is N+1 full re-folds of a log that only grows, every second. The archive check is also split between two modules: `run.ts` only learns of an archive through `built.stopped`.
review.fix: Acceptable for now. Better: keep a single watcher, either the merge loop passing an AbortSignal as before, or a shared board watcher, and have standalone `werk build` set up its own watcher at the CLI layer. That keeps `buildTicket` free of board polling.

review.impact: The interval starts before the `try` whose `finally` clears it. If anything between the two throws (`io.out`, or setting up `authorSteps`/`judge`), the timer keeps running and holds the process open.
review.fix: Start the interval inside the `try`, or move the `try` up so it begins right after `setInterval`.

review.impact: The changed doc comment line runs well past the line width used everywhere else in the file. The same happens at `web/src/BoardView.tsx:14`. It hurts readability and does not match the surrounding comments.
review.fix: Rewrap both comment paragraphs to the file's usual width.

review.impact: This adds a fifth copy of the pid liveness check. Copies already exist as `processAlive` in src/board/control.ts, `alive` in src/build/session-file.ts:40, src/cli/serve-board.test.ts:76 and src/cli/run.test.ts:312. The copies can drift apart, for example if one of them starts treating EPERM as alive.
review.fix: Import `processAlive` from '../src/board/control.ts', the same way BoardView already imports `ARCHIVABLE` from it, and delete the local `alive` function.

review.impact: The two new tests repeat the same code in both places: the `Bun.spawn` of `main.ts build 3 --cap 2`, the hand-written `ticket.archived` record, and the `writeFileSync` append to board.jsonl. A change to the board record shape or to the spawn has to be made twice.
review.fix: Move the shared code into helpers in this file: `spawnBuild(args)` for the spawn and `archiveByPerson(number)` for the append. Use them in both tests.

review.impact: The edited doc comment was not reflowed. One line now runs far past the width of the lines around it. web/src/BoardView.tsx:14 has the same problem. The comment is harder to read and doesn't match the wrapping used elsewhere.
review.fix: Rewrap both comment paragraphs to the same line width as the surrounding lines.

review.impact: This test used to check the run's exit code (1) and its final run.ended event. The rewrite drops both checks and adds nothing in their place. When a person archives the only ticket in a subtree, runMergeLoop exits the loop, finds no live tickets left, and falls through to openG2 on the unchanged main. That path could report G2 open, with exit 0 and run.ended without `stopped`, even though nothing merged. No test pins what should happen there.
review.fix: Assert `r.code` and `events().at(-1)` (run.ended with the expected `stopped` reason, or not). That fixes the outcome of a run whose only ticket was archived mid-build.

review.impact: The title says 'a drag back to ready is no stop', but the test never makes a drag or a move to ready. It only checks that no ticket.moved-to-ready event exists, and that holds trivially after an archive. The title claims coverage the test does not have.
review.fix: Either drop that clause from the title, or append a person ticket.moved to ready before the archive and assert that the builder is still alive.

review.impact: The check sleeps for 2s and the default poll is 1000ms, so the interval almost always aborts during the checks. As a result, the final `isArchived(o.log, o.ticket)` read after the last poll in loop.ts is never what the test depends on. If that fallback were removed, this test would still pass.
review.fix: Add a case where the archive lands after the last poll tick, for example with a very large `pollMs` (if it can be configured) or with a check that appends the archive itself just before the pass ends green. Then assert that the outcome is stopped.

review.impact: Restoring an archived building ticket is only checked for its column and the missing data-live attribute. No test shows that a later run resumes it as a rebuild, using the kept branch or main, without failing. A regression in how a restored building ticket is picked up would go unnoticed.
review.fix: In run.test.ts, after the restore, start `werk run root` again and assert that the builder for ticket 3 launches, and that the ticket goes on to merge or behaves as intended.

review.impact: The archive watcher runs `isArchived` inside a `setInterval` callback. `isArchived` calls `readLog`, which throws on any line that is not valid JSON. The board log is appended to all the time by the server, the merge loop and other builds, so a poll can catch a line half-written, or hit a corrupt line. A throw inside a timer callback is an uncaught exception, not a rejection of `buildTicket`, so the build process crashes. The `finally` never runs, the worktree is left on disk, and the builder agent's process group can keep running with no parent. The old code read the board in the merge loop's async path, where a throw became a caught rejection.
review.fix: Wrap the poll so that a log that cannot be read does not crash the process, for example `try { if (isArchived(o.log, o.ticket)) archive.abort() } catch { /* read again on the next poll */ }`. Also guard the final `isArchived` call after the loop, or let `isArchived` skip a torn last line.

review.impact: Each running build now starts its own `setInterval`, and every tick calls `isArchived`. That reads the whole append-only board.jsonl synchronously, JSON-parses every line and folds the full board, all to check one ticket number. Before this change the run loop read the board once per poll for all builds. Now there are `parallel` extra full reads, parses and folds every `pollMs` (1s by default), on top of the run loop's own poll. The cost grows with log size times parallelism. Because the work is synchronous, it also blocks the event loop that is streaming agent output and running checks.
review.fix: Keep a single board read per poll. One way: the run loop's existing poll checks for archived tickets (it already calls `liveTickets`) and aborts an AbortController that it passes to `buildTicket`. The interval stays only for the standalone `werk build` path. Another way: make the check cheap, e.g. skip the read when the board file's mtime or size hasn't changed since the last check, or scan only the bytes appended since the last offset for a `ticket.archived` event with this number instead of folding the whole log.

review.impact: Once the signal has aborted, the interval keeps re-reading and re-folding the board every tick until the `finally` block clears it. The loop may still be finishing checks or judges at that point, so this can be several seconds of wasted work. After the loop, line ~219 calls `isArchived` again even when `archive.signal.aborted` is already true. The `||` short-circuits there, which is fine, but the interval itself does not.
review.fix: Stop polling on the first hit. Call `clearInterval(watch)` right after `archive.abort()`, or guard with `if (!archive.signal.aborted && isArchived(...))`.

review.impact: The e2e harness has its own copy of the launch-log parsing (read the file, split on newlines, JSON.parse each line, take argv). src/test/harness.ts already does this with jsonLines and launches(). The fake agent's log format is now read in two places. If the format changes, for example to add a field or rename argv, both copies need the same edit, and they can drift apart without anyone noticing.
review.fix: Export the reader of the fake agent's launch log from src/test/harness.ts, either jsonLines or a small readAgentLaunches(path) helper. Then have e2e/harness.ts import it, the same way it already imports FakeScript from src/test/fake-agent.ts.

review.impact: The e2e harness now has its own copy of the launch-log parsing that src/test/harness.ts already does in `launches()`: read the JSONL file, split it into lines, drop the empty ones and JSON.parse each one into `{ argv }`. If the log format changes, both copies must be updated, and they can drift apart without anyone noticing.
review.fix: Move the parsing into one small exported helper (for example `readLaunchLog(path): { argv: string[] }[]` beside the fake agent or in src/test/harness.ts) and call it from both harnesses.

review.impact: The new test 'the fake agent exits with its scripted code after its last step' largely overlaps the test just above it, 'the fake agent exits with its scripted code', and the next new test, which also checks event/edit/event ordering. That leaves three nearly identical tests to maintain for one behaviour.
review.fix: Merge the exit-code check after steps into the existing scripted-exit-code test, or drop the stdout and file assertions here because the gated ordering test already covers them.

review.impact: The test 'plays an event, an edit and a second event in order' never fails without the fake-agent.ts:129 change, which waits for each event line to be written. The waitFor gate holds the agent after the first event, and its Bun.sleep polling yields to the event loop, so the buffered line is flushed anyway. The edit also always lands before the 'second' event no matter how stdout is flushed. If someone reverted the awaited write, events could again be read only after a later edit has already happened, and this test would still pass.
review.fix: Remove the gate and run the steps back to back as event → edit → event. Then assert that the reader saw 'first' while edited.txt was still missing, which only the awaited write makes reliable. Or give it an ordering that only the flush guarantees, such as an event followed by a synchronous edit of a file the reader checks. If you keep the gate, rename the test and change its comment so it doesn't claim to cover the flush ordering.

review.impact: The new 'no script installed' test covers only the branch at line 68, where the file is missing, because makeProject always sets WERK_FAKE_AGENT_SCRIPT. The branch where WERK_FAKE_AGENT_SCRIPT is unset, with its new message, is never run. A regression there, such as reading an undefined path and crashing with some other exit code, would go unnoticed.
review.fix: Add a case to harness.test.ts that runs claude with WERK_FAKE_AGENT_SCRIPT removed from p.env. Assert exit code 64, a stderr containing 'no script is installed', and empty stdout.

review.impact: 'exits with its scripted code after its last step' mostly repeats the existing 'exits with its scripted code' test and the new ordering test. It doesn't check that the exit code comes only after every step has run, because a fake that exited early with code 5 would fail the done.txt check for a different reason. So it adds little beyond the tests next to it.
review.fix: Either merge it into the existing exit-code test or make the final step observable on its own terms, for example by asserting the last event is present. As written, the stdout check already does this, so the cheapest fix is to fold it into one test.

causeOfLast.why: this ticket's browser harness wrote its own `claude` script, but the main line had moved that into the shared `writeFakeAgent` helper in the meantime.

review.impact: The e2e harness parses the fake agent's launch log in its own way, and src/test/harness.ts already does the same through its `jsonLines` helper. The record shape `{ argv, role, pid }` is defined by what src/test/fake-agent.ts writes, so the two harnesses now each keep their own copy of that format. If the log format changes, both parsers must be updated or they will drift apart.
review.fix: Export a small reader from the src/test side, such as `readAgentLaunches(path): { argv: string[]; role?: string; pid: number }[]` placed next to `writeFakeAgent` in fake-bin.ts or in fake-agent.ts's module. Then have both harnesses call it, as they already share `writeFakeAgent` and `FakeScript`.

review.impact: The new early guard `if (!existsSync(scriptPath)) fail(64, 'no script is installed at ...')` repeats the existing check at line 85 word for word, and both cite #werk-test-external. The line 85 check can no longer fire, so it is dead code, and the two copies can drift apart if one is edited later.
review.fix: Delete the check and its comment at lines 84–85, and keep the single guard at lines 65–68 next to the WERK_FAKE_AGENT_SCRIPT check.

review.impact: `agentLaunches` re-implements by hand the JSONL parsing that src/test/harness.ts already does with `jsonLines<{ argv: string[] ... }>(launchLog)` (line 100). The two harnesses now read the fake agent's launch-log format in two places, so a change to the log format has to be made twice.
review.fix: Export `jsonLines` (or an `agentLaunchesFrom(launchLog)` helper) from src/test/harness.ts and call it from e2e/harness.ts. That way the launch-log format is read in one place only.

review.impact: The new test 'exits with its scripted code after its last step' mostly repeats the existing 'exits with its scripted code' test. Its event-order and edit checks also overlap with the next new test, 'plays an event, an edit and a second event in order'. That makes three tests covering nearly the same behaviour.
review.fix: Merge the new exit-code check into the existing 'exits with its scripted code' test, for example by giving that test's script some steps before the exit, and let the ordering test cover the event and edit sequence.

review.impact: Undoing the change doesn't make this test fail. The `waitFor` gate after the first event already sleeps with `Bun.sleep`, and that sleep lets stdout flush. So the test passes against the old fire-and-forget `process.stdout.write` too. It checks step order, but it doesn't guard the new code in fake-agent.ts:131 that awaits the write before the next step runs. The `second: true` check can't fail either, because the edit always runs before the second event.
review.fix: Say in the test that it checks step order only, not that a write is flushed before the next step. Or add a case with no gate where many large events come before the edit, which only passes when each write is awaited. If that can't be made deterministic, leave out the claim that the await is tested.
