review.impact: This test mostly repeats 'the fake agent exits with its scripted code' and the order test below it. If the scripted exit code broke, several tests would fail at once without saying anything new.
review.fix: Merge it into the existing exit-code test, or drop the stdout and edit checks that the order test already makes.

grade.gap: Minor: src/test/fake-agent.test.ts tests 'a denial on the input channel settles the ask with an error tool result' and 'an input channel that closes with no answer settles the ask with a denial' cover behaviour that #werk-test-fake-ask-open-settle asks for (error tool result on deny, deny on input close), not this ticket's criteria or stories. The implementation needs that behaviour anyway, so it is tolerable, but those two tests could go to the settle ticket.

The card says the turn ends at the first scripted result event. src/test/fake-agent.ts keeps playing the steps after that first result: endTurn is called again on any later result, and other events still print. That is harmless, but it does not match the card, which ends the turn at the first result.

review.impact: Every `{ sleep: n }` step now sleeps n + 20 ms, and this changes every existing script too (build.test.ts, run.test.ts, serve-board.test.ts). A script no longer means what it says. A caller that sets a pause just above or below an overseer or cancel limit gets a different pause from the one it wrote. The extra 20 ms is there to absorb timer jitter, but that is the test's job, not the fake's.
review.fix: Make the fake sleep exactly `step.sleep`. In the tests that measure silence, allow for jitter in the assertion instead: lower the bound, or check against the sleep value minus a small margin.

review.impact: When `inputEnd` wins the race in `openAsk`, the `look` closure that `nextInput` registered stays in `onInput` and never resolves. The same happens for asks that are never answered. It costs little in a short-lived process, but the wait helper now cleans up after itself on only one of its paths.
review.fix: Give `nextInput` a way to cancel its wait, such as an AbortSignal or a returned unsubscribe function, and remove the `look` when the input closes. Another option is to have `nextInput` itself resolve to `undefined` on `inputEnd`.

review.impact: Every `sleep` step now silently lasts 20 ms longer than the script says. Scripts across the suite no longer mean what they say, and the test at src/test/fake-agent.test.ts:136 checks this padding rather than the pause. A reader of a script such as `{ sleep: 100 }` cannot tell that the real wait is 120 ms unless they find the note in the header comment.
review.fix: Give the `+ 20` a name, such as `const SLEEP_MARGIN_MS = 20`, and say in that comment why it exists (timer jitter). Better still, sleep exactly as long as the script asks and let the tests assert `>= step.sleep` with their own tolerance.

review.impact: `startWithInput` copies the code that spawns the agent and splits its stdout into JSON lines, which already exists in src/test/harness.test.ts:68-80. This file also repeats `r.stdout.trim().split('\n').map(JSON.parse)` three times (lines 105, 115, 123). A later change to how events are framed has to be made in every copy.
review.fix: Move a helper into harness.ts, such as `streamAgent(p, args, onLine)` together with an `events(stdout)` parser, and use it from both test files.

review.impact: The fake pads every sleep by 20 ms so that a test 'never measures a shorter silence' than the script asks for. This assertion checks for >= 120 ms on a 100 ms sleep, so the test uses up that padding itself. The gap is measured from when the test reads line 0, not from when the fake wrote it. If the test process reads line 0 late under load, the measured gap drops below 120 ms and the test fails even though the fake behaved correctly. The test can fail at random.
review.fix: Assert the scripted duration (`toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(100)`) so the 20 ms padding absorbs reader lag. The test still fails if the fake waits for the answer, because it would hang.

review.impact: Same problem: the test asserts that a 100 ms sleep shows a gap of at least 120 ms, measured on the reading side. The gap can only shrink when the reader is slow, so the test fails at random under CI load. It also tests the padding itself rather than the promise the padding is meant to keep: that a test never sees less than the scripted silence.
review.fix: Assert `>= 100`. If the padding needs its own test, measure the time between the two writes inside the fake (for example, with timestamps in the events) instead of on the reading side.

review.impact: No test covers two asks open at once, or an answer whose request_id matches no open ask. The new `onInput` Set and the `seen` offset in `nextInput` exist to match each answer to the right ask. If a regression settled the wrong ask or both asks from one answer, every current test would still pass.
review.fix: Add a test with two asks (r1, r2) that answers r2 with allow and r1 with deny, in that order. Assert that each tool_result has the right `tool_use_id` and `is_error`, and that the result comes only after both.

review.impact: If the fake ever regresses to waiting for the answer, this test shows a generic bun timeout instead of a clear assertion failure. The spawned agent also keeps running after the test fails, because nothing kills it.
review.fix: Race `lines` against a short timer that kills `agent` and fails with a clear message, or kill the agent in `afterEach`.

grade.gap: Extra behaviour: when a chat script gives one reply, or fewer replies than messages, src/test/fake-agent.ts turnReply plays the last reply again for every later message. The test 'a chat agent with one reply plays it for every message' in src/test/fake-agent.test.ts covers it. No criterion or story asks for this, so it is minor. Remove it, or tie it to criterion-3, if it is not wanted.

review.impact: roleOf treats a '<name>-' prefix as an area of every role, but only the reviewer has areas. So a name like 'chat-foo' or 'builder-x' resolves to that role, and 'chat-foo' would quietly get a conversation lifetime. This contradicts the test's claim that a name that only starts with a role name is not that role.
review.fix: Allow the area suffix only for the reviewer. For example, add an `areas: true` flag to the reviewer entry and check it in roleOf, or match only `name.startsWith(`${ROLES.reviewer.name}-`)` as the special case.

review.impact: The test helper still hardcodes the 'WERK_AGENT_ROLE' literal, even though this change adds ROLE_ENV and roleEnv to remove that literal everywhere else. If the variable is ever renamed, these tests would set the wrong variable without any error.
review.fix: Use `{ ...p.env, ...roleEnv(role) }` imported from '../agent/roles.ts'.

review.impact: The diff adds `roleEnv` and `ROLE_ENV` so the role variable is named in one place. This new helper still writes the literal `WERK_AGENT_ROLE: role`, so renaming the variable would leave the test using the old name without any error.
review.fix: Build the env with `{ ...p.env, ...roleEnv(role) }` from `../agent/roles.ts`.

review.impact: The parameter type `typeof ROLES.specWriter.name | typeof ROLES.ticketWriter.name` is long and repeats the role table inside a signature. That makes the line hard to read, and adding another writer means editing it again.
review.fix: Declare `type WriterRole = (typeof ROLES)['specWriter' | 'ticketWriter']['name']` once, or pass the role entry (`role: AgentRole`) and use `role.name`.

review.impact: There are now two ways to pick a reply from a list. `nthReply` counts launches in a file on disk, while `turnReply` counts turns and repeats the last reply. They differ in how they handle an empty list and the end of the list, so a reader has to work out which rules apply to which lifetime.
review.fix: Move the shared check (a non-empty list, clamp to the last reply) into one helper that takes an index, and keep only the index source different (launch counter or turn number).

review.impact: No test covers the documented exit code of a chat agent: 'exits when its input closes, with the code of the last reply it played'. Every chat test uses replies that exit 0. If the code were wrongly taken from the first reply, or always set to 0, the tests would still pass.
review.fix: Script the chat role with replies that have different exit codes, for example [{steps:[said('R1'),done],exit:2},{steps:[said('R2'),done],exit:7}]. Send two messages, close stdin, and assert `await agent.exited` is 7.

review.impact: No test checks that a list of chat replies repeats its last entry once the list runs out. The list test sends exactly as many messages as there are replies. Neither the Math.min clamp in turnReply nor the empty-list failure (exit 64, 'empty list of replies') is tested, so a bad index would go unnoticed.
review.fix: Send three messages against a two-reply list and expect ['R1','result','R2','result','R2','result']. Add a test where `roles: { chat: [] }` exits 64 and stderr contains 'empty list of replies'.

review.impact: One-pass behaviour changed without a test. A one-pass agent used to wait for the prompt with nextInput. Now nextUserMessage also resolves to null when stdin closes first, so the agent plays its reply even though no prompt arrived. Separately, a chat-role launch with no --input-format falls through to the one-pass path. Both paths are untested, so a regression in either would go unseen.
review.fix: Add a test that starts a builder with --input-format stream-json, closes stdin without sending a prompt, and asserts the chosen behaviour (exit code and events). Add one that runs the chat role without an input channel and asserts it plays one reply and exits.

causeOfLast.why: the two tests counted text boxes on the whole page, from before the chat pane was required to be on screen at all times, so the chat's own message box made them fail.

grade.gap: These behaviours go beyond the criteria and stories 41/42/44. (1) The end-of-turn line shows duration and cost: EndLine in web/src/ChatPane.tsx, the `.end` text '2.4s · $0.03' asserted in e2e/chat.spec.ts, and the duration/cost carried by the 'end' part in src/chat/parts.ts. (2) The '○ waits for the reply above' marker for a queued message: `waits` in src/chat/transcript.ts and TurnView in ChatPane.tsx. (3) Tool-call lines '⚙ <name>': the 'tool' part in parts.ts and the block in TurnView. (4) The e2e test 'Shift+Enter starts a new line and sends nothing'. (5) The synchronizer token, the werk-token meta tag and the loopback Host check on /api/chat: `untrusted` and the Vite plugin in src/server/server.ts, plus the 403 cases in serve-chat.test.ts. Some request guard is defensible because this route starts an agent. Items (1)-(4) are display extras: remove them, or leave them to the tickets that own #werk-progress, #werk-pane and #werk-fullerr.

The card says werk spawns its own claude child 'with the same flags' as Conductor: --output-format stream-json --input-format stream-json --verbose --thinking adaptive --thinking-display. CHAT_ARGS in src/chat/conversations.ts leaves out '--thinking adaptive --thinking-display' and adds '--include-partial-messages --permission-mode auto'. The added flags are needed for streaming and come from #werk-perm-mode. Either add the thinking flags or say in the comment why they are left out.

review.impact: Each stdout and stderr chunk is decoded with its own `new TextDecoder().decode(chunk)`. When a multi-byte UTF-8 character (such as the '—' that turnText itself writes, accented text or an emoji) falls across two chunks, both halves become U+FFFD. The reply text in the transcript and the quoted stderr in exit errors are then silently corrupted.
review.fix: Make one TextDecoder per stream outside the loop and call `decoder.decode(chunk, { stream: true })`. After the stdout loop ends, flush with `decoder.decode()` and hand any non-empty `rest` to `deliver`.

review.impact: The new header comment says every request that starts an agent carries the synchronizer token and passes the loopback Host rule. But `POST /api/board/start`, which spawns the run verb and so the builder agents, still goes through `boardControl` with only the Origin check. The written trust boundary and the code disagree, and two different trust mechanisms now guard routes that start agents.
review.fix: Run `untrusted(trust, req)` in `boardControl` for the `start` control, and have the board page send the `x-werk-token` header. Or, if that belongs in a later ticket, narrow the comment so it names only `/api/chat`.

review.impact: `readBody` was written for 4 KB bodies and now takes up to 300 MB. It does this with `text += String(chunk)`: repeated string concatenation at that size costs a lot of memory and CPU. `String(chunk)` also splits multi-byte characters at chunk edges, and `text.length` counts UTF-16 units, not bytes.
review.fix: Collect the chunks as Buffers, track their total `byteLength` against the limit, then `Buffer.concat(...).toString('utf8')` once before `JSON.parse`.

review.impact: ChatPane opens its own `EventSource('/api/events')`. The graph `useLive` that this change moved into App opens another, and BoardPage's `useLive` adds more on the board. Each SSE stream holds an HTTP/1.1 connection, and browsers allow about 6 per origin. Each new live consumer moves the page closer to stalled fetches, and every copy receives every event.
review.fix: Share one EventSource for the page, for example a small context or module-level hub that `useLive` and ChatPane subscribe to by event name.

review.impact: The `[Image #N]` tokens are numbered from `images.length` when the paste happens, but the images are only added to the list after FileReader finishes. If the person pastes twice before the first read completes, both pastes get the same numbers. The tokens in the text then point at the wrong files.
review.fix: Reserve the slots in the list at once, for example with a pending entry or a ref counter updated synchronously in `onPaste`, and fill in the data when the read finishes.

review.impact: ChatPane opens its own EventSource on /api/events, while useLive (web/src/useLive.ts:30) already opens one for every live view. The page now holds two SSE connections to one channel. Opening the channel, parsing events and cleaning up are written twice, so a change to how the client reconnects or handles events has to be made in both places.
review.fix: Pull one shared event-channel hook or module out of useLive, for example useLiveEvent(name, handler), on a single EventSource. Have both useLive and ChatPane subscribe through it.

review.impact: The fake-agent reply builders `stream` and `reply` and the input decoder `textOf` are written again almost word for word in e2e/chat.spec.ts:7-14. A change to the stream-json shape the fake agent emits has to be copied by hand into both suites.
review.fix: Export `streamStep`, `textReply(...pieces)` and `inputText(message)` from src/test/fake-agent.ts, which already owns FakeStep and FakeReply. Import them in both test files.

review.impact: The new `jsonLines` reader repeats the JSONL parsing that src/test/harness.ts already does (around line 53) for the same launch and input logs. agentRuns also repeats the pid join that agentInputs does there. The e2e and unit harnesses can drift on how they read the fake agent's logs.
review.fix: Move the JSONL reader and the pid-to-inputs join into a shared module under src/test/ next to fake-agent.ts, and use it from both harnesses.

review.impact: `withPart(blocks, part, turn)` takes `blocks` as well as `turn`, but every caller passes `turn.blocks`. The extra parameter means a reader has to check whether the two can ever differ, and they can't.
review.fix: Change the signature to `withPart(turn, part)` and read `turn.blocks` inside the function.

review.impact: The test 'an ended turn that never started does not wait' forces `started: false` by hand after `received`, because `received` always sets `started: true`. The test checks a state the code never produces, so it only tests `waits` in isolation while its name says it covers the fold.
review.fix: Either test `waits({ id: 'a', text: 'A', images: 0, started: false, blocks: [], end: { kind: 'end', error: 'refused' } })` directly under a name that says so, or drop it, since the fold can't produce that state.

review.impact: The error text hardcodes '20 MB' even though IMAGE_LIMIT_BYTES is defined two lines above it. CHAT_BODY_LIMIT in src/server/server.ts:60 is also hardcoded as 300 MB rather than derived from MAX_IMAGES and IMAGE_LIMIT_BYTES. If either limit changes, the message and the body cap silently go out of step with it.
review.fix: Build the message from IMAGE_LIMIT_BYTES / (1024 * 1024). Define CHAT_BODY_LIMIT as a value derived from MAX_IMAGES * IMAGE_LIMIT_BYTES * 4 / 3 plus some headroom for the text.

review.impact: No test covers what the page shows when a send fails. That includes a 403 or 400 from /api/chat, a network error, and a child that exits, which shows as `.end.error` in EndLine. The server tests check that the error event is emitted, but nothing checks that the person sees it. A regression in `fail()` or in EndLine's error branch would leave a turn that looks like it is still waiting, and no test would catch it.
review.fix: Add an e2e test in e2e/chat.spec.ts. Script a chat reply of `{ steps: [{ crash: 3 }] }`, send a message, and assert that the turn's `.end.error` text contains 'the agent exited with code 3'. Add a second case that sends with a wrong token: overwrite the werk-token meta with page.evaluate before pressing Enter, then assert that the 403 message shows in the turn.

review.impact: The rule that the board keeps the card the map showed last (`lastCard`) has no test. The e2e tests only send from the map view. If the board view sent no card, or the wrong one, every test would still pass.
review.fix: Add an e2e test: open #map-hash, go to the board with the nav link, and assert the chip still reads #map-hash. Then send a message and assert that the request body has card: 'map-hash' and that the agent's first input line is '[the map is now at #map-hash…'.

review.impact: `imageProblem` is a pure validator, and only one of its rejection branches is tested: a disallowed MIME type, through the server test. Nothing checks that bad base64 is refused or that the 20 MB limit holds, and nothing checks the over-10-images limit in server.ts. A broken regex or a wrong size calculation would pass every test.
review.fix: Add src/chat/attachments.test.ts with unit cases for `imageProblem`: each allowed type passes; non-base64 data such as 'a b!' is refused; data just over IMAGE_LIMIT_BYTES*4/3 characters is refused and data at the limit passes; null and {} are refused. In serve-chat.test.ts, add a request with 11 small images and expect 400.

review.impact: The server's header comment promises that the token goes into no agent environment. No test checks this, so a later change that passes process.env plus the token to the child would go unnoticed.
review.fix: Have the fake agent's launch log record whether any environment value equals the token, or record the env keys and values. Then, after a successful chat turn, assert that no env value of the chat child contains `s.token`.

review.impact: The test overwrites `started: false` after `received`. `received` always sets started to true, so the test checks a state the fold never produces, and it would pass even if `waits` ignored `end`. The real case, an error end on a turn that was sent and never started (the path `fail()` takes), is checked only indirectly.
review.fix: Assert on the real fold instead: `expect(waits(received(sent([], {id:'a',text:'A'}), 'a', {kind:'end', error:'refused'})[0]!)).toBe(false)`. If `waits` must also be checked against `end` alone, build the Turn literal directly instead of spreading a fold result.

review.impact: Every server and e2e test uses the single tab 'main', so nothing tests that conversations are separated by tab: one child per tab, with parts routed to the right tab. A bug that shared one child across tabs would pass.
review.fix: In serve-chat.test.ts, send turns on tabs 'main' and 'other'. Assert that agentLaunches() has length 2 and that each event's tab matches the tab its turn was sent on.

review.impact: The token and loopback-Host checks guard only POST /api/chat. GET /api/events has neither, and it now broadcasts the full chat transcript to every subscriber: agent replies that may quote repository code or secrets, tool names, and up to 4000 characters of the child's stderr in exit errors. A DNS-rebinding page (Host: evil.example resolving to 127.0.0.1) can open the event stream and read every conversation as it happens, even though it cannot send messages.
review.fix: Apply the loopback-Host rule from untrusted() to /api/events, and ideally to every route, whenever trust.loopback is set. Or require the token on the chat event stream, for example as a query parameter, since EventSource cannot set headers.

review.impact: `card` is checked only to be a string. It goes word for word into the first line of the agent's turn (`[the map is now at #${id}]`). A value holding `]` or newlines can fake the context line or add extra lines in front of the agent, and the length is limited only by the 300 MB body cap.
review.fix: Check `card` against a card-id pattern (like NAME, or the map's id rule), or refuse a card that the graph does not contain.

review.impact: Pasted screenshots can hold sensitive content. They are written with the default umask, usually 0644, so other local users can read them.
review.fix: Create the attachments folder with mode 0o700 and write each file with `{ mode: 0o600 }`.

review.impact: Each stdout chunk is joined onto the unfinished line (`rest`), and then the whole string is split again. A stream-json line can be very large: a verbose tool_result or assistant event that carries the contents of a file can run to megabytes. For such a line the parser copies and rescans the growing string on every 64 KB chunk, so the cost grows with the square of the line length. All of this runs on the server's event loop. The code also creates a new TextDecoder per chunk without `{stream: true}`, so a multibyte character split across two chunks is also decoded wrongly.
review.fix: Keep one `TextDecoder` per child and call `decode(chunk, { stream: true })`. Look for '\n' only in the new chunk. Collect the pieces of an unfinished line in an array and join them only when a newline arrives, or use a line reader that buffers each byte once. Apply the same TextDecoder fix to the stderr reader on line 71.

review.impact: ChatPane opens its own EventSource to /api/events. App now also keeps a `useLive('/api/graph')` connection open, and BoardPage keeps a third one. A page now holds 2–3 SSE connections that never close, where it used to hold one. Browsers allow 6 HTTP/1.1 connections per origin. With two werk tabs open on the board, all 6 are used, and new requests such as POST /api/chat, /api/graph fetches and board controls stall with no error. The server also writes every chat delta to every one of these connections, including the ones that ignore `chat` events.
review.fix: Share one EventSource for the page: a module-level singleton or a context that hands listeners to useLive and ChatPane. Each consumer then adds its own `addEventListener` to that connection instead of opening a new one.

review.impact: `useLive('/api/graph')` moved up into App, so the whole graph is now fetched and refetched on every `changed` event while the board view is showing, where it was not fetched before. The board view now refetches two full folds on each change.
review.fix: Accept this if the chat's card links need the graph on the board. Otherwise fetch the graph only when it is needed, for example only node ids for hrefOf, or only while the map view or the chat transcript is showing.

review.impact: `live.data?.nodes ?? []` makes a new array on every render until the graph loads. `useHrefOf` therefore returns a new function each time, which invalidates the `useMemo` in every `Markdown` of the transcript and re-renders all reply Markdown on every render during that time.
review.fix: Use a constant module-level empty array as the fallback, e.g. `const NO_NODES: MapNode[] = []`.

review.impact: Every chat message reads and folds the whole map log (`graphOf(readLog(logPath))`) only to look up one card's title. The cost grows with the size of the log on each message.
review.fix: Find the title from a cached graph that is rebuilt only when the log watcher reports a change, or stop scanning at the first event that names the card.

review.impact: `storeImage` writes each image with blocking `writeFileSync`. One request can carry up to 10 images of 20 MB each, so it can block the server's event loop, including SSE delivery, while about 200 MB is decoded and written.
review.fix: Use `fs.promises.writeFile` (and `mkdir`) and await the writes in `chat()`.

playwright.config.ts sets testMatch to '.werk-heldout/**/*.spec.ts', so the runner finds only held-out files named *.spec.ts. Nothing tells the binder to use that suffix: src/heldout/set.ts never mentions spec, playwright or e2e. A held-out browser test named like x.test.ts or x.ts would be skipped, and Playwright reports 'No tests found' and goes red, which is what this card exists to stop. Widen the held-out pattern to '.werk-heldout/**/*.@(spec|test).?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)', or tell the binder in src/heldout/set.ts to name its browser tests *.spec.ts.

review.impact: The path to the CLI entry point (`join(import.meta.dir, '..', 'cli', 'main.ts')`) now exists in two places: here and in `MAIN` in src/server/run.ts. If main.ts moves or is renamed, one copy may be updated and the other missed. A stale copy in the agent instructions would make the chat agent run a command that does not exist, and nothing would fail loudly.
review.fix: Export the entry-point path once (for example `export const MAIN = join(import.meta.dir, '..', 'cli', 'main.ts')` in werk-cli.ts or a small shared module). Build `WERK` from it and have src/server/run.ts import it.

review.impact: `werkCommand` puts the runtime and path in double quotes but does not escape characters that are special inside double quotes (`"`, `$`, backtick, `\`). An install path that contains any of them gives the agent a shell command that is broken or that expands to something else. The doc comment says the result is quoted, so callers will assume it is shell-safe.
review.fix: Use single quotes and escape embedded single quotes, e.g. `const q = (s: string) => `'${s.replace(/'/g, `'\''`)}'``. Alternatively, keep the current approach and change the doc comment to say plainly that paths with shell metacharacters are not supported.

review.impact: The entry-point path `join(import.meta.dir, '..', 'cli', 'main.ts')` is now written out separately here and in src/server/run.ts:11 (`MAIN`). Both files spawn the same werk command line. If the entry point moves, one of the two copies can be left pointing at the old path.
review.fix: Export the path once, for example as `MAIN` from src/agent/werk-cli.ts, and build `WERK` from it. Then have src/server/run.ts import that path instead of computing its own.

review.impact: The test reads `argv[argv.indexOf('--append-system-prompt') + 1]` before it checks that the flag is present. If the flag is missing, indexOf returns -1 and the read silently picks up argv[0]. The `toContain` assertion that comes next is the only thing guarding this, so the order is misleading.
review.fix: Move `expect(argv).toContain('--append-system-prompt')` above the line that reads the prompt.

review.impact: The self-contained check only rejects card ids that start with a fixed list of prefixes (werk, vi, st, lp, pr, al). If the text later cites a werk card with any other prefix, the test still passes. So it does not really check that the text cites no card of werk's own map.
review.fix: Write down which ids the text is allowed to show: the made-up examples (#order-export, #orders, #order-format, #x, #y, #z). Then assert that every `#[a-z][\w-]*` match in the text is in that list.

review.impact: The integration assertion only checks the pattern `"..." "...main.ts" show <id>`. If WERK pointed at the wrong main.ts, such as a wrong relative join from src/agent, the test would still pass. The command would then fail when an agent runs it.
review.fix: Import WERK and assert `prompt` contains `${WERK} show <id>`. Also add a unit check that the second quoted path in WERK resolves to an existing file, e.g. `existsSync(join(import.meta.dir, '..', 'cli', 'main.ts'))`, or check it against the path parsed out of WERK.

review.impact: The command is wrapped in double quotes but nothing inside is escaped (see `werkCommand` in `src/agent/instructions.ts`). The agent pastes this command into its system prompt and later runs it in a shell. If the runtime path or the install path contains `"`, `$`, a backtick or `\`, the shell expands it or splits it, and the command fails or runs something else. Both paths come from the local install (`process.execPath` and `import.meta.dir`), not from a user, so the risk is low.
review.fix: Make the quoting safe for a POSIX shell: wrap each part in single quotes and replace every `'` inside with `'\''`. Add a test with a path that contains a space, `$` and a quote.

causeOfLast.why: pass 1 wrote a local variable that shadowed a function and listed an extra effect dependency, and the lint rules flag both clearly.

grade.gap: Minor, may stay: e2e/reload.spec.ts adds a second test ('a client change that Vite applies in place reaches the page with no reload'). No criterion asks for it, but story 109 covers it. src/cli/verbs/serve.ts also logs a separate message for a reload that comes while the server is still starting ('reloaded the code while the server starts...'). review.impact: The page now opens a third EventSource to /api/events. useLive.ts and ChatPane.tsx already open one each. Under HTTP/1.1 a browser allows 6 connections per origin, so each tab now keeps 3 of them open. Two werk tabs fill the limit and stall every other request. The reload handling also sits apart from the live-channel code it belongs with.
review.fix: Listen for `reload` on the EventSource that useLive.ts already opens, or share one EventSource module that both useLive and ChatPane subscribe to, instead of opening a new connection in main.tsx.

review.impact: The server runs from the app copy, and the `app` field says a test that edits werk's code edits that copy. But `cli` and `start` (line 85) still run the checkout's src/cli/main.ts. A test that edits CLI or verb code in the copy will see the server use the edited code while its CLI calls use the old code. That mismatch is silent and confusing.
review.fix: Run `app.main` instead of MAIN in `cli` and `start`, and remove the MAIN constant. That way everything the harness launches comes from the same copy.

review.impact: The initial read uses `draftKey(tab)`, but the effect writes with `draftKey(MAIN_TAB)` and leaves `tab` out of its dependencies. Once tabs vary, the draft is read from one key and saved under another.
review.fix: Use `draftKey(tab)` in the effect and add `tab` to its dependency array.

review.impact: The module-level `const global = globalThis` hides Node's built-in `global` name in this file, which makes the code harder to read. serve.ts uses the name `running` for the same pattern, so the two files don't match.
review.fix: Rename it to something like `live` or `holder`, matching the `running` naming in serve.ts.

review.impact: `live.server` starts as a placeholder `{ port: 0, close: async () => {} }` and is filled in only after listen succeeds. The Live type therefore allows a state that looks valid but isn't, and code that reads it before then gets port 0 and a close that does nothing.
review.fix: Build `live` only after listen succeeds and have the request listener forward to a `let handle` variable, or make `server` optional in Live so the half-started state is visible in the type.

review.impact: `liveChannel` is a line-for-line copy of the SSE reader in `open()` in src/cli/serve-chat.test.ts:39-52: the same ChatEvent type, the same read/until loop, the same regexes and the same wait for ': connected'. The token regex is copied too (line 74 vs serve-chat.test.ts:37). A change to the live channel's wire format now has to be made in two places, and the copies will drift apart.
review.fix: Move a `liveChannel(url)` helper and a `tokenOf(url)` helper, with the ChatEvent type, into src/test/harness.ts. Have both serve-chat.test.ts and serve-hot.test.ts use them.

review.impact: `reloadOnLiveChannel` replaces Vite's `hot.send` at runtime and gets past the type checker with two casts (`as (...args: unknown[]) => void` and `as typeof hot.send`) and an `as { type?: unknown }` on the payload. The casts hide any change to Vite's `send` signature, and the wrapper hooks into Vite internals with nothing to catch a break when Vite is upgraded.
review.fix: Keep the overloads typed: wrap with `(payload: HotPayload | string, data?: unknown)`, narrow with `typeof payload === 'object' && payload.type === 'full-reload'`, and drop the casts. Or, if the Vite version allows it, catch full reloads in a plugin hook such as `hotUpdate`/`handleHotUpdate` instead of reassigning `send`. Add a comment that names the Vite version this relies on.

review.impact: `live.server` starts as a fake `{ port: 0, close: async () => {} }` and is replaced after listen. Readers have to work out that the placeholder is never seen, because `global[LIVE]` is only set later. It is an invariant held up by ordering, not by types.
review.fix: Build `state` and `handle` first and wire `http.on('request')` to a local `let handle`. Create the `Live` object only once `port` and `close` exist (`global[LIVE] = { state, handle, server }`), and have the request listener read `global[LIVE]?.handle ?? handle`. Or make `server` optional on `Live`.

review.impact: The initial state reads `draftKey(tab)`, but the effect writes `draftKey(MAIN_TAB)` and leaves `tab` out of the deps. Once `tab` stops being the constant, drafts would be read from one key and written to another.
review.fix: Use `draftKey(tab)` in the effect and add `tab` to the dependency array.

review.impact: This opens another EventSource to /api/events at module scope, alongside the ones in useLive.ts:30 and ChatPane.tsx:39. Each page now holds a separate live-channel connection only to listen for `reload`, and this one is never closed. That is one more copy of the same subscription code.
review.fix: Listen for `reload` on a connection the page already opens (for example, add a `reload` listener in useLive or in one shared live-channel module), or document why a separate connection is needed.

review.impact: The cast `(window as { beforeTheEdit?: true })` and the fill-the-draft-then-mark-the-window setup are repeated across both tests, four casts in all.
review.fix: Add small helpers, e.g. `const markWindow = (page) => page.evaluate(...)` and `const windowMarked = (page) => page.evaluate(...)`, or declare `beforeTheEdit` once on `Window` with `declare global`.

review.impact: `alive` re-implements the `process.kill(pid, 0)` liveness check that `processAlive` in src/board/control.ts:36 already exports. This adds one more copy to the several already in the codebase.
review.fix: Import `processAlive` from '../board/control.ts' and delete `alive`.

review.impact: The server now runs from `app.testServer` in the copy, but `cli` and `start` still run the checkout's `MAIN` (lines 85, 112). The CLI and the server can therefore run different code once a test edits the copy, and the fixture's 'the app the test may edit' wording no longer holds for the CLI.
review.fix: Use `app.main` for `cli` and `start`, and remove the now-unused `MAIN`/`ROOT` constants if nothing else uses them.

review.impact: Nothing tests the other half of the draft persistence in web/src/ChatPane.tsx: the draft key is removed from session storage once the draft is empty. If that removal breaks, a message the user already sent comes back in the composer after the next reload, and every test still passes.
review.fix: Add an e2e case: script a chat reply, fill the composer and send, check that the composer is empty, then edit main.tsx (or call page.reload()) and assert the composer still has the value ''.

review.impact: This test does not tell the new `reload` live-channel path apart from Vite's own `full-reload`. Before the change, Vite's HMR client would also have reloaded the page after an edit to main.tsx. So the test still passes if reloadOnLiveChannel swallows the payload and Vite reloads instead, or if the server-side forwarding is removed and the page's listener is kept. It only fails when both reload paths are gone.
review.fix: Assert that the reload came through the live channel. One way: before the edit, wrap EventSource in page.addInitScript so it records when a `reload` event arrives, and check that record after the page has reloaded. Another: assert that Vite's socket got no full-reload message.

review.impact: Two failure paths in the new code have no test. One is the run() branch for a reload during start-up, where reloadServer() returns undefined and the 'reloaded the code while the server starts' message is printed. The other is the new guard where startServer throws 'a server already runs in this process'. A regression in either one would pass unnoticed.
review.fix: Add a unit test in src/server: with no live server, reloadServer() returns undefined; after startServer, a second startServer rejects with the 'already runs' error; after close(), reloadServer() returns undefined again.

review.impact: `used.module.startsWith(used.root)` is always true, because the fixture builds `module` from `app.root`. It can never fail, so it checks nothing about where the edit landed.
review.fix: Drop it, or replace it with a check that matters, such as asserting that the checkout's src/server/server.ts does not contain '// An edit by the test.'

review.impact: Each page now opens a third server-sent events connection to /api/events. useLive.ts:30 and ChatPane.tsx:39 already open one each. The page only needs this connection for the rare `reload` event, but the server sends it every `changed`, `session` and streamed `chat` delta too, so each push costs one more write per open page. It also holds a long-lived HTTP/1.1 connection. Browsers allow 6 per origin, and Vite's HMR socket uses one too, so two or three werk tabs open at once run out of connections and stall requests.
review.fix: Listen for `reload` on a connection the page already has. For example, add the `reload` listener inside useLive's EventSource, or make one shared EventSource module that useLive, ChatPane and main.tsx all subscribe to. That keeps one connection per page.

review.impact: The 'dead' state of a chip depends on the client matching the start of a human-readable error string ('the agent exited') that src/chat/conversations.ts:124 builds separately. If that wording changes, the chip silently shows 'idle' for a dead child, and no type check or shared constant catches it. A turn-level error that happens to start with the same words would also be shown as dead by mistake.
review.fix: Make the exit a structured signal. One option is a field on the end part, such as `{ kind: 'end', error, exited: true }` or `reason: 'exit'`, set in conversations.ts and read by tabState. The other is a single exported constant in parts.ts that both modules import.

review.impact: The name of the first tab, 'main', is now defined twice: as a private constant here and as an exported one in src/chat/tabs.ts:13. The server's pre-seeded record and the client's first tab can drift apart without either side noticing.
review.fix: Import MAIN_TAB from './tabs.ts' (or from one shared place) instead of declaring it again.

review.impact: Entries in the `tabs` map are never removed. `recordOf` also creates a record for any tab name that `send` sees. Every tab opened (or messaged) during a server's lifetime keeps its record until the server restarts. There is no close path to pair with `open`.
review.fix: Add a close/forget operation for a tab, or note in the module doc that tabs live as long as the server does. Consider having `send` refuse a tab that was never opened, rather than creating it lazily.

review.impact: `stateOf` is typed as returning `string`, not the `TabState` union that tabs.ts exports. This throws away the type that ties `data-state` to the CSS selectors ('running', 'dead').
review.fix: Type the prop as `(tab: Tab) => TabState` and import `TabState`.

review.impact: ChatPane installs a capture-phase click listener on `document` that takes over Shift+clicks on every card link in the page, including links in the map view the pane doesn't own. The pane is now coupled to the markup of other views, and the link behaviour is hard to find from the map side.
review.fix: Move the Shift+click handling to the app level, or into the shared card-link component, and pass an `onFork(cardId)` callback down. That keeps ChatPane's work inside its own subtree.

review.impact: tabState decides that a tab is dead by checking for the prefix 'the agent exited'. That text is copied from the template literal at src/chat/conversations.ts:124, and the only link between the two is a comment. If someone rewords the exit message, the dot stops turning red, and no type or test catches it: tabs.test.ts hard-codes its own copy of the string.
review.fix: Export one constant (for example `EXITED = 'the agent exited'`) from a module that both pure files can import, such as tabs.ts or a small shared module. Build the error at conversations.ts:124 from it, and import it in tabs.ts and its test.

review.impact: MAIN_TAB = 'main' is now defined twice. conversations.ts has its own private copy, and tabs.ts exports one. The server and the client must agree on the first tab's id, and two separate literals can drift apart.
review.fix: Delete the local constant in conversations.ts and import MAIN_TAB from './tabs.ts'.

review.impact: openTab repeats the exact lookup in chat() that turns a card id into `{id, title?}`: graphOf(readLog(...)).nodes.find(...)?.title followed by the conditional spread. Two copies of the same lookup can drift, for example if a missing card is handled differently in one of them.
review.fix: Pull out a helper such as `openCardOf(logPath, id): OpenCard` and call it from both chat() and openTab().

review.impact: The SSE listener rebuilds the per-tab update inline (`{ ...all, [of]: received(all[of] ?? [], ...) }`). That is the same logic as the setTurns helper defined a few lines above, so the transcript map is updated in two places.
review.fix: Use the helper in the listener: `setTurns(of, (ts) => received(ts, turn, part))`. setTurns only calls the stable setTranscripts, so it is safe to call from the effect.

review.impact: TabStrip types `stateOf` as returning `string` even though tabs.ts exports TabState. This throws away the type checking on the data-state values that the CSS selectors depend on.
review.fix: Type the prop as `stateOf: (tab: Tab) => TabState` and import TabState.

review.impact: The new `tabs` helper copies the `chat` helper line for line, with only the route changed.
review.fix: Write one `post(route)` factory and define `chat = post('chat')` and `tabs = post('tabs')`.

review.impact: The locator chain `page.getByTestId('card').locator('..').getByRole('link', { name: /#map-hash/ })` appears three times in the spec. A markup change means three edits.
review.fix: Store it once as a named locator (for example `const mapHashLink = (page) => ...`) and reuse it.

review.impact: The rule 'fork only while the tab has no session of its own' is not tested. No test makes a forked tab's child exit and then sends another message, so nothing checks the two outcomes. First: a tab whose first child reported its session must not pass `--resume <parent> --fork-session` again. Second: a tab whose first child died before its init event must still fork from the parent. Swapping the condition, or dropping the `session === undefined` guard, would pass every test as written.
review.fix: Add a serve-chat test that forks a tab and scripts its first chat reply to report a session and then exit non-zero. Send a second message and assert the third launch has no `--fork-session`. Add a variant where the first forked child exits before its init event and assert the relaunch still has `--resume s-main --fork-session`.

review.impact: `expect.arrayContaining(['--resume', 's-main', '--fork-session'])` passes whatever order the flags appear in, and passes even if they are split up. A launch like `--resume --fork-session ... s-main` would pass. The first test checks the flags in order, but this one does not.
review.fix: Use the same slice check as the first test: `forked.slice(forked.indexOf('--resume'), forked.indexOf('--resume') + 3)` should equal `['--resume', 's-main', '--fork-session']`.

review.impact: No test covers what the client does when opening a tab fails: a non-OK `/api/tabs` response or a network error. A regression could show no alert, or add a chip and move the hash anyway, and no test would catch it.
review.fix: Add an e2e test that makes `/api/tabs` fail, for example with `page.route` returning 409. Assert that the alert shows the server text, that the tab strip still has only 'the map', and that the URL did not change.

review.impact: The 'dead' state depends on the exit message in conversations.ts starting with 'the agent exited'. The unit test types that string in by hand, and no test connects it to the message the server actually sends. If the server's wording changes, the dot stops turning red and every test still passes.
review.fix: Export the prefix from one module and use it in both conversations.ts and tabs.ts. Or add an e2e or serve-chat check that a tab whose child exited gets `data-state="dead"`.

review.impact: The handler accepts any string as `home`, of any length and with newlines or `]`, even when no card has that id. The text goes unchanged into the first-turn prompt line `[this conversation is a new tab, and its home card is #…]`, so a caller with the token can break that line's framing and add made-up bracketed context lines to the agent's input. The `x-werk-token` check limits the risk, and the existing `card` field in /api/chat has the same gap.
review.fix: Check `home` against the card-id pattern (or `NAME`), or require it to be the id of a node in `graphOf(readLog(logPath))`, and answer 400 otherwise. Apply the same rule to `card` in /api/chat.

review.impact: `open` adds a `TabRecord` for every new tab name and never removes one, and `recordOf` in `send` does the same for any tab name it has not seen. The `tabs` map therefore grows for the whole life of the server. Only a caller with the token can do this, so the risk is slow memory growth, not a remote attack.
review.fix: Put a cap on the number of open tabs (answer 409 or 429 once it is reached), or remove a tab's record when its conversation is closed.

review.impact: The red 'dead' dot depends on the client matching the prefix of an error string that is built in src/chat/conversations.ts:124. Nothing ties the two together. If someone rewords that message, every exited tab shows as idle, and no type check or unit test catches it, because tabs.test.ts hardcodes its own copy of the string.
review.fix: Make the exit a structured fact instead of a string. One way: add a field to the end part, such as `{ kind: 'end', exited: true }` or `{ kind: 'end', reason: 'exit' }`, and have tabState read it. The other way: export the prefix as one constant from the pure module src/chat/parts.ts, and have both conversations.ts and tabs.ts import it.

review.impact: The tabs.ts header says at most one tab has a given home, but open() does not enforce it. The ∅ control (fork=false) skips the tabAt check, so it opens a second tab with the same home. Two quick Shift+clicks also both see the stale `tabs` before the first fetch resolves, so both create a tab. After that, tabAt returns whichever duplicate comes first, and Shift+click no longer reliably switches to the tab the user expects.
review.fix: Enforce the invariant in one place. Check `tabAt` for both fork and empty opens, or relax the documented invariant if duplicate homes are meant to be allowed. Also check again inside the `setTabs((now) => ...)` updater, or guard against an open already in flight, so a concurrent open cannot add a duplicate home.

review.impact: The client (src/chat/tabs.ts:13) and the server each define MAIN_TAB = 'main' separately. If they drift apart, the server's seeded main record no longer matches the tab the client sends, and nothing flags it.
review.fix: Import MAIN_TAB from ./tabs.ts, which is pure and already sits in src/chat, instead of redefining it.

review.impact: When `from` names a tab the server has never seen, the open silently succeeds as an empty conversation with parent null. The caller cannot tell 'fork of a tab with no session yet' apart from 'fork of a tab that does not exist', so a client bug stays hidden.
review.fix: Return `{ ok: false, error: 'no tab <from>' }` when `from` is given but `tabs.has(from)` is false, and map it to a 4xx in openTab. Keep parent: null only for a known tab that has no session yet.

review.impact: tabState decides that a tab is dead by matching the prefix of a hand-written error string. That string is built separately in src/chat/conversations.ts:124. If someone rewords that message, dead tabs quietly show as idle, and no test fails, because tabs.test.ts hard-codes its own copy of the text.
review.fix: Export the prefix (or a function that builds the exit message) from one module, for example conversations.ts or a small shared constant in chat/, and use it both to build the message and in tabState. A better option is a structured flag on the end part, such as `exited: true`, so that nothing depends on matching strings.

review.impact: MAIN_TAB = 'main' is defined twice: once here and once as an export in src/chat/tabs.ts:13. The server and the client have to agree on this id, and two copies can drift apart.
review.fix: Import MAIN_TAB from './tabs.ts' in conversations.ts and delete the local constant.

review.impact: The fallback that reads the draft (`?? sessionStorage.getItem(draftKey(tab)) ?? ''`) is written twice, once in `draft` and once inside the setDraft updater. Someone could change one copy and miss the other.
review.fix: Pull it into a helper such as `const stored = (all: Record<string,string>) => all[tab] ?? sessionStorage.getItem(draftKey(tab)) ?? ''` and call it in both places.

review.impact: TabStrip types `stateOf` as returning `string`, but a TabState already exists for this. The union type is lost, so a mistyped state value would compile without error.
review.fix: Type it as `stateOf: (tab: Tab) => TabState` and import TabState from tabs.ts.

review.impact: The new `tabs` helper copies the `chat` helper line for line. Only the route is different.
review.fix: Add one `post(route)` factory and build both `chat` and `tabs` from it.

review.impact: The 'plain click keeps the active tab' test runs with only the main tab open, so main is the only tab that can be active. If a plain click wrongly focused or opened a tab, or moved an inactive tab instead of the active one, the test would still pass. It does not check that a move changes only the active tab when two tabs exist.
review.fix: Open a second tab first, with Shift+click or '+', then plain-click a different card link. Assert that the second chip is still aria-selected, that there are still 2 tabs, and that refocusing 'the map' brings back main's own card while the fork's chip label stays the same.

review.impact: The rule that a later child does not fork again is never tested. It covers a forked tab whose child already reported a session and then exits and respawns. In serve-chat.test.ts, f2 reuses the live child, so only the first-spawn branch runs. A regression that re-forks from the stale parent on every respawn, or that drops the fork on the first spawn after an early exit, would go unnoticed.
review.fix: Add a serve-chat test: script a forked tab's first reply to report its own session and exit with a non-zero code, then send another message on that tab. Assert that the third launch has no '--resume <parent> --fork-session', and pin whatever resume behaviour is intended.

review.impact: Keeping a draft per tab across switches and reloads is new behaviour (#werk-mc-follow), and no test covers it. If drafts leaked between tabs, or sessionStorage were keyed to the wrong tab after a switch, every test would still pass.
review.fix: In e2e/tabs.spec.ts, type a draft in main, open a fork, and assert the composer is empty. Type a different draft there, switch back to 'the map', and assert main's draft is restored. Optionally reload and assert the drafts survive.

review.impact: The 'dead' state depends on the exact error prefix that conversations.ts writes ('the agent exited with code …'), but the test uses its own literal. If someone rewords the message in conversations.ts, dead tabs would show as idle while this test still passes.
review.fix: Export the prefix from one place and use it in both conversations.ts and tabs.ts. Alternatively, add an e2e or serve-chat check that a child exiting with an error turns the chip's data-state to 'dead'.

review.impact: No test shows the UI's failure path: when POST /api/tabs is refused (403, 409 or a network error), the pane should show the refusal as an alert and open no chip. Nothing pins that a failed open leaves the tab list and URL unchanged.
review.fix: Add an e2e case that forces the open to fail, for example by routing /api/tabs to a 409 with page.route. Assert that the role=alert text appears, that the tab count stays the same, and that the URL does not change.

review.impact: `const [, forked, empty] = werk.agentLaunches()` never checks the number of launches. An extra or missing launch would shift which launch gets compared to which expectation without failing the length check, and could hide a duplicate spawn.
review.fix: Assert `expect(werk.agentLaunches()).toHaveLength(3)` before destructuring.

grade.gap: Everything here serves criteria 1-4, user story 49 or the decided #werk-mc-shared-convo-log card: the conversations log, the session sink, reference resolution and the agent instructions. One small extra: src/cli/recall.test.ts tests that `--context` is refused. Nothing asks for that flag, though refusing an unknown flag is ordinary argument handling and needs no change.

The card's list example prints `tab  session  #home` and leaves out the parent. convoLines in src/chat/convos.ts prints `tab  home  session`, with home before session, and adds a `forked from <parent>` column (tested in src/chat/convos.test.ts 'prints each conversation...' and src/cli/recall.test.ts 'convos prints...'). This is a small difference from the card, not a forbidden behaviour. To match the card exactly, print tab, session, home and drop the parent from the list output.

review.impact: `onSession` runs inside `deliver`, in the child's stdout loop, and nothing catches errors around it. If `appendConvo` throws (disk full, permissions, a read-only `.werk`), the `for await` loop stops. Its promise is fire-and-forget (`void`), so the rejection goes unhandled and may crash the server. Even if it doesn't, the rest of the reply is dropped and the open turns never get their `end` part, so the tab hangs. A bookkeeping write can break the chat itself.
review.fix: Keep sink failures out of the reply stream. Wrap the `onSession` call in `deliver` in try/catch and log the error, or make the server's sink catch its own errors: `onSession: (entry) => { try { appendConvo(...) } catch (err) { console.error(...) } }`. Either way, the parts of that line must still be delivered.

review.impact: `Convo` is just an alias of `ConvoEntry`, so two names cover one shape. Readers will look for a difference that isn't there, and the signatures of `convosOf`, `resolveConvo` and `readConvos` look more complex than they are.
review.fix: Drop the `Convo` alias and use `ConvoEntry` throughout. Or, if the log line and the folded conversation are meant to grow apart, say so in a comment.

review.impact: The pure fold hard-codes the CLI name in its error text (`werk convos lists them.`). Elsewhere the agent instructions name the werk command line by the command they are given (#werk-agent-selfcontained). An agent started with `/opt/bun /opt/werk/main.ts` is told to run a bare `werk` that may not be on its PATH.
review.fix: Have `resolveConvo` return just the problem (`no conversation "x"`), and let the `recall` verb add the hint about listing conversations, or pass the command name in.

review.impact: `Convo` is only another name for `ConvoEntry` (`export type Convo = ConvoEntry`). Readers will look for a difference between the log line and the folded conversation, and there is none. Both names now appear in signatures across convos.ts, convo-log.ts and the tests.
review.fix: Pick one type. Either use `ConvoEntry` everywhere and delete `Convo`, or give `Convo` a real distinction if one is planned.

review.impact: `convosOf` accepts `readonly unknown[]`, but the test casts its malformed inputs with `as ConvoEntry` and `null as unknown as ConvoEntry`. These casts are unnecessary type escape hatches, and they hide the fact that the function is built to take untyped log lines.
review.fix: Pass the malformed lines without casts: `convosOf([{ tab: 'main' }, { session: 's-1' }, null])`.

review.impact: `splitTerms` re-implements the `--name value` / `--name=value` handling and the 'needs a value' check from `parseArgs`, because `parseArgs` keeps only the last value of a flag. The two parsers can drift apart: they already split `--grep=` differently from `parseArgs`'s `indexOf('=')`, and they word their errors separately.
review.fix: Teach `parseArgs` about repeatable flags, for example a `repeats` list that collects values into `string[]`. Then use it here instead of the hand-rolled pre-pass.

review.impact: The duplicate line in this test is identical to the first `s-2` entry. The test passes whether `convosOf` keeps the first line or the last one for a session, so it never checks the documented rule that a later line replaces the earlier one. A regression to keep-first would go unnoticed.
review.fix: Make the repeated `s-2` line different, for example `{ tab: 'tab-a2', session: 's-2', home: 'other' }`. Then assert that `convos[1]` carries the later values and that `s-2` is still in second place.

review.impact: No test covers a reference that matches two kinds at once, such as a tab name that is also a home card, or a session id that is also a prefix of another. If someone reorders the `kinds` array in `resolveConvo`, the result changes silently. Also, the 'matches nothing' case `#x` sits in the 'matches two conversations' test.
review.fix: Add a case where the same reference is both a tab name and another conversation's home card, and assert that the home card wins. Add a case where an exact session id is also a prefix of a longer id, and assert that the exact id wins. Move the `#x` assertion into the 'matches nothing' test.

review.impact: Only the `--grep value` form is tested. The `--grep=value` branch of `splitTerms` is never run, and neither is `--grep` followed by another `--` flag. An empty `--grep=` matches every message without warning, and no test pins that down.
review.fix: Add a call with `--grep=fold` and assert the same output as `--grep fold`. Add `recall <id> --grep --grep x` and assert exit code 2. Decide whether an empty `--grep=` should be refused and test that behaviour.

review.impact: The fake agent gives both children the same session, so the fork's log line differs from main's only by its tab. The test therefore cannot show that dedup is per tab rather than per session id. It also never checks that a tab that later switches to a new session gets a second line.
review.fix: Script the fork's reply under its own session, for example `replyIn('s-fork', ...)`, if the fake supports it. Then assert that the fork's line names `s-fork` with `parent: 's-main'`. Add a turn that reports a new session on the same tab and assert that a second line is appended for that tab.

review.impact: The handler calls preventDefault before it checks whether the press does anything. Cmd+4 and Cmd+5 are blocked even when no chip sits at that position, so the browser's own Cmd+N tab switch stops working there and the keypress does nothing. The listener is also global, so Cmd+[ and Cmd+] are taken away from any other editable field on the page that handles them itself, such as outdent and indent.
review.fix: Work out `next` first, and call preventDefault only when a chip exists at that position, i.e. `next !== now`. You could also skip events whose target is an editable element other than the composer.

review.impact: No test fails if this line is reverted to `const card = mapCard`. The e2e test at e2e/tabs.spec.ts:141 checks that the turn names #log, and the test at e2e/tabs.spec.ts:130 checks that the scope chip shows #fold. Both checks run after the click has already changed the hash and the map prop has caught up, so the old code gives the same result. The behaviour this line adds is that the active tab's card applies at once, before the map follows. Nothing tests that, so a regression to the map's last card would go unnoticed.
review.fix: Add a test that only passes with the new line. One option: in an e2e test, delay or block the hash change (for example, stub `window.location.hash` assignment through `page.addInitScript`, or send in the same tick as the focus). Then check that the posted `card` in the request body is the tab's card and not the map's. Another option: move the scope choice into a pure helper in src/chat/tabs.ts and unit-test it with a map card that differs from the active tab's card.

review.impact: The `Meta+5` check passes at once because tab 0 was already selected, so it cannot catch a wrong focus that lands a moment later. It also does not check the URL, so a handler that moved the map without changing the selection would still pass.
review.fix: After `Meta+5`, also run `await expect(page).toHaveURL(/#fold$/)`. Better still, press a key that does change the selection afterwards (for example, `Meta+2`) and check the selection, so the test cannot pass trivially.

review.impact: `stepped` is not tested with a single tab or with an active id that is not in the list (`findIndex` returns -1). The modulo arithmetic behaves differently in those cases, and nothing checks the result.
review.fix: Add `expect(stepped(firstTabs('fold'), 1)).toEqual(firstTabs('fold'))`, which wraps onto itself. Also add a case where `active` is not in the list, to fix the expected behaviour.

causeOfLast.why: pass 1 correctly made a green build move its ticket to merging, but this test still expected the second build to find the ticket in building.
another ticket that merged first added a test at the same place at the end of `e2e/tabs.spec.ts`, and the two tests do not conflict in behaviour.
the code was right; the restore test starts 14 processes but kept the default 5 s timeout, so it timed out on a loaded machine, and the fix is a longer timeout, not a code change.

grade.gap: Per-tab drafts were built in an earlier pass (web/src/ChatPane.tsx:40-52). This diff only adds the e2e test 'a draft belongs to its tab and survives a switch', and that test covers the criterion.

src/cli/remove.test.ts adds a 20 s timeout to the remove/restore/find tests. This is a test-harness change with no ticket behaviour, not a product behaviour. It is minor, but it is unrelated to this ticket's stories.

review.impact: The handler calls preventDefault() before it knows whether a chip is at that position. With three tabs open, Cmd+4 and Cmd+5 do nothing in werk and also no longer switch browser tabs.
review.fix: Work out `next` first and call preventDefault() only when `next.active !== now.active` (or when `asked` is a step). If swallowing the key is intended, say so in the comment.

review.impact: `stepped` assumes the list is non-empty and that `active` is in it. With an empty list, `% 0` gives NaN and the `!` assertion lets `.id` throw on undefined. If `active` is missing, `findIndex` returns -1 and the step lands on the wrong chip without any error. `atPosition` handles its out-of-range case and returns the tabs unchanged, but this function has no such check.
review.fix: Return `tabs` unchanged when `n === 0` or `from === -1`, the same way `atPosition` does, and drop the non-null assertion.

review.impact: The new `focusRef` and its effect copy the `forkAt` pattern just below it (line 116): a ref that an effect with no dependencies sets on every render, then a document listener registered once that reads the ref. That makes two hand-written copies of the same latest-value-ref idiom in one component, and a third global handler would likely copy it again.
review.fix: Pull out a small `useLatest(value)` hook, or a `useDocumentListener(type, handler, capture?)` hook that keeps the latest handler, and use it for both the key and click listeners.

review.impact: All three new tests repeat the same setup: go to #map, find the chat pane and tablist tabs, go to #fold, click 'New empty conversation', then wait for two tabs. That makes the tests longer than they need to be, and a change to the tab strip's labels or roles means editing every copy.
review.fix: Move the shared setup into a helper, such as `twoTabs(page, werk)`, that returns `{ chat, tabs, composer }`, and call it from each test.

review.impact: The ChatPane change makes the scope chip and the turn's card come from `activeTab(tabs).card` instead of the map's `card` prop. This test can't tell the two apart. It waits for `toHaveURL(/#log$/)` and for the card to render before it types, and by then the map prop has already caught up to #log. So the chip and the '[the map is now at #log' prefix would also pass on the old code, which read the map prop. Nothing checks the window between a focus and the map following it, where the old code named the previous card.
review.fix: Add a check that fails on the old code. One way: delay or block the hashchange-driven map update, focus a tab, and assert that the `.chips` chip shows the tab's card before the map moves. Another: send a turn right after the focus with no wait on the URL, and assert that the server got that tab's card. The unit-level alternative is to render ChatPane with a fixed `card` prop, focus another tab, and assert the chip shows that tab's card.

review.impact: Drafts were already stored per tab under `werk-draft:${tab}` before this change, so the draft test passes without it. It adds coverage but doesn't guard anything the diff introduced.
review.fix: Keep it as regression coverage, or drop it from this change's scope. If it should guard the change, add a case that only the new code satisfies, such as a draft surviving a switch made with Cmd+1 or Cmd+[.

review.impact: 'a switch keeps the position of every tab' checks only that t-3 keeps its card after stepping away and back. It never checks that the other tabs kept theirs, for example that main and t-2 did not take 'cards'. The name says every tab, but a bug that copied the active card to the other tabs would still pass.
review.fix: Also assert the cards of the tabs that were stepped through, for example `expect(stepped(tabs, 1).list.map((t) => t.card)).toEqual([...])`, or assert `activeTab` after each step.

review.impact: No test covers `stepped` with a single tab, or with an active id that is not in the list (`findIndex` returns -1). The modulo arithmetic has the most room to go wrong in these edge cases, and the wrap tests cover only three tabs.
review.fix: Add `expect(stepped(firstTabs('x'), 1).active).toBe('main')` and the same for -1. Also add a case where `tabs.active` is not in the list, to pin down the intended result.

causeOfLast.why: pass 3 made the test run parallel but kept the 5 s per-test limit, and a test that starts many processes cannot finish in 5 s under that load.

review.impact: The ref still uses the key `tabs` but now holds the whole Strip (`{ tabs: strip, focusAt }`). The key handler then reads `now.tabs.active`, which looks like Tabs.tabs.active. The wrong name makes the keyboard path hard to read and easy to break.

review.impact: onClose and focusAt build the next strip from the `strip` captured at render time (`closed(strip, id)`, `inStrip(strip, ...)`). `change` and the send path use a functional `setStrip` instead. If two updates land in one batch, for example a send's `touched` and then a close, the second update overwrites the first, so the order in which tabs were last touched comes out wrong.

review.impact: msFromEnv uses a generic key and an `as` cast only so that its result can be spread into the options. This is more indirection than the rest of server.ts uses, and the cast hides type errors.
review.fix: Return `number | undefined` from `msFromEnv(name)` and pass `idleMs: msFromEnv('WERK_IDLE_MS'), checkMs: msFromEnv('WERK_IDLE_CHECK_MS')`. The `checkMs` fallback should then use `??` the same way, or startConversations should skip undefined keys.

review.impact: `alive(pid)` is copied word for word in e2e/park.spec.ts. Two copies of the test helper can drift apart.
review.fix: Move `alive` into a shared test helper module, for example next to src/test/fake-agent.ts, and import it in both places.

review.impact: The strip now has two update paths. `change` (line 63) uses the functional setStrip with `transcriptsRef`. The map-follow (line 105) and `focusAt` (line 110) call `inStrip(strip, ..., running(transcripts))` on the render-time `strip`. `focusAt` is also called through `focusRef` from the key handler. A reader has to work out which path each caller needs, and a later edit can easily pick the stale-closure one.
review.fix: Send every strip change through one helper. Make `focusAt` call `change(() => next)` and the map-follow call `change((t) => moved(t, mapCard))`. If the render-phase call has to stay synchronous, add a comment saying why.

review.impact: `window.location.hash = at === undefined ? '' : cardHref(at)` now appears three times (focusAt, open, and the new onClose). onClose also repeats focusAt's logic of updating the strip and then moving the map to the active tab's card.
