The builder did not name these cards. The next pass should name them in its record, but no new card is needed.

review.impact: `companions` and the loop that takes only the orphaned sources copy `discardSet` in src/map/stage.ts:9-51 almost line for line. The only difference is the ghost filter. A later change to which evidence goes with a card, such as excerpts shared by two cards or a new evidence kind, has to be made in both places. If it is made in only one, discard and remove will quietly disagree.
review.fix: Move one helper into tree.ts or removal.ts. It should take a card list, a 'taken' list and an optional node filter, and return the companions plus the sources that only those cards cite. Have both `discardSet` and `removalOf` call it.

review.impact: `refusedWithoutActor` and `ACTOR_FLAG` repeat the inline `--actor you` refusal in src/verbs/accept.ts:18. There are now two copies of the person-only guard and its wording, and they can drift apart.
review.fix: Put the guard and the flag definition in one shared verb helper, for example in src/cli or a small src/verbs/actor.ts. Use it from accept, remove and restore.

review.impact: `restoreRule` finds the card's parent by scanning `map.waiting` for a refines link. Every other parent lookup goes through the tree.ts helpers (`parentOf`, `linksFrom`). The rule depends on how fold.ts files links internally, so a change to where waiting links live would break this rule without any error.
review.fix: Add a tree.ts helper, e.g. `waitingParentOf(map, id)`, next to `parentOf`. Call it here.

review.impact: `refusedWithoutActor` and `ACTOR_FLAG` copy the `--actor you` refusal that `src/verbs/accept.ts:12-21` already has inline. There are now two versions of the same rule and message, and they can drift apart. They already differ in wording: 'They click the ✓' against 'They press the control'.
review.fix: Move the helper and the flag into one small shared module, for example `src/verbs/actor.ts`, and use it from accept, remove and restore.

review.impact: `map.removals.get(id) as Removal` hides the `undefined` case behind a type cast. The same cast appears in `src/verbs/remove.ts:62`. Both depend on `restoreRule` having run first. If that coupling breaks, the code crashes on `removal.taken` with no clear error.
review.fix: Narrow the type instead of casting. In fold, `const removal = map.removals.get(id); if (!removal) return;`. In the verb, use the events that `write` returns, or check for the value and fail with a clear message.

review.impact: The name `replace` reads as 'substitute', but the function places every link again. A reader can easily misread what it does at its three call sites.
review.fix: Rename it to `replaceAll`, `placeAgain` or `relink` so the name matches what the doc comment says.

review.impact: `as never` turns off type checking for the event passed to `step`, so the test would still compile if the Event shape changed.
review.fix: Build the value as a typed `Event`, for example `{ seq: 9, at: "t", type: "node.restored", actor: "you", payload: { id: "a" } } satisfies Event`, with no cast.

review.impact: No fold test removes and then restores a ghost card. The rule tests allow `remove("g")`, and on restore `replace` has to send the ghost's links back to `ghostEdges`, not `links`. A change that let a restored ghost's links go live, or that cleared its `proposed` flag, would pass every test.
review.fix: Add a fold test that proposes ghost g under b and gives it a link, then removes and restores g. Assert that `map.nodes.get("g").proposed` is true, that the link is in `ghostEdges` and not in `links`, and that `waiting` is empty.

review.impact: `removalOf` always takes an excerpt or option, even when another card still in the map is `supported_by` it. Sources get a check for other citers, but excerpts get none. No test covers an excerpt cited by two cards. So nothing pins whether such an excerpt is meant to go, or whether the other card is left with a waiting link to evidence that was taken out.
review.fix: Add a case where `d` is also `supported_by` `c:ex0`, and assert the intended result for `removalOf(base(), "c", false)`. If the excerpt should stay, give excerpts the same every-citer-is-taken check that sources get.

review.impact: The CLI tests cover a refused `restore` but never a refused `remove`, such as an unknown id, an option, or `--reparent` on a root card that has children. Nothing checks that a refused remove exits 1 with the rule message and leaves the log unchanged, or that `removalLines` is never reached after the refusal.
review.fix: Add a test that runs `werk remove auth:opt0 --actor you` and `werk remove nope --actor you`. Assert code 1, the `werk remove: refused: ...` message, and the same log length as before.

review.impact: `expect(removed.waiting).toHaveLength(4)` checks only the count. A fold that put the wrong links in `waiting`, for example a duplicate in place of the `b`→`a1` depends_on link, would still pass.
review.fix: Assert the exact contents, for example `toEqual` on the three refines links plus the depends_on link from `b` to `a1`, in fold order.

review.impact: `change.accepted` used to re-place only `ghostEdges`. It now calls `replace`, which rebuilds `links`, `ghostEdges` and `waiting` and copies every link in the map. Each accept, which is the most common event in a log, now costs time in proportion to all links. A full fold therefore costs about accepts × links. That is fine for today's map sizes, but it adds work that accepts did not do before.
review.fix: In `change.accepted`, re-place only `ghostEdges`, as before: `const held = map.ghostEdges; map.ghostEdges = []; for (const link of held) place(map, link);`. An accept cannot bring a waiting link back, because no node comes back into the map. Keep `replace(map)` for `node.removed` and `node.restored`.

review.impact: `removalHolding` searches every removal's `taken` array one item at a time. `addNodeRule` calls it for every `node.added`, and `missing` calls it on every refusal. Both run while folding each log line, so a fold costs about adds × all removed nodes. This grows as more removals pile up in a long-lived log.
review.fix: Give the fold an index from each removed node id to the removal that took it. It can be a `Map<string, string>` that `node.removed` and `node.restored` update, or you can look up `map.removed.has(id)` first and only search the removals when that is true. That makes the common case, an id that was never removed, a single lookup.

grade.gap: The command-line test 'an amend that misses a required fact is refused' in src/verbs/propose-verbs.test.ts uses a card that never had a kill criterion, so it tests a fact that is missing, not one that gets removed. The removal case is tested only in src/map/contract.test.ts: edge.removed followed by node.amended is refused for basis. That still covers the criterion.

Not asked for, but small and close to story 29: (a) proposing a change to an open or proto card, and accepting it with change.accepted (rules.ts pendingRule, fold.ts change.accepted on a real node). (b) A later proposal silently replaces the pending one (fold.ts change.proposed). Both are natural extensions of #al-diff-cli. Neither needs removing.

review.impact: The cover rule only checks the ops against the body as it was when the proposal was made. Edits to the node (node.bodyEdited, node.retitled) leave `pending` in place, and `pendingRule` does not check the ops again on accept or amend. So if the body changes between propose and accept, `takePending`/`applyOps` silently drops every block the old ops never named. The diff that `werk show` prints leaves those blocks out too, so the person accepting never sees what is lost. This is the exact loss the cover rule exists to stop.
review.fix: In `pendingRule`, for accept and amend, run `uncovered(node.body, node.pending.ops)` again and refuse when it is not empty. Or clear `node.pending` in the fold whenever the node's body is edited, so a proposal made against an old body cannot be applied.

review.impact: For an amend, `pendingRule` builds its message from the verb, so it reads "only a ghost or a pending change can be amended". But `amendRule` has already refused ghosts, so the message points to a fix that does not exist. The person also typed `werk accept`, not amend, so the word 'amended' does not match what they did.
review.fix: Give the amend case its own message, for example `#id is decided and has no pending change to accept`. Alternatively, check for a missing pending change in accept.ts before sending a node.amended event.

review.impact: The verb reads and folds the whole log a second time after `write`, only to print the pending change. That doubles the fold cost and writes a second fold-time entry for one command. It is also not how the other verbs work: they print from the map they already have.
review.fix: Build the output from the map you already have: take `map.nodes.get(id)`, add the `proposal` that was written, and pass that to `formatPending` (e.g. `formatPending({ ...node, pending: proposal })`). Then the second `readMap` is not needed.

review.impact: `logOf`, `lines` and `ok` are now copied word for word in three test files: map-verbs.test.ts, contract-verbs.test.ts and this one. A change to the log path or to the error format of `ok` has to be made in all three, and the copies will drift apart.
review.fix: Move `logOf`, `lines` and `ok` into src/test/project.ts next to `freshProject`, and import them in all three verb test files.

review.impact: The indent-a-block regex `replace(/^(?=.)/gm, "    ")` appears here and again in src/map/show.ts:62. The refusal and `werk show` are meant to quote blocks the same way, but nothing keeps them in step.
review.fix: Export one small `indent(text, prefix)` helper, for example from ops.ts or show.ts, and use it in both places.

review.impact: `diffOf` calls `op.old.trim()` and `op.new.trim()` up to three times on each path, and `quotes` trims again. The branches are harder to read, and a future edit could trim one path and miss another.
review.fix: At the top of the flatMap callback, trim once into locals (`const old = op.tag === "new" ? undefined : op.old.trim(); const next = op.tag === "removed" ? undefined : op.new.trim();`) and use those in every branch.

review.impact: `ghostRule` now also handles the pending change of a real node, through `pendingRule`, so its name no longer matches what it does. A reader looking for where accept and discard of a pending change are checked will not look here.
review.fix: Rename it to something like `acceptOrDiscardRule`, or add a doc comment saying it covers both a ghost and a real node's pending change.

review.impact: The verb repeats the amend-or-accept decision (real node and decided means amend) that `pendingRule` in rules.ts already encodes. If the status rules change, the verb and the rules can disagree.
review.fix: Export one predicate from the map layer, for example `takesAmend(node)`, and use it in both accept.ts and `pendingRule`.

review.impact: The cover rule is checked only when the change is proposed. A node.bodyEdited or node.edited after the propose keeps the pending ops (fold.ts does not clear `pending`). An accept or amend then rebuilds the body from the old ops with applyOps, so any block added by that edit is lost and nobody sees it. That is exactly what #al-diff-cli-cover forbids, and no test edits the body between a propose and an accept.
review.fix: In pendingRule, for accept and amend, check `uncovered(node.body, node.pending.ops)` again and refuse when it is not empty. Alternatively, drop `pending` in fold when the body changes. Add a rules or fold test: propose, then bodyEdited with a new block, then accept, which must refuse (or must find the pending change gone).

review.impact: fold.ts:103 says a later proposal replaces the pending one, but no test proposes twice. A regression that merges the two proposals (for example, keeping the title from the first after a why-only second) would pass every test.
review.fix: Add a fold test that proposes {title} and then {why} on the same node. Assert that `pending` equals only the second proposal, and that an accept leaves the title unchanged.

review.impact: `werk accept` on a decided card with no pending change writes node.amended. The refusal then reads 'only a ghost or a pending change can be amended', which names a verb the person did not run. No test covers this failure path, so the wording goes unchecked.
review.fix: Write node.amended only when `node.pending` is defined, so this case falls through to change.accepted and its 'can be accepted' message. Add a propose-verbs test that accepts a decided card with no pending change and asserts the exit code and the message.

review.impact: After `write`, the verb calls `readMap` a second time only to print the pending diff. That reads and folds the whole log again, so every `werk propose` folds the log twice and the cost grows with the log.
review.fix: Build the output from the node already in memory: `const node = map.nodes.get(id); if (node) formatPending({ ...node, pending: proposal })`. Or have `write` return the folded map so the verb can use that.

review.impact: `uncovered` calls `blocksOf(body)` itself and then again through `quotes`, so the body is split twice. This runs on every `change.proposed` in the rules check, both at write time and for every proposal line on each fold.
review.fix: Split the body once and pass the blocks in: have `quotes` take `blocks: string[]` (or return them with the indices), and filter that same array in `uncovered`.

causeOfLast.why: the notes ticket merged first and changed the same fold, rules, types and verb list that this ticket changed.

grade.gap: The `werk removed` listing verb (src/verbs/remove.ts) is not named by any acceptance criterion. User story 31 cites #werk-remove, which says 'can list what is out', and #werk-cli-remove defines the verb, so it stays in scope.

The data shapes, event names and refusal rules come from the decided cards #werk-remove-restore-undo-fold-shape, #werk-remove-restore-undo-event-types, #werk-write-remove-links-new-write-refuses and #werk-cli-remove rather than from the builder's named list, but those cards do cover them. The rest (the Removal field names `taken` and `moved.children/to`, and the refusal wording) is the inside of a helper or a list of values.

review.impact: `werk remove` prints its result from a second call to `removalOf` on the map before the write. This duplicates the fold's own calculation instead of reading what the fold recorded. Today the two agree because they share one function. If the fold ever changes the removal before it stores it (in `apply` for `node.removed`), the command line will report nodes the log did not remove, and nothing will catch it. `restore` already reads the fold's record from `map.removals`, so the two verbs now work in different ways.
review.fix: Apply the event to a copy and read the stored removal from it: `const after = copyMap(map); step(after, event); io.out(removalLines(map, id, after.removals.get(id) as Removal, ...))`. Or have `write` return the folded map. Then the printed lines come from the same record that `werk removed` reads.

review.impact: `refusedWithoutActor` and `ACTOR_FLAG` copy the inline actor check and refusal text in `src/verbs/accept.ts:12-21` almost word for word. That makes three verbs carrying two copies of the same rule, so changing the wording or the rule means editing both, and they will drift apart.
review.fix: Move `refusedWithoutActor` and an actor-flag factory into a shared verb helper module, and have `accept.ts` use it as well. The flag's help text and the refusal's 'They press/click …' line can be parameters.

review.impact: `linksTo(map, id, "refines").map((link) => link.from)` and `linksFrom(map, id, "refines")[0]?.to` repeat `childrenOf` and `parentOf` from `tree.ts`. `rules.ts` already uses those helpers for the same reparent check, so the two places are written differently for the same idea.
review.fix: Import `childrenOf` and `parentOf` from `./tree.ts` and use them here.

review.impact: `map.removals.get(id) as Removal` is a type escape hatch. It depends on `restoreRule` having run first, with no check at this point, so a later change to the rule order would crash with an unclear TypeError. The same cast appears at `src/verbs/remove.ts:63`.
review.fix: Narrow instead of casting, for example `const removal = map.removals.get(id); if (!removal) return;`. In the verb, use the result of the write, or a guard that throws a clear error.

review.impact: Inside the callback, `moved?.to` uses optional chaining on a value that is known to be defined there. The code reads as though `moved` might be missing.
review.fix: Bind the value once, for example `const { children = [], to } = removal.moved ?? {}`, or branch on `if (moved)` before mapping, so the callback uses `moved.to` directly.

review.impact: No fold test removes and restores a ghost card, which the rules allow (rules.test.ts checks remove("g")). Its links go from ghostEdges to waiting and must come back to ghostEdges, not links. If replace() or place() put them in the wrong list on restore, no test would fail.
review.fix: Add a fold test that proposes a ghost card with a link, removes it, then restores it. Assert that the link waits while the ghost is out, is back in ghostEdges after the restore, and is not in links.

review.impact: Nothing tests a reparent whose moved child is a ghost that is then discarded or accepted before the restore. After a discard, removal.moved.children still names the dropped child, so `werk restore` would print a 'moved … back under' line for a node that no longer exists. No test sees this.
review.fix: Add a fold test (and a remove.test.ts case) that reparents a card with a ghost child, discards the ghost, then restores the card. Assert the links and the restore output, and change the behaviour if the line for the discarded child is wrong.

review.impact: The command-line tests check only the --actor refusals and one restore refusal. Nothing checks the error text, the exit code or the unchanged log for `werk remove` on an unknown id or a non-card, or for `werk restore` of a card that is still in the map. A regression in how the verb reports a refused write would pass.
review.fix: Add cases for `remove nope --actor you`, `remove auth:opt0 --actor you` and `restore root --actor you`. Assert code 1, the exact `werk remove: refused: …` text, and that the log length does not change.

review.impact: `change.accepted` used to re-place only the held `ghostEdges`. It now calls `replace(map)`, which copies and re-places every live, held and waiting link. A fold runs on every CLI call, so folding a log costs O(accepts × links). The extra work grows with the whole map, not with the ghosts that changed.
review.fix: On accept, re-place only `map.ghostEdges` as before. A waiting link cannot go live because a ghost was accepted, since its missing end is still out. Keep the full `replace` for `node.removed` and `node.restored` only, or limit even those to links that touch the nodes in `removal.taken`.

review.impact: `removalHolding` scans every removal and runs `taken.includes` on each one. `addNodeRule` now calls it for every `node.added`, and `missing()` calls it for every unknown-id refusal. Over a fold that is O(adds × all removed nodes), linear work per event that a lookup would do in constant time.
review.fix: Keep an index from each removed node id to the removal that holds it, for example a `Map<string, string>` filled when `node.removed` applies and cleared when `node.restored` applies. Or derive it from `map.removed` plus a holder field, and look the id up directly.

review.impact: `removalOf` calls `linksTo`/`linksFrom` for each card and each source, and each call filters all links. It also uses `taken.includes` and `sources.includes` inside the loops. Removing a card near the root of a large map costs O(subtree × links) plus a quadratic membership check.
review.fix: Index the links by `from` and `to` once at the start of `removalOf`, and keep `taken` and `sources` in Sets for membership checks. Then build the `taken` array in order for the result.

review.impact: The verb reads and matches the chat log before it reads the map. For an unknown or non-card citing id, the user may see a chat-log or no-match refusal first. Only after rephrasing the quote do they learn that the card itself was wrong, which costs an extra round trip.

review.impact: `quoteRule` accepts any non-empty `conversation` string. The allowed conversation-name shape (the `NAME` regex) lives only in `chat.ts` and is enforced only by the verb. An `excerpt.quoted` event that is written by hand or by another writer can carry a name like `../x`. That pointer can never resolve through `chatLogPath`, so the map can hold an excerpt whose pointer leads nowhere.
review.fix: Export a name predicate from `chat.ts`, such as `isConversationName`, and use it in `quoteRule`. Then the log rules and the verb share one definition of a valid conversation name.

review.impact: `Draft` already includes `excerpt.quoted`, so this `as Draft` cast isn't needed. It also switches off type checking for the payload, so a misspelled or missing pointer field would still compile. The same cast appears at src/map/stage.test.ts:87.

review.impact: The full ten-field `excerpt.quoted` fixture is copied into rules.test.ts (twice: here and in the `quote()` helper below), stage.test.ts, notes-verbs.test.ts, fold.test.ts and show.test.ts. Adding or renaming a pointer field means editing every copy.
review.fix: Move the `quote()` helper above the note test in rules.test.ts and use it there. Add one shared test helper that builds an `excerpt.quoted` draft from an id, a card and optional overrides, and use it in stage, notes-verbs, fold and show tests.

review.impact: The `quote === ""` check runs inside the per-line callback, although it doesn't depend on the line. That makes the empty-quote case harder to see when reading the function.
review.fix: Return `{ ok: false, reason: "no match" }` at the top of `matchQuote` when `quote === ""`, and keep only the `kind !== "spoken"` filter in the loop.

review.impact: `only.at[0] as number` and `lines[only.message] as ChatLine` are non-null casts. Each one exists because the earlier checks proved a value the types can't see.
review.fix: Keep the line in each hit (`hits.push({ message, line, at })`) and destructure `const [start] = only.at` after the length checks. Then neither cast is needed.

review.impact: Of the four text fields in an excerpt's pointer that `quoteRule` checks, only `session` has a test. If a change dropped `conversation`, `speaker` or `said_at` from that check, every test would still pass.
review.fix: Add assertions that `quote({ conversation: "" })`, `quote({ speaker: "" })` and `quote({ said_at: "" })` each return "an excerpt's pointer needs its <key>", or loop over the four keys.

review.impact: Every quote span in the tests is ASCII. Nothing pins how `start`, `end` and the rule's `end - start === title.length` behave on text with surrogate pairs, such as emoji. A later switch to code points or bytes in either `matchQuote` or `quoteRule` would put the stored pointer out of step with the rule, and no test would catch it.
review.fix: Add a `matchQuote` case on a spoken line that has an emoji before the quote. Assert that `start` and `end` are UTF-16 offsets and that `end - start` equals `quote.length`, and add a matching case to the `quoteRule` test.

review.impact: Adding `& Partial<ExcerptPointer>` to `NodeFields` lets a `node.added` or `node.proposed` event for a card, option or source carry `conversation`, `session`, `message`, `start`, `end`, `speaker` and `said_at`. `addNodeRule` never checks these fields, and `fold` copies them into the node. A non-excerpt node can therefore hold a pointer that looks like a transcript citation but was never matched against a chat log. Today `show` prints the pointer only for excerpts, so the harm is limited to stored data that later code could trust by mistake.
review.fix: Keep the pointer fields off `NodeFields`: give excerpt nodes their own type, such as `MapNode = ... | (ExcerptFields & {kind: 'excerpt'})`. Alternatively, make the field check refuse any pointer field on a `node.added` or `node.proposed` payload.

grade.gap: src/agent/prompt.ts systemPrompt builds the builder prompt as base, then the werk text, then the build-rule titles. review.impact: There are two separate sources for the list of shipped subagents. `SUBAGENT_TEXTS` names each subagent file in its own import. The link check in `scripts/subagent-links.ts` instead reads every `.md` file in `src/agent/subagents` from disk. So a builder could add a third subagent file and its `.claude/agents` link, and every check would still pass. werk's own repository would use that subagent, but it would never be shipped to user projects: `--agents` would leave it out, while the instructions could name it. This is the drift between werk's own agents and users' agents that #werk-cc-subagents is meant to prevent. The test that checks the instructions name every subagent loops over `shippedSubagents()`, which comes from the import list, so it misses this case too.
review.fix: Make the folder and the import list agree, and fail a test when they don't. One way is to add a test to `prompt.test.ts` that reads the names in `src/agent/subagents/*.md` and expects them to equal `Object.keys(shippedSubagents(...))`. Another is to have the link check import `SUBAGENT_TEXTS` and parse the names from it instead of calling `readdirSync`. Either way, also export `SHIPPED_DIR` from one place so the path isn't written in both files.

review.impact: `parseSubagent` treats every front-matter line as a `key: value` pair. The shipped files begin with a blank line after `---`. That line, and any other line without a colon, still becomes an entry: `indexOf` returns -1, so `slice(0, -1)` produces a junk key such as "". A field on several lines, or a typo in a key, is silently dropped instead of raising an error. Today this works only by accident.
review.fix: Skip lines that are blank or contain no `:`. You could also reject unknown keys, or at least ignore them explicitly. Separately, remove the stray blank line after the opening `---` in `prototyper.md` and `test-scope.md`.

review.impact: `INSTRUCTIONS_INCLUDE` hardcodes the path of werk's own repository (`@src/agent/instructions.md`). Through `includesInstructions`, it is also the only way the prompt module can tell it is running in werk's own checkout. That ties a general-purpose module to the layout of one repository. If the file moves, the AGENTS.md include and this constant drift apart, and werk's own agents get the instructions and subagents twice. Nothing flags it.
review.fix: Build the constant from the module's own location, for example `@${relative(repoRoot, join(import.meta.dir, 'instructions.md'))}`. Or add a test that reads this repository's AGENTS.md and asserts `includesInstructions(...)` is true, the same way `subagent-links.test.ts` checks this repository.

review.impact: The shipped subagents are listed by hand in two places that can drift apart. `SUBAGENT_TEXTS` names the files `prototyper` and `testScope` through imports. `scripts/subagent-links.ts` reads the `src/agent/subagents` folder itself. If someone adds a third `.md` file to that folder, the link check asks for a link to it, and the check that every subagent is named in the instructions still passes. But no agent receives the new subagent, because the check iterates over `shippedSubagents()`, which comes from this same hand-written list. Nothing fails.
review.fix: Add a test in `prompt.test.ts` that reads the names of the `*.md` files in `src/agent/subagents` and checks that they equal `Object.keys(shippedSubagents(WERK))`. The imports stay as they are, since Bun has to embed the files, but the list can no longer drift silently.

review.impact: Nothing in `src/` outside the tests calls `agentArgs`, `systemPrompt` or `subagentsFor`. No code that starts an agent passes `--append-system-prompt` or `--agents`. So the module is dead code for now. The commit says every map-writing agent gets the instructions, but that only holds once a caller exists.
review.fix: Connect `agentArgs(setup)` to the place where werk starts the claude process, or say in the header comment that the module is waiting for that caller. Then a later reader won't take it for wired-up behaviour or delete it as unused.

review.impact: `MAP_WRITERS`, `STAGE_AGENTS` and `BUILD_RULES_CARD` are exported, but nothing outside this module uses them, not even the tests. The extra exports make the module's public surface bigger than it needs to be.
review.fix: Remove `export` from these three constants until a caller needs them.

review.impact: `parseSubagent` builds a key from every front-matter line. A line with no colon gives `indexOf` -1, and the line is turned into a garbage key that is silently ignored. The shipped files start the front matter with a blank line, so every parse already adds an empty-string key. A malformed definition doesn't fail clearly; it just loses fields.
review.fix: Skip blank lines and throw on any other line that has no `:`. Also remove the blank line after the opening `---` in `prototyper.md` and `test-scope.md`.

review.impact: The ghost in this test has no status, and the fold gives a new node the status "open" when it has none (src/map/fold.ts:101). So the open-card filter already drops the ghost. Agents would then be told to follow build rules that the person never accepted, and no test in this pure file would catch it.

review.impact: The test title says option nodes are skipped, but the map has no option node in it. If someone deleted `node?.kind === "card"`, every test would still pass. A decided option under #how (a rejected alternative) would then show up as a build rule to follow.
review.fix: Add `added({ id: "how-x:opt0", parent: "how", kind: "option", title: "Rejected way" })` with status decided, and assert that the output does not contain "Rejected way".

review.impact: The test asserts that the decided child of the open card appears. It never asserts that the open card itself ("Title of draft") is left out. So if the status filter broke for open cards, nothing would show it except the ghost check, and that check is itself mixed up with the status filter.
review.fix: Add `expect(buildRuleTitles(map, WERK)).not.toContain("#draft")`.

review.impact: ruleLines calls childrenOf once for every card under the build-rules card. Each childrenOf call goes through linksTo, which filters every link in the map (allLinks(map).filter). It is cheap for maps of today's size, but it grows quadratically as a project's map grows.
review.fix: Build a parent-to-children index once: one pass over the refines links into a Map<string, string[]>. Walk that index in ruleLines instead of calling childrenOf at each level. Or add an indexed childrenOf to src/map/tree.ts if other callers need it too.

review.impact: The cover rule is checked only when the change is proposed, not when it is accepted. review.impact: The fold and the contract check use different tests to decide what a `change.accepted` event means. The fold uses `!node.proposed` and the contract uses `pending !== undefined`. review.impact: types.ts is the shared module of shapes and constants (`NODE_KINDS`, `STATUSES`, `WHOS`). It now imports from the logic module ops.ts, which reverses the existing dependency direction. Every module that imports types.ts now depends on ops.ts as well.

review.impact: After writing, the verb reads and folds the whole log a second time just to print the pending change. Every other verb prints from the map it already holds. This doubles the I/O and is a different pattern from accept and discard.

review.impact: The indent regex `.replace(/^(?=.)/gm, "    ")` is copied in `src/map/show.ts:64`. If the indent of quoted blocks changes in one place, the refusal text and the `show` diff will stop matching.

review.impact: `ghostRule` now also checks accepts and discards of a real node's pending change through `pendingRule`, so the name no longer says what it does. A reader looking for the pending-change rule will not look in a function called `ghostRule`.

review.impact: The tag list in the error message is built with the regex `OP_TAGS.join(", ").replace(/, (?=[^,]*$)/, " or ")`. It is hard to read for one fixed string.

review.impact: After writing, the verb reads and folds the whole log a second time just to get the node with its pending change. The folded map from before the write is thrown away, and that adds cost and a second code path for a value the verb already has.
review.fix: Build the output from the node already in hand: `formatPending({ ...map.nodes.get(id), pending: proposal })`, or have `write` return the folded map.

review.impact: The cover rule runs only when the change is proposed. `node.bodyEdited` is still allowed on an open card that has a pending change. If someone edits the body between the propose and the accept, `takePending` rebuilds the body from the old ops alone. Any block the edit added is silently dropped, and an op that quoted a block the edit removed comes back as new text. No test covers an accept after the body changed underneath the proposal, so a regression here, or the existing silent loss, goes unnoticed.
review.fix: Add a fold or rules test: add a body, propose ops, run `node.bodyEdited` with an extra block, then accept. Assert the chosen behaviour: either the accept is refused because the ops no longer cover the body (check `uncovered` again in `pendingRule` for verb accept), or the proposal is dropped when the body is edited. Do not let the test pin the current behaviour, where the block is lost.

review.impact: The fold comment says a later `change.proposed` replaces the pending one (#al-diff-cli), but no test proposes twice. If the fold merged the two proposals instead of replacing the first, for example by keeping the first proposal's title when the second changes only the why, every test would still pass.

review.impact: The amend check only looks for a pending change in the `before` map. If one write has both a `change.proposed` and a `change.accepted` for the same decided card, the card's words still change, but the accept is never marked `frozen`, so the decide facts never run. A decided card with a missing fact, such as no kill criterion, could then be amended without being refused. No verb writes that pair in one batch today, so this is not reachable yet. It is still a gap in validation that sits in pure code which anything calling `write` can hit.
review.fix: Mark `change.proposed` as `frozen` for its id in `changes()`, or fold the events one at a time and check `pending` on the running map rather than on `before`. Either way the amend check no longer depends on the pending change already being in the log.

review.impact: After writing, `werk propose` reads and folds the whole log a second time just to print the pending change. Every other verb folds it once, so a propose costs twice the fold time, and that cost grows as the log grows.

review.impact: `uncovered` splits the body into blocks twice: once inside `quotes` and again for the filter. review.impact: Two places indent text the same way: coverRule does it with `replace(/^(?=.)/gm, "    ")`, and formatPending repeats the same regex at src/map/show.ts:64. If one changes and the other doesn't, the refusal and the pending-change diff will show indented blocks differently.

review.impact: At the command line, nothing checks that `propose` refuses an `--ops` value that is valid JSON but has the wrong shape (for example `{}` or `[{"tag":"moved"}]`), or a proposal on a ghost. review.impact: `opsRule` checks only that each op has a known tag and that its required `old`/`new` fields are strings. Any other keys in an op are allowed through. Those keys come from `werk propose --ops` JSON or from a hand-edited log line, and they get written to the log as they are. Any future code that spreads or iterates an op will then pick them up. In the fold, `const { id, ...pending } = event.payload` (src/map/fold.ts:161) copies unknown payload keys into `node.pending` in the same way. Nothing reads these keys today, so the impact is limited to unvalidated data being stored.
review.fix: Make `opsRule` refuse an op that has keys outside its tag's shape (for example, `removed` allows only `tag` and `old`). In the `change.proposed` fold case, copy only `title`, `why` and `ops` into `pending` instead of spreading the rest of the payload.

review.impact: After `write`, the verb calls `readMap` a second time only to print the pending change. review.fix:
Keep the map you already folded and print from it: `const node = map.nodes.get(id); io.out(`${id}: proposed
${node === undefined ? "" : `${formatPending({ ...node, pending: proposal }).join("
")}
`}`)`. This is safe because `write` has already checked the proposal against that map. Then remove the second `readMap` call.

review.impact: `uncovered` runs `blocksOf(body)` twice, once inside `quotes` and once directly. `coverRule` calls `uncovered` for each `change.proposed` event and for each accept of a pending change during every fold, so each of those events scans and splits the body twice.

review.impact: The verb only checks that the root id exists. If the root is a ghost, a note, a removed node, or has no decided cards under it, decidedCardsUnder returns []. review.impact: This error does not match the wording other verbs use for a missing node. show.ts prints 'werk show: no node #<id> in the map', but this verb prints 'no node "<id>"'. The command line describes the same error two different ways.

review.impact: The Failure type is the data model shared by own-checks, set-checks and check, but it lives in the output-formatting module. Every checker imports from the report formatter. In the same way, set-checks takes TicketFields from own-checks. Both create coupling between modules that should be independent, which works against small single-purpose modules.
review.fix: Move Failure and TicketFields (and Counts if you like) into a small types module such as src/tickets/types.ts. Have report.ts, own-checks.ts and set-checks.ts all import from it.

review.impact: ownChecks adds the ticket field to failures in two places: the early return for a missing title and the final return. The `empty` fields object is also created on every call. Each new early exit has to remember to add the ticket name again, or its failures will print as 'ticket set'.
review.fix: Use one local helper, e.g. `const result = (fields) => ({ failures: failures.map(f => ({ ticket: file, ...f })), fields })`, and call it from both return points.

review.impact: Nothing reads `Failure.tickets`. Only `blockedBy` in set-checks.ts writes it; `formatFailure` and the verb ignore it, and only tests assert on it. It is a dead field, and every blocked_by failure has to fill it in alongside `ticket`.
review.fix: Remove `tickets` until a consumer for #st-ticket-partial lands. If it must stay, add the code that reads it in this change.

review.impact: The order check is written twice, once for header lines (61-66) and once for sections (67-72), with the same `some((line, i) => i > 0 && line < (xs[i - 1] as number))` and its cast. If one copy changes, the two can drift apart.
review.fix: Pull out a small `outOfOrder(lines: number[]): boolean` helper, or loop over the two cases from a table of [lines, field, names].

review.impact: `failures.map((failure) => ({ ticket: file, ...failure }))` appears twice in `ownChecks`, once on the early return and once at the end. That makes the function harder to follow.
review.fix: Add a local `const owned = () => failures.map(...)`, or have the check functions take `file` and push owned failures directly.

review.impact: The stack is popped by a `for` loop whose update clause is a ternary (`top = top === ticket ? undefined : stack.pop()`), which is hard to read. The cycle code also leans on many `as number` casts on `index`/`low` lookups.
review.fix: Pop with a plain `do { top = stack.pop() as SetTicket; part.push(top); } while (top !== ticket);`. Keep the index/low numbers on one `Map<SetTicket, {index, low}>` to drop the repeated casts.

review.impact: `(/^#+/.exec(lines[start] as string) as RegExpExecArray)[0].length` stacks two type assertions to get a value the `findIndex` regex already matched. The User-stories regex and the heading regex also overlap.
review.fix: Find the heading with a loop that keeps the match, e.g. `/^(#{1,6})[ \t]+User stories\s*$/i.exec(line)`, and read the level from its capture group instead of re-running a regex and casting.

review.impact: The extension pattern `\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,5}` is written both in `EXTENSION` and inline in `PATH`, so changing what counts as an extension means editing two places.
review.fix: Build `PATH` from `EXTENSION.source` (minus the `$`), or define a shared extension fragment that both regexes use.

review.impact: The size test uses only ASCII padding. It cannot tell counting code points (`[...text].length`) from counting UTF-16 units (`text.length`). If someone later 'simplifies' to `text.length`, a ticket with emoji or other astral characters would start failing size, and no test would catch it.
review.fix: Add a case padded with an astral character such as '😀' that reaches exactly SIZE_LIMIT code points but goes over it in UTF-16 units, and assert that it passes.

review.impact: `blockedBy` maps one ticket number to a list of tickets (for example `02-a.md` and `02-b.md`), but no test has two files with the same number. A regression that keeps only the last ticket per number, and so misses cycles or edges through the other file, would go unnoticed.
review.fix: Add a cycle test where two files share a number and only one of them is on the cycle. Assert that the cycle names that file and leaves out the other.

review.impact: The verb sends `formatProblems(map.problems)` to stderr before it checks the root, but every test uses a clean log with err "". If someone drops that line, map problems would be hidden silently, and no test would fail.
review.fix: Add a test that appends a malformed event to the log, such as `node.decided` for an unknown id. Assert that stderr carries the problem line and that the exit code still reflects the ticket verdict.

review.impact: `specStories` splits on `\r?\n` and matches the heading case-insensitively, but both tests use LF line ends and the exact casing. A regression in CRLF handling would make a Windows-edited spec report no stories or no heading, and no test would fail.
review.fix: Add a case with a CRLF spec and a lowercase heading like `## user stories`, and assert the story numbers it returns.

review.impact: The make-targets failure echoes the raw text of a Checks bullet into the report. The ticket file decides that text, and an agent may have written the file. If the text holds terminal control characters such as ANSI escape sequences, they reach the terminal of the person who runs `werk ticket-check`, and they can rewrite or hide earlier report lines. The no-file-paths match is not affected, because its pattern allows only word characters, `*`, `.`, `-` and `/`.
review.fix: Before putting `command` into the message, replace its control characters (for example `/[\u0000-\u001f\u007f-\u009f]/g`) with a visible escape. Another way is to quote it with `JSON.stringify` instead of `"${command}"`. Do the same for any other text from the ticket that a message echoes.

review.impact: In the Tarjan cycle search, `stack.includes(blocker)` scans the whole stack on every edge, so the search costs O(V·E) instead of O(V+E). `next(ticket)` is also built twice per node (lines 47 and 58). A ticket folder is small, so this costs little in practice.
review.fix: Track stack membership in a `Set<SetTicket>`: add on push, delete on pop, and test with `onStack.has(blocker)`. Compute `next(ticket)` once at the top of `visit` and reuse it.

review.impact: `byNumber.set(n, [...(byNumber.get(n) ?? []), ticket])` copies the array each time a ticket number repeats. That is quadratic in the number of tickets sharing a number, and the extra work is pure waste.
review.fix: Push onto the existing array: `const list = byNumber.get(n); if (list) list.push(ticket); else byNumber.set(n, [ticket]);`.

review.impact: No CLI test quotes against a node that exists but is not a card, such as an option or a source. The rules test covers that refusal, but nothing checks that the quote verb sends it to stderr with exit 1 and writes no line to the log.

review.impact: quoteRule only checks that `conversation` is a non-empty string. review.impact: quoteRule writes out its own copy of the citing-card check and its message, 'supported_by links a card to a source or an excerpt'. linkRule already makes this check. If the link rules change, a quote can drift from them: it may accept a link that `werk link` refuses, or show a different message.

review.impact: NodeFields now takes `& Partial<ExcerptPointer>`, so the type of every node.added and node.proposed payload accepts conversation, session, message and the other pointer fields. Those fields belong only on an excerpt, and only excerpt.quoted can write one. The type therefore no longer shows that a pointer comes only from a quote.
review.fix: Keep the pointer fields off NodeFields. Model the folded node as a union, or widen only the MapNode type that fold builds, for example `MapNode = NodeFields & Partial<ExcerptPointer> & {...}`, so that the event payload types stay narrow.

review.impact: The verb looks at the chat log before it reads the map. A quote that names both an unknown card and a missing chat log reports the chat log, not the card. Every quote also pays for a full transcript scan before it learns that the card is invalid. This order differs from the other verbs, which read the map first and validate against it.
review.fix: Read the map first and refuse an unknown or non-card target before resolving and scanning the chat log, or check the card with nodeOf before calling matchQuote.

review.impact: excerptId takes the first free `<card>:exN` by looking only at map.nodes. After someone discards an excerpt, the next quote on that card reuses the id. In fold, addNode then attaches the discarded excerpt's thread, with its notes and a 'proposed again' marker, to an unrelated quote.
review.fix: Skip ids that still have a thread in map.threads as well (`map.nodes.has(id) || map.threads.has(id)`), so that a new quote never inherits the history of a discarded one.

review.impact: The same ten-field `excerpt.quoted` payload is written out by hand three times in this file: at line 324, in the note test at line 468, and in the `quote` helper of the `an excerpt` block. It is also copied in removal.test.ts (the `quote` helper), stage.test.ts:72, notes-verbs.test.ts:51 and fold.test.ts:387. If the excerpt pointer changes shape, for example by gaining or renaming a field, about seven places must be edited in step. A missed copy fails with an unrelated rule message rather than pointing at the shape change.
review.fix: Move the `quote(extra)` helper in rules.test.ts to the top of the file and use it at lines 324 and 468. Better still, add one shared `quoted(id, card, extra?)` Draft builder next to the other test helpers (for example src/test/) and use it in removal.test.ts, stage.test.ts, notes-verbs.test.ts and fold.test.ts as well.

review.impact: `only.at[0] as number` and `lines[only.message] as ChatLine` are type casts that hide the checker's index-access warning. The code then reads the line from `lines` again even though the loop already had it. If the indexing logic changes later, the casts keep the compiler quiet about the error.
review.fix: Push the line into each hit (`hits.push({ message, line, at })`) and read `only.line`. Destructure the start with a guard (`const [start] = only.at; if (start === undefined) return { ok: false, reason: "no match" };`) or keep the cast only for the start, which the length check above guarantees.

review.impact: The `quote === ""` check runs inside the `forEach` callback, once per line, even though it does not depend on the line. Because the empty-quote case is folded into the per-line filter, a reader has to work out that it is a whole-function early exit.
review.fix: Return `{ ok: false, reason: "no match" }` at the top of `matchQuote` when `quote === ""`, and keep only the `kind !== "spoken"` check in the loop.

review.impact: The two `fold([...].map((e) => JSON.stringify(e)).join("\n"))` blocks repeat the same card and quote events and differ only by the accept event. fold.test.ts:421 repeats the same serialise-and-join pattern. That adds noise to a test whose point is the words rule.
review.fix: Build `quoted` once and derive `accepted` by adding the accept event to the same event list. Or reuse the file's existing `mapOf`/sequencing helper so that seq and serialisation are not written by hand.

review.impact: Of the four text fields in the pointer, the test only checks `session`, and of the three positions it only checks `start` (negative) and `message` (not an integer). If `conversation`, `speaker` or `said_at` were dropped from the key list in `quoteRule`, or if `end` were left out of the `isPosition` check, every test would still pass. A quote missing who said it, or one with a bad end offset, would then be accepted.
review.fix: Add assertions for `quote({ speaker: "" })`, `quote({ said_at: "" })` and `quote({ conversation: "" })`, and also for `quote({ end: -1 })` or `quote({ end: 2.5 })`. Each one should give its own refusal message.

review.impact: The verb's refusal tests cover an unknown card but not a card that exists and is not a card, such as quoting for the source or for `x:ex0` itself. A regression there would let an excerpt get attached to an excerpt or a source, and nothing at the command-line level would catch it.
review.fix: After the first successful quote, run `werk quote x:ex0 pricing "do we bill"`. Assert exit code 1, the `supported_by links a card to a source or an excerpt` refusal, and that the log did not grow.

review.impact: The verb always adds a node.decided draft when --status decided is given, even when the card is already decided. Stale marks usually land on decided dependents, so `werk rederive c --confirm b,d --status decided` on a decided card is refused as a whole by decideRule ('#c is already decided'). The confirm is lost with it, and the user gets a refusal about something they never asked to change.
review.fix: Add the decide draft only when map.nodes.get(id)?.status !== "decided". Report the card as already decided instead, so the confirm still applies.

review.impact: `settle` repeats the stale-to-rederive / open-to-decide command mapping that contract.ts basisGap writes out inline. If the commands change, the two places can drift apart, and the refusal and the contract gap would then suggest different fixes for the same basis problem.
review.fix: Export one `settleCommand(id, problem)` from marks.ts, next to basisProblem, and use it in both contract.ts and review.ts.

review.impact: listKind copies the precedence logic of markOf in marks.ts (stale, then paused, then waiting) without the postponed step. There are two sources of truth for how a card reads, and a change to one will not reach the other.
review.fix: Build listKind from markOf, mapping "postponed" to undefined or to the paused/waiting check, or make markOf take an option that skips postponed.

review.impact: basisProblem, unsettledBasis and waitingOn return the problem as a bare string. contract.ts, review.ts and stale.ts all branch on the literal "stale", so the compiler cannot catch a typo or a renamed value.
review.fix: Type the problem as a union ("stale" | "missing" | Status) and use it in every return type.

review.impact: moveChildren records a time for the moved link's key, but nothing deletes that entry when a restore moves the link back. If the card is removed with reparent a second time, `has` is still true and the old seq is reused. Marks made over the first moved link would then hold again over a link that was made anew.
review.fix: On restore, delete the linked entry of the moved link before pointing it back. Or always set the key to the current seq when a move makes a link that was not live before.

review.impact: The rule that a stale basis is fixed with `werk rederive <id>` and any other unsettled basis with `werk status <id> decided` is written twice: inline here and as `settle()` in src/map/review.ts:10. If the fix command for a basis changes in one place, `werk decide` and `werk rederive` will give different advice for the same problem.
review.fix: Export one helper, for example `settleCommand(id, problem)` in marks.ts next to `unsettledBasis`, and call it from both contract.ts and review.ts.

review.impact: `listKind` repeats the order from `markOf` in marks.ts (stale, then paused, then waiting) but leaves out postponed. The two now have to stay in step by hand, so a change to the order in one will quietly make `werk stale` and `werk show` disagree.
review.fix: Build `listKind` from `markOf`, for example `const mark = markOf(map, id); return mark === "postponed" ? (isPaused(map, id) ? "paused" : undefined) : mark;`. Or keep one ordered list of kinds that both functions read.

review.impact: `basisProblem`, `unsettledBasis` and `waitingOn` give the problem back as a plain `string`, but callers compare it to the literal "stale" (contract.ts, review.ts). The type checker cannot catch a typo or a renamed value in those comparisons.
review.fix: Type the problem as a union such as `NodeStatus | "missing" | "stale"` and use it in all three return types.

review.impact: `lastLink` casts `hops[hops.length - 1]` to a non-undefined element to get around the indexed-access check. A mark with no hops would crash here, and the cast hides that from the compiler.
review.fix: Use `mark.hops.at(-1)` and handle undefined, or type `hops` as a non-empty tuple (`[Hop, ...Hop[]]`) so the last element is always present.

review.impact: None of reopenRule's refusals is tested anywhere: reopening an open card, a ghost, a missing card, an unknown reason written straight to the log, or a `why` that is not text. The CLI test for `--reason later` is refused in the verb before the rule runs. If the `status !== "decided"` guard were dropped, reopening an open card would put marks on its neighbours again, and every test would still pass. rules.ts is on the pure list, and rules.test.ts never runs these new lines, so its own-file coverage also goes down (#werk-reflink-own-test-coverage).
review.fix: In rules.test.ts, add one case per refusal: reopen an open card, reopen a ghost, a reason of "later" in the payload, and a numeric `why`. Assert each exact message, and assert that the fold records the event as a problem.

review.impact: rederiveRule's own refusals are untested: a confirm on a ghost, and `confirmed` that is not a list of ids. review.test.ts covers confirmRefusal, but nothing in rules.test.ts checks that a `node.rederived` event goes through the rule. If the `case "node.rederived"` line in check() were deleted, any confirm would apply, and no test would fail.
review.fix: In rules.test.ts, fold a `node.rederived` whose link reason is not confirmed and assert it lands in map.problems. Add a ghost id case and a `confirmed: "b"` (string, not list) case, each with its message.

review.impact: The new basis-gap branch is untested. That branch is where a stale basis makes a card wait and the fix offered is `werk rederive <id>` rather than `werk status <id> decided`. contract.test.ts was not changed, so reverting to the old decided-only filter would make every test pass, and a card on a stale basis could be decided.
review.fix: In contract.test.ts, add a case where an open card's depends_on target is stale after a reopen. Assert the gap problem `#n waits on its basis: #b is stale` and the fix `werk rederive b`. Add a paused-basis case that asserts no basis gap (#pr-wf-paused-basis).

review.impact: An `edge.added` on a link that already exists is meant to keep its original `linked` seq, so marks that passed over it still hold. No test re-adds an existing link with a new reason after a reopen. If findLink were dropped and `linked` set on every add, a reason edit would silently erase stale and paused marks, and all tests would pass. The only nearby test removes the link first.
review.fix: In marks.test.ts or fold.test.ts: chain(), reopen("a"), then edge.added b→a depends_on with a new why. Assert isStale(map, "b") is still true and the hop's `linked` is still 7.

review.impact: moveChildren now gives a moved refines link a new seq and leaves the old key's time untouched, "so a restore brings its marks back". Neither half is tested. A child's stale mark should drop when its parent is removed with reparent, and should come back on restore. A regression either way, such as resetting `linked` on restore, would pass.
review.fix: Add a fold or marks test: reopen a parent so its child is stale, remove the parent with reparent and assert the child carries no mark from that hop, then restore and assert the mark is back.

review.impact: The amend path is tested only for a decided card that has a review sentence. Two cases are untested: (1) an accepted change on an open card, which must not mark the next hop (the early return), and (2) an amend with no `review`, whose marks must carry no text. If the `status !== "decided"` return were dropped, editing an open card's words would mark its dependents stale, and nothing would catch it.
review.fix: In marks.test.ts, add an accept on an open card and assert its dependents carry no mark. Add an amend without `review` and assert the mark's `text` is undefined.

review.impact: The `--status decided` path is untested at the CLI seam: confirm and decide in one call, printing two lines. So is the refusal of another `--status` value. A broken output join or a wrong draft order would go unnoticed.
review.fix: In marks-verbs.test.ts, run `werk rederive c --confirm b,d --status decided` on a stale, open card and assert the two output lines and the decided status. Assert that `--status open` exits 1.

review.impact: The ghost assertion is vacuous. The link g→a is held, not live, so carriers() never reaches g, and the test passes even without the `node.proposed` guard in marksOn. The test doesn't check what its name says.
review.fix: Build a ghost that already has a mark in map.marks, for example by putting a mark on it directly, or a reached card that is later turned back into a proposal if the log allows that. Otherwise drop the ghost half and keep the missing-card assertion.

review.impact: The new check that a proposal's `review` is text has no test, so removing it would go unnoticed.
review.fix: In rules.test.ts, add a change.proposed with `review: 5` and assert "a review sentence is text".

review.impact: `carriers` filters every link in the map each time it is called. `pauseDownstream` (line 57) calls it once for each card the breadth-first walk reaches, and it pulls from the queue with `queue.shift()`, which also costs O(n) per call. Each postponed reopen therefore costs O(cards × links) inside `fold`. Every werk command folds the whole log again, so every command pays this again for each postponement in history. On a map with thousands of cards, that is millions of link checks per command.
review.fix: Build one index from link target to incoming depends_on and refines links before the walk, either once per `pauseDownstream` call or kept on the folded map. Then walk the queue with a moving head index instead of `shift()`.

review.impact: `holds` scans all of `map.links` for every hop of every mark. Many callers repeat this work: `marksOn`, `isStale` and `isPaused`, and through them `markOf`, `listKind`, `waitingOn` and `unsettledBasis`. `basisProblem` also calls `isStale` once for each basis card. `formatStale` calls `listKind` for every node and then again for every marked node. A single `werk stale` therefore runs about O(nodes × (marks × hops + basis) × links) checks.
review.fix: Check whether a link is live with a Set of `linkKey(link)` built once per call, or kept on `FoldedMap`, instead of `map.links.some(...)`. In `formatStale`, compute `listKind` once per id and reuse the result.

review.impact: When a link is removed, `edge.removed` drops it, but the marks that rode on it stay in `map.marks`. Removed cards keep their marks too. Each later `marksOn` filters those dead marks out again, and `copyMap` copies them every time. On a long-lived log, `map.marks` only ever grows.
review.fix: When a link is removed, prune the marks whose hops include it (`keepMarks` with a `holds` check over the affected ids). Or accept the growth and leave it; it is minor.

review.impact: `fs.watch(dirname(log))` throws ENOENT when the project has no `.werk` folder yet. `werk serve` then fails with a raw 'ENOENT: no such file or directory, watch …' message instead of a werk error. Before that, Vite has already been created, so a failed start, here or at `http.listen` (port in use), never closes Vite, the watcher or the HTTP server. Any in-process caller, such as a test, leaks them. The command line exits only because `cli.ts` calls `process.exit`.
review.fix: Check that the log's folder exists before starting anything, and fail with a clear message such as 'werk serve: no .werk folder in this project'. Wrap the steps after `createVite` in try/catch, close what was already opened, then rethrow.

review.impact: The client hardcodes its own 'missing card' HTML (`data-missing=""`, different wording), separate from `missingHtml` in `src/serve/card-html.ts`. review.fix: Have `/api/card/:id` return `missingHtml(id)` as `html` when the card is not found (keeping `found: false` and the 404). The client then always does `target.innerHTML = card.html`.

review.impact: The header name is the literal "x-werk-token", although the server exports `TOKEN_HEADER` for it. Renaming it on one side silently breaks every note write with a 403.
review.fix: Move the constant into a small module that both sides can import (e.g. `web/api.ts`, next to `escape.ts`), or import it from there in both `server.ts` and `note-box.tsx`.

review.impact: This is the first time server code under `src/` imports from the client folder `web/` (`escape`, `md`, `reflink`), and `web/index.css` points back with `@source "../src/serve"`. The two sides of #werk-stack-layout now depend on each other in both directions, which blurs the module boundary.
review.fix: Treat the shared pure renderers as a deliberate shared module: move them to e.g. `src/render/` (or a `shared/` folder) that both `src/serve` and `web/` import. Alternatively, record the dependency direction in a comment pointing to the deciding card.

review.impact: Any unhandled error returns its full stack trace in the 500 response body, so the browser sees internal file paths. The server already logs nothing, so the person running it never sees the error either.
review.fix: Write the stack to the server's stderr and send a short 'werk: internal error' body.

review.impact: `handle` is one ~60-line async closure that does the Host check, the SSE channel, the card API, note POST parsing, validation and writing, page rendering and the Vite fallthrough. It keeps branching on method and path inline. Each new route makes it longer, and you can't test any one route on its own.
review.fix: Split each route into its own small function, for example `events(req, res)`, `cardApi(path, res)`, `postNote(req, res)` and `page(url, res)`, with the shared state (listeners, token, log, vite) passed in or closed over. Then make `handle` a short dispatcher that does the Host check and picks a route.

review.impact:
The client has its own copy of the missing-card markup (`

No card is in the map with this id.

`), separate from `missingHtml` in src/serve/card-html.ts. The two already say different words and use a different attribute value. So a page that is redrawn after a discard looks different from a page that was loaded fresh, and a change to one copy will miss the other.
review.fix: Have `/api/card/:id` return `missingHtml(id)` in `html` when the id is not found, and have `redraw` always set `target.innerHTML = card.html`. Then the missing-card markup exists in one place only.

review.impact: The client hardcodes the header name "x-werk-token", while the server exports `TOKEN_HEADER` for the same name. Renaming it on one side silently breaks every note write with a 403.
review.fix: Move `TOKEN_HEADER` into a small shared module that has no Node imports (for example web/token.ts), and import it from both server.ts and note-box.tsx.

review.impact: `title()` builds `new Set(map.nodes.keys())` on every call: once for the hero and once for each sub-card link through `nodeLink`. `cardHtml` already builds the same `known` set. This is duplicated work and two sources for the same value.
review.fix: Pass `known` into `title` and `nodeLink` from `cardHtml` instead of rebuilding it in `title`.

review.impact: The card API parses its id by building a fake `/map/...` path and running it through `idOfPath`. That only works because a fake address happens to match, and it would return HOME_ID for `/api/card/` if the route matching changed.
review.fix: Pull the decode step (decodeURIComponent wrapped in try/catch, rejecting '/') out of page.ts into a separate exported `decodeId(segment)`. Call it from both `idOfPath` and the card API.

review.impact: The expression `existsSync(log) ? statSync(log).size : 0` appears twice, once for the initial size and once in the watcher.
review.fix: Add a local `const logSize = () => (existsSync(log) ? statSync(log).size : 0);` and use it in both places.

review.impact: `Awaited<ReturnType<typeof startServer>>` restates a type that server.ts already exports as `Server`. It is harder to read and drifts from the named type.
review.fix: Write `import { type Server, startServer } from "../serve/server.ts"` and declare `let server: Server;`.

review.impact: `entries[0]?.seq as string` uses a type cast to hide the undefined case. If the inbox format changes so the regex matches nothing, the next calls get `undefined` as an argument and fail with a confusing message, not at the real cause.
review.fix: Assert that the entry exists first, for example `const first = entries[0]; if (first === undefined) throw new Error("inbox listed no notes");`, then use `first.seq` without the cast.

review.impact: No test covers any refusal path of the server, either in a unit test or in e2e/notes.e2e.ts. The e2e tests only use the happy path, so the note is always posted with the right token from a loopback page. You could delete the sameToken check, the loopback Host check (line 77, including the bracketed [::1] form in hostName), the 405 for non-POST, the 400 for bad JSON or a missing id/text, or the 422 Refused mapping, and every test would still pass. These checks are the #werk-serve-trust boundary, so a regression that opens the write endpoint to any page or host would go unnoticed.
review.fix: Add src/serve/server.test.ts. It should start startServer(log, 0) on a temp log, removed in afterEach, and send fetch requests that check: (a) a Host of evil.com gets 403, while localhost:PORT and [::1]:PORT pass; (b) POST /api/notes with no x-werk-token or a wrong token gets 403 and the log is unchanged; (c) GET /api/notes gets 405; (d) a body that is not JSON gets 400, and {id:1} gets 400; (e) a note on an id that store.write refuses gets 422 with the message; (f) the token taken from the served page's meta tag gets 200, and the log gains one note.added by actor you. Also check that GET /api/card/%E0 gets 400 and an unknown id gets 404 with found:false.

review.impact: Only the e2e redraw covers the live channel, and only indirectly. No test asserts that /api/events sends 'changed' when the log grows, or that a size-unchanged watch event sends nothing. No test checks that close() ends open event streams. If close() leaves a stream open, the server hangs on shutdown and the e2e tests won't notice, because they kill the process with SIGTERM.
review.fix: In the server unit test, open /api/events, append a line to the log, and assert that an 'event: changed' frame arrives. Then call close() and assert that the stream ends and that close resolves within the test time limit.

review.impact: No test covers the --port validation (non-numeric, >65535) or the startup failure path (a port already in use returns 1 with a message). A regression here, for example accepting '-1' or crashing instead of returning USAGE_ERROR, would pass.
review.fix: Add a verb test that runs `werk serve --port abc` and `--port 70000`, expecting USAGE_ERROR and the message. Also run it with a port already bound by a test listener, expecting exit 1 and 'werk serve:' on stderr.

review.impact: Each e2e test starts a server whose Vite cacheDir is tmpdir()/werk-vite-<hash of log path>. That directory sits outside the test's root, so afterEach never removes it. Each run leaves one cache directory per test in the person's tmpdir, which goes against #werk-test-store (each store is removed when the test ends).
review.fix: Make the cache directory a sibling of the log under the project (e.g. join(dirname(log), 'vite-cache')), or let a WERK env/option set it inside root, so rmSync(root) removes it.

review.impact: No test covers the pending-tag branch of cardHtml (node.pending), or a sub-card link whose child is not a ghost (no '(proposed)' suffix). If either breaks, no test fails.
review.fix: Add a pending node to the fixture map and assert the data-tag="pending" span. Also assert that a non-ghost child's link has no '(proposed)' after it.

review.impact: toContain("written") matches any output that contains that word, so it does not show that the note landed on the excerpt. The check that follows in the page covers this, but the assertion itself is close to vacuous.
review.fix: Drop the assertion, or match the exact confirmation line that `werk say` prints, including the id.

review.impact: `entry.actor` goes into both an attribute and the element's content without escaping. The log parser (`parseLine` in src/map/fold.ts) never checks `actor`, so a log line with an actor like `` is stored XSS. A log line can come from a teammate's merged log, or be appended by hand, as the e2e `seed` does. The script runs in a page that holds the write token, so it can post notes as "you" to /api/notes, which then show in the agent's inbox as the person's words. It can also read files that the Vite dev middleware serves. `node.kind` and `node.status` (line 54 onward) are also interpolated raw. They are safe today only because `rules.ts` validates them, so this is a hidden dependency.
review.fix: Wrap `entry.actor`, `node.kind` and `node.status` in `escapeHtml`. Better still, also reject an unknown actor in `parseLine` or `check` so the fold never trusts it.

review.impact: Vite's dependency cache goes in a directory under `os.tmpdir()` whose name anyone can work out: a SHA-1 of the log path. On Linux, /tmp is shared by every user. Another local user can create `/tmp/werk-vite-<hash>` first and plant pre-bundled dependency modules there. Vite then serves those modules to the person's browser on the page that holds the write token, so the attacker's code runs in that page and can post notes as the person.
review.fix: Put the cache in a directory owned by the user: under the project's `.werk/` folder, or `node_modules/.vite-werk-<hash>` in the werk checkout. Or create a fresh `mkdtempSync` directory for each start, with mode 0700.

review.impact: The length check counts characters, but `timingSafeEqual` compares bytes. A header with non-ASCII characters can pass the length check and still give buffers of different sizes. `timingSafeEqual` then throws a RangeError, and the client gets a 500 with a stack trace instead of a 403. It is not a bypass.
review.fix: Convert both values with `Buffer.from` first, compare the buffers' `byteLength`, and only then call `timingSafeEqual`.

review.impact: Every unhandled error sends its full stack trace, with absolute file paths, to the HTTP client. Only loopback hosts can make requests, so the exposure is small, but this is information disclosure.
review.fix: Write the stack to stderr and send a short generic message in the 500 response.

review.impact: `readBody` buffers the whole request body with no size limit. Any local process can send a huge POST to /api/notes, and the server holds it all in memory before it checks the token.
review.fix: Check the token first (it already is for /api/notes), and stop reading with a 413 once the body passes a cap such as 1 MB.

review.impact: The new dependencies use caret ranges (`^8.3.5`, `^19.3.1`, and so on), while the existing ones are pinned exactly (`2.6.3`, `1.64.1`, `7.0.2`). A lockfile refresh can quietly pull in new minor versions of a dev server that runs inside the werk process. Also, `src/serve/server.ts` imports `vite` at runtime but it is listed under devDependencies, so a production install can't run `werk serve`.
review.fix: Pin the new dependencies to exact versions, as the existing ones are. Move `vite`, `@vitejs/plugin-react`, `@tailwindcss/vite` and `tailwindcss` to `dependencies`, since `werk serve` needs them at runtime.

review.impact: title() builds a new Set from every id in the map each time it is called. nodeLink calls it once per sub-card, so rendering a card costs O(children × nodes). The live channel redraws the card on every log change, so a card with many children on a large map pays this cost on each write. cardHtml already builds the same set as `known` at line 52.
review.fix: Have title() and nodeLink() take the `known` set as a parameter, and pass in the one that cardHtml builds, instead of rebuilding it from map.nodes.keys() on each call.

review.impact: Every 'changed' signal makes every open page call /api/card, and each call runs readMap: it reads and folds the whole log and appends a line to the fold-times file. With N tabs open, one write costs N full folds of the log, all for the same log state.
review.fix: Keep the last folded map in the server, keyed on the log size the watcher already tracks. Fold again only when the size changes, and use the cached map for /api/card, /api/notes and the page routes.

review.impact: After a note is sent, onSent() redraws the card, and the watcher's 'changed' event for the same write triggers a second redraw. The result is two /api/card requests and two full log folds for one note.
review.fix: Drop the onSent redraw and let the live channel update the card, or skip the redraw that follows when one is already in flight.

review.impact: readBody keeps every chunk of the request body in memory with no limit. A large POST to /api/notes, even from a loopback client that holds the token, gets fully buffered before it is parsed.
review.fix: Cap the body size (for example 1 MB). Stop reading and answer 413 once the running total passes the cap.

causeOfLast.why: pass 1 added the Options and Ev sections, but the ticket's two scenarios ask only for the excerpt under the card.

review.impact: The second fixture wraps its drafts in an array, casts it with `as Draft[]` and spreads it. That cast is a type escape hatch: the compiler stops checking the fixture's shape against `Draft`, so a typo in an event type or a payload field would still compile. The first fixture in the same test passes its drafts straight to `mapOf` without a cast, so the two calls are written differently for no reason.
review.fix: Pass the three drafts to `mapOf(...)` as direct arguments, the way the first fixture does, and drop the `...([ ... ] as Draft[])` wrapper. Then remove the `Draft` import if nothing else uses it.

review.impact: `sayLines` uses `.filter((node) => node.kind === "excerpt")` to leave sources out of the Say section, but no test covers a card that is supported_by a source. If the filter is removed or changed, a card citing a source would print a line like `  s  undefined: "Survey"`, and every test would still pass. A missing `to` node (the `?? []` branch) is also never tested.
review.fix: In src/map/show.test.ts, add a case where a card is supported_by both a source and an excerpt. Assert the full output with `toBe`, so the Say section lists only the excerpt and the source appears only as its `-> supported_by` link line.

review.impact: Both new tests use only one excerpt. Nothing checks how a Say section with several excerpts is ordered, or that a mix of ghost and live excerpts marks each one correctly. A change that prints only the first excerpt, or that puts `proposed` on the wrong line, would not be caught.
review.fix: Add a card with two excerpts, one accepted and one still a ghost. Assert both Say lines in link order, with `proposed` only on the ghost.

review.impact: The Say line prints the excerpt's `speaker` and `title` exactly as they appear. Both come from quoted chat transcripts. If a quote contains a newline, a carriage return or an ANSI escape sequence, it can fake extra lines in `werk show` output, such as a false `proposed` marker or a fake excerpt, or send control sequences to the terminal. Link lines already print titles without escaping, so this adds to an existing exposure rather than opening a new class of problem.
review.fix: Before interpolating `speaker` and `title`, escape or strip control characters (C0/C1, including \n, \r and \x1b), for example by replacing them with their JSON-escaped form. Put this in one shared helper so link lines and thread lines can use it too.

grade.gap: The listing gives the origin, the change kind and the day, and puts a basis first (src/map/stale.ts reasonLines and fixOrder). It does not print the reopen or amend text, so 'reason' only shows as the change kind. This passes if 'reason' means the change kind. If the reopen sentence is meant, add mark.text to the line.
