These go slightly past the criteria, but stories 38, 42 and 44 cover them: `werk rederive --status decided` (src/verbs/rederive.ts), the `--kind` filter and subtree scope of `werk stale` (src/verbs/stale.ts), and refusing a confirm while the basis is open or stale (src/map/review.ts). No clear out-of-scope behaviour.

The builder named only #werk-test-pure-list-union and #werk-verb-registry, but the diff makes choices that neither card gives:
(1) Link identity by creation seq (FoldedMap.linked, src/map/marks.ts holds). A mark drops when its link is removed and does not come back when the link is made again. A refines link moved by remove/restore counts as a new link (src/map/fold.ts moveChildren).
(2) A reopen with no reason defaults to 'invalidated' (fold.ts node.reopened, src/verbs/reopen.ts).
(3) Only a decided card may be reopened, and a ghost may not (rules.ts reopenRule).
(4) Accepting a change on a decided card is an amend: it clears the card's stale marks and marks the next hop, carrying a new Proposal.review sentence set by `werk propose --review` (fold.ts change.accepted, types.ts Proposal, src/verbs/propose.ts).
(5) A confirm is refused while the basis is open or stale (src/map/review.ts), and the stale fix command is `werk rederive <id>` (contract.ts basisGap).
(6) The event names node.reopened and node.rederived, and the data shape payload.confirmed as a list of ids, given on the command line as comma-separated `--confirm`.
(7) The postponed mark shows only while the card is open and its latest reopen was postponed (marks.ts isPostponed). Node.reopen stays after a decide.
(8) A marked card does not also read as waiting, and markOf ranks stale > postponed > paused > waiting. `werk show` prints the mark word in the header.
(9) The flagged-row note wording, including the 'further upstream' pointer (trace.ts flagNote).
The next pass should name the cards these come from (e.g. #rederive-reason, #werk-cli-reopen, #vi-prop-amended, #werk-depwhy, #map-wait, #vi-prop-bornstale) or propose cards for the ones no card gives, especially (1) and (2).

The card describes postponed as fanning out along the reverse depends_on closure. pauseDownstream (src/map/marks.ts carriers) also follows refines to children. #pr-wf-paused's 'every card downstream' and #vi-prop's children rule allow this, so it is not a contradiction.

The walk visits each card once, breadth first, and the trace lists the cards between, nearest to the origin first. The last-hop line is 'last hop: s -> r depends_on: <why>', not the card's 'last hop: depends_on'. It carries more but has the same content.

causeOfLast.why: #werk-serve-trust defines the refusals clearly, and the earlier pass wrote them without tests that would catch a regression.

review.impact: The runtime server code imports `vite`, and `vite.config.ts` imports `@vitejs/plugin-react` and `@tailwindcss/vite`, but package.json lists all three as devDependencies. An install without devDependencies has a `werk serve` that fails at import. This also ties the CLI's runtime to the dev toolchain even though `build.outDir` (dist/client) is set up and never used.
review.fix: Either move vite and its plugins into `dependencies`, or start Vite only in dev and serve the built `dist/client` otherwise. Load Vite with a dynamic import so the server module does not depend on it unconditionally.

review.impact: startServer has no cleanup when start-up fails. If `fs.watch` throws (for example, `.werk/` does not exist yet in a fresh project, so `werk serve` dies with a raw ENOENT 'watch' error) or `http.listen` rejects (port in use), the Vite server and its file watchers, and the fs watcher, are left open. The CLI hides this because it calls process.exit, but any in-process caller, such as the tests, leaks them and can hang.
review.fix: Create the log directory (mkdirSync recursive) before watching it. Wrap everything after createVite in try/catch, and on failure close the watcher and Vite before rethrowing.

review.impact: The client builds its own 'missing card' HTML (`data-missing=""`, different wording) instead of using the server's `missingHtml(id)`. A card that is discarded while the page is open therefore looks different from loading its address directly, and the two copies will drift apart.
review.fix: Have `/api/card/:id` return `missingHtml(id)` as `html` when the card is not found, and have `redraw` always insert `card.html`.

review.impact: The token header name is hard-coded as the string "x-werk-token" in the client, while the server exports `TOKEN_HEADER`. Renaming it on one side breaks every note silently, with a 403.
review.fix: Put the header name in a shared module under web/ (like escape.ts) and import it in both server.ts and note-box.tsx.

review.impact: Unexpected errors return the full stack trace in the HTTP body, which mixes up diagnostics with the API's `{error}` JSON shape. The client's `response.json()` fallback then shows a bare status code.
review.fix: Log the stack to stderr and answer 500 with `json(res, 500, { error: message })` for /api routes.

review.impact: The client has its own copy of the 'no card' markup, and its wording and empty data-missing attribute differ from missingHtml in src/serve/card-html.ts:81. So a card that disappears while the page is open renders differently from the same card loaded fresh, and a change to one copy will not reach the other. This happens because /api/card returns html "" for an unknown id, which leaves the fallback to the client.
review.fix: Make /api/card return `html: html ?? missingHtml(id)` in src/serve/server.ts, so the server renders the missing-card markup in one place. Then live.ts can always set `target.innerHTML = card.html`.

review.impact: `handle` is one ~60-line async closure that does the Host check plus four routes (events, card API, notes, page) and the Vite fallback. Each route has its own early returns and try/catch. It is hard to read and grows with every new route, which works against #werk-stack-modules (small, single-purpose modules).
review.fix: Pull the route bodies out into named functions, such as `events(req, res)`, `cardApi(res, path)`, `postNote(req, res)` and `page(res, url)`. Have `handle` only check the Host header and dispatch, or put the note route in its own module.

review.impact: The token header name is hard-coded as the literal "x-werk-token", while the server exports TOKEN_HEADER for the same value. If either side renames it, notes are silently refused with 403.
review.fix: Move TOKEN_HEADER into a small shared module that both the server and the client can import (for example under web/), and use it in note-box.tsx.

review.impact: The expression `existsSync(log) ? statSync(log).size : 0` appears twice, at lines 66 and 69.
review.fix: Add a small `const sizeOf = () => (existsSync(log) ? statSync(log).size : 0)` and call it in both places.

review.impact: `Awaited<ReturnType<typeof startServer>>` restates a type that server.ts already exports as `Server`, which makes the code harder to read.
review.fix: Import `type Server` from ../serve/server.ts and declare `let server: Server;`.

review.impact: Nothing uses the `outline` and `ghost` variants, the `sm` size or the `asChild`/Slot path. That leaves dead code, plus a runtime dependency (@radix-ui/react-slot) that only the unused path needs.
review.fix: Cut the Button down to the variant and size that are used and drop asChild and @radix-ui/react-slot. Or add them back when a screen needs them.

review.impact: None of the new `werk serve` verb's paths has a test. These include the --port check (non-numeric, above 65535), the exit code 1 when startServer fails (for example, the port is already taken), the printed URL line and the stop on SIGTERM. The e2e harness only uses the happy path through a regex on stdout. A regression in the usage-error code or the port check would pass every check.
review.fix: Add a verb test that uses the project harness. It should assert that `werk serve --port abc` and `--port 70000` exit with USAGE_ERROR and print the message. It should start `werk serve --port <taken port>` and assert exit 1 with a `werk serve:` error. It should start `werk serve --port 0`, read the `http://127.0.0.1:N/map` line, send SIGTERM, and assert exit 0 with 'stopped on SIGTERM'.

review.impact: Each startServer call in server.test.ts (six tests) and in each e2e test writes a Vite cache to `tmpdir()/werk-vite-<hash of log path>`. The log path is a fresh temporary directory every time, so each test run leaves new directories behind that nothing removes. This breaks #werk-test-store: each test must write to its own copy of every store, removed when the test ends.
review.fix: Remove cacheDir in Server.close(). Or put the cache inside the project's `.werk` directory (or let startServer take a cacheDir), so that the test's project cleanup removes it.

review.impact: The Host test covers a foreign host and the three loopback names. It does not cover a request with no Host header, an uppercase `LOCALHOST`, or a bracketed host that is not loopback (for example `[::2]:port`). These are the edge cases of hostName's parsing, so a regression there would not be caught.
review.fix: Add assertions: a request with the host header removed gets 403, `LOCALHOST:port` gets 200, and `[::2]:port` gets 403.

review.impact: The live channel (/api/events and the log watcher that sends 'changed' only when the log grows) has no unit test. It is only exercised indirectly through the e2e redraws, so a broken 'no signal when the size is unchanged' path, or a listener that is never removed on close, would go unnoticed outside the browser suite.
review.fix: Add a server test that opens /api/events, appends to the log through write(), and asserts that a `event: changed` frame arrives. Also assert that close() ends the stream.

review.impact: The `pending` tag branch of cardHtml (`data-tag="pending"`) is never rendered by any test. A regression in the pending marker would pass.
review.fix: Add a node with pending set to the fixture map (or build one directly) and assert that `<span data-tag="pending"` is present, and absent on a node that is not pending.

review.impact: The excerpt test filters the notes by text and checks the author, but it never asserts that exactly one such note exists. A duplicate render would fail Playwright's strict mode only by accident, not through a clear assertion.
review.fix: Add `await expect(note).toHaveCount(1);` before the author check, as the first test does.

review.impact: Vite's dependency cache goes into a predictable folder in the shared temp directory: a hash of the log path, which anyone can work out. On a machine with a shared /tmp (Linux), another local user can create `werk-vite-<hash>` first and put modified pre-bundled modules in it. Vite would then serve those modules into the person's page as trusted code. That code can read the werk-token meta tag and post notes in the person's name.
review.fix: Put the cache in a folder only this user can write. Two options: a folder under the project's `.werk/` (or the user's cache folder), or a folder from `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'werk-vite-'))` that is removed on close. If a fixed path stays, refuse to use it when its owner or mode is wrong.

review.impact: `readBody` reads the whole request body into memory with no size limit. The body is read only after the token check, so the risk is small, but a buggy or hostile local client holding the token can make the server hold any amount of data. The note text also has no length limit before it is written to the log for good.
review.fix: Stop reading after a fixed size, such as 1 MiB, and answer 413. Optionally also refuse a note whose text is longer than a set limit.

review.impact: An unhandled error sends the full stack trace to the client in the 500 reply. That shows absolute file paths and internal details to any page that reaches the server.
review.fix: Write the stack to stderr and send only a short message in the 500 reply.

review.impact: `entry.actor` (and `node.kind` and `node.status` at line 54) go into HTML text and attributes without escaping, while the id and the text next to them are escaped. These values come from the log file, which can be edited by hand, so an odd value would be written into the page as raw HTML.
review.fix: Wrap `entry.actor`, `node.kind` and `node.status` in `escapeHtml`, the same as the other values from the log.

review.impact: The new dependencies use caret ranges, but every existing dependency is pinned to an exact version (`@biomejs/biome` 2.6.3, `typescript` 7.0.2). The lockfile pins what gets installed, but a lock refresh can silently pull in new minor versions of vite, react and the rest. vite and its plugins run code inside the server process.
review.fix: Pin the new dependencies to exact versions, the same as the existing ones, so that each upgrade is a reviewed change.

review.impact: title() builds a new Set of every node id in the map each time it runs. nodeLink calls it once per sub-card, and cardHtml calls it again for the hero. A card with C children in a map of N nodes therefore costs O(C×N) allocations on every page load, every /api/card fetch and every live redraw. cardHtml has already built the same `known` set.
review.fix: Pass the `known` set that cardHtml builds into title() and nodeLink(), and drop the per-call `new Set(map.nodes.keys())`.

review.impact: Every write to the log sends a 'changed' signal to every open page. Each page then fetches /api/card, and each fetch calls readMap, which reads and folds the whole log and appends a line to the fold-times file. With T tabs open, one write costs T full folds of the log, and that grows with the log's length.
review.fix: Cache the folded map in the server and key it by the log size the watcher already tracks. Fold again only when the size changes, so /api/card, the page route and the note write share one fold per log change.

review.impact: After a note is sent, onSent redraws the card directly. The log append also fires the watcher's 'changed' signal, which redraws it again, so each note costs two /api/card requests and two server-side folds.
review.fix: Drop the onSent redraw and rely on the live channel, or skip the next 'changed' redraw when it follows the page's own write.

review.impact: readBody buffers the whole request body with no size limit, so a large POST to /api/notes with a valid token is held in memory in full before it is parsed.
review.fix: Cap the body size (for example 1 MB). Count bytes while reading, and answer 413 and stop reading once the cap is passed.

grade.gap: The diff is empty: commit 3c74be8 'werk build werk/50: pass 1' changes no files. Nothing in it makes every form of a reference (#al-diff, bare al-diff, `al-diff`, `#al-diff`) into the same monospace link to /map/al-diff. web/reflink.ts and web/md.ts already exist from earlier work. review.impact: `moveChildren` gives a link a new time only when its key is not already in `map.linked`, and a restore never deletes the key of the link the removal created. If a1 is later removed with reparent again, the new a2→a link reuses the old seq, so `holds()` accepts the old mark and it comes back on a link made later. This breaks #vi-prop-same-link.

When `node.restored` moves them back, delete the key of the link that is going away (`children→moved.to`), and keep the original key's seq so its marks return. review.impact: `pauseDownstream` calls `carriers()` once for every card it reaches, and each call filters every link in `map.links`. A single postponement therefore costs O(cards × links) while the log folds. `queue.shift()` adds a further O(n) per step. On a large map, a postponement near the root makes every fold of the log noticeably slower.
review.fix: Before the BFS, build one index from each target id to its incoming depends_on/refines card links (a Map<string, Link[]>), then look each card up in it. Walk the queue with an index (`for (let i = 0; i < queue.length; i++)`) instead of calling `shift()`.

review.impact: `formatStale` calls `listKind` twice for every marked card: once in the filter and again in the map step. Each call can run `marksOn` up to three times, plus `waitingOn` → `unsettledBasis` → `isStale` for each basis card. Each `marksOn` checks every hop with `map.links.some` (in `holds`), so `werk stale` over the whole map costs roughly O(cards × marks × hops × links), with work repeated for no reason.
review.fix: Compute `listKind` once per id, keeping pairs such as `[id, kind]`, and reuse the result when printing. Inside `listKind` and `markOf`, call `marksOn` once and derive stale/paused from that one array instead of calling `isStale`, `isPaused` and `waitingOn` separately.

review.impact: `status as Status` appears twice (lines 19 and 31), and `String(status)` is used to get past the `string | true` flag type. These casts skip the type checker: the narrowing done by the `includes` check is not carried to line 31.

review.impact: The new test only covers a verb whose single positional repeats. It never covers a fixed positional followed by a repeating one, for example `[id, term...]`, or a required (non-optional) repeating positional given no arguments. A regression in the `specs.at(-1)` fallback or the `missing` check for those shapes would still pass.
review.fix: Add a case with `positionals: [{name:'id', value:'id'}, {name:'term', value:'text', repeats:true}]`. Assert that `['#a','x','y']` parses to `['a','x','y']`. Also assert that a required repeating positional with no argument returns `needs <term>`.

review.impact: The failure-path tests check only that the exit code is 1. They would still pass if the command failed for an unrelated reason, such as a parse error or a crash in readMap, and not because of the status or subtree check.
review.fix: Also assert `run.err` contains `the status is one of` for the bad status, and `no node #missing` for the missing subtree and for `find missing`.

review.impact: An empty search term is never rejected. Running `werk search ""` or `werk search seat ""` lowercases the term to "", and `text.split("")` then splits the text into single characters. Every card counts as a match, and the empty term adds about as many hits as the card's text has characters. The ranking then favours whichever card has the longest text, not the most hits of the real terms.
review.fix: Drop blank terms before matching, e.g. `terms.map((t) => t.toLowerCase()).filter((t) => t.trim() !== "")` in formatSearch, and fall back to the index when no term is left. Or have `occurrences` return 0 for an empty term, or make the search verb reject a blank term with exit code 1.

review.impact: `wordsOf` filters all of `map.links` again for every card, so a search costs O(cards × links). Each search is a single CLI run over a map of hundreds of cards, so this is fast today. It will grow quadratically as the map grows.
review.fix: In `formatSearch`, make one pass over `map.links` before the card loop. Build a `Map<cardId, string[]>` from each `alternative_to` target to its options' why-not text, then read from that map inside `wordsOf`.

review.impact: `roots` calls `parentOf` for every node, and each `parentOf` call scans `allLinks(map)`, which copies `links` and `ghostEdges` into a new array. A bare `werk find` therefore costs O(nodes × links) and allocates one array per node.
review.fix: Collect the `from` ids of every `refines` link into a `Set` once. Then keep the real cards whose id is not in that set.

So showing a card near the root costs about 2 × O(subtree × links + subtree²). That is fine for the map sizes werk has today, but it grows quadratically as the map grows.

The PATH regex in src/tickets/own-checks.ts now also catches paths that start at the root (/etc/werk.conf) or the home folder (~/notes/d.md), and paths inside * or _ emphasis. review.impact: The emphasis group and the path body both accept `*` and `_`, so when the markers don't match, the backtracking moves a stray marker into the reported path. For example, `**src/a.ts*` reports `*src/a.ts`. The check still fails the ticket, but the message names a path that isn't in the text. The comment says nothing about this case.

review.impact: `match.groups?.path` uses optional chaining for a group the regex always captures. If PATH is later edited and the group is renamed, the message quietly becomes `line N: undefined` and nothing fails.

This doesn't match the one-behaviour-per-test style of the tests around it, and any change to the summary format breaks the test.

review.impact: `match.groups?.path` has type `string | undefined`, so the optional chaining hides a case that cannot happen. If the group were ever renamed, the message would quietly read `line 9: undefined` and no error would point to the cause.
review.fix: Read the group by position (`match[2]`), or assert it is present (`match.groups!.path` or a guard that throws), so a renamed group fails loudly.

review.impact: The extension pattern `\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,5}` is now written out inside PATH and again in EXTENSION on line 24. If someone changes the allowed extension length in one place, the two checks will disagree.

review.impact: One test covers two unrelated behaviours: a path inside emphasis and an oversized ticket. It also uses `slice(0, -2)` with no comment to drop the summary lines. When it fails, you can't tell which behaviour broke, and it is harder to read.

review.impact: The assertion that no failure mentions `Makefile` can never fail, with or without the change. review.impact: Nothing tests emphasis that does not match, such as `**src/a.ts*`. review.impact: If no .werk folder exists, logPath() returns <cwd>/.werk/log.jsonl. openSync(..., 'wx') in takeLock then fails with ENOENT, and the verb rethrows every error that is not LockHeld. `werk serve` now crashes with a raw stack trace. Before this change, the same failure happened inside startServer's try and printed a clean 'werk serve: …' message with exit code 1. openProject's mkdirSync runs too late to help.

review.impact: setPort rewrites the lock in place with writeFileSync, which first empties the file and then writes it. create() leaves a similar gap between openSync and writeSync. A competing start that reaches its deadline during either gap sees text that does not parse and treats it as a dead holder's lock. It removes the live server's lock and takes it, so two servers run on one store. That breaks the one-server-per-store guarantee this module exists for. The window is narrow but real when two starts overlap, which is the case the lock is for.
review.fix: Write the port to a temporary file next to the lock and renameSync it over the lock, so a reader always sees a complete holder. For the create gap, check the empty lock's mtime: only treat it as stale after it has stayed unparsable for longer than a short grace period, not only when the wait ends.

review.impact: If the lock disappears between the failed create and the read, `continue` retries without sleeping or checking the deadline. Normally the next create succeeds, but a filesystem where the read keeps failing for another reason, such as EACCES, makes this a tight spin that never times out.
review.fix: Only `continue` without sleeping when read failed with ENOENT. For any other read error, fall through to the deadline check and the sleep.

review.impact: The `projects` Map always holds exactly one entry and is only used to close it. It adds a layer for future multi-project support without using it yet, and every other line in the handler uses `project` directly.
review.fix: Drop the Map and call project.close() in close() until a second project actually exists.

review.impact: The card endpoint now folds the map once and builds both the HTML and the structured card read, so each card request does the work of two renderers. It also returns two parallel representations of the same card.
review.fix: Settle which one the client consumes. If both are kept for now, add a short comment saying the html field is going away.

review.impact: `if (text === undefined) continue;` goes back to the top of the loop without sleeping and without checking the deadline. If the lock file exists but cannot be read (EACCES, or EISDIR when it is a directory), `create` gets EEXIST and `read` returns undefined every time. takeLock then spins at 100% CPU forever and never throws LockHeld. Because `read` swallows every error, it also hides why it failed.
review.fix: Retry without sleeping only for ENOENT (the holder released the lock between create and read). For any other read error, either rethrow it or fall through to the deadline check and `Bun.sleep(POLL_MS)` like the unparseable case. A simple way: have `read` return undefined only for ENOENT and rethrow everything else.

review.impact: The `projects` map always holds exactly one entry, `project`, and it is only read in `close()`. This is speculative code for a multi-project future that does not exist yet. Readers have to work out why there is both a map and a single `project`.
review.fix: Drop the map and call `project.close()` in `close`. Add the map when a second context actually joins.

review.impact: `isAlive` is exported, but only this module uses it, so the module's public surface is larger than it needs to be.

review.impact: `mark?: ReturnType<typeof markOf>` couples the public API type to a function signature instead of a named type. That makes it harder to read and easier to change by accident.

review.impact: The card endpoint now runs both `cardRead` and `cardHtml` for every request and sends the card twice, once as structured data and once as HTML. That is two sources of truth for the same card, and they can drift apart.

review.impact: One new failure path has no test: when startServer throws after the lock is taken, serve.ts calls lock.release(). If that call is removed or moved, no test fails. A port that is already in use would then leave a serve.lock naming a live process. A later start on the same store would wait and refuse until that process exits, or forever if the process lives on.
review.fix: Add a test to src/verbs/serve.test.ts. Bind a port with a plain listener, then start `werk serve --port <that port>`. Check that the start exits 1, that it prints the error, and that `.werk/serve.lock` no longer exists afterwards.

review.impact: The test 'a write made before the server started shows in the first read after connect' passes without this change and without #werk-write-watch-start. Every read loads the log from disk on each request. So the test cannot catch a watch that starts late or misses writes. The named behaviour has no real check.
review.fix: Write to the log after startServer returns and before the page connects, then check that the first read shows the write. Also cover the race that #werk-write-watch-start is for: write between openProject and the first connect, and check that a later write still sends exactly one changed frame. Otherwise rename the test so it does not claim that card.

review.impact: No test covers ProjectContext.close(), which stops the watcher and ends every open live channel. That code moved into project.ts in this change. If close() stops ending the channels or closing the watcher, nothing fails, and on shutdown open SSE responses could hang or a watcher could leak.
review.fix: Add a test in server.test.ts: connect a live channel, call server.close(), and check that the channel's response emits 'end'. Or test openProject directly: call close(), then append to the log, and check that no frame arrives.

review.impact: Clearing a stale lock is a check-then-act race. Starts A and B can both read a lock left by a dead pid. A removes it and creates its own lock. B then runs remove(path) on what it still believes is the stale file, deletes A's live lock, and creates its own. Two servers end up writing the same store, which breaks the one-server-per-store guarantee (#werk-onelock) and lets their writes to the log interleave.
review.fix: Make the takeover atomic and conditional. One way is to rename the stale file to a unique name (for example serve.lock.<pid>.<random>), check that the renamed file still holds the dead holder's text, and only then delete it and retry create(). If the renamed text differs, rename it back or retry. Another way is to re-read the lock just before unlinking and unlink only when the text matches what was judged stale; this is still racy but the window is much smaller. An OS advisory lock (flock) on a file that is never deleted would remove the race entirely.

review.impact: parse() accepts any JSON number as the port: non-integers, negatives and values above 65535. A lock file that has been tampered with or truncated can therefore make LockHeld report a meaningless port. The value is only interpolated into a message and is not used to connect, so the effect is limited.
review.fix: Keep the port only when Number.isInteger(value.port) && value.port > 0 && value.port <= 65535, and drop it otherwise.

review.impact: WERK_LOCK_WAIT_MS accepts any string of digits, so a very large value such as 99999999999999999999 sets a deadline in the far future. A start that finds a live holder then polls forever and never refuses.
review.fix: Cap the parsed value (for example at 60000 ms), or fall back to LOCK_WAIT_MS when the number is not a safe integer within a sensible bound.

review.impact: shapeRead calls rollupOf once for every node. Each call walks that node's whole refines subtree through descendantsOf. That walk calls childrenOf for every node it visits, and each childrenOf call copies allLinks and filters the whole copy. The walk also checks for repeats with out.includes, which is O(n), and calls isStale, which runs marksOn and then holds, and holds scans map.links. So one shape read costs about O(N · depth · E), plus a new array for every visit. Pages fetch this read after every changed signal, and every open page gets that signal on each log growth. The read that was meant to stay cheap therefore gets more than linearly slower as the map grows, and that work is repeated for each open page.
review.fix: Compute every rollup in one bottom-up pass. Build the children index once from map.links and map.ghostEdges, visit the cards in post-order, work out each card's own counts once (status, unchallenged, and isStale called once per card), and add each child's rollup into its parent's. Keep rollupOf for single-card reads, and give shapeRead a new rollupsOf(map): Map<string, Rollup>.

review.impact: When create fails with EEXIST but read cannot open the file, for example because of EACCES or EISDIR, the `continue` runs before both the deadline check and the sleep. takeLock then retries create and read in a tight synchronous loop with no end. `werk serve` hangs at 100% CPU instead of refusing when the wait runs out.
review.fix: Retry at once only when the read failed with ENOENT, which means the holder released the lock between the create and the read. Rethrow any other error, or treat it like an unparsed lock: check the deadline and sleep POLL_MS before the next try.

review.impact: The card API now computes cardRead and cardHtml for every request. Both of them work out marks and the rollup, and look up neighbours, on the same map. Each card read pays for two derivations, and the client uses only one of them.
review.fix: Return only the structured card, and render the HTML on the client. If html must stay for now, have cardHtml take the CardRead that has already been computed, so the marks, rollup and neighbours are derived only once.

review.impact: `void read(proc)` throws away the reader's promise. `deliver` runs inside that loop, and in the server it calls `knownIds()` → `readMap`, which can throw (for example on a log line that is malformed or half-written) along with `renderMarkdown`. If any of these throw, the rejection is never handled. That can bring the whole server down, which `#werk-crash` forbids for request handling. When the loop dies, `child` is also never reset, so later messages go to a child that nobody reads.
review.fix: Wrap the reader in a try/catch, or add `.catch(...)`, so one bad part is logged or reported and the loop does not die. Reset `child` in a `finally` block.

review.impact: `send` only checks that `child` is set, not that the process is still alive. Between the child exiting and `read` clearing `child` (it first waits for stdout to end and then for `proc.exited`), a message is written to a closed stdin. Depending on timing, the write throws EPIPE, which becomes a 500 with a stack trace, or the message is silently dropped while `/api/chat` answers 200. Also, `close()` never clears `child`, so a send after close writes to a killed process.
review.fix: Before writing, check `child.exitCode === null && !child.killed`, or clear `child` in an `exited.then` callback that runs as soon as the process exits. Catch a failed write and relaunch, or return an error to the caller. Set `child = undefined` in `close()`.

review.impact: Agent failures never reach the person. stderr is ignored, and a crash or non-zero exit sends nothing on the live channel. If `claude` is missing, `Bun.spawn` throws, and the handler's catch returns a 500 whose body is a raw stack trace. In every case the pane either waits forever for a reply that will not come or shows an internal stack.
review.fix: Give `startChat` an error callback, or a `ReplyPart` kind for errors. Have the server broadcast it on the live channel when the child exits non-zero (with the tail of stderr) or fails to spawn, and show it in `ChatPane` the same way it shows a send error.

review.impact: `chat.send(text)` runs before the POST answers, and the client adds the person's message only after the response arrives. A fast reply on the live channel can therefore show up in the thread above the message it answers. Also, reply parts go to every open tab, but the person's message appears only in the tab that sent it.
review.fix: Broadcast the rendered user message on the live channel (for example as a `sent` event) before calling `chat.send`, and have `ChatPane` build the whole thread from channel events. Or add the user entry optimistically before the fetch.

review.impact: The `knownIds` cache does its own `statSync` size tracking, which duplicates the size bookkeeping the log watcher right above it already does. That gives two sources of truth for 'the log changed'.
review.fix: Invalidate the known-ids cache from the existing watcher callback (set `known = undefined` where `size = now`) instead of calling stat again on every rendered part.

review.impact: The /api/chat handler repeats the /api/notes preamble almost line for line (lines 123-131): the POST check, the token check, and JSON.parse in a try/catch that answers 400. Any later change to the token or body handling, such as handling a null JSON body or a size limit, has to be made in both places, and the next write endpoint will add a third copy.
review.fix: Pull out one helper, for example `readPost(req, res, what): Promise<Record<string, unknown> | undefined>`, that runs the method check, the token check and the JSON parse and sends the 405, 403 or 400 itself. Have both handlers call it and keep only their own field checks.

review.impact: `existsSync(log) ? statSync(log).size : 0` now appears three times (lines 69, 72, 84). The new knownIds cache and the watcher each track the log size separately.
review.fix: Add a small `logSize()` helper next to the watcher and use it in all three places. Better still, have the watcher clear the `known` cache when it sees the size change, so knownIds does not stat the log itself.

review.impact: The token header name is written as the literal "x-werk-token" here and again in web/note-box.tsx, while the server defines TOKEN_HEADER. If the server renames it, both clients silently start getting 403s.
review.fix: Put the header name in a shared module that both web/ and src/serve can import (web/escape.ts is already shared this way). Import it in chat-pane.tsx, note-box.tsx and server.ts.

review.impact: The `words` helper, which pulls the text out of a recorded user line, is copied almost exactly from src/serve/chat.test.ts:51. The `stream(event)` helper that wraps a fake-agent stream_event is also defined again in server.test.ts, chat-stream.test.ts and e2e/rendered-text.e2e.ts.

review.impact: The restart test waits a fixed 100 ms, hoping the reader has cleared `child` by then. On a loaded parallel worker (#werk-test-runner-parallel) the reader can still be running after 100 ms. `send` then writes to the dead child's stdin, the message is lost, and the `while (launches[1]...)` loop spins until the per-test timeout, so the test is flaky. The sleep also hides the real race in `startChat`: a message sent between the child's exit and the reader's cleanup is silently dropped, and no test catches that.
review.fix: Remove the timed sleep. Either expose a way to wait for the reader to finish (for example an `exited` promise or callback on Chat) and await it, or make `send` check `child.exitCode`/`killed` before reusing the child. Then add a test that sends right after the child exits with no delay and expects a second launch that gets the message.

review.impact: No test covers the pane's failure path: a refused POST (403/400), a body that isn't JSON, or a fetch rejection. Nothing checks that the alert shows, and nothing checks what happens to the person's words, which are cleared before the request and never restored when it fails. A regression in the error handling would pass every check.

review.impact: The server's `knownIds` cache is first filled by the chat POST, which comes after `al-diff` is written. A cache that never refreshes when the log grows would still pass this test, so the cache invalidation is never exercised.
review.fix: Fill the cache first (send a chat message), then append a card to the log, send a second message that references it, and assert that the reference now links.

review.impact: `launches()` is empty right after the 400 replies. The fake agent records its launch only after its own bun start-up, so a child launched by mistake would usually not have recorded yet, and the assertion would pass anyway.
review.fix: Spy on or count launches in a way that doesn't depend on the child starting. Or, after the refusals, send one valid message, wait for its launch, and assert that the first recorded message is the valid one and that there is exactly one launch.

review.impact: No test covers the `own` branch where a finished block's message id differs from the message now streaming. A change that lets a foreign message claim an open block would replace the wrong streamed text and still pass.
review.fix: In chat-stream.test.ts, add a case where an `assistant` event has an id other than the current message. Assert that it gets a fallback `:f<n>` id and that the open streamed block stays unclaimed for its own message.

review.impact: The live channel at /api/events needs no token. Before this change it only sent an empty `changed` ping. It now also sends the chat agent's full replies as `delta` and `chat` events (the `broadcast` call added near line 77). The agent works in the project folder and can quote file contents, secrets in .env files, or command output. Any local process or other user on the machine that can reach the loopback port can open /api/events and read every reply, with no token. A browser page on another site cannot read it, because no CORS header is sent. So the token now guards sending a chat message but not reading the answers.
review.fix: Require the page's token on /api/events, for example as a query parameter checked with `sameToken`. EventSource cannot set headers, so a header won't work. Alternatively, keep /api/events content-free and send chat parts on a separate channel that checks the token. Pass the token in `follow()` in web/live.ts.

review.impact: `/api/chat` reads the request body with `readBody`, which has no size limit, and sends the whole text to the agent's stdin and to `renderMarkdown`. A caller with the token, or a page script stuck in a loop, can send a very large body and make the server use a lot of memory and CPU. Only a token holder can do this, so the risk is low.
review.fix: Limit the body size in `readBody`, for example to 1 MB, and answer 413 when a request is larger. Optionally also cap the length of the chat text before calling `chat.send`.

review.impact: `tile()` builds `new Set(map.nodes.keys())` again for every sub-card that has a why line. A card page therefore costs O(children × nodes) in allocation and hashing. `cardHtml` already builds that same set as `known` at line 61. A wide card on a large map rebuilds the set once per child, and this repeats on every page render and every live redraw.
review.fix: Pass the `known` set from `cardHtml` into `tile(map, id, known)` and use it in `renderTileInline(node.why, known)`. Do not build a new set for each tile.

review.impact: Every `delta` part holds the whole text of the block so far (chat-stream.ts:49). The server runs `renderMarkdown` on all of it, including code highlighting, on each token. It then broadcasts the full HTML to every listener, and the client replaces the whole entry's `innerHTML`. Over a reply of n tokens, CPU work, SSE bytes and DOM work all grow as O(n²). A long reply with large code blocks gets slower as it streams and sends megabytes over the live channel.
review.fix: Throttle the delta broadcasts for each block id, for example to one render per animation frame or about 50 ms, coalescing the pending text. Always send the final `chat` part right away. The other option is to send raw text deltas and render only the finished block. Either way, keep the full-render path only for the final block.

review.impact: `knownIds()` calls `existsSync` and `statSync` on the log for every streamed delta, as well as on every chat POST. That is two synchronous filesystem calls per token on the server's event loop. The watcher above already tracks the log size.
review.fix: Clear the `known` cache from the existing log watcher callback, where `size` is already updated. Then `knownIds()` can return the cached set without a stat on each call.

The only code change is src/verbs/serve.ts:39-46. It installs the SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers before the lock names the port, and no criterion asks for it. It adds no new behaviour: it makes the existing lock release on a signal (#werk-onelock) reliable and fixes a test in src/verbs/serve.test.ts that failed at random on the main line. review.impact: The SIGINT and SIGTERM listeners are now installed before lock.setPort(), which calls writeFileSync and can throw. If it throws, the verb exits with the two process listeners still attached, along with the open server and the held lock (those two were already leaked before this change). After a normal stop, the listener for the signal that did not fire also stays on the process. A test or embedder that runs the verb in-process collects stale listeners that resolve a promise no one awaits.
review.fix: Keep the handlers as named functions and remove both with process.off() once `stopped` settles. Wrap setPort and the wait in a try/finally that removes the handlers, closes the server and releases the lock, so a failed port write cleans up the same way a signal does.

review.impact: The diff changes no test, so nothing reliably fails without the fix. Only "an interrupt stops the server and releases the lock" exercises the race: it sends SIGINT as soon as `listening()` sees the port. Without the fix it fails only when the signal lands in the short window between `lock.setPort` and installing `process.once`. Polling every 50 ms makes that window hard to hit. So this test passes almost every time on the old code, and a future reorder that brings the race back would most likely go unnoticed.
review.fix: Add a test that hits the window much more often. For example, watch the lock file with `fs.watch` instead of the 50 ms poll and send the signal the moment the port appears. Repeat that start-and-interrupt several times in one test. Each time, assert exit code 0, "stopped on SIGINT" on stderr, and that the lock is gone. Then confirm the test fails on the pre-change ordering by reverting `src/verbs/serve.ts` locally.

review.impact: The changed code installs handlers for both SIGINT and SIGTERM, but only SIGINT is tested. If the SIGTERM handler is lost or registered after `setPort`, the server dies from the default action without releasing its lock or printing "stopped on SIGTERM", and no test catches it.
review.fix: Make the interrupt test cover both signals, for example `for (const signal of ["SIGINT", "SIGTERM"] as const)`. For each one, assert exit code 0, `stopped on ${signal}` on stderr, and `existsSync(lock) === false`.

review.impact: The reader runs as a detached promise (`void read(proc)`), and every `deliver` call runs inside it. `deliver` calls `knownIds()` (which calls `readMap`), `renderMarkdown` and `res.write`. If any of these throws, the promise rejects with no handler. The request handler is guarded so that one error cannot kill the server (#werk-crash), but this path is not, so a rejection here can take down the whole werk server. The `child === proc` reset also never runs, so `child` keeps pointing at a dead process and every later message goes into it.
review.fix: Wrap the body of `read` in try/finally. Clear `child` in the finally block, or hang it on `proc.exited.then(...)` so it does not depend on the stdout loop. Catch and log errors from `deliver` per part, so one bad part cannot stop the loop or reject the promise.

review.impact: `send` only learns that the child has exited after the reader has drained stdout and awaited `exited`. A message sent in that window is written to the stdin of a process that has already exited: Bun's FileSink either throws EPIPE, which the request handler turns into a 500, or drops the message without an error. The server still answers 200 with the rendered message, so the person sees it in the thread and no reply ever comes. The new test needs `await Bun.sleep(100)` to step around this race, which shows the API is fragile.
review.fix: Track liveness from `proc.exited` directly (`proc.exited.then(() => { if (child === proc) child = undefined; })`) and check `proc.exitCode`/`proc.killed` before reusing the child. Wrap the write and flush in try/catch, and on failure start a fresh child and send the message again (or return an error) instead of reporting success.

review.impact: The child's stderr goes to `ignore`, and nothing reports an exit. When the agent fails (a bad flag, an auth error, a crash), the pane never gets a reply and neither the person nor the server log learns why. The HTTP layer elsewhere takes care to surface its errors, but this path stays silent.
review.fix: Pipe stderr and keep its tail. When the child exits with a non-zero code, broadcast an error event (or log it) so the pane can show that the agent stopped.

review.impact: `close()` kills the child but leaves `child` set and does not stop later `send` calls. A `send` after `close` (for example, a request that is still in flight while the server shuts down) writes to a killed process or, once the reader clears `child`, starts a new agent that nothing will ever stop.
review.fix: Set a `closed` flag in `close()`, clear `child`, and make `send` refuse or ignore messages once the chat is closed.

review.impact: `broadcast` sends chat replies to every open page, but the person's own message appears only in the tab that sent it, through the POST response. With two tabs open, the second tab shows agent replies with no message before them, so the shared live channel and the per-tab thread state disagree.
review.fix: Broadcast the sent message on the live channel as well (as a `sent` event), and have every pane, including the sender, build its thread from the live channel alone.

review.impact: The token header name `x-werk-token` is a literal string here, as it already is in `accept.ts` and `note-box.tsx`, while the server defines it as `TOKEN_HEADER`. With a third copy, a rename on the server would break the client without any error.
review.fix: Move the header name into a constant that both sides import (for example next to `web/escape.ts`), and use it in `server.ts`, `accept.ts`, `note-box.tsx` and `chat-pane.tsx`.

review.impact: The `words` helper is copied word for word from src/serve/chat.test.ts:51, and the `stream` event builder appears in four places: chat-stream.test.ts, server.test.ts, chat.test.ts (inline) and e2e/rendered-text.e2e.ts. If the fake agent's stream-json shape changes, each copy has to be found and changed separately.
review.fix: Move `stream(event)` and `words(message)` into a shared helper under src/test (for example next to fake-script.ts), and import them in the unit tests and the e2e test.

review.impact: The type `Subprocess<"pipe", "pipe", "ignore">` is written out three times: on `child`, on `read` and on `launch`. If the stdio choices change, all three must change together.
review.fix: Declare `type Child = Subprocess<"pipe", "pipe", "ignore">` once and use it in all three places.

review.impact: `await Bun.sleep(100)` guesses how long the reader takes to clear the dead child. On a loaded parallel worker the guess can be too short, and the test then fails at random.
review.fix: Wait on a state you can observe instead: expose whether a child is live, or poll until a send starts a second launch. Do not sleep for a fixed time.

review.impact: The comment says the effect needs only `events`, but its dependency list is `[events, apply]`. A reader can't tell which one is meant.
review.fix: Reword the comment to say `apply` keeps one identity, so the effect re-runs only when `events` changes. Or drop `useCallback` and call `setThread` inside the effect.

review.impact: The `reply.locator(".codebox code")` locator is written inline in one assertion and then declared again as `code` on the next line. The duplication makes the streamed and finished steps harder to read.
review.fix: Declare `const code = reply.locator(".codebox code")` once, before both assertions, and use it in both.

review.impact: This test is now weaker. The map pane in page.ts is `min-w-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto`, and setting overflow-y to auto also makes overflow-x compute to auto. So a code box that is too wide scrolls the pane, never the document, and `document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= clientWidth` holds whether the `<pre>` scrolls or not. The other check, `pre.scrollWidth > pre.clientWidth`, is also true when the content simply overflows a `<pre>` without a scroll bar. Together, nothing here now fails if the code box stops scrolling on its own.
review.fix: Check the container that can actually overflow. Assert that the map pane's scrollWidth is at most its clientWidth (for example, the `#card` ancestor with overflow-y-auto), or that the code box's own width is at most its parent's width. Also assert that `getComputedStyle(pre).overflowX` is `auto` or `scroll`.

review.impact: The restart test relies on a fixed 100 ms sleep for `read()` to clear `child` after the process exits. Under the parallel load of the unit run (#werk-test-runner-parallel), the reader can still be behind when that sleep ends. Then `send` writes to the dead child's stdin, the message is lost, and the `while (launches()[1]...)` loop waits until the test times out. The sleep also hides a real gap in chat.ts: a message sent between the exit and the reader clearing `child` is dropped, and no test covers that case.
review.fix: Don't sleep. Expose or await the child's exit (for example, let `startChat` return a promise for the reader finishing, or let `send` check `proc.exitCode`/`killed` before it reuses the child). Then add a test where `send` runs right after the exit, with no wait, and still starts a fresh child.

review.impact: The mid-stream assertion only works if Playwright sees the partial text within the fake agent's 2000 ms pause. On a loaded machine (user message rendering plus the polls before it), the pause can end first, and the test fails without any defect. The old version mounted the partial HTML directly and was deterministic.
review.fix: Make the pause long enough not to depend on load, or better, have the fake agent wait for a signal (for example, a file the test writes) before it sends the tail. Release it after the partial assertion passes.

review.impact: No test covers the branch where the finished block's message id differs from the streaming message (`own` false). A regression that let a finished block from another message claim a streamed block, and so replace the wrong text in the pane, would pass the suite.
review.fix: In chat-stream.test.ts, stream a text block under message `m1`, then send an `assistant` event with id `m2`. Assert that it gets a fallback `m2:fN` id and does not reuse `m1:0`.

review.impact: No test covers the pane's failure path: a refused send (403/400) or a network error that should show a `role=alert` message and add nothing to the thread. If this path broke, the person's message would disappear silently.
review.fix: Add a component or e2e test that makes `/api/chat` fail (for example, by changing the token in the page). Assert that the alert shows the server's error and that the thread has no user entry.

review.impact: Each text_delta makes the server re-render the whole block so far (`readLine` in chat-stream.ts returns the full `block.text`, not the new piece). The server then sends that whole HTML to every open page, and the client swaps the whole entry. One long reply arrives as hundreds of small deltas, so CPU and live-channel bytes grow with the square of the reply length. With several pages open, every page pays that again.
review.fix: Throttle the delta broadcast per block id, for example at most one render every 50–100 ms or once per animation frame. Keep only the latest text, and send at once when the block finishes ('block' parts). This keeps the replace-in-place design and caps the number of renders.

review.impact: `tile()` builds a new `Set(map.nodes.keys())` for each sub-card, on top of the one `title()` already builds for each sub-card. A card with many children on a large map costs O(children × nodes) on every page render and every live redraw. `cardHtml` already has `known`.
review.fix: Pass the `known` set from `cardHtml` into `tile()`, and into `title()`, instead of building a new one for each tile.

review.impact: Each stdout chunk adds to `rest`, and the code splits all of `rest` again. When one large stream-json line arrives over many chunks (for example a big assistant or tool-result message), the code scans the same text again for every chunk, so the work grows with the square of that line's length.
review.fix: Look for '\n' only in the newly decoded chunk, for example with `indexOf` from the end of the old `rest`, or keep the pieces in an array and join them only when a newline arrives.

review.impact: `go` runs `void refresh()` and nothing catches its rejection. `readCard` in web/main.tsx never checks `response.ok`. So when the server is down or answers with a plain-text 500, `response.json()` throws and every in-page navigation leaves an unhandled promise rejection. The note box's `onSent={() => void store.refresh()}` in web/view.tsx:17 has the same gap. Only the live-channel caller in web/main.tsx adds a `.catch`, so the store's callers handle errors in three different ways.
review.fix: Handle failure inside the store: wrap the read in `refresh` with try/catch, and either keep the last state or set an error state that `View` can show. Also make `readCard` throw a clear error when `!response.ok`. Then callers never need their own `.catch`.

review.impact: `firstState` builds the server-rendered read with `card: null` even when the card is found. Until the first live-channel read comes back, `CardTitle` shows no title and the `document.title` subscriber would write `#id` without the title. The client's first state therefore disagrees with what the server rendered, and the page only looks right because the channel's `open` event triggers a refresh straight away.
review.fix: Have the server put the card read, or at least the title, into the page as data the client can read (e.g. a data attribute on #card). Or leave `read` undefined and let the first refresh fill it, rather than storing a half-filled `CardResponse` that claims to be complete.

review.impact: The document-title format `${title} — #${id}` / `#${id}` is written twice: once here and once in `titleOf` at src/serve/page.ts:28. If either copy changes alone, the server-rendered title and the client-updated title will disagree after the first refresh.

review.impact: `export { HOME_ID }` re-exports a constant that now lives in web/routes.ts, and only page.test.ts imports it through page.ts. That leaves two import paths for the same constant.

review.impact: This change weakened a test. The old test checked that a page for an id missing from the map has no note box (`not.toContain("note-box")`). That assertion is gone. The note box now comes from `View` in `web/view.tsx`, which shows it only when `read.found` is true, but no unit or browser test checks that. If someone drops the `read.found` guard, people could write notes against a card that does not exist, and every test would still pass.
review.fix: Add a component test for `web/view.tsx`. Render `View` with a store whose read has `found: false` and check that no textbox named "Note" is present. Render it again with `found: true` and check that the textbox is there. Or add `await expect(p.getByRole("textbox", { name: "Note" })).toHaveCount(0)` to the browser test "an unknown id shows a page that says the map does not hold it" in `e2e/client.e2e.ts`.

review.impact: No test covers a card read that fails. `go()` calls `void refresh()` with no catch, and `View` also calls `store.refresh()` with no catch. So when a fetch fails during navigation, the promise rejection is never handled, and the view stays on "Reading the map…" for good. `page-store.test.ts` only tests reads that succeed.
review.fix: Add a page-store test with a `readCard` that rejects. Check what the store should do: either it keeps the state and calls no listener, or it records an error state. Then make `go()` handle the rejection, as the live channel already does with `.catch(() => undefined)`.

review.impact: The rules in `clickedRoute` have no test. These rules are: a modifier key, a non-primary button, `target=_blank`, another origin, an event that is already `defaultPrevented`, and a path that is not a view address. The browser tests cover only a plain left click. If a regression made in-page navigation take over Ctrl/Cmd-click or links to other sites, no test would fail. The unit run now has a DOM, so these cases are cheap to test.
review.fix: Add `web/navigation.test.ts`. Use a fake store, attach links to `document.body`, dispatch `MouseEvent` clicks with `ctrlKey`/`metaKey`, `button: 1`, `target="_blank"`, an href on another origin and `/api/x`, and check that `store.go` is never called and `defaultPrevented` stays false. Add one plain click that does call `go` and `pushState`, and one `popstate` event.

review.impact: Only one slow browser test (`e2e/client.e2e.ts`, the dev edit test) covers the hot-reload reuse branch, and `src/serve/hot.ts` has no unit test at all. Nothing checks these points: `keepLive` removes the entry once the server stops, so a later start does not reuse a closed server; the reuse branch takes no lock; and `liveServer` is keyed by log, so a second store does not reuse the first store's server. If the stop cleanup breaks, a closed server gets handed back.

review.impact: Outside dev mode, `builtClient(builtClientDir())` is chosen without checking that the folder exists. If the built client is missing (for example, the executable was copied without `dist/client`), `werk serve` starts, prints its address and takes the lock. Then every page request throws inside `template()` (`readFileSync` of `index.html`) and the crash handler answers with a 500, and every asset is a 404. The person sees a broken page instead of an error at start-up that names the cause.
review.fix: Have `builtClient` (or `startServer`) check that `<dir>/index.html` exists when it is created, and throw an error that names the missing folder. `serve.ts` then reports it, releases the lock and exits non-zero, as it already does for other start-up failures.

review.impact: `builtClient` serves any file under the built folder, `/index.html` included. That file is the raw template: its `<!--werk:head-->` and `<!--werk:view-->` slots are still unfilled and it has no token, so it is a second, broken copy of the app's page at an address the server never means to give out. Also, `root + sep` breaks if the caller passes a folder path ending in a separator: `normalize` keeps the trailing slash, so every asset becomes a 404.
review.fix: In `serve`, send `index.html` to `next()` (or leave it out of the static lookup), and strip any trailing separator from `root` before the `startsWith` check, for example with `resolve(dir)`.

review.impact: `go` calls `void refresh()` with no catch. The ✓ callback (`web/main.tsx:50`) and the note box's `onSent` (`web/view.tsx:18`) also call `void store.refresh()` with no catch. If the card read fails (server down during a restart, or a reply that is not JSON), each of these becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Only the live-channel path in `main.tsx` catches. Error handling for the same call is now inconsistent across its call sites.
review.fix: Catch inside the store: have `go` call `refresh().catch(() => undefined)`, or have `refresh` itself swallow or record a failed read. Then every caller gets the same behaviour and `main.tsx` no longer needs its own catch.

review.impact: Both tests clean up `werk:draft` in sessionStorage with `removeItem` after their `expect` calls. The DOM is shared by every test in the process (#werk-test-dom), so if an assertion fails the key stays behind. Any later Composer render in that worker then starts with a stale draft, and an unrelated test fails depending on worker order. This breaks #werk-test-store, which requires each store to be removed when the test ends, pass or fail.
review.fix: Move the cleanup into `afterEach(() => sessionStorage.removeItem(DRAFT_KEY))`, or clear the key in `src/test/dom-cleanup.ts`. Drop the inline `removeItem` calls.

review.impact: No unit test covers the hot-reload guard. That includes the `liveServer`/`keepLive` table, removing the entry once `stopped` settles, the identity check that stops an old Live from deleting a newer one, and the reuse branch in `src/verbs/serve.ts:26`. Only one e2e test covers it, and only through a full `bun --hot` server. If the cleanup broke, a restarted `werk serve` in the same process would reuse a closed server, and the unit run would not catch it.
review.fix: Add `src/serve/hot.test.ts`. Check that `keepLive` makes `liveServer(log)` return the Live, that it returns undefined after `stopped` resolves, and that a stale Live settling does not remove a newer Live for the same log.

review.impact: `go` calls `void refresh()`. If `readCard` rejects, for example during a navigation while the server is down, the rejection is never handled. No test covers a read that fails, so neither the behaviour nor the store's state after the failure is defined.
review.fix: Catch the error in `go` (`void refresh().catch(() => undefined)`) and add a page-store test where `readCard` rejects. It should check that the route stays on the new view and no rejection escapes.

review.impact: The old test asserted that the page loads the client entry script. The new index.html test checks the two slots and the chat pane but not `<script type="module" src="/main.tsx">`. If someone removed or renamed the entry, every unit test would still pass, and only the e2e run would show a page with no client.

review.impact: No test covers the composer's failure path, where `onSend` returns an error and an alert should show. Before this change that logic lived in ChatPane, and it moved here without a test.

review.impact: This timing log was written by a werk run made directly inside the fixture. Committing it puts run output into the shared fixture, and the next manual run inside the fixture will change it again.

review.impact: `devMode()` decides between dev and built mode by checking whether a file exists at `import.meta.dir/../../vite.config.ts`. In the compiled `dist/werk` binary, `import.meta.dir` points into Bun's embedded filesystem, so this path becomes the real `/vite.config.ts`. If a file exists there, the shipped binary loads Vite and runs that file as its config, executing whatever code it contains, and stops serving the built client. Writing to `/` takes root, so the risk is small, but the switch to dev mode depends on the environment instead of on how werk was built.
review.fix: Pick dev mode from an explicit signal that the build controls. For example, set a constant with `bun build --define` (such as `WERK_BUILT=true`) and use built mode whenever it is set. Check for the Vite config file only when that constant is absent.

review.impact: Outside dev mode, every request to a view address reads `index.html` from disk again with a blocking `readFileSync`. The built client cannot change while the server runs, so this repeats the same disk read on each page load.
review.fix: Read `index.html` once when `builtClient(dir)` is called, or on the first request, and have `template` return the cached string.

review.impact: Each request for a static asset makes three blocking calls (`existsSync`, `statSync` and `readFileSync`) on the event loop and sends no cache headers. The browser fetches the hashed bundle again on every load, and the server reads it fully into memory each time, which holds up other requests, including the live channel writes.
review.fix: Call `statSync` once with `throwIfNoEntry: false` instead of `existsSync` followed by `statSync`. Stream the file with `createReadStream(file).pipe(res)`. Send `cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` for files under `/assets/`, whose names Vite hashes.

review.impact: No test covers a card read that fails. `go()` calls `void refresh()`, so when `readCard` rejects (network drop, bad JSON) the promise is left unhandled, and the view stays on 'Reading the map…' with no state that reports the error. review.impact: `clickedRoute` and the popstate handler have no unit test. The e2e test covers only a plain left click on a same-origin link. Assert that `store.go` and `pushState` happen only for a plain left click on a same-origin view address. review.impact: Each test removes `DRAFT_KEY` only at its end. If an assertion fails first, the draft stays in the sessionStorage that the whole process shares, and later component tests in the same worker start with a stale draft, which hides the real failure behind follow-on ones.

review.impact: The send paths that moved out of ChatPane have no test: an empty or whitespace draft is not sent, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter sends, the draft clears on send, and an error from `onSend` shows as the alert. A regression in any of these goes unnoticed until someone uses the chat.

review.impact: Only the slow hot-reload e2e test exercises `liveServer` and `keepLive`. review.fix: Add `src/serve/hot.test.ts`. Keep a live entry whose `stopped` the test resolves by hand, and assert that `liveServer(log)` returns it before resolution and `undefined` after. Then replace the entry with a second one, resolve the first, and assert that the second is still kept.

review.impact: Vite's dependency cache lives at a predictable path in the shared temporary folder (`werk-vite-<first 12 hex characters of sha1(config path + log path)>`). On Linux, `/tmp` is shared by every user, so another user can work out the path from the checkout and log paths and create the folder first. They could then put pre-bundled dependency code in it, and Vite would serve that code to the werk page in dev mode, where it could read the write token. The predictable path was already there before this change, which only moved it and added the config path to the hash. On macOS, `tmpdir()` is per user, so this does not apply there.
review.fix: Put the cache under a folder only this user can write, such as `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/werk` or `~/.cache/werk`, or under the `.werk` folder of the project. Alternatively, before using an existing cache folder, check that the current user owns it and that its mode is 0700, and refuse it otherwise.

review.impact: Outside dev mode, `builtClient` reads `index.html` from disk with a blocking `readFileSync` on every view request. The built folder does not change while the server runs, so every page load repeats the same read.
review.fix: Read the template once when `builtClient` is created and return the cached string from `template()`.

review.impact: Each request for a built asset runs `existsSync`, `statSync` and `readFileSync`, all blocking, and loads the whole file into memory. A large bundle or font holds up the event loop, including the live channels, until the read finishes.
review.fix: Make one async `stat` call, which also confirms the file exists, then send the body with `createReadStream(file).pipe(res)` and set `content-length` from the stat.
