If a child never sends one (a different CLI version, or a fake without an init line), nothing reaches the chat log while the child is alive. The held list also grows without limit until the child exits.
review.fix: Put a bound on the holding. For example, write the held lines with an empty session as soon as the first reply part arrives before any session line, or write each line straight away and add the session to it once known. At least document that the log depends on the init line.

review.impact: `send` launches the child before it reads the map and writes the log. If `readMap` or the log append throws, the child is already running, but `sendTurn` never runs and no message reaches it. The person gets a server error, and an idle child is left behind with its `lastCard` state half updated.
review.fix: Build the open-card line and do the log writes before `child ??= launch()`, or launch the child just before `stdin.write`. That way a failure leaves no half-started turn.

review.impact: `chatFrame` is a pure translation from a chat event to a live-channel event, but it lives in the large `server.ts` request module. That goes against #werk-stack-modules (small single-purpose modules). It also keeps this code out of the pure-file coverage gate, even though `turns.ts` and `open-card.ts` from the same change were split out and added to it.
review.fix: Move `chatFrame` into its own module (for example `src/serve/chat-frame.ts`) with its own test, and add that module to `pure-files.txt`.

review.impact: `chatLogPath(log, CONVERSATION) as string` casts away the `undefined` return type. If `CONVERSATION` ever fails `NAME`, the code would append to the path "undefined" with no error.
review.fix: Check the result once and throw if it is undefined, or add a helper that returns a plain `string` for a constant conversation name, instead of the `as string` cast.

review.impact: `chatLogPath(...) as string` is a type cast that hides the `undefined` the function returns for a bad conversation name. It is safe today only because CONVERSATION is a valid name. If someone renames it to a name that fails NAME, appendFileSync gets `undefined` at run time, and the type checker says nothing.
review.fix: Remove the cast. Either throw once at start-up when chatLogPath returns undefined (`const chatLog = chatLogPath(log, CONVERSATION); if (chatLog === undefined) throw new Error(...)`), or add a non-optional helper for a name that is known to be valid.

review.impact: `heard()` copies the launches.jsonl parser that src/test/project.ts already has in `readLaunches`. The copy also differs from it: it uses `find` where the original uses `findLast` for a reused pid. If the fake agent's launch format changes, the two copies drift apart without anyone noticing.
review.fix: Export `readLaunches` (or one shared parser) from src/test/project.ts or fake-script.ts. In the e2e test, call it and map each launch's messages to their text.

review.impact: The last `readLine` call in the session-id test has no assertion. It only runs code for coverage, so it pads the coverage figure without checking that an image block changes no state and emits no part.
review.fix: Wrap it in `expect(...).toEqual([])`. Better still, move it to a test whose name describes that behaviour.

review.impact: The fallback id expression ``${text(message.id) || "m"}:f${state.finished}`` appears twice in `finished()`, once for tool_use and once for text. If one copy changes, the ids of the two block kinds stop matching.
review.fix: Compute the fallback id once, near the top of `finished()` after `state.finished += 1`, and use it in both branches.

review.impact: The `session` parameter of `append` shadows the outer mutable `session` variable. A reader can easily confuse the two in this closure-heavy function.
review.fix: Rename the parameter, for example to `named`, as `flush` already does.

review.impact: Three tests build the same chat-log path `join(project.dir, ".werk", "chats", "main.jsonl")`, which also hard-codes the CONVERSATION name that chat.ts exports.
review.fix: Add one helper next to `log()`, for example `const chatFile = () => chatLogPath(log(), CONVERSATION)`, and use it in all three tests.

review.impact: `chatFrame` is new and exported. No unit test checks the `tool`, `tool-result` or `exited` cases, or that `status` leaves out `tool` when there is no tool. The server test only covers started, status (writing), delta, chat and ended. The e2e test covers tool and tool-result only through the rendered DOM. If one of these frames gets a wrong channel name or field, for example `exited` sent as `ended` or `input` sent unstringified, no Bun test fails.
review.fix: Add a table test in server.test.ts. It calls `chatFrame` once for each `ChatEvent` kind and asserts the exact `[name, data]` it returns, including `input` as indented JSON and `{ turn, state: "exited" }`.

review.impact: This `readLine` call on a `content_block_start` of kind `image` asserts nothing. It runs the code only to count toward coverage. If the reader started emitting a status or delta for an unknown block kind, this test would still pass.
review.fix: Wrap the call in `expect(...).toEqual([])`. Also assert that a following `message_delta` emits no change of state, which shows that an unknown kind leaves the state alone.

review.impact: The title says the sent message 'shows at once', but the fake `post` answers right away and the test waits only for the server's HTML ("…!"). If someone removed the optimistic `sent` apply in chat-pane.tsx, the test would still pass.
review.fix: Make `post` wait on a promise the test controls. Assert that the thread shows "Make it three tries" and the waiting mark before resolving it, then resolve and assert that the server's HTML replaces the text.

review.impact: No test covers the branch where the network call throws. It should drop the optimistic turn and return the error message. A regression here would leave a message in the thread with a waiting mark that never clears.
review.fix: Add a chat-pane test whose `post` rejects with `new Error("offline")`. Assert that the alert shows "offline" and that the thread is empty.

review.impact: The negative check sleeps for a fixed 500 ms before asserting that no agent launched. If the server launched the agent slowly, after the sleep, the test would pass anyway.
review.fix: After the refused requests, send one valid message through the pane and wait for its reply. Then assert that `heard(w)` has exactly one launch holding only that message. This shows that the refused requests reached nothing, without depending on a timer.

review.impact: `logged` writes every tool call and its full result (for example `cat .env`, `env`, or `gh auth token`) as plain text to `.werk/chats/main.jsonl` in the project folder. Nothing marks that file as git-ignored and nothing redacts it. Secrets the agent reads can stay on disk and can be committed and pushed along with the rest of `.werk`.
review.fix: Keep `.werk/chats/` out of version control. For example, write a `.gitignore` with `*` into the chats folder when `append` first creates it. Or keep only the tool name and a short excerpt of `tool_result` output in the log instead of the full text.

review.impact: `turn` must match a strict name pattern, but `card` can be any string of any length. That string goes straight into the open-card line (`#${id} — …`), which is sent to the agent as werk's own framing and saved in the chat log as a 'werk' tooling line. A card value with newlines can therefore pose as werk's own context and bloat the log. Only a token holder can send one, so the risk is limited.
review.fix: Check `card` the way `turn` is checked: allow only the map's node-id pattern with a length cap and answer 400 otherwise, or reuse the existing card-id validation from the map module.

causeOfLast.why: the hero's list of marks (#vi-onview-hero) and story 46 were clear, and an earlier pass added a waiting tag, a waiting section and a postponed section that neither asks for.

grade.gap: The ghost tile is blue (border-blue-400 bg-blue-50 in boxAttrs, src/serve/card-look.ts), but it also keeps a dashed border, which #al-diff-render does not ask for. It still passes.

Every added behaviour traces to a story or a cited card: the copy-id button and the title that shrinks by depth come from #vi-onview-hero (story 12), the paused section and its path come from story 43, and the hatched postponed bar segment comes from #vi-onview-postponed (story 46). Nothing is out of scope.

Two small choices that no named card gives: (1) the page order of the lists in LISTS (src/serve/card-html.ts) puts Options, Evidence and Say above Depends on and the other link lists, and puts sub-cards after all the lists; (2) a separate 'Why this card is paused' section and a 'paused' tag in the tag row (src/serve/card-marks.ts markSectionsHtml, card-html.ts tagRow), which #vi-onview-hero does not list among its tags. Both are minor, so the line passes. Consider proposing a card for the order of the page sections.

review.impact: `postponedOf` walks the subtree again and repeats the filter rules of `rollupOf` (card kind, not a ghost). It also calls `rollupOf` only to check that the card exists. Each tile and hero builds the rollup up to three times (`tileHtml` 'below', `barHtml`, `postponedOf`). If the two filters ever drift apart, `rollup[status] - postponed[status]` in `barHtml` can go negative or stop adding up to the card count.
review.fix: Count postponed cards by status inside the one `rollupOf` loop, for example `postponed: Record<Status, number>` on `Rollup`, and drop `postponedOf`. Then `barHtml` and `tileHtml` read a single rollup.

review.impact: The tile's 'N evidence' count uses every `supported_by` link. That includes excerpts and held links to ghosts. The card page now splits excerpts out under Say, so the tile counts things the page's Evidence section does not show.
review.fix: Count with the same rule as the page's Evidence list (non-excerpt targets), or rename the count so it covers excerpts too. Keep the filter in one shared spot, such as the exported `isExcerpt`.

review.impact: `boxAttrs` and `tileHtml` are exported, but they cast `map.nodes.get(id) as MapNode` without a check. A caller that passes an unknown id gets a TypeError deep inside the template, not a clear result. `nodeLink` and `cardHtml` in the same files do handle a missing node.
review.fix: Pass the `MapNode` in from the caller, which already holds it, or return "" when the node is missing, as `nodeLink` does.

review.impact: When the clipboard write is refused, the error is swallowed (`() => undefined`). The user clicks and nothing happens, with no feedback and nothing logged.
review.fix: On rejection, set a visible state such as `data-copied="false"` or a title, or at least `console.warn`. A failed copy should be visible.

review.impact: `prose()` here, `field()` in card-html.ts:31 and the `why` block in card-html.ts:45 all do the same thing: they return nothing for empty text and otherwise wrap renderMarkdown in a div with a data attribute. The empty-text check and the markup are written out three times, so a change to one can drift from the other two.
review.fix: Export one helper from card-look.ts, such as `mdBlock(text, known, attr, value, classes)`, and use it in all three places.

review.impact: `count()` and `flagCount()` produce almost the same markup: a span with a dot followed by the number and the name. Only the dot class differs. Two copies of the template can drift apart.
review.fix: Replace them with one function that takes the dot class, for example `countHtml(name, n, dotClass)`. Pass `STATUS_BG[status]` for a status and `border-2 border-red-600` or `border-2 border-purple-600` for a flag.

review.impact: `postponedTag()` writes the tag-span markup by hand, while card-html.ts:121 has a `tag()` helper that builds the same span. The proposed tag in `tileHtml` is also hand-written. Tag markup now lives in two modules, so the tile and hero tags can drift apart.
review.fix: Move `tag()` into card-look.ts and add an optional title parameter. Build `postponedTag` and the tile's proposed tag with it, and import it into card-html.ts.

review.impact: `boxAttrs` and `tileHtml` (line 141) use `map.nodes.get(id) as MapNode`. The cast hides the case where the id is missing, so a caller that passes an unknown id gets a runtime TypeError instead of a type error.
review.fix: Take the `MapNode` as a parameter, since callers already have it or can look it up. Or narrow with an explicit check that throws or returns an empty string.

review.impact: `postponedOf` computes a whole rollup only to test whether it is undefined. It then walks the descendants a second time. `tileHtml` (card-look.ts:147) also calls `rollupOf` again after `barHtml` has already computed it. The repeated work makes it unclear which call is the authoritative one.
review.fix: In `postponedOf`, check the node directly, e.g. `map.nodes.get(id)?.kind !== 'card' || proposed`, the same condition `rollupOf` uses. Or pass the rollup that was already computed into `barHtml` and the tile.

review.impact: This test checks that the waiting tag and section are absent, but this change removed that feature and no code still produces them. The test guards dead code and will always pass, so it adds noise without protecting anything.
review.fix: Delete the test. If a regression guard is wanted, fold a single `waiting` absence assertion into an existing test.

review.impact: `POSTPONED_HINT` is exported but no other module imports it. card-html.test.ts and card-page.e2e.ts hard-code the same string, so a change to the wording breaks the tests in several places.
review.fix: Import `POSTPONED_HINT` in card-html.test.ts (and in the e2e test if the import works there), or stop exporting it.

review.impact: The `mapOf` and `dom` test helpers are copied into card-html.test.ts, card-look.test.ts and card-marks.test.ts, and `mapOf` also appears in map-api.test.ts. A change to the fixture format has to be made in each copy.
review.fix: Move `mapOf` and `dom` into a shared test-only helper module next to the tests and import them.

review.impact: The test 'an open card on an open basis shows no waiting tag or section' checks for markup that nothing in the codebase produces any more, because commit 451cfba removed the waiting tag and section. It passes whether or not the change is applied, so it guards nothing and implies the feature still exists in some form.
review.fix: Delete the test. If you want to guard against the waiting tag coming back, assert on the whole tag row of an open card on an open basis instead: data-tag values exactly ['kind', 'status']. That assertion would fail if any extra tag appeared.

review.impact: The success test never checks that the 'copied' mark is cleared after COPIED_MS, so that path has no coverage. The test also leaves a real 1.5 s setTimeout pending when it ends. The timeout's callback deletes a dataset key on a detached button, so nothing breaks, but the clean-up behaviour could regress without any test failing.
review.fix: Use fake timers (bun:test `jest.useFakeTimers()` / `setSystemTime`), or inject the delay. After the click, advance past COPIED_MS and assert that `button.dataset.copied` is undefined.

review.impact: Every card page request now works out the same subtree rollup several times. In the hero, barHtml (line 93), postponedOf (rollup.ts:44, used only as a guard) and rollupLineHtml (line 126) each call rollupOf. In each tile, tileHtml (line 147), barHtml, and postponedOf with its own rollupOf call each walk the subtree again. Each walk is costly: descendantsOf scans all links per node and uses out.includes, and rollupOf calls isStale per node, which scans map.links for each hop. So the root page does about 3 extra full-subtree O(N·L) walks for the hero plus about 4 per child tile. The old page did none of these. This runs on every /api/card request and every live redraw.
review.fix: Compute the rollup once per card and pass it in. barHtml and rollupLineHtml should take a Rollup | undefined, and tileHtml should reuse that same value for its 'below' count. Have postponedOf count postponed cards in the same descendant walk, or replace its rollupOf guard with a direct check of the node (a real, non-proposed card). Better still, have one function return both the rollup and the postponed counts from a single descendantsOf pass.

review.impact: tileHtml builds new Set(map.nodes.keys()) for each tile, and titleHtml (line 37) builds another one for each tile and each nodeLink row. A page with many sub-cards or links therefore copies every node id once or twice per row, which costs O(rows × nodes), although cardHtml has already built `known`.
review.fix: Pass the `known` set that cardHtml already builds into tileHtml, titleHtml and nodeLink instead of rebuilding it per call.

causeOfLast.why: another ticket added a chat-agent test to the same file, and that test used the send API this ticket had changed.

grade.gap: Nothing clearly outside the ticket. Two borderline items: (1) web/chat-pane.tsx ChatHeader shows a status row above the composer with the agent's state, seconds and tokens. Its code cites #werk-head-bottom, which no user story of the ticket lists, though #werk-progress may cover it. (2) The 'dropped' event in web/chat-thread.ts takes a refused message back out of the thread. Both are small, so this line passes.

The builder named only #werk-chat, #werk-chat-turn-id, #werk-agent-instructions and #st-build-howto-titles. The diff makes these choices that none of those four cards gives: (a) src/serve/open-card.ts: the open-card line '[the map is now at #id — title]', the fields of the compact block (kind · status · who, why, children, depends on), the reminder '[still on #id — title]', and the text for an unknown id. These come from #werk-card-blind or #werk-chat-no-card-line, which the builder did not name. (b) web/chat-thread.ts runSummary/callLine: the collapsed line names the latest call, shows the short form of its command, path or pattern, cuts it at 80 characters, and adds ' · N calls'. A run ends at text. This is #werk-tool-collapse, not named. (c) src/serve/server.ts chatFrame: the live-channel events 'turn' (started, ended or exited), 'status', 'tool' and 'tool-result', and the POST /api/chat body {text, turn, card}, where card defaults to the root and the turn name is checked against a pattern. (d) src/serve/turns.ts partTurn: a part with no open turn gets a turn that the server names 'agent-N'. (e) src/serve/chat.ts: the chat log keeps tool_call and tool_result lines, a tool_call line is written as 'name JSON(input)', and each line waits until the child names its session, or is written with an empty session if the child exits first. Point to #werk-excerpt-chatlog or propose a card. (f) the header row's state words and token count (#werk-head-bottom / #werk-progress). In the next pass, name the existing cards that give each choice, or propose a card for any choice that no card gives.

review.impact: The test 'the first card of an empty map has no parent to take' adds a card whose id is `root`. That means it only exercises the `fields.id !== ROOT_ID` guard. The `map.nodes.has(ROOT_ID)` guard has no direct test: no test adds a card with a different id to a map that has no root and then checks that the payload has no parent. The two contract-verbs tests reach that guard only by accident: they would fail through a refused dangling parent, not through a check of the behaviour. If a later refactor dropped that guard, nothing would show that the guard's absence caused the failure.
review.fix: In the same test, after adding `root` to a fresh project, add a second check on another fresh project: `werk add x --title X` on an empty map, then assert that `payload.parent` is undefined. Alternatively, give the empty-map case a separate test that uses an id other than `root`.

causeOfLast.why: the cited cards do not say which events the live channel carries, how the server names a turn it opens itself, or which parts the chat log keeps and when, so the pass had to make these choices and record them as cards.

grade.gap: No behaviour falls outside the ticket. Two borderline items stay because the ticket asks for them. The ChatHeader status row (web/chat-pane.tsx ChatHeader, statusLine in web/chat-thread.ts) shows the state, a seconds clock and tokens; user story 50 cites #werk-progress, and #werk-chat-turn-id-events defines the status event. The 'dropped' thread event (web/chat-thread.ts applyEvent) removes a refused message, which the immediate draw of a sent message needs.

Choices that no named or decided card shown here gives. Propose a card for each, or cite the card if one exists: (1) turn names are capped at 100 characters and may not start with a dot (src/serve/turns.ts NAME regex); (2) the page builds turn names as 't' + base-36 time + '-' + a counter (web/chat-pane.tsx newTurnName); (3) a message the server refuses is removed from the thread again (the 'dropped' event in web/chat-thread.ts, tested in web/chat-pane.test.tsx 'a refused send takes the message out again'); (4) the /api/chat answer now repeats the turn name ({turn, html}, src/serve/server.ts); (5) the wording of the end and header lines: 'the agent exited before the reply ended', 'working · 3s · 0 tokens', and the run summary 'latest call · N calls' (web/chat-thread.ts endLine/statusLine/runSummary). Point (5) passes if #werk-progress or #werk-tool-collapse sets these texts.

The card says a turn name is letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores. src/serve/turns.ts NAME also rejects a leading dot and any name over 100 characters, so a name like '.t1', which the card allows, gets a 400. Either loosen the regex to the card's rule or record the narrower rule on a card.

review.impact: `take` now does disk I/O (`appendFileSync` to the chat log through `write`/`append`) and calls `deliver`, which renders markdown and broadcasts, inside the stdout loop of `read`. `read` runs as `void read(proc)` and nothing catches its errors. A single throw kills the reader: the child's stdout is no longer drained, so the child can block on a full pipe; `endAll` never runs, so every open turn stays open in every page; `child` is never cleared, so later messages go to a child that nobody reads; and the error surfaces as an unhandled rejection.
review.fix: Wrap the per-line handling (or `append` alone) in a try/catch so that one failed log write or broadcast is reported and skipped, not fatal. Move the post-loop cleanup (flush, `child = undefined`, `endAll`) into a `finally` so that turns always end when the reader stops.

review.impact: `chatLogPath(log, CONVERSATION) as string` hides the `undefined` case of `chatLogPath` with a cast. If `CONVERSATION` is ever renamed to something the name rule rejects, every append writes to the path "undefined" and the compiler says nothing.
review.fix: Check the result once at start-up and throw if it is undefined, or add a non-optional helper for a known-good constant name. Drop the cast.

review.impact: `chatFrame` is a pure mapping from a ChatEvent to a live-channel frame, but it lives in the large server module. It is not on the pure-file coverage list and does not match the single-purpose module layout that `chat-stream.ts`, `turns.ts` and `open-card.ts` follow (#werk-stack-modules, #werk-test-gate-list).
review.fix: Move `chatFrame` into its own module (for example `src/serve/chat-frame.ts`) with its own test file, and add that file to `pure-files.txt`.

review.impact: `startChat` now has several jobs: it supervises the process, routes turns, builds the open-card line from a full `readMap` fold on every send, and keeps a session-buffered chat-log writer (`held`/`flush`/`append`). The log writer's buffering is stateful logic that could stand alone, and here it can only be tested through a real child process.
review.fix: Pull the session-buffered chat-log writer into a small module (for example `chat-log-writer.ts`, exposing `write`, `setSession` and `flushUnnamed`). `startChat` then only wires the child, the turns and the writer together.

review.impact: The server accepts a turn name that is already open and passes it to `sendTurn`, which pushes a duplicate onto `open`. Two pages, or a retried request, can then send turns with the same name. Their parts and end events become ambiguous, and both page entries are keyed by one name.
review.fix: Have `sendTurn` (or the handler) reject a name that is already open, for example with a 409, or have the server assign the name and return it.

review.impact: `heard()` re-implements the parsing of the fake agent's launch file that `src/test/project.ts` (`launches()`, line ~68) already does. The two copies have already drifted: this one matches a message to its launch with `find`, while the original uses `findLast`. A PID that gets reused, or a change to the launch-entry format, will now break one copy without breaking the other.
review.fix: Export one pure parser from `src/test/fake-script.ts` or `src/test/project.ts`, for example `readLaunches(text): Launch[]`. Use it in both places, and have `heard()` map each launch to the text of its messages.

review.impact: `chatLogPath(log, CONVERSATION) as string` uses a type assertion to hide the `undefined` case. If someone later changes `CONVERSATION` to a name that `NAME` rejects, the chat silently writes to the path "undefined" and the type checker does not complain.
review.fix: Narrow the type explicitly: `const chatLog = chatLogPath(log, CONVERSATION); if (chatLog === undefined) throw new Error(...)`. Alternatively, add a small helper that returns `string` for a name known to be valid.

review.impact: The last line of the session-id test calls `readLine` on an image `content_block_start` and asserts nothing. Its only effect is to cover a branch. If the behaviour on that branch changed, the test would not notice.
review.fix: Wrap the call in `expect(...).toEqual([])` so the test states that an image block changes no state, or delete the line.

review.impact: `chatFrame` is exported, but nothing outside `server.ts` imports it and no test calls it. The export suggests it is a public API, and it widens the module's surface for no reason.
review.fix: Drop the `export`. Or, if it is meant to be tested as pure code, move it into its own pure file with its own test and add that file to `pure-files.txt`.

review.impact: When the person stays on a card id that the map does not hold, the second turn sends the reminder before checking that the card exists. `titleOf` returns "" for that id, so the agent gets "[still on #gone — ]", which has an empty title and no note that the card is missing. The test file covers an unknown id only when the card has just changed (`openCardLine(map, "gone", undefined)`). No test covers `openCardLine(map, "gone", "gone")`, so this case passes unnoticed.
review.fix: Add `expect(openCardLine(map, "gone", "gone"))` to open-card.test.ts, and make the reminder name a missing card the same way the full block does, for example "[still on #gone — the map holds no card with this id]".

review.impact: The last call, `readLine(state, …content_block_start image…)`, has no assertion. It runs the branch where an unknown block kind changes nothing but checks nothing, so a change that sent a status or delta for an image block would still pass.
review.fix: Wrap the call in `expect(...).toEqual([])`. Also check that the next `message_delta` still reports the earlier state.

review.impact: Only a refused send (403) is tested. When `post` throws, as on a network failure, the `catch` branch drops the message and shows the error, and no test runs it. A regression could leave a message on screen marked as waiting for a turn that never starts.
review.fix: Add a test whose `post` rejects with `new Error("offline")`. It should assert that the alert shows "offline" and that the thread is empty.

review.impact: The token test waits a fixed `waitForTimeout(500)` and then asserts that the launches file is empty. On a slow machine, a regression that did start the agent could still pass, because the fake may not have written its launch line yet. The test can also never flake in the direction that would reveal the problem.
review.fix: Send one request with the correct token at the end and wait until `heard(w)` has exactly one launch, whose only message is that request's text. That proves the two refused requests started nothing before it.

review.impact: The handler maps both a missing `card` and `card: ""` to ROOT_ID, but only the missing case is tested. If the empty-string case regressed, the agent would get "[the map is now at # — …]".
review.fix: Post `{ text, turn, card: "" }` and assert that the message the agent hears starts with "[the map is now at #root — ".

review.impact: The server checks only that `card` is a string. It does not check that it is a well-formed card id, and it puts no limit on its length. `openCardLine` copies an unknown id word for word into the line that werk itself writes (`[the map is now at #<card> — …]`). That line opens every agent turn and is saved in the chat log as a werk `tooling` line. A card value with newlines or bracketed text can therefore make text look like it came from werk rather than from the person. The risk is low because only a caller with the token can do this, and that caller already controls `text`. Still, it blurs the line between what werk says and what the person says, and a very large value is copied into both the prompt and the log.
review.fix: Check `card` against the map's id pattern, which `isTurnName` already shows how to do (letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`, with a length cap). Answer 400 when it does not match, as the turn-name check does.

review.impact: `logged()` saves every tool result and every tool input in full to `.werk/chats/main.jsonl` inside the project folder. If the agent reads a file that holds secrets, for example `cat .env` or a credentials file, the secret is kept on disk next to the map log. If the project commits `.werk/`, the secret can end up in git. Every tool result is also sent to every open page.
review.fix: Keep the decided behaviour, but make sure `.werk/chats/` is git-ignored, for example by writing a `.gitignore` into the chats folder the first time it is created. Also consider capping how much of a tool result is logged.

review.impact: Each streamed delta, status event and one-second header tick re-renders every turn in the thread. review.impact: `expect(remove("g").hasAttribute("data-children")).toBe(false)` is meant to cover the `node.proposed ? undefined : ...` guard in removeButton. review.impact: The test is named "render in op order", but it only checks that the kept, removed and added parts are present, plus the order of the two removed parts. If bodyDiffHtml reordered its parts (for example, put every addition last), the test would still pass.

review.impact: The second `await screen.findByRole("alert")` resolves at once because the first failure's alert is still on screen. review.impact: Each handleRemove call creates a React root on a div in document.body, and nothing unmounts it. The afterEach only clears `document.body.innerHTML`, so the roots and click listeners from earlier tests stay alive in the shared DOM (#werk-test-dom). This can leak into later component tests in the same process.
review.fix: Pass a `host` element that the test owns and unmount its root in afterEach, or have handleRemove return a disposer that the test calls in cleanup.

review.impact: align() allocates an (a+1)*(b+1) Int32Array and does O(n*m) work. The server runs it on every card render, once for each title, why and body field that has a pending change. An agent can propose a large body edit, for example two blocks of about 20k tokens each. That allocates gigabytes, or stalls the single server process, on every read of that card and on every live refresh. The proposal persists in the log until someone accepts or rejects it, so the card page keeps failing until then.
review.fix: Cap the size of the diff input. Above a token threshold, for example when a.length*b.length exceeds a few million, skip the word alignment and fall back to wholeBlock(old, 'removed') + wholeBlock(next, 'added'). Alternatively, trim the common prefix and suffix before building the table, or use a linear-space diff such as Myers.

review.impact: Every card page now builds the ✕ by running the full subtree removal, `removalOf(map, id, false)`, just to count cards. For the root card, or any high card, that means walking the whole map. For each descendant it calls `linksTo`/`linksFrom` (via `childrenOf` and `companions`), and each of those filters every link in the map. It also checks membership with `Array.includes` over arrays that keep growing. The cost is roughly O(cards × links) plus O(cards²) on every render of the most-viewed pages, and `store.refresh` re-reads the card after every write. Before this change the work ran only when a removal event was folded.
review.fix: Build an index once per render: a map from parent to children over `refines` links, and a map of companions per card. Count the subtree with a BFS over that index using a Set. If `removalOf` must stay the single source of truth, give it a precomputed adjacency index and use Sets instead of `includes`, or memoise the counts per folded map.

review.impact: `align` allocates a dense (a+1)×(b+1) Int32Array and fills every cell. `wordSource` runs it on the tokens of a whole paragraph, a title, or a why block, where every word, space and punctuation mark is a token. A long paragraph of about 3k tokens on each side needs about 9M cells (36 MB) and about 9M calls to `same`, on the server, on every read of a card with a pending edit. The input comes from the proposal, which an agent writes, so its size has no bound.
review.fix: Before the LCS, trim the common prefix and suffix of the tokens, which usually shrinks the matrix to the changed region. Also cap the matrix size, for example at 1–2M cells, and above the cap fall back to marking the whole block removed and added (the `wholeBlock` path). Alternatively, use a linear-space Myers diff.

review.impact: `removeButton` calls `parentOf`, which scans every link. It then calls `removalOf(..., true)`, which scans every link again to find the same parent and the children. That is extra full scans of the links on every card render.
review.fix: Find the children and the parent once, with one pass or from the index suggested above, and reuse them for `data-parent` and the reparent counts.

review.impact: The search box sends a request on every keystroke and does not wait for typing to pause. Typing a 15-character query does 15 full folds and 15 file appends, and most of the answers are thrown away. On a large map this blocks the single-threaded server for chat and card reads while the person types.

Better still, have the server keep the folded map and fold again only when the changed signal says the log changed, rather than on every search request.

review.impact: `rollupOf` already walks the card and all of its descendants, calling `marksOn` (via `isStale`) on each. `headerRead` then calls `descendantsOf` again and runs `marksOn` (via `isPaused`) on every card a second time. `marksOn` checks every hop of a mark against all of `map.links`, so the header of the root does two full passes over the subtree, each costing marks × hops × links, on every card read.
review.fix: Count paused in the same single pass over the subtree: either extend `rollupOf` with a paused count, or call `marksOn` once per card and check its result for both stale and paused.

review.impact: On the board view, `refresh` calls `readCard(place.id)` only to get the header. That makes the server fold the log and render the full card HTML, then the client discards the HTML. This happens on every connect of the live channel and every changed signal while the board is open.

Most choices come from the decided cards on this ticket, not only from the three cards the builder named, so they are not new decisions. Two pane choices have no card: (1) the header row with no running turn falls back to 'idle', or to the end line of the last ended turn (web/chat-thread.ts lastEnded); (2) a sent message first shows as escaped plain text, and the server's HTML replaces it when the POST answers (web/chat-pane.tsx send). Both are small. Propose a card if they are meant to stay.

review.impact: `close()` waits only for `proc.exited`. It does not wait for `read(proc)`, and `read` still flushes held chat-log lines and delivers `exited` events after that point. So writes to `.werk/chats/main.jsonl` and broadcasts can happen after `close()` resolves. The e2e `stop()` in `e2e/project.ts` works around this with `rmSync` retries ('retries while the chat agent it stops still writes the chat log'). That hides the lifecycle race instead of fixing it, and any caller that tears down the project folder after `close()` can hit the same race.
review.fix: Keep the promise that `read(proc)` returns (for example `let reading: Promise<void> | undefined`, set in `launch`), and have `close()` await it after `proc.exited`. Then drop `maxRetries`/`retryDelay` and the comment about it from `e2e/project.ts` `stop()`.

review.impact: `chatLogPath(log, CONVERSATION) as string` hides the `undefined` case in the type. If someone later makes `CONVERSATION` a name that `chatLogPath` rejects, the cast compiles and `append` fails at runtime on `mkdirSync(dirname(undefined))`.
review.fix: Narrow it explicitly instead of casting: `const chatLog = chatLogPath(log, CONVERSATION); if (chatLog === undefined) throw new Error(...)`. Or add a non-optional helper for the fixed conversation name.

review.impact: `isTurnName` accepts names like `agent-1`, which is the same namespace `partTurn` uses for server-named turns. A page turn with that name would merge with an unasked agent turn, both in `turns.open` and in the page thread.
review.fix: Give server-named turns a prefix the page's names can't match, such as a leading character that `NAME` rejects. Or make `isTurnName` reject the `agent-` prefix.

review.impact: `chatFrame` turns chat events into the live-channel wire shape, and it is added to `server.ts`, which already handles HTTP routing, auth and client serving. This goes against the small single-purpose modules rule (#werk-stack-modules), and it means a change to the chat wire format touches the server module.
review.fix: Move `chatFrame` into its own small module, for example `src/serve/chat-frame.ts`, with its own test. Add that file to `pure-files.txt`, since the function is pure.

review.impact: `chatLogPath(log, CONVERSATION) as string` uses a type assertion to hide the `undefined` case. If CONVERSATION is ever renamed to something that fails NAME, the chat log silently writes to a path called "undefined" and the type checker cannot catch it.
review.fix: Narrow it explicitly, for example `const chatLog = chatLogPath(log, CONVERSATION); if (chatLog === undefined) throw new Error(...)`. Another option is a module-level constant that is checked once.

review.impact: The `session` parameter of `append` shadows the outer mutable `session`. That makes it easy to misread which value is written into the log line, in exactly the code that carries the held-until-named logic.
review.fix: Rename the parameter, for example `named` as `flush` already does, or `sessionId`.

review.impact: The fallback id expression `${text(message.id) || "m"}:f${state.finished}` is written twice in `finished()`, once for tool_use and once for text. The two can drift apart.
review.fix: Compute the fallback id once at the top of `finished()`, for example `const fallback = ...`, and use it in both branches.

review.impact: The last statement of the session-id test calls `readLine` with an image `content_block_start` and asserts nothing. It reads like an unfinished assertion and exists only to raise coverage.
review.fix: Add the expected result, for example `.toEqual([])` for a kind that changes no state, or remove the line.

review.impact: The chat log path `join(project.dir, ".werk", "chats", "main.jsonl")` is built by hand in three tests. It also duplicates `chatLogPath` and `CONVERSATION`, so a change to the layout breaks the tests in three places.
review.fix: Add one helper next to `log()`, for example `const chatFile = () => chatLogPath(log(), CONVERSATION)`, and use it in all three tests.

review.impact: `endLine(x.end, x.startedAt !== undefined)` appears in both TurnView and ChatHeader. That spreads knowledge of how a turn's end is worded across two components.
review.fix: Add a `turnEndLine(turn: Turn)` helper in chat-thread.ts that takes the whole turn, and call it from both places.

review.impact: The fallthrough `return [...items];` in `withItem` copies the array for events that never reach it, because `update` handles them first. It is unreachable in practice and allocates for nothing.
review.fix: Return `items` as it is, or narrow the event type of `withItem` to the part, tool and tool-result kinds so the fallthrough is not needed.

review.impact: `chatFrame` is exported, but only server.ts uses it and no test imports it. The export adds API surface for nothing. The function is pure mapping logic, yet it lives in an impure file outside the pure-file coverage gate.
review.fix: Either drop the `export`, or move `chatFrame` into its own pure module with a test and list that module in pure-files.txt, as the change already does for turns.ts and open-card.ts.

review.impact: `chatFrame` is new and exported, but no unit test calls it. Only the delta, chat, started, ended and tool-less status frames are covered, through `server.test.ts`. Nothing checks how the server turns `exited`, `tool-result` and a status with a tool into live-channel frames. A wrong frame name or a dropped field would break the pane without failing any test. Two cases matter most: an `exited` turn sent as `ended`, and the status `tool` field going missing. The pane tests build these frames by hand, and the e2e covers only the happy tool path.
review.fix: Add a `chatFrame` test to `server.test.ts` with one case for each `ChatEvent` kind. Check the frame name and data for `tool` (including `input` as `undefined` → ""), `tool-result` with `error: true`, `status` with `tool`, `exited` → ["turn", {turn, state:"exited"}], and `end`.

review.impact: The session-id test ends with a `readLine` call on an `image` `content_block_start` and never checks the result. It runs the 'kind that changes no state' branch of `stateOf` for coverage only. If that branch started emitting a status part, the test would still pass.
review.fix: Wrap the call: expect(readLine(state, stream({ type: "content_block_start", index: 0, content_block: { type: "image" } }))).toEqual([]). Better still, move it into a test whose name describes that behaviour.

review.impact: The server maps an empty `card` string to `ROOT_ID`, and no test sends `card: ""`. `server.test` covers only a missing card and `card: 3`. If the empty-string branch regressed, the agent would hear '[the map is now at # — the map holds no card…]' and no test would fail.
review.fix: In the rendered-chat test of `server.test.ts`, also send `{ text, turn, card: "" }`. Check that the agent's message starts with "[the map is now at #root — ".

review.impact: The test claims the message 'shows at once', but the fake post resolves straight away. It only checks the thread after the server's HTML has replaced the draft, so the optimistic draw before the answer is never checked. If the immediate `sent` event were removed, the test would still pass.
review.fix: Give the fake post a response that the test resolves by hand. Check that the turn shows the escaped words and a `data-turn` element before resolving, then check that it shows the server HTML afterwards.

review.impact: The server checks only that `card` is a string. It never checks that it is a card id, while `turn` has to match a strict name pattern. So a request with the token can send a card value of any length, including newlines. That value is copied straight into the open-card line: the agent reads it in its prompt, and it is written to the chat log as a 'werk' tooling line. A crafted value could fake extra werk-framed lines such as a second '[the map is now at …]' block in a line that is supposed to come from werk, and an oversized value makes every turn and its log line bigger. The token holder already controls `text`, so this crosses no privilege boundary. It is a gap in validation only.
review.fix: Check `card` against the same id pattern the map uses for node ids, for example one shared `isCardId` in the map module, with a length limit. Return 400 for anything else, as is already done for a bad turn name. Add a server test that sends a card value with a newline.

review.impact: Every live event (each streamed delta, status and tool result) runs applyEvent, which copies the thread, then re-renders every TurnView in the conversation. Each re-render runs runSummary, so callLine calls JSON.parse on the latest call's input in every tool run. During a long conversation the cost of each streamed token grows with the length of the whole thread, not just the running turn.
review.fix: Wrap TurnView in React.memo. update() already returns the same object for turns that did not change, so only the turn that changed re-renders. Or compute the summary line once, when the tool event arrives in withItem, and store it.

review.impact: Each kept part of a reply (finished block, tool call, tool result) runs a synchronous mkdirSync and appendFileSync on the server's event loop. While a turn runs many tools, this blocks HTTP handling and the live channel for each part.
review.fix: Create the chats folder once, when the chat starts or on the first append, not on every append. Keep appendFileSync if the log must be in order and durable, or write the lines through one append stream instead.

causeOfLast.why: the main line added the card removal to the same client entry and the same pure-file list that this ticket changed.

grade.gap: Of the cards the builder named, only #vi-routes touches this work, but the diff draws on many unnamed cards (#vi-crumbs-line, #vi-jump-hash, #vi-jump-row, #vi-counts-header, #vi-crumbs-place, #vi-tabs). These choices pass only if those cards give them; otherwise the next pass should name or propose a card for each: (1) src/serve/header.ts:30 shows no counts at all when the open card has no children (rollup.cards < 2); (2) web/crumbs.ts:6 shows a third crumb segment only when the left pane is at least 700px wide, measured on the pane, not the window; (3) src/serve/home-html.ts shows an empty build-rules card with the text NO_BUILD_RULES when there is no #how, and labels the columns 'What' and 'How'; (4) web/main.tsx stores the place under the key 'werk:place:<name>', and src/serve/page.ts names the meta tag 'werk-project'.

review.impact: The pure home renderer, and through it page.ts and server.ts, now imports src/agent/prompt.ts only to get one constant. That module builds the agent's prompt and bundles instructions.md and the subagent markdown files as text. The serve render path and its unit test therefore load the agent's prompt assets, so the module boundary points the wrong way (serve depends on agent). A change to the prompt module now reaches the home view.
review.fix: Move BUILD_RULES_CARD into src/map/types.ts next to ROOT_ID, since it names a well-known card id just as ROOT_ID does. Import it from there in both prompt.ts and home-html.ts.

review.impact: The project's folder is now worked out from the log path with dirname(dirname(project.log)) in two places in server.ts (here and the startChat call). Each request also repeats this to get the name. If the log's layout under .werk changes, both copies have to change together.
review.fix: Add a `root` (or `name`) field to ProjectContext, set once in openProject. Use it both for the page name and for startChat.

review.impact: A failed search is ignored without a trace, and the rows from the previous text stay open. The person then sees results that do not match what they typed, and Enter opens one of them. In main.tsx, search() also never checks response.ok.
review.fix: On rejection, clear the rows (setRows([])) when the effect is still current. Make search() throw on a non-ok response so that path is actually taken.

review.impact: The status colours are now defined twice more: as hex values in jump-box.tsx and as Tailwind classes in counts-strip.tsx, besides the colours the card look already uses. The two maps can drift apart, so a dot in the search list could stop matching the same status in the header counts.
review.fix: Keep one status-to-colour map in a shared client module and have both jump-box.tsx and counts-strip.tsx read it.

review.impact: The client now works out the page title for each view (Home, Board, or the card title plus its id) on its own. `titleOf` in src/serve/page.ts:31 does the same job for the first paint. The two copies can drift apart, and the tab title would then change after hydration.
review.fix: Move the title rule into one pure function next to `pathOf` in web/routes.ts, taking the route and an optional card title. Call it from both `titleOf` and the `store.subscribe` callback.

review.impact: `shown = route.view === "home" ? undefined : header` repeats a rule the store already enforces: `go` clears the header for the home, and `refresh` never sets one there. Because the rule lives in two places, a reader can't tell which one is authoritative.
review.fix: Use `header` from the store directly and drop `shown`. Alternatively, keep the rule only here and remove it from the store. Either way, keep a single owner.

review.impact: `GREY` repeats the same hex value as `DOT.excerpt` ("#9ca3af"). If someone changes one, the other will no longer match.
review.fix: Define `const GREY = "#9ca3af"` before `DOT` and use it as `excerpt: GREY`.

review.impact: The nested ternary `route.view === "map" ? route.id : place.view === "map" ? place.id : undefined` mixes two decisions in one line: which card's header to read, and whether there is one at all. That makes the board and home branches of `refresh` hard to follow.
review.fix: Pull it out into a small named helper, for example `headerIdOf(route, place)`, written with plain `if` returns.

review.impact: No unit or e2e test covers ArrowDown or ArrowUp moving the selection. The e2e test only presses Enter on the first row, so if the clamp at either end broke (for example, ArrowUp past row 0 or ArrowDown past the last row leaving `selected` out of range so Enter opens nothing), or if a stale `selected` carried over to a shorter result list, every test would still pass.
review.fix: In e2e/header.e2e.ts, after filling '#werk', press ArrowDown twice and assert that the row with aria-selected=true has data-id 'vi-werk'. Then press ArrowDown once more and assert the selection stays on 'vi-werk'. Press ArrowUp three times and assert it is back on 'werk'. Finally press Enter and assert the URL is the selected card's.

review.impact: The # branch lowercases both the query and the id, but no test uses a query or an id with capitals. If the `.toLowerCase()` on node.id or on the query were dropped, every test would still pass.
review.fix: Add `expect(ids("#WERK-STACK")[0]).toBe("werk-stack")`, and add a node with a mixed-case id that a lowercase # query must find.

review.impact: The paused count leaves out proposed (ghost) cards and nodes that are not cards, but nothing tests that filter. A proposed card under a postponed card could be counted as paused and no test would fail.
review.fix: Add a proposed card under the postponed card 'd' (or postpone a subtree that holds a ghost), then assert `headerRead(map, "root")?.counts?.paused` stays at the count of real cards only.

review.impact: `goTo` adds no history entry when the path is already the open one, so clicking the active tab or crumb does nothing. No test covers this, so a regression that pushes duplicate history entries, or that skips `store.go` on a real change, would go unnoticed.
review.fix: In e2e/header.e2e.ts, click the active Map tab, then call `page.goBack()` and assert that the URL is the previous view's and not the same card.

review.impact: The search box sends one /api/search request on every keystroke, with no debounce. On the server, each request reads the whole log from disk, folds it again, and appends a line to the fold-times file (src/serve/server.ts:166 calls readMap). The `current` flag only drops replies that arrive late; the requests still run. So typing a 15-character query does 15 full folds and 15 file appends, and that cost grows with the size of the log.
review.fix: Wait about 120–150 ms after the last keystroke before calling search (a setTimeout in the effect, cleared in its cleanup), and cancel the earlier fetch with an AbortController. The server could also reuse a cached fold while the log is unchanged, but the debounce alone stops most of the repeated work.

review.impact: On the Board view, refresh calls readCard for the last card open on the map only to get its header. That fetches /api/card, which builds the full card read and the card's HTML (cardRead and cardHtml) and then throws both away. This happens on every navigation to /board and on every live 'changed' signal while the board is open.
review.fix: Add a header-only read (for example GET /api/header/:id, which returns headerRead) and use it when the route is not a map route. Or skip the refetch on the board and keep the header already in state.

review.impact: headerRead walks the subtree twice: once in rollupOf and again here, calling descendantsOf and then marksOn for each node to count the paused cards. Each card read now pays for two subtree walks instead of one, which costs more for cards near the root of a large map.
review.fix: Count paused cards in the same pass as the rollup. For example, add a rollup variant that also counts the paused mark, so the subtree is walked once.

grade.gap: The scenario is covered end to end in e2e/excerpt.e2e.ts. It quotes into two ghost cards from one chat log, discards the first and checks that both seat and seat:ex0 show [data-missing]. It accepts the second from its page and checks that invoice and invoice:ex0 are no longer proposed. Then it checks the words, speaker, time, session, message and span on the excerpt page. I could not run the tests here, so passing them is not confirmed.

Minor: the card page also prints the excerpt's conversation (src/serve/card-html.ts pointerHtml via pointerFields), which the scenario does not list. #werk-excerpt-pointer names it as a part of the pointer, so this is acceptable.

The pointer appears on the card page inside the hero box, as a <dl data-field="pointer"> between the body and the rollup bar (src/serve/card-html.ts cardHtml). Neither #vi-onview-hero nor #werk-excerpt-pointer says where the pointer goes on the page. It is a small layout choice and could get a one-line note on #vi-onview-hero. Sharing one field list between the printed card and the page (pointerFields in src/map/show.ts) is internal to a helper, so it is not a decision.

review.impact: The card page now imports from `src/map/show.ts` just to get `pointerFields`. That module exists to produce the text of `werk show`. The web page now depends on the CLI's text formatter, so a change to `werk show` can quietly change the card page too. This works against #werk-stack-modules, which keeps modules single-purpose so that independent tickets touch different files.
review.fix: Move `PointerField` and `pointerFields` into a small module that both sides can use, such as `src/map/pointer.ts` or `types.ts`/`chat.ts` next to the excerpt node. Then have both `show.ts` and `card-html.ts` import it from there.

review.impact: Fields that are already strings (speaker, said_at, conversation, session) are wrapped in template literals like `${node.speaker}`. The wrapping does nothing and makes the reader wonder whether a conversion is needed.
review.fix: Use `node.speaker`, `node.said_at`, `node.conversation` and `node.session` directly. Keep `String(node.message)` and the span template for the numbers.

review.impact: `name` and `label` differ only in one entry (said-at vs "said at"). Every other entry repeats the same string twice, which adds noise and invites the two to drift apart.
review.fix: Store only `label`, and derive the markup name with `label.replace(/ /g, "-")` in pointerHtml. If two fields are kept, document why.

review.impact: The new test only uses plain values like 'person', 'pricing' and 's1'. If someone removed `escapeHtml(value)` from `pointerHtml`, the test would still pass, even though a speaker, session or conversation value containing `<` or `&` could then inject markup into the card page.
review.fix: Add a case with an excerpt whose session or conversation contains HTML characters such as `<b>&`. Assert that the `dd` text is the literal string and that no `b` element appears inside `[data-field="pointer"]`.

grade.gap: I read the code but could not run the test or the build because running commands needed approval. `src/verbs/index.ts` now imports every module that the `verbModules()` macro finds in `src/verbs`, so a new `ping.ts` that registers itself shows up in `werk help`, which lists `registry.list()`, with no other file edited. The test in `src/verbs/index.test.ts` covers the before and after verb names. It does not check that `git status` shows only the new module, though no step of the design writes a tracked file. Next pass, run `make build` and confirm `dist/werk help` still lists every verb. This matters because the compiled executable now depends on the template-literal dynamic import `./${name}` resolving inside the bundle, built with `--compile --splitting` and many entry points.

Two changes go beyond the story, but both are needed to keep the existing executable working once the shared import list is gone: the `package.json` build script that makes each verb module a separate entry point, and the Makefile comment. I found no new user-facing behaviour.

Two choices come from no card, though neither is large enough to fail this line: (1) every non-test `.ts` file in `src/verbs` except `index.ts` is treated as a verb module and loaded (`src/cli/verb-modules.ts:9`), so a helper module placed in that folder would also load; (2) the folder is listed at transpile or bundle time with a Bun macro (`with { type: "macro" }`) rather than a separate build step that writes a file list. #werk-dist allows either approach: the build writes the list and the code reads it. A short card could record the folder convention.

review.impact: The list of verb modules is now worked out in two places. The build script's shell glob (`ls src/verbs/*.ts | grep -v '\.test\.ts$'`) and the `verbModules()` macro filter use separate rules: the glob also picks up `index.ts`, and it does not use the macro's filter. If one rule changes without the other, for example to skip a helper file in `src/verbs`, the loader can import a module that the build never added as an entry point. Nothing catches this until the compiled `dist/werk` fails at run time, because the tests run from source.
review.fix: Make the macro the only source. Add a small build script, run through a make target, that imports `verbModules()` and passes those files as the entry points to `Bun.build` with compile and splitting. Or make the shell glob reuse the macro's output.

review.impact: The header comment still says "the list of verb modules holds only their imports". This change removed that list, so the comment now points readers to a design that no longer exists.
review.fix: Change the comment to describe the loader: `src/verbs/index.ts` imports every module in the folder, so a new verb needs no edit to a shared list.

review.impact: A module in `src/cli` hardcodes the layout of `src/verbs`: the `../verbs` path and the exception for `index.ts`. Moving or renaming the loader then means editing a file in a different module, which weakens the single-purpose module boundary.
review.fix: Move the macro next to its only user, for example to `src/verbs/modules.ts`, and leave out both `index.ts` and its own file. Or pass the folder and the loader's file name in as arguments.

review.impact: The rule for which files count as verb modules now lives in two places. `verbModules()` in src/cli/verb-modules.ts uses a TypeScript filter, and the build script uses an inline `ls src/verbs/*.ts | grep -v '\.test\.ts$'` pipeline. If the rule changes, for example to skip a helper file or to change the test-file suffix, one copy can be updated without the other. The loader would then import a module that the executable never compiled as an entry, or the build would add files the loader never loads. This failure only appears in the compiled binary, not under `bun test`. The shell pipeline is also hard to read inside a JSON string, with its double-escaped backslashes.
review.fix: Keep a single source of truth. Add a small script, such as `scripts/build.ts`, that calls `verbModules()` and passes `['src/cli.ts', ...verbModules().map(n => `src/verbs/${n}`)]` to `Bun.build`/`bun build --compile --splitting`. Point the `build` script at it. The Makefile comment can then point to that script instead of describing the mechanism.

review.impact: The length assertion uses `files.filter(!test).length - 1` to rebuild the filter under test. It relies on an implicit 'minus index.ts' rule and on every other file in the folder being a `.ts` verb module. It mostly repeats the implementation instead of checking a behaviour. A non-`.ts` file added to src/verbs, such as a README, would break it in a way that is hard to understand.
review.fix: Assert the expected set directly: `expect(verbModules()).toEqual(files.filter(n => n.endsWith('.ts') && !n.endsWith('.test.ts') && n !== 'index.ts').sort())`. Or drop the length check and rely on the `toContain`/`not.toContain` assertions together with the end-to-end 'new verb module appears' test.

review.impact: `verbModules()` is called four times in one test, and each call reads the directory again. This is small redundant noise.
review.fix: Call it once: `const modules = verbModules();` and assert on `modules`.

review.impact: Both tests run the loader from source with `bun src/cli.ts`. Nothing tests the compiled executable, and that is where this change carries the most risk. The new build depends on three things: `--splitting` with every verb as its own entry point, the macro writing in the list of names, and a template `import(`./${name}`)` that must still resolve to the `.ts` names inside the bundled filesystem. If the executable fails to resolve these imports or leaves out a verb, every test still passes, and the problem only shows when someone uses `dist/werk`.
review.fix: Add a test that builds the executable into a temporary folder with the same command as the `build` script. It should run `<tmp>/werk help` and assert that the help lists one verb for each entry in `verbModules()`. It should also add a verb module to a copy of the app and rebuild that copy, so the build is shown to pick up the new verb as well.

review.impact: `before` comes from the same loader that is under test, so `for (const name of before) expect(after).toContain(name)` only shows that the help is the same before and after. The only check on `before` is that it contains `help`. A loader that imported only some of the modules, such as just the first one or just `help.ts`, would still pass. Nothing ties the verbs that are actually registered to `verbModules()`.
review.fix: Assert that `before` covers every verb module. One way is to check that `before.length` is at least `verbModules().length`. Another is to check for a fixed set of known verbs (accept, add, status, serve, ticket-check, …), so the test fails when the loader drops modules.

review.impact: The count check repeats the filter from the implementation (`readdirSync`, then drop `.test.ts`, then subtract one for index.ts). A bug that is in both places will not be caught. The check also assumes that every non-test entry in the folder is a `.ts` file and that index.ts exists, so adding any other file, such as a fixture or a `.md` file, breaks it for no real reason.
review.fix: Compare against values written out in the test instead. For example, assert that the list is sorted, check it against a few known module names, and add a non-`.ts` file in a temporary folder to show that the filter leaves it out. Alternatively, use the same `.ts` filter for `files` so the subtraction counts only index.ts.

review.impact: When `werk help` fails in the copied app, for example because the macro import or a dynamic import breaks, the test reports only `expected 0, received 1`. The child process's stderr is captured but never shown, so the failure is hard to diagnose.
review.fix: Put stderr in the assertion. For example, run `expect({ code: run.exitCode, stderr: run.stderr.toString() }).toEqual({ code: 0, stderr: expect.any(String) })`, or throw an error that contains stderr when the exit code is not 0.

grade.gap: The story is covered from start to end in src/verbs/words-verbs.test.ts, in the test 'a retitle on a real card shows only the new title and keeps the old one in the log'. Steps covered: propose #a 'Use a log'; accept with --actor you; retitle prints 'a: retitled'; the log is exactly one line longer and all earlier lines are unchanged; show prints the new title and not the old one; the earlier log line still holds the old title; a body edit then shows the new body and the new title. The grader could not run the tests because the command was not approved.

A junk file is committed at the repository root: 'erk-cli-retitle), and#' (the name ends in a tab). It holds one stray comment line copied from the top of src/verbs/retitle.ts. Delete it. These behaviours also go beyond the one story: the --title flag form of retitle (retitle.ts, flags) and edit --why (edit.ts). The story only needs a positional retitle and edit --body. The refusal on a decided card can stay, because without it retitle would write over frozen words (#map-frozen).

Two choices in the diff come from no card the builder named. (1) The form of the retitle command comes from #werk-cli-retitle, which the builder did not name: the title as a second argument or with --title, refusing both together, the output '<id>: retitled', and the --why and --body flags on edit. Add #werk-cli-retitle to the named cards. review.impact: The `git` helper passes on the parent's whole environment and the user's global git config. review.impact: The test helper runs git with the global and system git config of the person running the test. If that config sets commit.gpgsign=true, the commit in the temporary copy uses their real signing key. That can prompt for a passphrase or touch a hardware key, and it fails on machines where signing is not set up. A global core.hooksPath also runs their own hooks against the temporary repo. This breaks #werk-test-external, which says a test never reaches the real data of the person who runs it, and the test's result then depends on the machine it runs on.
review.fix: Pass an isolated environment to Bun.spawnSync in git(): set GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 on top of process.env. As an alternative, add `-c commit.gpgsign=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null` to the commit call.

review.impact: `take()` runs inside the stdout read loop, and it now calls `appendFileSync` on every finished block, tool call and result (also through `flush` when the session arrives). If the chat log cannot be written (disk full, permissions, folder removed), the loop throws and the async `read()` rejects with no handler, because it is started as `void read(proc)`. The child's stdout is then never drained again. `child` is never cleared and `endAll` never runs, so every open turn stays open in every page and later messages go to a child that nobody reads. One failed log write breaks the chat until the server restarts.
review.fix: Keep the chat log from taking down the live channel. Catch inside `append` (as `readMap` does for its fold-time line), or wrap the body of `take` so that a failed write is reported but the parts are still delivered and the read loop goes on. Also add a `.catch` to `void read(proc)` that clears `child` and runs `endAll`, so a reader that fails still ends its turns.

review.impact: `send()` sets `lastCard = card` and writes the two chat-log lines before it calls `sendTurn` and writes to stdin. If a log write throws, the request fails, but `lastCard` already names a card the agent never heard. The next message on that card then sends only the one-line `[still on …]` reminder and never the whole card, which breaks #werk-card-blind for the rest of that child's life. The order of the side effects also lets the log, the turn queue and the agent's stdin disagree with each other.
review.fix: Write to the agent first, then update the state: build the line, call `sendTurn` and write to stdin, and only after that set `lastCard` and append to the log. Or make the log append unable to throw, as in the finding above.
