review.impact: The test says a sent message 'shows at once', but its only check on the thread waits for the server's rendered '!' HTML. It would still pass if the pane drew the message only after the POST answered, so the optimistic draw is untested.
review.fix: Give the test a post that resolves only on demand. Check that turns()[0] holds the escaped words before resolving it, then that the server's HTML replaces them.

review.impact: stop() waits for the server's 'exit' event without a time limit. A server that ignores SIGTERM hangs afterEach until the Playwright hook times out, and that failure would not say which server hung.
review.fix: Race the exit against a short timer, send SIGKILL if the timer wins, then remove the folder.

review.impact: The `card` field is only checked to be a string. It is not checked as a card id, and its length is not limited. It goes straight into `openCardLine` (`#${id}` in `src/serve/open-card.ts`), which builds the werk-written open-card line that reaches the agent and is saved in the chat log as a 'werk'/'tooling' line. A card value with newlines or brackets can therefore fake the open-card text that werk adds, for example a fake '[the map is now at …]' block or extra 'why:' lines. It also lets a very large value into every turn's prompt and log line. The sender already needs the token, so the risk is limited, but the server is trusting a field it builds its own framing from.
review.fix: Check `card` with the same rule the map uses for node ids (or a pattern like `isTurnName`'s: letters, digits, `._-`, with a length limit), and return 400 otherwise. Or, in `openCardLine`, name the card by its id only when `map.nodes.has(id)`, and fall back to the home card or a fixed 'unknown card' text instead of repeating the raw value.

review.impact: Each chat message runs readMap, which reads and folds the whole map log and appends a fold-time line. Right after that, the /api/chat handler calls knownIds(), which can fold the log again. That is up to two full folds per message, and a large map makes each send slower. It costs little now, but the cost grows with the log.
review.fix: Build the open-card line from one fold per message. Either pass the map to send(), or share the size-keyed cache that knownIds already uses in server.ts so the chat and the renderer reuse one folded map.

review.impact: Every streamed delta and status event creates a new thread array. That re-renders every TurnView and ReplyItem in the pane, not just the running turn, and each tool-run summary re-parses its call's JSON input through callLine/runSummary. In a long chat with many tool calls, the work per token grows with the size of the thread.
review.fix: Wrap TurnView and ReplyItem in React.memo. applyEvent already keeps the turns it does not touch, so they will skip re-rendering. Also compute runSummary with useMemo on item.calls, or once in withItem when a call is added, instead of on every render.

causeOfLast.why: decided cards contradict each other on whether a building ticket can be archived, and no card resolved that contradiction until now.

grade.gap: Not run here: running `make test-coverage` needed approval, so I could not confirm the result. Judged from the code: fold.ts, rules.ts and events.ts are in pure-files.txt. fold.ts and rules.ts each have their own test file, and events.ts has only types, so the gate passes it as having no executable lines. The `ticket === undefined` guards in fold.ts apply() can never run, which costs a few lines of coverage but should leave the file above 90%.

review.impact: appendBoardEvent writes `${JSON.stringify(event)}\n` without checking whether the file ends in a newline. A merge or a hand edit can leave the last line without one. The new event then joins the last line, so both events turn unreadable and the board loses a real event. The decision log's write() in src/map/store.ts:53-55 already handles this case with a `lead` newline, so the board log does not match the code beside it.
review.fix: Do what store.ts does. Read the text, prefix "\n" when the text is not empty and does not end with "\n", then append. The simplest way is to reuse the text that readBoardLog already reads.

review.impact: refusal() checks only that payload.id is a string. A line that parses as JSON but has the wrong shape can still crash the fold instead of being set aside. Examples are a ticket.planned without a blocked_by array, which throws in openBlockers when another ticket moves to building, and a bare `null` line, which throws on `event.type` in foldBoard. That goes against the stated intent that one bad line must not hide the rest of the board (#pr-log-refuse).
review.fix: Check the shape of each folded event before applying it. For ticket.planned, check that title is a string and blocked_by is a string array. For ticket.moved, check that `to` is a Column. Set aside any event that fails. In readBoardLog, put a parsed value that is not an object in unreadable.

review.impact: The board log reports a refused write with a `{ok:false,error}` result. The decision log next to it throws `Refused` from write(), so the two stores handle refusal in two different ways.
review.fix: Either throw a Refused-style error here as store.ts does, or add a comment saying why the board log returns a result instead.

review.impact: A move reads and folds the whole board log three times: once in readBoard for refuseAgentMove, once inside appendBoardEvent, and once after the write to print the column. The agent check and the append are two separate reads, and printing the column needs a third fold even though the column is already known.
review.fix: Fold the board once and pass it to the agent check and to the write, for example with an appendBoardEvent overload that takes a Board. Print the column from the written event or from the board already folded: `to` for a move, and the ticket's prior column for an archive or a restore.

review.impact: One `werk ticket move` reads and folds the whole board log three times: once for `refuseAgentMove`, once inside `appendBoardEvent`, and once to print the column. The extra reads make the log larger to parse each time, and the board printed can differ from the board that was checked.
review.fix: Print the column from the written event: `written.event.payload.to` for a move. For archive and restore, read the column from the board that was read for the check. Or have `appendBoardEvent` return the folded board, so the verb does not need a second `readBoard`.

review.impact: `apply` runs only after `refusal` has confirmed the ticket exists, except for a plan. So the `ticket === undefined` guards in the moved, archived and restored cases can never be true. They are dead code, and they suggest that `apply` can be called without the check.
review.fix: Have `apply` take the ticket that `refusal` already looked up, or assert that the ticket exists once. Then remove the three guards for the moved, archived and restored cases.

review.impact: The shape `{ line: number; reason: string }` for an unreadable line is written out three times: `Board.unreadable`, the `foldBoard` parameter, and `BoardLog.unreadable` in log.ts. A change to the shape has to be made in all three places.
review.fix: Export one type, for example `type Unreadable = { line: number; reason: string }`, and use it in all three places.

review.impact: `refuseAgentMove` repeats the body of `refusePlan`: a missing ticket or an open column means allowed, and anything else returns a refusal sentence. Only the wording differs, so the 'open column' check exists twice.
review.fix: Add a small helper that takes the board, the id and the refusal text. Have both `refusePlan` and `refuseAgentMove` call it.

review.impact: `as never` turns off type checking for the ticket argument. If the ticket were missing, the test would still compile.
review.fix: Assert that the ticket exists, for example `const t = b.tickets.get("s/02"); expect(t).toBeDefined();`, and pass `t as Ticket`, or narrow it with an `if`.

review.impact: This header comment line is much longer than the other wrapped lines in the same comment. It does not match the formatting of the surrounding comments.
review.fix: Rewrap the line to the same width as the other lines of the comment.

review.impact: readBoardLog only sets aside lines that fail JSON.parse. A line that parses but is not an event object, such as `null` or `42` (which a bad merge can produce), is pushed as an event. foldBoard then throws a TypeError at `event.type` in fold.ts:90, so the whole board and every `werk ticket` call crash. This breaks the promise in the comment that one bad line must not hide the rest of the board. No test covers a line that is valid JSON but not an event, so this failure path is unguarded.
review.fix: In readBoardLog, put any parsed value that is not a plain object with a string `type` and a numeric `seq` into `unreadable` (for example, reason 'not an event'). Add a case to the log.test.ts unreadable test with lines `null` and `42`, and assert that the lines after them still fold.

review.impact: The fold checks only that `payload.id` is a string. A ticket.planned event without a `blocked_by` array is applied and stores `blocked_by: undefined`. Any later move of that ticket to building then crashes in openBlockers (`ticket.blocked_by.filter`) in rules.ts:31. That crash happens inside foldBoard and appendBoardEvent, so one malformed event breaks every later read. The 'names no ticket' test covers a missing id but not a malformed blocked_by, title or `to`.
review.fix: In `refusal`, check each payload's shape: `title` is a string and `blocked_by` is an array of strings for planned, and `to` is a known Column for moved. Set aside any event that fails with a reason. In fold.test.ts, add cases for a planned event with no blocked_by followed by a move to building, and for a move to an unknown column. Assert that both are set aside and that the fold does not throw.

review.impact: The whitespace-only `--reason " "` case asserts only exit code 2. Any other usage error, such as a parsing change that rejects the flag value, would also pass, so the test does not pin the blank-reason branch.
review.fix: Also assert that `err` starts with 'werk ticket: move needs --reason\n'.

review.impact: The next seq is the last line's seq + 1, not the highest seq + 1. If a merge interleaves two board logs, the next write can reuse an existing seq, and setAside entries that are keyed by seq become ambiguous. No test covers a log whose seqs are out of order.
review.fix: Use the highest seq in the log + 1. Add a log.test.ts case that writes lines with seq 1, 3, 2 and asserts that the next append gets seq 4.

review.impact: readBoardLog only checks that a line parses as JSON. A line that parses but is not an object, such as `null` (for example from a bad merge or a hand edit), is pushed as an event. foldBoard then reads `event.type` on it (fold.ts:90) and throws a TypeError. One bad line then breaks every `werk ticket` call and every read of the board, which defeats the stated aim that one bad line must not hide the rest of the board. A non-numeric `seq` on the last line also makes appendBoardEvent write `seq: NaN`, and JSON.stringify writes that as `null`.
review.fix: Check the shape of each parsed line before keeping it: it must be a non-null object with a numeric `seq`, a string `type` and an object `payload`. Otherwise push it to `unreadable` with a reason such as "not a board event". Work out the next seq from the largest numeric seq in the log, not from the `seq` of the last line.

review.impact: refusal() checks only that `payload.id` is a string. A `ticket.planned` event whose `blocked_by` is not an array is still applied. Later, `openBlockers` calls `ticket.blocked_by.filter` (rules.ts:30) and throws when anyone moves that ticket to building. A `ticket.moved` event whose `to` is not a column, or whose `reason` is not a string, is refused or applied without a clear reason.
review.fix: In refusal(), check each payload against its type: `title` is a string, `blocked_by` is an array of strings, `to` is one of the columns, and `reason` is a string or absent. Set the event aside with a reason when its payload does not match.

review.impact: One `werk ticket move` reads and folds the whole board log three times: `readBoard` for `refuseAgentMove` (line 46), `readBoardLog` with `foldBoard` inside `appendBoardEvent`, and `readBoard` again to print the column. Archive and restore read it twice. Each read parses every line of a log that only grows, so every command does two or three times the work it needs.
review.fix: Read and fold the log once per command. Let `appendBoardEvent` return the folded board after the event applies; `tryApply` already updates it in place. Better still, have it take an optional pre-check, so `refuseAgentMove` runs on the same board. Then print `ticket.column` from that board and drop both extra `readBoard` calls.

review.impact: Each append re-parses and re-folds the full log to get the next seq and check the rules. One write costs O(n) and n writes cost O(n²). That is fine at today's sizes, but the board log is append-only build churn and never gets compacted.
review.fix: For now, accept it and share one fold per command as described above. If the log grows large, cache the folded board together with the file size or mtime, then parse and fold only the bytes added since.

payload.error: a Agent call froze with no process of its own

grade.gap: Some behaviour goes past what the ticket asks for, but each piece supports a criterion or story: (1) src/verbs/plan.ts adds user-facing --timeout/--silence flags, and src/agent/limits.ts adds clampSeconds with a 900s cap. No criterion asks for configurable limits, so the fixed defaults could be kept inside the writer launch. (2) src/plan/run.ts and src/plan/board-plan.ts move tickets named by a failed set check (blocked_by) into the blocked column with a reason. Criterion 5 only asks that a ticket failing its own checks stays off the board. (3) The `werk target` verb (src/verbs/target.ts) checks for a main line and for nesting with the store. This is fair coverage of story 82. None of these breaks a card. Note: the grader could not run the tests because the sandbox denied it, so this score comes from reading the code only.

review.impact: `runPlan` writes `plan.started` before it launches any writer. If `runWriter` throws, the plan never writes `plan.ended`. That can happen when `Bun.spawn` cannot find the `claude` executable, when `mkdirSync` or `writeFileSync` on the agent log fails, or when `projectAgentArgs` throws while reading the map. The board log then shows a plan that runs forever, and the verb crashes with a stack trace instead of the `werk plan: ...` refusal.
review.fix: Wrap the writer steps and the checks after `plan.started` in a try/catch (or try/finally) that calls `end("failed", <message>)`. Or have `runWriter` catch spawn and file errors and return `{ ok: false, reason }`, matching the `WriterEnd` contract.

review.impact: The plan writer imports `AGENT_PROGRAM` from `src/serve/chat.ts`. This makes the plan stage depend on the server's chat module, which breaks the single-purpose module boundary (#werk-stack-modules). Every launcher already gets its arguments from `src/agent/launch.ts`, but the program name still lives in the server's code.
review.fix: Move `AGENT_PROGRAM` into `src/agent/` (for example `launch.ts` or a small `program.ts`). Import it there from both `serve/chat.ts` and `plan/writer.ts`.

review.impact: `boardEvent` returns an append failure, but the calls for `plan.started`, `plan.step` and `plan.ended` drop it. If the board log cannot be written, the plan's run state is lost and nothing reports it.
review.fix: Add the failures of the run events to `problems`, or write them to `io.err`, as the code already does for `ticket.planned` and `ticket.moved`.

review.impact: The target repository is a project-level setting. The `target` verb and the later build stages use it too (#st-build-target), so keeping it under `src/plan/` makes the build code import from the plan module.
review.fix: Move `target.ts` into its own project-level module, for example `src/project/target.ts` or `src/build/target.ts`, and import it from there in both the plan and target verbs.

review.impact: A blocker entry is turned into an id with `ticketId(root, Number(entry))` without checking it. A non-numeric entry gives `app/NaN`, and a missing number gives a dangling id. These bad ids go into the `ticket.planned` payload even when the set check has already flagged the ticket.
review.fix: Map only entries that parse to a known ticket number in the set, and drop the rest. Or leave `blocked_by` empty for a ticket that a failed `blocked_by` check names.

review.impact: `clampSeconds` returns `number | string`, so the caller has to narrow it in a loop and then cast with `as number`. That cast is not checked, and a later edit could break the narrowing without the compiler noticing.
review.fix: Narrow each limit directly (`if (typeof timeout === "string") ...`) before using it, or return a discriminated result `{ ok, seconds } | { ok: false, error }`.

review.impact: runPlan runs to about 130 lines. It mixes validation, scope, five closures (boardEvent, end, rel, writerStep, propose), two writer steps, reading the ticket folder, writing to the board and building the result reason, all in one function. That is hard to read and to test in parts, and it goes against the rule that modules are small and single-purpose (#werk-stack-modules). The verb test is the only way to exercise any part of it.
review.fix: Pull out named functions: a preflight that returns the node, target and scope or a refusal; a `proposeAnswers(file, root, log, io)` helper; a `readTicketFiles(dir)` helper; and a `recordBoardPlan(plan, boardEvent)` that returns its problems. runPlan then only puts the steps in order.

review.impact: The loop that decodes the stream into lines (TextDecoder, `rest += decode(chunk, {stream:true})`, split on newline, `pop()` the rest) copies the one in src/serve/chat.ts:131-136. A fix to one, such as the handling of the last partial line, will not reach the other.
review.fix: Add one shared helper, for example an async generator `lines(stream)` in src/agent/, and use it in both chat.ts and writer.ts.

review.impact: The reference-id pattern and its guard characters `[\w/#:&-]` are written out again here. They already exist in web/reflink.ts (ID_PATTERN, JOINS). If #werk-reflink-guard changes, the two copies can drift apart, and scope.ts would then read references differently from how the client links them.
review.fix: Move ID_PATTERN and the guard class into one pure module that both sides import. If client code must stay out of src, at least name the twin file in the comment so a change updates both.

review.impact: `event as TicketEvent` is cast twice after `FOLDED.has(event.type)`. FOLDED is typed `ReadonlySet<string>`, so the compiler cannot connect the check to the cast. If someone adds a ticket event type to TicketEvent but not to FOLDED, or the other way round, nothing flags it.
review.fix: Replace the casts with a type guard, `const isTicketEvent = (e: BoardEvent): e is TicketEvent => FOLDED.has(e.type)`, and build FOLDED from the same list of literals that defines TicketEvent.

review.impact: `(timeout as number)` and `(silence as number)` are casts that only exist because the loop over `[timeout, silence]` does not narrow the original variables. If the loop's check is ever changed, the casts will hide a string reaching the `* 1000`.
review.fix: Check each value directly, e.g. `if (typeof timeout === 'string' || typeof silence === 'string') { io.err(...); return USAGE_ERROR; }`, so TypeScript narrows both without casts.

review.impact: planFiles returns an inferred type with the same four keys as PlanPaths. facts.paths then maps each key through `rel` one at a time, so adding a path means editing three places in step.
review.fix: Annotate planFiles as returning `PlanPaths`, and build facts.paths with `Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(files).map(([k, v]) => [k, rel(v)])) as PlanPaths`, or with a small `relPaths(files, rel)` helper.

review.impact: WRITER_TOOLS and writerFlags are exported, but nothing outside writer.ts imports them. The extra exports widen the module's public surface for no use.
review.fix: Drop the `export` keyword from both, or have plan.test.ts assert against WRITER_TOOLS instead of the literal "Read,Grep,Glob,Write".

review.impact: No test checks that the silence clock starts only at the first event (#lp-overseer-silence-start). If runWriter armed the silence timer at spawn, a writer that pauses before its first event would be killed, and every test would still pass. The silence test also never checks the exit code, so a stopped writer that still exits 0 would go unnoticed.
review.fix: Add a test where the spec writer pauses longer than `--silence` before its first event, then writes the spec and exits. Assert that the plan does not fail with 'was silent'. In the existing silence test, also assert `run.code` is 1 and that the last board event has result 'failed'.

review.impact: No test checks that `stream_event` lines are kept out of the step's agent log, or that a trailing line with no newline is still written. If either filter broke, the log could fill with token deltas or lose its last line, and no test would fail.
review.fix: In the plan verb test, make the scripted writer emit a stream_event and end on a line with no newline. Assert that the agent log has no '"type":"stream_event"' line and does hold the final result line.

review.impact: The verb test never covers the path where the root is a decided card that is stale or postponed. In that case run.ts stops with '#<root> is not decided, or it is stale' and writes plan.ended 'stopped'. If that guard regressed, the plan could launch writers with an empty first tier.
review.fix: Add a verb test that reopens 'app' as invalidated. Assert exit 1, the exact stderr line, no launches, and board events of only plan.started then plan.ended with result 'stopped'.

review.impact: The test is named 'the target stays', but it only refuses paths while the project has no target. A refusal that wrote over or cleared an existing target would still pass.
review.fix: Set a valid target first, then try an invalid path. Assert that `werk target` still prints the original path.

review.impact: Each writer runs inside the project folder with the Write tool, and the acceptEdits mode lets it write anywhere in that folder. werk's store (`.werk/log.jsonl` and `.werk/board.jsonl`) sits in that folder, so a writer could append forged map events, such as a `node.decided` event signed as the person, or forged board events. The only thing stopping it is the line in the prompt that says 'Never write to the map yourself'. That gets around the rule that a writer's own answers enter the map only as ghost cards, and the plan never notices.
review.fix: Make the writer unable to reach the logs instead of relying on the prompt. One way: add `--disallowedTools` entries such as `Write(.werk/log.jsonl)` and `Write(.werk/board.jsonl)`, or scope Write to the spec, answers and ticket paths with path-scoped `--allowedTools` entries. Another way: run the writer in a folder that holds only its output files. Alternatively, check the size and checksum of the map and board logs before and after each writer step, and fail the plan if either changed.

review.impact: Map card ids can be any non-empty text, but `planFiles` puts the subtree id straight into store paths (`specs/${root}.md`, `tickets/${root}`, `plans/${root}/…`). If a decided card has an id containing `/` or `..`, `werk plan` would delete files outside werk's store with `rmSync(…, {force: true})`, create folders there, and write files there. An agent can propose a card id like that, and a person can accept it without noticing.
review.fix: Before building any path, reject a root that contains a path separator, `..` or other characters outside the slug set, for example `/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/`. Or check that each path `planFiles` resolves still lies inside the store.

review.impact: The loops that put tickets on the board call appendBoardEvent once for each planned and each blocked ticket. Every call reads, parses and folds the whole board.jsonl again, so one plan costs O(tickets × board log). The plan.* events this change adds make that log grow with every plan run, so the cost rises over time.
review.fix: Read and fold the board once. Then check each event with tryApply against that in-memory board and append the accepted lines in one write, or add a batch form of appendBoardEvent.

review.impact: propose calls readMap("plan", log) for each answer, which reads and folds the whole decision log every time. write() then reads the log again, so the map is folded once per answer even though it was already folded at the start of runPlan.
review.fix: Collect all of a writer's answer drafts and pass them to one write() call against one fresh readMap. Or keep the folded map and re-fold only after a write succeeds.

review.impact: dependsOn scans every link in the map each time it is called. planScope calls it for every scope card, and cardText calls it again for every card in the prompt text. That makes building the scope O(scope cards × links) when it could be close to linear.
review.fix: Build a Map from each card to its depends_on targets once per planScope/scopeText call, and look targets up there.

review.impact: Each stdout chunk is added to `rest`, and then the whole of `rest` is split again. When one long stream-json line, such as a big assistant or result message, arrives over many chunks, the same growing buffer is scanned once per chunk. The work is quadratic in the line's length.
review.fix: Look for a newline only in the new chunk (for example with indexOf), and split only when the chunk contains one. Otherwise just add the chunk to the buffer.

causeOfLast.why: pass 1 returned a value from a function typed `void`, which the lint rule refuses, and the cards had no bearing on it.

grade.gap: The diff makes several choices that none of the named cards gives. (1) Where the session id lives: #werk-resume says `.werk/session`, but the diff puts the session, model, advisor, used and window together in one JSON file beside the chat log, `.werk/chats/main.json` (settingsPath in src/serve/chat.ts), and never reads `.werk/session`. It also adds a `used`/`window` field shape (ChatSettings in src/serve/chat-model.ts). (2) New addresses: `GET /api/chat/settings` and `POST /api/clear` (src/serve/server.ts). The cards give only `POST /api/model` and a 'model' SSE event. (3) A new 'cleared' live-channel event (noticeFrame in src/serve/server.ts) and an HTTP 409 answer with an error message for a busy switch or clear. (4) The `/api/model` advisor value is the pinned id `claude-opus-5-5`, but #werk-model-select says 'opus'. (5) The pane reads the settings again after each turn ends. The server does not push the fill, so the ChatNotice type carries only switch and clear (web/chat-settings.tsx). The next pass should propose a card that records these, or move the session back to `.werk/session` to match #werk-resume.

causeOfLast.why: the earlier pass made decisions that no card gives (the settings file, the request shapes, the live events) and did not propose cards for them.

grade.gap: Two choices come from no named card. (1) The request addresses GET /api/chat/settings and POST /api/clear (src/serve/server.ts). #werk-model-select names only POST /api/model, and #werk-model-select-requests names no addresses. (2) A clear keeps the chat log on disk: the Chat.clear doc in src/serve/chat.ts says 'The chat log keeps every line', and the chat.test.ts test 'a clear drops the session and the fill, keeps the chat log...' checks it. But #werk-context-pie says a clear 'drops the stored session id and the chat transcript'. Propose a card that records the addresses and says whether a clear keeps or drops the chat log on disk.

src/serve/chat-model.ts parseSettings: when the saved model and advisor pair is one the selector does not offer, the code falls back to the default choice but keeps the saved `used`, the saved `window` and a non-empty `session`. The test in src/serve/chat-model.test.ts ('a missing, broken or unknown file...') expects `used: 5` to survive with model 'gpt'. The card says an unknown pair gives the default choice with an empty fill and no session. Fix: when choiceOf returns undefined, return defaultSettings(), and change the test to match.

The refused image is left out of `images`. The `[Image #2]` token still goes out in the text, with no path for it (web/composer.test.tsx: 'a refused image shows its reason on its chip and is not sent'). The criterion only asks that the image is not sent, so this passes.

Three things go beyond story 56, which asks only for a pasted screenshot. 1. Dropping an image onto the form also uploads it (web/composer.tsx onDrop/onDragOver). Remove it unless a #werk-shot-chip card asks for drop. 2. The chat answer now includes thumbnails of the sent images (src/serve/server.ts sentImagesHtml, web/index.css .shots), which no criterion asks for. 3. An empty upload gets its own 'the image is empty' refusal (src/serve/image-check.ts checkImage). This one is minor.

When an upload is over the cap, readUpload keeps the first chunk (`chunks.slice(0, 1)`). The card says the server keeps none of an oversized image. The order of checks, the name format and the refusal reasons all match the card. It would be cleaner to return an empty buffer when size > IMAGE_CAP (src/serve/attachments.ts readUpload).

review.impact: `send` now waits for running uploads (`await Promise.all(uploads.current.values())`) before it clears the draft. The old code cleared it at once, and that was what stopped a second send. Now a second Send click or Cmd+Enter during the wait passes the `draft.trim() === ""` check again, and the same message goes to the agent twice: two turns, and two charges. Text typed or images pasted during the wait are also wiped by `setDraft("")`/`setChips([])`, even though they were never sent (a pasted image's token goes out without its path).
review.fix: Add a sending ref, or state that disables Send. Set it before the await and clear it in a finally, and return early while it is set. Clear the draft and chips straight away, as before the change, and keep the snapshot taken after the await.

review.impact: `sentImagesHtml` builds its markup from the raw, unchecked `message.images` through a cast. It relies on a comment saying `messageImages` already checked the same value. It also puts `name` into the URL without encoding, while the client's `imageUrl` encodes it. If either function changes, the HTML can carry a name that was never checked, and the two copies of the image address can drift apart.
review.fix: Have `messageImages` return `{ n, name, path }`, and pass the checked list to `sentImagesHtml`. Build the src with `encodeURIComponent`, or with one shared image-URL helper.

review.impact: The HTML for a sent image is built inside the request handler, while the other HTML the server makes lives in its own modules (card-html.ts, home-html.ts). That puts presentation code in server.ts and keeps it out of the pure-file coverage check.
review.fix: Move `sentImagesHtml` into a small pure module, such as src/serve/sent-images-html.ts, with its own test, and add it to pure-files.txt.

review.impact: `imageFile` checks the file with stat, and then `readFileSync` reads it with no error handling. If the file goes away between the two calls, the request throws instead of answering 404.
review.fix: Wrap the read in try/catch and answer 404 on failure, or stream the file with `createReadStream` and handle its error.

review.impact: sentImagesHtml takes the raw, unchecked `message.images` and casts it to `{n, name}[]`, even though messageImages has already checked the same value. The handler checks the images in one place and renders them from another, so the safety of the HTML depends on a comment saying both see the same input. Any later change to messageImages, such as skipping or rewriting entries, would let unchecked names reach an `` without anyone noticing. It also builds the `/api/image?name=` URL by hand, a copy of web/composer.tsx `imageUrl` that skips the encodeURIComponent call.
review.fix: Have messageImages return the checked `{n, name, path}` entries, and pass that result to sentImagesHtml in place of `message.images`. Then remove the `unknown` parameter and the cast, and encode the name the same way imageUrl does.

review.impact: Closing the menu is written four times, and the copies disagree. pick (126) and Escape (208) increment `lookups.current` and then call setMenu(undefined). send (175) and onBlur (281) only call setMenu(undefined). When the box loses focus or a message is sent, a lookup that is still running can open the menu again. A future edit is likely to repeat this mismatch.
review.fix: Add one `closeMenu()` helper that increments `lookups.current` and calls setMenu(undefined). Use it in pick, Escape, send and onBlur.

review.impact: onPaste and onDrop have the same body: gather the image files, return when there are none or there is no upload, otherwise preventDefault and addImages. Only the event source differs.
review.fix: Move the shared body into one helper, for example `takeImages(event, source)`, and have both handlers call it.

review.impact: The `[Image #${n}]` token format is written by hand here, twice in server.ts:146, and once in web/image-tokens.ts `imageToken`. If the format changes in one place, the composer's tokens and the agent's header will no longer match.
review.fix: Import `imageToken` from web/image-tokens.ts on the server side, as server.ts already imports web/md.ts and web/routes.ts, and use it in all three places.

review.impact: When the upload is too big, `Buffer.concat(chunks.slice(0, 1))` keeps the first chunk and nothing else. Nothing explains why. storeImage refuses an oversized image based on `size` alone, so these bytes are never used.
review.fix: For an oversized upload, return an empty Uint8Array. Or add a comment saying the first chunk is kept on purpose.

review.impact: The test defines its own `SentImageList` type, which copies the `SentImage` type that composer.tsx exports. If the real type changes, the test type will drift away from it without any error.
review.fix: Import `type SentImage` from ./composer and use `SentImage[]` instead.

review.impact: `expect(existsSync(...) ? 1 : 0).toBe(0)` is a roundabout way to check a boolean, and its failure message is less clear than it could be.
review.fix: Use `expect(existsSync(join(w.dir, ".werk", "attachments"))).toBe(false)`.

review.impact: `let chipKeys = 0` is a mutable counter at module level, so every Composer instance and every test shares it. Nothing else in the component keeps state outside React.
review.fix: Keep the counter in a `useRef(0)` inside Composer.

review.impact: The test says a chat message 'refuses a name that is not stored', but the only bad name it sends is '../log.jsonl'. isAttachmentName rejects that name before the stored-file check runs. If messageImages skipped the stat of the file, a well-formed name with no file behind it (such as 'none.png') would pass, and the turn would send the agent a path that does not exist. This test would still pass.
review.fix: Add a request with images: [{ n: 1, name: 'none.png' }] and expect a 400. You could also assert the error text 'no stored image is named none.png'.

review.impact: The tests only paste images. No test drops one. onDrop reads dataTransfer.files, which is a FileList, while paste reads DataTransferItemList. That FileList branch of imagesOf and the onDragOver preventDefault are never run, so if dropping broke, no test would catch it.
review.fix: Add a composer test that calls fireEvent.drop on the form with dataTransfer: { files: [new File([...], 'a.png', { type: 'image/png' })] }. Assert that the [Image #1] token is in the box and that an uploading chip appears.

review.impact: Some menu behaviour has no test: Escape closing the menu, a lookup answer that arrives after a newer lookup being dropped, and a bare '#' with an empty query opening no card menu. A regression in any of these, such as a slow card search reopening a menu the person already moved past, would pass the suite.
review.fix: Add a test for each: Escape removes the listbox. A cards() promise settled after a newer edit does not show its entries. Typing '#' alone shows no listbox.

review.impact: The image read sets its content-type from the file name's extension, but it sends no `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. The upload checks only the first bytes, so a file can start with a real PNG signature and carry HTML or script after it. The response does nothing to stop a browser from sniffing that file as another type. Current browsers do not sniff image/png as HTML, so the risk is small. Still, the server should state the rule itself and not rely on how a browser behaves.
review.fix: Add `"x-content-type-options": "nosniff"` to the headers in `res.writeHead(200, ...)`. Optionally add `"content-security-policy": "default-src 'none'"` as well, so a stored attachment can never run as active content.

review.impact: Every keystroke in a word that starts with # sends a request to /api/search, and nothing debounces it. Each request reruns readMap on the server, which reads and folds the whole map log, then runs jumpSearch on the result. Typing a card id therefore folds the full log about once per character, and on a large map this adds server load and slows the menu. The lookup counter throws away stale answers, but the server still does the work for each one.
review.fix: Debounce the card lookup in lookUp by about 100–150 ms so that only the last keystroke in a burst sends a request. Also consider caching the folded map on the server between log writes, or reusing the map that knownIds() already keeps.

review.impact: Every keystroke in a word that starts with / fetches /api/commands again. The command list only changes when the agent restarts, so most of these round trips are wasted.
review.fix: Fetch the commands once when the menu opens, or cache them for the life of the composer, and run matchCommands on the cached list for each keystroke.

review.impact: The image GET handler loads the stored image with readFileSync, and an image can be up to 20 MB. That blocks the event loop, which stalls the chat's live channel and every other request while the file is read. Each thumbnail and each sent image triggers this read.
review.fix: Stream the file to the response with createReadStream(file.path).pipe(res), or read it asynchronously, and set content-length from statSync.

review.impact: When an upload is over the cap, readUpload drops the extra bytes but keeps reading until the body ends, so a client can keep the request open and streaming with no limit. Only a client holding the token can do this, so the risk is low.
review.fix: Once size passes IMAGE_CAP, stop reading: answer 422, then call req.destroy() or req.resume() and drop the rest, and still count the bytes if the size has to appear in the error message.

causeOfLast.why: #werk-context-pie says a clear drops "the chat transcript", but no card said if that means the log file on disk, and no card named the addresses. The unknown-pair finding was a builder error, because #werk-model-persist-file was clear on that point.

pass_end.decision: the grader raised #unrecorded-decision in two passes in a row

grade.gap: Minor, but it passes. web/chat-pane.tsx adds a refusal alert line (role=alert) between the chat log and the chat header row. That puts a new row into the pane order that #werk-head-bottom sets out, and no named card gives it. The model switch and clear requests also pick specific status codes: 400 for a model and advisor pair the selector does not offer, and 409 for a conflict. If a card should record these choices, the next pass can propose one.

review.impact: chat-stream.ts now reads the error text of an `is_error` result into `end.error`, and chat.ts passes it through in the `end` ChatEvent. But `chatFrame` builds the "ended" frame from only durationMs and costUsd, and the web `End` type has no error field for a turn that finished. So when a turn ends with an error result after the agent wrote something (a rate limit, max turns, an API error), the pane shows the normal "Ns · $x" line and the error is silently dropped. That defeats the whole-error path (#werk-fullerr) that this change adds for exits.
review.fix: Add `error: event.error` to the "ended" frame in `chatFrame`. Widen `End` in web/chat-thread.ts so a finished turn can carry an optional `error`, read it in `threadEvent`, and render `ErrorView` for any `turn.end.error`, not only for an exit.

review.impact: The server helper `idle(res, change, chat)` has the same name as the `idle(what)` guard in chat.ts, but it does something else: it answers an HTTP request. Its parameter order (response, thunk, chat) is also unusual. A reader of either file can mistake one for the other.
review.fix: Rename it to describe what it does, e.g. `answerSettingsChange(res, chat, change)`, and put `chat` before the thunk.

review.impact: `report` creates a synthetic `agent-N` turn whenever a child exits with an error while no turn is open. A plain idle exit that writes something to stderr (for example a warning on shutdown) then shows the person an error turn they never asked for, with no message above it.
review.fix: Create the synthetic turn only when the plan is not "ended" or the exit code is nonzero. Otherwise log the idle error output without opening a turn.

review.impact: The colours for proto, open and stale (#0ea5e9, #f59e0b, #dc2626) are copied from the `DOT` map in web/jump-box.tsx:16. If someone changes a status colour in one file, the pie and the jump box will no longer match, even though the file's comment says the pie uses the card status colours.
review.fix: Move the status colours into one shared module, such as a small `web/status-colors.ts`, and import it in both jump-box.tsx and context-pie.ts.

review.impact: The dead-session branch removes the session inline with `const { session: _, ...rest } = settings`, which repeats the destructuring in `view` at line 109. That makes two places that know how to drop the session from settings.
review.fix: Add a pure `withoutSession(settings)` helper to chat-model.ts, next to `clearSettings`, so it is tested there, and use it in both places. Or build `view` on top of that helper.

review.impact: No test covers the case where the one retry succeeds. The retry test scripts both launches to crash, so it only shows the give-up branch. Nothing fails if the retried child gets the message but its reply never reaches the waiting turn: for example, if `run.inFlight` is not moved over, a `started`/`exited` event is sent twice, or an `exited` event is sent after the retry answers.
review.fix: Add a test with a stored session that crashes with stderr on the first launch only. Use a marker file in the fake, or switch the script before the second launch. Assert two launches, both with `--resume s-1`, that the turn ends with `end` and no `exited` event, and that the reply block is delivered under `t1`.

review.impact: Since this change, the second child of this existing test starts with `--resume s-1`, because the session is now saved. The fake still reports a new session `s-2`, which real Claude Code would not do on a resume. The test still passes, but it now relies on behaviour that cannot happen and checks nothing about resume.
review.fix: Either clear the settings file before the second send, or assert `--resume s-1` on the second launch and script it to report `s-1`, so the test matches the new resume behaviour.

review.impact: `windowOf` is only tested where the exact key is missing and it falls back to the bare model name. If the code stopped preferring an exact `claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]` entry over the bare one, no test would fail.
review.fix: Add `expect(windowOf({ [SONNET]: 1_000_000, "claude-sonnet-5-5": 200_000 }, SONNET)).toBe(1_000_000)`.

review.impact: The selector and the clear are only tested as disabled while a turn runs. Nothing checks that they are also disabled while a message waits (`thread.some(isWaiting)`), so dropping that half of the `busy` condition would pass.
review.fix: Send a message through the composer without a `started` event and assert that the Model select is disabled.

review.impact: The clear test checks only the path of the first change. It does not check that the token was sent, and it never asserts that the thread had a turn before `cleared`. A token bug on clear, or a delta that never rendered, would go unnoticed.
review.fix: Assert `changes[0]` equals `{ path: "/api/clear", body: {}, token: "tok" }`, and assert that the thread has one child before emitting `cleared`.

review.impact: parseSettings checks model and advisor against the selector's allowlist, but it accepts any non-empty string as the session. chatFlags then passes that string to the agent as the value of --resume. The settings file sits in .werk/chats/ next to the chat log, which can be committed and shared, so a cloned project could supply any value there. Bun.spawn uses an argv array, so this cannot inject shell commands. At worst it gives a confusing resume failure, or an argument that looks like a flag if the CLI parser ever treats a dash-prefixed value differently.
review.fix: Accept a session only if it matches the id format Claude Code reports, for example /^[0-9a-f-]{8,64}$/i. Otherwise drop it, the same way an unknown model pair falls back to the default. Add a test case for a session that starts with '-'.

review.impact: `read` now pipes the chat child's stderr and buffers all of it with `new Response(proc.stderr).text()`. Nothing reads that buffer until the child exits. One chat child stays alive for the whole conversation, across many turns, so any warnings or debug lines it writes to stderr pile up in the server's memory with no limit. It all becomes one string, then gets joined, trimmed and sent to every open page when the child exits.
review.fix: Read stderr as a stream into a bounded buffer. Keep only the last N bytes (for example 64 KB) or the last N lines, and drop the older chunks as new ones arrive. Pass that tail to `exitPlan` and `errorText`. The missing-session text and the fatal-error patterns appear at the end of the output, so the exit plan still finds them.

causeOfLast.why: another ticket that merged first added its own entries at the end of `pure-files.txt`, the same place this ticket added its entries.

grade.gap: Borderline items: dropping an image onto the composer (web/composer.tsx onDrop/onDragOver), where story 56 and the criteria ask only for a paste; Tab as a second key to pick and Escape to close the menu (web/composer.tsx onKey); and the closing of the menu on blur. The code comments put drop under #werk-shot-chip, which the story names. If that card does not cover drop, remove it.

The builder named only #werk-test-pure-list and #werk-test-pure-list-union, but the diff makes choices that neither card gives. (1) The addresses: POST and GET /api/image?name=<name> to upload and serve an image, and GET /api/commands for the slash commands (src/serve/server.ts). (2) The status 422 with {error} for a refused image, and 400 for a chat message with a bad images list. (3) The data shape of a chat message: images: [{n, name}], with the server turning each name into a path (server.ts messageImages). (4) The turn header the agent reads: '[Image #N] = <path>' lines, then the line 'Open each image above with Read before you answer.' (src/serve/open-card.ts turnMessage, OPEN_IMAGES). (5) The attachments folder at .werk/attachments beside the map log, with a .gitignore of '*' (src/serve/attachments.ts). (6) The rule for a valid stored name, isAttachmentName (src/serve/image-check.ts). (7) The sent images that the chat answer carries as HTML with data-role=sent-image (server.ts sentImagesHtml). (8) The send waits for every running upload and leaves out refused chips (web/composer.tsx send). (9) A backtick right before / or # opens no menu, and a word with a second trigger opens nothing (web/composer-menu.ts triggerAt). The next pass should name the cards these come from (for example #werk-chat-image-inline, #werk-shot-chip, #werk-shots, #werk-hash-trigger, #werk-chat-cmdmenu, #werk-crash) or propose a card for each.

The card says the server drops the bytes past the cap so that an oversized image costs no memory. src/serve/attachments.ts readUpload still holds up to the full 20 MB in chunks before it learns that the body is over the cap. This matches the card's wording about bytes past the cap, so the line passes, but the builder could drop the kept chunks as soon as the size goes over the cap.

causeOfLast.why: main added its own pure-file entries at the same end of `pure-files.txt` after this ticket was built.

grade.gap: The general path works: the session is kept, the agent retries once, then NOT_DELIVERED is shown (src/serve/chat.test.ts 'any other early exit keeps the session, retries once…'). But src/serve/crash.ts adds a 'fatal' plan. When the error matches FATAL (login problems, credential, unknown option, bad argument), the agent does not retry and shows FIX_FIRST instead. For those errors the criterion is not met. Either remove the fatal path, or point to the card that asks for it.

Stderr is now piped, and its whole text plus the text of the error result reaches the pane (server.test 'an exit carries the whole error'; chat-pane.test 'an exit shows every line'). Lines after the sixth are folded behind a <details> in web/chat-pane.tsx ErrorView. They are still in the DOM, so the criterion passes, but they are not visible until the person opens the fold.

src/serve/crash.ts FATAL / isFatal / FIX_FIRST: the agent skips the retry for login, credential and bad-flag errors and shows 'Fix the problem above, then send it again.' No acceptance criterion asks for this, and criterion-3 says another error retries once. Keep it only if #werk-crashmsg asks for it; otherwise remove it. The six-line fold in ErrorView (web/chat-thread.ts ERROR_LINES, foldError) is also not asked for by any criterion.

The builder named only #werk-test-pure-list and #werk-test-pure-list-union. The diff makes these choices that neither card gives, so each needs a card or a pointer to an existing one: (1) src/serve/crash.ts classifies some errors as fatal (FATAL regex list), skips the retry for them and shows a separate FIX_FIRST notice. (2) src/serve/crash.ts detects a dead session by matching the stderr text 'No conversation found with session ID'. (3) src/serve/chat.ts treats an error result that comes before any session or part as an early exit and replays the message, not as a finished turn. (4) src/serve/chat-model.ts: the window before a turn reports one is 1,000,000 for a '[1m]' model and 200,000 otherwise; a switch keeps the used tokens but resets the window to the new model's default. (5) src/serve/chat-stream.ts: used = input + output + cache_read + cache_creation tokens of the latest assistant message, and the window comes only from the conversation's own model in result.modelUsage. (6) src/serve/server.ts: a pair the selector does not offer gets 400; a busy switch or clear gets 409 with ChatBusy. (7) web/context-pie.ts: the pie is blue below 33%, yellow from 33% and red from 66%, and the clear action sits in a popover that opens from the pie. (8) web/chat-thread.ts: the error folds after 6 lines. (9) web/chat-settings.tsx: the client disables the controls while a message waits, not only while a turn runs.

causeOfLast.why: pass 1 left a test line that Biome's formatter rejects, and `make fix` corrects it with no ambiguity in the ticket or cards.

grade.gap: Reporting cards-cited failures (src/tickets/watch.ts uncitedFailures, src/tickets/watch-run.ts failures, and the plan.test.ts test 'a decided card added under a planned subtree reports a cards-cited failure') is not requested by any criterion or by stories 80 or 81. The decided card #st-ticket-watch-server does ask for it, so this passes. Keep it only if that card is in this ticket's scope.

src/serve/project.ts watchCitedCards breaks the card's rule that 'a failure line is written again only when the set of failures changes'. When a run moves any ticket to blocked (run.blocked.length > 0), the function writes all lines, and that includes every cards-cited failure line, even when the failures equal reported.text. Fix: always write the blocked lines, and add the failure lines only when the failures differ from reported.text. No test covers the server's stderr output, either at start or on log growth. Add one that runs openProject (or the server) on a project where a cited card was retitled before start. It should check the single 'moved to blocked' line, and check that a later note writes nothing.

causeOfLast.why: #st-ticket-watch-server says that a failure line is written again only when the set of failures changes, but the earlier code wrote every failure line each time a run blocked a ticket.

review.impact: When appendBoardEvent refuses a move to blocked, the `.filter(... .ok)` drops it and throws away its `error`. The ticket stays in ready even though a card it cites has changed. Nothing is reported, and every later run of the watch retries the same refused move without a word. That works against the server's rule of writing one line per failure.
review.fix: Collect each refused append as `{ id, error }` and return it in WatchRun, as a `refused` field or as extra lines in `failures`. watchCitedCards in src/serve/project.ts then writes it to stderr like the other failure lines.

review.impact: boardPlan works out `cleared` from a board it read earlier. The server's watch can append a move to blocked between that read and the plan's own appends. That move uses the old cites, and since the watch only ever blocks, the ticket stays in blocked with an out-of-date reason until the next plan.
review.fix: Work out the moves to ready after the planned events are written, by checking `after` for blocked tickets that the plan rewrote. Or have the watch also move a ticket back out of blocked when `watchReason` is undefined and the ticket's reason is a watch reason.

review.impact: The rule for 'open ticket' is now written out in three places that already differ: `isOpen` here (does not check archived), `isWatched` in src/tickets/watch.ts:16 (checks archived), and the inline column filter in src/plan/run.ts:115. The parsing of `<subtree>/NN` ids is also repeated in subtreeTickets, subtreeOf and run.ts `number`. The copies will drift apart when the columns change.
review.fix: Export one `isOpen(ticket)` predicate and one id split (subtree and number) from a single module, such as src/board/fold.ts or src/tickets/watch.ts, and use them in board-plan.ts, watch.ts and run.ts.

review.impact: This adds another hard-coded `board.jsonl` path beside the decision log, which ties the watch to where the board file lives instead of using the board module's own path logic (src/board/log.ts:11).
review.fix: Export a `boardPathBeside(log)` helper from src/board/log.ts and use it here and in src/plan/run.ts.

review.impact: The rule for an open ticket (column ready or blocked) is written three times. It appears as `isOpen` here, as `isWatched` in src/tickets/watch.ts:17 (which also checks `!archived`), and as an inline negated filter in src/plan/run.ts:116. The plan, the watch and the prompt's closed list must agree on which tickets are open, and a change to the columns could update one copy and miss the others.
review.fix: Export one `isOpen(ticket)` predicate, for example from src/board/fold.ts or src/tickets/watch.ts. Use it in board-plan.ts and in run.ts (as `!isOpen`). Define `isWatched` as `isOpen(ticket) && !ticket.archived`.

review.impact: Here `number` strips the subtree prefix from a ticket id with `id.slice(root.length + 1)`. `subtreeTickets` in board-plan.ts repeats the same slicing to compute `highest`, so the id format `<subtree>/NN` is parsed in two places beside `ticketId` and `subtreeOf`.
review.fix: Add a `ticketNumberOf(root, id)` (or similar) next to `ticketId` in board-plan.ts and use it in both places.

review.impact: `ownChecks` parses each ticket file once in the delivers loop (line 77) and again in the planned loop (line 99). run.ts:168 parses each file a third time to collect the cited cards. `checkTickets` probably parses them as well. The repeated parsing makes the flow harder to follow and the steps easy to let drift apart.
review.fix: Parse each file's fields once at the top of `boardPlan`, in a map from file to fields, and reuse that map in both loops. Alternatively, have run.ts pass the cited cards it already computed.

review.impact: The `Line` type and the `card`, `decided`, `logOf` and `BASE` helpers are copied word for word from src/tickets/history.test.ts. The `board(...)` and `planned` helpers are copied again in src/plan/board-plan.test.ts. A change to the log or board event shape has to be made in every copy.
review.fix: Move the shared log and board fixture builders into a test helper module under src/test/ and import them from each test.

review.impact: There are two separate import statements from "./history.ts" (a type import and a value import), which is inconsistent with the inline `type` imports used elsewhere in the diff.
review.fix: Merge them into `import { type CardChange, changesSince } from "./history.ts";`.

review.impact: A depends_on change only counts when the event type is in LINK_EVENTS. For every other event the snapshot reuses the old link set. The test covers only edge.added and edge.removed. Nothing tests a link that arrives through change.accepted, or one that goes away through change.discarded, node.removed or node.restored. If an entry is missing from this list or goes stale, the watch silently stops blocking tickets on link changes, and no test fails.
review.fix: Add a history test with a proposed depends_on edge that is then accepted (expect 'depends_on added'), and one where the target card is removed and restored (expect 'depends_on removed' then 'depends_on added'). Assert the exact kinds and positions.

review.impact: The `cleared` filter has two exclusions that no test runs: a ticket that a set check of this plan blocks again, and an archived blocked ticket. If either exclusion broke, the plan would send a ticket to ready while also blocking it, or move an archived ticket. No assertion would catch either.
review.fix: In board-plan.test.ts, plan a ticket that was blocked before and that a failing set check names again. Assert that `cleared` is empty and `blocked` holds it. Also add a blocked and archived ticket and assert it is not cleared.

review.impact: Nothing tests the catch branch, which keeps the server alive when the watch throws (#werk-crash). If someone removed the try/catch, a bad board or log would crash the server and the suite would still pass.
review.fix: Add a test that calls openProject on a log whose board file makes watchTickets throw, for example a board path that is a directory. Assert that openProject returns and that the line 'the watch of the cited cards failed' is written to stderr.

review.impact: The server test polls fs.watch frames for up to about 2s. Under the parallel worker load (#werk-test-runner-parallel), a late or merged watch event can make `frames.length` differ from the expected count, so the test can fail intermittently. The written.length check also runs only after the frame arrives, so if the frame comes late, the test does not show that the watch ran with no output for the note.
review.fix: Assert frames.length >= count rather than an exact count. Wait for the watch run itself rather than the SSE frame, for example by checking that the board file was written or by polling for a written-stderr condition, and allow a longer limit within the per-test timeout.

review.impact: No test archives a ticket without a reason after an earlier archive and restore with one. The `reason !== undefined` guard plus the delete on restore decide whether a stale archiveReason survives, and no assertion covers that order.
review.fix: Extend the archive test: archive with a reason, restore, then archive without a reason. Assert that archiveReason is undefined.

review.impact: The server calls `watchTickets` every time the decision log grows (src/serve/project.ts:58). Each call reads and re-folds the whole log twice: once in `cardHistory`, and again in `readMap` in watch-run.ts. Inside `cardHistory`, every event snapshots every watched card. `node.added` is in LINK_EVENTS and is one of the most common events, so on those events each card also runs `dependsOn`, which scans every link in `map.links`. One growth therefore costs about O(events × cited cards × links). All of this runs synchronously in the `fs.watch` callback, which blocks the server's event loop. As the log and the cited-card set grow, every map write stalls request handling and gets slower each time.
review.fix: Keep the work incremental across runs. Store the folded map, the byte offset already read and the last snapshots in the project context, then fold and diff only the lines that were appended. Pass that folded map to `uncitedFailures` instead of calling `readMap` again. So the chip still reads as "uploading" and is left out: the text carries `[Image #1]`, the agent gets no path for it, and the chips are then cleared. review.impact: Composer grew from about 55 lines to about 320, and it now does four jobs in one component: keeping the draft, looking up the slash-command and card menus (with stale-lookup numbering), uploading images (an upload map, a chips ref that mirrors state, the module-level chipKeys counter), and moving the caret. Under #werk-stack-modules, independent tickets should touch different modules. As it stands, any later change to the menus or to images edits the same large function, and the refs that copy state (current, chipsNow) make it hard to follow which value is current.
review.fix: Move the menu logic (menu state, lookups, lookUp, pick, the arrow/Enter/Escape handling) into a useComposerMenu hook in its own file. review.impact: sentImagesHtml casts the raw request value to {n, name}[] without checking it, and leans on a comment saying messageImages already checked it. review.impact: When the upload is over the cap, `Buffer.concat(chunks.slice(0, 1))` keeps only the first chunk, but `chunks` already holds only the chunks that fit under the cap. review.impact: The refusal message hard-codes '20 MB' next to IMAGE_CAP. If the cap changes, the message stays wrong.

review.impact: The steps for closing the menu (`lookups.current += 1; setMenu(undefined)`) are written out in pick and in the Escape handler. onBlur and send call setMenu(undefined) without bumping the lookup number, so a lookup that is still in flight can reopen the menu after a blur or a send.

review.impact: onPaste and onDrop have the same body except for their data source. That is duplicated guard logic to keep in step.

review.impact: send() waits for the uploads, then reads chipsNow.current. That ref only updates on a render, and settle() only queues a setChips call. In a real browser the Promise.all continuation runs as a microtask before React renders, so it sees the chip as still 'uploading' and drops it. The message goes out with '[Image #1]' in its text but no image entry. The unit test 'a send waits for a running upload' (web/composer.test.tsx:149) passes only because settle() runs inside act(), which flushes the render synchronously. No e2e test sends during an upload: the e2e test waits for the thumbnail before it clicks Send. So the bug can ship while every test passes.
review.fix: In settle(), update chipsNow.current at the same time as the state (compute the next array, assign it to the ref, then call setChips with it), the way addImages already does. Or build the images from the upload results directly. Add an e2e case that clicks Send while an upload is still running (for example, route /api/image through a delayed page.route) and checks that the fake agent got '[Image #1] = <path>'.

review.impact: Two chip edge cases have no test. First, removing a chip while it is still uploading: its promise stays in uploads, so the send still waits for it, and settle() runs against a key that is gone. Second, a refused send with images: the draft comes back but the chips stay. Either path could regress without a failing test.
review.fix: Add a test that pastes an image, removes its chip before calling settle, sends, and checks the sent text and that images is empty. Add a test where onSend returns an error with a stored chip, and check that the words and the chip both stay for a retry.

review.impact: The chat-message refusal is tested only with a traversal name ('../log.jsonl'). Nothing tests a well-formed name that is not stored (for example 'none.png'), so the existence check in messageImages has no test of its own.

review.impact: readUpload keeps reading an upload to its very end, even after the 20 MB cap has passed. It drops the extra bytes, so memory stays bounded, but the server still spends time and network reading them. One request that carries the token can stream gigabytes, or trickle bytes slowly, and hold the handler open with no limit. The route is reachable only on loopback and only with the token, so the exposure is small.
review.fix: Answer 413 at once when the Content-Length header is over IMAGE_CAP. Otherwise stop reading once the count passes the cap: answer 422 with the size refusal and call req.destroy(), or set a request timeout. If the page must still show the size in its refusal, report the size as 'over 20 MB' instead of reading the whole body to count it.

review.impact: Each image read loads the whole file, up to 20 MB, with readFileSync. This blocks the server's single event loop, including the live channel, chat streaming and every other request, until the read finishes. The composer and every sent message in the thread request these images, so a thread with several large screenshots stalls the server again and again.
review.fix: Stream the file with createReadStream(file.path).pipe(res), and set content-length from the statSync that imageFile already does, instead of res.end(readFileSync(...)).

review.impact: An oversized upload is read to its very end before it is refused. A 25 MB paste, or a much larger dropped file, still crosses the wire and the server counts every byte, so the person waits for the full transfer just to see the refusal.
review.fix: Refuse early. If the content-length header is over IMAGE_CAP, answer 422 with the size before reading the body. Better still, check file.size in the composer's upload() and give the refusal without sending, so the server check only guards against a lying client.

review.impact: Every keystroke inside a / or # word sends a new request with no debounce: /api/search for cards, or /api/commands for slash commands. The command list changes only when the agent starts, yet the composer fetches it again on every character. Answers that arrive late are dropped, but the requests and the server's work still happen.
review.fix: Fetch the command list once when a / menu opens and cache it, refreshing it on the next open or after a turn starts. Debounce the card search by about 100 ms.

review.impact: chat-stream.ts now puts `error` on an `end` part when a result has is_error. chat.ts passes that part through to deliver() once the child has written something, but chatFrame's "end" case still sends only durationMs and costUsd. review.impact: An error result that comes before the child has written anything is held back and does not end the turn, on the assumption that the child will exit and the exit plan will replay the message. The turn then stays open forever, and setModel and clear keep throwing ChatBusy, so the conversation is stuck until the server restarts.

review.impact: If a child is killed by a signal (code null) after it has written part of a reply and leaves no stderr, `failed` is false. review.impact: The `stopping` set never affects what happens. `stop()` already sets `current = undefined` before it kills the child, so in `read()` the check `current !== run` is already true for every child that was stopped on purpose, and `stopping.delete(proc) ||` adds nothing. review.impact: The proto, open and stale hex colours are copied from the status colour map in `web/jump-box.tsx:18-20`. If a status colour changes in one place, the pie and the search list will no longer match.

review.impact: The tests only cover an error result that comes before the agent writes anything. Nothing tests an `is_error` result that arrives after the agent has written part of a turn. The pane never sees that error, which breaks #werk-fullerr, and no test fails.

Assert that the delivered `end` event has `error: "boom"`. In server.test.ts, assert that the `turn` frame carries the error. Then make `chatFrame` pass `event.error` through so the new test passes.

review.impact: `toContain("Opus")` also matches the default label "Sonnet + Opus advisor". This `waitFor` passes even if the select never moves to the Opus choice, so it does not check that the selector follows the server's answer.
review.fix: Assert the exact choice: `expect(select.value).toBe("claude-opus-5-5|")` or `expect(select.selectedOptions[0]?.textContent).toBe("Opus")`.

review.impact: The retry tests only cover a retry that fails again, which ends in give-up. Nothing checks that a successful retry delivers the waiting message once and logs no duplicate lines. Nothing checks that its turn ends normally without an `exited` event either. A bug in how a retry hands over the waiting messages or the held lines could go unnoticed.
review.fix: Add a test whose first launch crashes early and whose second launch answers. For example, change `project.script` once the first pid is gone, or give the fake a reply for each launch. Assert two launches, one `end` and no `exited` event for the turn. Also assert that each chat-log line appears once, under the second child's session.

review.impact: The code accepts any non-empty string from the saved settings file (.werk/chats/main.json, which sits inside the project folder and may come from a shared or cloned repository) as the session. chatFlags (src/serve/chat.ts:100) then passes it to the agent as the value of `--resume`. A value that starts with `-`, such as `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, would probably be read as a separate flag, because Claude Code's `--resume` value is optional. That would let a crafted file loosen the chat agent's permission mode or add other flags.
review.fix: Accept only a session id in the form Claude Code issues. Check it against a UUID-style pattern such as /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i, or at least /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/ that does not start with '-'. Drop any other value in parseSettings, and do the same for the session read from the stream before it is saved. You can also pass it as `--resume=<id>` so it can never be read as a separate flag.

review.impact: The agent's whole stderr now goes to every open live channel, with no filtering. Login and credential errors (exactly the cases that crash.ts marks as fatal) can include parts of tokens, file paths or environment details, and every page that is connected sees them.
review.fix: Before the error output is broadcast, mask anything that looks like a key or token (for example, sk-ant-… or Bearer …), or confirm that the live channel requires the server token.

review.impact: The chat child now has `stderr: "pipe"`, and `new Response(proc.stderr).text()` holds everything it writes to stderr in memory until it exits. The chat child lives as long as the conversation, often hours across many turns, so warnings and debug output pile up without limit. The text is only used if the child exits, and then the whole of it goes into one `exited` event to every open page and into the `<pre>` in the pane, even though only the recent part says what went wrong.
review.fix: Read stderr as a stream into a bounded buffer: keep a tail of about 64 KB or a few hundred lines and drop the oldest data, or reset the buffer when a turn ends cleanly so only the output since the last finished turn is kept. Build `whole` from that buffer. If the start is cut off, put a marker like `[earlier output truncated]` at the top.
