review.impact: `answer()` removes the ask from `open` and writes the response to the child before it writes allow.json and appends to asks.jsonl. If either file write throws (disk full, permissions), the agent already has its answer but `notify({kind: "answered"})` never runs. The server returns a 500, every page keeps showing an ask that is closed, and a retry gets a 409. In the Always case the rule also never reaches allow.json, so later children start without it.
review.fix: Make the disk writes unable to strand the ask. Either put the allow-file and ask-log writes in a try/finally so `notify({kind: "answered", id})` always runs after `open.delete`, or do the persistence before writing to the child and deleting from `open`.

review.impact: Pages can get stuck showing a closed ask. The mount-time GET /api/chat/asks can resolve after an `ask-answered` event for the same id has already arrived, which puts the closed ask back in the list. The bar treats any refused answer as retryable: it shows the error and enables the buttons again, so a 409 for an ask that is no longer open leaves it on screen until reload. The same thing happens after a lost `ask-answered` frame.
review.fix: Have the answer callback tell a 409 (ask not open) apart from other errors, and on a 409 drop the ask from `asks` instead of showing a retryable error. Optionally, also ignore GET results for ids already seen as answered.

review.impact: An id in `answered` (tool_use_ids of answered questions) is removed only when its tool_result arrives. If the child exits or is stopped before that, the id stays for the life of the chat. `dropAsks` cleans up `open` but not `answered`, so the two collections drift apart.
review.fix: Store the run with each answered tool_use_id, or clear the entries belonging to a run in `dropAsks`/on exit, so `answered` has the same lifetime as `open`.

review.impact: The `sent` set only gets ids added on success and never removes them once the ask leaves `asks`. It grows for the life of the pane and duplicates state the parent already owns.
review.fix: Remove the id from `sent` (and from `errors`) once the ask is no longer in `asks`, or derive both from the current `asks` list.

review.impact: `answer()` has a five-way branch that is pure logic: it checks whether the decision is valid for the ask, then picks allow, always, answer, decline or deny and the message for each. That logic sits in the impure chat module, so it is outside the 90% pure-file gate (#werk-test-gate-list), and the next decision kind will make this closure longer. Line 437 also makes `answered.add` depend on `toolUseId` without saying why.
review.fix: Add a pure `responseFor(ask, decision, picks)` to asks.ts. It should return the line to write, or throw or return the reason for a refusal. Test it in asks.test.ts. Then `answer()` in chat.ts only checks the ask is open, writes the line, updates the allow file, appends to the log and sends the notice.

review.impact: The keyboard handler repeats the question-submit path. It reads the form back from storage with `readForm`/`formKey`, then runs `hasPick`/`picksOf`, which is the same work as `QuestionAsk`'s `onSubmit` at line 418. If the submit rule changes, both places must change together.
review.fix: Put the decision in one helper in ask-form.ts, such as `submission(state): string[][] | undefined`, and call it from both places. Or have Cmd+Enter call `requestSubmit()` on the first ask's form.

review.impact: `[...ask.rules, ...ask.dirs]` appears in both `askView` (line 144) and `askLogLine`, so the rule for what an Always allow widens is written twice.
review.fix: Add a `widenedOf(ask)` helper and use it in both functions.

review.impact: The ask step's shape `{ id?; tool; input; reason?; suggestions? }` is written out inline twice, once in the `Step` union and once for `parsed`, so the two can drift apart.
review.fix: Name it once, e.g. `type AskStep = Extract<Step, { ask: unknown }>["ask"]`, and use that type for `parsed` and for `askEvent`'s `extra` parameter.

review.impact: The `as never` cast on the expected value turns off type checking for that assertion. The suppression is only needed because the local `parse` cast types `response` too narrowly.
review.fix: Remove `as never`. Type `parse` so it returns `unknown`, or compare `JSON.parse(allowLine(ask, false))` directly.

review.impact: Each output line of the child is now JSON-parsed twice, once by `askOf` and once by `readLine`. The two parsers of the child's stream sit side by side but share nothing.
review.fix: Parse each line once and pass the object to both. You could also have `askOf` take parsed data, or let `readLine` produce an ask part.

review.impact: The test for 'its refusal is no failed call' only passes if `chat.answer` adds the question's tool_use_id to `answered` before the fake prints the tool_result. The fake does not wait for the answer before printing it. It prints the result on a fixed 800 ms + 20 ms timer after the ask. Unit tests run on parallel workers under shared load (#werk-test-runner-parallel), so a slow ask notice → `until` → `answer` round trip lets the result arrive first. It is then shown with `error: true`, and the test fails at random even though the code is correct.
review.fix: Make the order deterministic. Either give the fake a step that waits until a given ask is answered before it plays the next step, and put the tool_result after that step, or have the fake print the tool_result for an ask only after it reads that ask's answer. Then drop the 800 ms pause.

review.impact: No test covers `dropAsks(run)` inside `stop()`, which runs on close, model switch and clear. If it were removed, a page would keep showing an ask whose child was stopped on purpose. A later answer would also be written to a dead stdin and logged as answered, and no test would fail. The exit test only covers the crash path at line 331.
review.fix: Add a chat-asks test that opens an ask and then calls `chat.close()`. Assert that an `answered` notice arrives for the ask, that `chat.asks()` is empty, and that `chat.answer(id, 'allow')` throws AskRefused.

review.impact: allowFlags copies every stored rule and folder from .werk/allow.json straight into the child's argv after the variadic flags --allowedTools and --add-dir. The rules and folders are only checked to be non-empty strings, both when read back by allowedOf (strings()) and when taken from a suggestion (ruleText). An entry that starts with '-' (for example '--dangerously-skip-permissions' or '--permission-mode') would be parsed as its own CLI flag, so every later chat child would start with weaker permissions. To write such an entry, someone must already be able to edit the project's .werk folder or shape the child's suggestions, so the risk is small. Still, a file that widens permissions should not be able to inject flags.
review.fix: In allowedOf and in widening, drop any rule or folder that starts with '-'. Rules can also be held to the CLI's rule shape, a tool name with an optional parenthesised content (/^[A-Za-z_][\w.-]*(\(.*\))?$/). Pass folders as one --add-dir=<dir> each so a value can never be read as a flag.

review.impact: Every answered ask writes the full tool input to .werk/asks.jsonl, the file beside the map log. That includes the 'curl -s ...' commands, URLs and file contents the agent wanted to run. Nothing keeps this file out of git, and the map log in the same folder is meant to be committed. So an approved command that holds a token or credential can end up in the repository.
review.fix: Make sure werk keeps asks.jsonl (and allow.json, which is per-person) out of git, for example with a .gitignore entry that werk writes in .werk. Otherwise, write only the label and the tool to the ask log and leave out the full input.

review.impact: Every line the chat child writes is now parsed as JSON twice: once by askOf and again by readLine. This includes every streamed text delta and every large tool-result line. Permission requests are rare, so almost all of the second parse is wasted, and the cost of the stdout loop grows with the size of the output.
review.fix: Skip the parse cheaply before calling askOf, for example `line.includes('"control_request"') ? askOf(line) : undefined`. Or have askOf take the value that readLine already parsed, so each line is parsed only once.

review.impact: The keydown effect has no dependency array. While an ask is open, the document listener is removed and added again on every render of AskBar, and ChatPane re-renders AskBar on every streamed delta.
review.fix: Keep the latest `answer` and `first` in a ref and register the listener once, with a dependency on `first?.id` only.

review.impact: `wordsOf` rewrites the plain-words rendering that `describeKill` in src/map/show.ts:39 already provides, with different wording. review.impact: `--option` is stored without any check. `killRule` in src/map/rules.ts validates only the form's own words. review.impact: The `{ option?: string } & (union)` intersection makes the type harder to read and to narrow than a flat union. `KILL_WORDS` and `killRule` read `option` and `sample` as unknown keys, so nothing enforces them.

review.impact: The optional-field idiom (`text(x) === "" ? {} : {x: ...}`) is now written three times: `option`, `sample`, and the same check again for `option`. The `sample` copy is inline and the `option` copy is a separate const, so the two read differently.
review.fix: Add a small helper such as `const optional = (name: string) => (text(name) === "" ? {} : { [name]: text(name) })` and use it for both `sample` and `option`.

review.impact: `killHtml` repeats the `section("Kill criteria", ..., "kill")` call in two branches. The title and key are duplicated, so a rename has to touch both.

review.impact: `sample` is only on the metric form, but `option` is on all forms through the intersection. The `criterionOf` spread order and the `option` doc on the type are implicit, and nothing at the type says what `option` refers to.

review.impact: The new `--sample` and `--option` flags on `werk kill` have no test. No test in the repo passes either flag through the verb. review.fix: Add a verb-level test, for example in src/verbs/contract-verbs.test.ts. review.impact: The fallback link is only tested for a valid option. The guard `map.nodes.get(criterion.option)?.kind === "option"` has no test. review.fix: Add a case where `option` points to a missing node or a card, and expect no `[data-role=fallback]`. Add a metric without `sample` and expect the words to have no 'minimum sample'. Add a `manual` row and expect 'Manual test: ...'.

review.impact: The decided-card test only checks the `unchallenged` ring and text. It does not check that a card with criteria shows no ring. review.impact: `criterion.form` goes into the `data-criterion` attribute without `escapeHtml`. The CLI verb only produces the four known forms. review.impact: The short-number restore has untested edge cases. A number that matches no archived ticket should fall through to the board's own refusal. A number that matches only a non-archived ticket should be refused. A full id should be used as given when a short number also matches. Only one unique match and one ambiguous match are tested, so a change to the `endsWith` matching or the fallthrough would go unnoticed.
review.fix: Add tests for: `restore 09` with no match (exit 1, board's error, log unchanged); `restore 01` where the matching ticket is not archived; and `restore a/01` when both `a/01` and `b/01` are archived (restores `a/01` without an ambiguity error).

review.impact: The test title still says only a ready, blocked or building ticket can be archived. The done message is now a separate branch, but there is no direct test of the order of the checks. An archived ticket that is also in the done column should report 'already archived' rather than the done message, and that is not asserted.
review.fix: Add an assertion for an already-archived ticket in the done column, and rename the test to mention the done case.

review.impact: On restore, the board log is read and replayed once to resolve the short number and again after the append to print the result. That is two full replays per call, and the cost grows with the log length. It is a CLI that runs once per call, so the effect is small.
review.fix: Optional. Reuse a single readBoard result for the lookup, or pass the already-read board into the resolution step. Leave the post-append read as it is, because it needs the new state.

causeOfLast.why: the failing `plan.test.ts` test is timing-sensitive under full-suite load and passed 3 of 3 runs alone, so I changed nothing for it.

review.impact: `restoreTarget` is pure logic that resolves a short number against a board. It sits in the verb file next to `registerVerb`. The project rules (#werk-stack-modules, #werk-test-gate-list) say pure code moves into its own small file, so it can join the pure-file coverage list and be tested directly. Here it is only tested through spawned CLI runs. The list-line formatting has the same problem and is inlined in the handler.
review.fix: Move `restoreTarget` into a pure module such as `src/board/restore-target.ts` with its own test file. Add that module to the pure list. Consider also extracting a `listLine(ticket)` formatter.

review.impact: `targetId` is assigned, then copied to `shown`, then used. The extra variable is redundant. A short number that fits only a ticket that is not archived falls through unchanged, so the user gets a 'not on the board' style error instead of 'not archived'.
review.fix: Use `targetId` directly and delete `shown`. Optionally, in `restoreTarget`, return a clearer error when no archived ticket matches the number.

review.impact: The `targetId` variable is introduced and then copied into a second variable, `shown`, which adds nothing. Two names for one value make the end of the handler harder to read. `let targetId = id` is also reassigned only on the restore branch.
review.fix: Delete `shown` and use `targetId` directly: `board.tickets.get(targetId)` and `${targetId} ...`.

review.impact: The list line format (column, archived flag, reason) is built inline in a nested template literal inside the verb handler. It is hard to read and cannot be unit-tested without running the CLI.
review.fix: Pull it into a small `listLine(t)` helper, or build the pieces in named local variables.

review.impact: The header comment is a long run-on that mixes the new list text into the existing sentences. Lines run past the width of the rest of the comment.
review.fix: Rewrap the header comment so each sentence stays on lines of consistent width.

review.impact: No test covers a short restore number that matches nothing. `restoreTarget` then falls back to the raw argument and relies on the board's own error. No test covers a number that matches only a non-archived ticket either. That case is filtered out by `t.archived`, so a bare `01` cannot restore anything that is not archived. A change to the fallback or to the archived filter would go unnoticed.
review.fix: Add cases to the restore test. `restore 99` should exit 1, print the board's not-on-the-board error and append nothing. `restore 01` when `01` exists only as a non-archived ticket should also exit 1 and append nothing.

review.impact: The list test covers only a board with tickets. An empty board, which should print nothing and exit 0, is untested. The test also does not show that `list` appends nothing to the log, although the header comment says it writes nothing.
review.fix: Add an empty-board assertion (`code` 0, empty `out`). In the existing test, assert that `log()` is unchanged after `list`.

review.impact: `ticket list` prints each ticket's free-text `--reason` unescaped. The move verb only checks that the reason isn't blank. An agent-supplied reason that contains a newline or a terminal escape sequence could therefore forge extra ticket lines in the list, or alter the terminal. Anything that parses the one-line-per-ticket output would be misled. The list is meant to be read by people and agents.
review.fix: When printing, replace control characters, including newlines, in `t.reason` with a space or an escaped form. Alternatively, reject control characters in `--reason` when the move is written.

review.impact: The edited header comment line is about 125 characters. The surrounding comment is wrapped near 100 columns, so the header no longer reads like the code around it.
review.fix: Re-wrap the comment, for example: '(#vi-onview-postponed); a ghost has a grey dashed border and background (#werk-propose-new), and a real card' on one line, then 'with a pending edit a blue border only (#al-diff-render). ...' on the next.

review.impact: The edited header comment line is about 125 characters. The other lines in that block wrap at about 100, so the comment now reads unevenly and may fail the formatter's width check.
review.fix: Re-wrap the comment paragraph to the surrounding width.

review.impact: The `style` helper is a near-copy of the one in e2e/card-page.e2e.ts. It differs only in its union of property names, so the two copies can drift apart.
review.fix: Move a shared `style(at, property: keyof CSSStyleDeclaration)` helper into e2e/project.ts, or another e2e helper module, and import it in both specs.

review.impact: The regex `/oklch\(0\.9\d* 0\.00\d*/` is loose and is repeated in card-page.e2e.ts. It would also match other near-white greys, so it barely checks that the ghost is grey-100. A palette tweak would break both copies at once.
review.fix: Name the expected grey once in a shared constant, or compare against the computed colour of a throwaway `bg-gray-100` element.

review.impact: The diff changes three other ghost colours: the tag-row 'proposed' tag (text-gray-600), the tile 'proposed' span, and the nodeLink '(proposed)' span. No test asserts any of them. Because the old tests never checked the old blue classes, a regression back to blue in those places would pass unnoticed.
review.fix: Add assertions to the existing ghost tests. Check that `[data-tag="proposed"]` in the tile and in the tag row has the gray-600 class and not text-blue-700. Check that nodeLink for a proposed node renders text-gray-600.

review.impact: The background regex /oklch\(0\.9\d* 0\.00\d*/ also matches other near-white greys such as gray-50 (0.985 0.002). It does not pin the gray-100 shade, so the check is looser than the unit-test class assertion. The same regex is in card-page.e2e.ts.
review.fix: Tighten it to the gray-100 lightness, for example /oklch\(0\.96\d* 0\.00\d*/.

causeOfLast.why: the lock test (`of two starts on one store at the same moment…`) is timing-based and failed once under load, and it passed in my run.

review.impact: formatInbox no longer uses the file's `indent` helper. It inlines a second `text.replace(/\n/g, "\n      ")` with a different width, so the same continuation-line idiom now exists twice in one file. The two copies can drift apart.
review.fix: Give `indent` a width parameter, for example `indent(text, 6)`, or add a small `indentBy` helper. Use it in both formatThread and formatInbox.

review.impact: `groups.set(id, [...(groups.get(id) ?? []), ...])` copies the array on every note, so grouping is quadratic in the number of notes per card. The `-n` cap keeps the input small, so the effect is minor. It is still harder to read than a push.
review.fix: Get or create the array once, then push to it: `let g = groups.get(id); if (!g) groups.set(id, g = []); g.push({ note, earlier });`.

review.impact: `formatInbox` re-implements newline indentation inline with `note.text.replace(/\n/g, "\n      ")`. The file already has an `indent` helper at line 10, and `formatThread` uses it. The old inbox code used it too. The indentation logic now lives in two places, and the inline copy is hard to read.
review.fix: Parameterise the helper, for example `const indent = (text: string, pad = "    ") => text.replace(/\n/g, `\n${pad}`)`. Call it as `indent(note.text, "      ")` in the inbox. Alternatively, add a second small helper for the 6-space continuation.

review.impact: The grouping step copies the group's array on every note with `groups.set(id, [...(groups.get(id) ?? []), ...])`. That is needlessly quadratic and harder to read than a push into a `Map` of arrays.
review.fix: Get or create the array, then push: `const g = groups.get(id) ?? []; g.push({ note, earlier }); groups.set(id, g);`.

review.impact: The new test "an agent reads a whole card thread from the inbox, in order" overlaps the existing inbox tests in this file and in `notes.test.ts`. It also asserts order only loosely, through `indexOf` comparisons.
review.fix: Drop it, or assert the exact output as the neighbouring tests do.

review.impact: The diff replaces `indent(note.text)` with an inline `note.text.replace(/\n/g, "\n      ")`. This indents continuation lines to the new six-space depth. No inbox test, whether unit, verb or e2e, uses a multi-line note, so a wrong indent or a regression in that line would pass every test. The old path had the same gap, but the diff changes this code and still leaves it untested.
review.fix:
Add a unit test in notes.test.ts that calls `formatInbox` on a note with text "a
b". Assert the exact output `#x  X
  [2] you
      a
      b
`. Do the same for a note that carries the EARLIER_WORDS label.

review.impact: The test "an agent writes a note on a ghost card with no body" would also pass if `say` and `inbox` treated every card alike. It never checks the ghost-specific condition, such as that `werk-pane` has no body. It also never checks that the note's writer is shown as `agent`. This makes it a weak guard for the behaviour in its name. The test "an agent reads a whole card thread" has a similar problem: it duplicates the ordering assertions that the earlier tests already make.
review.fix:
Assert the exact inbox output for the ghost card: `#werk-pane  The pane
  [n] agent
      Describe the pane here
`. Also confirm the card really has no body before the `say`. Alternatively, drop the redundant tests.

review.impact: Each note copies its group's whole array with `[...(groups.get(id) ?? []), ...]`. Grouping is quadratic in the notes per card, and `-n` is user-set with no upper bound. A large `-n` on a busy card does needless copying.
review.fix: Get or create the group's array once, then push to it: `let g = groups.get(id); if (!g) groups.set(id, (g = [])); g.push({ note, earlier });`.

review.impact: The `entries.slice(index + 1).some(...)` check runs for every note and copies the rest of the thread each time. The old actor filter skipped agent notes before this check, and the diff removed it, so more notes now reach it. The cost is quadratic in thread length, and every note after `since` pays it, not just the `count` that get printed.
review.fix: Find the index of the last 'proposed again' entry once per thread, then set `earlier = index < lastProposedAgain`. Alternatively, apply `count` before computing `earlier`.

Probably within scope. src/toolchain.ts adds an exported production function (parsePinnedVersion) that no code uses outside its test. src/toolchain.test.ts also asserts that the pinned version equals Bun.version. No criterion asks for either. Criterion 2 already covers the version check in the Makefile. It looks like a placeholder so that `bun test` has a test to run. If a placeholder test is needed, keep it to a trivial test and do not add an unused production module.

review.impact: Bun test's default discovery also matches `*.spec.ts`. Playwright specs under `e2e/` (`testMatch: **/*.spec.ts`) will be loaded by `bun test` and `make test` as well. They will fail because `@playwright/test` cannot run under Bun's runner. This stays hidden until the first e2e spec is added, and the two runners then collide.
review.fix: Scope Bun's runner in `bunfig.toml` with `[test] root = "src"`, or add `client` as well if component tests live there. Alternatively, name the e2e files so Bun won't match them, and keep Playwright's `testMatch` consistent with that.

review.impact: `include` lists `src`, `client` and `*.ts`, but not `e2e`. The Playwright specs will be left out of the strict typecheck once they exist. The typecheck rule says it covers all of werk's code.
review.fix: Add `"e2e"` to `include`.

review.impact: The 15000 ms timeout is set in `bunfig.toml` and again as `--timeout=15000` in two scripts. The three copies can drift apart.
review.fix: Keep the timeout in `bunfig.toml` only and drop the flag from the scripts. Keep `--parallel=4` in the scripts.

review.impact: `help` depends on `bun-version`. A machine without Bun, or with the wrong version, cannot list the targets. That is the situation where the install hint matters most.
review.fix: Remove `bun-version` from `help`'s prerequisites. The README already covers install.

review.impact: `include` lists `src`, `client` and `*.ts`, but not `e2e`, which is where `playwright.config.ts` looks for specs. When Playwright specs are added they will not be type-checked, so `make typecheck` will pass on broken e2e code. This goes against the rule that TypeScript checks all of werk's code.
review.fix: Add `e2e` to `include`. This is harmless while the folder is empty. Also confirm that `tsc` does not fail on an `include` entry that matches nothing.

review.impact: The 15000 ms test timeout is set in `bunfig.toml` and again as `--timeout=15000` in both the `test` and `test:coverage` scripts. The `--parallel=4` flag and the Makefile description 'four parallel workers' repeat the same pair of values. Changing one of these means editing up to four places, and they can drift apart.
review.fix: Keep the timeout only in `bunfig.toml` and drop `--timeout` from the scripts. Alternatively, make `test:coverage` reuse `test` (`bun run test --coverage ...`).

review.impact: `parsePinnedVersion` is a one-line `trim()` wrapper. Its only use is its own test, which checks that `.bun-version` matches the running Bun. The Makefile's `bun-version` target does the same check in shell, so the check is written twice.
review.fix: Either let the test read the file and `trim()` it directly and drop the module, or keep the module and add a comment that it exists so the pure-file coverage rule has something to apply to.

review.impact: The `dev` script is a stub (`echo ... && exit 0`). `make dev` reports success without starting a server, which could mislead someone who runs it.
review.fix: Make the stub exit non-zero, or add a comment or ticket reference that says it is a placeholder until the server exists.

review.impact: The tests cover only a trailing LF. A CRLF ending or surrounding spaces is not tested. An empty or whitespace-only file, which would make the version check compare against '', is not tested either. `parsePinnedVersion` has no failure path.
review.fix: Add cases for "1.4.1\r\n" and "  1.4.1  ". Decide what an empty file should do: either throw in `parsePinnedVersion` or pin the behaviour with a test.

review.impact: The `bun-version` guard is the only protection against a wrong Bun version, and no test runs it. A regression in its comparison or its exit code would pass every check.
review.fix: Add a test that runs `make bun-version` with a stub `bun` first on PATH that reports a different version. Assert that it exits non-zero and prints the pinned version.

grade.gap: In src/test/coverage-gate.ts:16, ownLcov returns null when the own test file does not exist. judge then fails the file at 0% with 'missing test file', and this happens before anything checks whether the file has executable lines. A file of type declarations usually has no own test, so it fails. If it does have a test, Bun's transpiler drops type-only imports, so the module is never loaded and gets no lcov record. judge then fails it with 'does not load the file' (src/test/coverage-report.ts:63-70). The only test for this case (coverage-report.test.ts, 'a file with no executable lines passes') feeds judge a hand-written record with LF:0, which a real Bun run of a type-only file does not produce. Fix: before the own-test step, find out whether the listed file has any executable code. For example, transpile it with Bun.Transpiler and check whether the output is empty, or run the test and treat a missing record for a file with no runtime output as 'no executable lines'. Then add a gate-level test that lists a real types-only file with no test and checks that the gate passes it.

Minor, so this passes. #werk-reflink-own-test-coverage only says 'one fixed convention'. The diff picks the convention: the test sits beside the file, with .test inserted before the extension (ownTestPath in src/test/coverage-report.ts:12). It also moves the PURE list into its own module, src/test/pure-files.ts, where #werk-test-gate-list places it inside coverage-gate.ts. Both match Bun's default and the existing toolchain.test.ts. A short card or a line on the reflink card would record the convention.

The edge case 'a listed file with no executable lines, for example a file of type declarations, passes' does not hold in practice. A types-only file fails as 'missing test file' or as 'does not load the file' (src/test/coverage-gate.ts:16 and src/test/coverage-report.ts:63-70). See criterion-4.

The behaviour is met: src/fake-agent/run.ts playReply plays the ask, pause, event and crash steps without waiting for an answer, and a crash returns before any tool result or final result. The test only weakly shows that the steps play before any answer. In 'an ask, a pause and a crash play before any answer...' (src/fake-agent/fake-agent.test.ts) the test never sends an answer, so it does not prove that the pause and the crash come first. Optional fix: after the crash, send an answer to a1 and assert that the output still holds no 'user' and no 'result' line.

Some behaviours are asked for by no acceptance criterion and are required only by the cited decided cards: the next reply for each launch of a role, with an error when none is left (#werk-v0-seams-fake-script-next-reply); denying open asks when there is no input channel; the 20 ms pause margin (#werk-test-fake-ask-open); refusing an edit through a link (#werk-test-fake-edit-inside-cwd); and failing when the role is missing (#werk-v0-seams-fake-script-launch-env). The cards require all of these, so none needs removing. I found no behaviour that is not asked for at all.

review.impact: The chat loop can't tell a crash from a normal turn. `turn` returns either `crash ?? picked.exit`, and the loop continues only when `result === exit`. A scripted `{ crash: N }` where N equals the role's exit code (for example `crash: 0` with the default exit of 0) is read as a normal turn. The loop keeps waiting for input instead of ending the launch, and the test sees a different behaviour than the script asked for.
review.fix: Have `turn` return a tagged result, such as `{ crashed: number } | { exit: number } | { error: string }`. The chat loop can then return on `crashed` regardless of its value.

review.impact: `playReply` skips an edit whose path resolves to null without saying so. This is safe only because `escapingEdit` checks the whole reply first. The two checks are separate, so a later change to either one could silently drop edits.
review.fix: Throw or return an error when `resolveEdit` returns null inside `playReply`. Alternatively, have the pre-validation resolve the targets once and pass them in, so the path is resolved in only one place.

review.impact: `run` handles the chat role and the one-shot role in two branches. Each has its own message-logging and turn/exit handling, and the one-shot path re-derives the reply index from the launch log with `countLaunches(...) - 1`. This is an easy off-by-one to break. Reading the reply index back out of the log that was just appended to couples the log format to reply selection.
review.fix: Extract a helper such as `recordMessage(log, role, line)` and share the turn loop. Alternatively, compute the launch index before `appendRecord` so no `- 1` is needed.

review.impact: `isChatRole` is a one-line check against the hardcoded name "chat". It sits in the script module but is not part of the script schema. The rule that a chat role plays one reply per turn is hidden behind a magic string, and it is not tested with a script that sets it up directly.
review.fix: Make chat mode explicit in the script, for example `chat: true` on `RoleScript` validated in `parseScript`. Otherwise export a named constant for the role name.

review.impact: `isControlResponse`, `answerOf` and `messageText` each repeat the same try/parse/catch pattern. This is minor duplication, and parse failures are silently swallowed in two of them.
review.fix: Add a small `parseLine(line): unknown | undefined` helper and build the three functions on top of it.

review.impact: The test 'a pause lasts its time plus a 20 ms margin' hardcodes the margin separately from `PAUSE_MARGIN_MS`. It includes process spawn time, so it only checks a lower bound. The variable is misleadingly named `spawnOnly`. If the margin changes, the test and the code drift apart.
review.fix: Import `PAUSE_MARGIN_MS` (export it) and assert against `100 + PAUSE_MARGIN_MS`. Rename the variable to `elapsed`.

review.impact: The `launch` helper casts `child.stdin` to `FileSink` four times with inline `import("bun").FileSink`. This is repetitive and noisy.
review.fix: Bind `const stdin = child.stdin as FileSink` once, using a top-level `import type { FileSink } from "bun"`.

review.impact: The pause test asserts only that the whole child process, including Bun start-up, took at least 120 ms. Start-up time alone can cover the 20 ms margin, so the test can pass with `PAUSE_MARGIN_MS` set to 0. It does not check the behaviour in its name. The variable name `spawnOnly` is also misleading.
review.fix: Have the script emit an event before and after the pause, and compare the arrival times of the two lines. Assert the gap is at least 120 ms. Alternatively, unit-test the pause duration with an injectable sleep.

review.impact: A single test file drives everything through a spawned `bun` subprocess. The pure modules `script.ts`, `edit.ts`, `lines.ts` and `launch-log.ts` have no test file of their own, and subprocess runs are not counted in coverage. Under the project's per-file pure-file coverage rule, these files would fail the gate or sit at 0%. Several failure paths are never exercised: `parseScript` validation errors, a malformed script file, `LineReader` partial lines and a final line with no newline, `messageText` array content, and `answerOf` with bad JSON.
review.fix: Add `script.test.ts`, `edit.test.ts`, `lines.test.ts` and `launch-log.test.ts`. Each should call its module in process and cover the error branches. Register the pure files in the coverage gate list.

review.impact: The assertion `JSON.parse(l).type ?? JSON.parse(l).r` mixes two kinds of value, which makes it hard to read. The test never checks that a chat role with a non-zero `exit` stops after a turn that returns a different code. The crash-in-chat path is untested.
review.fix: Assert on the parsed objects directly. Add a chat test with a crash step and a test for a chat role whose exit is non-zero.

review.impact: `realWithTail` uses `existsSync`, which returns false for a dangling symlink. If the project has a symlink whose target is missing and points outside the folder, the walk skips the link and checks only its parent. `resolveEdit` then approves the path, and `writeFileSync` follows the link and writes outside the project. This is test-only code and the script is trusted, so the risk is small, but it breaks the stated guarantee that no edit goes outside the folder, including through a link.
review.fix: Test each path component with `lstatSync` instead of `existsSync`. If a component is a symlink that `realpathSync` cannot resolve, read it with `readlinkSync`, resolve it against its parent, and check that result. Or reject the edit when the target is a dangling symlink.

causeOfLast.why: The gate already stayed out of `make test`; the grader returned no line for criterion 5, so I only added a test that proves it.

review.impact: The exit code of the per-file test run is ignored. If the run crashes or exits before it writes lcov.info, `ownLcov` returns "". `judge` then reports 'own test does not load the file', which points the reader at the wrong cause.
review.fix: Check `await proc.exited`. If the exit code is non-zero, or the report is missing, return a distinct failing result such as 'own test run failed'. Capture or print stderr for that case.

review.impact: `judge` has a nested branch inside `counts === null || counts.found === 0`. The inner `if (counts === null)` is the only way into the first return, so the control flow is harder to read than it needs to be.
review.fix: Flatten it: `if (counts === null) return {…does not load…}; if (counts.found === 0) return {…no executable lines…};`.

review.impact: `lineCounts` repeats the `current === file || current.endsWith(`/${file}`)` check in two places, and the DA branch uses the negated form. This is easy to let drift apart.
review.fix: Extract a small `matches(current, file)` helper and use it in both branches.

review.impact: `package.json` and `Makefile` are read relative to the process cwd. The sibling `coverage-gate.test.ts` uses `import.meta.dir`. This test fails if bun is started from another directory.
review.fix: Use `join(import.meta.dir, "..", "..", "package.json")`, and the same for the Makefile.

review.impact: `judge` has a nested conditional: `if (counts === null || counts.found === 0) { if (counts === null) {...} return ... }`. It tests `counts === null` twice, which makes the three outcomes hard to follow.
review.fix: Flatten it into sequential guards. First `if (counts === null) return {...does not load...}`. Then `if (counts.found === 0) return {...no executable lines...}`.

review.impact: `lineCounts` writes the file-match test twice, as `current !== file && !current.endsWith(`/${file}`)` and again as `current === file || current.endsWith(...)`. The two copies can drift apart.
review.fix: Compute `const matches = current !== null && (current === file || current.endsWith(`/${file}`))` once per SF record, and reuse it in the DA and LF branches.

review.impact: The 'no executable lines' verdict is produced in two places. `check` gets it from `hasExecutableCode`, and `judge` gets it from `found === 0`. There are two paths to one outcome, and `hasExecutableCode` needs a Transpiler plus a regex that strips comments and can mangle strings containing `//`.
review.fix: Keep one mechanism. Either rely on `judge`'s `found === 0` case and let the gate run the own test where one exists, or keep `hasExecutableCode` and drop the `found === 0` branch in `judge`. Document why if both are needed.

review.impact: The own-test subprocess has stdout and stderr ignored and its exit code is discarded. When that test fails or crashes, the gate reports only a coverage percentage or 'does not load', which makes debugging hard.
review.fix: Capture stderr and the exit code, and put a failure note into the result, for example 'own test failed'.

review.impact: The test reads `package.json` and `Makefile` by cwd-relative path, so it breaks when run from another directory. The regexes over script text are also brittle against harmless reformatting.
review.fix: Resolve paths from `import.meta.dir`, for example `join(import.meta.dir, '..', '..', 'package.json')`.

review.impact: The gate ignores the exit code of each file's own test run (`await proc.exited`). It also discards stderr. If that run fails or crashes after writing partial lcov, the gate judges the partial coverage. A failure then shows up as a vague 'does not load the file' or a misleading percentage. No test covers this path: the gate test only has the missing-test-file case and the types-only case.
review.fix: Capture the exit code. When it is non-zero and there is no usable lcov, return a result with a note such as 'own test failed'. Add a gate test with a fixture whose own test fails or does not load the file.

review.impact: The test reads `package.json` and `Makefile` relative to the process cwd, but `coverage-gate.test.ts` uses `import.meta.dir`. If `bun test` is run from a subdirectory, this test fails with ENOENT instead of a clear failure.
review.fix: Resolve the paths with `join(import.meta.dir, '..', '..', 'package.json')`, as the gate does.

review.impact: `lineCounts` matches `current.endsWith('/' + file)`. A record such as `other/src/a.ts` would be counted for `src/a.ts`. The tests cover only a single matching absolute prefix, not this collision, so a wrong file's lines could count toward the 90% verdict.
review.fix: Match against a path made absolute from the repo root, or add a test that two similarly-suffixed records are not merged.

review.impact: Promise.all starts one `bun test` subprocess for every pure file at once. The list is two files now, but it only grows, since entries are never removed. A long list will start dozens of Bun processes at the same moment. That can overload a small CI runner and make the per-test 15s timeout flaky, which the project's parallel-worker rule is meant to avoid. The gate also re-runs each pure file's own test after the full coverage run. That duplicate work is by design, but it adds to the load.
review.fix: Cap the concurrency, for example by running the files through a small pool of 4 workers to match `--parallel=4`. Optionally add a timeout to each spawned process so a hung test cannot stall the gate forever.

review.impact: The git calls and every spawned program keep the real HOME and git variables. The user's global git config therefore applies to the fresh repository. For example, `commit.gpgsign=true` makes `newRepo` fail or prompt, and hooks or `init.templateDir` leak in. Test results then depend on the machine, and the harness reads the real data of whoever runs it.
review.fix: Add `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` and, if possible, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` to the git environment. Better, put them in `cleanEnv` or `envFor`, so spawned programs get them too.

review.impact: The preload replaces `Bun.spawn`, `Bun.spawnSync` and `Bun.which` by monkey-patching, and casts everything through `unknown`. It guesses at overloads: the `cmd` field, and a bare options object versus an argv array. A call shape the wrapper does not expect, or a Bun upgrade that changes the signatures, breaks silently, and `Bun.spawn` loses its typed overloads. Because the patch is global, it also changes the behaviour of the code under test.
review.fix: Keep the patch narrow and add a test that covers the options-object form (`Bun.spawn({cmd})`). Also state in the comment why `process.env` alone is not enough, so the patch can be removed once Bun honours it.

review.impact: The check that the fake agent is first is duplicated. `assertFakeFirst` repeats the same error text as `preload.ts`, so the two copies can drift apart.
review.fix: Export one `assertFakeFirst(path)` from `env.ts` and call it from both places.

review.impact: `dispose` kills only the direct child with SIGKILL. A grandchild, such as a process the shell or the fake agent started, survives, and `rmSync` runs while it may still write into the directory. `dispose` also runs the kill loop while the `.then` handlers delete from the same set, which is fragile.
review.fix: Take a snapshot with `const running = [...children]` before killing. Then kill and await that snapshot. If the child may spawn its own children, spawn it in its own process group and kill the group.

review.impact: `assertFakeFirst` repeats the check and the error message in `src/test-env/preload.ts` (lines 38-42). If the wording or the rule changes, the two copies can drift apart.
review.fix: Export one `assertFakeFirst(path = process.env.PATH)` from `env.ts` and call it from both `preload.ts` and `project.ts`.

review.impact: The `SpawnOptions` type has an unused `cmd?: unknown` member. The double casts (`as unknown as AnySpawn`, `as unknown as F`) and the wrapper that guesses between the array and options-object call forms are hard to read. They hide type errors, and they would silently mishandle any other overload.
review.fix: Drop the unused `cmd` member. Replace the casts with one narrowly typed wrapper, or explicitly handle the `{cmd: [...]}` form. Add a comment saying why each overload is handled.

review.impact: `cleanEnv(process.env)` is recomputed in `git()` and in `envFor`. The preload has already cleaned `process.env`, so the repeated call is redundant, and the two call sites can drift apart.
review.fix: Compute the cleaned environment once at module level, or add a small shared `baseEnv()` helper in `env.ts` and use it in both places.

review.impact: The preload patches Bun.spawn, Bun.spawnSync, Bun.which and Bun.$. Only spawn, which and the shell are tested. The `Bun.spawnSync` wrapper is not tested at all, and `project.ts` passes an explicit env, so nothing exercises its default. Two branches of `defaultSpawnEnv` are also untested: the options-object form `Bun.spawn({cmd, ...})`, and an explicit `env` that must not be overridden. If one of these breaks, a test could silently reach the real `claude` or a real WERK_* variable.
review.fix: Add tests that call `Bun.spawnSync(['claude','--version'])` with no env and expect the fake's error. Add tests for the `{cmd: [...]}` form, and for an explicit env that is kept as given.

review.impact: The test 'another sees none of it' only checks isolation if the preceding test ran first in the same file. Run alone, for example with `-t`, it passes without proving anything.
review.fix: Make the isolation check self-contained: in one test, create two projects through `createProject`, write to one, and assert that the other is untouched.

review.impact: The failure and edge paths are not covered. `cleanEnv` is not tested with `PATH` missing or with undefined values. `pathWithFake` is not tested with empty entries such as `a::b`. `assertFakeFirst` throwing is not tested. The cleanup when `newRepo` fails in `createProject` is not tested.
review.fix: Add cases to `cleanEnv` and `pathWithFake` for an undefined `PATH`, undefined values and empty segments. Add a test that `createProject` throws and removes its root when `PATH` has no fake first.

review.impact: cleanEnv removes only WERK_* variables. Git variables such as GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE and GIT_COMMON_DIR pass through to the `git init`, `git config` and `git commit` calls in newRepo (project.ts:46-52). When the tests run from a git hook, or from a shell that exports these variables, those commands can act on the real repository. They could write the test user.name and user.email into the real repo's config and add an empty commit to it. This breaks the rule that a test never touches the real data of the person who runs it. Real credentials such as API tokens also reach every spawned child unchanged.
review.fix: Also drop variables with the `GIT_` prefix in cleanEnv. Set GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 for the repo setup calls, so the user's global git config is not read.

review.impact: appendEvents folds the log, then reads it again with readText, then appends. Two werk processes running at once can both pass the checks against the same state and both append. That can produce a duplicate id or a second parent in the log. The fold then lists the later event as a problem, which defeats the 'a write never disagrees with the fold' guarantee in fold.ts. The two reads also parse the log twice and can see different text.
review.fix: Read the text once and use it for both the fold and the newline check. Hold a lock around the check and the append, for example an exclusive lock file or an O_APPEND write after a re-check. If concurrent writers are out of scope, say so in the doc comment.

review.impact: readMap is named as a read but writes fold-ms.jsonl into the project's .werk folder on every call. Every show and every append writes to disk, and each append writes twice, since appendEvents calls readMap. The file grows without bound. The write is hidden in a function whose callers expect no side effects.
review.fix: Move the recording into a separate function, such as recordFoldTime(logPath, entries, ms), and call it explicitly from the places that need it. Or make readMap's recording opt-in.

review.impact: A flag with no `=` takes the next argument as its value, even when that argument is another flag. `--title --why x` sets title to '--why' and treats x as positional. The 'needs a value' error fires only at the end of the arguments.
review.fix: Treat a next argument that starts with `--` as a missing value, or document that `--flag=value` is needed for values that start with dashes.

review.impact: The add verb checks the status against the full STATUSES list, but the error text says 'open or proto'. The 'decided' rule is hard-coded in the verb as a separate special case. If a status is added to fold.ts, this check and its message drift out of step.
review.fix: Build the accepted list from STATUSES without 'decided', and use it for both the check and the message.

review.impact: The `option-link` and `unknown-card` violations are built inline in two places each, in `checkEdge` and in `applyProposed`. The option-link message text is word-for-word the same in both. If one copy is reworded or fixed, the two can drift apart.
review.fix: Add small helpers such as `unknownCard(id)` and `optionLink(id, type)` that return a `Violation`. Call them from both `checkEdge` and `applyProposed`.

review.impact: `appendEvents` reads the log file twice: once through `readMap`, and again through `readText` to decide whether a newline is needed. `readMap` also appends a line to `fold-ms.jsonl` on every call, so every write adds to that file with no bound on its size.
review.fix: Read the text once and pass it to both the fold and the newline check. Split the fold-time recording out of `readMap` so a write does not trigger it, or document the growth and cap it.

review.impact: `const current = () => project;` only wraps the variable and adds nothing. Every call in the file reads `current().x` instead of `project.x`.
review.fix: Delete `current` and use `project` directly.

review.impact: `parsed.positional[0] as string` is a type assertion used to get past `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`. `args.ts` has the same pattern with `argv[i] as string`. The length check a few lines earlier is what makes it safe, so a later edit to that check could silently break it.
review.fix: Destructure `const [rawId] = parsed.positional` and check `rawId === undefined` in the guard, as `add.ts` does. That removes the cast.

review.impact: The status check is split in two. `decided` is refused by a hard-coded string compare, and the rest is checked against `STATUSES` with a cast, which also accepts `decided`. The error text 'open or proto' is a third hand-written copy of the same rule.
review.fix: Derive the allowed values once, for example `const ADD_STATUSES = STATUSES.filter(s => s !== 'decided')`. Use that list for the membership check and for the error message and the `USAGE` text.

review.impact: Two parseArgs edge cases have no test. First, `--title --why x` takes `--why` as the value of `--title`, because the next token is consumed without a check. Second, `--title=` gives an empty value, and `--title ''` gives another. A change to either behaviour would not be caught. The `--flag value` form is also never tested in a way that shows the value being skipped from the positionals.
review.fix: Add cases that pin the intended behaviour. Either the next token is refused when it starts with `--`, or it is taken as the value. Also add one for an empty `=` value.

review.impact: `add` has no test for `--status proto` succeeding. There is also no test that `--parent '#root'` loses its hash through the full path. The `--why` and `--body` text flags are only exercised in the hash test, and `--body` is never checked end to end. A regression in status handling would pass.
review.fix: Add an `add --status proto` test that checks the status shown by `show`. Add an `add --parent '#root'` test. Add a `--body` assertion.

review.impact: The "a second parent" test only covers two `edge.added` events. It does not cover a `parent` on `node.proposed` followed by an edge `refines` from the same card. It also does not cover `depends_on` and `supported_by`, which must not set a parent. The second-parent and cycle rules for non-refines links are not locked in.
review.fix: Add a test that a `depends_on` edge does not set a parent and does not trip second-parent. Add one for a proposed-with-parent card followed by an edge `refines`.

review.impact: `main` with a verb that throws, and `main` with `-h`, are untested. In the no-help-verb test, the `x` case never shows that no error output is lost. The assertions check exit codes but not what was printed.
review.fix: Assert that `io.lines.err` contains `unknown verb` in the no-help case. Add a `-h` case.

review.impact: appendEvents reads the log, checks the events, then appends, with no lock. Two `werk add` processes running at once can both pass the duplicate-id, second-parent or cycle check and both append. The log then holds an event that breaks a rule, and the fold reports it as a problem. This is an integrity gap, not an exploit.
review.fix: Hold an exclusive lock around the check and append, for example a lock file created with `wx` or an advisory lock. Alternatively, re-run the check on the text just before appending and compare the log size.

review.impact: Every read, including `show`, appends a line to fold-ms.jsonl next to the log with no size cap. The file grows without limit, and a read-only verb writes to disk. When WERK_LOG points elsewhere, the write goes into that directory as well.
review.fix: Cap or rotate the file. Alternatively, record fold times only when an env flag is set, or only from the write path.

review.impact: Card title, why and body come from the log and go to the terminal unsanitized. A log that was pulled in from elsewhere can embed ANSI or OSC escape sequences, and these can spoof output or the terminal title when `show` prints them. The same applies to problem details in show.ts.
review.fix: Strip control characters other than newline and tab from log text before printing it.

review.impact: A flag that takes a value consumes the next argument even when that argument is another flag. For example, `--title --why x` sets title to `--why`. This silently accepts malformed input and writes it to the log.
review.fix: Reject a space-separated value that starts with `--`. The `--flag=value` form already covers values that begin with dashes.

review.impact: Every readMap call appends a line to fold-ms.jsonl, so `show` and `add` each do an extra file write. The file is never trimmed or rotated, so it grows without limit and adds I/O to every command. Because `add` reads the map too, each write costs two appends.
review.fix: Bound the file by keeping only the last N entries or rotating it past a size limit. Alternatively, record only when asked (for example with an env flag), or log only the commands that write.

review.impact: appendEvents reads and parses the whole log in readMap, then reads the same file again with readText just to check the trailing newline. That doubles the file I/O on every add, and the cost grows with the log.
review.fix: Have readMap return the text it read, or split a helper that returns both the entries and the text, and reuse that text for the newline check.

review.impact: Stale-lock takeover is racy. Two starts can both read the same dead holder. Start A removes the file and creates a fresh lock. Start B then runs its own `rmSync` and deletes A's live lock, and B's `create` succeeds. Both servers end up holding the lock, which breaks the one-server-per-.werk guarantee. The same race exists in the unparseable-lock path at the deadline (line 111). The 'two starts at once' test only covers the case where no lock file exists.
review.fix: Make takeover atomic. For example, rename the stale file to a unique temp name and delete that. Rename fails for the loser, which then loops and retries `create`. Alternatively, re-read the file immediately before removing it and only remove it if it still names the same dead pid. The rename approach is the stronger of the two.

review.impact: `decodeURIComponent` throws a URIError on a malformed escape such as `/api/card/%E0%A4%A`. The handler catches it, so the client gets a 500 and an error log line instead of the 400 'bad card id' that every other invalid id gets.

review.impact: `{...} as unknown as Live` hides the missing `server`, `handler` and `done` fields from the type checker. If someone reorders the setup, they can read those fields before they are assigned, and no error will show.

review.impact: The test 'a hot reload keeps the token and the open live connections' never checks that a reload happened. review.impact: `decodeURIComponent` throws a URIError on a malformed escape such as `/api/card/%E0%A4%A`. The handler turns that into a 500 and writes an error log line containing the request URL. review.impact: The token is compared with `!==`, which is not constant-time. The server only listens on loopback, so the practical risk is very small.

review.impact: Every `/api/graph` and `/api/card/:id` request calls `readMap(ctx.logPath)`. I did not open `readMap` itself, so this assumes it re-reads and re-folds the whole event log on each call. That would make N card reads cost N full folds. Concurrent requests would repeat the same work.

review.impact: `applyProposed` and `applyEdited` each repeat the `who` validation: an optional read, a violation check, then a `oneOf(WHOS)` check with the same message. The two copies can drift apart.
review.fix: Extract a small `optionalWho(fields)` helper that returns a `Who`, `null` or a `Violation`, and call it from both places.

review.impact: The doc comment for applyEvent ('Checks one event against the map...') was left above applyAccepted when the new helpers were inserted. applyEvent is now undocumented and applyAccepted has a wrong doc comment.
review.fix: Move the doc comment back to sit directly above applyEvent, and give the helpers their own short comments or none.

review.impact: The verb accepts a --body flag only to refuse it. The USAGE and summary say edit sets who, but the code, the XOR check and the test keep a body path alive that always fails with 'frozen'. The edited event also carries a body field that applyEdited handles only as a refusal, which adds dead branching in the verb and the fold.
review.fix: Decide whether edit takes --body. If the refusal is meant to be reachable from the CLI, document --body in USAGE. Otherwise drop the flag and send why and body to applyEdited only as a guard.

review.impact: The kind check hardcodes the list ['card','option','source'] and then prints KINDS.slice(0, 3). This duplicates the list, and the slice silently breaks if KINDS is reordered. The allowed kinds sit in three places: the check, the message and the USAGE string.
review.fix: Define a local constant such as ADD_KINDS = ['card','option','source'] and use it for the check, the message and the USAGE. Drop the KINDS import.

review.impact: The 'who' validation (optional read, oneOf check, error message) is copied in applyProposed and applyEdited.
review.fix: Extract a helper such as checkWho(fields) that returns the value or a Violation.

review.impact: EVIDENCE is a mutable string[] that isGhostOf takes as kinds: string[]. The inline lists ['option'], ['excerpt'] and ['source'] repeat the same pattern. Kind strings are untyped here although a Kind type exists.
review.fix: Type the parameter as readonly Kind[] and the constant as readonly Kind[].

review.impact: acceptGhost makes one pass over ghostEdges when it collects carried evidence and options. That is fine for the current shape, but it relies on the order in which edges are held. The correctness of the ancestor-source pickup is not obvious from the code.
review.fix: Add a short comment saying one pass is enough because the carried cards are only ancestors, evidence and options. A second pass is not needed.

review.impact: The accept, discard, say and edit verbs repeat the same refused-event append and error-print block, so any change to the wording has to be made in four places.
review.fix: Add a shared helper, for example appendOrReport(ctx, events, usage?), in the verb support code.

review.impact: The new thread branch in renderCard (`thread:` heading plus threadLines) has no test in card-text.test.ts, which this diff leaves unchanged. Only the CLI test covers it. card-text.ts is in PURE_FILES, and #werk-reflink-own-test-coverage counts only lines run by the file's own test. So the 90% per-file coverage gate can fail, and a regression in the show output would not be caught by the unit tests.
review.fix: Add a test to src/map/card-text.test.ts. Fold a card with notes, then assert that renderCard prints `thread:` followed by the indented note lines. Also assert that a card with no thread prints no `thread:` section.

review.impact: The new `ghost-parent` branch in checkLink is only tested from ghost-rules.test.ts. link-rules.ts is in PURE_FILES, and its coverage counts only its own test file. The branch is not covered there, so the per-file gate can drop and a change to the rule may go unnoticed.
review.fix: Add a test to link-rules.test.ts. It should assert that a refines edge from a real card to a ghost is refused with `ghost-parent`, and that a refines edge from a ghost to a ghost or to a real card is allowed.

review.impact: A card proposed again after a discard with no notes still gets a `proposed again` marker, because the empty thread array is truthy. No test covers this case. The inbox and show output would then start with a marker that has nothing before it, and nothing says whether that is intended.
review.fix: Add a test that discards a card with no notes and proposes it again. Assert the intended thread: either no marker, or a marker. If a marker is not wanted, only push it when the existing thread has entries.

review.impact: The input-refusal test does not cover `-n 0`, a non-integer `--since`, or `add --kind excerpt`. Those are the new boundary checks in inbox.ts and add.ts, so a regression there would pass unnoticed.
review.fix: Add `["inbox","-n","0"]`, `["inbox","--since","1.5"]` and `["add","a","--title","A","--kind","excerpt"]` to the list of calls that must exit 2.

review.impact: Note text and the `by` field are printed unescaped by `show` and `inbox`. A note containing newlines can forge extra inbox rows or a fake `-- proposed again --` marker. Terminal escape sequences in a note also reach the person's terminal. The notes are written by an agent, so this is a small spoofing and injection risk.
review.fix: In `entryText`, replace control characters (newlines and ESC) in `by` and `text` before rendering, for example by escaping them or collapsing them to a space. Alternatively, reject control characters in `applyNote`.

causeOfLast.why: the ticket text names plan events as run events, but no cited card lists them, so the earlier pass added them in good faith.

review.impact: The doc comment on applyBoardEvent says a refused event 'changes nothing'. runEvent calls ensurePlan before it checks tier, gate or pid, so a refused run event still adds an empty plan to the board. foldBoard then shows plans that no valid event created. The tests exercise this path without noticing.
review.fix: Validate the event's field first, and call ensurePlan only when the event is accepted. Otherwise, correct the comment.

review.impact: The actor is cast to Actor without checking it. Any other value, such as 'robot', skips the person-move rule and acts as an agent. The restrictions on a person's moves can be bypassed with a typo or a hand-written log line.
review.fix: Validate actor against 'you', 'agent' and 'loop'. Return bad-event for any other value.

review.impact: appendBoardEvent folds the log, then reads it again, then appends, with no lock. Two writers running at once can both pass the check and append events that conflict, such as two restores or two moves. The pre-check exists to enforce the fold's rules, and this race defeats it. The file is also read twice.
review.fix: Read the text once and use it for both the fold and the newline check. Document the single-writer assumption, or serialise appends with a lock or an O_APPEND write.

review.impact: The actor error message reads '--actor is you' even though 'agent' is also accepted. The verb limits actor to you or agent, while the fold's Actor type also has 'loop'. The two lists can drift apart.
review.fix: Make the message say 'you or agent'. Better, export a shared actor list from board/fold.ts and validate against it.

review.impact: pidAlive is an OS process probe, and it sits in the board log store that handles reading and appending. It has nothing to do with the log. This goes against the rule that modules are single-purpose.
review.fix: Move pidAlive into its own small module, for example src/board/pid.ts.

review.impact: The tail of resolveTicket tests matches.length > 1 twice. The first test is hidden inside the destructuring check, and the second is in the error message. This makes the code harder to read.
review.fix: Branch separately on matches.length === 0, then on matches.length > 1, and then return the single match.

review.impact: The not-found and ambiguous cases share one branch that re-tests `matches.length > 1` inside the error message. A reader has to work out that `only === undefined` and `length > 1` are the two failures. This is harder to follow than two separate returns.
review.fix: Return the two errors separately: `if (matches.length > 1) return {ok:false, error: ...}; if (only === undefined) return {ok:false, error: ...};`.

review.impact: `TICKET_EVENTS` also holds the build, pass, merge, steps and held-out handlers, so the name is misleading. `RUN_EVENTS` is a separate Set that duplicates the `run.*` cases in the `runEvent` switch. A new run event has to be added in two places, and the switch `default` is unreachable in practice.
review.fix: Rename the table to `HANDLERS`. Either register the five `run.*` types in it with small handlers, or drop `RUN_EVENTS` and route on `type.startsWith("run.")`.

review.impact: The ticket-lookup preamble `const ticket = ticketOf(...); if (isViolation(ticket)) return ticket;` is repeated in about ten handlers. Each handler also uses `as` casts after manual checks, such as `pid as number`, `rec.n as number`, `reason as string` and `str(...) as Column`. The casts bypass the type checker and can drift out of step with the checks beside them.
review.fix: Add a helper like `withTicket(handler)` that does the lookup once, and a typed `int(rec, key)` helper that returns `number | undefined`, like `str`. This removes the casts and the repeated preamble.

review.impact: The `moved` handler is a long chain of guard clauses, about 50 lines, that mixes validation and mutation. This is the main complexity hotspot in the diff.
review.fix: Split the validation into a pure `checkMove(board, ticket, to, actor, reason)` that returns a violation or null. Keep only the mutation in `moved`.

review.impact: The finished-process check spawns the external binary `true`, so it depends on PATH. A recycled pid could also make it flaky. If the spawn fails, the test fails for a reason unrelated to `pidAlive`.
review.fix: Spawn `process.execPath` with `-e ''`, or use `Bun.spawn([process.execPath, '-e', ''])`. This also keeps the test independent of the host's binaries.

review.impact: Only the explicit `--actor you` path is tested. The default actor (`agent`) and `--actor agent` are not asserted, so the default could change without a test failing. The bad-input loop also checks only the exit code, not that nothing was written to the board log.
review.fix: Add a test that runs restore without `--actor` and asserts the appended event has `actor: "agent"`. In the bad-input test, assert that no board file exists afterwards.

review.impact: Several rules in `fold.ts` have no test. These are: a person moving blocked→ready (refused by PERSON_MOVES), reordering an archived ready ticket (`not-ready` via the archived branch), a `blocked_by` id that names no ticket (counts as an open blocker), and `ticket.merge` on an archived ticket. A regression in any of them would pass the suite.
review.fix: Add one assertion for each of these cases to the existing `moves`, `reorder` and `archive` tests.

review.impact: Number normalisation is only tested for one-digit and already-padded input. Odd inputs such as an empty string, `"001"` or a non-numeric argument are not exercised. A ticket with a malformed number could also resolve unexpectedly.
review.fix: Add cases for `""`, `"abc"` and `"001"`, and assert each is refused.

review.impact: `TICKET_EVENTS[type]` looks the event type up on a plain object, so inherited names resolve to a handler. A log line with `"type": "__proto__"`, `"hasOwnProperty"` or `"toString"` makes `handler(board, event)` throw a TypeError. That crashes `foldBoard`, `readBoard` and every verb that reads the board, so one bad line, which should only be a problem entry, takes the whole board down. `"constructor"` returns the `Object` function. It returns `board` as the 'violation', so the whole board object is spread into a problem entry. `appendBoardEvent` also takes caller-supplied event types, so the same input reaches it.
review.fix: Make the lookup own-property only. Either build `TICKET_EVENTS` as a `Map` or with `Object.create(null)`, or check `Object.hasOwn(TICKET_EVENTS, type)` before calling the handler. Add a fold test for `type: "__proto__"` and `type: "constructor"`.

review.impact: `actor` in `moved` is cast to `Actor` without checking it. Any value other than `"you"`, such as `"robot"` or a typo, skips the rule that limits a person's moves. The log is written by trusted tooling, so this is low risk. It does weaken the 'person's moves are rules in code' guarantee for hand-edited or malformed events.
review.fix: Accept only `"you" | "agent" | "loop"`. Return `bad-event` for any other value.

review.impact: `build.started` keeps the `log` field as an unchecked string, though it is a session log path (see the `Build.log` doc). A later reader that opens it could be pointed outside the session folder, for example with `../` or an absolute path, by a crafted board log line.
review.fix: Validate `log` as a bare file name, with no separators and no `..`, when the event is folded. Alternatively, have the consumer resolve it under the session directory and reject anything that escapes it.

review.impact: `appendBoardEvent` reads and parses the whole log through `readBoard`, then reads it again with `readText` just to check the trailing newline. Each append costs two full file reads plus a full fold, so the cost grows with the log. The log is append-only and never compacted. This is fine for a CLI at the current scale.
review.fix: Read the text once and pass it to both `parseLog` and the newline check. Alternatively, check the last byte of the file with a small read or `statSync`.

review.impact: `ticket restore` folds the board in the verb to resolve the number, and `appendBoardEvent` folds it again to validate. That is two full log reads and folds per invocation.
review.fix: Have `appendBoardEvent` accept an already-folded board, or expose a helper that resolves and appends from a single read.

review.impact: `leaveReady` rebuilds the whole `readyOrder` array with `filter` on every move out of ready. `reordered` also rebuilds it with a `Set`. Folding N events can therefore be O(N·R), where R is the ready-queue size. This is negligible for realistic board sizes.
review.fix: No change needed now. If the board grows large, use an ordered Set or Map for `readyOrder`.

causeOfLast.why: an earlier pass added the thread output to `renderCard` without a unit test, and the cards say the file needs its own test.

grade.gap: I could not run the tests in this environment. The pure files src/map/ghost-rules.ts and src/map/thread.ts are in src/test/pure-files.ts, and each has its own test file whose cases look like they cover every branch. Nobody has run the coverage gate yet.

The earlier gaps are closed. In src/map/fold.ts, applyEdited now refuses why and body on every card, ghost or real. src/verbs/edit.ts sets who only, and add.ts no longer takes --who. One small item is left: applyProposed in fold.ts still reads an optional `who` field on node.proposed, which no command writes. Remove that read unless another ticket needs it.

review.impact: The doc comment for `applyEvent` ('Checks one event against the map and applies it...') now sits above `applyAccepted`, because the new helpers were inserted between the comment and the function. `applyEvent` has no doc comment, and `applyAccepted` has a wrong one. Readers and the doc-pointer convention are misled.
review.fix: Move the comment back to directly above `export function applyEvent`. Leave `applyAccepted`, `applyDiscarded`, `applyNote` and `applyEdited` uncommented, or give each a one-line comment.

review.impact: The kind check uses a hard-coded list `["card","option","source"]`. The error message builds from `KINDS.slice(0, 3)`, which depends on the order of `KINDS`. The two can drift apart, and a change to `KINDS` would silently change the message. `excerpt` is deliberately excluded, but nothing says why.
review.fix: Define a `const ADDABLE_KINDS = KINDS.filter((k) => k !== "excerpt")`, or export one from fold.ts. Use it for both the check and the message, and add a comment saying that excerpts are not added by hand.

review.impact: `Number(...)` accepts an empty string, whitespace and negative values. `--since ''` is read as 0 and `--since -5` passes. The 'whole numbers' error is therefore not enforced for those inputs.
review.fix: Check each value against `/^\d+$/` before converting it. Also require `since >= 0`.

review.impact: `edit` registers a `--body` flag only so the fold can refuse it. The usage text hides that flag, and the summary says the verb only sets who. The 'frozen' rule is in the fold, but the verb contract is split between the two places.
review.fix: Add a comment saying that `--body` is accepted only so the fold refuses it with the 'frozen' rule. Alternatively, mention it in the usage text.

review.impact: The doc comment for `applyEvent` ('Checks one event against the map and applies it…') now sits above `applyAccepted`. It describes the wrong function, and `applyEvent` has lost its documentation. The new `line` parameter is also undocumented.
review.fix: Move the comment down to directly above `applyEvent`. Mention `line` there, or give `applyAccepted` its own short comment.

review.impact: The kind check hard-codes `["card","option","source"]` and uses `KINDS.slice(0, 3)` in the error message. `KINDS` was just extended with `excerpt`, so two lists must now stay in step, and reordering `KINDS` would silently change the message. The USAGE string repeats the list a third time.
review.fix: Derive a constant such as `ADDABLE_KINDS = KINDS.filter((k) => k !== "excerpt")`. Use it for the check, the error message and the usage text.

review.impact: The `who` parse and validation, including the `must be one of` error text, is duplicated in `applyProposed` and `applyEdited`. The two copies can drift apart.
review.fix: Extract a helper such as `optionalWho(fields): Who | null | Violation` and call it from both.

review.impact: `edit` accepts `--body` only to refuse it later in the fold, and the summary and usage text don't mention it. The 'one at a time' branch also exists mainly to serve that path, which makes the verb harder to follow.
review.fix: Drop the `--body` flag and let `parseArgs` reject it as an unknown flag. If the 'frozen' message is wanted, keep this verb as is but document why.

review.impact: Rewriting `-n` to `--n` by mapping over the raw args is a hack. It would also rewrite a literal `-n` that appears as a flag value.
review.fix: Add short-flag support to `parseArgs`, or document the alias next to the mapping.

review.impact: The `accept` helper takes `...actor: (string | null)[]` and tests `actor[0] === null ? … : actor[0] ?? "you"`. This overloaded variadic is hard to read.
review.fix: Use `accept(id, actor: string | null = "you")`.

review.impact: The test title says it checks 'each note and the marker', but the body only asserts `thread:` and one note. The marker is never covered here.
review.fix: Add a re-proposed case that asserts the `-- proposed again --` marker, or drop 'and the marker' from the title.

review.impact: The test is named "prints a thread with each note and the marker", but it adds one note and never asserts the "-- proposed again --" marker. The card-text test can't catch a `renderCard` that drops the marker from the thread. Only the cli test checks the marker in `show` output, and `thread.test.ts` checks `threadLines` on its own.
review.fix: Add a discard and a second `node.proposed` for the same id, with a second note, to the log. Then assert that `renderCard` output contains "proposed again" between the two notes. Or rename the test to say it covers notes only.

review.impact: `inboxLines` and `threadLines` print note text as written, including newlines. A note whose text has a newline can add a line that looks like another entry, for example `5  x  agent: ...`, or like the proposed-again marker. The inbox is read by people and agents, so a note can mislead them about log positions or authorship. The log itself is unaffected.
review.fix: Collapse newlines and control characters in `entryText` with `text.replace(/\s*[\r\n]+\s*/g, ' ')`. Alternatively, indent continuation lines so they cannot be mistaken for a new entry.

review.impact: For each candidate source, discardGhost builds a new array with `[...map.edges, ...map.ghostEdges]` and scans it. The cost is O(sources × edges) on every discard event. The fold replays the whole log on every verb call, so this repeats for each discard in the log. It only matters for large maps.
review.fix: Build one Set of `supported_by` targets from `map.edges` and `map.ghostEdges` after the edge filtering, and test each source against that set. This makes it a single O(edges) pass.

causeOfLast.why: the earlier pass copied only `src/` into the app copy, though `#werk-test-app-copy` names the configuration and package links, and it left its new naming and data-shape choices off the map.

grade.gap: All six choices flagged last time now have decided cards behind them. #werk-onelock-take-lockfile covers serve.lock and writing port 0 before the server listens. #werk-serve-trust-token-header-name covers x-werk-token and the werk-token meta tag. #werk-stack-api-shape-data covers: the 400 for a graph read without shape=1, the held and proposed flags, the per-card rollup with ghosts left out, {found, card}, and the neighbour direction. Two small things are left, and neither fails the line. First, read-api.ts writes the direction as 'out'/'in', but the card says 'incoming or outgoing'. Second, each neighbour also carries a 'type' field that the shape-data card does not list.

It links each package in node_modules to the checkout's copy, except .vite. Both hot-reload tests in src/serve/serve.test.ts use it. The repository has no client folder yet, so the copy has no client source to include.
