review.impact: The verb rebuilds the rule that no term and no status means the decided index. `searchCards` already holds that rule in `status ?? (terms.length === 0 ? "decided" : null)`. It also filters empty terms in both places. If one copy changes, the output format can stop matching the query that ran.
review.fix: Move the choice into `find-search.ts`. For example, export an `isIndexQuery(query)` helper, or have `searchCards` accept raw terms and the verb ask it whether the query is an index. Keep the empty-term filter in one place.

review.impact: The `.filter(option => option !== undefined && ...)` does not narrow the type. The next `.map` then needs `option?.why ?? ""`, which reads as if the option could still be undefined and hides the intent.
review.fix: Use a type-guard filter, or a `flatMap` that returns `[]` for a missing or proposed option and `[option.why]` otherwise.

review.impact: The unknown-card check `map.nodes.get(id)?.proposed !== false` is copied in `find` and `search`. It also accepts any node kind, including an option, as a known root. Nothing is wrong in practice, because `findOpen` filters the nodes it lists. The copied check is still fragile.
review.fix: Add a shared `isKnownCard(map, id)` helper next to `isRealCard` and use it in both verbs.

review.impact: `find` prints "no open card" when nothing matches, but `search` prints nothing. The two verbs report an empty result differently.
review.fix: Pick one convention for both verbs. If silence is intended for `search`, say so in the usage text or a comment.

review.impact: The new entry sits between `stale-list.ts` and `thread.ts`, which breaks the alphabetical order of the surrounding `src/map` entries. This is cosmetic. It may cause merge churn.
review.fix: Move `src/map/find-search.ts` to its sorted position, ahead of `src/map/reopen-rules.ts` or wherever it belongs alphabetically.

review.impact: The filter does not narrow the type, so the next map needs `option?.why ?? ""`. The optional chaining and fallback hide the fact that undefined was already removed.
review.fix: Use `flatMap` or a type-guard filter, then map `option.why` directly.

review.impact: The code does `status as Status | undefined` after a separate `includes` check. That is a type assertion, and the validation and the type can drift apart. The verb also repeats the empty-term filter and the `terms.length === 0 && status === undefined` default-index rule that `searchCards` already holds. The verb's rule and the function's rule must now be kept in step by hand.
review.fix: Add a `parseStatus(value): Status | null` type guard next to `STATUSES` and use it for both the check and the value. Have `searchCards` or a shared helper decide whether the result is the index, and drop the duplicated term filter in the verb.

review.impact: `find.ts` and `search.ts` each carry the same unknown-card check (`map.nodes.get(id)?.proposed !== false`, then an error and return 1). The `!== false` idiom is cryptic and has to be copied into every new verb that takes an id.
review.fix: Extract a helper such as `isKnownCard(map, id)` in a map module, and use it in both verbs.

review.impact: `subtreeOrder` runs `order.includes` inside a scan of every parent edge for each visited id. That is O(n²) or worse, and it is repeated per root in `findOpen`. Fine for small maps, but it will degrade as the map grows.
review.fix: Build a children index once and use a `Set` for the visited ids.

review.impact: The tests carry noise. `[...open("b", ...)]` spreads for no reason. In the second test, `open("top")`, `x` and `y` are set up but never asserted on.
review.fix: Remove the spread and the unused fixtures.

review.impact: `src/map/find-search.ts` is inserted after `stale-list.ts`, which breaks the alphabetical order of the surrounding entries and makes merge conflicts more likely.
review.fix: Move the entry to its sorted position, before `reopen-rules.ts` or wherever alphabetical order puts it.

review.impact: `renderMatches` is imported by neither the unit test nor any assertion in it. Only the CLI test in `src/verbs/find-search.test.ts` runs it, and #werk-reflink-own-test-coverage counts only a pure file's own test file. The 90% per-file gate on `find-search.ts` could fail or pass by luck. A change to the match line format would also not fail the unit tests.
review.fix: Add a unit test that asserts `renderMatches(...)` output exactly, for example `a  [decided]  Seat price`, including the empty-list case.

review.impact: The test is titled 'paused' but never creates a paused card, so the `marks.length > 0` branch is only covered through stale and postponed. The unused `open('x')` and `open('y')` fixtures add noise. A regression that listed paused cards would pass.
review.fix: Add a paused case, or drop 'paused' from the title. Remove the unused x and y cards.

review.impact: Several branches of `wordsOf` and `findOpen` have no test: a hit in `body`, a proposed (ghost) option whose why-not must be ignored, and `findOpen` with a root that is a ghost or unknown. The ghost-option filter could be removed without any test failing.
review.fix: Add a search case with a ghost option containing a term that must not match, and a case with a term only in `body`.

review.impact: `wordsOf` filters the whole `map.edges` list for every card that `searchCards` visits. A search therefore costs O(cards × edges), and it repeats the scan for cards that a status or subtree filter would already have dropped. The cost grows as the map grows.
review.fix: In `searchCards`, make one pass over `map.edges` to build a `Map<string, string[]>` from the target id to the why-nots of its non-proposed options. Pass that map to `wordsOf`, or look it up there. Lower-casing each card's text once would also avoid repeating that work on every search.

review.impact: `subtreeOrder` scans every entry in `map.parents` for each id it visits, and it uses `order.includes`, a linear scan, for the duplicate check. That makes it O(n²) per call. `findOpen(map, null)` calls it once per root, so the cost adds up on a large map.
review.fix: Build a `Map<parent, children[]>` once, either per call or shared across calls. Track visited ids in a `Set`. Then the walk is O(n).

causeOfLast.why: no decided card gave the event shape, the cause names, or the file layout that the code had to choose.

grade.gap: Closed. The decided card #werk-v0-pipeline-log-event-shape now gives every choice flagged in the earlier grade, and the diff matches it: the step.started/step.ended events with a build id separate from the ticket, a pass number on every step except a plan step, the result green or red, a red step with no gate named by its step kind, the first red step naming the gate of its pass, the cause and reason on the next pass's start event, kebab-case cause names, pipeline.jsonl in the map log's folder, and one detail folder with its own ignore rule and the [A-Za-z0-9._-] name rule. Pass 3 (e43f092) changed no code. The folder name 'pipeline-files' and the field names id/at/ms/cost are configuration. Remaining step: the builder should add #werk-v0-pipeline-log-event-shape to the cards it names, and the code comments in src/pipeline/fold.ts and src/pipeline/log-store.ts could point to it.

review.impact: appendPipelineEvent reads the whole log on every append just to check for a trailing newline. Each append costs O(log size), and a long build log makes every step event slower. The read and the append are also not atomic, so two writers can interleave and glue lines together.
review.fix: Check only the last byte of the file (stat, then read 1 byte), or always write a leading newline guard another way. Keep the append a single appendFileSync call.

review.impact: writeDetailFile sanitizes stepId but not extension. Two step ids that sanitize to the same name, such as 'check/unit test:1' and 'check_unit_test_1', silently overwrite each other's detail file. A caller-supplied extension containing '/' or '..' can write outside the folder.
review.fix: Sanitize the extension with the same regex as stepId. Fail loudly on a name collision, or add a short hash or counter to the name.

review.impact: A step.ended event from a non-pass step with result red leaves the pass 'running'. If the pass-ended event never arrives, the pass is never counted and never becomes `last`, so the retry cap undercounts. This depends on the writer always logging pass end.
review.fix: Document that the pass end is required, or have settle treat a running pass that has a gate as red.

review.impact: The new pipeline entry is inserted between board files, which breaks the list's grouping by folder.
review.fix: Put 'src/pipeline/fold.ts' next to the other new-module entries or at the end of the list.

review.impact: checkPipelineEvent is called from foldPipeline and then the event is cast with `as Rec` and `as number`/`as string`/`as Result` in several places. The validator and the casts can drift apart, because the type system does not link them.
review.fix: Have the validator return a typed event (a type guard or a parsed object) so the fold reads typed fields and needs no casts.

review.impact: applyStarted calls passOf before it checks that the step is `pass`. A started event for a check step creates an empty running pass as a side effect. That is surprising, and the early return placed after it hides it.
review.fix: Return early when `rec.step !== "pass"` before the call to passOf, or document that a started step creates its pass on purpose.

review.impact: The retry loop works around timing flakiness. It can hide a real watcher regression: the test passes if any of five appends signals, and it can take up to 15 seconds to fail.
review.fix: Keep the loop only if the late file event is a known platform behaviour. Otherwise raise the single wait timeout and keep one append.

review.impact: The `writeDetailFile` parameter `extension` is unconstrained and `stepId` is sanitized only by character replacement. Two different step ids, such as `a/b` and `a_b`, map to the same file name and overwrite each other.
review.fix: Add a short hash or the original id to the sanitized name, or document that step ids are unique after sanitizing.

review.impact: The new test appends to the pipeline log once and then waits for the measure signal. The same commit changed the log-watch append test because a single file event can arrive late under load, so this test can fail the same way on a loaded machine. It also never shows the reverse case: that an append to the map log sends no measure signal. A wrong watcher wiring, such as both watchers broadcasting the same event, would pass the changed-signal tests.
review.fix: Retry the append until the signal arrives, as log-watch.test.ts now does, or give `until` a generous time limit. Also assert that the existing map-append test sees `changed` and not `event: measure`.

review.impact: The test is titled as if it covers the fallback to the step name, but only the first red step, `reviewer`, is checked. The second red step, `merge` with gate `merge loop`, only proves that a later gate does not override the first. The rule that the gate is set once and `file` is taken only from the first red step has no direct assertion.
review.fix: Add an assertion that the gate is not overridden. Add a case where the first red step has no `file` and a later one does, and check that `file` stays undefined.

review.impact: The test runs real `git init` and `check-ignore` against a temp directory, so it depends on the user's global git config. It does not cover two step ids that sanitize to the same file name, where one detail file silently overwrites the other. It does not cover a red pass end that carries a `file`.
review.fix: Set `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` in the git spawn environment. Add a test for the collision of sanitized ids, or make `writeDetailFile` avoid it.

review.impact: `writeDetailFile` sanitizes `stepId` but not `extension`. An extension that contains `/` or `..` would write outside the `pipeline-files` folder, and the `.gitignore` rule wouldn't cover that file. Current callers pass fixed strings such as "txt", so this can't be exploited today. It would become exploitable if a later caller passed a derived value.
review.fix: Apply the same `[^A-Za-z0-9._-]` replacement to `extension`, or restrict it to `/^[A-Za-z0-9]+$/` and throw otherwise.

review.impact: `checkPipelineEvent` does not validate the optional `file` field. It is stored as-is and surfaced as `Pass.file` and `LastFailure.file`. A log line with `file: "../../x"` or an absolute path would be passed to any later reader that joins it onto the log folder, which allows path traversal. Nothing in this diff reads the file, so this is only a risk for later code.
review.fix: In `checkPipelineEvent`, require `file`, when present, to be a string that starts with `pipeline-files/` and has no `..` segment and no leading `/`. Alternatively, have the reader resolve the path and check that it stays under the log's `pipeline-files` folder.

review.impact: appendPipelineEvent reads and decodes the whole pipeline log with readText on every append, only to check whether the last byte is a newline. The log gains a line per step start and end, so it grows without bound, and each append costs O(file size). Total write cost over a build is quadratic, and the synchronous read blocks the event loop of whichever process appends.
review.fix: Read only the last byte. Open the file, fstat it, and if size > 0 read 1 byte at size-1 with readSync. Or keep the 'ends with newline' state in memory per path. Then use appendFileSync as now.

causeOfLast.why: an earlier pass put the server lock and the project lock in the same folder when `WERK_LOG` is set, and no test started a server that way.

pass_end.decision: the grader raised #werk-onelock in two passes in a row

grade.gap: Small point, not a failure: with WERK_LOG set, the per-user folder is now <dirname(WERK_LOG)>/server (src/projects/list-store.ts userHome). The 'server' subfolder name and this placement are not written in #werk-onelock or #werk-projects-list. A later card could record them.

Closed. When WERK_LOG is set, userHome returns <dirname(WERK_LOG)>/server, so the server lock is <dir>/server/serve.lock and the project lock is <dir>/serve.lock. They no longer collide. The new serve.test.ts case 'a server with WERK_LOG runs beside a first server...' starts a second server while a first one runs. Two small notes: the test does not check that the log watch follows WERK_LOG (projects.test.ts covers the context logPath), and I could not run the tests here because the command needed approval.

review.impact: This file is a runtime timing log (`at`, `events`, `ms`) written by the tool itself. It was already modified in the working tree at the start of the session, so it is a run artifact. Committing it adds noise and merge conflicts to every later change.
review.fix: Remove the file from the change and add `.werk/fold-ms.jsonl` to `.gitignore`. If the file is meant to be tracked, say so in the map.

review.impact: `start()` is launched with `void start()` and has no error handling. If `/api/projects` fails, returns non-JSON, or is unreachable, the `await fetch(...).json()` throws. That is an unhandled rejection, and the page stays blank with no message. The add-project flow in the same file does report its failures through `say`.
review.fix: Wrap the project-list fetch in `start()` in a try/catch, or use `start().catch((e) => say(String(e)))`. Also check `res.ok` before calling `.json()`.

review.impact: The inline type `{ name: string; missing: boolean }[]` duplicates `ProjectInfo`, which `client/lib/project-route.ts` already exports. The two can drift apart.
review.fix: Import `ProjectInfo` and use it in the cast.

review.impact: The `fetch` dependency passed to the map store also writes to the DOM through `say` when it sees a 409. A UI side effect inside the transport dependency couples the store's I/O to page rendering, and that behaviour is untested.
review.fix: Move the 409 handling into the store, for example as an `onRefused(message)` dependency, or into `show`. Keep `fetch` a plain pass-through.

review.impact: `ensureContext` checks `contexts.get(folder)` and then awaits `openContext`. The code after the await tries to keep the first context when two opens race, but `takeLock` is called twice on the same folder. The second call will probably be refused by the first call's own lock. The racing caller then gets `locked` and `refused.set(folder, ...)` stores a stale refusal, even though the folder is open. The `raced` branch is unlikely to be reached.
review.fix: Track in-flight opens in a `Map<string, Promise<OpenResult>>` and return the pending promise to later callers. Alternatively, check `contexts.get` again before recording a refusal.

review.impact: `addProject` runs `git init` with `Bun.spawnSync` inside an async request path. This blocks the server's event loop, which also serves live connections for every other project.
review.fix: Use async `Bun.spawn` and await `exited`.

review.impact: This is a runtime timing log, and the working tree already shows it modified. It is committed with machine-specific timestamps, so every run dirties the tree and adds merge noise.
review.fix: Remove the file from the commit and add `.werk/fold-ms.jsonl` to .gitignore.

review.impact: The page address `/p/${encodeURIComponent(name)}` is rebuilt by hand. `pageOf` in client/lib/project-route.ts already does this, and e2e/support/server.ts builds the address a third way, with `basename` and no encoding. If the address scheme changes, three places must change together.
review.fix: Move the page-address and API-path helpers to a module that both client and server import, or at least have attach.ts reuse `pageOf`. In the e2e server, encode the name.

review.impact: The inline type `{ name: string; missing: boolean }[]` repeats `ProjectInfo` from project-route.ts. The `start()` function also has no error handling around the `/api/projects` fetch, and `void start()` turns a failure into an unhandled rejection with nothing shown to the person.
review.fix: Use `ProjectInfo[]` for the type. Catch errors in `start()` and report them through `say`.

review.impact: `runningTurns: () => []` and `stopTurns: async () => {}` are placeholders that nothing real implements yet. Only the tests overwrite them. The removal and running-turns logic in projects.ts is therefore effectively dead until the turns are wired in.
review.fix: Wire the real turn tracking in, or mark the stubs with a comment that names the card that will replace them.

review.impact: The rule that WERK_LOG puts the lock beside the log is written twice. `userHome` in list-store.ts uses `dirname(WERK_LOG)/server`, and `openContext` uses `dirname(logPath)/serve.lock`. The two places can drift apart.
review.fix: Keep the lock-path rule in one helper that both call.

review.impact: `(entry as Entry).name` and `names[i] as string` in list.ts are casts that hide a possible undefined. A future change to the listing could throw a TypeError here.
review.fix: Make `listProjects` return the entry that matches the folder, or throw an explicit error when it is missing.

review.impact: A timing log written by a local run (`"events":0`, timestamps from 2026-10-25) was committed as a new file. It is not part of the change and not a test. It will change on every run and produce noise or conflicts. The git status also shows it modified again.
review.fix: Remove it from the commit with `git rm --cached .werk/fold-ms.jsonl`. Add it to .gitignore if the file is a run artefact.

review.impact: `client/lib/add-project.ts` has all its I/O injected through `AddDeps`, so it is pure code. It is not on the PURE_FILES list, so the per-file 90% coverage gate does not check it. A branch of it could go untested without failing the build. For example, nothing tests a thrown or non-JSON response from `/api/projects`, or a 409 whose `error` is not `git-required`.
review.fix: Add `client/lib/add-project.ts` to PURE_FILES. Add cases to add-project.test.ts for a 409 with another error code, a git-required refusal on the init retry, and a body with no `name`.

review.impact: The HTTP layer has no test for removing a project that runs agent turns. That covers the 409 `running` answer and `?confirm=1`. projects.test.ts covers only the registry function, and `server.remove` takes a `confirm` argument that no test passes. The query-string handling in routes.ts is untested. The `locked` project state is also untested over HTTP. The same goes for `attachToRunning` when the running server refuses or does not answer, and for `chooseFolder` when the dialog program exits non-zero or the platform is not macOS.
review.fix: Add an integration test that has a context report running turns, then does DELETE without and with `?confirm=1`. Add tests for the attach failure paths and for a dialog that exits non-zero.

review.impact: The test named 'an address with no project opens the first one' only checks that the URL matches `/p/` and that the map pane is visible. It does not check that the page went to the first listed project, nor that the 'Add project…' button exists. A redirect to the wrong project would pass.
review.fix: Assert that the URL equals `/p/<encoded first project name>`. Assert that the scope text names that project.

review.impact: The attach path takes the port from a lock file. It sends a token request and then a POST with the folder path to whatever listens on that port. A stale lock whose pid was reused, or a lock file that was edited, makes it talk to an unrelated local service. It would send that service the folder path and a token it read from that service's own page. The token is the server's own and is not leaked. The exposure is a local folder path and a confusing failure.
review.fix: Check that the reply from `GET /` carries the werk token meta tag, which the code already does, and also that `/api/projects` answers with a `projects` array before it POSTs. The first check alone does not identify the server.

review.impact: `POST /api/projects` accepts any folder path from the page and stores it. With `init: true` it runs `git init` in that folder. The token and the loopback Host check gate the route, so this is intended behaviour. But the server does not restrict the path, so a script with the token can register and initialise any directory the user can write to.
review.fix: No change is needed if this matches the decided design. As defence in depth, require an absolute path and refuse `init` on a folder that is the home directory or the file system root.

review.impact: Every project-scoped request (`/open`, `/graph`, `/card/*`, `/live`) calls `findEntry`. That calls `entries()`, which reads and parses `projects.json` from disk. It then runs `statSync` on every listed folder and builds a name list. Each page refresh and each `changed` signal pays this synchronous I/O, and the cost grows with the number of projects. `addProject` calls `entries()` again, and `ensureContext` stats the folder a second time. The sync calls block the single server thread.
review.fix: Resolve the name from the in-memory state. Cache the stored folders in `Projects` and update the cache in `addProject` and `removeProject`, which are the only writers. Compute `missing` only for the one entry that is looked up, and run the full `entries()` scan only for `GET /api/projects`.

review.impact: `entries()` calls `readStored` (file read plus JSON parse) and `folderExists` for every project each time it runs. `addProject` and `removeProject` each call it again after already holding the data.
review.fix: Have `addProject` and `removeProject` reuse the stored list they already read. Look up the single entry with `listProjects` instead of building the full `entries` list.

None of the named cards (#werk-projects, #werk-projects-one-process, #werk-write-measure-signal) gives these choices:
(a) Where the per-user list lives, in src/projects/list-store.ts:15-22: WERK_HOME first, then $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/werk or ~/.config/werk. With WERK_LOG set, it is <dirname of WERK_LOG>/server.
(b) The stored list's file and format: projects.json holding {"folders":[...]}, written with a rename. A file that does not parse is refused, never read as empty.
(c) Two locks. One server lock sits in the per-user folder (serverLockPath). Each project folder keeps its own lock in .werk/serve.lock, held by its context.
(d) The addresses: page /p/<encoded name>; project API /api/projects/<name>/{live,open,graph,card/<id>}; GET and POST /api/projects; DELETE /api/projects/<name>?confirm=1; POST /api/projects/dialog.
(e) How a second start reaches the running server, in src/serve/attach.ts: it reads the port from the server lock, waits up to 5 s for a port, takes the token from the page HTML (tokenOf), then posts the folder.
(f) The folder dialog runs on the server through osascript, works on macOS only, and WERK_FOLDER_DIALOG can replace it (src/serve/folder-dialog.ts).
(g) WERK_OPEN names the program that opens the browser (src/serve/open-browser.ts).
(h) The add protocol: a 409 git-required refusal, a retry with init:true after the person agrees, and a 400 not-a-folder refusal.
(i) A folder is stored under its real path, so a link is resolved first.
(j) A locked state for a project that another server holds.
(k) The naming rule for a third clash (the whole parent path) and the dev entry listed first.
(l) Removing the dev entry answers 403; removing a project with running turns answers 409.
(m) The root address redirects to the first project that can open.
Propose a card for each of these, or for a group of them, for example #werk-projects-address and #werk-projects-list-store.

In src/projects/names.ts:14-27, a third folder with the same name gets its whole parent path in brackets, for example 'api (/c/work)'. The card allows only the parent folder name. In src/projects/list.ts:52-63, listProjects puts the dev checkout first, then names the folders in list order. So a stored project whose folder name matches the checkout's gets a different name in dev mode than outside it. The card says the later project gets the brackets, and the dev entry can be later than the stored one. Either name each project by the order it was added, or record the dev-first ordering in a card.

review.impact: `sourceFile` is pure, but it sits in the same file as the hook's spawn and exit code. This repo moves pure code into its own file, as `subagent-links.ts` does beside `check-subagent-links.ts`. Here the pure logic cannot join the pure-file coverage list on its own. The file's own test also needs a real biome subprocess to cover the I/O path.
review.fix: Move `sourceFile` and `SOURCE` into a small pure module, for example `src/claude/hook-input.ts`, with its own test. Keep `lint-hook.ts` as the thin I/O entry point.

review.impact: A blank line follows the opening `---` in both definition files. The header is odd, and `parseDefinition` only copes because it stores a harmless empty-key entry. Each file also has a `name:` field that `parseDefinition` ignores, since the name comes from the `SHIPPED_SUBAGENTS` key. The file name, the key and the `name:` field can drift apart without any check catching it.
review.fix: Remove the blank line after `---` in both .md files. In `parseDefinition`, skip lines that have no colon. Optionally assert in `subagentDefinitions` that the `name:` field matches the key.

review.impact: The error 'A subagent definition needs a header.' does not say which definition is malformed. A bad file therefore fails at module-use time with no pointer to the cause.
review.fix: Give `parseDefinition` the subagent name and include it in the error message.

review.impact: Both definition files have a blank line right after the opening `---`, and test-scope.md has the same one. `parseDefinition` copes with it only by accident. The empty first line has no colon, so `indexOf` returns -1 and the parser stores a junk entry under the key "". The same blank line may also make Claude Code reject the front matter when it reads these files through the `.claude/agents` symlinks. That would make the one shared definition unreliable for its second reader.
review.fix: Delete the blank line after the opening `---` in both .md files. Make `parseDefinition` skip lines that have no colon, for example `if (colon < 0) continue;`, so a bad line cannot add a bogus key.

review.impact: The test 'a log that does not exist yet signals when it appears' now appends to the log again each time it polls, until a signal arrives. Those appends are ordinary growth of an existing file. They can trigger the signal even if the watcher never noticed that the file was created. The test therefore no longer proves that a late-created log is detected, and a regression in appearance detection would pass.
review.fix: Keep the single write that creates the file. Raise the wait timeout or retry only the creation, for example delete and recreate the file. Alternatively, assert that the first signal arrives with no append after creation, and tolerate slow events with a longer timeout.

review.impact: `parseDefinition` and `SHIPPED_SUBAGENTS` are new pure logic with no direct test. The only test that touches them is the existing prompt-substitution test in launch-options.test.ts. Nothing checks that `description` and `tools` are parsed, that the output matches the old definitions, or that a file with no header throws. Both shipped .md files have a blank line after the opening `---`. That line is parsed as an empty-key field and ignored, and the files may not be valid frontmatter for Claude Code, which reads them through the symlinks. No test would catch a broken header or a field that was dropped.
review.fix: Add subagents.test.ts. It should check that `parseDefinition` returns the expected description, tools array and prompt for a sample file, that it throws without a header, and that every shipped definition has a non-empty description and tools. Remove the blank line after `---` in both .md files and assert that the first line of the header is `name:`.

review.impact: The CLI entry (`import.meta.main`) is never exercised, so no test shows that a missing or copied link produces a non-zero exit and the `werk:` message. The tests cover only `readEntries` and `subagentLinkFailures` separately. The lint-hook test file already spawns its script, so the two files are inconsistent.
review.fix: Add one test that spawns `bun src/claude/check-subagent-links.ts <tmp repo>` against a temp repo with a bad entry and asserts exit 1 and the stderr line. Add a second spawn against a good repo that asserts exit 0.

review.impact: The hook tests run the real `bunx biome` and create temp directories inside the repository root. If the process is killed mid-test, a `.hook-test-*` directory is left behind and the repo-wide lint then sees it. The 30-second timeouts are fixed and ignore the shared parallel load. There is also no test that a non-source path produces no spawn and exit 0.
review.fix: Create the temp directory outside the repo, or add `.hook-test-*` to .gitignore and the Biome ignore list. Add a process-level test for a `.md` path that expects exit 0 and empty stderr.

review.impact: `replaceAll` with a string replacement reads `$&`, `$'`, `$1` and `$$` as special patterns. The old template literal did not. If the werk path has a `$` in it, such as a directory named `a$&b`, the prompt gets a mangled command path. The prompt is the agent's instructions, so a wrong path there breaks the subagent's `werk` calls.
review.fix: Pass a replacer function, which skips pattern expansion: `.replaceAll("`werk ", () => `\`${werk} `)`.

review.impact: Every project-scoped request (/open, /graph, /card, /live) calls findEntry, which calls entries(). That reads and parses projects.json from disk. Either cache the stored list in the Projects object and invalidate it in addProject and removeProject, or look the name up in listProjects output and stat only the matching folder. Let ensureContext be the only place that checks the folder exists.

review.impact: `load()` replays the server's kept events through `receive` on every channel `open`, and live events can arrive while it runs. A streaming `tool_use` delta appends its text to the existing input, so a delta delivered both live and by the replay doubles the streamed JSON. A replayed `turn-start` also stamps `startedAt` with `deps.now()`, so the seconds counter in the header restarts after each reconnect.
review.fix: Make replay idempotent. Have the server events carry the original timestamp for `turn-start`. For deltas, either replace the item's state when replaying, or apply no live events until `load()` has finished and drop events the load already covered.

review.impact: `receive` casts parsed JSON straight to `Action` with `as unknown as Action`. A malformed `chat` or `status` body that has a `turn` but lacks `block` or `id` reaches `reduce` and throws inside the SSE listener. For a `chat` event with no `block`, that happens on `const { block } = action; block.kind`.
review.fix: Check the required fields for each event type before calling `apply`, and ignore the event if a check fails, as already done for `turn`.

review.impact: The map store imports `CHAT_EVENTS` from `chat-store`, which ties the map module to the chat module just to register listeners. The chat event list lives in the chat module, but the map store has to know about every chat event name.
review.fix: Pass one generic hook, such as `events?: Record<string, (data: string) => void>`, in `MapStoreDeps`. Let `main.tsx` build it from `CHAT_EVENTS`, so `map-store` has no dependency on chat.

review.impact: `headOf` runs twice per render. The first call exists only to read `busy`, and it uses a `now` value that can be stale. When a turn starts, the effect and the displayed seconds lag by one render.
review.fix: Compute `head` once and derive `busy` from it. The effect can depend on `head.busy`.

review.impact: `headOf` runs twice per render, once to read `busy` for the effect and once for the view. The two calls can disagree if `now` changes between them, and the reader has to work out why.
review.fix: Compute `const head = headOf(state, now)` once, then use `head.busy` as the effect dependency.

review.impact: The `delta` and `chat` reducer cases each build an Item with near-identical tool_use and text/thinking branches. Each case repeats the `waiting: false` and `upsert` tail. A new Item field has to be added in four places.
review.fix: Extract helpers such as `toolItem(id, fields, have)` and `textItem(...)`, or a `withItem(t, item)` that clears `waiting` and upserts.

review.impact: `receive` casts the parsed body with `as unknown as Action` for turn-end, delta, chat and status. These casts skip type checking on server data. A malformed field such as a non-string `id` reaches the reducer unchecked.
review.fix: Add a small runtime check of the fields each action needs, or a typed parser per event. Then drop the double casts.

review.impact: `Composer` is rendered with no `onSend` when no project is open, so Enter silently does nothing. `onSend` is also optional on `Composer` only to support this case. The `chatReact?.render` calls are duplicated.

review.impact: The store has no unit test. It parses channel data and drops bad JSON or a missing turn. It maps events to actions. It replays server history in `load()`. In `send()` it turns a refusal, a non-JSON body, or a thrown fetch into an error turn-end. It sends the token header and the open card. A regression in any of these shows up only in e2e, and none of the failure paths is covered there.
review.fix: Add client/lib/chat-store.test.ts with a fake `fetch`. Cover malformed JSON, no `turn`, and `turn-start` taking `now()`. Cover `load()` on a non-ok response and on replayed events. Cover `send()` on 403 with a message, on a non-JSON error body, and on a thrown fetch. Check the POST headers and body, and that `subscribe` unsubscribes.

review.impact: The Enter handling is new and untested at unit level. composer.test.tsx was not changed. Nothing checks that Shift+Enter does not send. Nothing checks that Enter with no `onSend` does not throw. Only the happy path of Enter is covered, by e2e.

review.impact: The new wiring has no test: `connected` on each open, and forwarding of each CHAT_EVENTS event with `String(event.data ?? "")`. The existing tests only had their signatures adjusted. If the `chat` or `connected` dep is dropped, the late-join history and live chat break silently.
review.fix: Add map-store tests that emit a chat event with data and expect `deps.chat(type, data)`. Also emit one with no data and expect an empty string, and expect `connected` to be called on open.

review.impact: `ChatPane` re-renders `ChatLog` on every state change, and the stream sends one `delta` per token chunk. `Block` and `TurnView` are not memoized. So each delta runs `renderMarkdown` again for every text block of every turn, and it rebuilds `JSON.stringify` input text for every tool call. The work per delta grows with the whole conversation, so a long chat gets slow while the reply streams. The reducer keeps object identity for turns and items that did not change, so memoizing would work.
review.fix: Wrap `Block`, `TurnView` and `ToolRun` in `React.memo`, so only the streaming turn and block re-render. Also `useMemo` the rendered HTML on `item.text`.

review.impact: `within` and `upsert` do a linear scan plus a full `map` of the turns and items on every action. Replaying the kept events in `chat-store.load()` on each reconnect therefore costs O(n²) in the number of events. The replay also re-applies events the page already holds. For a long conversation this is a noticeable pause on every reconnect.
review.fix: In `load`, skip events that are already applied, or fold the whole batch into the state and notify listeners once. In the reducer, update only the last or matching turn without remapping the others.

grade.gap:
The diff makes these choices, and none of the named cards (#vi-onview, #vi-onview-hero, #werk-card-blind) gives them. (1) The address for reading a named card's page is GET /api/projects/

/open?card=, with a query parameter named card (src/serve/routes.ts, client/lib/map-store.ts). (2) The page has a 'Why this card is postponed' section that prints the traces of paused and postponed marks (card-page.ts traces()). No card asks for it, because #vi-onview-stale covers only stale marks. (3) The Rollup type gets new fields, paused and pausedBy, and paused counts the postponed card together with every card it pauses (src/map/rollup.ts). (4) An unknown id returns a 200 response whose OpenCard has the asked-for id and a 'The map has no card X.' article, not a 404 or { id: null } (open-card.ts). (5) Section headings for the page are 'Evidence and excerpts', 'Sub-cards N', and an excerpt row labelled by its kind. Propose a card for each of these, or name the cards that already give them.

rollupLine (src/serve/rollup-html.ts) puts unchallenged, stale and paused in the same line as the status dots. #vi-counts-card asks for this, and the hollow ring keeps those numbers apart from the dots, so the line passes. The chips stay separate as #ro-axes requires.

The count line in src/serve/rollup-html.ts rollupLine prints the word 'paused' ('1 paused'). #pr-wf-naming says every place the map names this state reads 'postponed', and the tag and the trace heading in card-page.ts already say 'postponed'. But #vi-counts-card lists 'paused' as the word that follows a ring number, so the two decided cards conflict. A person must decide which word the count line uses for this ring: 'paused' (#vi-counts-card) or 'postponed' (#pr-wf-naming).

Stale must win where the kind is shown (#pr-wf-paused, and the comment above addMark in src/map/mark-rules.ts). A card that carries both a stale and a paused mark still shows the postponed state: (1) card-look.ts cardClasses adds is-postponed next to is-stale, so the box is both striped and tinted red; (2) card-page.ts tagRow adds the postponed tag next to the stale tag; (3) map/rollup.ts counts the card in paused and pausedBy as well as stale, so the parent's bar hatches it and the line counts it as paused. When a stale mark is present, show it only as stale. Add a test where a card is both stale and paused.

review.impact: `buildRelease` runs `rmSync(options.out, { recursive: true, force: true })` on whatever folder the command line gives it. `bun src/release/build.ts ~/Documents`, or a mistyped path, deletes that whole folder with no check. The make target uses a safe default, but the argument is open to any path.
review.fix: Delete only the files the build writes: the executables, their `.sha256` files, `entry.ts` and `own-files.json`. Or refuse to run when the output folder exists and is non-empty, unless it is the default `dist/release`.

review.impact: `clientOut` is hard-coded as `dist/client`. It silently duplicates the `build.outDir` in `vite.config.ts`. If the Vite output folder changes, `filesUnder` reads a missing or stale folder and the executable embeds the wrong client, or `readdirSync` throws.
review.fix: Read the output folder from the same constant or resolved Vite config that the client build uses. Or pass `build: { outDir: clientOut }` to `viteBuild` so the build owns it.

review.impact: In a checkout, `werkCommand` returns the single string `${execPath} ${entry}`. A Bun or checkout path that contains spaces gives a command that cannot be pasted or run from the agent prompts.
review.fix: Quote each part when it contains whitespace. Or have `werkCommand` return an argv array and join it only where the prompt text is built.

review.impact: `files["/index.html"] as string` casts away the case where the list has no index. `Bun.file(undefined)` then throws an unhelpful error on every page request.

review.impact: The build function always writes to dist/client via Vite, but clientOut is hardcoded to join(REPO,'dist','client') separately from the Vite config's outDir. If the config changes, the two silently diverge and the build embeds stale or missing files. The Vite build also mutates a shared folder on every call, including from the test.
review.fix: Read the output folder from the Vite config or pass build.outDir explicitly to viteBuild so there is one source of the path.

review.impact: `files["/index.html"] as string` is a type assertion that hides a missing index. If the embedded list lacks it, Bun.file(undefined) fails with an obscure error at request time.

review.impact: `buildRelease` runs Vite with the repo's own config. Vite writes to the checkout's shared `dist/client`, not to the test's temp folder. Only `out` is private. review.fix: Check `await Bun.file(path).exists()` and return null when the file is missing, or let the caller turn the failure into a 404.

review.impact: A runtime timing log is committed, and each test or build run appends lines to it. This adds noise to the diff and invites merge conflicts.
review.fix: Revert these two lines and keep the file out of the commit, for example by adding it to .gitignore.

review.impact: `OwnList.subagents` is collected in build.ts and written to own-files.json, but entrySource never uses it. The own-files.json written beside the executables is also never read. Both are dead data that look meaningful.
review.fix: Drop `subagents` from OwnList and the build, or embed and register the files. If own-files.json is only a build record, say so in a comment.

review.impact: `verbNamesOf(dir)` is exported but only `verbNames` calls it. The same rule (a .ts file that is not a .test.ts file) is repeated in e2e/release.spec.ts and src/cli/registry.test.ts.
review.fix: Inline `verbNamesOf` and un-export it. Have the tests compare against the same helper, or keep the repeats as an independent check and note that in a comment.

review.impact: The platform list is hard-coded here and again in src/release/build.ts, so the two can drift apart.
review.fix: Import `PLATFORMS` from src/release/build.ts and derive the suffixes from it.

review.impact: The folder-listing guard is a regex scan of source text with a hand-kept skip list of directories and one file name. It is fragile, and it will either flag harmless text such as comments or miss other ways of listing a folder.
review.fix: Narrow the scan to specific known call sites, or document why each skip entry is needed. Strip comments before matching.

review.impact: The embedded-client test uses `own.ts` as the page and only checks status codes. It never checks that `page('tok')` puts the token into the HTML, or that `asset()` returns the file's bytes. If `injectToken` were dropped from `embeddedClient.page`, the test would still pass. A release executable with no token would then fail to authenticate in the browser.
review.fix: Use a temp `index.html` fixture that holds the placeholder `injectToken` replaces. Assert the response body contains the token and that the content-type is text/html. For the asset, assert the body equals the file's contents.

review.impact: The test cross-compiles four platforms in one test with a 120s limit. A Bun cross-target compile may download runtime binaries, so a cold cache or no network makes it flaky or reaches an external service. It also runs `vite build` into the checkout's `dist/client`, not a copy.
review.fix: Build only the host target in the e2e test, for example by letting `build` take a platform filter. Cover the four-platform list with a unit test, or raise the timeout and warm the cache. Build the client into a temp folder.

review.impact: The new executable-mode branches have no direct test. These are: no `--hot` child when `isExecutable()`, `dev` forced off in an executable, and `runHot` building its command from `selfCommand`. Only the slow e2e test touches them, and only for the happy path. A regression that spawns `--hot` from an executable would go unnoticed until release.
review.fix: Add a unit test that registers own files and checks `serve` runs in-process. Alternatively, extract the 'run hot?' decision into a pure function and test it.

review.impact: The folder-listing guard skips whole directories (`verbs`, `claude`, `test`, `test-env`, `release`), so a violation in any of them is invisible. It also scans only `.ts`/`.tsx` source text with a regex, so an aliased or wrapped `readdir` call is missed. The guard is weaker than its name says.
review.fix: Narrow the skip list to the specific files that legitimately list folders, with a comment for each. Keep the other directories under the scan.

review.impact: `stillLoaded` now turns any evaluate error into 'reloaded' (`false`), so an unrelated page crash or closed page reads as a reload. This loosens the test it serves.
review.fix: Catch only the 'Execution context was destroyed' error and rethrow everything else.

review.impact: selfCommandLine wraps each part in double quotes without escaping. An executable path that holds a double quote, `$`, a backtick or a backslash would be changed by the shell, or could run a command, when the line is used in a shell or an agent prompt. The code it replaced in chat-route.ts did the same, and the path is the user's own install location, so the risk is small. The release executable can now be installed anywhere, which makes odd paths more likely.
review.fix: Escape `\`, `"`, `$` and the backtick inside each part before quoting it. Alternatively, single-quote each part and replace each `'` with `'\''`.

grade.gap: Small extra: in AskBar (client/app/ask-bar.tsx, onKey), Ctrl+Enter answers the first ask the same way Cmd+Enter does. No criterion or card asks for Ctrl+Enter; #werk-approve-bar names only Cmd+Enter and Escape. Either remove it or keep it as the platform equivalent.

The card says the writer is appendAsk() in src/permission.ts. The diff puts appendAsk() in src/chat/permission-store.ts, and src/chat/permission.ts is a separate pure file. Move appendAsk to the place the card names, or have the card updated to point at src/chat/permission-store.ts. The fields (at, tool, label, input, reason, decision, widened) and the append-only writing match the card.

review.impact: In `answer()`, the ask is deleted and the reply written to the child before `appendAsk` and `keepAllow` run, and `ask-done` is emitted last. If either file write throws (full disk, permissions) the route returns a 500, and no `ask-done` is ever emitted. The child has already got its answer. The page's `answer` then re-enables the bar for an ask the server no longer holds. A retry gets 409, which the client treats as 'ask-done follows', so the bar stays stuck with `sending: true` until the child exits. A `stdin.write` on a closed pipe can also throw, after which the ask is still open but the client has no way to tell.
review.fix: Emit `ask-done` right after `asks.delete`. Wrap `appendAsk` and `keepAllow` in try/catch so a failed log write never undoes the answer. Report that failure some other way, or ignore it. Also guard the `stdin.write` so a failure returns `{ok:false}` before the ask is removed.

review.impact: A 409 returns without clearing `sending`, and the code relies on a later `ask-done`. Nothing guarantees that event arrives, for example when the stream has dropped. The bar then stays disabled permanently. The 400 path does re-enable it, which is inconsistent.
review.fix: On a 409, apply `ask-done` locally for that id. The reducer already ignores duplicates, so this is safe.

review.impact: The route tells 409 from 400 by comparing the reason string `"no such open ask"`, which is defined in session.ts. Changing that wording silently turns 409s into 400s.
review.fix: Have `ChatSession.answer` return a typed code, such as `{ok:false, code:'closed'|'invalid', reason}`, and map the status from that.

review.impact: The `ask` event's `turn` is set to `queue.active?.turn ?? ""`. If no turn is active, the client receives an empty turn string. The client's `receive` for `ask` does not check it, but the `PendingAsk.turn` field is then meaningless.
review.fix: Drop the field if nothing reads it, or skip or flag asks that arrive with no active turn.

review.impact: `suggestionLabels` and `allowFlags` both repeat `Array.isArray(update.rules) ? update.rules : []`. They also each split `addRules` and `addDirectories` handling separately. A new update type has to be added in two places.
review.fix: Add a small `rulesOf(update)` helper next to `directories()` and use it in both functions.

review.impact: The keyboard handler repeats the decision-to-answer mapping that the buttons in `Permission` and `QuestionForm` already encode. It also types the answer with `Parameters<ChatStore["answer"]>[1] | null`, although `AskAnswer` is already exported. The two paths can drift apart.
review.fix: Import `AskAnswer` from chat-store and use it as the type. Optionally pull the allow/deny/answer mapping into one shared function that the buttons and the key handler both call.

review.impact: `selections[qi] as Selection` is a cast that hides a possible `undefined`. It is safe only because `pickedOf` always fills every slot.
review.fix: Use `selections[qi] ?? noSelection` (export the constant), or map over `selections` directly.

review.impact: `body as Extract<Action, { type: "ask" }>["ask"]` casts untrusted JSON to the ask type without any check. The client `PendingAsk` question shape is also a second hand-written copy of the server `Question` type, so the two can drift.
review.fix: Add a small guard that checks the required fields before applying the ask. Alternatively, name the shape once as a client `AskQuestion` type and reference it from `PendingAsk`.

review.impact: `const { [action.id]: _gone, ...selections }` creates an unused binding. It depends on the linter's underscore exemption and is harder to read than needed.
review.fix: Copy the object and `delete` the key, or build the result with `Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(...).filter(...))`.

review.impact: The new `answer()` has three failure branches, and no test runs them. A 409 stays disabled and leaves the close to ask-done. A non-ok response or a thrown fetch re-enables the buttons. Dropping the re-enable would leave an ask stuck with every button disabled, and no test would fail. The `ask` and `ask-done` event parsing in `receive()` is also untested, including a body with no string id.
review.fix: Add a `chat-store` test with a fake `deps.fetch`. Cover: 200 and 409 leave `sending` true; 500 and a rejected fetch reset `sending` to false. Check the POST body and the `x-werk-token` header. Feed `receive` an `ask` event and an `ask-done` event, and one with a non-string id.

review.impact: The keyboard handler has branches that no test reaches. Escape on a question form should send decline. Cmd+Enter on a form with no picks should send nothing, yet still swallow the key. The Ctrl+Enter variant is untested. While `sending` is true, the handler should not fire, and that is untested too. The 'a' keypress in the existing test adds nothing, because the final answers check cannot tell it apart from no keypress.
review.fix: Add cases for Escape on a question form (expect decline), Cmd+Enter with empty picks (expect no answer and `defaultPrevented`), Ctrl+Enter, and a key press while `sending` is true (expect no answer).

review.impact: Stored Always-allow rules are joined into the comma-separated `--allowedTools` value with no escaping. A stored rule whose content contains a comma, such as `Bash(echo a,b:*)`, is split by the CLI into fragments. The rule then fails to match what the person approved, or becomes a different, broader entry such as a bare `Bash(echo a`.
review.fix: In `allowFlags`, skip any rule text that contains a comma. Alternatively pass each stored rule as its own `--allowedTools` argument, if the CLI accepts repeated flags.

review.impact: The keydown effect depends on `state`, which changes on every streamed delta. While an ask is open, the window listener is removed and re-added on each state update. The cost is small but it is churn.
review.fix: Keep the latest `state` in a ref and drop it from the dependency array. The effect would then depend only on `first` and `store`.

review.impact: `keepAllow` reads, parses, re-stringifies and rewrites the whole allow file with synchronous I/O on the server's answer path. Each Always allow does this, and `JSON.stringify` runs once per stored update to deduplicate. The file only grows by a few updates per answer, so this is cheap in practice.
review.fix: No change needed now. If the stored list grows large, cache it in memory in the session and write it asynchronously.

review.impact: The header index fetch and the card fetch share one Promise.all. If the /index request rejects (network error), the catch swallows it and the card page is never shown, even though /open succeeded. The header is an add-on, so its failure should not block the card.
review.fix: Catch the index fetch on its own (`deps.fetch(...).catch(() => null)`), or fetch it separately, so a failure there still lets `deps.show(view)` run.

review.impact: `recall` guards against a broken store, but `remember` calls `storage.setItem` with no guard. It throws when storage is full or disabled. `remember` is called from `route()` in main.tsx before `store.open`, so one throw stops the page from routing or rendering the card.
review.fix: Wrap `setItem` in try/catch inside `remember` and ignore the failure, to match the damaged-value handling in `recall`.

review.impact: `start()` now holds the routing, the view state, the header roots, the render logic and the board placeholder markup. That cuts against the small single-purpose modules rule, and it makes the header and routing behaviour hard to test apart from the page.
review.fix: Move the header wiring (roots and `renderHeader`) and the routing (`go` and `route`) into their own client modules. Move the board placeholder into a component.

review.impact: `HeaderIndex` is defined twice, here and in src/serve/read-api.ts, and the client types `kind` as a bare `string`. The client and server shapes can drift with no compile-time check, and `dotOf` casts `row.kind` to a narrow union.
review.fix: Share one type between the server and the client, or at least type `kind` as the union and drop the cast in `dotOf`.

review.impact: HeaderIndex is defined twice: once in client/lib/map-store.ts and once in src/serve/read-api.ts (with HeaderEntry). The client copy is a hand-written mirror of the server shape, using CountRollup and SearchRow. If the server shape changes, the client type will not fail to compile. The client also has separate Rollup/CountRollup and SearchRow/HeaderEntry types.
review.fix: Have the client import the server's type, or derive one from the other, so a change to the server shape fails the typecheck. If the client cannot import from src/, keep one documented copy.

review.impact: The board placeholder HTML is hard-coded inline inside route(). start() is now a long function that mixes header rendering, routing and history handling. Replacing the placeholder will mean editing this tangled closure. The #werk-stack-modules rule asks for single-purpose, small modules.
review.fix: Move the header wiring (the three roots, renderHeader and the ResizeObserver) and the route/view logic into their own modules. Move the board placeholder into a named constant or a component.

review.impact: The 'index' variable is assigned and read only through renderHeader. 'view' and 'openId' are mutable closure state that route(), show() and renderHeader() all touch. The implicit ordering is easy to break. For example, show() silently returns when view is not 'map', and the index and show callbacks both call renderHeader.
review.fix: Group this state in one small object or store with a single render function, so the update order is explicit.

review.impact: dotOf casts row.kind as a union of 'option' | 'source' | 'excerpt' even though kind is typed as string. An unexpected kind such as 'card' with a null status would produce a data-color with no CSS rule, and the dot would be invisible. The test casts the same way.
review.fix: Type SearchRow.kind as a union of node kinds. Otherwise narrow it in dotOf and fall back to a known color.

review.impact: JSON.parse returns any, so value.view and value.card are read untyped. The try/catch also swallows every error, including a setItem failure in a different path. remember() calls recall() and then writes without a guard, so a storage failure such as quota or private mode throws from route().
review.fix: Parse into unknown and narrow it. Wrap the setItem call in a try/catch, or document that it may throw.

review.impact: The Escape and selection reset logic (setTyped(''), setSelected(0)) appears three times (open, Escape, onChange). The onKeyDown handler is a long if/else chain inside JSX.
review.fix: Extract a reset() helper and move the key handling into a named function.

review.impact: The status colors (#f59e0b, #3b82f6, #22c55e, #ef4444, #a855f7, #9ca3af) are declared twice, once for [data-kind] and once for [data-slot=dot][data-color]. A palette change must be made in both places. [data-kind='open'] is also an unscoped global selector.
review.fix: Define the colors once as CSS custom properties, such as --status-open, and have both selector sets refer to them.

review.impact: The new test waits with `Bun.sleep(20)`, which is a timing guess and can flake on a loaded parallel worker. The neighbouring tests use `t.settled()`. The new refresh logic also has no test for the failure paths. These are an index fetch that returns not-ok or throws, so the card still has to show without the index. They are also a stale read superseded by a newer one, where the older index must not be handed over. A regression in either path would pass.
review.fix: Replace the sleep with the existing settled helper, or await the show call. Add two tests. In one, the index response has `ok: false`, and `show` is still called while `index` is not. In the other, two overlapping `open` calls resolve out of order, and only the latest result triggers `index` and `show`.

review.impact: The `headerRead` test only covers plain open cards. Nothing exercises `stale: true`, `postponed: true`, or a non-card node. An option, source or excerpt must get `status: null`. Breaking the `node.kind === "card"` check or the stale and postponed mapping would go unnoticed. The `/index` route also has no test of its own.
review.fix: Add a stale mark, a postponed card and an option to the fixture. Assert their `stale`, `postponed` and `status: null` values. Add a route test for `GET /api/projects/:p/index`.

review.impact: Three behaviours are untested: the old `/#id` redirect, a bare project address opening the remembered view and card, and the Board placeholder with its `popstate` routing. The e2e tests cover only the Board tab and the Back button.
review.fix: Add e2e cases. One visits `/#seats` and expects `/map/seats`. One opens a card, visits the bare project address and expects the remembered card. One checks that Back from the board restores the card.

review.impact: The new view routing tests miss some edges: a trailing slash on `/p/x/board/`, a project name that contains `board`, and a card page `/p/x/map/board`. `viewPageOf(project, "board", card)` silently drops the card, and no test pins that.
review.fix: Add assertions for `viewOf("/p/werk/board/")`, `viewOf("/p/board/map/x")` and the card-ignored case.

review.impact: The tests never give `proto` or `stale` a nonzero value. The ring order (unchallenged, stale, postponed) and the stale title are therefore unverified.
review.fix: Add a rollup with all counts nonzero and assert the full order and titles.

review.impact: The search e2e test never exercises ArrowUp, ArrowDown or wrap-around selection, nor a mouse click on a result. That keyboard logic in `SearchBox` is untested.
review.fix: Fill a query with several matches. Press ArrowDown and ArrowUp, assert which `li` has `aria-current`, then press Enter and check the URL.

review.impact: Every refresh also fetches /index, and refresh runs on every card open, every popstate and every live signal. The index is the whole map: one row per node plus the rollup of every card. The server rebuilds it with `readMap` plus `rollups(map)` on each request. `/open` reads and folds the log too, so each navigation folds the log twice and sends a payload that grows with the map, even though the index only changes when the map changes. Each fetch also delays `show`, because the card waits for both responses through `Promise.all`.
review.fix: Fetch the index only on connect and on a live map-change signal, not on every card navigation. Or cache it in the store and refetch only when a signal arrives. Or send an ETag from `/index` so unchanged reads are cheap. Do not make the card HTML wait for the index.

review.impact: The ResizeObserver calls `renderHeader` on every resize notification. A drag-resize of the pane fires this per frame. Each call runs `pathTo`, which builds a Map of all rows, then `countsOf`, then re-renders three React roots including the SearchBox, which re-runs `search`. The work is O(n) in map size per frame, though only the crumb layout depends on the width.
review.fix: Re-render only when the derived room, `paneWidth >= WIDE_PANE`, changes. Alternatively compute `pathTo` once per `openId` or `index` change and reuse it, and render only the Crumbs root from the observer.

review.impact: `search` runs on every render of SearchBox, including arrow-key selection changes. Each run lowercases id, title and why for every row, three allocations per row, before it slices to 12. The cost is linear in map size per keystroke and per arrow press.
review.fix: Wrap the call in `useMemo` keyed on `[rows, typed]`. Optionally precompute lowercased fields once per index load, and stop filtering once `LIMIT` rows match in the non-hash branch.

causeOfLast.why: an earlier pass left `e2e/chat.spec.ts` unformatted, and the cards were clear enough to get it right.

grade.gap: Drag-and-drop upload (client/app/composer.tsx onDragOver/onDrop) is not in any acceptance criterion or in user story 62, which asks only for paste. It is allowed only because #werk-shots, which the story cites, names dragging. If the next pass wants the slice limited to paste, this is the one extra behaviour to remove.

The card says to drag an image 'onto the pane', but client/app/composer.tsx attaches onDragOver/onDrop to the Textarea only. An image dropped elsewhere on the chat pane is not taken. Move the drop handlers to the pane or the composer wrapper (the data-slot=composer div or ChatPane), or remove drag from this slice.

review.impact: `settle` sends every ready image, whether or not its `[Image #N]` token is still in the text. If someone deletes a token by hand, the agent gets a header that maps a token the message doesn't mention. The `[Image #N]` numbers can also fall out of step with the chips.
review.fix: In `settle`, drop any chip whose token is missing from the text and renumber the rest. Or only send images whose token is still present.

review.impact: `typeOfName` re-declares the ext/type table that `imageKind` already hard-codes. Adding a format means editing two places, and they can drift apart.
review.fix: Define one `KINDS` table and derive both `imageKind` and `typeOfName` from it.

review.impact: `storeImage` reads the whole body with `arrayBuffer()` before checking the size when there is no content-length, for example with chunked uploads. A large body is therefore buffered in memory first. `mkdirSync` and `writeFileSync` failures also throw instead of returning the JSON refusal the chip expects.
review.fix: Cap the stream while reading it. Wrap the filesystem writes in try/catch and return a 500 refusal with a message.

review.impact: A `biome-ignore` suppresses `useExhaustiveDependencies` on the effect that sends after the last upload. The effect calls `send`, which closes over `text` and `chips`. It works only because `chips` is in the dependency list. A later edit to `send` could make it use stale state without any warning. The waiting-then-send flow (a `waiting` state plus an effect) is also more complex than it needs to be.
review.fix: Remove the suppression. Either make `send` stable (for example through a ref to the latest text and chips), or drop the effect and call `send` from the upload-completion handler when `waiting` is set and no uploads remain.

review.impact: `typeOfName` repeats the ext-to-type table that `imageKind` hard-codes (png, jpg, gif and webp, with the same MIME types). Adding a format means editing two places, and they can drift apart.
review.fix: Define one `KINDS` table (`{ ext, type, magic }`). Derive both `imageKind` and `typeOfName` from it.

review.impact: `serveImage` is `async` with no `await`. It calls `typeOfName` a second time, although `attachmentPath` already rejects names that have no type. The `type === null` check is therefore dead. In `storeImage`, `?? "png"` is also unreachable, because `refusal` has already ensured the bytes are an image.
review.fix: Make `serveImage` synchronous. Drop the redundant null checks, or have `attachmentPath` return `{ path, type }`. Reuse the `imageKind` result in `storeImage` instead of calling it again with a fallback.

review.impact: The `count` ref is a second source of truth for the number of chips, kept in step by hand in `add`, `remove` and `send`. The index-based numbering also depends on that count staying in sync with `chips`. The `Chip` type has optional `name` and `reason` fields, so every use needs an `undefined` check.
review.fix: Derive the next token number from the chip list instead of the ref. Make `Chip` a discriminated union by status, so `ready` always has `name` and `refused` always has `reason`.

review.impact: The new `upload` and `imageUrl` have no test. The failure paths are all untested: a non-JSON response, a non-2xx status with no `message` (the "the server answered N" fallback), a thrown fetch error, and a 2xx response without a string `name`. `send` now also puts `images` in the request body, and no test checks that. The composer tests stub `upload`, and the e2e tests only cover the happy path and the 20 MB refusal.
review.fix: Add chat-store unit tests with a fake `deps.fetch`. Cover a success, a 413 with a `message`, a 500 with an HTML body, a rejected fetch, a 200 with no `name`, and the `images` field in the `send` body. Also check that `imageUrl` encodes special characters.

review.impact: Several composer branches have no test. These are the drop handler and `onDragOver`, a pasted non-image file (it must fall through and not be prevented), and a composer with no `upload` prop (it must ignore image pastes). The Enter-while-uploading wait also has no test for the case where the uploading chip is removed or refused, which should send the message. Only the happy-path wait is tested.
review.fix: Add a drop test, a text-file paste test (default not prevented, no chip), a test with no `upload` prop, and a test where Enter is pressed during an upload that then fails or is removed.

review.impact: The send-validation tests cover only one bad name, `../../log.jsonl`. They do not cover `images` that is not an array, an array with a non-string element, or a well-formed name that is not stored. The upload tests also do not check that an upload on a project with no attachments folder creates the `.gitignore`.
review.fix: Add cases for `images: "x"`, `images: [1]` and `images: ["missing.png"]`, each expecting 400. Assert that `.werk/attachments/.gitignore` exists with `*\n` after a successful upload.

review.impact: The magic-byte tests have only positive cases and one SVG negative case. A `RIFF` header without `WEBP` at offset 8 is not tested, nor is a truncated PNG signature (such as the first 4 bytes alone) or a bad GIF version. `typeOfName` is also not tested on uppercase extensions, double extensions, or names with a path. A regression that accepts any RIFF file, such as a WAV, would pass.
review.fix: Add negative cases for `RIFF....WAVE`, a truncated PNG signature and `GIF90a`. Add `typeOfName` cases for `a.PNG` and `a.png.txt`.

review.impact: The 20 MB cap is only enforced early through the Content-Length header. A chunked upload, or one with no Content-Length, is read fully into memory by `req.arrayBuffer()` and only rejected after that. The server's own body limit and the token check reduce the risk, but a token holder can still force a large allocation per request.
review.fix: Stream the body and stop reading once the byte count passes MAX_IMAGE_BYTES. Alternatively, rely on an explicit `maxRequestBodySize` set to slightly above 20 MB for this route.

review.impact: The 20 MB cap is only checked against the declared Content-Length. A chunked upload with no Content-Length skips that check, and `req.arrayBuffer()` buffers the whole body (up to the server's global body limit) before `refusal` rejects it. A large or repeated unauthenticated-size upload can use a lot of memory, since the check runs after the read.
review.fix: Reject a request with no Content-Length (411), or read `req.body` as a stream and stop with 413 once the running total passes MAX_IMAGE_BYTES. Alternatively, set a per-route body limit.

review.impact: `mkdirSync`, `existsSync`, `writeFileSync` and `statSync` run synchronously on the server's single event loop. Writing an image of up to 20 MB blocks every other request, including the live SSE stream, for the duration of the write.
review.fix: Use `await Bun.write(path, bytes)` or `fs/promises` for the file write. Keep the sync calls only for the cheap directory checks.

review.impact: The `images` array has no length limit. Each entry costs a `statSync` on the event loop, so a large list from a single request multiplies the blocking work.
review.fix: Cap the list, for example at 20 entries, and refuse a longer one. Also dedupe the names before the stat calls.

causeOfLast.why: an earlier pass wrote an unsafe optional chain in a test, and the cards were clear enough to avoid it.

grade.gap: The ✕ can name the wrong number of cards that go with it. In src/serve/card-page.ts, descendants() loops over `[id, ...found]`. That array is built once, before the loop starts, so the function only collects direct children and never grandchildren. For a card whose children have children of their own, data-cards (and so the confirmation's 'N cards leave the map') is lower than the number that removeCard really takes out. Fix: walk a queue that grows as children are found (for example, push onto `found` and iterate with an index), and add a card-page test where a card has a grandchild and data-cards counts it. Also consider counting the options and excerpts that removal takes along (#werk-remove), so the named count matches what actually leaves.

A pending removal gets a blue badge on its tile. The tile of a card with a pending removal draws `proposed` without the tag-removal class (src/serve/card-tile.ts, the hasProposal branch). The box is red (is-removal) but the badge is proposal blue, and the card requires a red 'proposed' badge. Fix: add ' tag-removal' when node.removal is set, the same way tagRow in card-page.ts does, and add a card-tile/card-page test for a removal tile.

causeOfLast.why: an earlier build (werk/23) added a pure file to the gate list without writing its test file.

grade.gap: src/verbs/quote.ts adds a second way to pass the quoted words, the `--text` flag, and refuses a call that gives the words both ways ('give the text once'). No criterion or story asks for this. Remove the flag, or record it if a person wants it. Not out of scope: the extra build-rules.test.ts file is a test only and adds no behaviour.

grade.gap: src/map/quote-match.ts is on PURE_FILES and has its own test, src/map/quote-match.test.ts, which exercises every branch. The grader was not allowed to run bun test or the coverage gate, so this score comes from reading the code only.

The earlier gaps are closed. The event type `excerpt.quoted` and the field `said_at` come from #werk-excerpt-event-type. The command line shape and `--text` come from #werk-cli-recall-quote-form. A proposal, an accept and a discard of a change on an excerpt all refuse, through target() and withPending() in change-rules.ts. But applyEdited in src/map/fold.ts refuses a node.edited on an excerpt only when it carries why or body. A node.edited that sets who, noBasis or unchallenged on an excerpt still applies. That gives an owner to something nobody can decide, which this card's reason rules out. Fix: refuse every node.edited on an excerpt in applyEdited, and add a test for it in quote-rules.test.ts.
