review.impact: applyQuoted validates each field, then rebuilds the same values through a series of `as string` and `as number` casts. The null checks sit in loops, so TypeScript cannot narrow the values, and the casts hide that gap. If someone adds a field and forgets its check, the code compiles and a null reaches the pointer. The function is also long, doing validation, building the pointer, checking ids and building the node.
review.fix: Return a typed result from a small `readPointer(fields)` helper. It should check each field and return either a `Pointer` plus id, title and card, or a Violation, with no casts. Then applyQuoted only has to do the id and card checks and build the node.

review.impact: The test title says it covers 'a who edit on the card', but the body only adds a note to the excerpt. The title overstates what is tested, which misleads whoever reads it later.
review.fix: Rename the test to 'a note on an excerpt works', or add the who-edit assertion.

review.impact: The `quoted(id, card)` event builder is copied word for word into ghost-rules.test.ts and removal-rules.test.ts. quote-rules.test.ts and the card tests also build the same event by hand. A change to the event shape means editing four or five places.
review.fix: Move one `quotedEvent` builder into a shared test helper, such as src/test-env, and import it in these tests.

review.impact: `bad` is redefined here with the same body as in change-rules.ts. The id-taken and unknown-card checks also repeat logic that applyProposed and target() already have, so the three copies can drift apart.
review.fix: Export `bad` and the shared taken-id and unknown-card checks from one module, and use them in all three places.

review.impact: The test is named for refusing a hand-added excerpt, but it only asserts `code` is not 0 for that `add`. The `add` could fail for an unrelated reason, such as a bad flag or a missing `--kind` option, and the test would still pass. It would not catch the `excerpt` rule being removed if `add` rejected the flag some other way.
review.fix: Assert `added.code` is 1 and that `added.stderr` contains "excerpt" or "only by a quote". Also assert that `project.events()` has length 1 after the failed add.

review.impact: The test name promises "a who edit on the card", but the body only adds a note to the excerpt. The who-edit path is untested, and the name is misleading.
review.fix: Add a `node.edited` with `who` on card `x`, or drop that phrase from the test name.

review.impact: The test for quoting a removed card uses `toContain("unknown-card")`, which is weak. It would also pass if an unrelated problem happened to produce that rule. There is also no test that an excerpt id held by a removed card is refused as `duplicate-id`. That is the `isOut` branch in `applyQuoted`, and the `freeId` skip in the verb depends on it.
review.fix: Assert `toEqual(["unknown-card"])`. Add a case that quotes, removes the excerpt, then quotes the same id again, and expect `duplicate-id`.

review.impact: The span offsets are UTF-16 code-unit indexes from `indexOf`. No test uses non-ASCII text, such as an emoji or accented characters. No test uses CRLF line endings in the chat log either. A later change to code-point offsets, or `\r` leaking into messages, would go unnoticed.
review.fix: Add a `matchQuote` case with a surrogate-pair or accented character before the match. Pin the intended offset unit. Add a `spokenMessages` case with `\r\n` line endings.

causeOfLast.why: an earlier pass built the subtree walk over a fixed array and left the removal tile badge without the red class, and the cards stated both rules clearly.

review.impact: The POST route list now appears twice: once in the `/accept` / `/remove` dispatch and once in the `createRoute` allow-list. The `rest.slice(1) as "accept" | "remove"` cast hides the link between them. Adding a third card action means editing both places, and a missed edit fails without any error.
review.fix: Export a `CARD_ACTIONS` tuple or an `isCardAction(rest)` guard from card-action-route.ts. Use it in both places and drop the cast.

review.impact: The accept event hardcodes `actor: "you"`. Server-side card-action code now fixes who counts as the person. If `actorRefusal` or the actor convention changes, this silent literal will not follow it.
review.fix: Name the actor as a shared constant, or take it from the same source as the CLI's `--actor` default.

review.impact: `askRemove` builds the confirmation panel with imperative DOM code inside `start()`, in a client that is otherwise built from React components. The panel is not covered by unit tests, and a live redraw will drop it without notice. `start()` also gets longer.
review.fix: Move the panel into a small component or a function in client/lib that builds the DOM. Keep only the event wiring in main.tsx.

review.impact: The red `#dc2626` is repeated across `.is-removal`, `.tag-removal`, `.card-accept.is-removal` and `.remove-confirm`. The `.hero .tags` rule is appended at the end of the file, apart from the other hero rules. Both make later restyling harder.
review.fix: Define a `--removal` custom property beside `--proposed`. Move the `.hero .tags` rule next to the `.hero` rules.

review.impact: pairItems copies the LCS table and the two-pointer walk from lcsTable and wordSegments in src/map/edit-diff.ts, with different element types. A fix to the tie-break or the walk would have to be made in both places, and the two could drift apart.
review.fix: Export a generic lcsTable<T>, or a shared diff walker, from edit-diff.ts. Use it for both the word diff and the list item pairing, so each module only decides how to group the runs.

review.impact: acceptRemoval and discardRemoval build the same 'not-removed' violation inline. The message can drift between them.
review.fix: Add a small helper such as noRemoval(id) that returns the violation, and call it from both functions.

review.impact: descendants() walks map.parents once per found card, which is quadratic. It uses a loop that grows its own array and starts at index -1. The direct children are then counted separately with a second scan of map.parents. The same subtree and child logic probably already exists in removeCard in removal-rules.ts, so there are now two definitions of 'the cards that go'.
review.fix: Reuse or export the subtree helper from removal-rules.ts. Build a children index once and derive both the child count and the subtree size from it.

review.impact: The accept and remove routes are listed twice, once in the dispatch and once in the POST allow-list. The dispatch also casts rest.slice(1) to CardAction, which bypasses the type check. Adding a third action means editing both places and the cast stays unchecked.
review.fix: Define a CARD_ACTIONS constant, or an isCardAction type guard, in card-action-route.ts. Use it in both places and drop the cast.

review.impact: The .hero .tags rule is appended at the end of the file, away from the other .tags rules, and so is easy to miss. The red #dc2626 is hard-coded in about six rules without a variable, unlike --proposed.
review.fix: Move the rule next to the other .tags rules. Add a --removal custom property and use it in every red rule.

review.impact: askRemove builds the confirmation panel with imperative DOM calls inside the already large start(). The rest of the client is built from components, so this logic is hard to test and extend.
review.fix: Move the confirmation into a small component, or at least into its own module such as client/lib/remove-confirm.ts.

review.impact: The mark helper repeats the ternary on kind three times to pick the tag name. The local html wrapper in diffInline adds nothing, and escapeHtml is applied to a constant string.
review.fix: Compute the tag name once in mark, inline html(run), and write the diff note as a plain string.

review.impact: The accept route is tested only for a ghost and for a proposed removal. A pending edit (`change.proposed`) is one of the three proposal kinds that `hasProposal` admits, and its ✓ goes through `acceptChange`. No route test covers it, so a regression in that path would go unnoticed outside the browser e2e. The e2e does not cover it either, because it only checks that the edit is drawn, not that its ✓ works.
review.fix: Add a route test that seeds a `change.proposed` event, posts `accept`, and asserts a 200 and that `node.pending` is null.

review.impact: The failure-path test covers a non-JSON body, an invalid id and a root removal. It does not cover a body that is valid JSON but not an object, such as `null` or `5`. `body ?? {}` guards `null` only. It also does not cover an accept for a card that does not exist, which should return `no-proposal` with 409.
review.fix: Add assertions for `post('accept', {card:'missing'})` returning 409 and `post('remove', null)` returning 400.

review.impact: After the ✓ click the test calls `page.goto` straight away, without waiting for the POST to finish. The navigation can abort the in-flight request, or load the root before the event is appended. The assertion then depends on the live channel reloading the page, which makes the test racy.
review.fix: Wait for the accept response with `page.waitForResponse` around the click, or assert on the current page that the card has left the map, before navigating.

review.impact: `descendants` scans every entry of `map.parents` once for each card in the subtree, so it costs O(subtree × all cards). `actions` then scans `map.parents` again to count children. This runs on every render of a card page. On a large map, opening a high-level card, such as the root, does millions of comparisons. It can't hang the page, but it adds avoidable latency.
review.fix: Build a parent-to-children index in one pass over `map.parents`, then walk it breadth-first. That makes the walk O(n). Take the direct child count from the same index instead of filtering `map.parents` again.

causeOfLast.why: another ticket added excerpt fields and imports in `fold.ts` after this ticket was built, and both edits overlapped.

grade.gap: Borderline: src/verbs/remove.ts adds a command-line `--propose` flag with the output "removal proposed". That is a new agent-facing verb behaviour, and no criterion or user story asks for it. The e2e test for criterion-4 uses it as a fixture. Unless another ticket owns the command line for proposed removals, keep the flag minimal or seed the event in the test. The removal.proposed fold support is needed for criterion-4, so it may stay.

None of the named cards gives these choices. src/serve/image-route.test.ts 'a send names its images…' checks that the launch record holds the path but never checks that it lacks the bytes. Only the e2e test checks `not.toContain(PNG_BASE64)`. Add the same check to the unit test, for example that the record text has no PNG signature or base64.

Not asked for, but small: the MAX_IMAGES = 50 limit on a send in src/serve/chat-route.ts, and the content-length check before reading the body in src/serve/image-route.ts. Both are defensive limits. Remove them or keep them; neither fails the line. Drag-and-drop is asked for through #werk-shots.
Not a contradiction: the sent message in the chat log does not show each image under its number (the `sent` event in client/lib/chat-store.ts carries only the text). Another ticket can build this.

review.impact: The 20 MB cap is enforced only through the declared Content-Length header. A chunked upload, or one with the header missing, goes through `req.arrayBuffer()` with no limit. The whole body is held in memory before `checkImage` rejects it. The header check also relies on `Number()`, which gives NaN for a malformed value, and NaN is never greater than the cap.
review.fix: Read the body with a running byte count and stop once it passes MAX_IMAGE_BYTES, or rely on a server-level max body size. Treat a NaN length as not declared and still enforce the cap while reading.

review.impact: The chips and the `[Image #n]` tokens in the text are two pieces of state tied together only by position. If the person edits or deletes a token by hand, or retypes the numbers, `settleSend` and `remove` pick the wrong token. A refused image can leave its token in the sent text, a still-attached image's token can be removed, and the text can name different images than the list of names sent. `remove` also renumbers only the tokens that are still in the text.
review.fix: On each text change, reconcile the chips against the tokens present. Drop the chips whose token is gone and renumber the rest. Alternatively, derive the names at send time from the token numbers found in the text, not from the chip positions.

review.impact: The `take` function numbers new tokens from `chips.length`. That count can be stale when two pastes land before React re-renders, and it can also disagree with the tokens actually in the text. Two chips could then get the same token number. Separately, the `as Chip` cast and the nested ternary inside `setChips` make the upload-result handling hard to read.
review.fix: Number new chips from a ref that tracks the chip count, or derive the numbers inside a functional `setChips` update. Move the upload-result mapping into a small pure helper in image-chips.ts, for example `settleChip(chip, done)`, and give the chip literal a type annotation instead of casting it.

review.impact: Two `biome-ignore useExhaustiveDependencies` suppressions hide stale-closure risks. The send-on-wait effect calls `send()`, which closes over `text` and `chips` from the render in which the effect ran. This is fragile, and it is the kind of escape hatch that hides real bugs.
review.fix: Remove the effect-based send. For example, keep a ref to the latest `send` and call it from the place where the last upload settles. Or make `send` a stable callback with the deps listed explicitly, so the suppressions are not needed.

review.impact: The 20 MB size message is built here again from `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`, and `checkImage` in image-rules.ts builds the same message. If one is reworded, the two drift apart.
review.fix: Export the message from image-rules.ts, or a `tooLarge()` result helper, and use it in both places.

review.impact: `mimeOfName` finds the type by searching `Object.keys(EXTENSION)`, which is an indirect reverse lookup. `EXTENSION` and `IMAGE_MIME` are two parallel tables.
review.fix: Build one table keyed by extension, or have a single `{ext, mime}` record per type, so no reverse search is needed.

review.impact: `basename()` is applied to the name before `findImage`, which already rejects anything that is not a stored name through `isStoredName`. The call does nothing and suggests a second layer of protection that does not exist. The `if` also has no braces, unlike the surrounding code.
review.fix: Drop `basename` and pass the raw query value to `findImage`. Brace the `if` to match the surrounding style.

review.impact: The new `upload` has three failure branches: a non-JSON body, a non-ok status that falls back to `the server answered N`, and a thrown fetch error. None has a unit test. `createChatStore` has no test file at all. Only the e2e 25 MB case runs it, and only on the server's `message` path. `send` now posts `images`, and nothing checks that body shape or the default `[]`. `imageUrl` is untested too, including its `encodeURIComponent` call. A regression here would show up to the user only as a chip that stays stuck or shows a wrong reason.
review.fix: Add `client/lib/chat-store.test.ts` with a fake `deps.fetch`. Cover the three `upload` outcomes: success returns `{name}`, a non-ok response with no JSON returns `the server answered 500`, and a thrown fetch returns `{error}`. Also assert that `send` posts `images` (default `[]`) and that `imageUrl` encodes the name.

review.impact: The drop path (`onDrop` and `onDragOver`) is untested, and so is the rule that non-image files are ignored. A paste with no `images` sink, and a paste with a mix of image and non-image files, are also untested. So are removing a chip that is still uploading, and an upload that is refused while Enter is waiting. The tests only exercise paste of PNGs.
review.fix: Add composer tests for these cases: a drop of an image file creates a chip, a drop of a non-image file does nothing, a paste with no `images` prop leaves the default paste alone, and a pending send whose upload is refused still sends without that token.

review.impact: The `MAX_IMAGES` limit of 50 on `/chat` has no test. A request body that does not match the shape (`images` not an array) is covered, but a list over the limit is not. Removing the limit would pass every test.
review.fix: Add a case that sends 51 names and expects a 400.

review.impact: `imageFileName` and `mimeOfName` are tested only for jpeg and png. The `.gif` and `.webp` extension mappings are never checked. A wrong entry in `EXTENSION` for those two types would go unnoticed, and so would a `sniffImage` change that rejected them in a stored name.
review.fix: Loop over all four types in the stored-name test, asserting the file name, `isStoredName` and `mimeOfName` for each.

review.impact: The 20 MB cap is only checked against the declared Content-Length header. A chunked upload has no such header, or the header can be wrong. `req.arrayBuffer()` then reads the whole body into memory before `checkImage` measures it. A client holding the token can use this to exhaust server memory with a very large body. The token check limits who can do it, but the cap does not hold.
review.fix: Enforce the cap while reading. Stream `req.body` and abort with 413 once the running total passes MAX_IMAGE_BYTES. Alternatively, set Bun's `maxRequestBodySize` for this route. Also treat a missing or non-numeric Content-Length as unknown and rely on the streamed limit.

review.impact: Stored images are never removed, and each upload is up to 20 MB. Repeated uploads, including ones the user later removes from the composer, grow `.werk/attachments` without bound.
review.fix: Prune old attachments, for example by age or total size, or delete them when their chat is cleared. At minimum, note the retention decision in the card.

review.impact: The 20 MB cap is only checked against the declared Content-Length. A chunked upload, or one with a false or missing Content-Length, goes through `req.arrayBuffer()` and is held in memory in full. Only after that does `checkImage` reject it. The only limit is the server's own body-size default. The route is local and needs the token, so the risk is limited.
review.fix: Read the body as a stream and stop with 413 once the running byte count passes MAX_IMAGE_BYTES. Or check `bytes.byteLength` before any copy, and return 411 when Content-Length is missing.

review.impact: `readFileSync` on read, and `writeFileSync` and `mkdirSync` in `storeImage`, block the event loop for the whole file. An image can be up to 20 MB, so a request can stall the SSE live channel and the other routes. Each thumbnail request also reads the full original image with no caching headers, so the browser may refetch it.
review.fix: Serve with `new Response(Bun.file(path))` and write with `Bun.write` or the async fs API. Add `cache-control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable`, because the stored names are unique.

review.impact: Each of up to 50 image names runs a synchronous `statSync`, on top of the 200 KB text cap. The cost is small, but it is repeated work on the request path.
review.fix: No change is needed. You could deduplicate names before checking them.

causeOfLast.why: #vi-remove-btn-reparent implied a ✕ on a proposed card, while #al-diff-cli-btn forbids a discard button, and no card settled which wins.

pass_end.decision: the grader said a person must settle: The card says 'A card with no children, and a proposed card, keep the one plain question'. That implies a proposed card has a ✕ with a plain question. src/serve/card-page.ts actions() withholds the ✕ from every proposed card (`!node.proposed`), and card-page.test.ts asserts 'no ✕' on a ghost. But the fold refuses to remove a ghost (remove-target), and #al-diff-cli-btn says discard has no button. A ✕ on a ghost would therefore have to be a discard button, which that card forbids. A person must decide one of two things: does the ✕ on a proposed card discard it, which narrows #al-diff-cli-btn? Or does a proposed card have no ✕, which changes the wording of #vi-remove-btn-reparent?

grade.gap: Pass 1 and pass 2 change no code. The proposed card #vi-remove-btn-ghost-no-x now records three of the earlier choices: (4) the ✕ removes at once while an agent proposes, (5) a ghost has no ✕, and (6) the confirmation sits inside the card, under its buttons. These choices are still unrecorded, so propose a card for each one or one card for the group: (1) the new log event type `removal.proposed` with the fields {id, reparent?}, the new MapNode field `removal: {reparent: boolean} | null`, and the CLI flag `remove --propose` that writes the event (src/map/fold.ts, src/map/removal-rules.ts proposeRemoval/acceptRemoval/discardRemoval, src/verbs/remove.ts). (2) A proposed removal is accepted and discarded through the existing `node.accepted` and `node.discarded` events: applyAccepted and applyDiscarded check `node.removal` before they treat the event as an edit or a ghost. (3) The button addresses POST /api/projects/<name>/accept and POST /api/projects/<name>/remove, with the body {card, reparent?}, a 409 `no-proposal` refusal and a 400 `bad-request` refusal (src/serve/routes.ts, src/serve/card-action-route.ts).

The earlier conflict now has a recorded answer. The proposed card #vi-remove-btn-ghost-no-x says a proposed card has no ✕, and that the one plain question covers a real card with no children. This matches src/serve/card-page.ts actions(), which leaves out the ✕ when `node.proposed` is true. The wording of #vi-remove-btn-reparent ('a proposed card keep the one plain question') still reads differently, so it settles only when the person accepts #vi-remove-btn-ghost-no-x.

review.impact: `rowsOf(list, null)` always passes a null home folder. The `~` abbreviation in `client/lib/switcher.ts` (`tilde`, with its tests) is therefore never used in the app, and the menu shows full absolute paths. The tested pure code and the running code don't match.
review.fix: Pass the real home folder, for example from the `/api/projects` response if the server returns it. If no source exists, drop the `home` parameter and `tilde` until one does.

review.impact: The remove handler has no error handling. A rejected `fetch` becomes an unhandled promise rejection. A non-ok reply, such as the server refusing a remove that needs confirmation because a turn started after the last 3s poll, is swallowed and the list just refreshes. The user sees nothing.
review.fix: Add a `.catch` that calls `say(...)`. On a non-ok response, report the server's error text before refreshing.

review.impact: The local `Listed` type repeats the shape of `SwitcherProject` from `client/lib/switcher.ts`. The two can drift apart.
review.fix: Import and use `SwitcherProject` for `readList` and the `list` variable.

review.impact: The `setInterval` poll is never cleared and `refresh` has no unmount path. It only lives for the page, but it keeps polling `/api/projects` every 3s in hidden tabs.
review.fix: Skip the refresh while `document.hidden`, or pause it on `visibilitychange`.

review.impact: The open menu closes only on a row action. There is no outside click or Escape handling, so it stays open over the page.
review.fix: Add a document-level `pointerdown` and `keydown` (Escape) listener, installed in an effect while the menu is open.

review.impact: Runtime telemetry lines that tests produce are part of the diff. This is noise unrelated to the change.
review.fix: Leave `.werk/fold-ms.jsonl` out of the commit (`git checkout` it).

review.impact: The `Listed` type duplicates `SwitcherProject` from client/lib/switcher.ts, which has the same fields (name, folder, missing, dev, running). Two copies of the server's project-list shape can drift apart.
review.fix: Delete `Listed` and use `SwitcherProject` for `readList` and the `list` variable.

review.impact: `mountSwitcher` calls `rowsOf(list, null)`, so `home` is never passed. The `~` abbreviation in `rowsOf` and its tests is dead in the running app, and folders show as full paths.
review.fix: Pass the home folder if the server exposes it. If it doesn't, drop the `home` parameter and the `tilde` logic.

review.impact: The `setInterval` that polls every 3s is never cleared, and each `mountSwitcher` call starts a new one. It also runs `refresh()` while the menu is closed. This is fine for a single mount but fragile if the mount ever repeats.
review.fix: Keep the interval id and clear it on teardown, or document that the switcher mounts exactly once per page.

review.impact: The empty-list branch builds a button imperatively with `innerHTML` and `createElement`. This duplicates the Add button that the switcher already renders, in a different idiom from the rest of the React client.
review.fix: Render a small React component for the empty page, or reuse the switcher's add-button markup.

review.impact: The remove handler nests the confirm/remove branches, and `close()` is skipped when the user cancels the confirm. The nesting is harder to read than needed.
review.fix: Flatten it: `const turns = running(row.name); if (turns.length && !window.confirm(stopQuestion(row.name, turns))) return; onRemove(row.name, turns.length > 0); close();`

review.impact: `list-style: none` and `margin` on `switcher-menu` are list leftovers, because the menu is a div. There are also hard-coded colors (#d4d4d8, #9ca3af, #16a34a) rather than theme variables.
review.fix: Remove the list-style declaration and use the existing CSS variables for colors where they exist.

review.impact: Every test renders with `running={() => []}`. The failure path of the × button is never run: a project with running turns, `window.confirm` called with `stopQuestion`, `onRemove(name, true)` on OK, and no remove and an open menu on cancel. If the confirm branch were deleted or inverted, all the tests would still pass. That branch is the one that stops running agent turns.
review.fix: Add a test that gives `running` a non-empty list for one project and stubs `window.confirm`. With confirm returning true, expect `remove checkout true`. With confirm returning false, expect no `remove` call, and expect the menu to still be open.

review.impact: The test for clicking the already-open project (`pickOf` returns "stay") only runs in the pure-function test. No component test checks that the click closes the menu without calling `onOpen`. The test for the missing row doesn't check that the menu stays open either.
review.fix: Click the `werk` row in the component test and expect `calls` to be empty and the menu to be closed. In the missing-row case, also assert that `[data-slot=switcher-menu]` is still present.

review.impact: The empty-list page, which has a `start-add` button, has no test. The e2e test covers only the case where a project exists.
review.fix: Add an e2e or component test for an empty project list. It should check that the `start-add` button is present and that it calls the same add action as the switcher.

review.impact: Running the tests appended four lines to a tracked data file in the checkout, and the lines are part of this change. That suggests a test writes to the real store, which #werk-test-store forbids. It also adds noise to the diff.
review.fix: Redirect that store to a per-test temporary copy, and drop these lines from the change.

review.impact: mountSwitcher calls setInterval(refresh, 3000) with no cleanup. It keeps polling /api/projects while the tab is hidden. It also starts a new fetch even if the last one is still pending, so requests can overlap when the server is slow. Every tick also calls root.render with a freshly built rows array, even when the list has not changed, so the switcher re-renders every 3 seconds. The server handler is cheap, so this is a small constant overhead per open tab.
review.fix: Skip the tick when document.hidden or a refresh is already in flight. Skip draw() when the new list equals the old one, for example by comparing JSON.stringify of both. Better still, refresh on a server event, such as the existing live signal, instead of polling.

review.impact: When the address has no project, start() calls readList() itself, and mountSwitcher has already started its own readList() through refresh(). That makes two identical /api/projects requests at page load.
review.fix: Have mountSwitcher expose its first list promise, or let start() reuse it, so the page makes one request.

causeOfLast.why: no card covered the pending-removal event, its reuse of accept and discard, or the ✓ and ✕ request shape.

pass_end.decision: a pass named a spec gap as the cause of a failure: #vi-remove-btn-reparent implied a ✕ on a proposed card, while #al-diff-cli-btn forbids a discard button, and no card settled which wins.

grade.gap: Pass 3 changes no code. The earlier gaps (1) to (3) are now covered by the proposed card #vi-remove-btn-pending-removal. It records the removal proposal as its own event that names the card and whether its children move up, and the card carrying a pending removal (`removal.proposed`, `MapNode.removal`, and `remove --propose` as the agent's staging command). It records that accept and discard reuse the existing events, with the fold checking for a pending removal first (applyAccepted and applyDiscarded). It records the accept and remove requests with their body {card, reparent}, a conflict refusal when no proposal is pending, a bad-request refusal for a malformed request, and the token requirement (src/serve/card-action-route.ts). The card does not spell out the literal names `removal.proposed`, `--propose`, `/accept` and `/remove`, but these are labels for choices it already makes. No unrecorded choice remains.

review.impact: `askRemove` builds the confirmation panel by hand with `document.createElement`, inside `start()` in the entry file. The client rules say screens are built from components on one framework and from shadcn/ui, and this panel is neither. Its DOM wiring has no test, since only the pure helpers in `card-actions.ts` are covered. It also grows the entry file, which `#werk-stack-modules` wants kept small.
review.fix: Make the confirmation a React component, for example a shadcn AlertDialog, in `client/app/`. Mount it on the `data-action="remove"` click and pass it `removeQuestion(removeFactsOf(...))`. Move `act` out of `start()` as well, so `main.tsx` only wires the click delegation.

review.impact: `pairItems` re-implements the LCS table and the backtrack walk that `edit-diff.ts` already has as `lcsTable`, which already takes `string[]`. Two copies of the same algorithm can drift apart.
review.fix: Export `lcsTable` from `edit-diff.ts` and use it in `pairItems`. Only the flush-and-pair step stays local.

review.impact: The list of POST routes appears twice: once in the allow-list array and once in the `rest === "/accept" || rest === "/remove"` check, which then needs the cast `rest.slice(1) as "accept" | "remove"`. A new action has to be added in both places.
review.fix: Export an `isCardAction(name)` type guard or a constant list from `card-action-route.ts`. Use it in both places so the cast goes away.

review.impact: The route decides whether a card has a proposal by importing `hasProposal` from `card-look.ts`, a module about how cards look. That is a domain rule, so the write path now depends on a view module. The route also hardcodes the actor `"you"`.
review.fix: Move `hasProposal` next to the fold, for example in `removal-rules.ts` or `map/`, and let `card-look.ts` import it. Name the actor as a constant.

review.impact: `actions` walks `map.parents` once in `descendants` and again to count children. `descendants` rescans the whole parents map for every card it visits, so the work is quadratic in the number of cards on each page render.
review.fix: Build a children index once, or compute the children and the subtree from one pass. The direct children are the first level of `descendants`.

review.impact: The red `#dc2626` is repeated in `.card-box.is-removal`, `.card-accept.is-removal`, `.remove-confirm` and `.tag-removal`, while other colours use variables such as `--proposed`.
review.fix: Add a `--removal` variable beside `--proposed` and use it in all four rules.

review.impact: `pairItems` builds its own LCS table and runs its own walk, with the same tie-break and the same removed/added run flushing. `lcsTable` and `wordSegments` in src/map/edit-diff.ts already do this for words. The two copies can drift apart, and a fix to one will not reach the other.
review.fix: Make the LCS walk in edit-diff.ts generic over `string[]`. Export it, or export a helper that returns the same/removed/added runs, and build item pairing from that. `pairItems` then only has to pair the removed and added runs by position.

review.impact: `descendants` rescans all of `map.parents` once per visited card, which is quadratic. `actions` then scans `map.parents` a third time to count direct children. This runs for every card page render.
review.fix: Build a parent-to-children index once. Take the child count from it, and do the subtree walk over it.

review.impact: The accept and remove routes are listed twice, once in the dispatch and once in the POST allowlist. The dispatch also casts `rest.slice(1) as "accept" | "remove"`. A new action means editing both places, and the cast hides a mismatch between them.
review.fix: Declare a `CARD_ACTIONS` map from path to action, for example `{"/accept": "accept", "/remove": "remove"}`. Use it in both places and drop the cast.

review.impact: `acceptRemoval` and `discardRemoval` each build the same `not-removed` violation with the same message.
review.fix: Pull out a small `noRemoval(id)` helper that returns the violation.

review.impact: The red `#dc2626` is hardcoded in about six new rules, and `#fee2e2` and `#991b1b` are hardcoded beside it. The `.hero .tags` rule is tacked onto the end of the file, far from the `.hero` and `.tags` rules it belongs with.
review.fix: Add a `--removal` custom property next to `--proposed` and use it. Move the `.hero .tags` rule beside the other `.hero` rules.

review.impact: `askRemove` builds the confirmation dialog by hand with `document.createElement` inside `start()`. The rest of the client is built from React and shadcn components. This is a new imperative DOM path that is hard to test, and it makes `start()` longer.
review.fix: Move the confirmation into a small component or a `client/lib` module. At minimum, pull the DOM-building out of `start()`.

review.impact: In the proposed-removal test, the ✓ click is followed at once by `page.goto(.../map/root)`. The click only starts an async fetch, so the navigation can cancel that POST before the server gets it. The test is then flaky, and it can fail for a reason unrelated to the code. The 'moving up' test avoids this by waiting for the heading to disappear before it navigates.
review.fix: After the click, wait for an observable effect before navigating. For example, `await expect(hero).not.toHaveClass(/is-removal/)`, or wait for the `/accept` response with `page.waitForResponse`. Then go to the root page and assert the tile count.

review.impact: Two edge cases are untested. First, a card with both a pending edit (`change.proposed`) and a proposed removal: `applyAccepted` takes the removal branch first, so the edit is dropped silently. Second, `removal.proposed` on a card that already has a proposed removal. A later change to that precedence would not be caught.
review.fix: Add tests that propose an edit and then a removal on the same card and assert what an accept does. Add one that proposes a removal twice and asserts the result.

review.impact: `descendants` scans every entry of `map.parents` once for each card it has found, so it costs O(descendants × cards). `actions` then scans `map.parents` again to count children. This runs on every render of a card page. The page of a root or other high-level card on a large map is close to quadratic: a few thousand cards means millions of iterations per render, and the live channel redraws the page on every change.
review.fix: Build a parent-to-children index once with a single pass over `map.parents`, then walk it breadth-first. Take the direct child count from `index.get(id)?.length`. The walk then costs O(cards), and the second scan goes away.

review.impact: The accept path reads and folds the whole log with `readMap` to check for a proposal. `appendEvents` then reads and folds it again to validate the event. Each ✓ click folds the log twice.
review.fix: Let the fold inside `appendEvents` produce the refusal. For example, have `applyAccepted` return a `no-proposal` violation, or reuse the map that `readMap` already returned. That drops the extra read.

causeOfLast.why: another ticket merged first and changed the same CSS, route table and pure-file list.

grade.gap: None of the named cards gives these choices, so each needs a proposed card. (1) The addresses POST /api/projects/<name>/accept and POST /api/projects/<name>/remove, and the request body {card, reparent} (src/serve/routes.ts, src/serve/card-action-route.ts). (2) The log event name "removal.proposed" and the folded field MapNode.removal = {reparent} (src/map/fold.ts, src/map/removal-rules.ts). (3) The command line flag `remove --propose` and its output "removal proposed" (src/verbs/remove.ts). (4) The ✕ is also drawn on option nodes, not only on cards (src/serve/card-page.ts actions(): node.kind === "option"). (5) A root with children gets only the subtree answer, with no move-up choice (client/lib/card-actions.ts removeQuestion). (6) A sub-card tile shows the "proposed" badge for a pending edit or removal, and the badge is red for a removal (src/serve/card-tile.ts).

causeOfLast.why: the cited cards give no route addresses, removal event name, remove flag, ✕ on options, root behaviour or tile badge, so these choices needed their own cards.

grade.gap: Each of the six choices that the earlier grade flagged now has a proposed card. (1) #al-diff-cli-btn-accept-route covers the accept and remove addresses and their body. (2) #vi-remove-btn-pending-removal and #vi-remove-btn-pending-removal-fold cover the removal event and MapNode.removal. review.impact: `diffInline` renders each word run separately with `renderInline` or `renderTitle`. Inline markup that spans runs, such as `**two words**`, a backtick span with spaces, or a link with a multi-word label, is split. It then shows as literal markers or broken HTML whenever a diff boundary falls inside it. This affects titles and why text on any card with a pending edit.
review.fix: Diff the plain text, then render each run only when it holds no unbalanced markup. Or diff the already-rendered text tokens. At the least, fall back to a whole-text del/ins pair when a run's markers are unbalanced.

review.impact: `askRemove` builds the confirmation dialog by hand with `document.createElement`, inside `start()`. The client is built from React and shadcn/ui components. The hand-built dialog is outside that stack, repeats the dialog behaviour, and leaves `start()` with more untested code. The component-level pieces are tested, but not the DOM wiring.
review.fix: Move the dialog into a small component or module under `client/app` that uses the shadcn dialog primitive, and have the click handler only open it. If the server-rendered card page rules this out, move at least `askRemove` out of `main.tsx` into its own module.

review.impact: `pairItems` writes out another LCS table and walk. `edit-diff.ts` already has `lcsTable` and the same walk in `wordSegments`. The two copies can drift apart.
review.fix: Export a generic LCS helper from `edit-diff.ts`, or `wordSegments` itself, and use it for the item pairing.

review.impact: `descendants` and the `children` count in `actions` scan all of `map.parents` once per visited card. That is O(n²) on every card page render. `children` repeats a scan that `descendants` already did.
review.fix: Build a children index once and read both the descendant count and the direct child count from it.

review.impact: `rest.slice(1) as "accept" | "remove"` casts a string to the union. The allowed route names are also listed in a second place in `createRoute`, so the two lists can drift apart.
review.fix: Declare one `CARD_ACTIONS` const array, probably next to `CardAction`. Use it for both the method gate and the dispatch, and drop the cast.

review.impact: A runtime timing log is committed in the change. It adds noise to the diff and can cause merge conflicts.
review.fix: Leave this file out of the commit, or add it to .gitignore.

review.impact: pairItems duplicates the LCS table and the walk-and-flush loop already in src/map/edit-diff.ts (lcsTable and wordSegments). Two copies of the same diff algorithm must be kept in step, and a fix to one is easy to miss in the other.
review.fix: Export a generic LCS diff over string arrays from edit-diff.ts. Build wordSegments and pairItems on top of it.

review.impact: actions() computes the child count by scanning map.parents, and descendants() scans it again for every card in the subtree. That is O(n²) work per page render. The second scan also repeats the check in `descendants`, so the two can drift apart.
review.fix: Build one children index (parent to children) and derive both the direct count and the subtree size from it. Alternatively reuse an existing rollup or cardsBelow helper if one fits.

review.impact: The `actions` function builds long HTML strings with several nested conditionals inline. The ✕ button's data attributes are hard to read and hard to change.
review.fix: Extract the ✕ button and its parent data attributes into a small helper such as removeButton(map, node).

review.impact: `rest.slice(1) as "accept" | "remove"` is a type cast that hides a coupling. The route name has to equal the action name, and the POST allow-list on line 178 repeats the same two strings.
review.fix: Define a shared ACTION_PATHS map ("/accept" to "accept", "/remove" to "remove"). Use it for both the dispatch and the allow-list, and drop the cast.

review.impact: The `mark` helper repeats the `kind === "add" ? "ins" : "del"` ternary for both the open and close tags. diffInline then re-maps run.kind from "added"/"removed" to "add"/"del", so there are two vocabularies for the same thing.
review.fix: Compute the tag name once in mark. Have it accept the Segment kind directly, or use a single vocabulary.

review.impact: act and askRemove add about 45 lines of imperative DOM code inside start(). That makes an already large function longer, and the code can't be unit-tested.
review.fix: Move askRemove into a client/lib module, for example a function that builds the confirm panel from removeQuestion and takes callbacks, and import it.

review.impact: Six timing lines from a test run were committed to this tracked file. That means a test or the dev server wrote to the repository's real .werk store, not to a per-test copy (#werk-test-store). The file will now change on every run and produce merge noise.
review.fix: Drop these lines from the change. Find which test calls the fold timer against the checkout's .werk directory, and point it at the test's own temporary project. Alternatively, untrack the file or add it to .gitignore.

review.impact: The route's failure paths are only partly covered. A body of `null` or a non-object body, such as `"null"` or `[]`, hits the `body ?? {}` branch and is never tested. A `reparent` that is not a boolean is never tested either. Neither is an accept of a card with a pending edit, which is the third kind of proposal that `hasProposal` counts. A change to those branches would not fail any test.
review.fix: Add a case that posts `null` and expects 400. Add an accept case on a card with a `change.proposed` and expect 200 with the edit applied. Add a case that posts `reparent: "yes"` and expects a subtree removal.

review.impact: The tests do not cover empty or edge input. These are an empty old `why` going to a new one, a pending `why` of "", and a list whose old and new items are all different. Also, `known` is always false, so the code that links known card references inside marked words is never run.
review.fix: Add a test for `diffInline("", "x", plain)` and for an all-replaced list. Add one that passes a `known` returning true and checks that the link survives inside an `ins` or `del`.

review.impact: `wordSegments` is a new exported function that was refactored out of `wordDiff`. It has no direct test. The changed `close()` flushing logic, which now runs when a run of shared words ends, is checked only indirectly through `wordDiff` strings. A bug in segment boundaries, such as an empty segment or a removed run placed after the added run, could be hidden by the join.
review.fix: Add a test in the edit-diff test file that asserts `wordSegments` returns exact `Segment[]` arrays for a replace, a pure insert, a pure delete, and identical or empty input.

review.impact: `descendants()` scans all of `map.parents` once for every card it has found, so it does O(subtree size × total cards) work. `actions()` then scans `map.parents` a third time to count the children. This runs on every render of a card page with a ✕. On a root or a high-level card of a large map (thousands of cards) it costs millions of iterations per request, and the live channel redraws the page on each change.
review.fix: Build a parent-to-children index once with a single pass over `map.parents`, then walk the subtree breadth-first from that index. This is O(N). Take `children` as the length of the index entry for the card instead of re-filtering `map.parents`.

review.impact: Each accept click reads and folds the whole log in `readMap` to check for a proposal, and `appendEvents` then folds it again to validate the event. This is two full folds per click. It is bounded by log size and by user clicks, so the cost is small.
review.fix: Skip the pre-check and let `appendEvents` refuse the event. For example, map the `not-removed` or `accept-ghost` violations to a 409 `no-proposal`. Or have `appendEvents` return the folded map so the log is read once.

grade.gap: Minor: Escape closes the menu and remembers which word it closed (client/app/composer.tsx `closed` state, test 'Escape closes the menu and Enter then sends the message'), and a mouse click picks an option (onMouseDown). No criterion asks for either, though both are ordinary menu behaviour. The server side (session.commands, /commands route) is needed so the menu has commands to show, so it is in scope.

None of the named cards gives these choices: (1) The command list comes from the `slash_commands` field of the agent's stream-json `system`/`init` line, with any leading slash removed. The session keeps the list from the most recent start and gives none before the first start (src/chat/start-line.ts, src/chat/session.ts commandNames). start-line.ts cites #werk-chat-cmdmenu-source, but no such card exists in the map. Propose it. (2) A new address, GET /api/<project>/commands, that returns `{commands: string[]}` (src/serve/routes.ts, client/lib/chat-store.ts commands()). The client reads it again each time a slash word opens. (3) How cards are ranked in the # menu: the #vi-jump-hash id search comes first, then cards whose title contains the query, capped at LIMIT. An empty query (just `#`) shows nothing (client/lib/word-menu.ts cardMatches). vi-jump-hash says a # search matches ids only, so adding title matches is a new choice. (4) What counts as a trigger word: it must start right after whitespace, and a second / # or ` inside the word closes the menu (wordAt). (5) The menu sits above the composer, and choosing an option inserts the trigger, the choice and one trailing space (insertChoice, index.css word-menu).

review.impact: `clearRoute` never checks the request method. The dispatcher in `src/serve/routes.ts` lets every GET through to `projectRoute`, so `GET /api/<project>/clear` clears the session and transcript. It needs no body, and any token check that only covers POST is skipped. Any page, link or prefetch can wipe the conversation. `modelRoute` and `askRoute` are protected only because they fail to parse a body on GET.
review.fix: Make `clearRoute` return 405 unless `req.method === "POST"`, passing `req` in. Do the same in `modelRoute` so it does not rely on JSON parsing failing.

review.impact: A `model` event is accepted when only `body.window` is a number, then cast with `as unknown as ModelSettings`. A malformed event could put a bad `model`, `advisor` or `used` into the header state.
review.fix: Validate `model`, `advisor` and `used` before applying. The server-side `parsePick` logic could be shared.

review.impact: `refused` is set on every call, but it is never cleared when the person acts again or the turn state changes. A stale 'a turn is running' alert stays on screen after the turn ends.
review.fix: Clear `refused` when `head.busy` changes, or when the person starts another action.

review.impact: `session.ts` is larger and now holds restart, crash retry, session-id tracking and usage tracking in one closure. The `attempts`, `stopped`, `initSeen` and `earlyError` flags are coupled. This works against the single-purpose small modules rule (#werk-stack-modules).
review.fix: Move the usage and settings tracking, and the init/result interception in `noteSession`, into a separate module as the rest of the change already does with `crash-rules` and `context-fill`.

review.impact: The diff includes four lines of runtime timing output from a local run. This is noise in the change, and it will conflict with other branches that append to the same file.
review.fix: Drop the change with `git checkout bf28cd1 -- .werk/fold-ms.jsonl`. If the file is generated, add it to .gitignore.

review.impact: `& { role?: string }` is redundant, because `React.ComponentProps<"div">` already includes `role`. It adds noise to a shared UI primitive.
review.fix: Use `React.ComponentProps<"div">` alone.

review.impact: `pie` is null exactly when `settings` is null. The controls only render when `settings` is non-null, but the JSX still uses `pie?.level`, `pie?.percent ?? 0` and `pie ? pieGradient(pie) : undefined` in three places. This is dead branching that hides the invariant.
review.fix: Compute `pie` unconditionally inside the `settings !== null` branch, for example by extracting a `ModelControls` component that receives non-null settings and pie. That also shortens the large ChatHead.

review.impact: The CHOICES table repeats the three-way model/advisor choice from the server's `parsePick`. The two lists can drift apart.
review.fix: Share the choice list from a module both sides import. If that is not feasible, add a comment pointing to src/chat/model-pick.ts.

review.impact: `body as unknown as ModelSettings` is a double cast that bypasses type checking. Only `window` is validated before it. A malformed event can put a settings object with wrong or missing fields into state.
review.fix: Add a small `isModelSettings` guard that checks model, advisor, used and window, and use it instead of the cast.

review.impact: The local `window` shadows the global `window` name. In `settings()` and `noteSession` it is easy to misread, and it invites mistakes if DOM types are in scope.
review.fix: Rename it to `contextWindow`.

review.impact: `emit` now excludes four event names by chained `!==` tests. The next live-only event needs another clause.
review.fix: Use a `const LIVE_ONLY = new Set(["delta","status","model","cleared"])` and test `!LIVE_ONLY.has(event.name)`.

review.impact: The `names` helper now has a nested ternary inside a template literal, which is hard to read.
review.fix: Extract a small `idOf(e)` function with early returns.

review.impact: The `refused` alert in `chat-head.tsx` is never tested. If `setModel` or `clearContext` returns a reason, nothing checks that the header shows it. The fake store only ever returns null, so the busy-refusal path from the server is unverified.
review.fix: Add a test where the fake `setModel` or `clearContext` resolves to "a turn is running…". Assert that `[role=alert]` shows that text, and that it clears once a later call returns null.

review.impact: The new `post` helper, `load` with `settings`, and the `model` and `cleared` event handling have no unit test. A non-ok response with a JSON message, a non-JSON body, a network throw, and a `model` event without a numeric `window` (which is ignored) are all untested. No `chat-store` test was added in the diff.
review.fix: Add chat-store tests with a fake `deps.fetch`. Cover: ok gives null; a refusal gives its `message`; a non-JSON error gives `the server answered N`; a throw gives a string; `load` applies `settings`; a `model` event with no `window` is ignored; `cleared` resets the turns.

review.impact: Several session paths have no test: `setModel` to the same pick (a no-op that should not restart); `clear` or `setModel` called before any child has launched (`restart` returns early, so settings change but nothing relaunches); a dead-session replay with a second failure (it must report, not loop); and a `result` before `init` for a login error.
review.fix: Add a same-pick no-op test that expects one launch. Add a test for `setModel` before the first send that checks the first launch uses the new model. Add a test where the replayed session also crashes with the dead-session text.

review.impact: The existing test "an exit ends every open turn…" now needs a fatal stderr to avoid the new retry. Its original case, a bare `crash: 3` with no stderr, is no longer covered as ending the turn with `exited with code 3`. The retry test only covers the stderr "boom" case.
review.fix: Add a case with two bare `crash` replies that asserts the `the agent exited with code N` text plus the delivery notice.

review.impact: A `model` live event is cast to `ModelSettings` after checking only that `window` is a number. If the payload is malformed, a bad `model` or a non-number `used` reaches state. `selectValue` then yields a value that matches no option, and `pieOf` gets a non-number. The channel is server-originated and token-protected, so this is a robustness gap and not an exploit.
review.fix: Validate `model`, `advisor` and `used` before the cast. A small `isModelSettings` guard would do, and `load()` could use it for `settings` too.

review.impact: `STDERR_LIMIT` rises from 4,000 to 50,000, and the full agent stderr, now prefixed with `earlyError`, goes to the browser in `turn-end.exited` and into the kept history. If the agent prints environment details, credentials or paths on failure, more of that reaches every page that loads the chat. The report is meant to be complete (#werk-fullerr), so the exposure is by design.
review.fix: Keep the full-error behaviour. Optionally redact obvious secrets (tokens, `sk-…` strings) from stderr before emitting it, and keep the limit as the cap.

review.impact: `readSettings` accepts any numeric `used` and `window`, including negative numbers, NaN-like values and huge values. A hand-edited `chat-model.json` could set `window` to 0 or a negative number. The client clamps the pie, but the server would carry that `window` until the next turn result reports a real one.

review.impact: `menu={{ commands: store.commands, cards }}` builds a new object on every render. Composer's effect lists `menu` as a dependency (composer.tsx ~line 83), so it re-runs on every ChatPane render. ChatPane re-renders on every store update, including each streaming delta. While a `/word` is open, that sends a `/commands` request for each delta and resets `names` each time.
review.fix: Keep the `MenuSource` object stable. Build it once with useMemo or at module level, or have the effect depend on `menu.commands` instead of `menu`. Passing a stable `commands` function would also work.

review.impact: `closed` is set on Escape and never cleared. The comment says it lasts until the word's start or trigger changes. `track` only resets `selected`, and it leaves `closed` alone when the word becomes null. After Escape on `/re`, the user can clear the text or send, then type `/` at position 0 again. The key `/0` still matches, so the menu stays suppressed. The user has to type a different trigger or position before it comes back.
review.fix: In `track`, call `setClosed(null)` when the new word is null, or when its `trigger + start` differs from the closed key. Also reset it in `send` and `choose`.

review.impact: Composer now holds a lot of menu state: word, names, selected and closed. It also has the command fetch, the item building and the key handling. That makes it harder to test and read than the single-purpose modules the project asks for.
review.fix: Move the menu state, the command fetch and the key handling into a `useWordMenu` hook or a small WordMenu component. Composer would then only pass in the text and caret and receive items and handlers.

review.impact: `text.slice(0, caret).search(/\S*$/)` backtracks from every start position. When the text before the caret is a long run of non-space characters followed by whitespace, the cost grows quadratically. It runs on every input and select event, so pasting a very large unbroken string could freeze the user's own tab. It is a self-inflicted slowdown only, with no server or cross-user effect.
review.fix: Find the word start with a linear scan. For example, loop `i` back from `caret` while `!/\s/.test(text[i - 1])`, or take `lastIndexOf` over the whitespace characters. Use `start = i`.

review.impact: `menu={{ commands: store.commands, cards }}` builds a new object on every ChatPane render. ChatPane re-renders on every chat store update, including each streamed delta. Each run cancels the previous request, sends a new GET `/commands`, and calls `setNames` with a fresh array. That gives a fetch per streamed chunk and extra composer re-renders.
review.fix: Keep `menu` referentially stable. Build it once with `useMemo(() => ({ commands: store.commands, cards }), [store, cards])`, or define it outside the render. Alternatively, depend on `menu?.commands` in the effect. Also keep `cards` stable in main.tsx, or read it through a ref.

review.impact: restart() sets child to null, then awaits the old child's pump and only then calls launch(). If a send arrives during that await, dispatch() runs `child ??= launch()` and starts a new child. restart() then overwrites `child` with a second launch. The first new child is leaked, keeps running, and its pump exits quietly because `child !== spawned`. The race window is narrow, but setModel and clear are both open to it.
review.fix: Launch only if child is still null after the await (`child ??= launch()`). Alternatively, hold a `restarting` flag that makes setModel, clear and send wait or refuse until restart() finishes.
