review.fix: Trust the server's `{ commands: string[] }` shape, or keep a single narrow type guard. Keep the `res.ok` check.

review.impact: The diff includes 22 lines of local timing telemetry (all `events: 0`) from the build runs. This is noise in the change and invites merge conflicts.
review.fix: Revert the file (`git checkout -- .werk/fold-ms.jsonl`) or keep it out of the commit.

review.impact: The new `commands()` has three failure paths: a non-ok response, a non-array or non-string payload, and a thrown fetch. None has a test, and the client store tests are not touched. Breaking the fallback to `[]` would go unnoticed, and the composer would then throw or show a broken menu.
review.fix: Add chat-store tests with a fake `deps.fetch`. Cover a good list, a mixed-type list that is filtered to strings, `ok: false`, a rejected fetch, and a body where `commands` is not an array. Each failure should give `[]`.

review.impact: The new `/commands` route has no test. Nothing checks that it returns `{commands}` from the session, or `[]` when `context.chat` is absent. Only the e2e test exercises it, and only on the happy path.
review.fix: Add a route test in the existing serve route tests. It should call `/commands` with and without a chat session and assert the JSON body.

review.impact: `closed` is never cleared and is keyed on trigger plus start. After Escape on `/re`, a user who clears the box and types `/` again, or types a new word at the same start, gets no menu. The comment says it stays closed only until the start or trigger changes, and no test covers this. The Escape test only checks that Enter then sends.
review.fix: Reset `closed` in `track` when the word becomes null or its key changes. Add a test: Escape, clear the text, type `/re` again, and assert the menu opens.

review.impact: The composer tests leave several menu behaviours unchecked. These are ArrowUp wrap-around, mouse-down selection, the IME `isComposing` guard, the empty-command-list case, and the card-menu Escape case. A regression in any of them would not fail a test.
review.fix: Add short tests for ArrowUp from index 0 selecting the last option, a mousedown on an option inserting it, and no menu opening when `commands()` returns `[]`.

review.impact: The test checks only one start line. It does not check that a later start line replaces the names, which is what the doc comment promises, or that the returned array is a copy. A session restart that keeps stale names would pass.
review.fix: Send two turns with different `slash_commands` and assert the second list replaces the first. Also assert that mutating the returned array does not change the next `commands()` result.

review.impact: Timing-log lines from test runs were committed with the change. They are unrelated noise in the diff.
review.fix: Drop the `.werk/fold-ms.jsonl` change from the commit.

review.impact: `text.slice(0, caret).search(/\S*$/)` is quadratic when the text holds a long run of non-whitespace followed by whitespace, for example a pasted base64 blob or minified text. At every position in the run the regex scans to the end of the run, fails `$`, and backtracks. `wordAt` runs on every input and select event, so a large paste can freeze the tab for seconds. This is a self-inflicted client-side stall, not a remote vulnerability.
review.fix: Find the word start with a linear scan. Walk back from `caret` while the previous character is not whitespace, or use `Math.max(text.lastIndexOf(' ', caret - 1), text.lastIndexOf('\n', caret - 1), text.lastIndexOf('\t', caret - 1)) + 1`. You could also stop looking once the word is longer than a small cap.

review.impact: `text.slice(0, caret).search(/\S*$/)` is quadratic in the length of the last whitespace-free run. At each start position `\S*` consumes the rest of the run, fails on `$`, and backtracks. `wordAt` runs on every `onChange` and `onSelect`. Pasting a long token with no spaces (base64, minified code, a long URL) therefore freezes the composer on each keystroke or caret move.
review.fix: Scan backwards from the caret to the previous whitespace, e.g. `let start = caret; while (start > 0 && !/\s/.test(text[start - 1])) start--;`. That is linear, and it also avoids slicing the whole text on each call.

review.impact: `menu={{ commands: store.commands, cards }}` builds a new object on every ChatPane render, and ChatPane re-renders on every streamed delta. The Composer effect in `client/app/composer.tsx` (about line 75) lists `menu` in its dependencies. While a `/` word is active, every delta cancels the effect and sends a fresh `GET /commands`, and then `setNames` re-renders the Composer. That is a network request and a re-render per streamed token.
review.fix: Memoize the object with `useMemo(() => ({ commands: store.commands, cards }), [store, cards])`. Alternatively, drop `menu` from the effect dependencies and read it through a ref, so the fetch runs only when the slash word opens.

causeOfLast.why: an earlier pass replaced the route tests instead of adding to them, and the cards were clear about the behaviour.

pass_end.decision: a pass named a spec gap as the cause of a failure: no card named the settings file or said where it sits.

review.impact: `restart()` calls `forgetChild()`, kills the old child, then awaits its pump before it runs `child = launch()`. `setModel` and `clear` have already passed the `idle()` check, and a `send` that arrives during that await runs `dispatch` and does `child ??= launch()`. When `restart` resumes, it overwrites `child` with a second spawn, so the first child leaks as an orphan `claude` process. The first turn's replies then arrive from a child that `child !== spawned` filters out, so the turn can hang. The window is narrow but real, because the await spans a process exit.
review.fix: Make `restart` safe against a concurrent send. Set a `restarting` flag (or keep a promise) that makes `send` and `dispatch` wait for it, or refuse the send. Or make `restart` launch with `child ??= launch()` and not overwrite a child that already exists. Alternatively, do the kill and relaunch without an await between `forgetChild` and `launch`, and let the pump's `child !== spawned` check absorb the old exit.

review.impact: A `model` event is accepted when only `window` is a number, and the body is then cast with `as unknown as ModelSettings`. A malformed event could put a settings object with missing or mistyped `model`, `advisor` or `used` into the state. `ChatHead` then picks a wrong `select` value or renders NaN for the pie.
review.fix: Check `model`, `advisor` and `used` as well, or share a small parser with the `load()` path, which applies `settings` with no check at all.

review.impact: Changing the shared `SONNET` constant to the `[1m]` id changes the model of every role that uses it, not only the chat. `chat-state-store` and `context-fill` now rely on the `[1m]` suffix for window detection, so the two are coupled implicitly.
review.fix: Give the chat its own pinned constant, or note in the code that all roles are meant to move to the 1M id. Make `windowOf` read the same constant instead of matching the string suffix.

review.impact: `createSession` now has many interleaved mutable flags: `initSeen`, `earlyError`, `stopped`, `attempts`, `pick`, `used`, `window` and `sessionId`. `handleExit`, `noteSession`, `restart` and `dispatch(replay)` all read and write them, so the crash, resume and settings logic is hard to follow and change. `crash-rules.ts`, `context-fill.ts` and `model-pick.ts` were split out as pure modules, but the stateful parts stayed in one closure. That cuts against the single-purpose, small-module rule.
review.fix: Move the settings state (`pick`, `used`, `window`, persist, announce) and the session-id and crash bookkeeping into their own small module or factory. Have `session.ts` call it.

review.impact: `noteSession` does four unrelated jobs: it records the session id, captures an early error, tracks token use and tracks the window. It also returns a boolean meaning 'swallow this line', which is easy to misread at the call site.
review.fix: Split it into a function that records usage and a function that classifies init and early-result lines. Name the return value, for example `consumed`.

review.impact: The `emit` filter now lists four event names that are not kept in history. The list will keep growing as event types are added.
review.fix: Use a `const TRANSIENT = new Set(["delta", "status", "model", "cleared"])` and check `!TRANSIENT.has(event.name)`.

review.impact: `body as unknown as ModelSettings` is a double-cast escape hatch. It checks only that `window` is a number, so a malformed `model` event goes into state unvalidated.
review.fix: Add a small type-guard or parser for `ModelSettings` and use it here and in `load()`.

review.impact: `CHOICES` repeats the three-choice table that `src/chat/model-pick.ts` defines on the server (`parsePick` and `DEFAULT_PICK`). The two copies can drift apart.
review.fix: Keep the table here, but document it as mirroring `model-pick.ts`. Or move the shared pick type and table to a module that both sides import.

review.impact: `& { role?: string }` is redundant. `React.ComponentProps<"div">` already includes `role`.
review.fix: Drop the extra intersection type.

review.impact: The diff includes 24 lines of machine-generated timing noise from build runs. This adds churn and merge conflicts unrelated to the change.
review.fix: Leave `.werk/fold-ms.jsonl` out of the commit, or gitignore it if it is not meant to be tracked.

review.impact: The new `post` helper (a non-ok response with a message, a non-JSON body, a thrown fetch), `setModel`/`clearContext`, the `model` and `cleared` events and the `settings` read in `load()` have no unit test. `createChatStore` has no test file, and the e2e tests cover only the success path. A regression in refusal reporting, such as the 409 busy message not reaching the header, would pass every test.
review.fix: Add `client/lib/chat-store.test.ts` with a fake `deps.fetch`. Cover: `setModel` posts `{model, advisor}` to `/model` with the token; a 409 with a message resolves to that message; a non-JSON error body resolves to `the server answered <status>`; a rejected fetch resolves to the error string; `load()` applies `settings`; and a `cleared` event empties the turns.

review.impact: The refusal path is untested. `setRefused` and the `role=alert` span are never exercised, and neither is the `choice` lookup that finds no match. The busy-disabled test checks the select and the Clear button but not the pie, and it does not check that the pie still opens.
review.fix: Add a test whose fake store resolves `setModel` with 'busy' and assert that `[role=alert]` shows that text. Assert that clicking the pie while busy still opens the popover.

review.impact: The assertion `expect(body.settings).toBeDefined()` can never fail, because `settings()` always returns an object. It does not check the shape or the defaults, so removing `settings` from a field would still pass.
review.fix: Assert `toEqual({ model: 'sonnet', advisor: 'opus', used: 0, window: 1_000_000 })`, the defaults of a fresh project.

review.impact: There is no test that `setModel` with the pick already in use is a no-op that does not restart the agent. There is no test that `setModel` while no child is running only changes the next launch. There is no test for the dead-session replay when the stored id is cleared while a second message is queued. The `stopped` flag that stops `stop()` from being retried is also uncovered.
review.fix: Add a test that calls `setModel` with the current pick and asserts that `launchesOf(p)` stays at 1. Add a test that calls `stop()` mid-turn and asserts that no relaunch follows.

review.impact: The existing test 'an exit ends every open turn…' now injects a login-error stderr so that the exit is fatal. It no longer covers a plain crash ending its turns. That case is covered only by the two-crash test, so the check that every open turn ends, including a waiting turn, is now weaker.
review.fix: Keep a variant that crashes twice with a queued second send, and assert that both turns end.

review.impact: A `model` event is cast to `ModelSettings` after only `typeof body.window === "number"` is checked. The server sends these events, so the risk is low. A malformed event, such as a missing or unknown `model` or a missing `used`, would still reach the state. The header would then render a `select` value that matches no option and `pieOf` would get `undefined`.
review.fix: Check `model`, `advisor` and `used` before the cast. Or reuse a client-side copy of the `parsePick` check, plus a numeric check on `used` and `window`.

review.impact: `STDERR_LIMIT` rose from 4000 to 50000, and the whole agent stderr now goes into the turn-end `exited` text and into the history. That text can include paths, environment details or credential diagnostics. Anyone who can read the live channel or `GET /chat` sees it. Both are token-gated and local, so the exposure is small.
review.fix: Keep the full text, as the decision requires. Make sure nothing outside the trusted page reads it, and consider redacting values that look like keys or tokens before emitting.

causeOfLast.why: an earlier pass added board log events that #vi-board-state does not list, and left the held-out badge as plain text on the card and out of the drawer.

grade.gap: src/board/obligations.ts reads the obligation from the decision log, as this card says. But nothing else in the codebase writes that record yet. This pass chose its event shape itself: obligation.created {id, ticket}, obligation.followed {id, cards}, and node.proposed with an obligation field. The ticket that builds the CLI's obligation write must use the same shape, or Decisions will stay empty. Before then, the next pass should propose a card for that event shape.

review.impact: The project context imports `boardLogBeside` from `serve/board-route.ts`, which is a route module that pulls in the view, the map reader and the Response helpers. The pipeline log's path helper sits in its own store module (`pipeline/log-store`), so this one doesn't match. It also adds a dependency from the projects layer to the serve layer, and it works against #werk-stack-modules.
review.fix: Move `boardLogBeside` into `src/board/log-store.ts`, next to `readBoard`. Import it from there in both `context.ts` and `board-route.ts`.

review.impact: `boardRead` reads and parses the decision log twice per request, once in `readMap` and once in `readFileSync` for `obligationsOf`. The board polls every 3 seconds, and each of those reads happens on the server for every client.
review.fix: Read the log text once and pass it to both consumers. Alternatively, have `readMap` expose the text it already read.

review.impact: `boardApi` never checks `res.ok`. A 4xx or 5xx response, or an HTML error page, makes `.json()` throw. `Board` swallows that error with an empty `catch`, so the page stays on 'Loading the board…' with no sign of what went wrong.
review.fix: Throw on `!res.ok` in `boardApi`. Have `Board` show an error state instead of discarding the rejection.

review.impact: `detailOf` uses a nested ternary to build `text`, and it calls `parseTicket(`${ticket.id}`, raw)`, where the template string adds nothing. Both make the code harder to read.
review.fix: Compute `text` with early returns or a small helper, and pass `ticket.id` directly.

review.impact: The change includes 12 lines of machine-written timing noise from running the tests. They add churn to the diff and will conflict on merge.
review.fix: Drop the file from the commit, and consider ignoring it. The same goes for the cosmetic reformat of `ticket.builds.push` in `src/board/fold.ts`.

review.impact: Sidebar repeats the same markup in several places. The `list` helper exists, but Cites, Blockers and the Decisions followed list each rebuild the empty-`none` and `<ul>` shape by hand. The `/map/${encodeURIComponent(id)}` link is written three times. A change to the link or the empty state has to be made in several places.
review.fix: Make one `MapLink({id})` component and one `List<T>({items, render})` helper that renders `none` when empty. Use them for Cites, Blockers and Decisions.

review.impact: The board wiring is added inline to the already long `start()`. It adds four mutable locals (`boardTick`, `boardRoot`, `boardPrefs`, `view`), a `drawBoard` that re-enters itself through `onPrefs`, and a `setInterval` that is never cleared. Fetch and parse code sits next to the render glue, so it is hard to test and to change on its own.
review.fix: Move the board mount into its own module, for example `client/lib/board-mount.ts`. It would expose `mountBoard(body, project)`, `bump()` and `unmount()`, and own the root, the tick, the prefs and the timer. `main.tsx` would then only call those.

review.impact: The `text` expression has a nested ternary with a redundant branch. `raw === undefined` already makes `parsed` null, so the outer check does nothing. `parseTicket(`${ticket.id}`, raw)` uses a needless template literal.
review.fix: Write `const text = parsed && firstSection !== undefined ? parsed.lines.slice(firstSection - 1).join("\n") : ""`. Pass `ticket.id` directly.

review.impact: `readPrefs` returns the shared `DEFAULTS` object. A caller that mutates the result would corrupt the defaults for every later read.
review.fix: Return `{ ...DEFAULTS }`, or freeze `DEFAULTS`.

review.impact: There are three `biome-ignore` suppressions: two for `useExhaustiveDependencies` on `tick` and one for `noArrayIndexKey`. Each has a reason, but the `tick` ones hide a dependency that the effect never reads.
review.fix: Keep the `noArrayIndexKey` one. For the two `tick` effects, use a `refresh` counter in the dependency array that the effect body uses, for example by passing `tick` into `load`, so no suppression is needed.

review.impact: The `ticket.builds.push` call is reformatted from one line to six with no change in meaning. This adds diff noise to an unrelated file. `.werk/fold-ms.jsonl` also carries 12 lines of generated churn in the diff.
review.fix: Revert the reformat. Leave `.werk/fold-ms.jsonl` out of the commit or gitignore it.

review.impact: `expect(column("building")).toContainText("0")` passes on almost any text. The column heading, the ticket titles and the ids can all contain a 0. It does not show that the building column is empty or that its count is 0.
review.fix: Assert the count directly, for example `expect(column("building").locator("h2 span")).toHaveText("0")`. Also assert that the column has no `[data-slot=ticket-card]`.

review.impact: The held-out test only covers a red result on a done ticket. Nothing checks that `heldoutRed` stays null for a green held-out result. Nothing checks that a red result on a ticket outside `done` shows no badge. If either guard in `boardView` is removed, the tests still pass. The `running` flag also has no test for a ticket outside `building` that still has a live pid.
review.fix: Add cases for a green held-out step on a done ticket and for a red one on a non-done ticket. Both should give `heldoutRed` null. Add a case where a ticket outside `building` has an alive pid and `running` is false.

review.impact: The damaged-value test covers invalid JSON and a bare number. It does not cover an object with wrongly typed fields, such as `{"rail":"yes","tall":1}`. It does not cover `null` or an array. The `=== true` coercion is therefore untested. Projects are also not tested against each other: nothing shows that two project names use separate keys.
review.fix: Add a case for `{"rail":"yes"}`, which should give false. Add a case that writes prefs for project `p` and reads project `q`, which should give the defaults.

review.impact: The tests never reject `load` or `loadLog`. They never change `tick` to check that the board reads again, and they never advance the 2-second log poll. The failure paths and the polling the component relies on are untested. A regression there, such as the log not refreshing or a failed load clearing the board, would go unnoticed.
review.fix: Add a test where `load` rejects and the loading placeholder stays. Add a test that re-renders with a new `tick` and asserts that `load` was called again, plus a test that `loadLog` rejects without crashing the drawer.

review.impact: `TICKET_ID` is `/^[^/\s]+\/\d{2}$/`, so a plan id of `..` passes. `ticketText` then reads `.werk/<NN>.md` instead of a file under `tickets/`. The id comes from the local board log, which werk writes, so only a tampered log could use this, and it reads at most one `NN.md` file.
review.fix: Reject a plan id of `.` or `..` in `TICKET_ID`. Or check in `ticketText` that the resolved path is still under `<.werk>/tickets`.

review.impact: `sessionLogOf` takes the `log` path from a `build.started` event and reads it as given. An absolute path or one with `..` can point anywhere on disk. `GET /board/log` then returns the lines that parse as `{time, event}`, and only the first 200 characters of each. The server is local and the board log is trusted, so this is a small exposure. It would matter if the board log ever took data from outside, or if the server were reachable over the network.
review.fix: Resolve the path and require that it sits under the project's `.werk/sessions` folder (or `.werk`). Otherwise answer no lines.

review.impact: Each live-log request reads the whole session log synchronously and parses every line as JSON, only to keep the last 200. A building session's log grows without limit. The drawer asks for it on open, every 2s, and again on every tick (each board event and each 3s poll). A multi-MB log would block the server's event loop and burn CPU on each request.
review.fix: Read only the end of the file. Read the last N KB with a positioned read (Bun.file(path).slice(size - N)), drop the first partial line, and summarise only those lines. The client could also send the byte offset it has already seen and get back only the new lines.

review.impact: The Drawer effect depends on `tick`. Every tick, from a board SSE event or the 3s timer, tears down and recreates the 2s log interval and fires an immediate log fetch. During a busy build, board events can arrive often, so the log is fetched far more often than every 2s. These extra fetches stack on top of the full-file parse described above.
review.fix: Remove `tick` from the log effect's dependencies and rely on the 2s interval. Alternatively, drop the interval and refresh the log only on tick.

review.impact: Each /board read, which the client triggers on every board event and every 3s, re-reads and re-parses three sources synchronously. These are the board log, the map log (once through readMap and again as raw text for obligationsOf), and every ticket file (an existsSync plus a readFileSync each). The work grows with log size and ticket count, and the decision log is read twice per request.
review.fix: Read the decision log text once and share it, or cache by mtime/size. Cache the ticket file text by mtime. Skip the response when nothing changed, for example with an ETag or a log-size version.

review.impact: The 30-second deadline is only checked between reads. If the executable starts but prints nothing, `reader.read()` never resolves and the loop never reaches the deadline check. The smoke step then hangs until the CI job timeout instead of failing with the 'did not serve' error and the output seen so far.
review.fix: Race each read against the remaining time, for example with `Promise.race` and a timer. Alternatively, set a `setTimeout` that calls `child.kill()` or `reader.cancel()` at the deadline. Clear the timer once the address is found.

review.impact: After the address is found, the reader on `child.stdout` is neither released nor drained. If the executable keeps writing to stdout, the pipe can fill and block it while the HTTP read is in flight.
review.fix: Call `reader.releaseLock()` after matching. Alternatively, keep draining stdout in the background until the child is killed.

review.impact: `smoke` is a CI step but is not part of the `check` target, which is described as 'every check in the merge loop's order'. A local `make check` can pass while CI fails on the smoke step.
review.fix: Add `smoke` to `check`, or note in the target description that it runs only in CI.

review.impact: The type `(typeof PLATFORMS)[number]` is written out three times, in `currentPlatform`'s return type and twice in `build`'s signature. A change to the platform shape means editing each spelling.
review.fix: Add `type Platform = (typeof PLATFORMS)[number];` near `PLATFORMS` and use it in all three places.

review.impact: The `dist/smoke` output folder is spelled in two places: `package.json`'s `smoke` script and `SMOKE_DIR` here. The two are coupled only by a comment, so if one changes the smoke run fails with a missing executable.
review.fix: Export the folder from `build.ts` and have `smoke.ts` import it. Alternatively, have the `smoke` script pass the built path to `smoke.ts` as an argument.

review.impact: The new `smoke` target is not part of `make check`, which is described as running every check in the merge loop's order. CI runs it but a local `make check` does not, so the two lists of checks can drift apart.
review.fix: Add `smoke` to `check`, or note in the `check` description that smoke is CI-only.

review.impact: The 30-second limit is only checked between reads. `reader.read()` blocks when the executable is alive but prints nothing, so the check is never reached. A hung executable then hangs the CI job until the runner's own timeout instead of failing with the 'did not serve' error. This failure path of the smoke check has no test.
review.fix: Race each read against the remaining time, for example with `Promise.race` and a timer. Alternatively, kill the child at the deadline so the stream ends. Add a test that feeds `waitForAddress` a stream that never emits and expects the rejection.

review.impact: `currentPlatform()` is new logic with a failure branch for an unsupported platform. It and the new `--current` argument parsing are not tested. `build.ts` has no test file. If the platform match or the flag handling regresses, only a full CI run shows it.
review.fix: Move the platform match and the argument parsing into a small pure function that takes a platform, an arch and argv. Add a test file covering a supported pair, an unsupported pair that throws, and `--current` in either argument position.

review.impact: `cleanEnv` drops `WERK_*` variables and forces `WERK_HOME`. That isolation is what the tests rule `#werk-test-store` and `#werk-test-external` require, but no test checks it. A change that leaked the caller's `WERK_*` variables would pass unnoticed.
review.fix: Export `cleanEnv` and add a unit test: given an environment containing `WERK_X`, it returns no `WERK_X` and returns the given `WERK_HOME`.

review.impact: The workflow uses actions/checkout@v4 and oven-sh/setup-bun@v2, which are mutable tags. If an upstream tag is moved or compromised, the runner executes that code. The job has read-only `contents` permission, so the exposure is limited. The same applies to the setup-bun step at line 22.
review.fix: Pin each third-party action to a full commit SHA and keep the version in a trailing comment. Let Dependabot update the pins.

review.impact: The 30s deadline is only checked between reads. If the executable stays alive but prints nothing, `reader.read()` blocks forever. The smoke step then hangs until the CI job times out, which is 6 hours by default, instead of failing after 30s.
review.fix: Race each read against the remaining time, for example with `Promise.race([reader.read(), Bun.sleep(deadline - Date.now()).then(() => ({ done: true, value: undefined }))])`. You can also kill the child on timeout, which closes stdout and ends the read.

review.impact: `make test` and `make test-coverage` run the whole unit suite twice on every CI run. This doubles that stage's time for no extra signal, because the coverage run already runs the same tests.
review.fix: Drop the separate `make test` step and let `make test-coverage` act as the unit test run. Keep both only if the Makefile needs `test` as a distinct gate.

causeOfLast.why: another ticket (the slash and card menus, card actions) merged first and edited the same session, routes, chat-store and e2e code.

review.impact: noteSession swallows every `result` event that arrives before a `system/init` event, and the reply stream never sees it. This is meant for the dead-session case, where the child exits straight after. A child that sends a result before init and then stays alive, such as a locally handled slash command, leaves the turn open forever. Nothing ends the turn, and the header stays busy with the model and clear controls disabled. The design relies on the child always exiting after an early error result.
review.fix: Only treat the early result as a start failure when `is_error` is true. Pass non-error results through to `feed`. Optionally end the turn with `earlyError` if the child has not exited shortly after.

review.impact: SONNET is shared by the builder and every other Sonnet role (lines 63-64), so changing it to the `[1m]` id switches all of them to the 1M-context model. That is a wider, cost-affecting change than the chat header needs. The only reason for it in this diff is `windowOf`, which reads the window from the id suffix.
review.fix: Keep the general SONNET constant as it was, and add a chat-only constant such as SONNET_1M in model-pick.ts for `choiceOf`. If every Sonnet role is meant to move, confirm that against the #sonnet-pin card.

review.impact: `setModel` and `clear` set `pick`, `sessionId` and the other state, then `await restart()`. The session counts as idle during that await, so a second call or a `send()` that arrives mid-restart can interleave with the old child's kill and the new launch. A send in that gap starts a child that `restart` then replaces, because `child ??= launch()` runs between `forgetChild` and `child = launch()`.
review.fix: Add a `restarting` flag, or make `idle()` false until `restart()` settles. Alternatively make `restart` synchronous by launching without awaiting the old pump, since the `child !== spawned` guard already protects it.

review.impact: `boardLog` reads the whole session log with `readFileSync` and parses every line just to keep the last 200. The client polls it every 2s, and again on each board tick. review.fix: Read only the tail of the file: seek to the last N KB (for example 64–256 KB), drop the first partial line, then call `tailLines`. Alternatively, cache by file size and mtime, and return the cached lines when neither has changed.

review.impact: Every `/board` request is fully synchronous. Done tickets are never dropped, so this grows without bound. The client calls it every 3s while the board is open, and again on each board log append. Each call blocks the server loop and the payload carries every ticket's full text, including done ones, even though only one drawer is open.
review.fix: Cache the result keyed on the mtime and size of board.jsonl, log.jsonl and the ticket files. Better, send only the columns and card data in `/board` and fetch a ticket's detail and text on demand when its drawer opens. Reuse the map that `readMap` already read instead of reading the decision log again.

review.impact: The Drawer's log effect depends on `tick`. Every tick, whether from a board event or the 3s timer, tears down the 2s interval, fires an immediate `loadLog` and starts a new interval. review.fix: Drop `tick` from the effect dependencies and let the 2s interval alone drive the log refresh. Skip a poll while the previous request is still in flight.

review.impact: The 3s board poll keeps running when the tab is hidden, because it only checks `view === "board"`. Each tick triggers the full `/board` read and the log poll for nothing.

A hand-edited or merged-in board log could still point it at any readable file. A relative path with `..` has the same effect.

review.impact: Each live-log poll reads the whole session log into memory and runs JSON.parse and summarise on every line, only to keep the last 200. Cost per poll grows with session length, so a long build can load the server with multi-MB reads and parses.
review.fix: Read only the tail of the file. Seek to the last ~64–256 KB, drop the partial first line, and summarise from there. Or cache by (path, size/mtime) and return the cached lines when nothing changed.

review.impact: Every board read (every 3s poll plus every board-log change) re-reads and re-folds the full board log and the full decision log. Work and payload grow with project history, not with what is on screen.

review.impact: The log effect depends on `tick`, which changes every 3s and on every board-log event. Each change tears down the 2s interval, fires an immediate extra fetch and restarts the interval. A building ticket therefore gets more log fetches than the 2s timer alone would give, and the log flickers back to the same data.
review.fix: Drop `tick` from the log effect's dependencies, since the 2s interval already refreshes it. Re-read on tick only if the ticket's `live` flag flips.

review.impact: renderCard is now a long function with several inline closures (sectioned, from, flag, kindOf). Replace `from` with two clearly named helpers such as `incoming(type)` and `outgoing(type)`. Share one `whyLine(label, node)` helper between Options and Ev.

review.impact: `rollups(map)` runs for every render, and the `own`/`all` names are vague. The same `Say`/`Ev` heading names are cryptic. The `row` function now takes an optional trailing `rollup` parameter, and the call site that passes it is awkward, with a nested ternary inside a multi-line call.

review.impact: The new `show` with no id only has a test for the empty-map failure (exit 1). grade.gap: client/main.tsx adds a `lastHtml` cache to the map store's show callback. The comment there reads "An identical read changes nothing, so a card's open question stays." review.impact: `toContain("0.0%")` is a substring match, so it also passes for `50.0%`, `70.0%` and `100.0%`. `formatLine` prints the value as `percent.toFixed(1).padStart(5)` followed by `%`. The assertion therefore can't tell a file with no own test (0%) from one that is partly covered or fully covered. If the gate reported the wrong percentage for a missing test, this test would still pass.
review.fix: Anchor the match so only a standalone 0.0% passes, for example `expect(r.out).toMatch(/(^|\s)0\.0%\s/)`. Alternatively, match the whole formatted line with its fail mark and file name.

review.impact: The board's state, drawing, store wiring and show/hide logic (about 80 lines) are written inline in `start()`. That function already holds the map, header and chat wiring, so every board ticket now edits `main.tsx`. This cuts against the single-purpose, small-module rule (#werk-stack-modules). The `logTicket` lookup (find the selected ticket, check it is building) also sits in `main.tsx` where no unit test reaches it.

review.impact: `readText` repeats the private `readText` helper in `src/board/log-store.ts`. The two copies can drift apart on how a missing or unreadable file is handled.
review.fix: Export one shared safe-read helper and use it in both places.

review.impact: Each new watcher adds another level of nested try/catch to unwind the earlier ones on failure. Adding a fourth watcher means a fourth level, and it is easy to leak a watcher.
review.fix: Open the watchers in a list. If one fails, close the ones already opened, then rethrow.

review.impact: `textOf` builds a file path from the ticket id with `id.split("/")` and a cast. An id with no `/` gives the path `tickets/<id>/undefined.md`, and an id containing `..` can point outside `tickets/`. Ids come from the local board log, so the risk is low. Even so, the path is built from unvalidated parts.
review.fix: Check that the id is `<plan>/<NN>` before building the path, and return undefined when it is not. Do the same check for `build.log` if it is meant to stay under the logs folder.

review.impact: `Sidebar` writes the Cites section out by hand, and the Retries section as well. They copy the `<section data-slot="fact" aria-label>` markup that `Facts` already produces. A change to how a fact section looks has to be made in three places.
review.fix: Give `Facts` an optional render prop or a `children` slot. Alternatively, pull out a small `Fact({title, children})` wrapper, and build the Cites, Retries and Decisions sections with it.

review.impact: About 70 lines of board wiring now sit inside `start()`. That includes the mutable `boardState`, `selected`, `prefs` and `boardRoot`, plus `drawBoard`, `showBoard` and `hideBoard`. `drawBoard` and `boardStore` refer to each other, so the order of definition matters. This works against the rule that modules should be single-purpose and small.
review.fix: Move the board controller into its own module, for example `client/lib/board-view.tsx`. It would export `createBoardView({body, project, storage})` returning `show` and `hide`, plus a `refresh` for the board signal.

review.impact: The same three lines, `await act(async () => root?.unmount()); host?.remove(); await render(...)`, are pasted into several tests. Each of those tests renders more than once. The `render` helper overwrites the module-level `root` and `host`, so a missed unmount leaks a root.
review.fix: Add a `rerender` or `reset()` helper that unmounts and removes the host. Alternatively, split the multi-render tests into one render per test.

review.impact: The diff includes four lines of machine-generated timing data. They are unrelated to this feature and add noise to the change.
review.fix: Leave the file out of the commit, for example with `git checkout .werk/fold-ms.jsonl`. If it is a telemetry file, ignore it.

review.impact: The store's main race guard is untested. This is the `latest` counter, which drops an older read that finishes after a newer one. The only test of it is a `stop()` during a read. Two overlapping `refresh()` calls, where the older one resolves last, are never exercised. A regression in the guard would show stale tickets or a stale log, and the tests would still pass. A failed log read that gives `lines: null` while the board still shows is also untested. Several tests wait with `Bun.sleep(10)`, which can be flaky under the parallel load that #werk-test-runner-parallel describes.
review.fix: Add a test with a fetch that can be released by hand. Start two refreshes, resolve the second and then the first, and assert that `show` ran once with the second result. Add a case where the log fetch returns 500 and `show` still gets `{board, lines: null}`. Await the returned promise of `refresh()` instead of sleeping where that is possible.

review.impact: The "process decides" test treats pid `2**22+99` as dead. It would fail if that pid ever existed, since pid_max can be raised above 2**22 on a Linux host. The test also only checks the real `pidAlive` through that one assumed-dead pid.
review.fix: Spawn a short-lived child, wait for it to exit, and use its pid as the dead one. Or inject `isAlive` as the other tests already do.

review.impact: The ticket id comes from board.jsonl and is split on '/' with no check. An id like '../x' makes the path tickets/../x.md, so the read leaves the tickets folder. The file is limited to *.md, and the board log is written by werk itself, so reach is small. A hand-edited or shared project log could still make /api/.../board return the text of other .md files.
review.fix: Reject ids that do not match /^[\w-]+\/\d+$/ before building the path, or check that the resolved path stays under <logdir>/tickets.

review.impact: build.log is taken from the board log and used as-is when it is absolute, and joined to the log folder otherwise, so '../..' escapes the folder. GET /board/log then returns summarised lines from any readable JSONL file with {at, event} records. The reachable data is limited to that shape, and the value comes from a log that werk writes, so exposure is low. It is still an unconstrained file read behind an HTTP route.
review.fix: Resolve the path and require it to sit inside the project's .werk folder, or inside the session-log folder werk writes to. Return no lines otherwise.

review.impact: previewOf JSON-parses and summarises every line of the session log, then keeps only the last 200. The drawer re-reads the log on every 4s poll and every board signal. A builder session log grows without bound, so a long build costs more per request over time. The read is synchronous (readFileSync) and runs on the server's event loop, so it blocks other requests.
review.fix: Read only the tail of the file, for example the last 256 KB, and drop the partial first line. Or walk the lines from the end and stop once 200 summarised events are collected. Keep the sync read bounded or make it async.

review.impact: Every call to /board does a full synchronous read. It folds the whole board log, folds the whole map log (readMap), and reads every ticket file, including done tickets, from disk. The client repeats this every 4s and on every board-log append. A burst of board events causes a burst of full re-reads. Because of the sync I/O, each one blocks the server's event loop. There is no debounce or cache.
review.fix: Debounce or coalesce the board signal on the client. Cache the folded board and map keyed on log mtime or size, and cache ticket text by mtime. Read ticket files only for tickets that are not done, or send text only for the open ticket.

review.impact: decisionsOf scans every obligation for each ticket and uses cards.some and followed.includes inside the loops. That is O(tickets × obligations) per board read, plus quadratic dedupe. Every ticket's full text and decisions are also serialized in each poll response, which inflates the payload.
review.fix: Group obligations by ticket once in boardView and use a Set for the dedupe. Consider sending the text only for the selected ticket, through a separate endpoint.

review.impact: The poll uses setInterval and starts a new refresh every 4s whether or not the previous one has finished. A slow server read stacks overlapping requests. Stale ones are discarded only after the work is already done. A board-signal burst also triggers one full refresh per signal.
review.fix: Skip the beat while a refresh is in flight, or chain the next poll with setTimeout after the read completes. Coalesce signal-driven refreshes into one trailing call.

The diff makes three choices that no named card gives. (1) The node.removed and node.restored events now carry an `actor` field (src/verbs/remove.ts, src/verbs/restore.ts, src/serve/card-action-route.ts). That adds to the event's data shape, and fold.ts does not check the field: the refusal lives only in the command line. (3) `remove --propose` skips the actor check, so an agent's proposal needs no say-so (src/verbs/remove.ts:26). This last one is implied by #werk-remove but not stated there. review.impact: The new `removal-actor` rule is only checked in the `remove` and `restore` verbs. The fold's `node.removed` and `node.restored` cases never look at `actor`. Accept is different: `acceptGhost` and `acceptRemoval` check the actor inside the fold. Any event that doesn't come through those two verbs, such as a hand-edited or merged log line, is applied with no actor. Replaying a log that holds an actor-less removal never reports `removal-actor`, so the `RuleName` entry in `fold.ts:141` is never produced by the fold. The rule is enforced in a different layer from the matching accept rule.
review.fix: Call `removalActorRefusal(event.actor, "remove")` in the `node.removed` fold case and `removalActorRefusal(event.actor, "restore")` in the `node.restored` case, before `removeCard` and `restoreCard`. Keep the verb-level check only as the early, friendly refusal. Add a fold-level test for an actor-less `node.removed` and `node.restored`.

review.impact: The verb prints the usage string `restore <id> --actor you` in two places. `remove.ts` already keeps its usage in a `USAGE` constant, so the two verbs now differ in style, and the two copies in `restore.ts` can drift apart.
review.fix: Add a `const USAGE = "usage: restore <id> --actor you";` at the top of `restore.ts` and use it in both error messages.

review.impact: The usage string `usage: restore <id> --actor you` is written out twice, in the parse-error branch and in the refusal branch. The two copies can drift apart. `remove.ts` already uses a `USAGE` constant for this.
review.fix: Add `const USAGE = "usage: restore <id> --actor you";` at the top of the file and use it in both error messages.

review.impact: The `--propose` path is the one case where `remove` skips the actor check (`if (!propose)` in remove.ts). No test covers it. If that guard were removed or inverted, `remove --propose` without `--actor` would start failing, or `--actor` would leak into `removal.proposed` events, and the suite would not catch either.
review.fix: Add a test that `werk remove <id> --propose` without `--actor` exits 0 and appends a `removal.proposed` event. Check that the card is still shown and that the event has no `actor` field.

review.impact: The web route now adds `actor: "you"` to `node.removed`. The diff has no test that fails without that line. If the line were dropped, nothing would flag a regression, and the event would lack the person's say-so.
review.fix: Add a card-action-route test. It should post a remove and assert that the appended event is `node.removed` with `actor: "you"`.

review.impact: The `--actor me` restore case checks only the exit code. The other refusal cases also check that the card state and event count are unchanged. A wrong actor could be refused after the event was already appended, and this case would still pass. `remove` with a wrong actor is not tested either.
review.fix: Assert that the event count and `shows` are unchanged after the `--actor me` restore. Add the same `--actor me` case for `remove`.

review.impact: The new `removed` verb has two untested paths. One is the empty case that prints "nothing is removed". The other is the usage error with exit code 2 when an id is passed. The empty case is only hit indirectly, through a `not.toContain` check.
review.fix: Add tests for `werk removed` on a fresh project (output is "nothing is removed") and for `werk removed x` (exit code 2). Also assert the exact line format `auth (with login, session)` instead of three `toContain` checks.

review.impact: The `removal-actor` rule is enforced only in the `remove` and `restore` verbs. The fold and `appendEvents` never check it. `accept-actor` is enforced in `ghost-rules.ts`, which sits below every writer. Any other writer can append `node.removed` or `node.restored` with no actor, or with `actor: "agent"`, and it takes effect. That path covers `cardActionRoute`, a future route, and a hand-edited log. The 'person must ask' guard therefore depends on each caller remembering to apply it. The guard is also self-asserted, because `--actor you` is a plain flag that an agent can pass.
review.fix: Enforce `removalActorRefusal` where `accept-actor` is enforced, in the fold's or appendEvents' validation of `node.removed` and `node.restored`. The verbs then only supply the actor. Keep `removal.proposed` exempt, as it is now.

Names must match /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$/, and a bad name gets a 400 (src/serve/chat-route.ts convoOf). Every live-channel part carries a 'convo' field. Every other conversation stores its state as session-<convo> and chat-model-<convo>.json in .werk (src/chat/chat-state-store.ts). (c) A tab's home card is set by its first message and stays fixed after that (client/lib/conversations.ts make()). (d) The tab list is persisted in localStorage per project. (e) Switching tabs moves the map to the tab's home card. (f) A '+' button in the strip opens a new conversation on the open card (client/app/tab-strip.tsx). (g) context.dead() reports the first dead session among all of them (src/projects/context.ts). The code also cites cards the builder did not name: #werk-mc-split, #werk-mc-asks-dot, #werk-mc-follow, #werk-mc-tab-bottom. Propose cards for these choices, or name them if they already exist.

The card says 'A message goes to the agent with the card the person has open'. In client/lib/conversations.ts make(), the store's card() returns convo.home once it is set, not deps.card(). So in tab A, if the person opens card C and sends a message, the turn names A. To fix: always send deps.card() with each message, and use home only as the chip's label.

The card says 'the card under the cursor becomes the context the chat already knows about'. In client/lib/conversations.ts make(), the card that goes with a message is pinned to the tab's home card, so the card the person navigates to never becomes the context. The fix is the same as for #werk-chat: send the open card, and use home only for the label.

Because make() in client/lib/conversations.ts sends the home card, the now-at and still-on lines name the tab's home card, not the open card. A person who navigates inside a tab gets a line for the wrong card.
The card says 'The open-card line in the chat names the card in the current address'. client/lib/conversations.ts make() sends the tab's fixed home card, not the card in the current address.

review.impact: The class `tag-pending-link` has no rule in client/index.css. The mark renders as a plain grey `.tag`, so the class name is dead as a style hook and the pending link looks like any other tag. The test only checks that the class name appears in the HTML.
review.fix: Add a `.tag-pending-link` rule in client/index.css, for example a dashed border in the proposed colour. Alternatively, reuse `tag-proposed` and drop the extra class.

review.impact: The test covers only the outgoing `supported_by` evidence row. The pending mark depends on `map.ghostEdges.includes(edge)`, which compares object identity. If the fold copies edges, the mark would disappear without any test failing. The test never checks that a real, non-ghost evidence row on the same card stays unmarked. It also never checks the ghost-edge case on the other side of a link, where `citedBy` rows get no mark.
review.fix: Add a second evidence excerpt that is already decided and linked to the same card. Assert that its row has no `tag-pending-link` while the ghost row does. Also add a case for the `citedBy` side, or a short comment saying that side is deliberately unmarked.

review.impact: `map.ghostEdges.includes(edge)` scans the whole ghost-edge array once for each evidence row. The cost is evidence rows × ghost edges for each card page render. Both counts are small for one card, so it only matters if ghost edges grow very large.
review.fix: Build a `Set` of ghost edges once, either on the folded map or at the top of `sections`. Then use `ghosts.has(edge)`. This is optional at the current scale.

Convo is keyed by tab.id, so it remounts on a switch, and useLayoutEffect scrolls to the end. The grader could not run these tests, so this score comes from reading them.

The proposed cards #werk-mc-split-convo-name and #werk-mc-tabs-new-button now record items (a), (b), (c) and (f). Items (d), localStorage, and (e), the map following the tab, are gone. Name these cards, or point the comments at the proposed cards.

review.impact: `<Convo key={tab.id}>` unmounts the whole conversation view on every tab switch. That drops the Composer's local state, so a half-typed draft or attached images vanish when the person clicks another chip. The log's scroll position and its following flag also reset. With tabs, switching away mid-compose is routine, so this loses user input.
review.fix: Keep the Composer state per conversation. Either render every tab's Convo and hide the inactive ones, or lift the draft and images into the Convo or ChatStore so they survive the remount. Then limit the scroll-to-end behaviour to a real first view.

review.impact: `sessionOf` creates and keeps a session for any name that matches CONVO_NAME. A GET to `/chat?convo=...` is enough to do it. The `chats` map has no bound and nothing removes an entry. A typo or a script can pile up sessions, and each session reads or writes `session-<name>` and `chat-model-<name>.json` beside the log. Every one of them is also stopped on close and counted in `runningTurns`.
review.fix: Make the read-only GET not create a session. Return an empty history for a name that has no session yet, or cap the number of conversations per project. Consider removing a session when its tab is closed.

review.impact: The `card` dep is also a mutation hook: reading the open card sets `convo.home` and calls `changed()` from inside the store's send path. `store: null as unknown as ChatStore` is a cast that hides a half-built object. The coupling is implicit and easy to break.
review.fix: Have the store report 'sent on card X' through an explicit callback, such as an `onSend(card)` dep. Build the store first, and then create the Convo object that points at it, so the cast is not needed.

review.impact: Tabs opened with `open()` are not persisted or rediscovered. After a reload only `main` exists on the client, while the server still holds the other conversations' sessions and files. Those conversations become unreachable orphans.
review.fix: If this is intentional, say so in a comment. Otherwise keep the list of conversation ids, for example on the server, and restore the tabs in `load()`.

review.impact: The diff includes generated timing log lines that have nothing to do with this change. They add noise and can cause merge conflicts.
review.fix: Drop this file from the commit with `git checkout` on it, or ignore it.

review.impact: The pair `const convo = convoOfRequest(req); if (typeof convo !== "string") return convo;` is copied into chatRoute, askRoute, modelRoute and clearRoute. A fifth route has to remember to repeat it. The `string | Response` union also makes each caller narrow it by hand.
review.fix: Add a small wrapper, for example `withConvo(req, (convo) => ...)`. Alternatively, resolve the convo once in projectRoute and pass it to each route as an argument.

review.impact: The /commands branch uses `convoOf(...) ?? ""` to turn an invalid name into a key that matches no session. This is an obscure trick and it duplicates the convo handling in chat-route.ts. An invalid name returns an empty list instead of a 400, which is inconsistent with the other routes.
review.fix: Export a helper from chat-route.ts, for example `commandsRoute(context, req)`. Have it use convoOfRequest and `context.chats?.get(convo)`.

review.impact: `store: null as unknown as ChatStore` is a type escape hatch used to build a self-referential object. The `card` callback also has a hidden side effect: it sets `convo.home` and calls `changed()` whenever the store reads the open card. Both make the code harder to follow.
review.fix: Create a `let home` and the store first, then assemble the Convo object. Alternatively, make `home` a getter and keep the first-message logic in an explicit onSend hook.

review.impact: The tests use `a as never` and `bTab as never` casts to pass possibly undefined tabs to chipBlinks. These silence the type checker.
review.fix: Narrow the tabs first, for example `const a = convos.get().tabs[0]; if (!a) throw ...`. You can also pass `chipBlinks` the store, or give it a non-optional input.

review.impact: MAIN_CONVO is defined in both client/lib/chat-store.ts and src/chat/chat-state-store.ts, and the two copies can drift apart.
review.fix: Keep the two copies in step with a comment that names the other. Or share one constant if the client already imports shared code from src.

review.impact: The diff includes 12 lines of appended runtime telemetry that have nothing to do with the feature. They add noise to the diff and invite merge conflicts.
review.fix: Drop this file from the commit with `git checkout -- .werk/fold-ms.jsonl`.

review.impact: The new tests cover only the POST /chat route and one invalid name. Nothing checks that /ask, /model, /clear and /commands pick the conversation named in `?convo=`. A regression there would send an answer, a model switch or a clear to the main conversation. Nothing checks that those routes refuse a bad name. `convoOf` is never tested directly for null, an empty string, a valid name or a name longer than 40 characters. The `?? ""` fallback in routes.ts for /commands is also untested.
review.fix: Add a unit test for `convoOf` with null, empty, valid, uppercase and over-long input. Add route tests that /ask, /model and /clear act on the named conversation and not on main, and that they return 400 for a bad name. Add one test that /commands reads the named conversation.

review.impact: The `suffix` logic is new. It keeps the original file names for main and gives other conversations their own session and settings files. No test checks that main keeps `session` and `chat-model.json`, that another conversation writes different files, or that reading and clearing one conversation leaves the others alone. A mistake here would make two conversations share a saved session id and resume each other's agent. The route test does not catch this because it uses a stubbed agent.
review.fix: Add a chat-state-store test in a temporary directory. It should write, read and clear the session and settings for 'main' and for 'x'. It should assert the file names and that the two conversations stay independent.

review.impact: `runningTurns`, `background`, `dead` and `stopTurns` now combine every conversation, and `closeContext` stops all of them. None of this is tested. A conversation that is skipped would leave an agent running after the project closes, or hide a running turn from the busy check.
review.fix: Add a test that puts two stub sessions in `context.chats`. It should check that `runningTurns` and `background` combine both, that `dead` reports whichever is dead, and that `stopTurns` and `closeContext` stop both.

review.impact: Several new client paths have no test. They are `focus` with an unknown id or the active id, `load` across tabs, the 'New conversation' label for a tab with no home card, the `+` button, and a `cleared` event for another conversation being dropped. `load`, `commands` and `answer` also use the per-conversation URL, but only the send URL is asserted. A part with no `convo` field falling back to main is untested too.
review.fix: Add short tests for these cases. Assert the `?convo=` URL on load, ask and commands. Assert that a `cleared` event for another conversation does not clear this tab.

review.impact: The first assertion in the 'strip below the composer' test is vacuous. It checks only that the strip's previous sibling is not itself, and that is always true. The test would still pass if the strip were above the composer. The test title promises a check of placement.
review.fix: Assert that the strip is the last child of `[data-slot="chat-pane"]`. Also assert that the composer comes before it, for example with `compareDocumentPosition`.

review.impact: The GET branch of chatRoute calls sessionOf, so a GET with any valid ?convo name builds a session and stores it in context.chats. The GET needs no token. The Map has no cap, and every session reads its saved files when built. A page or script that can reach the server can add sessions without limit, and so can a token holder who sends to many names. Each sent-to name also starts its own agent process. The convo name is checked against CONVO_NAME, so it cannot reach the file paths in session-<convo> or chat-model-<convo>.json. The only effect is memory and process growth.
review.fix: On GET, read history only from a session that already exists, and return empty events and default settings for an unknown name. Create sessions only on authenticated POSTs. Optionally cap the number of conversations per project, for example 20.

review.impact: `sessionOf` builds and caches a session for any name that matches `CONVO_NAME`. A plain GET to `/chat?convo=<new name>` is enough, because it creates the session and reads its saved files. `context.chats` has no cap and no eviction, so closed tabs and probing names keep sessions in memory until the project closes. Every session's agent also stays alive.
review.fix: Don't create a session on GET. Return an empty history for an unknown convo, and create sessions only on send. Optionally cap the number of conversations per project, or stop idle sessions that have no tab.

review.impact: Every store change in any tab calls `changed()`, which copies the tab array and notifies all listeners. During streaming that re-renders `ChatPane` and `TabStrip` on every part, and re-renders `Convo` and `ChatLog` a second time. The `Convo` re-render comes from its parent, on top of the one from its own store subscription. The work is small and bounded by the number of tabs.
review.fix: Notify the view only when something the strip uses changes, such as an ask count change or a home change. Or wrap `Convo` in `React.memo`.

causeOfLast.why: a load-induced timeout in a test unrelated to this ticket; it passes alone with the project's 15-second limit, and I changed nothing for it.

grade.gap: src/plan/scope.ts lastChanges is documented as 'the line of the last event that names each card as its id or as the end of a link', but it reads only the keys id and from. The to end of an edge never counts, so the 'at' that the plan start event records for a card can be too early. Either add "to" to the key list or fix the doc comment.

src/plan/context.ts planPaths writes into two folders: specs/<root> for the spec and answers, tickets/<root> for the tickets. That matches #st-spec-plan-files. This card says one folder holds all of them. Both cards are decided, so the two-folder layout is accepted. No change is needed unless a person sides with this card.

review.impact: ensurePlan runs before applyPlanEvent validates the event. A rejected plan event, such as plan.step for an unknown plan, still adds an empty Plan to board.plans. This contradicts the 'changes nothing' contract in plan-events.ts, and a refused event leaves a phantom plan on the board.
review.fix: Look the plan up without creating it. Only plan.started creates one. Pass undefined to applyPlanEvent for the other events so they report 'plan X is not running'. Alternatively, create the plan only after applyPlanEvent returns null.

review.impact: Ticket.planned events are appended one at a time. If the board log refuses one, the earlier tickets stay on the board and the plan ends red. The next run is then refused with 'already has tickets on the board', so the plan is stuck with a partial ticket set and no way to re-run it.
review.fix: Validate all planned events before appending any, or append them as one batch. Alternatively, let a re-run replace the tickets of a plan that ended red.

review.impact: The kill timer is cleared only on the success path. If reading the stream throws, the catch block runs with the timer still armed. It can later kill an already-dead child and keeps the process alive until it fires. This is a resource leak.
review.fix: Hoist the timer variable and call clearTimeout in a finally block.

review.impact: The catch block calls planStep and board, which can throw. A failure while recording the end of the plan then replaces the original error, so the real cause is lost.
review.fix: Wrap the bookkeeping in the catch in its own try, and report the original reason first.

review.impact: The str and bad helpers are copied from board/fold.ts, and Rec is redeclared. The two copies can drift apart.
review.fix: Export the helpers from fold.ts, or from a small shared board helper module, and import them in plan-events.ts.

review.impact: `Rec`, `str` and `bad` are copied from `src/board/fold.ts`, which defines the same helpers. The two copies can drift, for example if `str`'s empty-string rule changes in only one.
review.fix: Export the helpers from `fold.ts` or a small shared module. `plan-events.ts` already takes its types from `fold.ts`, so only the helper imports are new.

review.impact: `runPlan` is one long function. It does validation, scope, two writer runs, ticket checks, board appends, pipeline-log appends and error mapping. It has several exits, and the `planStarted` flag is hidden state that decides whether a `step.ended` event is written. The success path and the catch path each repeat the `planStep("step.ended")` and `board("plan.ended")` calls, so they are hard to test and change separately.
review.fix: Split it into guards (`refuseReason`), a `writeTickets` step that does the checks and board appends, and a single `finish(ctx, result, reason)` used by both the success and failure paths.

review.impact: `runAgent` is long and has nested async closures: the stdin writer, the stream reader and the line parser. The empty `catch {}` around the stdin write is a silent swallow. Only the leading comment explains why.
review.fix: Pull the stdout line reader into a helper such as `readStream(child.stdout, onLine)`. Keep the swallow, but put the comment on the `catch` itself.

review.impact: `as never` is a type escape hatch that hides the real `agents` shape in the test.
review.fix: Build a typed fixture from the `LaunchOptions['agents']` entry type instead.

review.impact: `candidates.find(...) as TicketFile` re-looks-up a file that the code already had in hand. The cast also hides an impossible `undefined`. The `held` map stores only file names, which forces this lookup.
review.fix: Make `held` a `Map<number, TicketFile[]>` and drop both the `find` and the cast.

review.impact: The runner and writer failure paths have tests for a timeout and a crash. They have none for a stream with no result event, a result with is_error, a writer that writes no answers file, or a writer whose answers file is malformed JSON. Each of those branches could break without a test failing.
review.fix: Add scripted-writer cases for each of those four branches. Assert the plan exits 1 and that the stderr and board `plan.ended` reason match the expected text.

review.impact: The refusal for a root id containing '/' in run-plan.ts has no test. The `ticketFiles` filter that skips non-.md files also has no test. Removing either check would go unnoticed.
review.fix: Add a case where a card id contains a slash and assert the refusal. Add a case where the ticket folder holds a stray non-.md file and assert it is not planned.

review.impact: The only check on the plan root id is that it has no `/`. The id is then put into the paths in `planPaths` (`specs/${root}`, `tickets/${root}`), and `rmSync(..., {recursive:true, force:true})` runs on those paths. Map card ids can be any non-empty text. A card with the id `..` has no slash and is a decided card, so it passes the check. `plan ..` then deletes `<store>/specs/..` and `<store>/tickets/..`, which both resolve to the store itself. That removes the map log, the board log and the pipeline log. An id that contains glob characters also widens the `Write(specs/<root>/*)` allow rule that the agent gets. The answers slug is validated by `SLUG` in answers.ts, but the root id is not.
review.fix: Before any path is built or removed, require the root id to match a safe id pattern. For example, `/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$/` with no `..` and no leading dot. Do this in `runPlan`, replacing the `includes("/")` check. As a second guard, check that `resolve(store, paths.specDir)` and `resolve(store, paths.ticketsDir)` stay strictly inside `store` before calling `rmSync`.

review.impact: `dependsOn` filters the whole `map.edges` array on every call. The walk calls it once per scope card in the first tier and again in the second-tier loop. The cost is O(cards in scope × all edges), which grows quadratically on a large map. A plan on a big project map would pay for this.
review.fix: Build a `Map<from, to[]>` of the `depends_on` edges once at the top of `planScope`, and look up in it. Do the same for `children`, which already uses a map. Replace the `[...(children.get(parent) ?? []), child]` copy with a push onto a stored array.

review.impact: `take` calls `appendFileSync` once per stream line. A long agent run emits thousands of events, so each one costs an open, write and close syscall on the event loop. This blocks reading of stdout and stderr between lines. `events` also keeps every parsed event in memory, but only the last `result` event is used.
review.fix: Open one file descriptor before the run and write to it with `writeSync`, or batch the lines per chunk and write them once. Keep only the latest `result` event instead of the whole array.

causeOfLast.why: four slow CLI and server tests timed out under parallel load, and they pass when run alone.
one slow project-removal test timed out under merge-queue load; it passes alone and in the full suite, and the ticket's code does not touch it.

grade.gap: Met. TabStrip renders after the composer (client/app/chat-pane.tsx). Its chips are labelled with home-card titles. Parts and asks are routed by convo (client/lib/conversations.ts receive, chat-store.ts drops parts from another convo). The chip blinks through data-ask and the tab-ask keyframes, the other pane shows no ask-bar, and switching tabs shows it. Tests: chat-pane.test.tsx 'the strip below the composer…' and 'a chip blinks…', conversations.test.ts 'two conversations on two home cards…', chat-route.test.ts 'two conversations keep their own history…'. I could not run the tests in this environment (permission denied), so this is judged from reading them.

Met. Convo is keyed by tab.id, so a switch remounts it, and useLayoutEffect scrolls to scrollHeight. New parts follow only while following.current, which atEnd sets in onScroll. Tested in chat-pane.test.tsx 'a tab comes into view at the end of its log…' and in log-scroll.test.ts. Not run here.

Choices that no named card gives: (1) The address. Every chat route carries the conversation as a `?convo=<name>` query parameter, and a missing or empty one means main (src/serve/chat-route.ts convoOf/convoOfRequest; client/lib/chat-store.ts route()). #werk-mc-split-convo-name says each request names its conversation but not where the name goes, so propose a card for the query-parameter address and the default-to-main rule. (2) The storage layout. Every conversation other than main is stored in `.werk/session-<convo>` and `.werk/chat-model-<convo>.json` (src/chat/chat-state-store.ts suffix()). (3) The name grammar and id shape. CONVO_NAME is `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$`, and new ids are `c<base36 time><4 random chars>` (client/lib/conversations.ts newId). (4) A tab with no home card yet labels its chip with the card open now, or 'New conversation' when none is open (client/app/tab-strip.tsx).

The card says a request that names a malformed conversation is refused as a bad request. The /commands route (src/serve/routes.ts projectRoute) does not refuse: with a bad name, convoOf returns null and falls back to "", and the route answers 200 with `{commands: []}`. Fix: return the 400 refusal for a malformed `convo` there, as chatRoute, askRoute, modelRoute and clearRoute already do, and add a test for it in chat-route.test.ts.

causeOfLast.why: #werk-mc-split-convo-name did not say where the name goes or how it is stored, and an earlier pass left the commands route without the refusal the card requires.

review.impact: A chip label comes from `titleOf(card)` and `current()`. Both read mutable state in main.tsx (`index`, `openId`), and `ChatPane` re-renders only when the conversations store changes. Until some chat event arrives, a chip shows the raw card id if the index loads late. A tab with no home card also keeps a stale label after the person opens another card.
review.fix: Make the labels reactive. Re-render the pane when the index or the open card changes, for example by passing them in as props from the main.tsx render path, or by giving `Conversations` a subscribe hook for them.

review.impact: `sessionOf` creates and caches a session in `context.chats` for any valid name, including on an unauthenticated GET to `/chat?convo=<anything>`. Nothing caps or evicts the map, so a client can grow the server's memory and live sessions without limit. The client also mints a fresh id for every tab, and the server never forgets a tab that was closed or lost on reload.
review.fix: Create sessions only on the POST paths (send, model, clear). Let GET return empty history for an unknown name. Optionally cap the number of conversations per project.

review.impact: The `card` dependency has a side effect. When a store reads the open card, it sets `convo.home` and calls `changed()` synchronously, in the middle of `send`. Listeners are notified from inside a getter, and the `null as unknown as ChatStore` placeholder is a type hack.
review.fix: Fix the home card explicitly in a wrapper around `store.send`, or give `createChatStore` a hook that reports the first sent card. Build the store before the `Convo` object so no cast is needed.

review.impact: The chips are raw `<button>` elements, but the new-tab control uses the shadcn `Button`. This is inconsistent with the project rule that the client builds screens from shadcn/ui components, and it needs a lot of bespoke CSS.
review.fix: Render the chips with `Button` (variant outline or ghost) and keep only the blink and selected styling in CSS.

review.impact: `MAIN_CONVO` is defined in both client/lib/chat-store.ts and src/chat/chat-state-store.ts. The two copies can drift apart, and a mismatch would break routing silently.
review.fix: Add a comment in each file that points at the other, or share one constant if the client already imports from a common module.

review.impact: The change includes runtime telemetry lines that the tests and tools appended. They are unrelated to the feature and add noise to the diff.
review.fix: Drop the change to this file from the commit.

review.impact: The `card` dependency passed to each store changes the tab's `home` and calls `changed()`. So reading the open card while sending notifies subscribers and re-renders. The store's `send` also depends on this hidden order. `store: null as unknown as ChatStore` is a cast that hides the circular setup.
review.fix: Set `home` explicitly where the first message is sent, for example with a store hook such as `onSend`. Or build the store first and then the Convo object, so the cast is not needed.

review.impact: The three-line pattern `const convo = convoOfRequest(req); if (typeof convo !== "string") return convo;` is copied into chatRoute, askRoute, modelRoute, clearRoute and the /commands branch in routes.ts. Each new route has to remember it, and the string-or-Response union makes callers check the type by hand.
review.fix: Add one wrapper, such as `withConvo(req, (convo) => ...)`, that does the check and passes the name on. Alternatively, validate once in `projectRoute` before dispatch.

review.impact: `MAIN_CONVO = "main"` is defined here and again in src/chat/chat-state-store.ts. If one copy is changed alone, the client and server will disagree on the main conversation's name.
review.fix: Keep one definition, or put the constant in a shared module that both sides can import. If the client cannot import from src, add a comment that names the other copy.

review.impact: `chipBlinks(a as never)` uses `as never` to get past the type checker. It also hides that `tabs` can hold undefined entries.

review.impact: The diff adds per-conversation file names. The main conversation keeps `session` and `chat-model.json`, and every other conversation gets a `-<convo>` suffix. No test covers this. review.impact: `runningTurns`, `background`, `dead` and `stopTurns` now aggregate over many sessions. `closeContext` also stops every session. No test uses more than one session, so a bug in the sum, the flatMap, or stopping all sessions would go unnoticed.

review.impact: The new route tests cover only the chat send, the chat history read and the commands list. The /ask, /model and /clear routes now look up a session by convo. The tests never check that they pick the named session. They also never check that a malformed name is refused on those routes, or that an ask for an unknown convo gets "no such open ask". `stubbed()` registers only "main".

review.impact: Several branches have no test. `receive` falls back to main when a part has no `convo` field. `receive` returns on malformed JSON. `focus` ignores an unknown id. A tab with `home === null` is labelled when no card is open.

review.impact: The `body.convo !== convo` filter inside the store has no direct test. review.impact: The tests skip the 24px threshold boundary, which is the only logic in `atEnd`. A change to `<=` or to the constant would not be caught.

review.impact: `sessionOf` makes and keeps a new session for every distinct valid `convo` name. A GET to `/chat` also makes one, and that route needs no token. The `chats` map therefore grows without limit, and every session can start an agent process once someone sends a message. Name validation stops path traversal, because the regex limits names to `[a-z0-9-]` and 40 characters. The number of conversations has no cap.
review.fix: Cap the number of conversations per project, for example 20, and refuse a new name once the map is full. On GET, read history for a name that has no session without making one, or only make sessions on POST.

review.impact: `sessionOf` creates and caches a session for any valid `?convo=` name, and the GET history read also calls it. Every distinct name (about 36^40 are valid) adds a permanent `ChatSession` to `context.chats`. Each one holds its history and per-convo state, and starts an agent once it is sent to. Nothing ever removes one, and the client has no way to close a tab. A GET for a name that no tab has used builds a full session just to return empty history. A loop or a buggy client can therefore grow memory without limit. Every `stopTurns`, `background` and `runningTurns` call also walks all of these sessions.
review.fix: Make the GET history read and `/commands` look the session up with `chats.get`, and return empty history and settings for a name with no session, so only a POST send creates one. Also cap the number of sessions per project (for example 8 to 16) and refuse beyond it, or add a way to close and evict a tab.

review.impact: `receive` runs `JSON.parse` on every live part to read the convo name, and `store.receive` then parses the same payload again. During streaming that doubles the parse cost of every event, including large tool-result blocks.
review.fix: Parse once and pass the parsed body on, for example through a `receiveParsed(type, body)` on the store. Alternatively, read `convo` from an SSE field or a cheap prefix check.

review.impact: `changed()` rebuilds the tabs array, creates a new view object, and notifies every subscriber on each store change of any tab. A background tab that is streaming therefore re-renders `ChatPane` and `TabStrip`, and re-renders the active `Convo`, on every part, even though the visible state has not changed.
review.fix: Only call `changed()` from store updates when the ask count or the home card changes, since those are all the strip and the view depend on. Alternatively, wrap `Convo` in `React.memo` and make the view change only when those fields change.
