The build integration tests only reach these paths through the overseer, so a regression in `runProcess` would show up as a confusing build failure. The `watch-agent.ts` behaviours that matter are also untested: dropping `stream_event` lines from the log, closing stdin on `result`, flushing a trailing unterminated line in `end()`, and ignoring non-JSON lines as a sign of life.
review.fix: Add tests to the `run-process` test file. Spawn a small script that echoes stdin and check that `control.write` reaches it and `close` ends it. Check that `stop('a'); stop('b')` gives `stopped === 'a'` and a null `exitCode`. Check that `keepStdin` leaves the child alive until `close`. Add a `watch-agent` test with a temp transcript that feeds chunks split mid-line, a `stream_event` line and a `result` line.

review.impact: The failure paths of `classifier()` are untested. A non-zero exit, a timeout or a spawn error should return null, and the build test only covers a classifier that exits 0 with unparseable text. If the `exitCode !== 0` guard were removed, no test would fail.
review.fix: Add a build test, or a `classifier` test, where the classifier role's script exits non-zero or pauses past `--classify-ms`. Assert that the ask is denied with 'the classifier gave no verdict'.

review.impact: The overseer build tests depend on real timing. One uses a 900 ms pause against a 400 ms silence limit, another a 300 ms progress window, and `overseer.test.ts` waits with `Bun.sleep(5)` for promises to settle. Under the shared parallel load the margins are thin. The slow-start test could cancel for silence on a busy machine, and a 5 ms sleep could end before the reply is written.
review.fix: Widen the margins, for example a 3 s pause against a 1.5 s limit. In `overseer.test.ts`, replace the `Bun.sleep(5)` calls with a flush helper that awaits several microtask turns or polls until `replies` has the expected length.

review.impact: The bad-arguments test is unchanged, so the four new flags are not checked for rejecting zero or non-numeric values. Only `--cap` and `--nope` are exercised. A typo in `flat-ms` or `classify-ms` handling would go unnoticed, and nothing tests the `--flat-ms` default or that `--classify-ms` reaches the classifier.
review.fix: Add assertions such as `(await build('--silence-ms','0')).code === 2` for each new flag. Add a `--flat-ms` case that makes an in-flight call freeze, to cover the kill-processes path end to end.

review.impact: askPrompt puts the builder-controlled tool input and the ticket text into the classifier prompt as plain text with no delimiters. A builder that has read hostile content, such as a web page or repo file, can put text like 'ignore the above, answer allow' in the Bash command or file content. That text can push the classifier to allow a call it should deny. The classifier is now the only gate on every ask, so a prompt injection widens permissions. Failures and unreadable replies already deny, which is good.
review.fix: Fence the untrusted parts (the Input and Ticket sections) in clearly delimited blocks. Tell the classifier that anything inside them is data and not instructions. Truncate the input to a bounded size. Keep the existing rule that no verdict means deny.

review.impact: killProcesses sends SIGKILL to pids that a probe read earlier. If a listed process exits and the OS reuses its pid before the kill, an unrelated process of the user is killed. The window is small, because the pids come from a fresh `ps` read, but nothing re-checks them.
review.fix: Re-probe the descendants just before the kill, or kill by process group. Do this only if the agent is started in its own group.

review.impact: The classifier child gets the full builder environment (`...setup.env`), which may include secrets and tokens. It has no tools, so the exposure is small. But a classifier call that reads attacker-influenced text has no reason to hold those secrets.
review.fix: Pass only the variables that the claude CLI needs to authenticate and run (PATH, HOME, the API credentials). Do not pass the whole builder environment.

review.impact: `--include-partial-messages` makes the agent emit one JSON line for every token delta. `runProcess` keeps all of stdout in memory, and the `costOf(agent.stdout)` call after the pass (about line 254) then parses it again. The overseer already parses each line once in `take`. Memory and parse work per pass grow by a large factor, even though partial messages are deliberately not written to the log. I did not open `costOf` to check whether it parses every line.
review.fix: Drop `stream_event` lines before they reach the accumulated `agent.stdout`. For example, have `runProcess` accept an `onStdout` that can opt out of buffering, or let `watchAgent` build a filtered buffer for `costOf`. In `take`, a cheap `line.includes('"stream_event"')` check would skip the `JSON.parse` for partial messages.

review.impact: `onStdout` concatenates `pending` and splits the whole string on every chunk. A very long line with no newline, such as a huge tool result, is rescanned for each 64 KB chunk, so the work grows quadratically with line length. The log write also changed from one `appendFileSync` per chunk to one per line, which adds syscalls on busy streams.
review.fix: Split only the new chunk and join its first piece onto `pending`. Optionally batch the lines of one chunk into a single `appendFileSync`.

review.impact: When the classifier gives no verdict, `judged` is not advanced and `calls` keeps growing. Each retry, every `progressMs`, sends a larger prompt. `calls` is never truncated, so with a long run and a failing classifier the prompt is unbounded.
review.fix: Cap the calls included in a loop prompt, for example the last 100, or advance `judged` after a bounded number of failed attempts.

causeOfLast.why: #st-grade-defer (quote each gap as written) and #st-ticket (no file paths) conflicted, and no card said which wins for follow-up tickets.

pass_end.decision: the grader said a person must settle: src/build/followup-ticket.ts copies each grader gap into the follow-up ticket word for word. #lp-prod-judge tells the grader to name the file and line in each gap (for example 'src/build/grade.ts:12'), so the follow-up tickets will usually name file paths, and #st-ticket says a ticket names no file paths. The cards conflict: #st-grade-defer says to quote each gap as the grader wrote it. A person must decide whether follow-up tickets are exempt from the no-file-paths rule, or whether paths are taken out of the quoted gaps.; src/build/file-followup.ts appends ticket.planned for the follow-up without running the own-ticket checks. #st-ticket-partial says a ticket that fails its own checks gets no ticket.planned event. A follow-up whose quoted gaps contain file paths, or that is longer than 4000 characters, still goes on the board. If the checks run, such a follow-up never reaches the board, and that defeats #st-grade-defer. A person must decide which rule wins for follow-up tickets: run the checks and drop the follow-up, change the quoted text, or exempt follow-ups.

review.impact: `fileFollowup` returns null for four different reasons: no free number, the ticket fails its own checks, the board refuses the planned event, or the source has no plan. The loop then drops that null and still reports a plain `merging` result. The deferred small gaps are lost without a trace, and the reason is not recorded anywhere. `file-followup.ts` can also leave an orphan ticket file when the planned event is refused. It also ignores the result of the final `ticket.followup` append.
review.fix: Return a result type such as `{ok: true, id} | {ok: false, reason}` from `fileFollowup`. In the loop, put the failure reason in `BuildResult.reason`, or in the pass log, so a person can see the gaps were not filed. Write the ticket file only after the planned event succeeds, or delete it when that event fails. Check the result of the `ticket.followup` append.

review.impact: `judgePass` takes the ticket text and the stories in `Grading`, takes the other values in `JudgeContext`, and has five positional arguments. It builds the red outcome, runs the grader, and runs and merges the reviews all in one function of about 120 lines. That runs against the small-single-purpose-module rule (#werk-stack-modules), and the file is hard to change one part at a time.
review.fix: Split it into `runGrader` and `runReviews`, each returning a outcome or a small result. Let `judgePass` only chain the two.

review.impact: judgePass is about 100 lines and does five jobs: it runs the grader, parses and settles the grade, fans out the reviewers, folds the reviewer results into findings, and builds the failure text and reason. The `red` closure and the `none`, `judged` and `reviewed` variants add to the branching. Changing one stage means reading all of them.
review.fix: Split it into `gradeStage(...)` and `reviewStage(...)`. Have `reviewStage` return `{ broken, findings, recorded }`. Keep `judgePass` as a short sequence of the two.

review.impact: `runJudge` copies 13 fields from `JudgeRun` into `runAgent` and adds only `tools` and `allow`. The `JudgeRun` type repeats most of `runAgent`'s options, so a change to the options has to be made in both places.
review.fix: Make `runJudge` take `Omit<AgentRunOptions, 'tools' | 'allow'>` and spread it, or have `judgePass` call `runAgent` with the exported constants.

review.impact: `as never` casts, repeated across the isSmallGap assertions, switch off type checking in the test. If `GradeLine` changes shape, the tests will not report it.
review.fix: Add a `lineOf(grade, id): GradeLine` helper that throws when the line is missing, and use it instead of the casts.

review.impact: Several tests declare `const result = await build()`, which shadows the module-level `result()` reply helper. One test also contains a hand-written result event literal that duplicates what `result()` and `findingsOf()` build. The test titled 'a broken grader and a silent reviewer each fail the pass' only exercises the grader.
review.fix: Rename the local variable to `run` or `out`. Use `findingsOf()` in the reviewer-crash test. Rename the broken-grader test, or add the reviewer case.

review.impact: `source.id.split("/") as [string]` is a type assertion that hides a missing-element case. The ticket is also parsed twice, in `touchesOf` and in `gatherGrading`.
review.fix: Take `plan` as an argument or destructure it with a guard. Parse the ticket once and share the result.

review.impact: `fileFollowup` has four paths that return null: no free number, a follow-up that fails its own checks, a board that refuses the planned event, and an unparseable ticket. No test covers any of them. Only the success path runs, through one build.test.ts case. The null returns are the failure behaviour of the last-pass deferral. A regression there would silently merge a ticket with no follow-up filed, or leave an orphaned ticket file behind. That orphan can happen when the board refuses the event after the file is written.
review.fix: Add a `file-followup.test.ts` with temp map and board logs. Cover a plan with 99 tickets, a gap set whose follow-up fails `ownChecks`, and a board that rejects `ticket.planned`. Assert null in each case, and assert that no ticket file is left behind when the board refuses. Consider writing the file only after the board accepts the event.

review.impact: The title says a broken grader and a silent reviewer each fail the pass, but the test only covers the broken grader. The silent reviewer is covered by a separate crash test. The title overstates what this test checks.
review.fix: Rename the test to cover only the broken grader. Also assert that the failure text reaches the next builder prompt, as the reviewer crash test does.

review.impact: The new judging path has no test for an archive while a judge is running, or for a judge that times out or goes silent. `judgePass` returns `archived` after the grader and again after the reviewers. A regression there would go unnoticed, for example a build that keeps going after the ticket is archived or a pass recorded as green.
review.fix: Add a build test that archives the ticket during the grader or reviewer session and asserts the `archived` result and that no merge happens. Add a test for the judge timeout or silence path.

review.impact: `isSmallGap` is called with `line(...) as never` and `delivery.lines[0] as never`. This turns off type checking in the test. If `GradeLine` changes shape, or `find` returns undefined, the test fails at runtime with a confusing error instead of a compile error.
review.fix: Use a helper that throws when the line is missing and returns a `GradeLine`, and drop the `as never` casts.

review.impact: The judge allow-list uses prefix rules: `Bash(git diff:*)`, `Bash(git log:*)` and `Bash(git show:*)`. These also match `git diff --output=<path>`, `git log --output=<path>` and `git show --output=<path>`, and git writes the diff to that file. The grader and reviewers are meant to be read-only, but a judge could overwrite a file in the worktree. A judge could also be steered into this by prompt injection from builder-written diff content. `--ext-diff` and `--textconv` can run configured helper programs too. The read-only guarantee in #lp-prod-judge-read-only is therefore weaker than the comment claims.
review.fix: Narrow the Bash rules, or pass `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv` and forbid `--output`. A stronger option is to pre-compute the diff, put it in the prompt or a file under a read-only path, and drop Bash from `JUDGE_TOOLS`. At the very least, add a launch-record test that `git diff --output=x` is refused.

review.impact: The grader's gap text is written into a ticket file inside double quotes without escaping `"`. A gap that contains quotes, or a `## ` heading after whitespace flattening, produces a malformed or misleading ticket. `parseTicket` and `ownChecks` catch most failures, and the gap text is flattened to one line so it cannot inject headers. This is a hardening gap for model-authored text that ends up as a durable ticket, not an exploitable hole.
review.fix: Replace `"` with `'` or `\"` in `quotableGap`, and add a test for a gap that contains quotes.

grade.gap: The diff is empty: commit 6dabab0 ('pass 1') changes no files, and nothing already in the checkout covers the scenario. The client has no chat tab strip and no tab chips. 'dead' only exists as a single-pane flag (client/lib/chat-log.ts:86, client/lib/chat-store.ts:99) and as a project-switcher mark (client/app/switcher.tsx:44-62), which is per project, not per conversation tab. Nothing is missing on the server side, but the client still needs all of these: (1) the dead state kept per conversation tab, keyed by tab, so that a dead event for tab A reaches the page while tab B is shown; (2) the A chip blinking red while A is dead; (3) one line in the pane of every other tab that names tab A and its error; (4) the whole error in A's own pane; (5) sending in A starts a new agent, which then replies; (6) after that, the blink and the line in B both clear. Each step needs a unit test at its seam, for example a chat-log/tab reducer test: A dead → B shows the line → send in A → the line and the blink are gone. Or a Playwright test that runs the scenario from start to end.

The code meets this criterion but no test checks the path. sweepDeadBuilds writes build.ended with result died plus a red ticket.pass, and spawnFreshPass sweeps again when the child exits. The new branch is built from the existing branch: src/build/died.test.ts checks that kept.txt is kept and lost.txt is gone. But no test kills a build process that the server started and checks that onExit runs the sweep. In died.test.ts, `start` is a stub that never calls onExit, and src/serve/dead-builds-watch.ts spawnFreshPass has no test. Add a test that starts a fresh pass through spawnFreshPass (or a start that runs a real child), kills it, and checks the end with died and the next pass. Note: a build started from a terminal with `werk build` and killed while the server runs is found only at the next server start. That matches the card, which names only 'a build process it started exits' and server start.

src/projects/context.ts openContext calls restartDeadBuilds, so the sweep runs when a project opens. But no test opens a context or server over a board log that has a dead build and checks the died end and the spawned fresh pass. died.test.ts calls sweepDeadBuilds directly. Also, restartDeadBuilds swallows every error with an empty catch, so a broken sweep at start-up is silent. Add a test through openContext.

This holds only for the default cap. sweepDeadBuilds uses DEFAULT_CAP = 5 (src/serve/dead-builds-watch.ts), and spawnFreshPass starts `werk build` with no --cap. A build started with `werk build r/01 --cap 2` that dies on pass 2 is therefore restarted as pass 3, past its own cap. The sweep has to use the cap of the build that died, for example by recording it in the build's start event, so that 'its last allowed pass' means that build's cap.

These choices come from no named card: (1) The server restarts a build by spawning the public command line `werk build <ticket> --after-death <session>`. That is a new flag on the build verb (src/verbs/build.ts USAGE) and a new boundary between the server and the build loop. (2) The sweep assumes the default retry cap of 5 (DEFAULT_CAP in src/serve/dead-builds-watch.ts) and does not use the cap the build ran with. That is a trade-off. (3) The fresh pass keeps the dead build's build id and obligation, and opens no new obligation.opened (src/build/loop.ts). (4) A death is recorded as a red ticket.pass, and as a pipeline step.ended with reason died, ms 0 and NO_COST. Propose a card, or extend #st-build-died, for each of these.

The card's premise is that a build runs in its own process, apart from the server, and keeps running without it. spawnFreshPass (src/serve/dead-builds-watch.ts) uses Bun.spawn without `detached: true`, so the child stays in the server's process group. A Ctrl-C on `werk serve` (src/verbs/serve.ts already runs the server as a child) sends SIGINT to the whole foreground group, which kills every fresh pass that the server started. Each such pass then counts as a death against the cap at the next start. Spawn the build detached, in its own process group, and unref it so that it outlives the server. Separately, the cap mismatch in the criterion-3 gap means that a build which dies on every pass of a custom cap does not stop at its own cap.

The pipeline step.ended that the sweep writes for the dead pass has `ms: 0` (src/serve/dead-builds-watch.ts). The card says an ended event carries the wall time. 0 is wrong, and it distorts every wall-time fold. Compute the time from the matching step.started `at`, or leave the field out so it is not reported as zero.

causeOfLast.why: #st-build-died did not say how the server starts the fresh pass, which cap it uses, or how a death is recorded, and its premise of a build apart from the server was not met by the first spawn.

review.impact: The sweep writes build.ended and the red pass before it calls options.start. If Bun.spawn throws, openContext's catch swallows the error. The ticket then stays in building with an ended build and no live process. The next sweep skips it because deadBuilds sees last.ended, so it is stuck and nothing restarts it. A thrown error also skips handled.push and aborts the rest of the loop, so later dead tickets in the same sweep are not handled.
review.fix: Wrap options.start in try/catch inside the loop. On failure, move the ticket to ready with a reason such as 'could not start a fresh pass', then continue to the next dead build. Alternatively, have the sweep's own error handling put the ticket back in ready.

review.impact: `void child.exited.then(onExit)` runs sweepDeadBuilds with no catch. If readBoard or appendBoardEvent throws, the rejection is unhandled, which can crash or destabilise the server. The same sweep is wrapped in try/catch when it runs from restartDeadBuilds, so the two call paths handle errors differently.
review.fix: Catch inside the exit handler: `child.exited.then(onExit).catch(() => {})`, or have onExit swallow errors the way restartDeadBuilds does. Better, pass one guarded sweep function used by both paths.

review.impact: restartOf uses `build.cap ?? options.cap ?? DEFAULT_CAP`. spawnFreshPass passes `--cap` only when `dead.cap` is set. When a start records no cap, the new build process falls back to the verb's own default, not the cap the sweep used. Because DEFAULT_CAP is a second copy of the verb's default, the two can drift apart.
review.fix: Compute the effective cap once, pass it to the spawned command, and have both build.ts and this file import one shared default constant.

review.impact: The resume flag adds several separate `resume !== undefined` branches to buildTicket. These cover the column check, the board move, the obligation and the pass loop start. The next reader has to track all of them together, and the column check now repeats its condition in both the test and the message.
review.fix: Derive `const expected = resume ? 'building' : 'ready'` once and use it in both places. Group the start-up differences in a small helper.

review.impact: The resume mode adds `resume !== undefined` checks at about six places in `buildTicket`. These include a ternary inside a condition, a ternary inside the error message, a fake `{ ok: true as const }` standing in for the `ticket.moved` result, and a skipped obligation block. This makes an already long function harder to read, and the two modes (fresh build and resume) are hard to tell apart. A later change to either mode has to check every branch.
review.fix: Derive the mode once, for example `const expected = resume ? "building" : "ready"` and a `startedFresh` flag. Move the 'move to building and open the obligation' step into a helper such as `beginBuild(...)` that resume skips. Drop the fake `moved` object.

review.impact: `DEFAULT_CAP = 5` repeats the default of `werk build --cap`, which is defined in `src/verbs/build.ts`. If one default changes, a dead build with no recorded cap restarts under a different cap than a normal build uses.
review.fix: Export one default cap constant from a shared module, such as the build loop or its options, and use it in both the `build` verb and the watch.

review.impact: `died as string` and the spread `dead ? {...} : {}` make the `--after-death` handling awkward. The `DeadBuild` object is rebuilt in the verb only to call `deathText`, so the verb knows the structure of a dead build.
review.fix: Make `deathText` take `{ pass }`, or add a helper in `dead-builds.ts` such as `resumeOf(session)` that returns the `resume` object (or null). The verb then only calls it, and the cast goes away.

review.impact: The bare `catch {}` hides every sweep failure, including real bugs such as a malformed board log. A dead build then stays stuck with no signal.
review.fix: Log the error, for example to stderr, before swallowing it, or catch only the expected failures.

review.impact: The test creates a temp directory with `mkdtempSync` and never removes it, so temp directories pile up on every test run. The `bun CLI build r/01 --after-death ...` invocation is also written out three times.
review.fix: Remove the temp directory in `afterEach` or use the project's temp helper. Add a small `runBuild(...args)` helper for the repeated CLI calls.

review.impact: `sweepDeadBuilds` uses `build.cap ?? options.cap ?? DEFAULT_CAP`. No test covers a recorded cap that differs from the option cap, or the `DEFAULT_CAP` fallback. Every sweep test uses a seeded start with no `cap`. If the recorded cap were ignored, such as `options.cap` winning, no test would fail. The same gap hides whether `loop.ts` records `cap` in `build.started`, and whether `spawnFreshPass` forwards `--cap`.
review.fix: Add a sweep test that seeds `build.started` with `cap: 2` on pass 2, calls `sweep(5)`, and expects a stop with no start. Add one test with no cap anywhere that expects `DEFAULT_CAP`. Add a `spawnFreshPass` argument test, or an assertion that a real build's start event carries `cap`.

review.impact: The test makes a `mkdtempSync` directory under the OS tmpdir and never removes it. `releaseBranch` deletes only the `wt` subdirectory, so the parent stays behind after each run. If an assertion fails first, the worktree is also left registered in the project repo. This breaks the rule that each test removes its own copies when it ends.
review.fix: Remove `dir` with `rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })` in `afterEach`, or create the worktree inside `project.dir`'s disposable tree.

review.impact: The new rule that `build.started` accepts `cap` only as an integer of at least 1 has no test. A `cap` of 0, a fractional `cap`, or a string would silently be dropped, and that path is unchecked. The `fold.ts` change is also untested apart from the one positive case in `dead-builds.test.ts`.
review.fix: Add fold tests with `cap: 0`, `cap: 1.5` and `cap: "3"` that expect `builds[0].cap` to be undefined.

review.impact: The stop case only checks `action` and never the reason text. `parseSession` is not tested with extra colons, such as `a:p1:p2`, or a leading-zero pass such as `x:p01`. The `[1-9]\d*` regex handles these, but the tests do not pin it.
review.fix: Assert that `last.reason` contains `died on pass 5`. Add `parseSession` cases for `a:p1:p2` (expect buildId `a:p1`, pass 2) and `x:p01` (expect null).

review.impact: `werk build <ticket> --after-death <session>` checks only that the session string parses and that the ticket is in `building`. It never checks that the session is the ticket's last build, or that the build has ended or its process is gone. A mistyped or stale session id run against a ticket with a live build calls `releaseBranch`, which runs `git worktree remove --force` and `rmSync`. That deletes the live build's worktree and its uncommitted work, and a second builder then starts on the same branch. Only the server sweep guarantees the build is dead. The verb itself trusts its argument.
review.fix: In `buildTicket`, when `resume` is set, require that `ticket.builds` has a last build whose `session` equals the given session, and that the build has ended (the sweep writes `died` first) or `pidAlive(pid)` is false. Otherwise throw `BuildRefused`. Also check that `afterPass` matches the pass in the session id.

review.impact: `releaseBranch` takes the directory from the `worktree <path>` line of the porcelain output and force-removes it, then calls `rmSync(dir, {recursive, force})`. It never checks that `dir` is not the main checkout or the current repo. If the ticket's branch is checked out in the main worktree, `git worktree remove` fails because of `git()`. `rmSync` would then still delete that directory recursively.
review.fix: Skip the first porcelain entry, which is the main worktree, and any entry that resolves to `repo`. Only call `rmSync` if `git worktree remove` succeeded.

causeOfLast.why: the ticket assumed a multi-conversation server and tab strip that the code lacked, so pass 1 changed nothing.

grade.gap: This now passes through the fallback clause. client/lib/chat-tabs.test.ts runs the whole scenario on the tab reducer: tab A goes dead while B is shown, A's chip blinks red, B's pane shows one line about A, A's own pane shows the whole error, then a message in A plus the server's dead:null clears both the blink and the line. client/app/tab-strip.test.tsx checks the chip blink, the one line and the whole error in the DOM. A person still cannot run the scenario in the browser, because nothing connects these pieces: client/main.tsx:304 renders <ChatPane store={chat} …> without `tabs` or `onSelect`, nothing calls reduceTabs, and chat-store.ts only feeds a single-conversation chat-log reducer. The 'replies' step is assumed in the test, not shown. The next pass could connect the SSE events, keyed by tab, to reduceTabs in main.tsx and pass `tabs`/`onSelect` to ChatPane, if another tab ticket does not already do this. I could not run the tests here because running bun test needed approval.

Small extras the scenario does not ask for. An event for an unknown tab opens a new tab (reduceTabs, and the second test in chat-tabs.test.ts). A select for an unknown tab is ignored. These are defensive edge cases and fine to keep.

This passed before and nothing broke, but the diff makes choices that neither named card (#werk-chat, #werk-chat-turn-id) gives, so the next pass should propose cards for them: (1) the default tab id is the constant 'main' (client/lib/chat-tabs.ts:21); (2) an event for a tab that is not open opens it (chat-tabs.ts:30-41); (3) the line in another tab's pane holds the first non-blank line of the error and reads '<tab> stopped: <line>' (chat-tabs.ts firstLine, tab-strip.tsx DeadLines); (4) a dead tab's chip keeps blinking while that tab is the shown one (chipsOf). The code also cites #werk-mc-live-dead, #werk-mc-asks-dot, #werk-mc-live-line and #werk-fullerr, which the builder did not name.

review.impact: Nothing wires the new tab code in. `main.tsx` still renders `<ChatPane store={chat} .../>` without `tabs` or `onSelect`, and no code calls `reduceTabs`. `chat-tabs.ts` and `tab-strip.tsx` only run in tests, so the blinking chip and the dead-line never appear in the app. `ChatPane` would also have two sources of truth for chat state, the `store` prop and `tabs.chats`.
review.fix: Make `reduceTabs` the owner of the per-tab chat state and feed `ChatPane` from it. Otherwise derive the shown tab's state from `tabs` and drop the separate `store` state. If a later ticket does the wiring, say so in the card.

review.impact: `tabs` and `onSelect` are separate optional props. With `tabs` but no `onSelect`, the dead lines show and the strip does not. That half-enabled state is easy to hit by mistake.
review.fix: Pass one optional prop, such as `tabs?: { state: TabsState; onSelect }`, and render all three pieces together.

review.impact: A runtime metrics log is part of the diff. It is unrelated to the change and adds noise and merge conflicts.
review.fix: Drop it from the commit with `git checkout .werk/fold-ms.jsonl`, or ignore the file.

review.impact: The test builds a state with `settings: null as never`, which bypasses the type check and builds a state the app never produces.
review.fix: Use a real settings fixture, or open the tab with the `cleared` action as tab B does.

review.impact: The chip's blink check, `state.chats[tab]?.dead != null`, repeats the dead lookup that `deadLinesOf` and `ownErrorOf` already do, and it uses loose `!= null` where the rest of the file compares with `=== null`. The 'dead' rule is therefore written in three places, and `undefined` and `null` are handled differently in each.
review.fix: Add a small helper such as `const deadOf = (state, tab) => state.chats[tab]?.dead ?? null`. Use it in `chipsOf`, `deadLinesOf` and `ownErrorOf`, and compare with `!== null`.

review.impact: `settings: null as never` is a type escape hatch. It builds a fake `model` action only to open tab A, and it hides a mismatch if the `Action` shape changes.
review.fix: Open tab A with a simple valid action, such as `{ type: "cleared" }`, as tab B does. Alternatively, build a real settings value.

review.impact: `tabs` and `onSelect` are separate optional props that only work together. The pane renders the dead lines when `tabs` is set. It renders the strip only when `tabs && onSelect` is set. Passing one without the other gives a half-working pane, and the two conditionals invite drift.
review.fix: Group them into one optional prop, such as `tabs?: { state: TabsState; onSelect: (tab: string) => void }`. Alternatively, make both required once a caller exists.

review.impact: Nothing in the diff passes `tabs` or `onSelect` to `ChatPane`, and nothing uses `reduceTabs` outside its test. The tab strip, `DeadLines`, `OwnError` and the reducer are therefore unreachable in the app.
review.fix: Wire the reducer into the page that renders `ChatPane`, or note which ticket does it.

review.impact: `firstLine` has branches that no test runs: a multi-line error whose first line is blank, an error that is only whitespace, and an empty-string error. An empty-string error counts as dead (`!= null`), but its chip and line are never tested. The 90% pure-file gate would still pass.
review.fix: Add a case with error "\n  \nreal" that expects line "real". Add a case with error "" that expects the chip to blink red.

review.impact: No test covers how `ChatPane` uses the new `tabs` and `onSelect` props. Nothing checks that the pane renders no strip without `tabs` or `onSelect`. Nothing checks that the dead lines, the own error and the strip are all wired in. If the wiring broke, the unit tests would still pass.
review.fix: Add a small `ChatPane` render test. Without `tabs`, it expects no `[data-slot=tab-strip]`. With `tabs` that hold a dead tab, it expects a dead line, an own error and a strip.

review.impact: The test comment says a sent message starts a new agent and clears the blink. In fact the `sent` action does not touch `dead`, and the explicit `dead: null` event does the clearing. The `sent` event is decoration, so the test does not show the real reset path. The `settings: null as never` cast in `twoTabs` also hides the real type.
review.fix: Reword the comment to say that the `dead` event with a null error clears the state. Build `twoTabs` from a valid action, such as `{ type: "cleared" }`, instead of casting.

review.impact: reduceTabs spreads the whole chats record and uses order.includes on every event. Streaming events at high frequency then cost O(tabs) per event, and every event gives the subscriber a new state object. The tab count is small, so this is negligible today.
review.fix: No change is needed now. If tab counts or event rates grow, keep order membership in the chats record (`action.tab in state.chats`) and memoize chipsOf, deadLinesOf and ownErrorOf per state.

review.impact: The infinite tab-blink animation animates opacity and runs for as long as a tab is dead. Its cost is small, but it keeps running and ignores reduced-motion preferences.
review.fix: Wrap the animation in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`.

grade.gap: Minor, not failing: JUDGE_ALLOW in src/build/judge-run.ts allows Bash(git diff:*) and Bash(git log:*) with any arguments. Under those rules `git diff --output=<file>` or `git log --output=<file>` could still write a file in the worktree. A future pass could deny the --output flag, or pass the judge only the diff text.

review.impact: fileFollowup returns null when the plan has no free number, the follow-up fails its own checks, or the board refuses it. The loop then merges with `followup` unset and does not say why. The deferred small gaps are dropped without a trace. The grade that treated them as deferrable was only green because they would be filed.
review.fix: Have fileFollowup return a result with a reason on failure. When deferred gaps could not be filed, either fail the last pass instead of merging, or put the unfiled gaps and the reason into the BuildResult reason and the pipeline log.

review.impact: The ticket file is written before the `ticket.planned` event is appended. If the board refuses the event, the function returns null but leaves an orphan ticket file on disk. That file takes a number and may be picked up later as an unplanned ticket.
review.fix: Append the planned event first, then write the file. Or remove the file when the append fails.

review.impact: The ticket folder is found by calling `dirname(ticketPath(mapLog, plan, "01"))` with a dummy number. This couples the code to ticketPath's layout and reads as a workaround.
review.fix: Add a `ticketFolder(mapLog, plan)` helper in gather.ts, and have ticketPath use it.

review.impact: `launchInput` is declared after the `run` object whose `launchFor` closure uses it. It works only because the closure runs later. A reorder or an eager call would hit the temporal dead zone.
review.fix: Declare `launchInput` before `run`.

review.impact: Several tests declare `const result = await build()`. That shadows the module-level `result(text)` reply helper added in the same diff. It works today, but a later edit that calls `result(...)` in one of those tests would hit the wrong binding.
review.fix: Rename the local to `done` or `out`, or rename the helper to something like `resultReply`.

review.impact: The test is titled 'a broken grader and a silent reviewer each fail the pass as a failed step', but it only exercises the broken grader. The silent-reviewer case is covered by a different test, so the title misleads.
review.fix: Rename the test to cover only the broken grader, or add the silent-reviewer assertion.

review.impact: The reviewer-tests crash test writes out a full `result` event literal by hand. The `findingsOf()` helper added in the same diff already builds that reply, so this is duplication.
review.fix: Replace the literal with `findingsOf()`.

review.impact: The tests use repeated `as never` casts, for example `isSmallGap(line(small()) as never)` and `delivery.lines[0] as never`. These switch off type checking and hide the real `GradeLine | undefined` type.
review.fix: Add a small helper that finds a line by id and throws when it is missing. It returns `GradeLine`, so no cast is needed.

review.impact: `touchesOf` parses the ticket text again with an empty file name. `gatherGrading` has already parsed the same text. The ticket is now parsed three times per build, and the third parse runs only when a follow-up is filed.
review.fix: Read `touches` once when `gatherGrading` or `gatherTicket` parses the ticket, and carry it in the input. Alternatively, accept the small cost and drop the empty-string file name.

review.impact: `judgePass` is a single long function, about 100 lines. It covers the grader run, the reply parse, the verdict, the parallel reviewers, the finding aggregation and the failure text. It builds the `red(...)` outcomes in several places, which makes it harder to follow and to change.
review.fix: Split it into `gradeStep` and `reviewStep` helpers. `judgePass` would then only sequence the two.

review.impact: The change adds review-prompt.ts to PURE_FILES in src/test/pure-files.ts, but the file has no review-prompt.test.ts. The coverage gate judges each pure file on its own test file (src/x.ts maps to src/x.test.ts). It counts only the lines that this file runs, so lines run from review.test.ts do not count. The only test of reviewPrompt is at review.test.ts:111. The gate therefore fails on a pure file with no test, and `make test-coverage` and CI go red.
review.fix: Create src/build/review-prompt.test.ts. Move the reviewPrompt test out of review.test.ts and add assertions for the area name, the focus text, the `git diff <base>` line and the JSON reply format. The test file must cover at least 90% of the file by itself.

review.impact: Only the success path of fileFollowup is tested, through the build.test.ts follow-up scenario. These null-return paths have no test: no free ticket number, a follow-up that fails its own checks, and `appendBoardEvent` refusing the event. The callers' handling of a null follow-up is also untested. A regression there would silently drop the small gaps, or leave a ticket file with no planned event.
review.fix: Add a file-followup test that uses a temporary store. Cover a plan with all 99 numbers taken, a source whose checks make the ticket fail `ownChecks`, and a board that refuses `ticket.planned`. Assert that each case returns null and that no ticket file is written.

review.impact: The test is named 'a broken grader and a silent reviewer each fail the pass as a failed step', but it exercises only the broken grader. The silent reviewer case lives in a separate test. The title overstates what this test covers.
review.fix: Rename it to 'a grader reply that is not the format fails the pass as a failed step'.

review.impact: The test for the last counted pass with a small gap asserts `first?.result` is "red", but the comment says it is checking that the first pass was not the deferred one. The assertion would also pass if pass 1 failed for any other reason, so it does not show that the deferral applies only on the last counted pass.
review.fix: Assert on pass 1's gate and reason instead: gate is "grader" and the reason names card-top. Also assert that pass 1 did not file a follow-up.

review.impact: The judge allow list has `Bash(git diff:*)`, `Bash(git log:*)` and `Bash(git show:*)`, which match on prefix only. `git diff --output=<path>` and `git show --output=<path>` write a file, and `--ext-diff` or a configured textconv can run an external program. A judge session reads the builder's untrusted diff, so a prompt injection in that diff could make the judge write files in the worktree or run a program. That breaks the 'read-only, cannot change anything' guarantee that the header comment and the prompts claim. The write lands in the pass worktree, which limits the damage.
review.fix: Narrow the rules to the forms the prompts use, for example `Bash(git diff <base>)`, or add deny rules for `--output`, `--ext-diff` and `--textconv`. If the runtime supports it, run the judge with `GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF` unset and `diff.external` and `core.pager` neutralised (`git -c diff.external= --no-ext-diff`). Add a test that the launch args hold no write-capable git flag.

review.impact: The follow-up ticket file embeds the grader's gap text. A gap that contains a double quote, or a newline-like sequence that survives `quotableGap` (which only collapses whitespace), can end the quoted string early or inject markdown, such as a new `## Checks` heading, into a ticket that later builds read as instructions. The `ownChecks` validation catches only part of this.
review.fix: Escape or strip `"` and leading `#` or `-` markers in the quoted gap. Alternatively, have `fileFollowup` re-parse the ticket and verify that its Checks section equals `source.checks` before it writes the file.

causeOfLast.why: the main line's overseer ticket also added flags to the build verb's usage and flag list.

grade.gap: Met for a build that the server spawned. `spawnFreshPass` (src/serve/dead-builds-watch.ts:84-111) runs `sweepDeadBuilds` again when the child exits. The sweep writes `build.ended` with result `died` and spawns `werk build --after-death <session>`. `buildTicket` with `resume` (src/build/loop.ts) releases the branch's worktree and continues from the branch's last commit, which src/build/died.test.ts checks ('the fresh pass starts from the last commit of the branch…'). Weak spot: no test drives the exit callback of a real spawned child. Every sweep test stubs `start`. Add one test that spawns through `spawnFreshPass` (or a fake start that runs `onExit`), kills the child, and asserts that a second `died` end and a further pass follow.

Met. `openContext` calls `restartDeadBuilds` when a project opens (src/projects/context.ts:100). It sweeps the board for builds that have a start, no end and a dead pid. src/build/died.test.ts 'a dead build gets its end with died, and a fresh pass starts' covers the sweep. No test goes through `openContext` itself, so nothing shows the startup wiring calls it.

Met. `restartOf` returns stop when pass+1 > cap (src/board/dead-builds.ts:55-63). The sweep then moves the ticket to ready with the reason 'died on pass N, the last of the retry cap of N' and starts nothing. Covered by the test 'a build that dies on its last allowed pass stops with died and starts nothing'.

Met. `build.started` records `cap` (src/build/loop.ts `runPass`). The fold keeps it, and the sweep passes it on with `--cap`. One risk: when a start records no cap, the server applies its own copy, `DEFAULT_CAP = 5` (src/serve/dead-builds-watch.ts:22), but it spawns the build without `--cap`, so the build applies its own default. If the two defaults ever differ, the server's stop-or-restart decision and the build's real cap disagree. Take the default from the build verb's single source, or always pass the cap the server used.

review.impact: The sweep writes build.ended and ticket.pass before it starts the fresh pass. If Bun.spawn throws, the ticket stays in building with an ended build. The next sweep skips it because its last build is ended. The same happens when the fresh `werk build --after-death` exits before it writes build.started, for example on a BuildRefused or a git failure in releaseBranch. The ticket is then stuck in building with no process. The catch in restartDeadBuilds also hides the spawn failure.
review.fix: Catch a failed spawn in the sweep and move the ticket to ready with a reason. Make the exit handler check the board after the child exits. If the ticket is still in building and its last build is ended, move it to ready with a reason.

review.impact: `void child.exited.then(onExit)` runs onExit, which is sweepDeadBuilds, with no catch. A throw from a board read or write becomes an unhandled promise rejection in the long-running server process.
review.fix: Use `.then(onExit).catch(() => {})`, or wrap the onExit callback in a try/catch as restartDeadBuilds does.

review.impact: DEFAULT_CAP = 5 repeats the default that `werk build` has in src/verbs/build.ts. The two can drift apart, and a drift would change the cap that applies to a dead build with no recorded cap.
review.fix: Define the default cap once, in a shared module such as the build loop's options module, and import it in both places.

review.impact: The verb builds a fake DeadBuild, with a cast `died as string`, only to call deathText. This couples the verb to the DeadBuild shape. It also creates a `dead` object that the lines around it must treat as possibly null.
review.fix: Make deathText take `{ pass: number }`, or build the whole resume object in a helper in dead-builds.ts, for example `resumeOf(session)`.

review.impact: The resume checks are spread through buildTicket: the column check, a fake `{ ok: true }` for the move, and the obligation condition. This makes the function harder to follow. Nothing checks that the session passed to --after-death is the ticket's last ended session, so a manual `--after-death` can start a second build on a live ticket.
review.fix: Pull the resume setup into a small helper. Check that the last build of the ticket is ended and that its session equals the `--after-death` session.

review.impact: DEFAULT_CAP = 5 copies the default that `werk build` already has, and the comment admits it. If one default changes, the sweep's stop decision and the spawned build's cap silently disagree.
review.fix: Import the default cap from one shared constant, and have both src/verbs/build.ts and this file use it.

review.impact: `resume !== undefined` is tested about six times in `buildTicket`. The checks cover the expected column, the error text, the worktree release, the move event, the build id and the obligation. Each one is a separate branch, so the ready-build and resumed-build paths are hard to follow and easy to let drift apart.
review.fix: Compute `const resuming = resume !== undefined` and a small `expectedColumn` once. Move the start-up differences (move to building, open the obligation, release the branch) into one helper or a single branch.

review.impact: The `resume` block uses a truthiness test on `dead` and an `as string` cast on `died`. It also builds a throwaway DeadBuild with a made-up shape just to call `deathText`. The cast and the fake object hide the types.
review.fix: Narrow once with `if (died !== undefined && dead !== null)`. Give `deathText` a `(pass: number)` parameter, or build the resume object in a small helper.

review.impact: The cap validation repeats `as number` casts, and the conditional spread makes the push call harder to read.
review.fix: Use `typeof cap === "number" && Number.isInteger(cap) && cap >= 1` in a local `validCap`. Assign `cap` on the build object after the push, or spread once.

review.impact: The empty `catch` drops every sweep error with no log. A persistent failure, such as a bad board or a missing binary, would leave dead builds unrestarted with nothing to show for it.
review.fix: Report the error through the project's existing warning or log path, or narrow the catch to the errors that are expected.

review.impact: The resume test makes a temp directory with `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "werk-died-"))` and never removes it. The worktree and its parent directory stay on disk after every run. This breaks the #werk-test-store rule that each test's stores are removed when the test ends. Also, if an assertion fails before `releaseBranch` removes the worktree, the repo's worktree registration points at a leaked path.
review.fix: Create the directory inside `project.dir`, or track it and remove it in `afterEach` with `rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })`.

review.impact: Every sweep test passes a `start` stub that ignores `onExit`. Nothing tests that `onExit` sweeps again after a fresh pass exits, which is the repeat-sweep path in `sweepDeadBuilds`. Nothing covers `spawnFreshPass` either: its argument list (`--after-death`, `--cap`) and its `WERK_LOG` env. Breaking either would go unnoticed. Nothing covers `restartDeadBuilds` in `context.ts` swallowing errors from the sweep.
review.fix: Add a test that captures `onExit` in the stub, calls it, and asserts a second sweep runs. Add a test for `spawnFreshPass` with an injected `selfCommand` or env that checks the spawned arguments.

review.impact: The sweep also writes a `ticket.pass` event and a `step.ended` pipeline event with `reason: "died"`. Only the board-side `passes` is asserted, so the pipeline event could be dropped or malformed without a failing test. The precedence `build.cap ?? options.cap ?? DEFAULT_CAP` is not tested at sweep level either. No test shows that a cap recorded on the start overrides the sweep's `cap` option.
review.fix: Read the pipeline log in the first sweep test and assert the `step.ended` record. Add a case where the start records `cap: 2`, the sweep option is 5, and the death is on pass 2, so the ticket stops.

review.impact: The parsing of `cap` in `fold.ts` `buildStarted` is tested only for a valid value. Invalid values (0, negative, a non-integer, a string) are meant to be dropped, but nothing asserts that. The fold edge could regress and give a dead build a nonsense cap.
review.fix: Add cases with `cap: 0`, `cap: 1.5` and `cap: "3"`, and expect `deadBuilds` to return no `cap` key.

review.impact: The resume path in `buildTicket` is not tested for these cases: `--after-death` with a pass already at or above the cap, `releaseBranch` when no worktree holds the branch, and the obligation not being reopened on resume. Each of these could regress silently.
review.fix: Add a test that resumes with `--cap` equal to the dead pass and checks the outcome. Add a test that checks no second `obligation.opened` is appended after resume.

review.impact: `releaseBranch` runs `git worktree remove --force` and then `rmSync(dir, {recursive: true, force: true})` on any worktree listed for the branch. It never checks that the path is a build worktree. If the branch is checked out in the main working tree, the first entry in the listing, it force-removes and recursively deletes the user's repository checkout. This can happen if someone checked out the ticket branch `r/01` in the main checkout. `--after-death` is also callable directly from the CLI.
review.fix: Skip the first `worktree` entry, which is the main working tree, and skip any `dir` equal to `repo`. Ideally only remove worktrees under the directory that `addWorktree` creates. Do the `rmSync` only if `git worktree remove` succeeded.

review.impact: `--after-death` takes any string that matches `<x>:p<n>`. The build id and pass number are not checked against the ticket's last recorded build. A hand-run command can graft a fresh pass onto an unrelated build id, which skips the obligation-open step and uses attacker-chosen pass numbering. The server path is trusted, but the verb is a public entry point.
review.fix: In `buildTicket`, when `resume` is set, check that `resume.buildId` and `afterPass` match the ticket's last unended or died build session in the board. Refuse the build otherwise.

review.impact: `dead.session` comes from the board log and is passed as an argv value after `--after-death`. A session id that starts with `-`, such as `--cap:p1`, could be parsed as a flag by `parseArgs`. There is no shell injection, because `Bun.spawn` takes an array, but the argument is not guarded.
review.fix: Make `parseSession` require that the session start with an alphanumeric character, or pass the value as `--after-death=<session>`.

causeOfLast.why: an earlier pass added `review-prompt.ts` to the pure-file list without a test file of its own, which the pure-list card requires.

review.impact: When a last counted pass defers small gaps and `fileFollowup` returns null, the ticket still merges. The null can come from no free number, a follow-up that fails its own checks, or a board refusal. The grader's gaps are then dropped with no follow-up and no record of why. `BuildResult.reason` is left unset, so the loss is invisible to the person and to the board.
review.fix: When `deferred` is non-empty and `fileFollowup` returns null, set `reason` on the merging result, for example 'small gaps not filed: <why>'. Or have `fileFollowup` return a discriminated result with the failure cause, so the loop can report which step failed.

review.impact: The ticket file is written before the `ticket.planned` board event. If the board refuses the event, the function returns null and leaves an orphan ticket file. The next number scan skips it, but the file stays on disk without a board entry.
review.fix: Append the board event first and write the file after it succeeds, or remove the file when `planned.ok` is false.

review.impact: The result of the `ticket.followup` link event is ignored. If the link append fails, the follow-up exists but the source ticket does not point to it, and the loop still reports the follow-up as filed.
review.fix: Check `.ok` on the link append and treat a failure like the other failures, for example by returning null or reporting it.

review.impact: judgePass is about 100 lines and does six jobs in one body: running the grader, parsing and settling the grade, running the reviewers, collecting findings, writing the findings file, and building the red text and reason. It has a dozen exits and two local closures. This is hard to follow and hard to change, for example if the reviewer step changes without the grader step.
review.fix: Split it into `gradeStage(...)`, which returns a red outcome or a Judged, and `reviewStage(...)`, which returns the outcome. Move the reason and text assembly into a pure helper in review.ts.

review.impact: `as never` casts on `isSmallGap(line(...) as never)` and `delivery.lines[0] as never` hide the type of the argument. They also silence the type check if GradeLine changes. These are type-suppression escape hatches.
review.fix: Make a helper `const lineOf = (g: Grade, id: string): GradeLine => { const l = g.lines.find(x => x.id === id); if (!l) throw new Error(id); return l; }` and pass its result directly.

review.impact: The test name says 'a broken grader and a silent reviewer each fail the pass', but it only exercises the broken grader. The reviewer case is a separate test further down. The name is misleading.
review.fix: Rename it to 'a broken grader reply fails the pass as a failed step'.

review.impact: The `reviewer-tests` crash test builds the same success result event by hand that the new `result()` helper already produces. Several tests also declare `const result = await build()`, which shadows the module-level `result` helper. That is easy to misread and breaks if someone calls the helper after the shadow.
review.fix: Use `result('{"findings":[]}')` in the crash test, and rename the local variables to `run` or `out`.

review.impact: `touchesOf` parses the ticket text again, and `gatherGrading` already parses the same text and strips the leading `#` from the cites. The ticket is parsed twice for one build, and the parsing logic is split across two places.
review.fix: Have `gatherGrading` also return `touches`, or parse once in the caller and pass the Ticket to both.

review.impact: The ticket file is written before `appendBoardEvent` for `ticket.planned`. If the board refuses the event, the function returns null and the `.md` file stays on disk as an orphan. The next call counts that file as a taken number through `ticketFileNumbers`.
review.fix: Write the file only after the board accepts the event, or delete the file when `planned.ok` is false.

review.impact: The follow-up failure path in `src/build/file-followup.ts` has no test. That path covers no free number, a follow-up that fails its own checks, and a board refusal. It returns null and the build still merges, with no follow-up and no trace of the dropped gaps. A regression there would pass every test, and the `fileFollowup` file I/O is only checked on the success path.
review.fix: Add a test that makes `fileFollowup` return null, for example by filling the plan's numbers or giving the ticket a check that breaks the size limit. Assert that the build still merges, `followup` is undefined, and no `r/02` exists. Also assert what the output says about the dropped gaps.

review.impact: The test title says 'a broken grader and a silent reviewer', but the body only covers a broken grader reply. A reader assumes the reviewer case is covered here. It is covered in the next test, which crashes the reviewer rather than leaving it silent. Nothing tests a grader or reviewer that times out or goes silent, or an archive that lands during judging (`kind: "archived"` from `judgePass`).
review.fix: Rename the test to 'a broken grader reply fails the pass as a failed step'. Add a case for an archive or abort while a judge runs, and assert the build ends as archived with no merge.

review.impact: The test finds the recorded findings by string-matching raw pipeline log lines (`includes('"step":"pass"')`). It then reads `.findings` from the first matching line. A change to JSON key order, spacing or event shape breaks it with an unclear failure. It also assumes that the first matching line is pass 1.
review.fix: Read the pass through the existing `readPipeline` fold, or a helper that parses each line as JSON and filters on `step` and `type`.

review.impact: The scripted-ask test switched from `overseen()` to `build("--silence-ms", "5000", ...)`. It also dropped the `messages().map(role)` assertion, which was replaced by a filtered launch-role check. This keeps the test from flaking under the new judge launches. The prompt-level role assertion is gone, so it no longer checks that the classifier's message record is present.
review.fix: Restore a role assertion on the filtered message records. Use `project.launches()` filtered to `kind === "message"` and `role` in builder/classifier, so classifier prompt delivery is still checked.

review.impact: The judges are meant to be read-only, but the allow rules `Bash(git diff:*)`, `Bash(git log:*)` and `Bash(git show:*)` match any arguments. `git diff --output=<path>` and `git log --output=<path>` write a file, so a judge steered by prompt injection from diff content could overwrite a file in the worktree. I did not read the part of the diff that was cut off, so I did not check whether the runtime blocks this some other way.
review.fix: Deny `--output` in the judge permissions, for example with a deny rule for `Bash(git * --output*)`. Alternatively, give the judge a wrapper that runs only fixed git invocations. Add a test that the judge's launch args hold that deny rule.

review.impact: The follow-up ticket quotes the grader's gap text inside `"..."`, and the gap is only flattened and path-stripped. A gap that contains `"` or backticks, or that mimics ticket headers or markdown, breaks the quoting. That text goes unescaped into a ticket file that a later builder reads as instructions, so the grader's model output can inject text into the next builder's prompt. The ticket's own-checks validation catches size and file paths, not this.
review.fix: Escape or replace `"` and backticks in `quotableGap`. Strip leading `#`, `-` and similar markdown from the quoted text.

review.impact: closureOf copies the whole adjacency array for each edge (`[...(dependsOn.get(...) ?? []), edge.to]`). It also scans `found` with `includes` for every queued id. That is quadratic in the edge count and the closure size. It runs once per build, and map graphs are small, so the cost is negligible today.
review.fix: Use `dependsOn.get(from)?.push(to)` after creating the array when it is missing, and track visited ids in a `Set` alongside the ordered `found` array.

causeOfLast.why: the main line merged grading and review into the build loop after this ticket's restart logic was written.

grade.gap: Passes: a dead build gets its end with died, and the fresh pass starts from the branch's last commit, so committed work is kept and uncommitted work is lost (src/build/died.test.ts). Not covered: the loop writes build.ended as soon as the agent exits (src/build/loop.ts:282), before the checks, the grader and the reviewers run. A process killed during those steps leaves no start without an end, so deadBuilds (src/board/dead-builds.ts:35) never finds it. The ticket then stays in building with no restart. Also untested: no test kills a process that spawnFreshPass started and checks that its onExit sweep writes died and starts the next pass. The sweep is only called by hand in died.test.ts.
openContext calls restartDeadBuilds when a project opens (src/projects/context.ts:100). No test drives this through server start: the tests call sweepDeadBuilds directly.

A dead build is found only while a builder session's start has no end. A build process that dies during its checks, grader or review after build.ended is never found as dead (src/build/loop.ts:282, src/board/dead-builds.ts:35). The card says the server looks for any dead build.

When the cap stops a build, the sweep moves the ticket from building to ready (src/serve/dead-builds-watch.ts:68). The builder loop already does the same at its retry cap, but the card says only an archive returns a building ticket to ready.

review.impact: `void child.exited.then(onExit)` runs `sweepDeadBuilds` with no catch. `restartDeadBuilds` in `context.ts` swallows sweep errors, but this path does not. A throw from `readBoard` or `appendBoardEvent` after a fresh pass exits becomes an unhandled promise rejection. In the long-lived server process that can crash it, or it fails silently. The sweep also stops quietly.
review.fix: Wrap the exit callback in a try/catch, for example `child.exited.then(() => { try { onExit(); } catch {} })`, or give `sweepDeadBuilds` one shared error boundary that both callers use.

review.impact: The sweep writes `build.ended` (died) for the old session before the fresh `werk build --after-death` process starts. If that process is refused or crashes before `runPass` appends `build.started`, the ticket stays in `building` with its last build ended. Refusals include a missing ticket file, a grading failure and a `releaseBranch` or `addWorktree` error. `deadBuilds` only looks at the last build's `ended` flag, so no later sweep will find it. The ticket is stuck in `building` and nothing retries it.
review.fix: On a failure before the first resumed pass starts, move the ticket back to `ready` with a reason. Alternatively, have the sweep also treat a `building` ticket whose last build has ended and which has no live process as stuck.

review.impact: `DEFAULT_CAP = 5` repeats the default that `werk build` applies in `verbs/build.ts`. If one changes, a death at the cap boundary is judged with a different cap than the build used. The sweep passes `--cap` only when the start recorded it.
review.fix: Export one default-cap constant from a shared module, such as `build/loop.ts` or a small constants file. Have both the verb and the watch import it.

review.impact: The resume branches are spread through `buildTicket`. The column check is a nested ternary that duplicates the column name in the error message. A fake `{ ok: true as const }` stands in for the `ticket.moved` result. The obligation-open step is also conditional. This makes the main function harder to read.
review.fix: Compute `const expected = resume ? "building" : "ready"` once and use it for both the check and the message. Pull the 'enter building' step into a small helper that is a no-op on resume.

review.impact: `resume` is checked in six places in `buildTicket`: the column check, the error text, `releaseBranch`, the `ticket.moved` event, the obligation, and the loop bounds. The column check is also written twice, once as a condition and once inside the message. The `moved` fallback `{ ok: true as const }` is a fake result that only exists to satisfy the type of the branch below it. This makes the function harder to follow and easy to get wrong when changed.
review.fix: Compute `const expected = resume !== undefined ? "building" : "ready"` once and use it for both the check and the message. Pull the start-up steps into two small helpers, one for a fresh build and one for a resume. The `moved` and obligation steps then live only in the fresh-build helper, so no fake `ok` object is needed.

review.impact: `DEFAULT_CAP = 5` is a second copy of the default retry cap that the comment says `werk build` has. If one changes without the other, a restart's cap check and a manual build's cap disagree.
review.fix: Export the default cap from one place, such as `src/build/loop.ts` or a small constants module, and import it in both `src/verbs/build.ts` and this file.

review.impact: The `resume` option is built by testing `dead` for truthiness and then casting `died as string`. The `Build` that `deathText` takes is rebuilt by hand from `dead`, and this couples the verb to the shape of `DeadBuild`.
review.fix: Narrow with `if (died !== undefined && dead !== null)` so no cast is needed. Alternatively, give `dead-builds.ts` a helper such as `resumeOf(ticket, session)` that returns the `resume` object or null.

review.impact: `TICKET`, `writeLines`, `builder` and `CLI` are copied from `build.test.ts`. The two files will drift apart.
review.fix: Move the shared test helpers into the new `judge-fixtures.ts`, or into a neighbouring fixtures file, next to the helpers that this change already extracted.

review.impact: The `cap` validation is an inline ternary with two casts inside the `push` call. It is hard to read and is not covered by a test for an invalid cap.
review.fix: Compute `const cap = Number.isInteger(rec.cap) && (rec.cap as number) >= 1 ? (rec.cap as number) : undefined` before the push. Then spread `cap === undefined ? {} : { cap }`. Add a test for a start with an invalid cap.

review.impact: The empty `catch` hides every failure of the sweep, including real bugs. The comment says only that the sweep runs again later.
review.fix: Log the error to stderr in the catch, or catch only the expected errors.

review.impact: The change to `buildStarted` in `src/board/fold.ts` drops an invalid `cap` silently. The tests only cover a valid cap (2) and an absent cap. If the guard `Number.isInteger(cap) && cap >= 1` were removed, a start with `cap: 0`, `cap: 1.5` or `cap: "3"` would pass through to `restartOf`. A cap of 0 would stop every dead build, and no test would fail.
review.fix: Add a test that folds a `build.started` with `cap: 0`, `cap: 1.5` and a string cap. Assert that `deadBuilds` returns no `cap` property for each.

review.impact: `spawnFreshPass` is untested: its argument list (`--after-death`, `--cap`, `WERK_LOG`) and the `onExit` re-sweep. `restartDeadBuilds` in `src/projects/context.ts` and its swallowed-error path are also untested. All the sweep tests pass a stub `start` and never call `onExit`. If the spawn arguments or the re-sweep were broken, the whole restart feature would fail in the real server and every test would still pass.
review.fix: Test `spawnFreshPass` with an injected `selfCommand` or a fake `env`, and assert the argv it builds. Add a sweep test whose `start` calls `onExit` and checks that a second death is handled. Add a test that `openContext` restarts a seeded dead build.

review.impact: The `restartOf` stop case only checks `action`, not `reason`. The `deathText` test only checks for the substring "Pass 3 died". A wrong reason or a degraded failure text would pass.
review.fix: Assert the full stop reason (`died on pass 5, the last of the retry cap of 5`). Assert that the death text names the lost uncommitted work.

review.impact: Edge cases in `parseSession` and `deadBuilds` are not covered. `parseSession` is not tested with a leading-zero pass (`p01`), an empty build id (`:p3`) or a non-numeric pass. A ticket in building with no builds (the `last === undefined` branch) is not tested. A ticket whose earlier build is unended but whose last build has ended is not tested.
review.fix: Add those cases. They are cheap and they pin the regex and the last-build selection.

review.impact: `releaseBranch` is only tested through the end-to-end CLI test, in the case where a worktree exists. The case with no worktree for the branch is not tested. Neither is a worktree directory that has already been removed. The resumed build also does not assert that no second `obligation.opened` is written.
review.fix: Add a `git.ts` unit test for `releaseBranch` with and without a holding worktree. Assert in the resume test that the map log has no new `obligation.opened`.

review.impact: `releaseBranch` runs `rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })` on any worktree path that git lists for the branch. It does this even when `git worktree remove --force` failed, because the `git` helper does not throw. If the ticket branch (for example `r/01`) is checked out in the main checkout, the first entry in the listing is the main worktree. `git worktree remove` refuses to remove it, and `rmSync` then deletes the whole repository directory. A worktree with a locked or odd state is also deleted unchecked. The path comes straight from git output, with no check that it is a werk-created worktree.
review.fix: Skip the main worktree, which is the first entry in the listing or the one equal to `repo`. Only call `rmSync` when the `git worktree remove` call exited 0. Better, only remove worktrees under the directory where `addWorktree` creates them.

grade.gap: In a real run, later grades never judge against the decision pass's proposal. proposedBriefs (src/build/gather.ts) reads map.obligations.get(buildId).proposed. The fold only fills that list when a node.proposed event carries an `obligation` field (src/map/fold.ts ~line 356). No verb ever writes that field: `werk add` (src/verbs/add.ts) has no --obligation flag and reads no env var, and the loop does not pass the obligation id to the agent in a form `add` reads. So when the builder runs `werk add` in the decision pass, the card is a ghost with no link to the obligation. proposedBriefs returns [] and gradingWith adds no `card-<id>` line. The decision-pass brief (src/build/brief.ts, DECISION) also does not tell the agent how to tie the card to the obligation. Only the fixture in gather.test.ts covers the path, because it writes `obligation: "o1"` into the ghost by hand. Fix: (1) let a builder's proposal carry the build's obligation id, for example `werk add ... --obligation <id>` or an env var that the loop sets and `add` reads; (2) tell the decision pass in the brief to use it; (3) add a build.test.ts case where the decision pass's fake agent proposes a card, and assert that the next grade includes the `card-<id>` contradiction line and that the brief's 'Cards proposed by this build' section lists the card.

The brief tells the pass to close the obligation with a proposed card, but no verb links a proposal to the obligation. Until then, a pass that proposes cards leaves its obligation open (see criterion-4).

nextIsDecision (src/build/decision-pass.ts) treats two failed passes in a row on the same delivery or scope line as a missing decision. gapsOf counts every failed delivery line as a question that no card answers, so an ordinary builder bug that fails the same criterion twice also triggers a decision pass. The card asks for findings 'and no cited card answers the question behind them'. Consider limiting the area rule to lines whose question no cited card covers, not every failed criterion.

Not a failing gap, but outside the scenario: the diff also sends the tab name on the model, clear, ask and commands routes (src/serve/chat-route.ts modelRoute/clearRoute/askRoute/commandsRoute, client/lib/chat-store.ts urlOf). It also adds the '+' button that opens a new tab (client/app/tab-strip.tsx tab-new, tabs-store open()). The story needs two tabs, so the button supports it. The per-tab routing keeps each tab's agent consistent. Remove any of it only if another ticket owns the multichat tabs (#werk-multichat).

review.impact: A GET to /chat?tab=<any valid name> calls sessionOf, which creates and keeps a ChatSession. Any request that names a new tab adds a permanent entry to context.chats and to the /tabs list. Nothing closes or limits these sessions, and closeContext stops them all only when the project closes.
review.fix: Make GET /chat for an unknown tab return empty history without creating a session. Create the session only on send, model or clear. Alternatively, cap the number of tabs.

review.impact: open() picks the next tab name from this page's own order. A tab that another page opened but this page has not loaded yet gets the same name, so two pages share one session by accident. The server's /tabs list is the real source of names, and it is read only at load.
review.fix: Make the server allocate the name of a new tab, or re-read /tabs before choosing a name. Use unique ids instead of counters.

review.impact: tabOf checks tab names with TURN_NAME, which is the pattern for turn ids. The two uses are coupled by accident, and a later change to the turn pattern would silently change which tab names are valid. The tab name also goes into file names (session-<name>).
review.fix: Define a separate TAB_NAME pattern for tab names, for example one that excludes '.' and ':'.

review.impact: The emit wrapper spreads event.data and adds the tab name. If any event's data is not a plain object, the spread corrupts it, and the type system does not guard this.
review.fix: Confirm that all ChatEvent data is object-shaped and type it that way. Otherwise wrap the data as { tab, data }.

review.impact: ChatPane takes three optional props (tabs, onSelect, onOpen) that must all be present for the strip to render, so valid and invalid prop combinations are both expressible. The dead-line and own-error rendering are also gated on tabs alone.
review.fix: Group them into one optional prop, such as tabs?: {state, onSelect, onOpen}, or move the strip fully into TabbedChat.

review.impact: The constant "main" is defined three times: MAIN in src/serve/chat-route.ts, MAIN_TAB in client/lib/chat-store.ts, and the literal "main" in the Context comment and the tests. The server and client names have to stay in step, and nothing enforces that.
review.fix: Keep one constant for each side and comment the coupling. On the server, export MAIN from a small module and have tabsRoute and the context use it.

review.impact: The two lines `const tab = tabOf(req); if (typeof tab !== "string") return tab;` are repeated in chatRoute, askRoute, modelRoute, clearRoute and commandsRoute. Each new route has to remember them, and a route that forgets them silently acts on the main conversation.
review.fix: Add a helper such as `withTab(req, (tab) => ...)`, or parse the tab once in projectRoute and pass it to the handlers.

review.impact: modelRoute and clearRoute check the tab only after the method check, but modelRoute parses the body and validates the pick before it reads the tab. A bad tab name is therefore reported after the other errors, and the order differs from the other routes.
review.fix: Resolve the tab at the top of each handler, as chatRoute does.

review.impact: The tab name is checked with TURN_NAME, a regex made for turn ids. If turn id rules change, tab validation changes with them without anyone noticing.
review.fix: Define a separate TAB_NAME regex, or rename the shared one.

review.impact: refresh() reads `stores.get(tab) as ChatStore`, a type cast that hides a possible missing entry. The `as Record<string, ChatState>` cast after Object.fromEntries is another cast.
review.fix: Build the chats object from the stores map without casts, for example by looping over `stores` in `order`.

review.impact: A generated timing log is committed with the change and adds noise to the diff.
review.fix: Leave it out of the commit, or add it to .gitignore if it is not meant to be tracked.

review.impact: ChatPane takes three optional props that only work together (tabs, onSelect, onOpen), and it re-checks all three at render. A caller can pass only some of them and get no strip with no error.
review.fix: Group them into one optional `tabs: {state, onSelect, onOpen}` prop, or render the strip in TabbedChat.

review.impact: After the second send, the test waits for `deadOf('A')` to be undefined, then checks for a `turn-end` event once, with no wait. If the dead flag clears when the message is accepted, before the new agent replies, the wait passes at once and the `turn-end` check can run before the reply arrives. The test would then fail intermittently. `deadOf` also returns undefined when no `dead` event exists, so the wait cannot tell 'cleared' from 'not yet reported'.
review.fix: Wait on the thing being asserted: `await until(async () => events.some(e => e.name === 'turn-end') || undefined)`. Skip the wait on `deadOf`, or make it look for a `dead` event whose error is null.

review.impact: Per-conversation file names (`session-<name>`, `chat-model-<name>.json`) are new behaviour, and no test covers them. Nothing checks that a named tab's session and settings stay apart from the main conversation's, or that `clearSessionId` on one tab leaves the other alone. A regression would mix the saved state of different tabs without any test failing.
review.fix: In the state-store test, write the session and settings under `main` and under a name. Check that each reads back separately, and that clearing one leaves the other.

review.impact: `runningTurns`, `background`, `dead` and `stopTurns` now combine every chat, and `closeContext` stops every chat. No test covers the combining, such as dead picking the first non-null error or background summing across chats. The stubbed `Context` in the route tests leaves these functions out.
review.fix: Add a unit test that puts two or more fake sessions in `context.chats`. Assert the summed `background`, the concatenated `runningTurns`, the first non-null `dead`, and that `stopTurns` and `closeContext` stop all of them.

review.impact: The tab-name validation is tested only for `GET /chat`. The `/commands`, `/ask`, `/model` and `/clear` routes also call `tabOf`, and none is tested for a bad tab or for routing to a named tab. `/tabs` ordering is checked only once.
review.fix: Add a short test that sends an invalid `?tab=` to each route and expects a 400. Add a case where `commandsRoute` or `askRoute` gets a tab that does not exist.
