review.impact: The test run appended timing lines to the tracked `.werk/fold-ms.jsonl` in the checkout, so a test wrote to real project data. It also adds noise to the diff. This goes against the rule that each test uses its own store copy.
review.fix: Revert this file in the change. Point the fold timing log at a temp directory while tests run, or leave it out of version control.

review.impact: The strip test never checks `data-current`, which drives the current-tab style. It does not cover an empty `chips` list, or the pane showing no dead lines when `tabs` is missing from `ChatPane`.
review.fix: Assert `data-current` on the chips, and add a `ChatPane` test with no `tabs` that expects no strip and no dead lines.

review.impact: A GET to /chat?tab=<name> builds and keeps a new session for any valid name, and the GET needs no token. Names are limited to 80 characters but their number is not limited. A local page or script can create sessions without end, and each one stays in `context.chats` until the project closes. Sessions only write files once a model or session change is persisted, so the cost is memory and a growing /tabs list.
review.fix: On GET, do not create a session for an unknown tab. Return an empty history instead. Create sessions only on authenticated POSTs, and cap the number of tabs, for example 20.

review.impact: The tab name goes straight into file names (`session-${name}`, `chat-model-${name}.json`). The TURN_NAME regex blocks `/` and a leading dot, so path traversal is not possible. The regex is case-sensitive, though, and macOS file systems usually are not. Tabs `a` and `A` would then share one session file and one settings file, so their sessions and models would mix.
review.fix: Lowercase tab names before use, or reject names that differ only by case. Alternatively, encode the name in the file name, for example as a hex string.

review.impact: Any request with a new valid `?tab=` name builds a session and stores it in `context.chats`, forever. A GET to `/chat` does this and needs no token. Each session reads its state files from disk and holds an event history. Each tab that gets a message can also start its own agent child process. A page, script or loop that varies the tab name makes the server's memory and process count grow without limit. `tabsRoute` also returns every such name to all pages.
review.fix: Cap the number of conversations per project, for example 8 or 16, and refuse a new name past the cap with a 4xx. Make the GET and history read create a session only for a name that already exists, or for the main tab. Create a session only on an authenticated POST.

review.impact: `receive` calls `storeOf(...).receive`, which already triggers `refresh` through the subscription. It then calls `refresh()` again. Each streamed part rebuilds the whole `TabsState` and notifies the listeners twice. The shown pane re-renders each time, because `TabbedChat` passes it a new `tabs` object. A delta from a background tab also re-renders the shown pane.
review.fix: Drop the explicit `refresh()` in `receive`. It is needed only when `storeOf` just created the store, and `storeOf` can refresh then. Keep `chats` entries referentially stable for tabs whose state did not change, and memoize `ChatPane` so it re-renders only when its own state or the dead lines change.

causeOfLast.why: the failing tests were unrelated to this change and timed out under load, and they pass in a full run with no code change.

review.impact: sweepDeadBuilds writes the build end and the red pass before it calls `options.start`. If `start` throws (for example Bun.spawn fails), the old build already has an end. The ticket stays in `building` with no live build, so no later sweep sees it as dead and it is stuck. The exception also skips every other dead build in the same sweep. `restartDeadBuilds` in context.ts then swallows the error silently.
review.fix: Wrap `options.start` in a try/catch inside the loop. On failure, move the ticket back to `ready` with a reason, as the stop branch does, and carry on with the remaining dead builds.

review.impact: The bare `catch {}` hides every sweep failure, including a corrupt board log or a bad spawn. Nothing is logged, so a stuck restart cannot be diagnosed.
review.fix: Log the error, or surface it, instead of discarding it.

review.impact: `DEFAULT_CAP = 5` duplicates the default that `werk build` applies to `--cap`. `options.cap` is used to decide whether to restart, but `spawnFreshPass` never forwards it. When a start records no cap, the decision and the spawned build can use different caps if either default changes.
review.fix: Share one cap default constant with the build verb. Have `spawnFreshPass` pass the effective cap to the child.

review.impact: The verb builds a fake `DeadBuild` with a placeholder ticket and session just to call `deathText`, which only needs the pass number. This couples the CLI to the whole DeadBuild shape.
review.fix: Have `deathText` take `pass: number`, or build the failure text from `dead.pass` directly.

review.impact: DEFAULT_CAP = 5 restates the default retry cap that `werk build` already has, and the comment says so. If one default changes, the restart cap of a build without a recorded cap will quietly differ from the cap of a build started by hand.
review.fix: Export the default cap from one place, for example the build module or verbs/build.ts, and import it here.

review.impact: `resume !== undefined` is tested five times in buildTicket (column check, error text, release, move event, obligation). The expected column is worked out twice, a fake `{ ok: true as const }` stands in for the move result, and the function is harder to follow.
review.fix: Compute `const expected = resume ? 'building' : 'ready'` once and use it in both the check and the message. Pull the move and obligation steps into a helper that is skipped on resume, so the fake result goes away.

review.impact: The TICKET text, `writeLines`, `builder`, `boardPath`, `ticket` and `git` helpers are copied from build.test.ts. The judge fixtures were extracted but these were not, so the two test files can drift apart.
review.fix: Move the shared ticket and file helpers into a fixtures module next to judge-fixtures.ts and import them in both tests.

review.impact: `died as string` is a cast, and the `dead ? ... : {}` spread rebuilds a DeadBuild by hand only to call deathText. Both exist to get around the types.
review.fix: Have deathText take `{ pass }`, or narrow once with `if (died !== undefined && dead !== null)`. That removes the cast and the fake `ticket` and `session` fields.

review.impact: The `Number.isInteger(cap)` check is followed by two `as number` casts and an inline conditional spread. This is noisy, and a bad cap is dropped without any message.
review.fix: Use a small helper such as `positiveInt(rec.cap)` that returns `number | undefined`, and spread its result.

review.impact: The empty `catch {}` hides every sweep failure, such as a malformed board or a failed spawn. A dead build then stays unrestarted with no trace.
review.fix: Log the error, or at least report it through the project's existing warning path, before moving on.

review.impact: The `onExit` re-sweep callback is the only path that restarts a build that dies again after the server started its fresh pass. Nothing tests that path, and nothing tests `spawnFreshPass` (its argv, `--cap` forwarding or `WERK_LOG`). The sweep tests use a fake `start` that never calls `onExit`. A broken chain, such as a missing `--cap` or a dropped `onExit`, would pass the suite.
review.fix: Add a sweep test whose fake `start` calls `onExit` after appending a new dead start, and assert the second death is handled. Add a `spawnFreshPass` test with a stub command or injected spawner that checks the argv and env.

review.impact: The new `cap` validation (`Number.isInteger(cap) && cap >= 1`) has no test for invalid values. A cap of 0, 1.5 or a string should be dropped. A regression would let a bad cap through, and a cap of 0 would make `restartOf` stop every build.
review.fix: Add fold tests in the board fold test file. A `build.started` with `cap: 0`, `cap: 1.5` and `cap: "3"` should produce a build with no `cap`. A valid cap should be kept.

review.impact: `resume.afterPass >= cap` is untested: `--after-death X:p5 --cap 5` makes the loop body run zero times. The resume failure path is also untested for a ticket that is archived or missing. `releaseBranch` is only tested when a worktree holds the branch, not when none does. It is also not tested when the worktree directory is already gone.
review.fix: Add a CLI test for `--after-death` at pass equal to cap, and assert a defined outcome. Add a `releaseBranch` test with no worktree for the branch.

review.impact: The stop case asserts only `action === "stop"`, not the reason. Several scenarios are missing. The tests cover one build per ticket, so they would not catch `deadBuilds` picking the first build instead of the last. An earlier ended build followed by a dead one is not tested. Several dead tickets in one sweep are not tested. `parseSession` is not tested with extra colons or a leading-zero pass such as `:p01`.
review.fix: Assert `reason` contains "died on pass 5". Add a ticket with two builds, one ended and one dead, and a two-ticket board. Add parse cases for `a:b:p2` and `x:p01`.

review.impact: The sweep writes a pipeline `step.ended` event with a red result and reason `died`, but no test reads the pipeline log. Removing or breaking that write would not be caught.
review.fix: In the first test, read the pipeline log with `readPipeline` and assert the `died` step for pass 2.

review.impact: releaseBranch force-removes whatever directory `git worktree list` reports for the branch, then runs `rmSync(dir, {recursive, force})` on it. If the branch were checked out in the main worktree, `git worktree remove` would refuse, but `rmSync` would still delete the whole repository checkout. A ticket-id branch such as `r/01` is not normally checked out in the main worktree, so this is unlikely. The recursive delete has no guard.
review.fix: Skip the first `worktree` entry in the porcelain output, which is the main worktree. Also skip any dir equal to `repo`. Run `rmSync` only when `git worktree remove` succeeded or the dir is not the main worktree.

review.impact: `--after-death` takes any string ending in `:pN`. `buildTicket` uses its buildId and pass number as the obligation id and the resume point without checking them against the ticket's recorded builds. A wrong or hand-typed value attaches the pass to an unrelated obligation or skips passes. `werk build` is a local CLI, so this is only an input-validation gap.
review.fix: In `buildTicket`, when `resume` is set, require that the ticket's last build has the session `${buildId}:p${afterPass}` and has ended with `died`. Otherwise throw BuildRefused.

causeOfLast.why: the loop wrote the obligation id to the ghost only in a test fixture, and no verb ever set it, so the earlier pass left the link unfinished.

grade.gap:
Still open. Parts (1) and (2) of the earlier fix are done: `werk add --obligation` exists in src/verbs/add.ts, and the decision-pass brief in src/build/brief.ts tells the agent to pass it. Part (3) is missing. git diff 64f0980 HEAD shows no new build.test.ts case. The only new test is src/verbs/add.test.ts, which runs `add` directly against a log that already holds the obligation.

Without that test, the real path is still broken. buildTicket (src/build/loop.ts ~line 388) reads proposals from mapLog, which is the project's log. runPass, though, starts the agent with cwd tree.dir (the worktree) and env {...options.env, ...launch.env}, and it never sets WERK_LOG to mapLog. The chat session sets it (src/chat/session.ts:271), and so does run-plan.ts:220, but the build loop does not. So the agent's `werk add ... --obligation build-...` resolves logPathFor to <worktree>/.werk/log.jsonl. That writes the ghost into the worktree's log, not the log where the loop opened the obligation. As a result, proposedBriefs(readMap(mapLog).map, buildId) returns [], and gradingWith adds no `card-<id>` line.

Fix:
(a) Give the agent WERK_LOG=mapLog in runPass's env.
(b) Add the build.test.ts case asked for before: a decision pass whose fake agent runs `werk add <id> --obligation <buildId>`. Then assert two things: the next pass's brief has '## Cards proposed by this build' with the card, and the next grading has a `card-<id>` contradiction line.

The new `--obligation <id>` flag on `werk add` (src/verbs/add.ts) is a CLI surface that #werk-cli-add does not list. It carries the obligation field that the fold already reads. It is minor and follows the earlier grader's fix, but the next pass could propose a card that refines #werk-cli-add to record the flag.
The decision pass's proposal does not reach the grader in a real run, because the agent writes to the worktree log and the loop reads mapLog. See criterion-4.

When several tabs each have a chat, src/serve/chat-route.ts commandsRoute decides that 'the first chat that has any wins'. It takes the first entry of context.chats, in Map insertion order, whose list of names is not empty. The card says the server keeps the command names from the start line of the most recent agent. src/serve/chat-route.ts commandsRoute instead answers the names of the first chat in context.chats insertion order that has any. That is often the main tab's older agent, not the most recently started one. The test in src/serve/chat-route.test.ts:253 locks in the first-wins behaviour. Keep the names from the most recent agent start across the project, for example a project-level slot that each session's start line overwrites, or pick the chat whose agent started last, and update the test to match.

review.impact: The cap loop can run without a bound. A pass names its cause in the next pass's reply, and the loop writes it back onto the earlier history entry only after that next pass has run. That entry then stops counting, and `nextIsDecision` has already been evaluated. Each failed pass is therefore counted until the pass after it names `spec-gap`, and then it becomes free. Only the latest failed pass ever counts, so `counted()` stays at 1 and never reaches `options.cap` when the cap is above 1. A builder that keeps naming `spec-gap` with changing finding areas gets endless free passes, because the decision-pass trigger only fires on a repeated gap area or a `spec-gap` cause already known at that time. The `countsAgainstCap` comment promises 'never an unbounded number'. The loop does not enforce that.
review.fix: Bound the loop independently of the retroactive naming. Cap the number of free (non-counted) passes, for example `history.length < options.cap * 2` or one free pass per build. Alternatively, force the next pass to be a decision pass whenever the last pass named `spec-gap` on the earlier entry. Then `countsAgainstCap` is true for that pass. Add a loop test with a builder that names `spec-gap` on every pass.

review.impact: The rule for which failed passes are free is written twice. `settle` in pipeline/fold.ts inlines `conflict || (spec-gap && !decision)`. `countsAgainstCap` in build/decision-pass.ts has the spec-gap half. The old shared `FREE_CAUSES` constant is gone. The loop's cap and the folded `counted` can drift apart and show a different pass count than the loop used. The conflict half has no counterpart in `countsAgainstCap`.
review.fix: Keep one pure predicate, for example `countsAgainstCap` taking `{failed, archived, cause, decision}`, in a module that both the fold and the loop import. Have `settle` call it.

review.impact: The loop re-implements the fold's `nameCause` by mutating `earlier.cause` in place. `PassOutcome.cause` is therefore set in two places: `history.push` and this back-patch. This is hard to follow and easy to break.
review.fix: Move the back-patching into a small helper in decision-pass.ts, such as `nameEarlier(history, cause)`, and unit-test it. Alternatively, build the history from the folded pipeline.

review.impact: No loop-level test covers the new path where a later pass names a cause. That path is the one that sets `earlier.cause` and so decides whether a failed pass counts toward the cap. review.impact: Each pass reads cards the builder wrote into the project's decision log. The loop puts them in the next brief and adds a grader contradiction line for each. Their title, why and body come from the agent and are not sanitized. A builder could propose a lenient card, and the grader would then judge against it 'as if decided'. The brief tells the builder to choose the safest answer, but nothing enforces that. A person reviews the card only after the ticket has merged.
review.fix: Keep the grader's treatment of builder-proposed cards advisory. For example, mark any ticket that merges against a proposed card so that it needs human review. Optionally cap the length of a proposed card's text before it goes into a brief.

review.impact: The loop can run without bound, and each pass costs an agent run, the checks and a grading run. The loop condition is `counted() < options.cap`. After each pass, the code gives the previous failed pass the cause that the new pass named (loop.ts:540-541). If every pass ends with `cause: spec-gap`, each new failed pass starts with no cause, so it counts. The next pass then names `spec-gap` for it, and it becomes free. `counted()` stays at 1, so the cap is never reached. A decision pass is the only thing that would break the cycle. `nextIsDecision` only sees that last pass's cause as undefined, and then only forces one when the failed gaps of the last two passes overlap. A builder that names `spec-gap` while its grader gaps differ, or that has no grade, never gets one. Before this change the loop ran `for n <= cap`, so it was bounded.
review.fix: Bound the loop by total passes as well as by counted passes, for example `n <= options.cap * 2` or a hard maximum on `history.length`. Also resolve the pass's cause before it enters `history`, or treat a retroactively freed pass as having used up the free allowance. Then at most one free pass per open question can occur, and a decision pass always follows it. Add a test where the builder names spec-gap on every pass and the grader gaps never overlap.

review.impact: UserMessage computes offsets with a mutable `offset` variable inside a `.map` callback, only to produce stable React keys. This is a side effect in a render path and harder to read than it needs to be. The same `imageUrl?: (name: string) => string` prop type is also repeated in three components.
review.fix: Key by the part's index, since the list is static per render, and drop the offset bookkeeping. Optionally extract a shared `ImageUrl` type alias.

review.impact: This diff includes machine-generated timing log lines, including a reordering of two existing lines. It adds noise to the change and invites merge conflicts.
review.fix: Leave this file out of the commit with `git restore`, or gitignore it if it is not meant to be tracked.

review.impact: The `sent` handler repeats an inline array filter to parse `images`. If other events need the same parsing, it will be duplicated. The `newTurn` default of `[]` and the optional `images?` on the `sent` action also let an undefined value through quietly.
review.fix: Extract a small `stringList(value)` helper. Consider making `images` required on the `sent` action.

review.impact: The component test covers only one image with one matching token. `UserMessage` also has untested paths: a token whose number has no image (out-of-range or `images` empty, as for a turn another page sent), a message with several images, a message with no `imageUrl`, and a literal `[Image #1]` in text with no image. A regression such as an off-by-one in `Number(n) - 1` for a later image, or a crash on a missing image, would pass.
review.fix: Add cases for two images (`[Image #1] [Image #2]` maps to `a.png` and `b.png`), a token with no image (no ``, and the text is still shown), and no `imageUrl` prop (no ``).

review.impact: The new parsing of `body.images` is untested. It has three branches: an array of strings, an array with non-strings that get filtered out, and a missing or non-array value that becomes `[]`. Nothing checks that a live `sent` event from another page or a replayed history event reaches the reducer with its images. The other pages' view of images depends on this code. Only the e2e test covers the sender's own page, because `send` applies the images locally.
review.fix: Add a chat-store test that feeds a `sent` event with `images: ["a.png", 3]` and expects `turns[0].images` to equal `["a.png"]`. Add one for an event with no `images` field, which should give `[]`. Also add a reducer test in the chat-log lib tests that `sent` stores `images` and defaults to `[]`.

review.impact: The test checks only a single path with a simple basename. It does not check that a nested or Windows-style path gives the stored name, or that several images keep their order. The ordering is what ties each image to its `[Image #N]` token.
review.fix: Send two image paths in one message and expect `["a.png", "b.png"]` in order.

review.impact: The fatal test only calls `onCrash` for the login error. The bad-flag text is checked with `isFatal` but never passed to `onCrash`. No test uses a fatal text with `retried: true` or `hasSession: false`. The rewritten condition `!isFatal(text) && !state.retried` could break on those inputs without any test failing.
review.fix: Also assert `onCrash(flag, fresh)` and `onCrash(login, { hasSession: true, retried: true })`. Both should return the same `report` message.

The 'bad call' test now runs `remove --reparent` against a live subtree instead of the state left after restore. It checks a slightly different case than the original did.

review.impact: The diff includes runtime telemetry lines that the tests appended. They have nothing to do with the change and add merge-conflict noise.
review.fix: Leave this file out of the commit with `git checkout -- .werk/fold-ms.jsonl`.

review.impact: `as never` silences the type check on the whole deps object. If the store's deps shape changes, this test keeps compiling and fails with an unclear error. It is a type-suppression escape hatch.
review.fix: Build the deps with the real type, for example a typed helper or `satisfies Partial<Deps>`. If the repo has a shared test-deps factory for the chat store, use it. Otherwise cast only the unused fields.

review.impact: Timing lines appended by running the tests are included in the change. They add noise to the diff and can cause merge conflicts, and they have nothing to do with the feature.
review.fix: Drop this file from the commit with `git checkout .werk/fold-ms.jsonl`. If the file is meant to be a local artifact, gitignore it.

review.impact: The new test only covers a file 5 MB over the limit. The client check is `file.size > MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` and the server check is `byteLength > MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`. A change to `>=` or an off-by-one on either side would not be caught, and the client and server could disagree at exactly 20 MB. A file under the limit is also not shown to still reach `fetch`.
review.fix: Add a case with a `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`-sized blob that expects the request to be sent, and a case with `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES + 1` that expects the refusal. Import the constant instead of hard-coding 25 * 1024 * 1024.

review.impact: The deps object is cast with `as never`, so the test type-checks even if `createChatStore`'s dependency shape changes. It can also pass or fail for the wrong reason if the store starts using other deps.
review.fix: Build a typed deps object, or use an existing test helper for store deps if the repo has one.

review.impact: The client-side size check is only a UX convenience. The server's 20 MB limit stays the actual enforcement, and this is correct as written. The check trusts `file.size`, but a client that skips it still hits the server limit, so there is no security impact. The client now imports from `../../src/chat/image-rules`. That file is pure constants with no server-only dependencies, so no secrets or server code reach the bundle.
review.fix: No change needed.

review.impact: This runtime telemetry file was changed by the build, and the changes are unrelated to the feature. It holds timing data only and no secrets, but it adds noise to the diff.
review.fix: Revert the file with `git checkout .werk/fold-ms.jsonl`, or ignore it in .gitignore, so it stays out of the change.
